(A short novel published ten years ago.
"An outrageous best-seller, banned by the Order three times!"
"Only one-tenth of readers truly understand it—are you one of them?"
"Incredible! The Russellian's satire remains as insightful as ever, even after all these years!"
So reads the editor's recommendation page… Clearly, this book stirred up quite a bit of controversy a decade ago.)

Far out across the stormy waters filled with jagged ridges and giant beasts on the surface of Solaris lies a group of small, unregarded islands. On this archipelago, the exiles-descended cultures are so amazing that they still think a unified thought is a pretty neat idea. These islands have—or rather had a problem, which was this: most of the people on them were unhappy for pretty much of the time.

After retirement, I kept thinking back to that afternoon when my friend and I first met.
Ford Percival. He was an alien.
On his first day in Egla Town, he ate ten baton bread without paying anything. Before the Divine Envoys could punish him for theft, I quickly paid off his debt.
Since the prayer, the Oracle of Mercy had wandered in my mind in search of something to connect with—until I met him, the poor outlander. He must have been starving.
"Hi, I'm Ford. I'm an alien. I'm analyzing your weapons. Quite odd components."
He said after I saved him. "And what is this place?" he continued.
An alien? Oh, I'd heard this kind of tale once from someone who claimed to be from a federation. He said Solaris was actually a living tomato—a tomato that could turn, breathe, even dance. And aliens, apparently, were from other tomatoes, living or dead.
"Egla Town," I replied.
"Egla Town, good. Wait, what is that?" He pointed at the windmills in the distance.
"Those are windmills. A cluster of Cyclop windmills, Briareos." Born and raised in Egla, I replied almost instinctively.
"C-Cyclops! Ah, I know about those! I've seen them before! But my stars—you actually managed to kill them? How did you people pull that off? Are those auto-rotating arrays made from their dead bodies? And what exactly is Briareos? A cooling device? A propeller engine? Or something to open up a network channel?"

(Continued)

After hearing my explanation, the self-proclaimed alien Ford seemed completely fascinated by the Cyclops. His emotions became so agitated that he plopped down on the ground, muttering some unintelligible words while pointing at the windmills in the distance.
So it was true—no matter where they came from, no matter what "tomatoes" they hailed from, anyone who laid eyes on the scenery of Egla couldn't help but fall in love with the chivalric literature.
So I straightened up, took three steps forward, and adjusted the nonexistent necktie, then explained graciously, "Exactly! That's right! Once, a righteous knight guided us to defeat the giant. Before that, all the people and Echoes in Egla Town were driven to the high ground in the south, fleeing from the giant's threat. Now, that oppressor lies buried beneath the sea of flowers. We built majestic windmills to irrigate the flowers and the farmlands, and named our past home Briareos, in honor of that knight's heroic deeds!"
After hearing my speech, Ford sat frozen on the ground, as if ten thousand Cetus the Tidebreakers had roared at him all at once, shattering his perception.
After a long pause, he asked me in disbelief, "Do you still have knights here?"
What did he just ask me?
Praise be to Imperator!
I could finally deliver the ranked No. 1 answer in the Top 10 Most Satisfying Moments for Egla People.
Putting on a solemn expression like the Acolytes of the Order, I envisioned a halo of nobility above my head, envisioned the almighty Imperator spreading wings before me, envisioned myself crowning a laurel at the Carnevale, envisioned standing in the grand church, wielding a sword as I was knighted, relishing the reverent gazes of the noble lords of Ragunna!
I replied, stressing each word with great emphasis:
"OF COURSE—"
"However, there are too many outsiders who seek the path of knighthood. Are you confident enough to accept the trial?"
The alien named Ford, whose Tacet Mark was blinking along excitedly, quickly grabbed my calf and shook it furiously, as if clinging to a log in the midst of a drowning. He cried out, "I am! I am! Please guide me to the legendary knight! As long as I can return to the planet Russel and save my hometown, I am willing to pay any price!"

(A feature on the culinary traditions of Ragunna.)

[Top Chef's Super Secrets]
Imagine yourself asking anyone on the streets of Ragunna, "Which restaurant is the best in Ragunna?"
Six out of ten will answer, "Trattoria Margherita!" Three will point to the family restaurant downtown, and the last one will say, "It's the place where the soft-tailed chef works!"
That's right! Such is the clout of Trattoria Margherita in Ragunna!
Amazing!
But what many don't know is that Trattoria Margherita is actually a family-run restaurant inspired by traditional Ragunna cuisine. From our investigation, we found that Egla Town still preserves this classic culinary tradition to this day. To maintain the special flavors of her dishes, Miss Margherita even takes time off to gather ingredients in Egla Town or Riccioli Islands!
Now, you might be wondering: "What? I can understand why Miss Margherita would go to Riccioli Islands for the fish harvest, but Egla Town? Isn't that a backwater town? And can the cuisine of Egla really be called Ragunna cuisine?"
Indeed, life in Egla isn't as thrilling as in the bustling Ragunna. People there live quietly, following the rhythm of nature. The town's trade and logistics are tied to Ragunna City. The people rise with the wind and rest by it, living a life shaped by windmills, wheat farms, and pastures.
But that's exactly why, for hundreds of years, the cuisine of Egla has remained unchanged. Here, the original flavors and cooking techniques of Ragunna have been preserved—using windmills to process crops and cooking food in traditional ways.
"This way, the ingredients and the food are especially precious! The cheese made from local pastures is creamy, and the meat is tender and flavorful! It's the perfect food to fill your belly!"
Miss Margherita commented during our interview.

[Comments from Special Guests]
Former Tax Envoy of the Order: The traditional cuisine is a remembrance of Rinascita's past. To forget it is to betray our heritage!
Orlando the Gourmet: The old man earlier sounded like he was chanting a slogan! What traditional cuisine? The bread from your town is as hard as a lethal weapon!

Former Privy Councilor's Notes (Part I)
...

At dawn, the Primus and I stood to bid farewell to the Pilgrim's Sail as it prepared to depart. Both the crowd and the acolytes watched with reverence as the believers boarded the ship. Only the most devout and courageous among them were chosen to embark on the Pilgrim's Sail, destined to meet the Sentinel in the distant sea.

For countless ages, Sentinel Imperator has rarely lingered in any one place, choosing instead to roam the seas, aiding vessels on their journeys. The Sentinel's guiding light has always led those lost upon the waves, helping them find their way back home or seek new lands for settlement. The Order believes that to face the storms and tides in search of the Sentinel's heavenly voice is one of the greatest honors a soul can aspire to.

Yet only those with practical experience can grasp the immense cost of each pilgrimage. Taxes and provisions are drawn from the commoners, skilled workers and sailors are taken from prominent families, and seasoned captains and chief mates are hired at great expense. All who embark on these treacherous seas are devout, but only those truly blessed by the Sentinel return with the promised glory and honor. Reflecting on history, the number of such fortunate souls is vanishingly small.

I have never questioned the purpose of the pilgrimage. My only concern is the immense cost it demands. Can we, in good conscience, allow these devoted believers to embark on a journey that burdens both mind and body? And as for our new Primus... What are his thoughts on this matter?

I looked to my side, surprised to find that my former seminary classmate, Lord Fenrico, had his face shrouded in a strange shadow.

...

Former Privy Councilor's Notes (Part II)
...

How has it come to this? After a sleepless night, I retreated to a secluded prayer room, seeking solace as I lay my confession before Sentinel Imperator. My hands trembled as I put these words to paper.

For a time, the Order ceased organizing large-scale pilgrimages, and the burdensome taxes were lifted. Though the people of Ragunna still honored the devotion of those who once sought the Sentinel across the distant seas, the Pilgrim's Sails had become a relic of the past. But everything changed after the bloody Carnevale... No, in truth, the shift began even earlier than that...

I still remember when the Primus delivered the order for correction, and I dutifully transcribed it: the Order would send violators of doctrine aboard the Pilgrim's Sails, stripping them of all official identities and setting them back onto the path of pilgrimage. Who could have foreseen that an act once meant to embody faith would come to serve as a form of punishment?

"The power of punishment and indoctrination shall be returned to the Sentinel," the Primus proclaimed to the assembled crowd. "Those transgressors who embark upon the pilgrimage in sincere repentance will, by their journey's end, be absolved of all transgressions and granted the Sentinel's forgiveness."

Yet no one truly knows if transgressors can fulfill their salvation, for no one has ever returned from the pilgrimage alive. "Those who commit acts of foolishness shall be sent to the Pilgrim's Sails"—this has become a steadfast law of the Order Penitentiary. Vandals defacing sacred statues, disloyal acolytes distorting doctrines, and even troupe members crafting satirical comedies—all have been condemned to the Pilgrim's Sails for their acts of blasphemy. Recently, however, familiar faces have joined their ranks, faces of those who had openly questioned the Primus's decrees.

I could have sworn my integrity on their faith and character, yet I stood by and watched as they were sent aboard the Pilgrim's Sails, doing nothing. No, it's no longer fitting to call them the Pilgrim's Sails. The common folk have given them a more appropriate name—the Fool's Sails, a vessel filled with those who have committed foolish acts.

Oh, Primus Fenrico... Is this the dream world you so passionately spoke of in the seminary?

...

Former Privy Councilor's Notes (Part III)
...

I was surprised at how calm I felt upon hearing the sentence from the Order Penitentiary. Perhaps my heart had grown as still as that of a dead person.

At dawn, like others before me, I was escorted by the Executors to board a Fool's Sail. Before the ship set sail, I glanced back at the port, only to find the Primus absent. Just as I expected, that man, now in control of unmatched power within the Order, has no need to concern himself with a fool stripped of his identity.

The Fool's Sails are nothing like the Pilgrim's Sails of old. Gone are the smooth, spacious decks and well-maintained sails. Instead, all I saw were rickety planks, loose screws, and splintered masts. The narrow cabins clearly lacked food and fresh water. I stared blankly at the other pilgrims around me. For now, we still manage to maintain some semblance of decorum and restraint, but I know that, before long, this ship will become nothing more than a cage filled with rampaging desires.

And even if we do reach the so-called destination, what awaits us there?

I once read the investigation reports sent back by the expatriate acolytes. That Penitent's End, shrouded in mist, is littered with the wrecks of Pilgrim's Sails. During those fateful voyages, the Fools who braved the storms never met the Sentinel. Instead, driven by the sea's undercurrents, they were cast ashore on that island, where the eerie glow of phosphorescence mingles with an unmistakable aura of death. I've even heard whispers of something far more terrifying lurking there, and the "Fire of Judgment"—a force so dreadful that even the Privy Council dares not speak of it.

...

Food is running out... Last night, someone lost control again, trying to lock themselves in the cabin to hoard the dwindling supplies...

O great Imperator, if you can hear my prayer, please grant us your final mercy through a storm. Absolve us from our misery, and let us... find peace at last.

(The remainder of the notes has been blurred by the seawater and is unreadable.)
Former Privy Councilor's Notes

Later, with the assault of the Lament, the civilization of the archipelago teetered on the brink of destruction and our family became one of the founders of the Ark, embarking on a quest to find a new settlement. The journey across the sea was treacherous. The fleets of the Ark were either swallowed by thick fog or torn apart by fierce storms. Yet, our family's Ark, guided by a heavenly voice, led the fleet to a lush archipelago, following the faint glow of a distant lighthouse. One of those islands would later become what is now Ragunna. The newly founded Ragunna was still in a state of flux. To strengthen the family's rule, our family head declared that the manifestation of ▇▇▇▇ was a symbol of the deep-sea faith and a response from the marine divinity to our devotion. This proclamation proved to be successful. As the number of believers grew, so too did the stability of our family's power. Later, some fishermen claimed that they had been assisted by ▇▇▇▇ during their fishing trips. This entity, long known as the Giant One, had existed for ages. Its shadow beneath the sea guided Ragunna's fishermen and fleets, helping them weather storms and bringing in harvests far greater than before. The Fisalia family was the original ruler of Ragunna, and we also laid the faith foundation of the Order. Yet, why have generations of family heads chosen to conceal this history? Why can't I remember Its name? Cursed be it, the wound... it is throbbing again. Something must be wrong with the air... I must find a safer place. Excerpts from The Hammer of Heresy (The pamphlet presents several radical opinions that appear to reflect the theories of an extreme school of thought.) What is witchcraft? And what is its true nature? The power of Resonance wielded by Resonators is known as a blessing from Sentinel Imperator. Devout followers of the Order are granted this blessing by adhering to its precepts, allowing them to channel the divine force through mortal bodies. Witchcraft, however, arises from vain desires—faithless souls, drawn by Leviathan, form a contract to practice forbidden arts. In doing so, they forsake the divine blessing bestowed upon them at birth and abandon their humanity, transforming into witches who seek to taint the mortal realm with profane power. The Divinity has shaped our world, and all that we hold dear flows from Their blessings. Yet witches, seduced by the Arch Enemy, pervert these divine creations into impure, disgraceful entities, crafting a false Resonance with them. The enemy's mark upon these witches is proof of their transgressions. With the aid of the Vessel of the Enemy, they can even transform into Tacet Discords, posing a grave threat to Imperator's faithful followers. Caution is essential, for anyone who craves freedom and worldly desires is vulnerable to becoming pawns of Leviathan. Thus, we must regularly cleanse and exorcise such souls. If we allow these heretics to grow unchecked, wielding their tainted power to defile the mortal realm, they will inevitably bring the Dark Tide upon Rinascita. It is the Order's duty to guide and govern them, ensuring they align with Imperator's divine will. Should they refuse to join the Order, swear loyalty to Imperator's statute, or diligently uphold its teachings, their misguided fate will be set right by the Pilgrim's Sails. We shall pray for them day and night, that they may be saved by our Sentinel Imperator. Praise be to Imperator. The Spy Network of the Order the Deep Ah, my friend, my companion on this quest for freedom and truth, I implore you—open this pamphlet only in a secure place, away from prying eyes. What I am about to reveal is crucial to your safety. Learn now how to identify the spies of the Order the Deep and evade their grasp. All Echoes bearing a golden halo upon their heads are spies of the Order the Deep, serving as "Angels." They are always seen alongside the Acolytes, serving as the Order's minions to take out the heretics. Rinascita, the Land of Echoes? Ha... not even the greatest satire could ever truly capture the utter absurdity of the reality we endure. First, you must beware of those lantern Echoes, known as Lucerna. Though they may appear harmless, they possess the ability to reveal so-called heretics hiding in the shadows of the night. Their light can illuminate the path ahead, yet it also serves as a blinding weapon, causing one to lose their sense of direction. There was once an instance where someone used Fae Ignis's Echo ability to remain concealed, only to be exposed under the unforgiving glow of a Lucerna's light. Next, there are the most commonly seen plaster statues, the infamous La Guardia, the most loyal guardians of the Order. Without commands from the Acolytes, they stand motionless, like silent statues. However, if you find yourself pursued by La Guardia, do not waste time fighting them. Instead, focus on locating the Acolyte of the Order Penitentiary who is issuing the command. Among all these minions, the most detestable is Vox Sanctus, perched high atop the church buildings. They serve as the Order's guards of honor. While they cannot move freely, they use their instruments to preach false doctrines day and night. These sermons infiltrate the souls of the Ragunnesi, poisoning their thoughts. Can you imagine that the children of Ragunna are forced to hear this nonsensical preaching the moment they are born into this world? Oppression by force may still leave room for resistance, but in Ragunna, how can one escape the spiritual chains that seep into every corner of life? Drawing on the diverse research and perspective studies from the New Federation in recent years, the paper also incorporates insights from Huanglong's archaeological experience in studying historical relics. Laurel and Sword (Part I) Laurel and Sword: On the Divine Imagery in The Golden Bough Journal Title: Ragunna Sea Breeze Drama Society Research Journal, Volume 1 Category: Literary Studies, Literary Theory, Theater, The Golden Bough The Golden Bough, a Ragunnesi narrative epic rich in history and deeply influenced by primitive religious culture, is renowned for its prominent theatrical elements. The epic begins with pastoral plays that draw on the primitive beliefs and customs of various tribes during the Age of a Thousand Islands. As the story unfolds, these diverse narratives converge under the guidance of Sentinel Imperator. The author employs the perspectives of the Divine Envoys to provide Imperator's view, allowing the characters to assume their roles in classical plays. Throughout the work, recurring symbols of religion and totems appear, echoing metaphors commonly found in traditional plays. The use of these theatrical elements has helped establish the epic as a beloved classic, cherished by both officials and commoners in Ragunna. Furthermore, it embeds the author's profound reflections on the will behind the Oracle delivered by Sentinel Imperator, as well as the social changes occurring in the region of Rinascita. ...(Some of the pages are missing) One of the most commendable scenes in The Golden Bough is the concluding Scene 3, where five storylines dramatically converge at the climax of the Carnevale: the Holy Forest of the Fagaceae Peninsula, the Order of Ragunna, the Keepers of Secrets in Thessaleo Fells, the successor of the governor in Septimont, and the gladiators, all merging in a grand finale. In this scene, the author masterfully interweaves characters and plotlines, capturing the unique allure of a grand historical tragicomedy. This convergence in Scene 3 has served as a template, inspiring countless plays thereafter. The scene's influence owes much to its intricate plot design, which displays a skillful technique that sets a standard in narrative structure. Beyond the theoretical framework of the work itself, this design—where each element reflects the core theme and draws from historical settings—has solidified this epic as a timeless classic, maintaining its relevance and reverence across cultural shifts in literary history. (See Note 23) The Golden Bough is recognized as the earliest work of art to connect tribal folklore with the Sentinel (see Note 24). In the climactic Scene 3 of the Carnevale, the five masks stand together, each pursuing their own faith, when Sentinel Imperator descends from above, bestowing the laurel upon the chosen Enlightened One—the main protagonist on stage. This ritual has since become a lasting cultural emblem in the hearts of the people of Rinascita. From this scene onward, every heroic journey must conclude with the ritual of "being laureated," whether the hero takes on the role of an actor on stage or a playwright behind the scenes during the Carnevale. Laurel and Sword (Part II) Laurel and Sword: On the Divine Imagery in The Golden Bough Journal Title: Ragunna Sea Breeze Drama Society Research Journal Category: Literary Studies, Literary Theory, Theater, The Golden Bough (Continued) The reason for Sentinel Imperator's descent at the climax of the Carnevale in The Golden Bough remains an open question, one largely unexamined in the epic itself or in related research. Historically, the prevailing view in the Seminary held that the Laureate must be the individual who most aligns with Rinascita's ideals and resonates with the Sentinel—not driven by dramatic passion or ulterior motives. For a long time, this perspective dominated studies of The Golden Bough and the broader field of Laureate literature, with the laurel seen as a symbol of immense honor and the embodiment of Rinascita's collective will. (See Note 25) However, following the cultural events after the Seminary incident, the Laureate's symbol and performances are now seen as expressions of the Sentinel's divine will—the guiding force behind delivering the Oracle and unifying the doctrines. The image of laurel has also come to represent this sacred intent. The author raises an intriguing question: given this interpretation, could the selection of the Laureate itself be seen as an indoctrination of freedom—a concept seemingly at odds with The Golden Bough? Can freedom, once indoctrinated, still be considered freedom? ...(Some of the pages are missing) [23] Charlie Welbeck, "The History of Reforms on the Rinascita Drama Aesthetics," published by Avinoleum Theological Seminary Culture Journal. Timeworn Logbook 2
Logbook_Number_#17
Mom, I miss you.
It's pretty misty here, and whenever it's like this, I can't help but think back to when I was little, back when we were together.
We used to live in a house out in the countryside. It was a thatched cottage, and in the summer, I could hear the dried hay on the roof crackling as the sun beat down. In the winter, the walls would get damp.
Inside, the house had a narrow hallway that led to the kitchen, where a broken lightbulb, somehow always mysteriously fixed, hung from the ceiling. The exposed wires were wrapped in black tape.
Along the hallway were two rooms. I slept in the smaller one, the one on the north side. The gauzy curtains, printed with the sacred verses of the Order, always felt a little eerie at night. When I couldn't sleep, I'd sneak out to the narrow hallway. It didn't matter if I kept my eyes open or closed. With my back against the damp walls, it was pitch black, and I couldn't even see my own breath.
The wind tried to sneak in through the cracks, and the door frame seemed to shrink. The old wires were starting to tear, and the damp air pressed against the bricks. My hair brushed against the wall, and behind it, a patch of quilt slowly shifted. All these sounds tangled together in my head, floating from my ears to my skin, then rushing back inside, shaking my bones with a soft, mesmerizing tremor.
I can't shake this feeling of dampness that echoes in my mind. Today, it's here again.
I just passed through the misty barrier on our route. It felt like an unsettling dream.
But don't worry about me. The safety manual says this mist can cause hallucinations, but it's harmless. I've made it through safely. Now, I need to check the inventory again, just in case someone took something while I was dreaming.
I really miss you, Mom. Don't forget what I promised. Once I've made my name here, I'll bring you to Ragunna.

I should tell you something to lift your spirits. Once I'm done with this job, I should have some time off to come and visit you.
Even though my job keeps me in the cabins, I get to see a lot of interesting things along the route.
Here, they don't use words like sunny or cloudy to describe the weather. Instead, they use emotions, which is kind of interesting, don't you think?
When it's "happy," we get to see rainbows, and the Nimbus Wraiths even dance under them.
When it's "gloomy," like today, it's cloudy, and we usually get to take the rest of the day off.
A "forced smile" is when it's sunny, but with a hint of rain. At times like that, the train picks up speed on purpose, and some of my colleagues will start telling loud jokes from the back of the train.
When it's "sorrowful," it rains, and the train moves very slowly.
"Unhappy" weather means thunder or strong winds. On days like that, we definitely take the day off. I just sleep through it.
And then there's "angry" weather, which is the scariest. The entire sea of clouds turns red. If we encounter that in the middle of the journey, our superiors make us wear soundproof earmuffs to work.
According to the route map, we'll be passing through a place called the Atrium of Reflections. I'd never heard of it before, but the seniors say we usually avoid it unless it's absolutely necessary.
I'll be careful, though. Don't worry about me. It's just a small challenge. Tough jobs need to be done, right?
As long as I put in the effort, I know I'll get the reward I deserve. Just wait for me, Mom. I'll bring you to Ragunna.

... very few people, including those within the Montelli family know when the Vitreum Dancers first appeared, even though these unobtrusive, unremarkable Echoes have long served the family. In fact, most of the Montellis do not know of Vitreum Dancers as anything other than their domestic security detail. Thus it remains easily overlooked that no two Vitreum Dancers are alike.

Knowledge gleaned from the stained-glass artwork found in the ruins around Ragunna suggests that Vitreum Dancers were once Tacet Discord frequencies. They appear in stained-glass art along with general depictions of The Order's religion. To this day Montelli explorers have yet to find two identical panes of stained glass. The Order's artists took pains to alter the composition of panes that depict the same story or motif. This suggests that the frequencies of modern Vitreum Dancers each contain unique information, much like their Tacet Discord forbearers.

According to the book "The Wealth and Legend of the Montellis," the origin of the Vitreum Dancer dates back in history to a time when a Montelli ancestor received the Laurel during the Carnevale from Imperator who then instructed him to go to a tower abandoned by The Order. Upon his return, he would not divulge what he saw and forbade all Montellis from approaching the tower again. Undoubtedly this Montelli ancestor brought back the very first Vitreum Dancer. On his deathbed, his last words were that the Sentinel's Oracle would not exert influence over Montellis at present, but would determine their future course of events.

And with that the tower was barred to all subsequent Montelli, and as the family's cohort of Vitreum Dancers expanded, the legend of their origins faded into obscurity.

Then came the tightening of the winch and the splintering of the keel.

After that, there was nothing but darkness. In that void, I couldn't see my ship, my crew, or it.
 
At first, my "leg" twitched uncontrollably... I thought I had died.
 
I lay on the beach, alone. There was no ship, no crew, and no sign of it.
 
I had none of its blood on my hands, no ship's wheel, no ropes, no harpoons. Nothing to grasp onto. 

But the sea breeze felt unfamiliar. I realized I'd never set foot on this beach before. Since we set sail from Cape Bedford, I remembered every passing port and beach, but this one... this one was unfamiliar.
 
It wasn't until a young man, dressed in foreign attire, kicked my boot to check if I was still alive that I realized I hadn't gone to hell, nor had I ascended to heaven.
 
"Ugh...Where am I?"

"Riccioli Island, Rinascita"

"Rinascita...."

"Did you suffer a shipwreck at sea?"

"My ship... My crew..."

"There's no one else nearby."

"If that's true... then in the end, I only am escaped alone..."
A Sealed Confession: Part 2

...Later, I came to realize that we were "blessed."
 
The people of Rinascita said that whale guided ships and sailors who perished at sea to the afterlife, like a ferryman of the underworld. I heard that the merchants of the Forgotten Sea could weigh memories and souls on their scales, exchanging them for an equal weight of gold.
 
But for some reason, we're all still alive. Or rather, we exist in a state between life and death.
 
Yes, in time, I found Starbuck and Queequeg on this island. They're still alive. "It," the whale they call "Cetus the Tidebreaker," was also still alive.
 
How can this be a "blessing"? This is nothing but a "curse!" I cannot accept this!
 
Once I've had my vengeance, death may take me. But if my vengeance fails, I cannot bear to remain in this world as a mere plaything for those I sought vengeance against! My fate is mine to decide, and only true death can end my conquest.
 
They don't understand. That whale, though it appears tame and gentle, is cunning and violent. It transforms death into an unjust eternity, making my vengeance just a footnote in its mockery of the sea… No, I will never accept this. I will never compromise!
A Sealed Confession: Part 3

All whales carry oil, and this oil can dissolve many things that water cannot. This is the conclusion we reached after crossing every sea.
 
It can dissolve things of every shape and nature into one, and there are even stories of people who fell into a whale's oil-filled brain and drowned, with no bones ever found. But I have never seen what oil this whale holds... Perhaps I never will.
 
More than twenty years have passed, and Pequod seems cursed. No matter what Queequeg tries, we cannot repair her. My crew, those "resurrected" sailors, have long since forgotten how to wield their harpoons. They no longer know how to fight the sea.
 
And it seems as though the whale is toying with me. Since that time, whether at sea or ashore, I have never laid eyes on it again. I do not wish to give up. I refuse to. As long as I can kill it, I will be freed from this curse-like "blessing" to find eternal rest.
 
But I... I am too old now. I can no longer lift a harpoon. I cannot fight that giant creature aboard one of these tiny "Gondolas."
 
Yes, my ideals, my beliefs, my fate, my vengeance—everything is gone. Everything has been swallowed by these foreign seas.
 
You are, of course, welcome to mock me. The rope of that harpoon, while I lived, bound me tightly to that whale. Even now, after death, I am still bound by it. In the past, I was unwilling to sever that rope. Now, I remain unwilling still...  But I can no longer drag it into the black depths of the sea.
 
Sometime later, a young man came to find me. He said his name was Ishmael, a sailor's apprentice, and he wanted to learn how to fish.
 
At that moment, I recalled that before Pequod's final voyage, there was a sailor named Ishmael at the Bedford dock. But he did not board my ship. He stayed at the port, and if he is still alive at sea, he would likely be as old as I am now. How ironic...

"Cultural Insights"

Literary works draw their vitality from two sources: The creator and the readers.

The creator gives it new life, while the readers help extend it through reading. Each time they share a piece of work or publish their thoughts and reviews, they breathe new life into it.

Some may find the term "life of a work" elusive, as it's too abstract and intangible.

However, a parallel can be easily drawn from human life. When discussing the concept of life, one essential topic is inevitably brought up—name. A name is a symbol of existence, one of the most important markers that separate individual lives. If one desires to feel the vitality of a work, the most direct approach would be to feel its name, the various names bestowed by creators and readers.

I once heard an eerie tale from a land in the east that spoke of a lady with skin as fair as snow who would stand in a snowstorm, cradling a wailing baby in her arms, begging the passersby to hold the baby for her. If some kindhearted individual agrees to that request, they'd soon find themselves unable to let go, bound to freeze to death.

Intriguing, isn't it? But, by this point, it's a fascinating tale that evokes many distinct images that cannot yet form the entirety of "life." 

But what if we give it a name? Like... "The Snow Woman." This name alone captures the entire narrative and defines its essence.

However, even with the name anchoring people's imaginations, the unusual nature of words means each person takes a narrative differently.

Hence... The life of a creative work is less controllable than human life.

So, if one day, people's understanding of a work is led astray, then words could turn into a devastating weapon.

What would we do then? Show anger? No, absolutely not! Anger is the cheapest outlet of dissent. As creators, all we can do is believe. Believe that our words can live in their most genuine form.
<alignright/>—Exclusive interview with the Golden Anthem

Day 1 – Unknown (The sky looks like broken, fractured glass) 15:49. I'll never forget this number. Just one minute before the observation was complete, a dark rift suddenly tore open from the device in front of me, shredding the stream of data across the screen. My boots were still stuck to the lab floor, but my upper body had already been pulled into a strange, chaotic storm. That was the beginning. Now I find myself in a city I don't recognize, having just survived a bizarre Lament. It slices through buildings, people, space, everything two-dimensional, three-dimensional… and maybe things beyond that, though my eyes can't quite make sense of it anymore. My Forte is Sealing, something that might be considered a way to resist the passage of time. Maybe, if I keep trying, I can use it to record the abnormalities in this city and figure out how to break through it. I'm not going to sit here and wait for the end.
Sumika's Notes - Entry 7

Day 7 – Cloudy (If what's above my head can still be called "weather.") When I woke up and checked my watch, I noticed something odd. Moss had started growing beneath the glass. This city, fractured and folded in on itself, seems trapped in some kind of temporal loop. Time moves forward and backward within a fixed range. But oddly enough, the plants don't seem bound by each "reset." The moss shouldn't be able to grow between the gears... unless time isn't flowing normally here. It's eroding, rushing, and spawning things that shouldn't even exist in the first place. Still, I'm grateful for this strange, unreasonable growth. It made me realize this city isn't beyond saving. There is a way out. (The pen seems to pause, leaving a small blot of ink on the paper.) There's one thing I still can't let go of. That rift... In my blurred memory, it sealed shut almost as soon as I was pulled into the storm. But if I can't figure out what caused it, or how to stop it. There's no way to guarantee it won't open again. And if it does... someone else could get dragged in. However, time's against me.

Day 136 – Abnormal Pressure (If this constant pressure in my ears counts as such) Among the supplies Chisa brought back today was a can of oranges, the label printed with a production date long past... but that hardly matters anymore. These so-called "foods" are really just compressed Remnant Energy. Chisa gave the can to me. She sat off to the side with a piece of spring steel she'd salvaged, slicing it into a curved blade using her Forte, turning it into a new weapon. Watching her, I suddenly recalled another day. She was sitting just like this, halfway through organizing supplies on the sofa, when she turned and asked me what my Forte really was. I showed her a small amber, the one containing a preserved memory of the first time we worked together at this home base: the lights were dim, she was repairing a weapon, and I was taking notes on anomalies in the city's time flow. It was a rare, peaceful night, as long as we could ignore the fact that we were still trapped in a city sealed off from the outside world. To hold out against the erratic occurrences of the Lament, I once tried to learn Chisa's practical skills, but I failed. Of course I did. Still, she taught me a few special ways to leave markings. I remember what she said back then: "Stop treating everything like a science experiment. Think of every piece of scrap metal as a blade that never misses—" (The pen pierced the page, leaving a blot of ink.) And I know she truly meant it. This city, drenched in Lament, is riddled with danger. And yet, she always throws herself forward to shield everyone else. She thinks I haven't noticed how much she's burning herself out... doesn't know her body's running at the edge of collapse. But I've done the calculations many times. I know exactly how long she has before she crosses the breaking point. The only good thing is that this Sonoro seems to have stalled time and her condition. But I can't let her stay like this forever. I want to take her back. Back to the Black Shores, to the people I trust. There has to be a solution waiting there. I'll bring her back. From the large terrace on the second floor, you can see a beautiful view of the city center. It's been a long time since I've seen her this excited. It feels like we're one step closer to breaking the loop. And in fact, we are making progress. (The handwriting sharpens slightly.) "Excuse me... I'd like to read this book. Do I need to register here?"
 
Accompanying the timid voice before me was a biography, its cover bearing the portrait of the Blessed Maiden. I looked up from the desk and saw a small girl with pale violet curls. There was a mole just beneath one of her eyes. Tiny and delicate. Her skin was so pale that it was nearly translucent like someone who hadn't seen sunlight in a very long time.
 
"You're free to read anything here. Just remember to put the books away when you're done," I said as gently as I could, worried the solemn atmosphere of the library might frighten her away.
 
She was clearly not an Avinoleum student, yet she began appearing regularly in the library in the days that followed. She wandered between the circular shelves, always quietly absorbed in whatever book she picked up. Sometimes she asked me to help her find specific texts. Some were dense theological books, while others were thick volumes on the ocean or pharmacology—not quite the usual interests for someone her age. We grew acquainted. I learned that she'd been brought to Avinoleum by her relatives. They had their own matters to attend to and left her to wander freely in this comparatively safe library.
 
Her departure was as sudden as her arrival. That afternoon, as if answering some unseen summons, she closed the book in her hands and slid it back onto the shelf. I remember it. It was a study of the traditions of the Blessed Maiden in Ragunna. In the slanting dusk light, a long shadow stretched across the floor. Her guardian, presumably.
 
"Thank you for looking after me these past few days." She stood in front of me, doing her best to smile. "Cantarella... I'm Cantarella Fisalia."
 
That surname explained a great many things. Her belated introduction. The sorrow hidden in her words. The flicker of bitterness as she looked toward the door. I rose and took her hand. At the very least, I didn't want her to feel alone on the walk back to the threshold.

Retirement drew closer with each passing day, and time flowed quietly within the library. I thought there would be no more ripples.
 
"Excuse me... I'd like to read this book. Do I need to register here?"
 
Accompanying the timid voice before me was a biography, its cover bearing the portrait of the Blessed Maiden. I looked up from the desk and saw a small girl with pale violet curls. There was a mole just beneath one of her eyes. Tiny and delicate. Her skin was so pale that it was nearly translucent like someone who hadn't seen sunlight in a very long time.
 
"You're free to read anything here. Just remember to put the books away when you're done," I said as gently as I could, worried the solemn atmosphere of the library might frighten her away.
 
She was clearly not an Avinoleum student, yet she began appearing regularly in the library in the days that followed. She wandered between the circular shelves, always quietly absorbed in whatever book she picked up. Sometimes she asked me to help her find specific texts. Some were dense theological books, while others were thick volumes on the ocean or pharmacology—not quite the usual interests for someone her age. We grew acquainted. I learned that she'd been brought to Avinoleum by her relatives. They had their own matters to attend to and left her to wander freely in this comparatively safe library.
 
Her departure was as sudden as her arrival. That afternoon, as if answering some unseen summons, she closed the book in her hands and slid it back onto the shelf. I remember it. It was a study of the traditions of the Blessed Maiden in Ragunna. In the slanting dusk light, a long shadow stretched across the floor. Her guardian, presumably.
 
"Thank you for looking after me these past few days." She stood in front of me, doing her best to smile. "Cantarella... I'm Cantarella Fisalia."
 
That surname explained a great many things. Her belated introduction. The sorrow hidden in her words. The flicker of bitterness as she looked toward the door. I rose and took her hand. At the very least, I didn't want her to feel alone on the walk back to the threshold."

Ecological Field Notes on Scourgewings

As the name implies, Scourgewing dragons are often associated with ill omens in folklore, their appearance believed to be a harbinger of disaster. The first wave of sightings coincided with the eve of the first Dark Tide. Since then, their silhouettes have been reported ahead of nearly every major catastrophe.

But is such a connection real? Unlikely. It's a classic case of mistaking correlation for causation. In truth, Scourgewings don't bring disaster, certainly not the Dark Tide. They merely appear beforehand.

...

Some ecologists argue that the creature's frequency dates all the way back to the Age of a Thousand Islands. Though rare, the species has endured, likely owing to their acute sensitivity to environmental changes. The antennae on their heads can detect subtle environmental shifts, allowing them to avoid danger preemptively. The pattern we've observed points to a more grounded explanation: the Scourgewings sense the coming of disaster, and perhaps, in their own way, try to warn us.

They are not harbingers of disaster, but early messengers.

Worn Journal of a Gladiator I

Every Gladiator in Septimont knows this place. It's where we hunt and test our mettle.

The dragon corpse lying out there draws in all sorts of TDs, beasts, and glory-chasing Gladiators like us. I've no doubt Flavio was here. I saw his breastplate in one of those old halls. His family sigil was split in half, perhaps his way of cutting ties with his House. I also couldn't help noticing the dents and gashes all over the armor, some deep, some just scratches. To us, those are medals.

Locals say this battered piece once belonged to a man who tamed a damn dragon, a Scourgewing. Faced it alone and made it submit to his will. While I was drowning in ale over my sister's death, Flavio was out in the wilds conquering with his sword. No one knows where he went with the dragon, but I know he's walking the path toward glory... He's becoming a legend.

A pack of Gladiators swaggered past me, fully armed. I overheard them talking. They were tracking a Scourgewing near the Border Mountains. But unlike Flavio, they weren't after a duel, only a dirty hunt.

They'll probably haul it back to the city and sell it off for a good price. That's all it is to them.
Worn Journal of a Gladiator II

...

It's certain now. Something unnatural is happening outside. Every exit is sealed by forces not of this world. Iaen and I have no way out. Whispers claw at my ears. Only the pain of my wounds is keeping my mind from slipping away. This journal will likely be my last testament.

Here's the truth I've choked on for too long. Flavio and I, we swore to face off fair and square in the Colosseum finals, to settle our rivalry the right way. But the night before, his House sent someone to me with a message to hold back if things got rough. The offer came with better money than the prize, and a promise to find the best doctor for my ailing sister. I said yes... sold my honor as cheaply as those scum hunting Iaen. I disgraced that sacred fight with a pathetic show, and he saw right through me. I've never seen a man look so disappointed. In me, in his House, and in the arena itself. He vanished into the wilds and never returned.

After my sister passed, I tried to find him in Septimont. Thought I could square the debt and give him a real fight. As I write these words, I realize it wasn't just guilt that led me here. It was regret that I never faced him as a true Gladiator. Now I'll never have the chance.

I'm leaving this to Iaen. It will outlive me, no doubt. If someone ever reads these words, know they are the last confessions of Levis. I pray that Flavio, wherever the wilds have taken him, has found the glory that he deserves.

May applause greet all who walk the path of glory.

"Project Echo Reborn" Meeting Record

"Project Echo Reborn" Meeting Record

- Many TDs inherently possess consciousness. Even after being cut and bridged, their chaotic consciousness persists. That means they still tend to evolve by absorbing Reverberations after being stabilized into Common Echoes. While we've managed to suppress their absorption instinct post-frequency cutting, preventing their chaotic evolution, but to fully eliminate their consciousness...

- Perhaps we should change course and create entirely new consciousness modules. We can implant only the consciousness we need into the Echoes, forcibly overriding their original consciousness. The power They granted to us allows this. I've tested it.

- Overwriting their consciousness will only further destabilize the Common Echoes and disrupt the established methods of their creation.

- I think there might be a solution. The new consciousness module could be planted deep within the Echoes' original consciousness, functioning only when needed. In the meantime, we can continue researching how to improve the stability of consciousness transformation. But there's one thing, if the deeper consciousness is activated, it would be irreversible.

-We must delay activation indefinitely until we can ensure the Echoes' stability after alteration.

I'm sorry, Misha. It's been so long since I last reached out… You must've been so worried. This letter should've been in your hands days ago. But something happened. We were ambushed. A sudden attack by the Dark Tide's creations. The captain acted fast. Thanks to him, the team survived with just a few wounds.

Just before I wrote this, I buried the captain beneath a tree outside town. I've done this before, burying a companion's body. But no matter how many times I touch blood and soil, it never stops hurting. It never gets easier.

I'm scared, Misha. I wish I could come back to you right now. I wish I could hold you and Ina in my arms one more time. But I can't—not yet. Discarded Log I

It's been forty-eight hours. I don't think they'll find us now.
 
You've done well, old friend. This is where your journey ends. I never expected a Sabercat Reaver. Without the proper tools, I can't fix you.
 
It seems I was born worthless and will die the same. I had originally hoped for you to record the effects of the Void Storm on the human body and the surrounding environment when I entered it, then deliver the data to the Spacetrek Collective. A coward's last shred of dignity.
 
The Academy will find the note in my room soon enough. Yes, this is a journey to die. I intend to let the Void Storm take my life.
 
Perhaps someone will find this journal long after I'm gone. Let it serve as my farewell to you, stranger.
 
Forgive me for leaving without a proper farewell. Please understand, this isn't a sudden impulse, but the final compromise after a long and painful struggle.
 
As a researcher who once held science as my faith, I believed that the pursuit of knowledge is civilization's most noble mission. My field once granted me glimpses of the universe's profound beauty. Those elegant equations on the blackboard seemed to guide me toward pushing open the doors of progress.

But perhaps every era is destined to face the same tragedy. Researchers believe they stand on the shoulders of giants, only to look down one day and find themselves standing on the ruins of their own idealism. Failure, after failure, after failure... Was this always my limit?
 
That's when a colleague reached out. He claimed he could help me overcome my technical bottlenecks, but everything had to be done in secret. I later discovered he was a Fractsidus spy. On the day he was captured, he never revealed our collaboration. He only left me with a smile. What was he smiling at? That I was next? Or that I was no longer the man I used to be? In our work together, I had already crossed lines that violate scientific ethics.
 
The purity of knowledge in my eyes had long been corrupted. Whenever I heard my colleagues' praise during academic conferences, I felt my stomach twist. Their admiration was evidence of my betrayal of science.
 
Death is all that's left for me now. But even though my soul is sullied, I wish to leave one last, small thing of value before I go.
 
The Void Storm. None would volunteer to enter it. I imagine if someone would go into it... It would certainly garner data of immense value.
 
I do not seek forgiveness, nor do I expect to be understood. I only hope my departure becomes a question mark, lingering in the minds of those who still believe in the purity of knowledge...

Death only gives one chance. I can't waste it. First, I must observe the Void Storm. Perhaps I'll stay with the Roya tribe until I'm ready.
Discarded Log II

Time has lost all meaning to me. It's nothing but a countdown now.
 
I haven't encountered the Void Storm yet, but I've learned much from the Royan archives. Their records speak of survivors. What allows one to live through it? Where is the line that decides what gets erased and what remains?
 
Ugh... this fever won't break. I should set aside these heavy thoughts for today.
 
Why is it that whenever I relax, I am reminded of the Roya tribe members from when I first arrived?

I watched them live alongside the Exoswarm, toiling with simple tools. I saw them observe the night sky and strange phenomena with their own eyes, patiently calculating, step by step, summarizing patterns.
 
At night, they would sit around the campfire. No one dwelled on the day's troubles. They simply planned for tomorrow, then sang a song with a strange, simple, repetitive melody, as if speaking to Lahai-Roi. Or perhaps it was their way of encouraging themselves.

Watching the firelight dance on their faces—wrinkled and young—a profound confusion struck me.
 
We, in our "advanced" civilization, seek to master nature through technology, to eliminate all uncertainty and pain. When progress stalls, we despair, even betray our morals for a breakthrough. We believe human dignity lies in "conquest."
 
But for the Roya... even though a "small" storm could wipe away everything they worked so hard to build, they show no despair. Their dignity isn't about "conquest." Instead, they chose silence. Time and time again, they bend their bodies, measure the broken land with their feet, and begin anew.
 
I once despised this "inefficient" struggle, seeing it as a sign of an unprogressive society. But now, what rises in my heart is… respect.
 
Such a feeling of contradiction claws at me from the inside. The "pure science" I've pursued my entire life, if it ultimately led me to betrayal and nihilism, then where is its purity? These tribal people, who knew nothing of "science" at first, have proven a more fundamental purity through their very existence—the will to struggle and live, no matter how many times they're beaten down.
 
Here I am, the lofty professor, brought down from my high horse. I'm driven to suicide by the "impurity" of my ideals, while they, with their hands in the dirt, fight to live. In that struggle, they embody life's truest purity.
 
The rain outside grows louder, much like their song… I'll leave once the fever breaks. I need to get closer to the Void Storm, to understand it more. My old droid friend may be broken, but I still have a way to record it all. If I remember correctly, there should be an Outcast camp up ahead.
Final Log

This is likely my final recording. I haven't formally introduced myself yet. I am Sestan, a professor from Startorch Academy.
 
I don't know what awaits me now...
 
I was perched at a high point, recording data on the Void Storm. While adjusting my instruments, I saw a mech reindeer, unaware, drifting too close to the edge of the distortion. Slowly. So slowly. I knew an invisible force would snuff out its fragile life in an instant.

In that moment, my mind went blank.
 
I did not weigh the value of life, did not calculate the odds of success, did not look back on a lifetime of sins and confusion. My body acted before any rational thought could intervene.
 
I rushed forward and pushed the reindeer out. And I was pulled in instead.
 
Life is full of surprises. To be honest... I had already let go of any thought of suicide. This journey, the people I've met along the way... they showed me how.
 
In the Roya tribe, I witnessed the strength of the human spirit. In the Outcast camp, among fellow traitors, I learned about forgiveness from their struggle to survive. Everyone was just trying to live, while I was wallowing in self-pity, clinging to the guise of an idealist.
 
My life and my ideals had strayed from their path. And so... in this moment, I rushed forward. Not just toward death, but toward a reunion with the true spirit of science: to protect life, no matter how small.
 
Before I vanish completely, I'll try to remain conscious. I will record my physical sensations and the frequency fluctuations, then upload the data to this Cassette and a data drive. Consider this my final observation report. I hope it proves useful.
 
Body temperature: normal... Wrist movement: normal... Feet, hmm... losing sensation...
 
………………
 
Twenty-three minutes have passed...
 
…………
 
Hmm... Death, is it always this quiet? I used to think my students were too noisy. But now, haha, I find myself missing the noise...
 
External sound... decaying rapidly...
 
Hmm... after the sounds disappear, will the light go next...?
 
Finally... I'm home...

What You Should Never Do As A Startorch Express Passenger (Excerpt)

1. Food and Beverages For your safety, eating and drinking are strictly prohibited while the Express is in motion. Due to potential environmental hazards or Exoswarm activity, the Express may execute emergency braking at any time. Violation of this rule may result in choking, or injury from food packaging. The risk is significantly higher during vertical transit phases within the Starward Riseway. The high acceleration forces present a severe health hazard if consumables are ingested. 2. Pets, Bionic Units, & Exoswarm To maintain onboard safety and order, all pets and bionic devices must be checked in for transport. Live animals must be placed in sturdy carriers. Bionic units must be powered down and stored in secure containers before check-in. Bringing them into passenger carriages is strictly prohibited. Exoswarm may board only in designated compartments under the supervision of a licensed Shepherd. Exoswarm must undergo prior training to prevent panic responses during sudden acceleration, which could compromise the safety of all onboard. If you require a pet carrier or storage container, please visit the loading area for assistance. 3. Jumping During Vertical Acceleration or Descent This rule may sound absurd, but every absurd rule comes from an even more absurd real incident. A rumor once circulated claiming that a person "cannot jump" during vertical acceleration or descent. While basic physics, some students took it as a personal challenge. They fabricated exoskeleton rigs, smuggled them aboard, and attempted to "challenge the laws of nature." Fortunately, staff intervened in time to prevent what would have been certain injury and significant damage to the Express. During all operations, please remain seated with your safety belt fastened. Under the stars, we are both observers and part of the cosmos itself. When you close this guide, your real journey has only just begun.

Forget the names of the constellations. What matters is that you looked up and let the starlight in. The moment you first lost yourself in the beauty of the stars is more precious than any astronomical fact.

A gentle reminder for every stargazer:
1. There's no need to bring advanced telescopes. A curious heart is all you need.
2. Pick a night when the moon is shy, and the sky is clear.
3. Bring a star chart, a flashlight, and a friend who'd love to share the quiet of a starlit night with you.

When the starlight touches you, remember this: every cell, every fiber, every element that makes you you was born in the heart of a star. You are, in your own way, stardust made manifest.

May the stars always bring you peace and inspiration.

Dedicated to all those who have ever stopped and looked up.

She mixed me a drink once, called "Starfall."
It was the most exquisite taste I've ever known.
But she left no recipe.
She said it wasn't necessary. That even with a recipe, the taste could never be recreated.
"If you love it," she told me, "then cherish the moment you drink it."

She said eternity is a lie, a delusion.
"Then what is real?" I asked.
"The answer is where a river of stars falls. Come with me, and we'll see it together."
But I could not go.
Our visions of life were too far apart. I would not yield.
So I swore I would recreate the taste of "Starfall."
What was in it? Grenadine, Bols Blue, sparkling water, salt on the rim, and a lemon wedge.
Or was there something else?
Perhaps a hint of regret, or the weight of a sigh?

She always loves fleeting things.
She loves the flicker of light, the glow of dusk, the fall of a flower.
Meteors in the night sky, ripples on a lake.
She loves the tide rising and falling.
A dancer leaping in midair.
And most of all… fireworks.
Those moments are beautiful, I know.
But what comes after?
How do I face their vanishing?
I wish such moments could last forever.
But she never seemed to care.
I don't understand.
I truly don't.

Log Entry–No. 322 I
Created by: Amur
 
The Shimmer was not present, and Void Storm concentration remains within normal parameters. However, a Void Storm burst occurred moments ago, engulfing our research outpost. The storm caught two personnel off guard, sweeping them both away. Fortunately, they sounded the emergency alarm in their final moments, ensuring that Tavia and I could evacuate just in time.
 
The storm took our vehicles, and it's only a matter of time before it catches up to us.
 
Haha, I heard that very few manage to survive a Void Storm. We've already encountered a Void Storm burst, which they call a one-in-a-billion event, so who's to say we won't end up meeting another that could save our lives? My vacation was supposed to start in two days... I even planned to call my mom.
 
The storm is closing in, but thankfully, I found a sled some researcher was kind enough to leave behind. I'm going to take a gamble: if we slide down this steep slope, we might be able to outrun the Void Storm. I think our chances are pretty good—after all, the odds of finding something like this in the access-restricted Roya Frostlands were small to begin with, so it looks like our luck is holding up.
 
Wish me luck, Mom.
 
Log Entry–No. 322 II
Created by: Tavia
Amur was taken by the Void Storm. I'll be joining him soon.
 
The sled was broken—that's why it was left behind. We spent too much time checking it and lost valuable time. But even if we hadn't picked it up, the Void Storm would have still swallowed us whole sooner or later. It's unfortunate we took a gamble and lost.
 
The Void Storm is growing stronger. I'm afraid I won't make it. Even so, I'll keep running to minimize Voidmatter corruption to the FCR.

16.2.1 Procedure for Being Stranded on Ice
 
Should you become stranded on ice after a slip or fall, do not attempt to stand up on your own, as concentrated ground force may cause the ice to fracture, or you may suffer injuries from falling a second time. Instead, remain prone and use your hands and feet to push along the ice, gradually moving your body toward the edge of the ice surface. Only attempt to stand once you have reached the edge.
 
If others are nearby, have them use a rope to pull you off the ice. Under no circumstances should you venture into an area of hazard before a careful assessment has been made of the conditions of the ice underfoot.
 
Researcher's annotation: Given the correct posture, you can remain steady even on slippery ice. The key is to keep your center of gravity as low as possible, keep your upper body upright, and use both hands to balance… All right, this might not sound very intuitive, but you'll probably understand after one or two falls. If you do end up falling, just call out to me—I'll get you off the ice with practiced ease.

Today, I walked through the valley of the shadow of death. I was surrounded by a swarm of Tacet Discords.
Right when I'd given up hope, I heard a noise. It wasn't the wind, but a crisp, rhythmic "ding... ding..." like a sharp blade tapping against ice.
I forced my eyes open. They were practically sealed shut with the frost.

A figure appeared before me. A girl, I think. White robes. She held a long, straight blade made of ice, transparent and clear. As she moved, the tip would occasionally graze the ground, making that cold "ding-ding" sound.
 She didn't say a word. Just walked toward the swarm. The snow swallowed her fast. I heard the "ding... ding..." of her blade against the ground a few more times before everything fell silent. When I looked again, both she and the Discords were gone.
 
I didn't think. I just ran. When I got back to camp, my colleagues  looked at me like they'd seen a ghost. Turns out I'd been missing for four hours. I told them everything. They said it was a hallucination.
So... was it?
Does a woman with a blade of ice truly walk the frostlands of Lahai-Roi?
Maybe I should go back there tomorrow and take another look.

My aunt hails from Egla Town, a place where the windmills never tire and the wild winds carry the legends of the knights on every breeze. I once dreamed of journeying there, but Rinascita is a world away. My studies have ever kept me from following where the knights might lead.

...

I managed to lead them to safety... but in the doing, I myself was claimed by the storm.
Is this where my journey ends? A fitting conclusion to my tale, I suppose.
But then... Hogarth, the Seventeenth Grand Commander, appeared.
Though small in stature, he pulled me into the safety of his hollow frame—his "trash bin" vessel—and with every ounce of his strength, he scaled the high ground.
"Joljotra, your summer vacation ends today as the true Seventeenth Grand Commander. You shall begin a glorious new semester for yourself... while I take up the mantle as the Grand Commander who follows."
So it declared.

[Large sections of the notebook are illegible, corroded by some unknown force. From the remaining fragments, you deduce it's the diary of a Roya girl named Lotta.]
...
Today, Papa took me to see the Solsworn lady. She said a lot of things I couldn't really understand... something about my Forte being special. So that's why the Exoswarm flee the second they see me. On the way home, Papa wouldn't stop sighing. I've never seen him look so worried before.
I think I know why. Last time, when I tried to play with the Exoswarm he was herding, they just... snapped. They panicked and ran wild. They even hurt Mama.
"Was that my fault?" I asked him. He just sighed, then reached out and rubbed my head with his big, warm hand.
"Do not fret, little one," he said, his voice light like always. "If you are not meant to be a Shepherdess, you are still a good girl."
...
Papa came home with nothing today. He said he gave the Exoswarm to the other Shepherds. I know he is afraid they will hurt Mama again.
This is all my fault. If I weren't like this, Papa wouldn't have lost his job. He'd still be out there, like one of those proud Shepherds guiding the Exoswarm across the frostlands, paying tribute to Baldur for the sunlight and everything we have.
...
Papa seemed happy today. I think it's because Mama is almost healed. He took me to a village far, far away. There's an old granny living there, and he asked me to stay with her to learn stone carving. The granny told me she has a power just like mine, something that makes the Exoswarm angry, so she moved out here to be alone. Papa promised me that carving is a lot of fun, and that he and Mama would come visit me as often as they could.
...
He was right. Stone carving is fun. The granny has taught me everything she knows. She even told me I have a "natural gift." That's the first time anyone has ever said that to me! Mama and Papa must be really busy, though. They haven't visited in over ten days. But it's okay, because I've made some new friends: Fenrir, a Toskr Lemming who can't stop dancing; Dallas, a Fluffguin who loves eating fish, and Bori, a Kronapuff who loves to nibble on flowers.
I carved all of us together onto a big stone slab. Granny says that means we'll be friends forever and ever.
...
Mama and Papa still haven't come. I asked Fenrir, Dallas, and Bori to go to the village and look for them. I miss them so much.
But I waited and waited... and nobody came back. Not Mama, not Papa... not my fluffy friends.
A few days later, Uncle Vilhelm from the village came to talk to Granny. He didn't look like the proud, strong Shepherd I remembered. He looked exhausted. They talked for a long time while I hid outside. I caught Papa's name, something about our village, and things like "Void Storms" and "Tacet Discords."
Just hearing those names makes my stomach do flips... I think I should sneak back to the village and see for myself. As long as I stay away from the Exoswarm, it should be fine.
Lotta's Diary - II

[Large sections of the notebook are illegible, corroded by some unknown force. From the remaining fragments, you deduce it's the diary of a Roya girl named Lotta.]
...
...
It's all gone. Everything.
I searched for so long for where the village used to be. All I found was a small patch of scorched fur, a tuft of feathers... and half a beak. Papa. Mama... everyone in the village... my friends... they're all gone.
Something is watching me. I don't want to run anymore.
...
It took me a long, long time to learn how to speak again. Even longer to find the courage to open this diary.
The woman who saved me from those monsters called herself a professor from Startorch Academy. She's beautiful, but she doesn't look like anyone from our village. She told me I have a rare kind of Forte, something that makes me a "potential Synchronist."
I told her everything that happened to the village. I asked her: is this a blessing from <ano=the Exostrider>Baldur</ano>? Or the cruelest curse <ano=the Threnodian>Hvedrungr</ano> ever devised?
She was silent for a while. Then, she told me her own homeland had been swallowed by a similar disaster. She crossed an ocean so vast I can't even imagine it, all to find a way to free the world from this fate. She asked me to join the Academy. She said that whether my power is a blessing or a curse, it might be the key to opening the door to our future.
...But I have nothing left. Even if <ano=the Exostrider>Baldur</ano> is waiting behind that door, it can't give back what I've already lost.
...
I went back to Granny's place to say goodbye and thank her for everything. I told her I was leaving for the Academy.
"We Roya carve our words into stone," she said, her voice as kind as ever, "so that <ano=the Threnodian>Hvedrungr</ano> cannot erase our existence. And those children at the Academy use something they call 'Cassettes' to do the same. To me, you're just going somewhere else... to carve the statue that belongs to you."
"As long as the memory remains, so does the soul."
After I arrived at the Academy, I read this notebook from the very first page to the last. Papa, Mama, Fenrir, Dallas, Bori... Granny was right. They're still alive here in these pages, and deep within my mind. Maybe, without even realizing it, I've become a living statue carved with all their names.
I'll carry their souls with me, wherever I go. I promise.
...
Void Storms. Even the name is terrifying.
I've spent my life trying to outrun its shadow. It's one of <ano=the Threnodian>Hvedrungr's</ano> venomous tendrils, dragging everything I love into the nothingness. I thought... I thought I had learned how to ignore it.
But seeing it appear again, I realized something. All these years of study... they were just preparation for this exact moment. Again and again, I've pushed my Forte to its limit, right to the edge of Overclocking. And now, I finally understand. I'm ready.
Just like the professor said, only I, only my Forte, can save that village from being wiped out. I couldn't save my own home back then. But this time, I won't stand by and watch the dark take the people I love.
It's time to go.

In the outlying corner of the Fabricatorium lies an Echo burial ground embedded into deep-sea canyons. Here, heaps of abandoned Brooders cover the floor. Decommissioned Echoes wait in lines to be dismantled and incinerated in the workshops. Their frequencies will be recycled and redirected across the Fabricatorium, feeding the creation of new Echoes.
Fallen Grave

The core area in the Fabricatorium of the Deep for developing Common Echoes. Endless arrays of Echo Brooders line the space, cradling Echoes awaiting rebirth.
As the foundation of the Common Echo system, this site commands heavy investment of security and research resources by the Order.
Anima Cradle

The energy storage and distribution center of the Fabricatorium.
The recycled energy from the Fallen Grave converges here, waiting to be distributed to other areas as needed. All energy is reserved in liquid media. Frequencies born of the tides once again dissolve in water.
Energy Hub

A praying ground dedicated to the Acolytes dwelling under the sea, the only sanctuary of the Order's undersea expanse that remains untouched by the Fractsidus.
These broken Acolytes are the willing victims of the Order's experiments to free Ragunna's consciousness from the Dark Tide. The countless failed trials shattered their minds, yet still they cling to their fervent memories of faith. Fenrico placed them beneath the waves to live peacefully, away from the prying eyes of the world.
Sanctuary of Faith

The central tower of the Fabricatorium of the Deep, where the Lost Beyond is created.
As the control hub of the entire Fabricatorium, the tower regulates the activities in all other areas within the facility. Deep in the tower keeps the lantern of the first Primus, the first gift bestowed upon the Order by Sentinel Imperator.
Lumen Tower

A natural pass of solid bedrock, marked by jagged cliffs and towering stone pillars. As the gateway to the Sanguis Plateaus, it has stood witness for generations as Gladiators embarked on their sacred hunt, all under the silent watch of the stone colossus of Atilius, the Hero of Heroes.
Atilius Canyon

A sprawling encampment near Atilius Canyon. This well-equipped base offers rest and recovery to battle-worn Gladiators. Supported by skilled personnel and Echoes, the camp ensures every Gladiator returns to the hunt at their best, ready to face the Dark Tide creatures once more.
Hunter's Den

The primary hunting grounds for Septimontians for generations. Legend has it that the forest's eternal crimson hue comes from blood spilled in battle. Gladiators drive the Dark Tide's creations into the woods, using traps, tactics, and brute strength to stem the Dark Tide.
Maroonwood

A plateau blooming with Asphodels, where spring winds never quite manage to carry the blossoms out to sea. Here, "spirits" linger where they sought glory while alive, and where death cut their dreams short.
Asphodel Barrens
A town wiped out by the Dark Tide. All that remains are the Threnodian Leviathan's whispers and thoughts. People call this place Murmurstown in a desperate attempt to bury an agony too great to bear.
Murmurstown

The highest peak in the Sanguis Plateaus, named for both its unique summit and the three Heroes of Heroes who once stood there. To Gladiators, it is sacred ground. Legend says that each Hero of Heroes faced their final trial there, and only then would they conquer fate and be cloaked in glory.
Three Heroes' Crest
A quiet, deserted quarter, where the city's busiest crossroads once bustled with life. Rows of commercial towers and shops line the street, and at the corner stands the famous Shashou Cafe.
Honami Crossing

Built under the City Hall's initiative, this once-grand football arena has long fallen into neglect. In its prime, however, the annual "Harukaze Cup" drew school teams from across the region and filled the stands with cheering crowds.
Harukaze Stadium

Nestled in the city's center, this park was once a beloved retreat, its gardens draped in cascades of wisteria. The fish windsocks floating above the park used to be a popular sight, but now, for some reason, they all seem to be slowly drifting toward a single spot...
Honami Central Park
A cultural passage beneath the city, famed for its flower trees and the celebrated Seisen Garden. It was once the city's hub for film festivals and photography exhibitions.
Hanakage Underground Street

Once Honami's business center, this area is now a graveyard of empty skyscrapers, collapsed passages, and abandoned convention centers. The giant cherry blossom trees rising from the ruins have become its new landmark.
Commercial District

This area was once known as "Honami's most beautiful living quarter," where homes and cherry blossoms stood in perfect harmony. Though the houses now lie hollow and lifeless, the cherry blossoms only flourish more vibrantly…
Sakura Quarter

Named after the colossal Exostrider greatsword that holds up the underground dome, its dark waters feel like a gateway to another world. As one of the few regions shielded from Void Storms, it became the foundation for the Spacetrek Collective's Starward Riseway, a lift that scales the greatsword's spine to link this subterranean oasis with the Roya Frostlands.
Sundermere

A sacred homeland of the Roya and the habitat of the Soliskin. Bathed in the radiance of the Reactor Drive, its towering trees reach hungrily toward the light, their deep, interwoven roots returning that energy to the earth.
Bjartr Woods

A vast waterfall often visited by Jetrays. When they leap in unison, their silver wings form a shimmering curtain, hence the name. They travel in flocks for mutual protection, and Roya herders are often seen being carried by their wings, crossing the skies together in serene harmony.
Argentflare Drapes

A grand observational array established by Startorch Academy. Unlike the Cassettes, which record humanity, this system was built to record Lahai-Roi. It continuously tracks terrain shifts, ecological cycles, and celestial disturbances wrought by Void Storms and the Threnodian, like a giant eye observing the turning of the ages.
Spacetrek Observatory

Officially Spacetrek Collective: Startorch Academy, it stands as a borderless scientific community dedicated to the pure pursuit of knowledge. Its name reflects its ethos, "to carry the flame of inquiry and ignite the torch of civilization." Within this vast academic city, knowledge flows freely and cultures meet in harmony.
Startorch Academy

A terrifying creature born from the Threnodian's influence, found primarily in the hinterland of Lahai-Roi known as the "Mawburrow Desert." Its source of power and its fatal weakness are the Voidmatter Regulators on its head. Wherever it passes, life is extinguished, leaving only the void in its wake.
Voidworm

A lightweight, all-terrain vehicle co-developed by the Department of Exostrider Engineering and the Department of Voidmatters at Startorch Academy. Indispensable for field expeditions, the Academy has created specialized driving courses and multiple training tracks around the campus to cater to the adventurous spirit of its students and faculty.
Expedition Motorbike

A colossal lift linking Lahai-Roi to the Roya Frostlands, its structure resembling a spine piercing both heaven and earth. Powered by orbital-acceleration technology, it plummets and ascends through the deep cavern, serving as one of Lahai-Roi's most important transportation hubs.
Starward Riseway

A warm, humid haven beneath the Roya Frostlands. Following an ancient polar shift, this region became the new Solaris pole, prompting the Roya to migrate below ground. Here, the Spacetrek Collective established Startorch Academy. Today, this borderless academic city has become a cradle for countless rising scholars.
Lahai-Roi

The music persists, and the crimson curtain rises once more.
In this endless drama, you have no choice but to accompany her, one dance after the other.
Nightmare Revisited: Crimson Finale
An artificial Sonoro built by Phrolova in the Fabricatorium, a manifestation of her life's dreams and aspirations. It is so vast that it defies conventional measurement.
The Lost Beyond

A shifting realm between life and death, existence and nothingness. It is not a place in the physical sense, but a convergence of infinite possibilities that includes all of Iuno's emotions, memories, and connections. 
Here, her specter wanders, stuck reliving her past… until enough fragments of hers are captured and anchored. Only then can the girl erased by the world reclaim her future.
Chaos
