Keep an eye on her for now. If she tries anything, take her out.
Understood.
Zhezhi plays the recorded content.
This must be the warehouse they were talking about...
There's still some leftover ink lying around.
These paintings...
They're all from the list.
So all those copies from the studio...
These aren't just simple copies anymore... It's obvious now... she was working with them to create forgeries... for her own gain.
In the end, this is the path she chose... I-I suspected as much, though I couldn't quite... I mean, I wasn't sure until I saw the paintings myself.
I'll notify the Patrollers.
Wait. This painting... it's the "Serenity of Xiehua Village" original. Not a copy... Shouldn't it be at the studio?
Oh, I see it now. This was the painting they stole from the studio!
How can you tell them apart?
These copies, they're almost identical to the original... but there are some details, subtle ones, that reflect the artists' quirks, not just their technique. The painter copied them well.
How do you know so much about the original painting?
Well, that's because I...
This batch is all "Serenity of Xiehua Village"... Mingyan's work.
But if you look closely, you'll find that the finishings are a bit, um, more rigid in some areas.
—Look out!
Are you hurt?
Phew... No, no. I'm just catching my breath...
But where did these Tacet Discords come from...
The researcher mentioned a link between Mingyan and TDs.
Her emotions caused the painting's frequencies to fluctuate, attracting the monsters.
But she's not even here.
You said art always reflects the artist's mood.
It's just... I'm not sure why her mood is, um, reacting to us...
Maybe... could it be because I'm here?
She did see what I could do with my Resonance ability, once.
Ever since I saw her diary, I've been wondering... Maybe it was seeing my ability that inspired her to start creating those phantasms. Maybe that's why she began to lose herself in her art...
It seems like all those accumulated emotions just... just burst out whenever we get close to her or one of her paintings.
It's neither your fault nor the paintings'.
But...
More Exiles from the Art Exchange!
More on that later!
It's all my fault...
Did you really think we'd let you just walk away after you destroyed our warehouses and interfered with our business?!
Business... Why is everyone so obsessed with making money...?
Fellas, whaddya say we grab that compensation from our friends here for all the trouble they've caused us?
A creator's passion... Does it not mean anything to you...?
Uh... You don't look like you work at the mine. Can I help you with something?
Tell me about the recent event at the mine.
Oh yes, that strange event. It's the talk of the town right now.
I've conducted several investigations and found that those monsters tend to appear around midnight. Their locations seem random, though.
Fortunately, they haven't caused much harm. I think it's because they always show up and vanish in the dead of night.
If you ask me, these monsters are a new type of Tacet Discord. Since they're unrecorded, our Terminal can't trigger an alarm when they're nearby.
For safety reasons, we have increased our patrols around the mine.
Did you notice anything else unusual?
Could it be related to the Arcane Artist?
Anything else unusual? Hmm... Yes there was one thing.
Do you mean the mysterious painter who can bring fantastical creatures to life? That could explain it, but a Forte tied to painting is rare.
Aside from the blurred silhouettes I saw that night, I remember hearing voices—like people talking.
The voices came from where those silhouettes were, but they sounded like... vague muttering.
Thinking about it now, if it was a human voice, how could someone get so close to those monsters without crying out for help?
I see. Thank you for the information.
You... who exactly are you people? You don't look like you're Patrollers... What do you want?
If it's the paintings you're after, take as many as you want! We can always make new ones.
Oh, so you're also here for the money? Look, name a figure, we'll pay double if it'll make you shut up! How does that sound? Take it and scram!
Then what the hell do you want from me?!
...I-I want to expose everything to the public.
What?
Aside from reporting you to the Patrollers, I want to let the public know about all the forgery and smuggling you've been doing.
I-Is something wrong...?
I like the idea. You have my support.
I...I can't remain silent about this any longer. This is the only way more people can learn about the truth...
You'd better think this through! The Shanyun Art Exchange is not a group you wanna cross...
I never painted for the Art Exchange's approval. If no one else dares to speak up, then... then I'll be the one to do it!
I might have just the plan.
First, we keep these guys on close watch. Then, we need to catch them off guard, and the best way to do that is...
Forcing people to make copies like a factory line... it's disrespecting the creators' dignity.
Oh, it's just a couple of stones and trees on a piece of paper, for crying out loud. Even I can draw one with a flick of the wrist, who cares if they're real or not...
For the amount of paint and ink that goes into them, I'd even go so far as to say paying those painters 20 credits each is a rip-off.
How could you measure the value of creation in such a way...?
That's not what I meant.
The way you coerced the painters... a-and put their lives at risk for profit... I'll expose it all!
That's quite the story. At best, this merely proves our involvement in the incident at best, yet the real culprit remains unknown. Your accusations are groundless.
Allow me to remind you, she was the one who created those paintings, insisted on selling them, and concocted the entire terrifying incident.
Do you honestly believe her paintings would've earned a single penny without my intervention?
B-Before we proceed, I wish to present this audio recording to the court.
"Ugh, Mr. Baici stopped by again, grumbling about the delay in getting Mingyan's paintings to the Shanyun Art Exchange..."
"If Yinfeng hadn't pushed her, she wouldn't have gotten hurt. Now she can't even paint, and our order is gonna be late."
"She's been rebellious and a bit too smart for her own good lately. I just wanted her to keep her head down and work. Who knew she'd crack and cause that mess."
Mingyan was initially only making copies. Everything changed after you stepped in.
Trickery, misinformation, and later on even threats... She was led down the path of forging artworks for you.
I do understand that... if her own heart hadn't wavered, none of this would've happened... But there was already no turning back by the time she wanted to quit.
So, saying she was the mastermind behind it all... that's just not fair.
Even so, how is forgery a valid accusation? Nothing like that was mentioned in your recording, now was it?
We found the original painting in the hidden warehouse.
We found evidence of forgeries being bought and sold.
This evidence clearly shows that these paintings are no ordinary copies, but your way of making a profit.
Heh, there's no such thing as real or fake paintings. You're not fooling anyone.
...Mr. Baici, do you recognize this painting?
Well, of course. It's "Serenity of Xiehua Village," the work of the Arcane Artist.
Then can you tell the difference between this one and the others?
Of course, this piece possesses a lifelike quality unmatched by any other, all thanks to the Resonance ability of the Arcane Artist—Mingyan.
However, judging from these paintings, it seems Mingyan's ability never stabilized successfully, except for this original piece.
What does this have to do with anything? Do you have solid evidence to prove the differences between these paintings?
What you're saying is all speculation. There's no guarantee a painter won't make mistakes, is there?
Artists seeking perfection always choose the highest quality pigments for their most important pieces.
The original paintings had pigments that were purer and brighter, able to blend more naturally and retain color for longer.
In contrast, the forgeries used pigments made from mineral scraps. These don't hold up the same, smudging at the slightest touch.
We can distinguish the real paintings from the fakes simply by analyzing the ink used.
Doing so only proves the so-called "original painting" is created differently from the others. Are you implying that Mingyan is only allowed to use a single kind of pigment throughout her work?
How is this supposed to prove that we are behind the forgeries?!
Because the original creator of "Serenity in Xiehua Village" is me.
No... Mr. Baici, you're changing the subject.
How ungrateful. She ensnared us in this debacle, and now you dare to lay the blame at our feet?
For it to be forgery, there has to be another original artist. These paintings are all the work of Mingyan. Even if she made dozens of identical copies, it wouldn't be considered forgery.
During our investigation of the studio, I accidentally got paint on me and discovered something interesting about the materials used in these paintings.
When I was a child, painting was the only way I could express myself freely.
Everything I did and didn't understand... it all flowed through the tip of my paintbrush.
All that I saw, lived within my paintings.
This power to turn fantasies into reality gradually caught the interest of many.
I took great joy in my skills improving, however...
They were sold at unbelievable prices.
Some sought beauty in enchanted worlds...
Others resorted to hellish nightmares...
My own abilities had led my paintings astray.
After I realized this...
My parents scolded me for it.
After the family business fell apart, my parents vanished without a trace.
Xiehua Village was my first stop upon arriving in Jinzhou alone.
Waters and mountains rest by the pane, valleys and peaks in the dream remain.
A poem I wrote, inscribed on "Serenity in Xiehua Village."
And that painting, well... it became the "Arcane Artist's" final piece of art.
Ever since that day...
Whatever I thought, I painted into reality.
Tales of the Arcane Artist spread far and wide.
I discovered, to my dismay, that my parents were using my creations to turn a quick profit.
Using the paintings as a distraction from reality.
To inflict torment upon those they desire.
They were being exploited, and everything was spiraling out of control.
I began to fear holding a brush.
I tried to paint without relying on my abilities, but...
They called anything painted without using my abilities worthless.
They may have left behind a considerable mess...
But freedom has also been returned to my brush.
Colors of vanity washed away; the painted world fades, forgotten today.
I know it's not that well-written.
But it's proof of my decision to stop everything I was doing.
Paintings with special abilities gradually faded from everyone's minds.
And I never used my abilities to paint again.
Well, that was certainly a touching story. But I'm afraid your words alone won't be enough to prove you created this painting.
...Madam Juyao, to prove my statement, I request your permission to use and paint with one of these copies.
Granted.
Are you sure you want to do this?
Yes. Mingyan's experience has made me realize something.
The paintings I drew in the past... they were heartfelt creations, pieces of my life. They formed my past and shaped who I am today.
It's not just about proving a single painting... it's about so much more...
If my Forte is the cause behind all this, then I must take responsibility... I can't just let this go on and hurt others.
To create art that truly resonates, I must first accept myself.
So the rumors are true...
Th-these paintings are really coming to life?!
What's happening?!
Why is the world inside this painting so distorted?
"Spectacle is born from the mind."
Wait, did you hear something?
Why...
I've painted it exactly like hers...
It's all right. It's okay, she's gone now. Soon... I'll be an even better painter than she ever was!
Watch out!
Zhezhi?
That voice...
This place must be a manifestation of Mingyan's mind when she created it...
So why is everyone still praising her work...?
When I learned the truth, I was heartbroken...
I believed that by sealing my Forte, no one would get hurt because of my paintings. I never expected them to continue causing harm after all these years.
But {PlayerName}'s words made me realize something.
It was never about the paintings themselves, but rather those who sought to use them to hurt others.
Mr. Baici, you run a highly esteemed calligraphy and painting institution, yet you've suppressed the creative spirit and violated these artists' dignity, all for the sake of wealth.
Everything they cherished has now become a tool for profit... The works they held dear are just tools for your gain, insulting to both the original artists and their imitators.
Set before you is the original painting from many years ago and the one I've just completed. Now, everything has been brought to light.
We received word from the Public Security Bureau ten minutes ago that they have taken the Exiles into custody and found the location where the paintings were hidden.
Mr. Baici, do you have anything else to add to your defense?
Very well. We will re-evaluate Mingyan's charges, determine the Shanyun Art Exchange's involvement in the incident, and conduct a comprehensive investigation as soon as possible.
This hearing is adjourned.
I've gathered enough information. It's time to check the scene where those monsters were spotted.
It's finally over... I didn't miss anything important, did I?
You did great.
You hid your nerves well.
Huh? No, not at all... I was just coming up with things to say as I went. My palms were sweating the whole time...
I definitely couldn't have done it if you weren't there with me... Thinking about the feeling when we were investigating the case together is what kept me calm during the trial.
Wh-what I meant to say is, back then, everything I said felt right, like I could just be myself around you. It felt so good to be that relaxed...
Thank you for helping me through this. You... you helped me find the courage to believe in myself. Thanks to you, look at everything we accomplished.
The Shanyun Art Exchange is undergoing investigation. It'll be the end of their businesses... And the painters they coerced are finally set free.
Thank you, {PlayerName}. I haven't felt this happy in a long time!
Don't mention it.
I want to pay Mingyan a visit. After all, she was involved in all of this, and I want to tell her everything.
What do you think?
Can I come with you?
My commission started with her, plus you and I solved the case together. Why don't you come with me?
Is the commission over?
Yes, I already had it taken care of the day we found out the truth.
All right, let's go.
Zhezhi... It's been a while.
Your injuries...
The researchers have taken good care of me. A chat won't hurt. And you must be... the Rover?
You know me?
I heard about everything you did. Thank you for freeing me from those nightmares.
You know what, Zhezhi? You may seem soft and gentle on the outside, but if your boundaries are crossed, I think you can be tougher than anyone else.
And... I still owe you an apology.
Forgive me. Because I was so obsessed with wanting to be you... to be better than you, I've caused you so much trouble...
...The pain of these injuries managed to put a stop to my obsession with imitating your paintings.
Heh. Maybe... I was never meant to be a painter to begin with...
I brought you a gift...
Mingyan accepts a scroll of painting from Zhezhi, staring at it for a long time after opening it.
Hehe, see...? Only you can create a painting with such life. I still have a long way to go.
This is your painting.
It's the one you gave me when we first met.
I... Hehe... How ironic. I've been trying to imitate you for so many years that now I can't even tell my own paintings apart anymore.
Your paintings were never inferior to mine. Just look at this piece, even you approve of its value. It doesn't matter who painted it.
Mingyan, I hope you can find your true self, whoever she is. I know you can do it.
Mingyan opens the scroll painting once again and stares at every detail for a long time. She appears lost in thought. Zhezhi and you leave quietly after seeing this.
...Thank you for bringing me this painting... Really.
I think it's safe to say she'll give it some thought.
During the few times we met, she was always passionate about discussing art with me. I think that fire inside her won't just fade away.
Come to think of it, the deep discussions we had and the painting duels back then felt like true friendship.
I think she understood what you meant earlier.
To be honest, I didn't just see this case through to correct mistakes or help the artists. Deep down, I...I didn't want to let you down.
I wanted to tell you this back at the mine, but the words just didn't come out right...
It's fine, I understand what you're trying to say.
I'm glad you finally said it.
Thank you for being my friend and helping me through all of this, {PlayerName}.
I can say the same to you.
While I have yet to uncover my past and who I am, every moment with you is a new and special memory.
Thank you for your help, Zhezhi. This experience has helped me understand you and the world a little better.
You seem to be pretty slow on the news, {PlayerName}.
So you know how to tell jokes now?
Hehe... You've given me the courage to joke around.
Does that mean you can do the same in front of others?
Hmm... well...
Let's take it slow for now.
So... seeing her in so much pain, I just had to help.
I don't want Mingyan to lose hope and have someone who loves painting so much just disappear...
That's so scary...
It's just a prank, I bet.
You see my arm here? The monsters mauled me.
I heard laughter, voices with them. Will there be half-human Tacet Discords? Like... hybrids?
Stop. You're giving me the chills...
Stop being so paranoid. Remember last time, when that guy was collecting laundry on a skateboard and you thought it was a ghost? You need to calm down.
What, a new urban legend? Man, our mine is really cool...
What urban legend?
Our mine is full of urban legends and strange stories. Strange comm message from a mysterious train? A certain survey team's bizzare discoveries underground? And now, a new tale has surfaced!
What urban legend?
About the Arcane Artist, of course! A legendary tale with paintings, monsters, and humans? I can already smell the suspense and surprises.
What is it about, exactly?
What a fascinating place! So much character and charm. I must write down this story right away.
Wait. What on earth happened?
No. The paintings came first, then the monsters and humans followed.
No. The humans came first, then the monsters and paintings followed.
No. The monsters ARE the humans.
There's... something ahead...
That figure... that paintbrush... Could it be...
I've been seeing her around here often.
She said she's here for inspiration.
But I bet she's hiding from something.
Wasn't someone standing there with the painter before it happened?
Wasn't someone standing there with the painter before it happened?
Really? Should we go tell the Patrollers about it?
Maybe, but I don't even remember what that person looked like...
Was that her partner in crime, maybe?
They were arguing over something... The painter looked ready to snap...
That sounds concerning. We should tell the Patrollers.
Yeah, let's go.
These legs still ache from hauling that last shipment.
Then come exercise with me!
...Nevermind, I'll just go back and rest. That'll only make me more tired.
I should be able to sneak a painting out, right? Bet they won't notice.
Hey, I'm thinking... Have we been demoted? Is that why they've sent us here?
You don't get it. This is how we really learn the business. They're setting us up for a promotion in the future!
Oh, I see! Then I better work harder!
Nothing here. That's odd... Did I just imagine that?
Unfortunately, I'm... not very good at investigating, so I haven't found any major clues yet.
Zhezhi...?
R-rover? You're here...
I'm fine. Why are you here?
...F-finding inspiration.
The night... often sparks my creativity...
...Don't tell me you are actually the Arcane Artist.
Of course not!
I... I heard about the tale of the Arcane Artist and hoped to find out who they are...
You too? Why are you investigating this?
Are you also a ghost story enthusiast?
Bringing painted creatures to life, making fantasies real—it sounds like a fairy tale, but when the Arcane Artist first caught people's attention in Jinzhou years ago, it was more than just a tale.
Yes, there was once an artist who could create paintings that felt so real, you could almost step into them...
I'll go with you. It's linked to the case I'm investigating.
Sorry, did I scare you just now?
Sorry I lied to you, I just... didn't want to drag anyone else into this...
N-no, I'm not into ghost stories.
Now this story is making the rounds again. Most don't see the dangers it holds. As someone who feels the threat, I... I want to uncover the truth before it's too late.
The Arcane Artist showed up before?
But these paintings, they strayed from the artist's original intentions and... caused a lot of trouble.

I don't know who's behind these latest events, but if it's really the Arcane Artist... their paintings will bring nothing but trouble. T-that's why I... I have to stop them, to prevent the past from repeating itself...
I'm here for the Arcane Artist, but also hoping to meet an old acquaintance. Maybe he knows what happened in the mine...
Is that so? O-ok.
Don't go easy on them!
Ow... That must've hurt...
Pretty sure I would've won.
It's my turn next!
You gotta strike faster! Like this! Hah!
Waaahhh, please go easy on me!
You done with the paint we're using?
Of course not! Just ran outta material again. I'll go see if we still have some left in the camp.
Be quick. We can't afford to miss the deadline.
Why do I have to go down to the warehouse and count those paintings again...
No one ever goes there. Is this really necessary at all?
I never want to take on such boring tasks again....
Hmm, what's for dinner today... Hey! My pot! Who the hell messed it up?
Our current plan is weak. Too slow, not secret enough. We need to step up.
Let's lock up all the artists somewhere, and assign them each a piece to complete.
We'll control their breaks and work them around the clock. It's gonna double our output for sure.
Interesting...
You know, I reached out to one of our customers the other day...
Shh! You can't just bring that up out loud!
You meet Zhezhi at the entrance of the Public Security Bureau. Relieved to see you, she gathers her courage and decides to speak the truth about the art forgery case during the hearing.

As the hearing unfolds, Baici, the founder of the Shanyun Art Exchange, casts doubt on Zhezhi's statement with his slippery arguments. Nervous and shaken, Zhezhi finds it impossible to refute him. You decide to step in and explain the events of three days ago. Your support gives Zhezhi the confidence to continue, and she uses her paintbrush to paint an image of the scene.
Three days earlier, Gupan had entrusted you with investigating the "Arcane Artist" in the Tiger's Maw. You then decide to track down witnesses and begin gathering information.

Huaijin reveals that the monsters lurking around the mine have been acting strangely, and hints that they might be linked to some painting scrolls. Huaijin also warns you that there is likely more than one person involved in the case.
Jifeng elaborates on more key details of the attacks, leading you to suspect that they are not random events, but something far more deliberate.

While investigating sightings of the monsters and the Arcane Artist, you run into Zhezhi. She explains she is also investigating the chaos caused by the Arcane Artist. Realizing you are after the same thing, you suggest asking a local mineral merchant for more information.

With the merchant Shilang's encouragement, Zhezhi drums up the courage to ask to be your friend and is relieved by your response. To shift the conversation away from Shilang's friendly teasing, she mentions the Arcane Artist. You learn that some suspicious individuals had purchased heaps of leftover ore and even stole from Shilang at night. To confirm the details, you check Shilang's transaction records.

Your discussion is interrupted by Chixia's arrival. Zhezhi, feeling shy and a little awkward, is unsure how to decline Chixia's invitation to return to the city. Just when she is about to give in to Chixia's friendly insistence, you politely excuse both of you from the gathering. Chixia mentions she is also investigating the Tacet Discords that have been acting strangely. Just then, a loud noise nearby interrupts your conversation and you all decide to check it out.
Regretting her earlier hesitation, Zhezhi promises to speak up more decisively as you make your way to the scene.

You learn from Chixia and a researcher that the Tacet Discords had gone wild due to a frequency fluctuation from a painting scroll found at the site. The scroll's power came from the artist's nearly Overclocked Forte.

While investigating Mingyan, the artist in question, you discover she had once studied art alongside Zhezhi. Although Mingyan's fragmented speech suggests that she may be guilty, her expression hints at a more complicated story. However, she is unwilling to reveal more.

From the witness Su, you learn that Mingyan appeared lost, waving her paintbrush moments before a swarm of Tacet Discords emerged from nowhere. It also seemed like she had tried to stop the monsters from harming anyone.
Yinfeng, another witness, claimed that Mingyan created the dangerous painting purely for personal gain.

After piecing together the clues, you uncover the truth. Mingyan used her Forte to create temporary phantasms in her art that attracted Tacet Discords. The "monsters" reported by witnesses were merely distorted phantasms seen by frightened people in the dark. Zhezhi insists that Mingyan was not motivated by personal gain, and asks that you continue to search for evidence to clear her name in her art studio.

In Mingyan's studio, you discovered pieces of "White Jade Paper." Zhezhi introduces its unique qualities with an artist's keen eye. Drawing from her understanding of the paper and Mingyan's habits, Zhezhi begins to build a theory about what happened prior to Mingyan's incident.

Among Mingyan's drafts, Zhezhi recognizes copies of the "Serenity of Xiehua Village," each painted in subtly different ways. As you examine the details, Zhezhi notices pigment stains on her clothes and quickly realizes that the quality of the paint is lower than usual.
A find a stained piece of clothing, prompting Zhezhi to recall how she used to use her clothing as makeshift canvases. She suggests that Mingyan might have done something similar.

You find Mingyan's notes that reveal her struggles as an artist and the pressure she felt while painting against her true desires. Zhezhi reflects on how common this feeling is among creators. Having once faced the same confusion, Zhezhi expresses her determination to uncover the truth and help save Mingyan.

You stumble upon medicinal herb residue. Zhezhi, inexperienced with such materials, initially thinks it is just leftover pigment. Finding this makes you realize that Mingyan had not been feeling well before the incident.

Zhezhi speculates that a Gulpuff might have escaped from the studio. While the theory seems questionable, you appreciate her effort, spurring Zhezhi to try again. Impressed by her Forte use, you learn that Zhezhi rarely uses her Resonance abilities. Zhezhi confesses that her Forte, which closely resembles Mingyan's, may somehow be connected to Mingyan's uncharacteristic outburst.

At an Exile camp, you find piles of ore fragments and handmade pigments. The amount perfectly matches what you saw in Shilang's transaction records. This confirms that these Exiles were the ore thieves and that Mingyan had purchased their low-quality pigments.
The Exiles admit to knowing Mingyan and admiring her exceptional art. They claim they tried to stop her from creating dangerous paintings, but their efforts had been in vain.

Zhezhi senses that neither the Exiles nor Mingyan are being truthful. She notices that some Exiles have blackened hands, a sign they are secretly producing pigments and inks for some unknown purpose. Suspicious of their deception, you decide to sneak into the camp at night to uncover the truth.

During your infiltration, you overhear a conversation revealing that these supposed Exiles are actually employees of the Shanyun Art Exchange. This confirms that the Art Exchange is involved in Mingyan's plight and hints at their involvement in churning out art forgeries.

From their conversation, you discover that Yinfeng, the witness from the crime scene, had signed Shilang's transaction record. Yinfeng had framed Mingyan to cover up their illegal activities. To verify Zhezhi's suspicions about a certain "batch of paintings" mentioned in the Exiles' conversation, you decide to disguise yourselves and investigate further.

During your infiltration, you overhear a conversation revealing that these supposed Exiles are actually employees of the Shanyun Art Exchange. This confirms that the Art Exchange is involved in Mingyan's plight and hints at their involvement in churning out art forgeries. You also learn that Yinfeng, the witness from the crime scene, had signed Shilang's transaction record. Yinfeng had framed Mingyan to cover up their illegal activities. To verify Zhezhi's suspicions about a certain "batch of paintings" mentioned in the Exiles' conversation, you decide to disguise yourselves and investigate further.

You find a recording of Mingyan asking to leave the Art Exchange's schemes, only to be threatened by Yinfeng. It appears that Yinfeng has also been reporting all of Mingyan's actions to Mr. Baici, his boss.

Inside the camp's warehouse, you find countless copies of famous artworks, proving that Mingyan had been coerced into creating forgeries for the Art Exchange. You immediately share this information with the Patrollers. Meanwhile, Zhezhi discovers the original "Serenity of Xiehua Village," the stolen masterpiece. She begins to explain how she recognized it amidst all the forgeries, but is interrupted by a horde of Tacet Discords.

After defeating the monsters, you realize that the painting's frequency had attracted them. Zhezhi laments that her presence must trigger the emotional frequencies in Mingyan's paintings and that her Forte may have played a role in inciting Mingyan's obsession. You reassure Zhezhi that the blame lies neither with her nor the painting.

Yinfeng dismisses the value of an artist's passion and tries to silence you with money. Outraged but resolute, Zhezhi stands her ground, determined to expose the dark side of the Shanyun Art Exchange and save all the artists who are been coerced into producing forgeries.

In the hearing, you present the evidence—the recording, art forgeries, and the low-quality pigments—to prove how the Art Exchange coerced painters into producing counterfeit works. However, Baici defends himself with different excuses. At that moment, Zhezhi gathers her courage and reveals a hidden truth: she is the original creator of "Serenity of Xiehua Village."
Zhezhi faces her past and takes control of her Forte, preparing to use it to back up her claim and embrace the responsibility that comes with her talent.

The painting Zhezhi creates during the hearing, combined with the message you sent to the Patrollers, leaves Baici no choice but to confess. The Public Security Bureau announces they will re-evaluate Mingyan's charges and launch a full investigation. Victory is yours.
After the hearing, Zhezhi thanks you for your unwavering support and expresses her relief at the outcome. Together, you plan to visit Mingyan.

When Mingyan learns about your efforts, she expresses her deep gratitude and apologizes to Zhezhi. She admits that the incident makes her question whether she is truly meant to be an artist.
