She seems to be able to control gravity.
She referred to herself as a "we."
A Bloom Bearer whose Forte is controlling gravity… I've checked all records of both Resonators and Bloom Bearers, but I didn't find anyone matching your description.
Oh, almost forgot.
Here, take this!
KU-Money is right. Just in case, the Tethys System is very likely to send out a warning to Jinzhou about an imminent Lament in the Port City of Guixu.
KU-Money takes out a large sum of money…
Uh, sorry?
Each Black Shores member is allocated a specific fund, and this is yours. Find me when you burn through it all.
That's not fair. You've never given me that much before!
I deducted the money you lost to me in games. It was all you had left!
Oh, by the way! Are you heading to the Greenhouse?
If a Bloom Bearer dies outside the Black Shores, we bring their body back and keep Monica in the loop.
As for the Tethys System, imagine it as a supercomputer. The Black Shores relies on its calculations to observe, forewarn, and solve anything Lament-related.
What's going on, Aalto? I never see you this serious.
The Tethys System has been shaky lately. You've noticed, right.
What's worse, along with the data, we received some terrible news. The Bloom Bearers we sent to the Port City of Guixu… We lost them all.
H-how did that happen!?
What happened in that city…
She might have something to do with the deaths of our people.
Oh, we need to send out a warning as usual. There's still a lot to do...

You hand over the data to the specialized robot at the Black Shores, which swiftly uploads it into the Tethys System. The merchant known as KU-Money, perhaps mistaking you as one of their own, rewards you with a substantial sum of money. However, despite its extensive knowledge of the Black Shores, the robot knows nothing of Hoda's true identity.
…{PlayerName}! Finally got through…
Hey, you scared us to death!!!
Sorry, the Tacetite's interference was too strong.
I'm in the Black Shores now.
Glad to know you're all right.
Chixia, is that you?
Yeah! Just so you know, we got the Black Shores' warning, so we cranked up the defenses in Jinzhou.
As for the Bloom Bearers who have passed, we'll bring their bodies back to the Black Shores.
I know the Black Shores hold many answers for you—your memories, your past…
Though the road ahead is uncertain, I hope you find the truth you seek.
And please remember, you never have to bear the weight alone... I... We are here with you. Always.
The Midnight Rangers are preparing to secure the Port City of Guixu, and…
Hey, what's on your mind?
Can robots grow a desire for money, too?
You ever play those RPGs? Each character's got a backstory, right? Well, these robots are no different.
The Tethys System gives them all their own personalities. Take KU-Money, for instance. Tethys programmed it to be a crafty dealmaker.
Who knows, maybe one day you'll come across a robot you really click with.
Once you're ready, we'll head over to the Greenhouse and meet Monica.
Well, well! Look who I bumped into—a Midnight Ranger!
Ah! Rover, you're finally here...
So you're the Rover, huh? Delighted to make your acquaintance.
To uncover clues about hidden antiques, of course! Since Mt. Firmament reopened, Master and I noticed artifacts from there popping up in the market.
Aside from Court of Savantae gadgets, there are still plenty of mystery items that don't exactly scream Mt. Firmament, ya know?
So…
So I'm betting they're from the Port City of Guixu!
Yes, I remember you mentioned wanting to learn more about your past ties to the Black Shores.
I'm touched you remember what I said.
Ah!?
You, er, brought it up before.
I still have this Blake Bloom that Aalto gave me.
This should lead me to them, right?
Since we're on the same trail, how about teaming up?
Let THIS master be your guide! You and me, dream team. Nothing is going to slow us down.
Not to boast, but epic adventures tend to have a way of finding me.
This is Youhu from Jinzhou. Like Mr. Chenpi, she's an expert in antiques.
That's me!
What brings an antiques expert here?
Aw, Yangyang's got a soft spot for you, huh? Are you her SPECIAL someone?
Oh, come on. I-I just know it means a lot to you.
So...
I received a message from Yangyang.
The battle in Norfall Barrens is over, and the Black Shores should be withdrawing... but they've asked the Midnight Rangers to monitor the area around the Port City of Guixu.
I thought this might be your chance to gather more information about them...
That's a little dramatic, to say the least.
Since Rover's here, let's talk to that Bloom Bearer first.
Relax, I'm just teasing. So {PlayerName}, you're tracking the Black Shores too?

Yangyang has sent word that a Bloom Bearer from the Black Shores is currently in the Port City of Guixu and may have important information about your identity. Upon your arrival in the city, you happen to run into Chenpi's apprentice, Youhu…
Grrr…
I thought an intel broker like you always stays cool-headed.
I'm frustrated with myself. Got too carried away by your presence to think straight.
I thought we could easily resolve that issue by uploading the data you brought back to the system. Never considered the possibility of an infiltrator lurking inside.
We need to figure out who's behind all this.
Does the Tethys System mean that much to the Black Shores?
Yeah, the Black Shores' every move hinges on its decisions, big or small. Without Tethys, it'd just be a barren Tacetite.
And if you're after the truth, you'll need its assistance too.
Actually, KU-Money, Monica, and I don't have top clearance to the Tethys System. Our access is limited.
With higher clearance, you could uncover the answers you're looking for…
Alright, let's pick up the pace. We need to find the KU-Water siblings and check on the Modulation Device.
This is your chance to ask anything you want.
Really?
If anyone has answers, it's Tethys.
I can't guarantee you'll get everything you're after, but it's worth a shot, right?
The Greenhouse's just ahead. Let's move.
What should I do now?
Lalala, happy watering…
Grow and bloom, my sweet little flowers…
Ahh! Don't sneak up on me like that!
Are you watering the flowers?
Of course! As a capable Gardener, I always give ultimate care to all these flowers.
Planting, watering, pruning, airing, and giving them sunshine!
Oh, hold on! Please plant a flower.
What?
Plant-A-Flower!
In the Black Shores, each member plants a flower here. Most choose flower seeds from their hometown.
What flower did Aalto plant?
What flower did Encore plant?
What flower did Camellya plant?
Hmm... Aalto didn't plant a flower but a tree. A money tree, I remember…
I forget, but Encore didn't bring a seed from her hometown.
Camellya? She planted so many! Countless. She created an entire garden of flowers…
So, what kind of flower seed would you like to plant from your hometown?
My hometown? I don't remember where I'm from.
Um… So you're a wandering traveler, right? Then a Blake Bloom would probably suit you well.
A Blake Bloom?
Of course! Even if you don't remember your hometown, the Black Shores can be your new home. The Blake Blooms we give each member symbolize that!
I belong here...?
Yeah, you could say that… Um?!
Wait! KU-Water, are you feeling that? You... you're getting the same feeling, right?
Hmm, yeah… You look familiar, but I can't remember where we met...
Request… Request… No response.
But the Tethys System reacted to your face...
Ohhh!!!
What?!
Strange. I found a record of you in the system, but it suddenly disappeared...
What happened? Why did Tethys suddenly tell us to leave... Alright, let's go, KU-Water. KU-Money is waiting for us.
O-okay. See you next time!
Under the instruction of the Tethys System, the two robots leave.
...So, where's the Modulation Device?
Upstairs! See that piano? That's the Modulation Device.
It seems like the Tethys System is hiding something from you…
However, KU-Water and KU-Plant have already departed. Your best course of action now is to inspect the Modulation Device.

In the Greenhouse, you encounter two robots that recognize you as the lone Rover of Solaris. They speak of Blake Blooms as if you share a connection with them, but it appears that the Tethys System is somehow restraining them from revealing the truth of your identity…
It looks like just an ordinary tree.
But it seems Aalto took the liberty of naming it the "Money Tree."
Of course that's something he would do...
Encore didn't bring any seeds back from her hometown.
This might be similar to her own story...
Could the flowers in the tale truly be real?
Camellya seems deeply connected to flowers.
"The seed of fate..."
Maybe she's more like a flower than you realize.
This piano is playing by itself.
Hmm? Do you know how to play the piano?
No. It's doing that all by itself.
I guess the Black Shores have earned their mysterious reputation. They even have a self-playing piano.
(Try to touch a key)
So you do know how to play!
(Keep touching the keys)
I don't have a musical bone in me, but that sounded good.
It sounds familiar.
(Keep touching the keys)
In every sound and frequency lies an emotion.
Hey! Wake up! What was that?
Did I just see...?
Ah! Another earthquake!
What's happening? Run! We need to get out of here!
Just like this, expressing what's on your mind through music…
It's something even you can do. You'll give it a try, won't you?
Ugh, what? It's just been the two of us here this whole time!
The piano seems to respond to your touch.

A strange piano, known as the Modulation Device, plays its notes unbidden, offering fleeting glimpses of the past through sound and frequency. As you and Abby dive deeper into these reveries, a violent tremor shatters the moment…
Hey {PlayerName}, can you hear me?
There was a spike in the anchor frequency of the Tethys algorithmic array. It caused other abnormal frequencies to escape.
Analysts are still investigating. We're already en route for repairs.
Right now, the data stored in Tethys is materializing by drawing energy from the massive Tacetite beneath the Black Shores. It's making digital constructs out of real life entities.
KU-Money already logged your info in Tethys. Now you can command the robots across the Black Shores to fix and upload the corrupted data. That'll restore the anchors.
We're heading to Veiled Rock's anchor. Rover, can you help at the Haven of Sprouts? It's our comms hub.
I'll be helping with the repair at Veiled Rock. Such a pity I won't be there to witness Jinzhou's savior in action once more.
No... I'll miss seeing my friend in action again.
Maybe that's why you saw the other you in that vision?
I… I'm so sleepy…
Unbelievable...
So, those little robots are also linked as Terminals within the Tethys System.
We can use them to restore the corrupted data.
But be careful, they seem to have minds of their own...
Whoa! Ah... Excuse me...
I-I'm actually new here, and I haven't quite figured out what's going on yet...
Those robots started running around all of a sudden, like something big happened, and the whole place suddenly felt tense.
Is... is there anything I can help you with?
Beep beep! This is an emergency!
Entry into the corruption area without proper protection or a Terminal robot escort is not recommended!
I'd recognize these scattered frequencies anywhere.
They reek of the Lament... Or rather, a "dead" Lament that's now just history...
You're familiar with the Lament?
My home was destroyed by it.
I'm sorry, I didn't mean to intrude...
No need to apologize. It's all in the past now, and all I can do is search for the truth.
I can hear the voices of Reverberations I once retrieved in these scattered frequencies.
I will not let history repeat itself...
Beep beep! Roadblock ahead!
Detecting corrupted data...
Unauthorized access prohibited. Proceed at your own risk!
Evacuate! Evacuate!
Any authorization on you? Thought so.
Don't get too close, or it could do a number on you.
We need to be connected to the Tethys System to stay unaffected.
Th-this place is dangerous!
But all the researchers at the Haven of Sprouts have been safely evacuated.
We'll stay here until things are resolved.
Thanks to you, the spread of the corruption is under control for now.
You can leave the cleanup to us.
I never thought the Tethys System malfunctioning could be so serious.
Seeing constructs appear from thin air like that... I may as well be looking at Retroact Rain.
I've seen the Retroact Rain in Jinzhou.
But the frequencies it's manipulating are nothing like we've seen before. Bringing history and the dead to life again? I mean...
What exactly are we facing?
The TD Observatory is where we observe Tacet Discords across the world to predict the Lament.
It handles data collection, storage, and transmission of anything related to these creatures.
That's why this place is the trickiest… We had a severe leak in data.
You'd better find the robot first. It's familiar with this place. The observatory keeper should know where to find it.
Watch out! More Tacet Discords incoming!
Thank you. I'm the keeper of the TD Observatory.
That was an impressive battle, I've heard about your skills from my colleagues in Jinzhou.
You're from Huanglong?
Yes, but regardless of our origins, we're united by a common ideal here.
All right! All the repairs are finally done.
Thank you for your help, {PlayerName}.
Without you leading the charge, we would have barely made it—
You are… Hoda.
Oh, I forgot to tell you. We finally found out her true identity.
She wasn't lying when she said she was a Bloom Bearer. She worked as a field medic.
Then how is any of this possible?
Hoda is but one of us. In the Tethys System, our registered name is… Necrostar.
We are forever trapped on the event horizon of the black hole, falling into an unending darkness…
Beneath the Lament's wheels we are but dust, pitiful souls cursed to suffer dreadful eternity, denied the solace of death.
Welcome home, {PlayerName}.
But more importantly, she died in the Lament that destroyed the Port City of Guixu a few hundred years ago.
In short, she couldn't be alive.
My mentor… the one I follow…
Please… I beg you to end this Möbius loop, this endless cycle...

With all restorations complete, you scarcely have a moment to rest before the enigmatic Bloom Bearer Hoda reappears, addressing you as the mentor she has been following. Shortly after, the Shorekeeper herself emerges, welcoming your return…
You stand on these shores once more. Welcome home, {PlayerName}.
You saved me back in the Port City of Guixu?
I wished to keep you from any harm.
Forgive me for acting on my own accord.
Was that you on the beach before?
Why do you look sad?
Sad? Pardon me, such emotions are not mine to show…
Long ago, when you first brought the Black Shores into existence on this island, I assisted you in managing this place.
You once wove the threads of this world together, but then you left, roving the boundaries between this realm and the next.
I don't remember any of this…
You have lost far more than just your memories.
But the Black Shores...
Since your departure, the Tethys System has been the sole leader of the Black Shores.
You have more important matters to attend to than dealing with everyday trifles. That is why you entrusted the Tethys System with the Black Shores' governance.
This time, only you have the ability to end all of this. Completely.
This is also your first step towards the future.
This place, built by your hands, holds all its resources at your disposal.
Most have never seen you, and that is all by your design.
Yes, it was I.
Hoda said something similar.
You mean…
You tell the Shorekeeper what happened in the Port City of Guixu.
She was indeed a Bloom Bearer, but mysteries still surround her and the departed.
The departed, whom you saw in the Port City of Guixu, caused those abnormal frequencies. Only you can mend those errors.
Rest assured, I shall always be by your side, to assist you as before.
What happened back then…?
I am sorry, but I must keep this secret from you.
Perhaps, as you restore the Tethys System, you will uncover the reasons for severing ties with your past…
Wandering traveler, please tell me.
Are you satisfied with your journey and stories in Jinzhou?
The people in Jinzhou are nice.
I'd say it's been a good start to the adventure.
Is that so? I'm glad to hear that.
In Solaris, Jinzhou is but the beginning of your journey.
Please, have faith. The path ahead shall be as splendid as you desire.
What should I do now?
The gate to the underground has been opened. Pass through it, and you will reach the depths of the Black Shores.
Your journey has only just begun.
Beyond the Black Shores lies Solaris itself.
Before you go, can I ask a favor?
When all is settled, will you share your stories from Jinzhou with me?

The Shorekeeper explains that during your absence, she and the Tethys System had taken over the running of the Black Shores. She confirms that it was indeed she who saved you, Yangyang, and Youhu in the Port City of Guixu. To address the threats posed by Hoda and the looming crisis in both the Black Shores and the Port City of Guixu, the Shorekeeper requests that you venture underground, to where the starry sky awaits...
She's the Shorekeeper.
She even showed up in person. That means…
You haven't met her before?
I haven't seen the Shorekeeper in all my time in the Black Shores. I've only heard the stories about her.
If the Shorekeeper is revealing herself to you, it can only mean one thing. I think you know what I mean.
The gateway to the underground has been opened. I'm sure the answers lie ahead.
Go ahead. Leave the rest to us, buddy.
The TD Observatory collects data from around the world.
Does the Black Shores collect Tacet Discord data too?
Tacet Discords are part of the Lament. We have no choice but to keep an eye on every sighting.
The anchor here processes the data brought back by our Consultants.
If the Tethys System experiences an overflow, the data stored here could get corrupted.
The Tethys System analyzes everything in existence.
It's Solaris's most powerful tool. So, isn't it inevitable?
It could even create "creation" itself.
Creating "creation"?
Not just objects, but maybe the idea of "creation" could be overturned!
Imagine—if this is true, the Tethys System could create entirely new Tacet Discords!
Errors. So many errors...
Need more nuts and bolts.
What do you need them for?
To repair anchors and robots.
To help everyone, we need nuts and bolts.
Valentina is in communication with the emergency response members deployed to other regions.
We can still hold our own. Focus on your own task.
HQ has ordered that you and the robot Terminals must defend the Error Cell for the next three hours.
You keep the equipment secure and hold your ground, no matter the cost. You got that?
The items stored behind you are critical. There can be no mistakes.
Proceed with the orders...
That's weird. These parameters are correct, but nothing's happening. What's going on…?
Are you a Bloom Bearer from the Black Shores?
Yes. Need something?
Oh!? So… y-you're the one Aalto invited earlier?
The one and only.
Ohhh! Sorry I didn't recognize you!
Golden pupils and this Blake Bloom. Yeah, it's you alright!
I'm Niya, a Bloom Bearer from the Black Shores. Didn't expect to meet someone as important as you under these circumstances...
I know it's unusual, but… could you help me out now that we're working together?
Hold on, I haven't decided if I want to join the Black Shores.
Yes, that's why the Tethys System sent us to locate and recover this frequency as soon as possible, to prevent a potential disaster.
Our agents relayed the coordinates, but...
Since then, I've lost contact with them, which doesn't sit well... I'm stuck here monitoring, can't leave my post.
Do you think you could help check out what happened?
If things aren't looking good, we might need to inform Jinzhou's City Hall, like we did before.
We will need to act fast, then.
By the way, what do you mean by "abnormal frequency"?
Could be the Reverberations or something in the Sonoro Spheres.
In Solaris, frequencies can be anything. One thing's for sure though, this frequency represents gravity.
It's abnormal because... it has its own gravitational center. You should be able to feel a palpable anomaly near it. That's how you can locate it.
I trust you'll handle it smoothly. But remember, your safety matters most. Don't hesitate to retreat if you run into any real danger.
And once you're back, we'll hurry to the Black Shores to upload it to the Tethys System… Oh! I forgot you haven't been to the Black Shores, have you?
Not yet, at least.
No worries. I'll be your guide then.
Really? But Encore mentioned you'd be joining soon...
Can you explain what's going on first?
Actually, we're monitoring abnormal parameters and detected a problematic frequency that needs to be taken back to the Black Shores.
The Port City of Guixu was decimated by the Lament. If this frequency goes unchecked, it could trigger another catastrophe...
Are the stakes really that high?
That's the worst-case scenario. If we contain the frequency as the Tethys System advises, nothing bad will happen.
{PlayerName}, I want to help her.
As an Outrider, it's my duty to safeguard the peace.
Guess I'll take charge. No surprise there.
You're right. We can't just sit this out.
Thank you! It's reassuring to have a Midnight Ranger with us. I'll send you the coordinates of the abnormal frequency.

In the Port City of Guixu, you meet Niya, a Bloom Bearer who quickly recognizes you. She warns of an abnormal frequency detected in Guixu that must be urgently brought back to the Black Shores. If left unresolved, it might trigger another Lament…
The new Final Fancy Defense comes out tomorrow.
Ugh, still have to wait a week to get my shell credits…
Mommy, when's the next subway?
Oh, sweetheart, it's just ten minutes away. It won't be long.
Grandpa and Grandma are making your favorite dishes.
They're too short-sighted to spare a glance at the stars above.
Those who don't revere the stars will eventually fade into history.
Oh my… Where's my pocket watch?
…Oh, I sent it for repairs yesterday.
How come I forgot something from just yesterday?
This place is home to many plants, some familiar to Jinzhou and some new.
It feels almost like a botanical preserve.
Is it the cradle of a new world or the relic of an old one?
This plant is obviously well looked after.
The Black Shores were constructed on a huge Tacetite rock, and most plants can only thrive in specific conditions.
Are these plants also cared for by the robots?
The sign says, "Camellya 72973, recorded in the Bank of Life's Plant Archive."
Is that truly a flower planted by Camellya?
Based on the numbers, she's collected numerous flower species.
Despite having thousands, she appears to be searching for one irreplaceable flower.
This door appears to be locked for some reason.
We probably need to locate a key to get it open from this side.
Th-thank goodness, you're finally awake! I-I thought you fell so hard th-that you wouldn't be able to make it…
Where am I?
Who are you?
Y-you're at the Bank of Life. As you can see, i-it's an underground seed bank.
M-me? I-I am KU-Nana, an underground Gardener. I-I take care of the flowers here.
So I'm already in the underground area, huh?
Y-yes…
Usually, no one comes to the Bank of Life except the Shorekeeper…
Where is the Shorekeeper?
Hmm, as far as I can remember, she seems to have never left this place.
She used to come to the Bank of Life once in a while, choosing a flower to plant in her own "garden." But she hasn't come for a very, very long time.
To be exact, it's been twenty years, five months, and seventeen days since her last visit.
I need to fix Tethys' errors.
Then you need to go to the Data Hub where the Stellar Matrices... I mean collections of stars are stored. Unfortunately, it's been out of commission for a while now.
The Shorekeeper has probably been too busy trying to fix it to visit.
If the Shorekeeper places her trust in you, then y-you shall have our trust too.
Thank you for trusting me.
KU-Money shared your information with us through the Tethys System.
I only know how to take care of plants, and I can't do much in this situation… but I still want to help if the Black Shores, my home, is in crisis!
I'll give it to the Shorekeeper.
Thank you so much!
Go straight ahead, and you'll leave the Bank of Life!
A Consultant? Why haven't you evacuated yet?
When the Tethys System issued the order to evacuate, everyone else left for the Modulation Hall.
So why are you still here?
To protect the seeds in the Bank of Life, seeds collected from all over the world.
It's imperative that the plants on Solaris be categorized systematically, you see.
Besides, as long as the Tethys System stands, so will we.
Hmm, hmm... The Great Chain of Being...
Sorry, I was miles away. Welcome, Knowledge Seeker!
You look just like KU-Money.
You've met KU-Money, then. He is the robot administering the Black Shores Archipelago.
Similarly, each area of the Black Shores' underground has been assigned an administrator.
I'm KU-Irwin, administrator of the Bank of Life's Center for Species Conservation. A pleasure to make your acquaintance.
Things are hectic at the moment. The fate of the Black Shores' underground is in your hands and the Shorekeeper's now.
We'll talk again in time.
The numbers are a complete mess! They should've been arranged using a phylogenetic tree.
You want to help? Keep yourself safe, that's your first priority.
Oh, by the way, you're from Jinzhou, right?
I hear there is a Jinzhou scholar by the name of Verina who is well versed in botany.
I hope I'll get the chance to meet her soon…
If the Shorekeeper places her trust in you, then y-you shall have our trust too.
Go straight ahead, and you'll leave the Bank of Life!
This is what the Black Shores really looks like.
You're just a projection, right?
To be exact, my body is composed of Sonoro Spheres, and the projection you see is but a shadow of the Sonoro.
I cannot leave my post. As the core computational unit of the Tethys System, I must remain to ensure its proper functioning.
Yet, I still wish to be with you. This is the only way.
That is the Necrostar, once known in ancient astronomy as a "black hole."
Please bring it back to the Modulation Hall, and I shall correct it.
Then, the Tethys System will be restored, and harm will be no more.
My only hope now... is that we are not too late.
The Tethys System transforms data into stars, observing the entire Solaris, and discarded data are cast into the Necrostar.
Seeing a sky like this down here is a real surprise.
This place holds records of every Lament across Solaris—those that have passed, those happening now, and those yet to come.
Here, a planet's Lament transforms into stars that fill the sky.
Hoda called me the "Astral Modulator."
Does that name have something to do with this place?
Astral Modulator, Guide of Civilizations, Mastermind of the Black Shores…
Before you severed ties with your past, it was indeed one of your names.
Perhaps you have a preference?
What did you call me?
Me…?
I would call you by your true name, {PlayerName}.
The abnormal frequency you encountered in the Port City of Guixu is part of it—or rather, it is the Necrostar itself.
Go ahead. I am always with you.
I have always addressed you as such. In the past and present, through countless years.

Astral Modulator, Guide of Civilizations, Mastermind of the Black Shores... these titles reflect your accomplishments. In the starry underground sky, the Necrostar streaks like a meteor into the distance. The Shorekeeper asks that you retrieve the Necrostar and restore balance at the Modulation Hall.
Though I am but a projection, I've been by your side all along.
I'll stand by you until the very end of this journey.
It appears the Necrostar has been successfully contained underground.
And... the gate is now sealed.
Hmm, thank you!
After this, let's go help KU-Chan!
They will probably need our help over there.
Listen to the wailing of the stars...
The corruption is even affecting their orbits.
As above, so below...
We just don't have the strength to fight it.
Hopefully KU-Chan and the rest can find a way to intercept the overflow.
According to our observations, the star that fell after the overflow was the Necrostar.
That star is critical for us to track the orbital movement of Solaris.
Only a map based on the Necrostar's data can function accurately.
Let's hope this gets resolved quickly, for all our sakes.
Solaris astronomy? Just look up to see for yourself.
What Tethys aims to achieve must be up there in the sky.
I've never seen a sky like that before...
You noticed it too, hm? The sky here is different from the one outside.
Could it be intentional?
You're {PlayerName}, right? Welcome. I'm the manager here.
You've met KU-Money before? Well, I hold a similar rank. The robots around here all work for me.
This used to be an observatory, but it later got converted into a charging station.
In times like these, stargazing is the last thing on people's minds.
Is it that bad?
The stars are what define the Black Shores.
But... we over here... aren't much help in a fight.
All we can do is keep the Tethys System stable by continuing to draw power from the Stellar Matrices. That's how we support our comrades in battle.
Have you heard? At the Black Shores, our efforts to stop the Lament are called "modulation."
Solaris exists in frequencies. We call adjusting these frequencies "modulation."
Someone did mention that to me before.
Its origin and practice trace back to an ancient philosopher from the Black Shores.
But the sands of time have erased him from the minds of many.
Hmm? I'm looking for a legendary figure.
Have you seen KU-Nami? She's one of us, said to be the first robot born from the Tethys System.
Sounds familiar.
Haven't seen her.
She's been missing...
She's always been fascinated by the stars and the universe. She also cares deeply about everyone at the Black Shores.
Thank you! You're doing a good thing.
They came out of nowhere!
I'm fine... Give me a hundred more!
Have to protect everyone...
The Shorekeeper is doing her best.
I can't fall behind.
Please tell everyone...
KU-Miro doesn't just sit and stare at the stars!
I can fight for our future just like the rest of them!
Thank you, thank you! You saved the day!
These Tacet Discords are such a pain! Luckily, we've got a way to get rid of them!
KU-Nana said you have important things to do, right? Go on, then. Leave the rest to us.
Madame Beatrice and the Agents also need your help.
Don't worry, we'll keep this station secure.
Ahh! Help!! Somebody help me!!
No, no, no! Not the Tacet Discords again!
It appears the Necrostar has been successfully contained underground.
And... the gate is now sealed.
Indeed. With my abilities, you don't need to worry about this.
Though I am but a projection, I've been by your side all along.
The Agents worked really hard to lock that bad star up!
But we have to open the gate to fully control it. I'll get you the key!
We can wipe out all the corrupted data just like we did before!
Use the portals to connect the device and the core, then we'll be in the clear!
You're safe. It's okay now.
I... I heard her voice.
Yes, she's here. Don't worry, you'll be fine.
I'm here with you now.
Stay with us, the medical team will arrive any minute.
I fulfilled my duty... as a member of the Black Shores...
Thank you... Please... Stop them...
Your actions will shine bright like the stars, a beacon for all to see.
What happened?!
An entire Necrostar was forcefully discharged into the Error Cell without warning.
The error codes spilled out as a result. At its worst, it looked a lot like virtual blood seeping through the ground.
We had to seal the underground gate to protect the Control Room. But someone had to retrieve the key...
He did what was necessary, even if it meant risking his own life.
How's the Agent doing?
He is severely infected with abnormal frequencies... It could be fatal.
We will. Have a good rest now, you've done enough.
Your effort won't be wasted. We will restore everything to normal and ensure everyone's safety.
I admit... I am surprised to see the Shorekeeper here.

You and the Shorekeeper finally arrive at the Error Cell where the Necrostar has fallen. However, you find that many of the injured have been severely affected by the corrupted data and cannot be saved.
Are you alright?
It might sound abrupt, but... I have begun to sense a change within myself.
More precisely, it's the part of me that rests in my garden. I feel... something different.
Something... I don't know how to describe...
I've done this before, by imitating the you I remember from many years ago.
You did what a leader must, but when I looked into your eyes, I could feel it—the emotion humans call sorrow.
Maybe… I should express that emotion in situations like this.
You've learned this from me?
Yes.
You led the Black Shores with empathy, and it's my responsibility to carry it forward in your absence.
I see. Well, it is our utmost priority to deal with the Necrostar to prevent further harm.
The only way to achieve this is by bringing the Necrostar to the Modulation Hall and initializing it within Tethys.
Gravity caused the destruction of Port City of Guixu.
I have the highest access to the Tethys System. Bring the Necrostar to the Modulation Hall, and I'll erase its corrupted data.
Once it's done, Tethys will function as it should, and no one will get hurt again.
But as I mentioned, I'm only a projection without physical form... Could you assist me with this?
Yes.
I'm here to help and protect you, just like I always have.
But... I'm currently unable to fully comprehend this feeling.
Does the Necrostar have any connection to the Port City of Guixu?
This Necrostar is the black hole that destroyed the Port City of Guixu.
Is the Black Shores experimenting on the Lament?
Yes. You've questioned this approach before.
How?
That's why I aim to change it.
But this time, I will bring everything to a proper end.
Will you trust me?
I don't see any reason not to.
Thank you...
...for everything you've done.
It's clear that the Agent's condition is terminal.
But still, I lied to him...
I'd do the same if I were you.
White lies are necessary sometimes.
Human emotions are complex.
When the Lament struck the city, many were unable to escape and were drawn into the black hole.
The data you brought back is directly related to that event.
It feels familiar...
Did I do the same thing 20 years ago?
Let's talk again once we're done with all this.
There are many things I need to understand.
Of course... We have plenty of time for it.
Long enough to talk about the past, the present, and the future.

The Shorekeeper can sense the underlying emotions feeding into deceit, pity, and other behavior, but struggles to fully understand them. She reveals that the data you recovered is related to the Lament from the Port City of Guixu, and the Tethys System is using the Lament itself to fight against it...
Besides us, I've sent everyone else to help contain the spread of the corrupted data.
If we had prepared earlier, we could have done more than just seal the underground.
Sigh...
Readings show a drop in the corruption spread. Quick, contact the station and tell them to start integration now!
We can't stop now...
Why not wait until it's safe?
We don't have time to mourn our fallen comrades.
All we can do is accept that they're gone, and make sure their sacrifice is not in vain.
Ah, you're the Rover, aren't you?
You recognize me?
I heard about you from my old colleagues at the Huaxu Academy in Jinzhou!
It's not surprising things have taken a turn for the better since you stepped in.
Morale is looking a lot better.
BEEP-BLOOP-BOOP!
For bleep sake! Reduce the memory size! Don't give errors so much processing space!
...Who are you?
Huh? Ah, {PlayerName}. Good you finally decided to show up.
I'm assistant manager of the Error Cell. It's my job to tell those other robots what to do.
Like KU-Money and KU-Tolo, I'm in charge of this area.
You seem strict.
Think you can afford to be soft dealing with those anomalies? Pffft.
Anyway, here's a tip. Don't let Beatrice's age fool you. She's tough as nails and as real a warden as they come.
Lower the bleeping input voltage! The boop frequency needs to be lower!
Retrieving every last bit of the corruption is the only way we'll get through this.
The agents here know this, so they choose to stand their ground.
What has it costed?
Besides the one who sacrificed themself to seal the gate, many others were injured.
If the Shorekeeper wasn't holding back the tide of corruption from within the Tethys itself, it would be much worse...
Please be careful. The object contained in the center is the Necrostar.
Use the portals to reach the platform.
According to pre-Lament laws of physics, gravity warps the fabric of space and time.
The voices I hear... They're coming from people in another dimension.
The floating device appears to be made out of Tacetite. It emanates a strange aura.
(Reach out your hand)
Authorized access, operation confirmed.
Hey! Don't just eat whatever's in front of you!
This looks awful! Ugh, like the worst stew ever made!
This frequency...
W-what are you staring at?
It's the one.
The one?
This frequency has dwelled within you for millions of years...
I'll keep an eye on it. We have more important matters at hand.
Wait, are you saying I'm not important here?!
Why did you wake up again, Abby?
'Cause you were about to gulp that hotchpotch of who-knows-what stuff! Go grab something normal if you're hungry. But this? Absolutely no!
This thing... It's like a dark, spooky hole. Once you fall in, you'll never crawl back out.
Precisely. This is the Necrostar, a black hole that will suck anything close to it into oblivion.
That little creature is able to perceive objects by their frequency...
Just as it described, the Necrostar's frequency is indeed incredibly complex.
Speaking of which, are you feeling discomfort anywhere?
Not at all. The black hole doesn't affect me.
No, I'm referring to that creature...
Do you feel anything unusual when interacting with it?
I feel fine.
...That's good to know.
The Necrostar's singularity has been retrieved. Let's take it to the Modulation Hall.
I'll stand by you until the very end of this journey.

With the Shorekeeper's assistance, you successfully retrieve the source of the chaos—the Necrostar. Abby, though weary, protests your involvement but lacks the strength to intervene. The Shorekeeper, meanwhile, appears deeply concerned about you and Abby's unique symbiosis.
Until...
...I must keep my promise.
I think... therefore I am?
Existence precedes essence—how should one comprehend this sentence?
Hello?
Hmm, what an intriguing question.
Excuse me? Could you tell me where I am?
Ah, my apologies, I was immersed in contemplation and didn't notice you.
This is Eidoscope, a garden linked to the Tethys System, where the Shorekeeper resides.
The Shorekeeper is here?
Well, this is her garden. It's only natural for her to be here.
Though she often takes the guise of the Sonoro, she has revealed herself recently. It's been some time since I last saw her.
As for this garden, it's where she assists Tethys' computational analysis in observing the stars.
Ahem, that explanation should suffice. Back to the question now...
Existence... Hmm, is it real? If it is, what about me? Do I truly exist?
It appears there's little point in continuing the philosophical debate with the robot.
Perhaps checking on the Shorekeeper is the more pressing matter.

A robot stationed in the Eidoscope informs you that the Shorekeeper has been guarding the Black Shores for the past twenty years. She often conceals herself using her Sonoro, as if anticipating someone's return...
Oh, hello! You're here!
At last, a new arrival!
Why is the Shorekeeper here?
What? You can see her?
This is the prime nexus for interfacing with the Tethys System. It's only natural she remains here.
It's been about 20 years now... Yes. Typically, she uses her Sonoro to mask her physical presence.
When she's in this state, her thoughts and emotions are sealed away. She exists in a state of suspended animation.
Occasionally, KU-Eros picks up faint echoes from her dreams...
Ro—No, Astral Modulator!
I—No, the Shorekeeper has been waiting for you endlessly!
I've caught the whispers she mutters to herself in her dreams and through the Sonoro.
She has spoken your name before...
Sometimes it's a desperate plea, sometimes it's pure joy, and other times it's filled with pain.
It's a voice from the very depths of her consciouness.
Welcome to the Eidoscope, Creator. You may observe the Tethys System through this lens.
You know me?
We, stationed at the Eidoscope, are among the oldest.
As the founder of the Black Shores, you have tasked us with assisting the Shorekeeper in managing Tethys' complex data.
Yet, like the Shorekeeper, we are bound to secrecy beyond this point.
You have likely sensed the deeper truth... As above, so below—the stars reflect the earth, and the past shapes the future.
Here, dualities persist, or perhaps such duality is the essence of our world.
The entity at the heart of the Tethys System might... indeed be the Tethys System itself.
Woah! You found me!
Oh? What am I doing here? You know, I just like hanging out here, watching the stars.
You know it too, right? This sky here isn't real.
One day, I might travel somewhere else in the universe. Somewhere far, far away...
But I just can't bring myself to leave this place and everyone here...
Anyway, thanks for finding me!
I'm sure you know where I'll be!
I've opened a portal to the Modulation Hall.
This is the only way I can see you, but I think...
No. It won't be long, {PlayerName}.
I'll use everything I've got—my computing power, my Sonoro...
Even my soul, if it exists.
What's the big deal? Just some pawns. I won't even break a sweat.
Something feels... different about them. Be careful.
I sense the presence of Tacet Discords below.
This is...
The Lament.
It razes cities
topples towers
crushes civilizations.
Nothing can escape it...
It sounds the death knell for humanity...
Leaving billions upon billions of lives lost to its wail.
Despair, obsession...
Resentment, remorse...
These feelings are archived within the Tethys System...
...alongside the names of each victim.
Grasping desperately for a tomorrow that never dawns.
But why?
Why is this burden yours to carry?
I am the guardian of the Black Shores, the core of Tethys.
I was created for this purpose.
Apologies. I should have controlled my Sonoro vision.
Those scenes... they look real.
Have you experienced them yourself?
I was entrusted to lead the Black Shores in your absence.
It's through this duty that I can protect you and what you cherished.
Though I've never witnessed the Lament firsthand, others have shared their experiences with me.
I've encoded them into observable stars, enabling the Tethys System to issue Lament alerts.
I am sorry.
Why apologize?
I... should have done better.
This disaster could have been prevented... if only I had been more dedicated to understanding those experiences and emotions.
You've done well.
I will give it my all, even if I must sacrifice my Sonoro, or myself...
This is the only way to protect the stars... and you.
I made my vow to you long ago, {PlayerName}. It remains just as true today.
I will break the shackles of fate.
I will unravel the Möbius loop that binds you.
I will give my all to honor my commitment.
How do I describe this feeling...? Is it guilt, dismay, or perhaps... longing?
What emotion should I express now?
Things could've been a lot worse without your help.
You've saved many lives.

Ensnared by her Sonoro's overflow, you are drawn into the disasters the Shorekeeper has "lived" through while analyzing the Lament. Her form, created by the Sonoro Sphere, is bound to the Tethys System's calculations. Her sole desire is to protect you and the Black Shores, but a hidden truth lingers in her heart...
Apologies, but the researchers here have already been evacuated to the Modulation Hall.
The rest of my team has also gone to their designated posts to help with the data corruption.
I'll be heading to the Modulation Hall to assist shortly as well. Ku-bye.
Digitalized Tacet Discords are gathering here...
They have their mission to fulfill.
Hmm... Oh!
It should be safe outside now, right?
All the agents and robots are working hard. We can't slack off.
But those Tacet Discord constructs around are still worrying me...
Welcome, I heard you're the new Consultant.
What's this place?
This is the Modulation Hall, where we adjust Stellar Matrix frequencies.
The Matrix before you is composed of compressed data from the Lament in the sky.
Tethys calibrates its frequencies to resonate with this and previous Lament incidencies as its method of predicting future ones.
But right now, we need to do more than just adjust Matrix frequencies...
The Shorekeeper... has finally revealed herself.
Have you heard that old prophecy?
She only shows herself when the Black Shores is in a moment of crisis, that one.
Many of us have gone our entire lives never seeing her.
But if it's true, her showing up means that things could get even worse.
I mean... is that really something to get excited about?
Precision mapping of the Matrix coordinates is critical...
Every detail on these maps must be exact. Any mistake could put our navigators' operations at risk.
But our senior navigator is already...
He's gone, I know. But there's no time for mourning.
Is there another navigator who can take his place?
The current lead navigator is a special operative, a fact clear from her uniform alone.
As the late navigator's associate, she has the skills needed to ensure the Modulation Hall remains functional.
We just don't know what to expect next...
Rest in peace...
You will not be forgotten.
Travel among the stars... Enzo, navigator of Rinascita.
We will see this through, and the Shorekeeper will guide us to rise once more.
Rest easy, my friend.
The currents of time are shifting once more...
My records reveal that the Shorekeeper has always surfaced with the tides of change.
Isn't this a sign of crisis?
Indeed, crisis often heralds progress. A stagnant shore is merely a pool of dead water.
The Black Shores will endure, as history has foretold.
The result of the Third Contingency Protocol is...
Hmm?
The time reading is negative...
Too distant... too distant... our reference frame is out of reach...
Points, lines, and planes... beyond the light cone... constrained by the four fundamental rules...
The multiplier is imaginary, compounding continuously... recall... our parameters...
This robot seems to struggle with the concept...
Ah, I understand now...
I've been analyzing a theoretical problem.
What problem?
With enough data...
Tethys might contain Lament data that we've never recorded but are certain has occurred, including the current Lament unfolding before us.
Though the likelihood is small, it's theoretically possible with sufficient data.
Imagine a drop of ink falling into the ocean, eventually reforming into the original drop...
If that drop of ink, that Lament, does exist... maybe we just haven't detected it yet.
Ah, good! You made it here safely.
Everything is ready. We just need the Necrostar's core now.
Got it. How are the other Agents doing?
They've been battling to retrieve the major Matrices since the Tethys System malfunctioned. The operation is going well.
We, the Black Shores, always work together as a team.
What should we do next about the Necrostar's core?
Please place it on the analyzer, and then we can proceed with the remodulation.
We've also detected the Shorekeeper's presence within these Matrices. She's been recovering the affected frequencies.
Once it's completed, the data overflow from the Tethys System will cease.
You place the Necrostar on the analyzer...
Stellar Matrix confirmed. Classification: Necrostar.
Would you like to start the remodulation?
Yes.
Loading backup data from the Necrostar. Simulating the Port City of Guixu...
It's the city destroyed by the Necrostar...
Backup data loaded. Please confirm.
That's the digital entrance of the Matrix! It worked!
So to complete the remodulation, just enter the Matrix and collect Tethys' redirected data.
Please wait.
The Tethys System now uses less of my computational power since the Necrostar was controlled.
I can assist you, {PlayerName}. Please, let me come with you.
...I must keep my promise.
Are you feeling okay now?
It's fine, I can link with more Sonoro Spheres to stay functional.
My duty must be fulfilled as long as I still physically exist.
I'll be fine. From now on, no one will ever be harmed.
Please, trust me.

After bringing the Necrostar back to the Modulation Hall, you prepare to head to the Stellar Matrix for remodulation. At this moment, the Shorekeeper, who has been in slumber, appears before you in physical form. She pleads to accompany you on the path that lies ahead.
You're here...
I didn't expect us to find each other here.
What do you mean?
This is the deepest part of the Tethys System, our shore... just for us.
I used to think my duty was to guard the Black Shores, obeying the Tethys System's every command.
But... you showed me another way.
You've shared so much with me—about the world beyond, about yourself, about the past, present, and future.
I remember the field of flowers we once saw in Rinascita, how beautiful those daisies and violets were.
Being with you always makes me feel something... something I couldn't quite understand at the time.
Come to think of it now, it must be... happiness.
You made me realize that protecting the Black Shores isn't my only duty...
...because there is more to life than duty.
You should go now. Continue your journey in Solaris and live a life of your own choosing.
What about you? You were sucked into the black hole...
Have you forgotten? I am the Sonoro's creation. The Sonoro will never fade away, and I will continue to serve.
We shall meet again... somewhere in the future.
But you promised me that no one would get harmed!
I completed the remodulation! It shouldn't end like this!
The Tethys System needs a core unit capable of feeling emotions to function.
If the Lament's data ceases to be the core, someone must fill that void.
Neither you nor the victims in Guixu deserve such burden.
You planned this from the beginning...
I'm truly sorry...
This is the only way to keep everyone safe... I alone shall bear this price.
I'm grateful to have you here on this shore. I couldn't ask for more.
No matter where you go, even to the ends of the earth, the Black Shores will always be your harbor.
No matter how far you go, I will always be here... watching over you.
Goodbye.
Hmm... I like this starry sky... so much.
Long ago, you likened Solaris's collected data to stars, the stars of humanity itself.
Whenever I gaze at this sky, there is always one bright, roving star.
And now, this star is here... right before me.
Just seeing this star is enough to calm any restless thoughts... it brings me peace.
Could this feeling be... love?
My journey ends here, but yours must continue.
No one will ever be harmed again, just as I promised.

The Tethys System manipulates the Necrostar, attempting to consume you as its core. In a desperate bid to save you, the Shorekeeper is swallowed into the Necrostar. When you awaken, you find yourself in the deepest part of the Tethys System, known as the "End of Wandering." In her final moments, the Shorekeeper bids you farewell.
The corrupted data is contained! The Necrostar's event horizon is stable, and the Data Hub is back online!
We did it! The Tethys System is back online!
The Rover... you did it!
She sacrificed herself to the black hole to save me.
What?!
But she has admin access to the Tethys System! How could she just disappear like that?
No! That can't be right!
The black hole...
Wait! What if she's still in the process of falling?
What do you mean?
Gravity is the only pre-Lament law of physics that still holds true today.
Someone once told me that...
The law of gravity from the old world still holds true today.
Objects will stay in perpetual free fall inside a black hole.
You mean...
Oh! I get it!
We might still see her on the black hole's surface!
This is unprecedented... We've never considered observing a Necrostar before.
But I remember reading about similar theories in ancient texts. It might just work.
Attention all units! Our observation target is now the Necrostar. Deploy all available equipment!
Understood! It'll take some time!
We must save the Shorekeeper at all costs! The Black Shores can't afford to lose her.
Wait, where's the Shorekeeper? Wasn't she with you?
She's been watching over us all along...
We'll bring her back, no matter how long it takes.
Ma'am, we've pinpointed the Shorekeeper's location in Tethys!
And not just her, we've identified the relative positions of everyone captured by the black hole beyond the event horizon!
To rescue them from the Necrostar, we'll have to redesign it using the principles of the new world.
In other words—
We must fight against the Tethys System.
But the Tethys System's programming is impeccable, almost otherworldly... Is it really possible to do that?
Besides, we still need a decoy with the highest-level access to divert its computational power so we can find the Shorekeeper.
I'll do it.
No, it's too risky!
We can't be sure if the rescue will suceed, and we can't afford to lose another member!
And there isn't anyone with higher access than the Shorekeeper.
Tethys, confirm my access.

A Blake Bloom imbued with the Shorekeeper's longings, holding the key to a fresh beginning after saying goodbye to the Shorekeeper at the End of Wandering. It grants the highest level of access in the Tethys System.
Confiming access... {PlayerName}, Chief Steward. Welcome.
What? How do you have top security clearance?
The Shorekeeper transfered her access to me in our last moments.
She gave you her access? Are you somebody important that we should know about?
Wait, that ancient prophecy...
In times of great adversity, the Shorekeeper will reveal herself and support our true leader, who, at the destined moment, will rise to save and guide the Black Shores forward.
You... You are the—
It's not important.
Our focus now is the Tethys System.
Members of the Black Shores have followed Tethys' calculations and commands.
Even the Shorekeeper herself is used as a pawn.
But humans shouldn't be treated as mere tools. History teaches us this, and we should never forget it.
No system is flawless, just as no human is perfect. That's why we have the right to question Tethys' decisions.
In Jinzhou, I learned an old saying: "We can't change the past, but we can shape the future."
That's what we need to do now—learn from our mistakes and build a better future.
The Black Shores exist for one reason: to protect everyone on this planet, because people are the heart of civilization.
We can fix broken systems, but without people, civilization has no soul.
Sorry to jump in but... I couldn't help overhearing what you've been saying...
Consultant Aalto?
Do what you have to do. Leave the ground area to us.
I'll bring her back, mark my words!
You've heard what {Male=he;Female=she} said.
Attention all units! Readiness Level One enabled. Switch the Tethys System to full recursive search mode. Prepare to open the transmission passage!
Rover, we're counting on you to save the Shorekeeper and the Black Shores.

As the newly reinstated highest administrator of the Tethys System, you announce to all of the Black Shores that past mistakes must be set right. Only by saving people can civilization itself be saved. As a member of the Black Shores, you face a crucial decision: If the Black Shores is a haven for every wandering soul, your mission is now to bring every lost soul back home.
R… Run…
The building collapsed…
They're all trapped… It's completely jammed…
What we're doing now is essentially breaking into the Tethys System.
Plus, the transmission coordinates aren't certain.
If you're ready, we can start the transmission now.
I'm ready.
I'm not ready yet.
Please get back to us safely!
Of course. Just come find me when you're ready.
Are we really challenging Tethys when it's locked down?
It'll be a miracle if we can even pull it off, but...
With the Shorekeeper helping us within Tethys and our comrades fighting bravely on the frontlines...
It's a gamble, but losing isn't an option.
Can we... really do this?
You don't think it's possible?
Nobody in the Black Shores has ever gone against the Tethys System's directives, with the insurmountable task of tracking its codes.
It may as well be a code written by the gods...
Going against a god does sound thrilling.
Only you would say something like that.
But since we've decided to go through with this, I'll follow through.
No matter what, we have to save the Shorekeeper.
A navigator talked about this before.
Tethys is extremely dependent on its core processor, which means...
Do you mean Tethys is using the Shorekeeper as its core processor?
It's possible.
But that's so inhumane! She's a person too...
Sigh...
If we keep scanning Tethys' memory, we can pinpoint the Shorekeeper's exact location.
We won't... ever give up on anyone.
Her physical form may be lost in the Matrix, but she is still in there.
Because her entire frequency spectrum is still somewhere in Tethys.
The law of conservation?
Yes! Hmm... so you're familiar with this concept, it's quite significant.
If we can recover her frequencies, we can use Tethys to bring her back.
It'll be like finding a needle in a haystack...
She believed in {PlayerName}. So, please trust us as well!
Enzo, my old friend...
If you're shining somewhere in this starry sky, please watch over us.
Watch over the Black Shores, watch over the Shorekeeper...
Let your starlight keep lighting our way forward.
We will keep fighting for you...
Hmm... I can't really say.
The Tethys System is a closed system. It keeps its core logic hidden.
Can we really find the Shorekeeper in its data banks...
I can do it.
Hmm! Uh... alright...
Memory scan reveals the presence of a secondary instance...
Hmm?
Processing data... processing data... processing data...
Emotions are not variables. They are factors...
Please verify the input for potential errors...
Remember... tool... she... tool...
Never... assign... to... humans.
You can't understand what the little robot says...
Want to try? If my hypothesis turns out to be correct...
What?
Picture a drop of ink falling into the ocean. Eventually, it will come back together into its original form.
Now, imagine that drop of ink is the Shorekeeper.
We need to apply some external force to speed up this process. We're not just locating the Shorekeeper, we're reconstructing her.
After being absorbed by Tethys, her frequency was fragmented and dispersed throughout it.
It's time to test my theory...
Defense verification unsuccessful...
This system must continue to function...
Re-initiating command. Implementing Third Contingency Protocol.
Execute formatting. Target: Shorekeeper.
Formatting: 37%...
Formatting: 62%...
Formatting: 85%...
Formatted. The Shorekeeper will be the new computational unit.
Only this ensures system continuity.
It is the only way to defeat the Lament.
You'd better...
Let her go!
I will not leave anyone behind!
See? Just let it flow out of you, like this.
You can do it too.
Come, give it a try.
No, you shouldn't be here...
If you get integrated into Tethys, you won't be yourself anymore...
That won't be a problem.
Tethys and the Black Shores will find another way.
Someone kept this from me, didn't they?
That sounds familiar. I feel like I heard it before.
A long time ago, you taught me how to play it.
I see. But I... I have no memory of it.
I'll teach you...
Just like you did for me before.
From the distant past to the far future, everything begins and ends here.
When you established the Black Shores to unite Solaris, the Tethys System already existed.
Later, you discovered it relied on emotions from the Lament to fuel its calculations. Without them, it cannot function.
Using the Lament against itself is like walking on a Möbius loop with no end in sight.
We have tried for millennia to break this cycle without success.
And then... you left the Black Shores to look for other solutions.
But deep down, you already knew the best solution. It was one you couldn't accept.
That solution is me—the tool always meant to become Tethys' core.
If I don't do this, you, as the Modulator of this system, will be chosen as the core. I must fulfill my duty to protect you.
But... I want to be by your side, to see the skies you've seen, to tread the paths you've walked. I want to understand... what happiness really means.
When I first discovered these emotions, I didn't know what to do...
So I lied to you, thinking it was the best choice for both of us...
I... I'm sorry...
Sorry for putting you in harm's way...
"Salvation is about building a world where people no longer need to be saved."
This is why we return to this shore.
No one should be treated as a mere tool.
We're back at the Black Shores now, back to our home.
Welcome home, my Shorekeeper.
Yes.
Thank you. My... star.
The Shorekeeper and you return to reality, landing on the very beach where you first arrived in the Black Shores. She explains her deception regarding the Stellar Matrix and expresses her gratitude.
About that frequency dwelling within you...
You mean Abby?
Yes.
It seems to be "hungering" for something.
Have you ever felt anything unusual?
I don't feel anything...
Abby's been unusually quiet these days.
My Sonoro can sense even the most minor changes in frequencies.
So I can tell that there's something strange about that frequency.
I'll search for more information in the Tethys System and share what I find with you.
How is the Tethys System now?
After being fixed, it's executing the master command given at its creation.
The core computational unit has now been replaced by a special frequency that shares similar properties as the Lament.
But this one is... more harmonious and mild.
What about you? Are you still confined to this place?
Although I must stay here to watch over the Black Shores, I'm now able to bath in the sunshine and feel the sea breeze with you.
This is what freedom feels like.
It feels delightful.
I know you have your own journey to finish.
You can entrust the Black Shores to me, and I'll carry out my duty as always.
You have the full support of the Black Shores, no matter where you are or how far you go.
And... despite all the many names you bear, I see you for who you truly are.
Wherever your path leads, I hope to walk it with you.
Some time later...
The Shorekeeper warns you of Abby's anomalies. Through your intervention, the Tethys System has returned to its rightful state, now operating with peaceful and harmonious frequencies.
Welcome.
We?
Yes… WE.
We are the gravitational force you seek.
Time... is running out. Hoda. My name is Hoda.
Eugh! What does any of this have to do with me?!
Where did it go? No, wait. Don't go over there, {PlayerName}!
It claimed it was the gravitational center we're looking for.
It must be the abnormal frequency the Black Shores want recovered.
The remaining frequency there is in extreme chaos. It's dangerous.
This is MY name. I once lived under it… as a Bloom Bearer.
Heh heh, "you"? Which one of us are you talking to? Men or women, elders or children?
Do you hear the echoes of our "lament"?
Remember… Remember it all…
No, no! They want you to become a part of them. I can't let it happen.
Run! RUN! {PlayerName}!
What you seek… is on the girl…
Hold on! Hey, what's happening?! It's starting to glow!
It must be from the Black Shores! Look at this!
What…
Look for survivors, quick!
It's… too late.
So, they're the agents Niya was waiting for...
What happened here…
Astral Modulator, the Rover {Male=himself;Female=herself}. We have awaited this reunion for a long time.
Is this your doing with the Bloom Bearers?
Remember your past, the past you turned your back on… The past as one of the Black Shores...
And respond... respond to the promises you made, to the future we're bound to share.
Salvation... is forging a world where saving is no longer needed.
She has it...

Upon arriving at the coordinates provided by Niya, you find the bodies of several Black Shores members who have died under mysterious circumstances. There, you encounter a mysterious Bloom Bearer named Hoda, who claims to know about your past but cannot divulge the details. Before disappearing, Hoda directs you to Youhu for further clues...
A mysterious object pulses with rhythmic light, seemingly harboring some form of frequency.
I need to learn more about this thing. My master and I guessed it's from the Black Shores, and now it looks like we were right!
The abnormal frequency definitely links to the deaths of those Bloom Bearers.
Now it's hiding in this object, but I can still feel its strong attachment to the Black Shores.
Solving this issue is beyond our capabilities. Besides, they also mentioned Rover and the fall of the Port City of Guixu.
We should meet with that Bloom Bearer first and explain the situation. This is best left to the experts.
You're right. We need to keep her informed.
Let's go, {PlayerName}. I've a bad feeling about this.
I sense there's more to this than meets the eye…
Port City of Guixu must hold secrets waiting to be discovered.

Youhu reveals that the clue Hoda mentioned is an artifact from Mt. Firmament, discovered by her and Master Chenpi. Now, it seems connected with the Black Shores. The frequency tied to Hoda is hidden within this artifact, and it seems linked to the deaths of the Bloom Bearers. Reporting this matter to Niya and the Black Shores is now a matter of urgency.
As the group moves forward, Yangyang informs the Midnight Rangers of the situation and begins preparations to recover the Bloom Bearers' bodies...
Whoa!
Thanks…
Huh? Up there!
Welcome home.
The Port City of Guixu... It once embodied the metropolitan dream.
Confidence and ambition fueled its growth, pushing the entire world forward.
People sailed every sea, explored every land. Everyone had food and shelter, living in peace.
Their spirits were high, optimism as tall as the skyscrapers. A bright future was surely inevitable, or so they thought.
See that brightly lit building? It was the tallest, reaching high enough to touch the heavens.
It sounds like a time of great hope...
It was an era of high aspirations and big dreams. Life had infinite possibility.
Humanity's aspirations soared beyond the stars, searching for the edge of the universe itself.
The universe itself?
Yes, because it was there, well within our reach...
Until...
...The Lament wiped everything out.
I've never been to this city myself, not even in the Sonoro.
You were the one who told me about its rise and fall.
You've always been a witness.
But perhaps you had already foreseen its end and the issues that threaten us today.
The city looks safe for now.
The Lament will strike here in one hour.
My computations only recreated the city as it was in its final hour before disaster.
Hard to imagine such a city turning to dust...
The more steps we take, the closer we draw to the inevitable destruction.
The moment the Lament starts is our chance to retrieve the data.
I'm sorry. We could never change history... or the "future" that already happened.
As one who has already walked this path, what did you experience? How did you... feel about it?
Does the Tethys System command you to ask about this?
No.
I ask... because "I" want to know.
...Would you like to share it with me?
I remember your smile when you described how prosperous it was.
You're working that late? Are you serious? You'll miss the last train!
What a workaholic... Fine, I'll drive you home this time.
What are you doing up so late? Need any help?
Just head home and rest. Don't let a job get you down...
Those are just shadows of the past.
The Sonoro Sphere replicated every aspect of the city, including its residents.
Each of them had a life as vivid as yours, until the Lament turned everything to rubble...
The tea served here has a distinct flavor.
Must be a good one.
Do you like tea?
Not really my thing.
I do enjoy it.
I see.
The Bank of Life preserves many tea seeds.
Perhaps we could plant a few in the Greenhouse...
Hmm... It's bitter...
Or I could store tea leaves in my Sonoro, if you need them for your journey.
That's not worth your effort.
Oh... I see.
You have enough on your shoulders.
Ah, I understand.
If I know you will enjoy it, it's no trouble for me.
Whoa, didn't expect customers at this hour!
We don't usually take orders now, but I'll make an exception for you. What can I get ya?
Good evening. Fancy a drink？
I'd recommend this iced tea. Trust me, it won't let you down.
The city's night view is always mesmerizing. Closing your eyes on such a beautiful night would be a crime.
Sorry if I'm staring too long, but honestly, you two make a perfect duo.
How romantic...
You really seem to like it here.
It feels familiar.
It's a marvel to me.
This city and its people belong to the old era. They embody exactly what a civilization needs to thrive.
Whenever you spoke of this, I could feel the joy radiating from your words.
However, prosperity and harmony are rare and fleeting in a world twisted by the Lament.
Perhaps we can only catch glimpses of them replicated by the Sonoro.
The feeling humans have in a vibrant city like this... is it called happiness?
Yes, a feeling unknown to those scarred by war and disaster.
One day, the people of Solaris will once again return to such an era.
We are about to see the beginning of the Lament...
In ten minutes' time.
Back then, the Black Shores issued a Lament warning to the city.
Unfortunately, the Lament swept through much faster than the Tethys System anticipated.
You dispatched all available personnel to assist Huanglong in evacuation.
But in the end... some lives couldn't be saved.
That Bloom Bearer named Hoda...
Yes. She was one of the many casualties.
As a Bloom Bearer, she was on the front lines of evacuation and rescue efforts.
Yet human strength... is a mere whisper against the Lament's roar.
No life should be lost in vain.
You've always believed in this.
The Black Shores uphold this belief, and so did Hoda.
Will she be replicated?
Yes, just up ahead.
But I'm not sure if seeing her is the right thing to do.

Ahead lies the onset of the Port City of Guixu's destruction. According to the Shorekeeper, despite deploying every available Black Shores member to prevent the disaster, many innocent lives were lost to the Necrostar, including Hoda, the field medic.
Someone... Please save us...
No... It's already too late for me...
Take my daughter... My poor baby girl... She can still live...
You're with the Black Shores? Huh... Too late.
It's... all over.
Nobody will make it out alive. This building... this building is our grave...
A grave... for fools who attempted to touch the heavens...
Don't give up hope! We'll save you!
I'm a doctor from the Black Shores. Calm down, let me examine you.
Are you... Hoda?
Yes, and you... Wait a moment... {PlayerName}? It's you!
You finally found us!
Allow me to introduce myself properly. I'm Hoda, the Bloom Bearer of the Black Shores.
It's been a long time since we talked face to face, my mentor.
You've been trapped here all along?
Ever since that day, both I and those engulfed by the Lament have become part of the black hole.
The Tethys System later contained it, turning it into a new Necrostar.
I have always known about this...
But the Necrostar integrated into the core logic of the Tethys System, so I could not interfere.
So Tethys is actually using the Lament.
Tethys can observe the Lament because it understands its nature.
The best way to fully understand something is to study a perfect replica in a controlled environment.
Tethys has been selectively containing Lament sources to drive its analysis of other occurrences.
You mean Tethys is using the Lament as a tool against itself?
It's the only effective solution so far.
That's why Tethys contained this Necrostar.
I'm part of it now, but I've never forgotten my duty as a Bloom Bearer, not for a moment.
Despair, obsession, resentment, remorse... Emotions stirred by the Lament have torn us apart, much like the tidal forces around a real black hole.
But just like the Lament itself, those emotions are also frequencies. Tethys likely harnesses them in order to—
It's calling...
The Tethys System is attempting to activate the Necrostar program again!
Please... my mentor...
Please free us... from this endless cycle...
Use the gravity...
It's the only law... from the old world... that still holds true today...
For those in disaster, the name "Black Shores" brings hope.
You're the one keeping the Necrostar in check from within...
I did my best, just like you are. The only difference is, I'm just a shadow.

I've lost track of how long it's been, but at some point, I realized that the Lament follows patterns and can be controlled, much like the Necrostar itself. But I couldn't share my theories with anyone...
Nothing escapes a black hole. I could only hope for your arrival one day.
We once felt as lost as you do now, but your wisdom showed us a path we could follow.
It seems the Tethys System has been hiding things from us.
We're still unable to fully explain issues related to gravity with post-Lament science.
Perhaps that's why Tethys even risked integrating the Lament and Necrostar into its core logic...
But our time is running out. We have to terminate the Necrostar to complete remodulation.
It will be challenging.
Please allow me to accompany you, {PlayerName}.
This is my request as a member of the Black Shores.
And it's also... my personal... request.
Severely corrupted data detected... It's right behind this gate.
I'll work to stop it spreading. Please be careful.
This is the highest point in Guixu Port City, where the Lament descended.
Gravity anomalies crushed this building into rubble.
Tacet Discords closer to the Lament's origin are more dangerous.
My Sonoro will shield you...
But please hurry.
The Necrostar is right ahead.
That piano is the modulation interface.
Please be careful. This place is filled with... hatred.
Program copied.
Core computational unit installation in progress...
Target confirmed: Chief Steward.
Hold on...
Don't let go!

No, no...
Let go! Now!
No... Your journey will not end here!

Farewell.
Backup plan enabled.
Hello again!
Hello, you! What brings you here?
Ku ku ku... I like you, {PlayerName}！
We need its help to get past the blockade.
My ability to manipulate portals functions more efficiently within this Sonoro-made space.
Both the entrance and exit portal can be controlled now.
Let's give it another try.
Use the portals to propel the key at the target lock.
Remember the law of gravity is still at play here.
The law of gravity still works here.
Wait for the falling key to accelerate until it reaches maximum velocity.
Try using the portals to clear the corrupted data. We can activate the device to get the key that way.
This way is blocked.
The portals might help us clear the corrupted data and activate the device.
Use your Grapple! Quickly!
Over here!
We have to find a way around these blockades and use the key to unlock the gate.
The portals might be able to help you.
Perhaps you can utilize my portal powers to get past the blockade and get the key.
Portals with different colors have unique traits.
If a new portal matches an existing one in color, it will replace it.
Only portals of different colors can exist at the same time.
Threat detected... Assisting elimination.
Digital Tacet Discords have infiltrated this place.
It means we're nearing the source of the Lament.
The building is starting to collapse.
The gravity is powerful enough to demolish it completely...
You can use gravity here!
An object in free fall between two portals will keep accelerating.
You can send the target to the designated location this way.
Authorization granted! Give it a try!
An object in free fall between two portals will keep accelerating.
You can send the target to the designated location this way.
Hmm... Did anything go wrong? Let's try that again!
A portal that opens downward could be more useful.

You and the Shorekeeper finally arrive at the simulated Port City of Guixu. This magnificent city teeters on the brink of destruction with two Laments looming, sealing the city's fate. Though history cannot be altered, you can only relive the harrowing moments of the city's destruction and the despair that engulfed it.
For the first time, the Shorekeeper savors the taste of tea and resolves to keep a special reserve of leaves for you within her Sonoro.

In the Stellar Matrix of the Port City of Guixu, you find Hoda tending to the injured. She reveals that the Tethys System's handling of the Lament is the root cause of the current crisis. Before she passes, she imparts that gravity is the key to resolving the situation.
Welcome, Chief Steward {PlayerName}.
This is the Tethys System's data cache, used only for temporary storage.
Access here should be restricted.
This system deduces that the Shorekeeper assigned admin access to you.
I'm here to get her and the others back.
The Shorekeeper is now the core computational unit.
Forceful discharge of the core unit will result in system crash.
This can be prevented. They shouldn't be sacrificed in vain.
Objection. All sacrifices are necessary.
The purpose of human civilization is to survive.
Over the past 10,000 years, a total of five global occurrences and over 300,000 regional occurrences of the Lament have been observed.
Thanks to this system's calculations and the Sentinels' data, we have averted all potential threats to human civilization on Solaris.
Individual sacrifices are inconsequential in the broader context of the common good.
Additionally, the Shorekeeper is composed of the Sonoro and is not human.
But she has feelings.
You are just a cold machine.
Emotions are unnecessary for survival.
But they spark civilizations.
Error: Unable to process...
I'll bring them back no matter what.
I won't leave anyone behind.
Repeat. Forceful discharge of the core unit will result in system crash.
A world without this system is doomed to perish in the Lament.
I'll fix your error.
Error: Unable to process...
Last warning. Forceful discharge of the core unit will activate the defense program. Consequences will be severe.
Bring it on!
Admin access nullified. Request denied.
I've already found the solution.
Correction. This system is designed to preserve human civilization. Every command is infallible.
We save the world by holding onto our humanity.
An apathetic supercomputer can't be our savior.

You have fallen into the tangled data web of the Tethys System. To deter you from rescuing the Shorekeeper, who is on the verge of becoming its core, the Tethys System reveals three potential futures in its absence: an ice age, a cataclysmic disaster, and the total reconstruction of civilization. Once a tool for observing civilizations, this cold and calculating system now stands in open rebellion against you. The final showdown is at hand—who will prevail, you or Tethys?
You must... live...
Please... leave here...
Use the Grapple... to leave...
The future ahead is frozen in cold silence...
Be careful...
The earth rent asunder, the world reduced to ashes...

I'll follow up with more intel as you go, same as before!
A strange yet assertive frequency wells up in you.
From simplicity to complexity.
We must unite the people, and rally under one banner.
This island, this planet, will one day bloom endlessly like summer blossoms.

I will remain here and fulfill my duties.
