We witnessed the final fate of those knights.
Seeker… This place is not the beginning of your quest…
Beneath the firelight, shadow loses its refuge.
Huh? Is this some sort of riddle?
"Firelight"... Maybe it's related to the torches around here? And the "shadow" could be—
Did you see that? Something just fell off that spooky knight!
It seems to be a scrap of paper.
Wait a minute... You think the TD you fought was the same one in this journal?
"Ruins in the southwest," let's check it out.
It's the same kind of knight TD. These ruins must be connected.
And here come more bits and pieces!
Things were really going downhill for them! What relic were they after that was worth all this?
It's still too soon to tell.
There's a mark on the map for a third ruin. Let's continue following their trail.
Hey, remember how those Fae Ignises lit up the torches at the other ruin?
Maybe we can use that to our advantage.
A Trial Invitation letter? Looks like this was meant for someone else. How did it end up here?
Something about a trial... and a miraculous elixir? Smells fishy. Better take a trip to Porto-Veno Castle and see what's really going on.
At long last... after the skies had wept their fury, the fleet spied a new island on the horizon.
That thing I found around here earlier. Was it the medal you mentioned?
...It's true there's only four medals. Now that I have them all, does this mean I passed all the trials they were talking about?
Upon this island, the people tamed its wilderness and built new homes.
That makes all four badges. But I haven't seen Chloe...
Maybe she's back at the castle? Time to find out.
My lord...
Can you see me?
I collected all four medals.
I passed all the trials.
I now present to you these four medals!
She still can't hear me...
Huh? I was the one who passed the trials...
You are too kind, my lord... Does this mean I am to be accepted as ██?
And the elixir mentioned in the letter. Please, I need it to cure Jojo's illness...
Is that all there is to the trials...?
Could such a miraculous elixir really exist...?
Hmm? I see. So the trials before were only the beginning...
Yes. I will give everything to pass the remaining trials, my lord. I will become ██!
Jojo needs that elixir to get better!

With her decision made, you watch Chloe walk towards Porto-Veno Castle without any hesitation.
Instead of opening the gate, she passes right through it.

You give the gate a push, but it won't budge.
For some reason, you get the feeling of a swiming above water for a breath of fresh air, the moment you placed your hand on the gate.
This feeling... Was everything just an illusion? Did it begin the moment I met Chloe? Or was it when I received that letter?
Chloe must've been the first to face whatever trial this was at some point in the past.
If what I saw in that illusion is true... then she entered Porto-Veno Castle afterward.
But did she finish the trial? Did she even make it out...?
Yes, my lord...
I will give everything to pass this trail!
Who are you talking to?
Are you one of the candidates?
I believe this letter belongs to you.
My lord said there are four trials scattered around Porto-Veno Castle. Each one holds a medal... I need to complete them all!
I've got to get that elixir and become ██ to save Jojo!
Hello? Can you hear me?
Who's Jojo?
I can't waste another moment. I must go.
Chloe disappears into the distance just as she finishes her sentence.
Was that an illusion? Or some vision from the past?
Hmm... I should probably find those trials she mentioned to understand what this it about.
Here lies the Trial of Swiftness.
As ██, wherever you wish to go, you shall arrive; whatever you seek to accomplish, you will see through. No obstacle can stand before your great purpose.
Use the puzzles along the path to defeat your foes and reach the objective. Only then will you pass this trial.
Here lies the Trial of Bravery.
O great ██, wield your sword and strike down all who stand before you.
Make a stand here, and the heretics will bow before our might! Defeat all foes to pass this trial.
Here lies the Trial of Perception.
Rinascita will be greeted by an inevitable storm. O great ██, find the calm within its eye.
Amid a battlefield of constant change, find a safe passage and avoid rampaging foes to pass this trial.
Here lies the Trial of Wisdom.
The chaotic world is steeped in murmurs... Do not be led astray by the chaos of falsehoods. Seek the truth that history hides.
Decipher the hidden meaning in these paintings, and restore them to their rightful places to pass this trial.
Floods surged as the earth cracked and fell away. Islanders were torn from their homes.
Through the raging storm, a handful of ships fought their way through the storm's wrath.
Ahoy there, young stranger.
Hi, What are you doing here?
Feel the briny wind from the sea? A perfect day for a voyage with the calm waves, eh?
See, that's my Gondola over there. As long as she's with me, there is no place in Rinascita we can't reach.
Ah, where are my manners? Name's Davide, Captain Davide, or... boatman perhaps. Doesn't matter which to me.
I'm retiring anyway.
But you don't look ready to retire just yet.
You've got that right. I can still run a full trip to Septimont, singing shanties and puffing on my pipe the whole way.
No storm's ever bested me and my Gondola, and none will.
But every tale needs a proper ending. I reckon it's time for my last grand voyage.
Last voyage? That sounds ominous.
Nah, it's alright. All I want is one last sail to somewhere I've never been to, before I settle down for good in the city.
I've crossed Nimbus Sanctum, seen Lorelei dancing among the stars, and ventured to forbidden lands, through reefs sharp as daggers.
From the dread lurking in the abyss to the beauty of fantasy islands, I've seen more than enough.
There's only one place left in all of Rinascita that I haven't conquered—the sky.
The sky?
Aye! Now you probably think I've got a few bolts loose, eh? Older and crazier than the lot on Pilgrim's Sails.
But this is no joke. There were nights I dreamed of my Gondola and I gliding on the wind.
We would pass the rainbow bridge and see birds flashing beneath the boat like fish in a coral reef. Imagine that—a voyage like no other.
But can a Gondola really fly?
I've got faith in her. All she needs is the right push, and she'll take me up there.
I know what I'm talking about. In fact, we did come close one time.
We were out at sea when we got caught in a... what do they call it? Tornado? Felt like a giant hand grabbed us and flung us into the air.
A tornado?
Wouldn't that be dangerous?
Ah, no need to worry. That was just a starter compared to the worst I've seen. Now, you seem like a kind soul. Think you can help me find something as powerful as that tornado?
Naturally, there's something in it for you. Whatever treasure I find on this journey is yours.
Treasure? What treasure?
There's a treasure in the sky?
They say, "At the end of the rainbow lies gold." The same goes for the clouds. In Rinascita, there's a tale of a ruin from the Dark Tide, said to be filled with treasure.
But for me, steering my Gondola toward treasures lost to time is worth more than any treasure itself.
So, what do you say? Not a bad offer, eh?
What kind of power do you need?
Let me think... I remember, in Ragunna, there's a TD built like a giant stuffed toy but packed with raw strength.
If we can turn it into an Echo, it should be strong enough to launch us into the sky. Then I'll just leave the rest to my Gondola—I trust her.
It worked! We're flying! Keep it steady, partner! Take us to the clouds!
See that, my friend? We made it! Want to join us for a view of the heavens?
Wait… how do I control this thing… no, no, how do I stop it?
N-no matter! This is my last voyage! Onward! Nothing can stop me now!
So we meet again, my friend.
Are you alright?
Me? Couldn't be better. The view above the clouds was exactly like what I dreamed.
For a final voyage, it was everything I ever wanted, and deeply satisfying.
Allow me to thank you once more. My dream has finally come true.
Where is your Gondola?
Oh, don't remind me. That Wingray had a mind of its own—it wouldn't change course or land.
Eventually, hunger got the better of me, so I jumped into the sea, watching my partner and the Wingrays fade into the horizon...
I'm sorry to hear that.
What a bittersweet ending.
That's alright. She seemed happy as could be. My partner loved the thrill of adventure as much as I do—we're two of a kind.
She'll continue that grand, mysterious voyage, and I'm sure she'd find plenty of joy along the way.
And, well, I did manage to find a little surprise.
A surprise?
You found the ruin?
It's that chest over there. I stumbled upon a floating platform in the clouds, and it was sitting right on top. No idea who left it there.
No, not really. Just a chest resting on a platform in the clouds. No idea how it got there.
It could be the origin of that tale, even if it turned out, well, less impressive than I imagined.
Anyway, as we agreed, everything in it is yours.
What will you do now?
Me? I'll go back to Ragunna and live the quiet life of a retired captain, telling my tales to anyone who'll listen.
A captain who flew his Gondola to the sky… Well, who'd believe that?
Farewell, my friend. May the Sentinel always bless you.
Time to set sail!
Give it all you've got, big fella!
We've got it this time...
Hold on... these Fae Ignis are acting strange.
Ah-ha! That's the Echo! Thank you, young one!
Ahem... though I do have one more favor to ask.
Go ahead.
I'd like to share with you this moment of thrill as I break free from the earth and reach for the sky.
Would you do me the honor of witnessing my voyage?
With pleasure.
Excellent! Now, eyes on me!
Ugh... guess my old bones weren't ready for that.
Are you okay?
*Coughs*... Oh, it's you. Gave you a bit of a laugh, did I?
But for me and my Gondola here, this is nothing at all. Right, partner?
*A confident whistle*
If you'd seen us take on the raging seas, you'd know this is smooth sailing.
We've ridden down waves taller than mountains without a scratch. This drop's barely worth mentioning.
Oh really?
Anyway, glad you're okay.
It clearly didn't go as planned. What's holding us back?
Maybe Gondolas aren't built for flight, eh? Even with a boost, all we'd get is a short glide.
Isn't that obvious?
Short glide? More like a nose dive.
Alright, alright, I may have put too much faith in my old partner. She's always been unstoppable in my memory.
Hard to believe there are things she can't do...
*A protesting whistle*
Easy there, partner. I'm not griping. Just saying we need a new plan.
Let me see... Ah, yes. There's a flying TD in Penitent's End called Fae Ignis.
If we turn them into Echoes and load them aboard, there's a fair chance they'll give us the lift we need.
Now that sounds like a plan.
Cool, but please stay safe.
So, mind making one more trip for this old man?
Leave it to me!
No problem.
Thank you, young one.
In my younger days, I saw flying balloons at the Carnevale that could lift a single person up into the air.
But I can't just leave my boat behind. What kind of captain would I be without her?
Still, it's not a bad starting point. Now, what could we use instead of a balloon?
Aye, that's the one!
Thank you. I'll be ready in a minute!
Good luck!
I've got bad feelings about this...
I'll take that blessing!
Rest easy! No storms can get the best of me!
Brace yourself—you're about to see us conquer the sky!
Well, it's good to see you again, my friend.
Are you alright?
Your Gondola exploded.
*Coughs*... No need to worry. Just a minor setback, nothing I can't handle.
Rough landing aside, I'd say things went fairly well.
At least my partner and I managed to fly, though it was not the voyage I had in mind.
Maybe I'm just getting old, old enough to forget Fae Ignis can go off like firecrackers...
Are you giving it another go?
Maybe it's time to stop.
For sure! Even if I wanted to quit, my partner would never allow it.
Not a chance. Even if I wanted to quit, my partner would never allow it.
*A supportive whistle*
Hah! That's right, partner! We'll be above the clouds!
Could you do me one more favor, my friend? I swear this will be the last one.
Alright… so what's the plan?
I believe we are on the right track. Echoes can make a Gondola fly, but only the right ones can make a Gondola soar.
If, just if, we could get our hands on a calm flying Echo like a Wingray...
Come to think of it, there used to be Wingrays here, but they've all vanished recently.
Could it be… those masked fellas in red uniforms?
The Fractsidus again?
Ah yes, the Fractsidus! They've got a camp around here. Haven't been there, but I've spotted them firing at the sky.
Are they… poaching the Wingrays? By the Sentinel, those transgressors will answer for this!
Would you mind heading over to take a look? If they've taken the Wingrays, please save them.
The Fractsidus has locked up the Wingrays.
These doors look flimsy. Perhaps a heavy blow may break them down.
The gate's open.
Let's bring this Wingray to Captain Davide.
A Wingray! Thank you, my friend.
So, you taught those poachers a lesson, eh? The Sentinel will smile upon that.
Now let's see if it would give me and my partner a ride to the sky.
I can feel the wind beckoning us from afar... urging us to start our voyage.
Thank you for everything. Now, I hope you'll stay to witness the moment we take flight!
I'm looking forward to it.
Hope this one goes smoothly.
Off we go, partner!
*A spirited whistle*
I think we've been spotted... Or maybe it's just paranoia.
Either way, we must stay on our toes.
Steady. The alarm's moments from triggering.
Hurry, take cover! We're almost exposed!
Seems we're in the clear now.
Let's move on.
The Vitreum Dancers shouldn't be patrolling here. Someone's heightened vault security. I wonder who.
The good news is they don't seem aggressive.
But they could still trigger the alarm. Better stay away.
Even the surveillance cameras have increased. This bodes ill.
Quite a few cameras here... Could the prisms be of any help?
Found some prisms here.
I'll use them to pass through.
…This doesn't seem to be working.
I'll try a different one.
I'm in the control room, just a moment.
Switching view to your side now.
Done... The door before you should be open.
Beyond the door you should find the other control room. Beware of the patrolling Echoes.
{PlayerName}, there should be a monitor you can operate.
Let me know once you find it.
I'm at the monitor.
Give me a moment. I'll upgrade your access so you have control of the vault's systems.
Looks like some Echoes are approaching. Stay alert.
Can you see me?
Clear as day.
I need to cross the hall from above. People might spot me if I make too much noise.
So could you maneuver these chandeliers to form a pathway for me?
Lower the chandelier on the right.
Wonderful.
Rotate the chandelier 90° clockwise.
Rotate the chandelier 180° clockwise.
Perfect.
Wait… the chandelier dosen't seem to be positioned properly.
Rotate the chandelier 90° counterclockwise.
Well done.
Sway the chandelier.
Splendid, I've made it across.
It's my turn now.
I'll see you in a moment.
How did these artifacts get here? Hmm, strange.
The door should be open, {PlayerName}, and we will soon meet—
{PlayerName}? Looks like the signal has been jammed…
Thank the Sentinel, it didn't set off the central alarm. I should still be under the radar.
The path is blocked… Wall-dashing seems to be the only option.
Is that a screen?... Perhaps I can use Grapple to pull it over.
These scatter prisms might come in handy.
Must be more cautious…
…Heh.
Carlotta, hello?!
The comms are cut off. She must be in trouble.
Gotta hurry up.
The blockdown is lifted. I need to keep moving.
Need to get rid of them fast.
...Impeccable timing, {PlayerName}. You never disappoint.
I notice surprise in your eyes. Let me guess…
"That's quite some skill for a lady of nobility."
In fact, beyond being the second daughter of the Montelli family, I have a even more... significant title.
The family's Executor.
Be it a traitor within the family or a threat from outside, I locate, observe, and address these risks in secret and with tact.
Say, the ones hiding in the tuning room.
The room is that way. Time to see what kind of mischief they are up to…
It seems they've left a little surprise for us. But if they think this will stop you and me...
Then they're gravely mistaken.

As Carlotta falls from a great height, you reach the depths of the vault just in time to catch her safely.
Her agility raises questions in you, and she finally reveals her hidden identity: she is the family's Executor, tasked with handling disputes and eliminating traitors. 
Just then, traps set by the traitors activate, calling guards to stop you—but none can stand in your way.
The future of Rinascita... rests with all of us.
And the Montellis will make sure everyone has a equal share of it.
Ragunna will enter a new era united.
United under the promise of our Terminals.
Whew, and it saved me some footwork.
Just moments ago, you lost contact with Carlotta when she fell underground.
Could you do me a favor, Ms. Zani? Please secure the evidence in the property room and... fetch me the "jewelry" and "perfume."
Jewelry and perfume? You mean…
Ahem, yes. You know where to find our… "dressing room," I presume? Inform the "stylist" it's my request. She'll prepare everything. Meet us at the vault's side entrance.
Got it. I'll go right away.
Onto the real matter.
Surely you've sensed it—a darker force lurks behind both the Order and the Fisalias.
The Fractsidus.
Correct. We Montellis have had some… unpleasant encounters with them. Their motives remain shrouded, yet the Order and the Fisalias clearly benefit from them.
The Montelli family's interest aligns with yours. An uninterrupted Carnevale for you… an unfettered Ragunna for us.
The invitation we sent was meant to be a token of goodwill.
I'd appreciate it if you could return the favor.
Splendid. So we are in the same boat, again.
I must first deliver the evidence you and Ms. Zani collected to my uncle, Mr. Capollo.
He oversees Carnevale affairs and liaises with the Fisalias. I'm sure he'll find the Fractsidus information… most intriguing.
I'm afraid I must take my leave. Please, feel free to explore the vault at your leisure.

Carlotta leads you into Averardo Vault, explaining that her family is aware of the Fractsidus's evil doings and is willing to help. 
She plans to deliver the evidence you've collected to her uncle, Capollo, who will arrange a formal meeting to exchange information about Fractsidus. 
Before the meeting, you take time to explore the vault.
What's today's transaction volume?
It's around 3.7% higher than yesterday. I double-checked it, should be correct.
The Carnevale is really packing this place...
Can't afford to make any mistakes at this point.
Ah, my dear friend, we meet again!
What a coincidence.
You come to deposit?
Haha, indeed, fate has its way of bringing people together.
Ah, of course not. If my pocket was too full, a bank would suffice.
I'm here for a bit of inspiration, that's all.
Again?
Why not? Given that the Carnevale performances always revolve around Order lore, perhaps… a touch of secular themes might be refreshing?
Maybe, a tale of a shrewd moneylender, undone by a trite legal technicality?
Sounds uninspiring.
…Not a believable story.
True, but that's why where some inspiration could be useful.
Is it really why you are here?
Well, I suppose I can't hide it from you. I'm here for the auction, hoping to acquire some rare, ancient manuscripts.
Oh, speaking of scripts! Did you have the chance to read mine? The one with the maiden? Please, I'd love to hear your thoughts.…
The martyrdom of the maiden is quite moving.
There's something more behind the tale.
I haven't read it.
It's the climax of the play. Ha, I'm glad you enjoyed it!
Indeed? You have a discerning eye. My research did unearth some… intriguing rumors, but they didn't find their way into the script.
You see, those stories might be too much for the Carnevale crowd.
Ah... I see. So my script wasn't quite up to par.
Anyway, I appreciate your thoughts... Let's hope I outdo myself with the next one.
Until the Carnevale, traveler from afar.
Good day! Are you here for the Ducat Auction? I'm afraid we've closed entries for today's session. We would be delighted to see you at our next auction though.
The Ducat Auction?
The Ducat Auction is held regularly in the Auction Hall.

Here at Averardo Vault, we pride ourselves on our transparent and fair auctions where only bids matter. We welcome all lawful Ragunna citizens to make their offers. Any item appraised by our agents is eligible for auction.
Be it selling collections or hunting for prized possessions, this is the place to be.
Here's the catalog for our next auction. Please take a look.
If you cannot attend in person, simply use our Terminal service, and our Averardo professionals will handle all your bidding and selling needs.
I'm sorry, Lady Carlotta. I've just confirmed with the office that Mr. Capollo is not in the vault.
I see.
That's quite alright. Please inform me the moment he returns.
Understood.
Is everything okay?
Oh, {PlayerName}. I'm afraid we've hit a slight snag.
I just learned that Uncle Capollo was called away on pressing matters, so we won't be able to see him at the moment.
This does alter our plans, but worry not. I already have some other surprises up my sleeve.
Please come with me. We need more privacy.
{PlayerName}, remember Gilberto?
The noble from the Fisalia family?
Yes, thanks to you and Ms. Zani, he could not escape and is now in our custody.
The family gave him a rather… spirited "welcome." As it happens, his bravado crumbled quite quickly. Once he saw the Niumbus Sanctum restored, he sang like a canary.
Your quick action has secured us vital intelligence.
To put it simply, Gilberto revealed that we have traitors in our family.
Which is not entirely surprising. Our family has always had its cracks. Given the right incentives or pressures, human weaknesses are all too easily exploited.
I'd actually begun to look into this matter before your arrival at the vault.
And now it's confirmed that the traitors are in the vault's <ano=Frequency Modification>tuning</ano> room, doing what they believe to be secretive with the help of the Fractsidus.
Now they probably won't even notice us with their attention fixed on the property room.
I guess that they are desperately destroying any evidence against the Fisalia family and the Order.
That was clever.
Thank you. Right, as for the next move, I have a plan.
There's an alternate passage into the vault leading straight to where they are. We can surprise them when they least expect it.
But I can't manage this alone... I could really use your help.
My pleasure.
Your plan is bold, but practical.
I'm glad I have you with me, {PlayerName}. Please take a moment to prepare, and I'll see you at the entrance.

After waiting for Carlotta for a long time, you search for her and discover she's in trouble—Capollo has vanished. 
In private, she reveals information from Gilberto's interrogation: there are traitors in the family who have been bribed by Fractsidus.
Carlotta requests your help to reach the traitors' hideout deep within the vault via an alternate passage. She hopes to capture and interrogate them to gain more information.
...Everything has been taken care of, Lady Carlotta. Here is the "jewelry" and "perfume" you requested.
Perfect. Thank you, Ms. Zani.
But I have one more task for you, one of utmost importance.
I need you to guard the property room and stop anyone who attempts to break in, whatever it takes—by force if necessary.
…Is someone targeting the evidence?
Relax, it's only a precaution.
Leave it to me. I'll make sure no one touches the evidence.
{PlayerName}, we've implemented a two-tier security system. Once inside, please hold your position until I signal. I'll clear the path for you from above.
Then, you may need to use the Terminal to unlock the path on my side.
Two-tier security system? Could it be…
…Sadly yes, our family built this vault with the foresight of possible betrayal.
Most family members only know how to pass one of the two layers. And alliances forged amid all these locks tend to breed treachery and mistrust.
To enter the vault without being trapped to death, two people must have absolute trust in each other. So... do you trust me, {PlayerName}?
Not really, but we have the same goals.
I trust you.
We are already in the same boat, after all.
Very sensible, but good enough.
Oh, I appreciate your trust. It will not be abused.
Ha, very good. I can work with that.
Now, let's go, {PlayerName}.

Before you enter the alternate passage, Carlotta assigns Zani to create a diversion by drawing attention of the traitors' helpers in the property room. 
With everything in place, you and Carlotta prepare to venture into the depths of Averardo Vault.
Can you hear me, {PlayerName}?
Loud and clear.
Just a moment, I need to access the upper control room to unlock the door on your end.
So, can you figure it out?
Let's try again. The frequency of the Tacet Discords… What a genius idea, but I can't reverse-engineer the frequency it's using.
Seems like the key is not these flowers, but their creator. She must be an insanely powerful Resonator to be able to… shatter and recontruct these frequencies.
Then we'd better speed up. Once their plan succeeds, there won't be another chance like this!
W-who sounded the alarm?
It's me. Most likely by mistake. I apologize for interrupting your work.
La…Lady Carlotta? How… what brings you here?
Oh, nothing, just curious what you are working on, locked away in this tuning room…
The flowers. No doubt they're from the Fractsidus.
Care to defend yourselves? While you still have the chance.
Lady Carlotta, we… we're just following orders.
Following orders, you say? Do you recall the very first "oath" we all took upon joining the family?
None… shall h-harm the family's interests.
And?
Any who defy shall…
Shall be brought to reckoning.
You've appropriated family assets and turned these Echoes into… ticking time bombs.
Once they detonate, the countless efforts and fortunes spent on the Carnevale will all vanish instantly, taking the Montelli's name and future with them.
Lady Carlotta, p-please, we can explain...
What's going on here? Oh, Lady Carlotta…
Just in time. I've found some family traitors. But hold on, I have a few more questions for them.
I will only ask once. Who are you taking orders from?
I only know he's one of the top brass in the family… always using encrypted channels and ordering us to pick up flowers from masked strangers.
How many of these Echoes have you made?
…A lot. The first shipment reached the venue as early as a week ago. They look so identical to regular ones that even we can hardly tell them apart.
Good.
Take them away and scrutinize all their recent transactions, including the source of every last credit. Then handle them as per the family rules.
Yes, ma'am.
I appreciate your help, {PlayerName}.
I knew those <ano=Frequency Specialist>tuners</ano> wouldn't dare do this alone. Someone far more dangerous is pulling the strings.
Using Echoes to disrupt the Carnevale, having family weakness on a silver platter… enemies within are far more deadly than those without.
Their schemes won't prevail. I will not sit idly by and watch them ruin the long-awaited Carnevale.
We're done here. Let the guards take care of the rest. So, Ms. Zani mentioned you heard the Sentinel's oracle when you met the Vitreum Dancer?
Yes. Not directly, but close enough.
The seasoned artisans in our family restored the Vitreum Dancer you retrieved and discovered something fascinating in its records.
Come with me. This might answer your questions.

You and Carlotta reach the tuning room in the depths of the vault and catch the <ano=Frequency Specialist>tuners</ano> tampering with the family's Echoes using Lycoris. 
Intimidated by Carlotta, they confess their betrayal: they altered the Echoes and sent them to the rehearsal venue. 
While the traitors are taken away, Carlotta suspects an even more dangerous traitor is involved. 
To thank you, she offers to take you to the family's Echo Collection Room, where you might uncover connections between the Sentinel and the Vitreum Dancers.
Here we are. The true splendors of Montelli's heritage.
Are these all Echoes in the cases?
Yes, and no. They are Echoes but also the promise of Rinascita's future—and, above all, freedom.
Rinascita may be a fledgling country, but it boasts centuries of history. Its foray into the wider world, however, only began a few years ago.
Don't you find it peculiar? Rinascita, the Land of Echoes… leads the world in Echo technology, yet stands so insular and unadventurous.
What do you suppose is behind all this?
The "Echoes" themselves.
Sharp as always. Rinascita's Common Echoes are bound to Genesis Nexus, making seafaring with them almost impossible.
But their power is essential for dealing with Tacet Discords and other threats at sea. You could say the reliance on Common Echoes has shackled our ambitions to venture beyond our borders.
To break these shackles, the Montelli family has invested in Reserved Terminals. It's not about short-term benefits, but the future for the whole of Ragunna.

The Order has monopolized the use of Common Echoes and kept a tight leash on Reserved Terminals, claiming that individual ownership would sully the sanctity of the Echoes they so fervently preach about.
But you see their real objective, don't you? To keep Rinascita isolated so they can shape its entire narrative.

Don't be so quick to deny it. If you truly never craved acceptance and recognition, would I even exist?
Since praise and affirmation aren't enough for you... I'll give you a chance to prove yourself. Show me how much your sweat and tears are worth!

Carlotta demands that her mirror self reveal the way out. However, this reflection, sharing the same memories, past, and desires, exposes Carlotta's complex emotions—her fear of abandonment, gratitude for her family's protection, and relentless drive to live as their blade, bringing honor to the Montelli name.
Why, then, does she reject the perfect life offered in the mirror?
Frustrated, the mirror self recreates the "stormy night," forcing Carlotta to prove her worth and make up for regrets once more.
Nice work, but this is only the beginning.
You must be dying to know which part of the past this is. Would you like a little hint?
The wind abruptly ceases, leaving Carlotta enveloped in an oppressive, humid stillness tinged with a metallic scent.
As she gazes up at the overcast sky, a haunting memory of that fateful, rain-soaked evening resurfaces, one she had desperately tried to leave behind.
Blood debts will catch up with those who have to pay. The storm is coming...
Ah, now you remember. I knew you'd never forget. The rain that night never ceased in your heart.
Help... Help...
Damn it! This is a trap! They've taken what's ours! In the name of the Montellis, this won't go... unpunished...
Did you hear that? Oh, the panic in their voice! How they must be begging for a capable leader to come and save the day?
Damn it all! You think you could've breached our defenses so quickly without someone backstabbing Padrino?
Blood debts must be paid with blood. We will not let this slide, not while a single Montelli lives!
Thanks, milady… Our men need help... Please, they're in the back…
How did this happen? How much intel do the Fisalias have on us... The West End, our mansion... both under siege...
We can't just sit idly by and let them have their way... What now? We need a plan before it's too late!
Three key areas have been hit one after another: South Second Block, West End dock, and our headquarters.
Intel says the Fisalias are gearing up for another hit on our headquarters. As usual, we can expect the Order to turn a blind eye.
They ambushed Father first, before we did anything to them... It is beyond unforgivable!

We're running out of time. Capollo, we need a plan before Padrino wakes up. Call for reinforcements from the East End. It's risky, but if they don't smell our manpower shortage… we might just make it through.
(No, we shouldn't do that...The Fisalias were keeping an eye on our other territories.)
No, we're not doing that. They can take the West End. Our men will retreat to headquarters.
Why? They're tough, but we're no pushovers either! We earned our turf fair and square. Why should we back down now?
When Padrino eventually wakes, how do you plan to explain that we have let his and the entire family's efforts go to waste?
(But we still risk exposing the location of our headquarters. It's all about predicting their moves... and keeping ours hidden.)
...What about you, Carlotta? What do you think?
(Once again, this deviates from my past experience... Well, I'll point them down the right path this time.)
We'll hit their base.
Our people on the East End, the South Second Block, and the dock will stay put to give the impression we know nothing.
Then we'll send our main forces to where the Fisalias keep their Echoes. The trade routes mean nothing compared to that.
As they know what we value most, we need to demand something of equal worth from them as our bargaining chip.
Is this really going to work?
We can't afford to lose our people. Everything else, even the mansion are simply assets.
I'll cover the rear.

During an attack by Fisalia, Padrino is gravely injured. As senior members like Capollo gather to devise a plan, for the first time, they turn to Carlotta for advice. She seizes the moment to voice what she couldn't on that fateful day, "hit Fisalia's base."
Carlotta proposes evacuating the exposed headquarters while launching an offensive against Fisalia's key locations, volunteering to stay behind and cover the retreat.
Wow, look at you with your brilliant plan. So clever. It could have saved us from our humiliating defeat.
And of course, you didn't just come up with it because you knew what happened... No, that idea has been brewing in your mind since that very day.
How does it feel to finally have your dismissed plan validated?
Back then... No one bothered to ask for your input, did they? The big shots like Capollo and those old timers couldn't care less.
The family ended up making the worst possible choice. They called for reinforcements, depleting resources in both headquarters and the East End.
No, Cynthia! Look at me, please... Why is this happening? The West End... It's all my fault. I should've been more careful...
You're the only family I have left... "The Montelli's motto is Enterprise," huh... But there's no end to this enterprise, no end to the ambition, no end to chasing wealth…
In the end, your dear grandfather had to step in and fix the mess you all made. The plan advanced, but the dead were forever gone. It stands as the greatest tragedy in our family's history.
With that blood debt haunting you, you became the sharpest blade, working harder than ever to protect the family's interests.
And Capollo... Did he think of seeking the Order's protection after that? When it became painfully clear that his power alone couldn't secure his ambitions.
Come to think of it, what's so wrong with that? Sacrifices are inevitable, and someone must bear the burden.
By doing so, the family's interests can be preserved. Is this not the balance you wish to maintain?
You were never meant to make decisions for the family. Do you really have what it takes to reshape the order of things?
No matter what you say, I must... stop him.
Why? Didn't I just show you a better future than what you face now?
Merely an illusion of your making! My choices may have altered the outcome, but it's impossible to prove now.
The past is set in stone. We only have one path before us.
Yes, the cold rain from that night still haunts us. But we cannot be shackled by the past.
I might not be in charge, but my principles are clear. Every action I take is for the benefit of the family.
I must leave here and stop Capollo. Whatever the consequence.
Our negotiations have reached a dead end. Then I'll need to try something else to make you stay.
Hmm... You're unshakable, aren't you? So you've made up your mind already?
How much more do we have to lose?

Reality is completely different—no one listened to Carlotta's opinions that day. The family's wrong decision led to the tragic fall of the headquarters. Duncan lost his last family member, and Padrino was left to hold the family together despite his injuries.
Now, Carlotta's mirror self reveals the harsh truth: she has never been trusted to lead. 
Tempted by an illusory perfect future, Carlotta steels herself against the deception, resolved to stop Capollo.
Her defiance enrages the mirror self, who then traps her in an endless labyrinth.
No, not this way, piccolina. You should try another way...
Choose wisely. You still have a chance to make things right.
Wrong, wrong again... Do you really think you can choose the right path?
Stay, let's get lost in this maze together, from one window to another… I'll keep your company..
Left! You should've gone left! Wait... Or maybe not?
Think it over, I told you before. You should take the easier way out!
Do you truly think you are worthy of the Montelli name?
Just give up... What an embarrassing sight. It's so painful to watch.
You might have another chance up ahead. Don't disappoint us, okay?
Yes, that's right... Keep moving forward, you're getting close.
You have to press ahead. Don't doubt yourself.
Don't you see? This is what happens when you choose the wrong path and back the wrong horse!
The cost... will be far greater than you thought. Why do you always end up on the losing team?
Why are you...
I was worried you might be in danger.
Also, I'm here to deliver this.
The gun was always there. You earned the right to use it the moment you chose to act on your own accord.
Looks like you've made up your mind.
Concerned for Carlotta's safety, you enter the mirror as well and hand her the gun that Francesco entrusted to you.
The Padrino's gun never leaves his side.
You've been entrusted with the authority to act
Now...
Whether it fires, and where it aims...
If he places it within your reach,
it can only mean one thing.
in the name of Montelli.
The choice is mine alone!
I am merely a blade made for killing. Am I really qualified to change the status quo?
Why won't you obey my orders!
I'm getting old. We should take the easier approach.
If we can make other people pay the price...
So...
Why can't you just give in to me and stay here?
H-how dare she eat the tribute...
Prayer alone
Nanny always said
Repurposing decoration into a weapon,
Come with me.
The family will shield you
You will rise to become...
A true Montelli.
In the face of survival,
Who would have thought
This suits a Montelli well.
Offers no salvation.
Creed becomes meaningless.
The food is for tribute,
She's a Montelli after all.
The hall is in chaos,
What a monster!
Defying indoctrination
Her blood runs with the same fierce will as ours.
And open your eyes to a new world.
You're a bad girl...
I'm telling Nanny!
Stop!
Catch her!
it's not for eating!
Yet she clings to her weapon...
To chart the course forward.
How did you let go of confusion and doubt so easily? Those were your true feelings..
You and I... What makes us so different?
{PlayerName}, care for a story?
A story about why a certain girl was adopted.

As Carlotta's mirror self begins to fade, she desperately questions the real Carlotta about what makes them different. 
Carlotta, however, silently walks past her and joins your side, beginning to share the beginning of her story with you.
The choices seem endless, yet you suddenly notice a path that has never been taken—not left, not right, but something entirely different—
<color=yellow>Turn back</color>, back to where <color=yellow>you started</color>, just like rediscovering your original self.
Nice and easy. We're right on track.
...Thanks.
Huh?
Hoo hoo...
Coo coo...
Squeak squeak...
Err... Looks like they were trying to sneak away with the star, but hit the light switch by accident.
Hoo hoo... Hoo hoo!
Coo...
Squeak squeak!
What are they saying?
They're saying, "We're not going down without a fight!"

You venture into the cavern, and Roccia—who is usually calm—shows fear of the dark. With you by her side, she steadies herself. 
Inside, the cavern opens into a wide space where a group of Plushie Echoes are busy at work. 
Could this so-called "Archdemon" really just be a bunch of Plushies?
Golden Fleece, a worn playbook, old instruments...
Are they supposed to be the Archdemon?
Or the Fools hiding from the Tacet Discords?
Hoo hoo...
Coo coo...
Squeak squeak... Squeak squeak...
The Plushies are defeated, but they seem to have something they want to say.
Are these Echoes the Archdemon in the opera?
Oh, no. They're just abandoned Echoes.
They used to have homes and their own masters. They still don't understand why they got kicked out all of a sudden one day.
Even after being abandoned, they never forgot about their masters and managed to find their way home... but their masters were no longer there.

They scoured the whole of Rinascita, refusing to give up and accept the truth... But even now, when they've reached this Land of the Banished, they still couldn't find a single trace of their masters.
Just when they were about to lose hope, they found solace in the emotional frequencies left on personal items.
So they made this place their home. Little by little, they scavenged things to bring the home from their memories to life.
That's how they came across the "star."
Right when the Tacet Discords attacked the ship.
So they just snatched it and ran.
Yes. They're not really the brawling type. The Tacet Discords scare them, so they sneak around, grabbing anything not nailed down while trying not to get caught.
With so many Tacet Discords wandering around the Strand, all they can do is scatter Golden Fleece, spooking the Tacet Discords to give them the chance to sneak out.
They're willing to risk it all to find trinkets to make this place... feel more like home.
Whether you're a person or an Echo, everybody needs a place to call home.
They heard the Pegasus opera from their masters.
That's why they went for the star when they saw it rolling away. They wanted the good, hopeful frequencies it was radiating.
These Echoes knew the star wasn't theirs, but they weren't keen on giving it up, either. So they cooked up all those spooky tricks to scare us away.
Turns out, this maze wasn't hiding an Archdemon or a hero. Just a bunch of Fools.
Fools, huh? Let's welcome them to the Fool's Troupe then.
They want a home? They can join the troupe.
Good idea. Let's bring these Echoes along. Plus we could use some extra help with the opera.
And all this stuff they worked so hard to collect... Let's bring it with us too. It must mean a lot to them.

It turns out the Plushies are abandoned Echoes, and all they want is to reunite with their owners. 
Even after reaching this desolate island, the Plushies couldn’t find their owners. 
Instead, they take comfort in the emotional frequencies lingering on objects and begin piecing together "homes" from these fragments of memory. That’s how they discovered the "star." 
Roccia believes both people and Echoes need a place to return to. You offer to bring the Plushies back to the Fool's Troupe with you.
Squeak squeak... Squeak...
What's wrong?
What's that about?
She says this accordion was from her master.
Even though she hasn't found her master yet, this accordion left her with many fond memories.
"As the mist fades, so shines the star's unbound light—"
Her master used to sing this to lift the spirits of people who had been wronged, and naturally, she picked up the tune.
The misty maze we just went through was her attempt to recreate the opera. She used the misty coastline as a stage, with the help of her Echo friends, of course.
You did a great job.
I guess she was trying her best to protect all her memories with her master.
But protecting your own shouldn't come at the cost of everyone else's memories and hopes.
For anyone who's been hurt, we're probably better off sticking together than dragging each other down, right?

Lottie Lost’s owner used to sing "Pegasus" to inspire those who suffered injustice, and Lottie learned it too. 
The maze you encountered earlier was their attempt to recreate scenes from the play, blending the foggy seaside environment with its imagery.
Pero and I are almost done packing everything up.
Shall we head back, {PlayerName}?
Okay, let's go.
I still need to check around.
All right. Back to the troupe.
Okay. We'll be here when you're ready.
Roccia asks Pero to bring along the Echoes and their items as they all return to the Troupe.
Ack!
The Dragon of Dirge? No, wait.
It's alright. They're just shadows.
Yes. I'm not afraid.
Eek!
It's okay. We're nearly there.
Okay.
"The midnight chime has faded, yet the night endures. Restless hearts long for an understanding that should be ours."
"In the freest place of Ragunna, I await your arrival..." This should be the place Capollo mentioned in his invitation.

"With this invitation, I wish to personally thank you for all you have done for the Montelli family and to amend the slight misstep in your reception. I hope this gesture will help to mend any misunderstandings and strengthen our alliance."
"In the name of the Montellis, I shall honor my allies as I do my own kin and blood."
"In the freest place of Ragunna, I await your arrival... Yours sincerely, Capollo Montelli."
I knew it, another invitation. That's kind of their signature, huh? But this wasn't Carlotta, who's this <color=yellow>Capollo</color> guy?
He's the uncle Carlotta told us about.
He's the owner of that pendant.
Oh, yeah. The big boss of the vault and all that jazz? Guess it won't hurt swinging by Carlotta's family. They do owe us a big one!
I remember now, didn't he get nabbed by the Order?
Then he's got a lot to thank you for. When that sneaky Priest tried to use him as a pawn, things could've gotten messy without you and Carlotta's quick thinking.
I bet he's got something good planned. A pile of money? Maybe a mega feast?
Ugh... hic! I've been feeling pretty weird lately, my head's all wobbly. I might not be able to show right when you need me!
Just get some rest, I can manage.
I'll make sure to eat all the food for you.
Okay, you've got this. If anything happens, just smash your way through!
Alright, alright! No need to rub it in!
Hm, to locate me so precisely and deliver the invitation right into my hands... this Capollo Montelli knows what he's doing.
Anyway, I'll leave this to you then. But hey, if you ever need my help, just give me a shout, okay?

At midnight, you arrive at Liberty Square, responding to an invitation from Carlotta's uncle, Capollo.
Though the invitation seems genuine, you remain wary of his true intentions. You and Abby suspect he has ulterior motives beyond mere gratitude.
Oh, there you are. I noticed you as soon as you walked in.
Care to join me for a drink?
So, will you take this drink?
Don't get me wrong. I've only been here long enough to recognize that drink, but I'm not making any guarantees beyond that.
Hmm, that swagger and flair... You're with the Montelli family, am I right?
I know I'm not the one you came for, but don't dash off just yet. You don't know what I have up my sleeve, you know.
How about you let me prove how reliable I can be for your family? Go on, test me.
Ask about Benett.
Ask about Scarlet Velvet.
Ask about Carlotta.
Tell me the most curious thing you've heard.
Hmm, if you're talking about Benett Montelli, he's right at the heart of the family's latest drama. Word is, he has broken the family's oath.
But one of his greatest moments was recovering a lost shipment with the family's young lady. Isn't life full of ironies?
She may not carry the Montelli name, but she's got that same pioneering spirit. She's leading a team of Resonators now, hunting down Tacet Discords in the wild.
It's a shame though, she recently decided to cut ties with the Montellis. And here I thought they were kindred spirits.
Oh, that name? She's the second Montelli daughter, but she usually goes by another codename—Opal—when on duty.
Er, but you'd better ask the lady next to you yourself. In our line of work, it's considered rude to discuss someone when they're within earshot.
I heard some rumors that the Montellis and the Order might have closer relationship than they're letting on... But I wouldn't bet on it.
When change is coming, you can always sense it in the air. It's hard to pin down at first, but when you do, it's often too late.
For an instant, you feel a gaze from where you got your drink, but it vanishes as soon as you turn to look.
Impressive. You've proved yourself capable.
Three days from now, at this hour, return here and order a "Golden Ears Mambo." Watch for someone wearing a green tourmaline.
But why... why would Bennett betray us?
Maybe, because he was in charge of the vault. Another soul lost to the greed for money...
I still remember the last time I saw him. It was raining, heavily. He gave me his only umbrella with that bright, reassuring smile, told me he was fine, then walked straight into the downpour...
Had he already started stealing the goods and secretly selling them for money then?
Was it really worth it? To betray the family... for money? Was it so tempting that he could abandon the vows he swore and the values he held?
What if... what if there's more to it, though? After all, no one's found the stolen goods yet. Maybe he never sold them...
Don't fool yourself, Adriana. This is the result of a full investigation by Mr. Capollo and the higher-ups at the vault. It's as certain as it gets.
Think about all the other traitors we've caught from the vault. Those tuners. Who'd thought they were hiding their true selves until it was too late?
Does it even matter why he betrayed us?
If Padrino steps down, do you think Mr. Capollo will be our next head? What's your take?
Well, I thought that was already settled, isn't it? Why bring it up now?
Something tells me the next head might be someone else.
Ha, well, if you're so sure, how about you tell me if we can get that special Margherita pie? I hear they're only making thirty of them today.
Hey, you should trust my intuition! It's saved me from the reaper more times than I can count!

But seriously, not long ago they caught another traitor from the vault, and then Benett's betrayal hit... It's no surprise people are starting to question Mr. Capollo's ability to lead. And I heard he hasn't been looking too well lately...
Meanwhile, Lady Carlotta's reputation has been growing. She's helped a lot of people in the family with her actions and words.
True, but you're missing the most important point—the will of Lady Carlotta herself.

You know she's never wanted to put her relationship with Mr. Capollo or Padrino at risk. As an adopted member of the family, she's always felt she doesn't deserve a position like that. But, of course, opinions differ on why she's reluctant to take the role.
But one thing's clear—Lady Carlotta has no interest in becoming the next head. If she did, the family‘s balance would’ve been disrupted a long time ago.
So, for now, just save that intuition of yours for the pie, alright?
If only I were Lady Carlotta! I'd love to have the power to create gems whenever I wanted!
They're so dazzling and mesmerizing. If I were her... actually, just giving me the chance to pick them up would be enough, hehe.
But... don't you know those aren't real gems?
Wait, really? They're not?
Nope. Someone who thought they could make a fortune from those "gems" tried, only to find out that they couldn't even sell them, let alone use them for anything useful.
Those "gems" are actually a medium for deconstruction and reconstruction. They're capable of collapsing and disintegrating the target's frequency they hit before the target vanishes completely.
So they just look like gems. When needed, they can transform into the shape of firearms or bullets.
W-well... what happened to those who actually got their hands on them?
Hard to say. Maybe they ended up as sparkling fragments... Haha.
Any recommendations? Isn't the drink you ordered enough for now?
More wine, more secrets.
I'm a fan of good alcohol. Bring me more!
Well, I was just asking...
Ha, well, whether you're indulging in your desires or giving in to them, I'm here for both.

We've got a menu on the table for newcomers. Maybe you'll find something that catches your eye, or you'd prefer to find someone who shares your taste for a <color=yellow>Scarlet Velvet Ribbon</color> first. What do you think?
Forgive me for not meeting you properly until now.
Guest from the Black Shores, Laureate of the Carnevale, savior and friend of the Montellis... {PlayerName}, your presence is an honor.
Allow me to formally introduce myself. I am Capollo Montelli, Carlotta's uncle, <color=yellow>son of the Padrino</color>, and <color=yellow>the next head of the family</color>.
(Given Capollo's stature, a private meeting at this hour... is it really just about gratitude?)
Why the sudden invite from someone of your rank?
I hope this meeting is as simple as it seems.
Of course, just as stated in the invitation. I'm a man of my word.
Without you, the traitors wouldn't have been captured, and I freed from their hands.
While Carlotta has expressed our family's gratitude, I feel obliged to do it in person.
But unfortunately, the traitors had little to offer, and the one behind them is still in the shadows. Unnerving, isn't it?
Don't worry, Carlotta is on it.
I heard it's someone high up in the family.
Sorry, your family issues aren't my concern.
I'll wait for her findings then.
Hmm... that does narrow down the possibilities.
Be as involved as you like, {PlayerName}. I won't think any less of you.
Things aren't as bright for the Montellis as they may seem. The Order, Fisalias, and the Fractsidus... Any attempt to break the status quo puts us at risk.
The traitors we captured were a warning, but also a reminder—to survive, I must seek alliances beyond the family.
Especially with you, just as Carlotta did.
Thought I was already an ally to the entire family.
Now that you mention it, let me be clear.
Carlotta is dear to me, and nothing will change that.
But she's from the lesser branch of the family. Tradition says I, the rightful heir, should manage dealings with the Black Shores, not her.
Restoring order and benefiting the family as I intended... that's what I meant in the letter by amending a slight misstep.
The leader of the Black Shores must have sent you here with a purpose. Tell me, and I will offer you support far beyond what Carlotta could provide.
I can't give you an answer now.
Support with a high price, I suppose.
The choice is yours, of course... But as the family heir, I will not see my authority undermined, even by those I consider allies.
So if you can't stand by my side, I'd prefer you stay out of the Montellis' affairs.
Otherwise... believe me, you won't want to find yourself at odds with us, no matter how strong you are.
You're welcome to remain an observer from the sidelines. But once you join the table, you play by the rules—my rules.
Well said. But the rules are not set in stone, are they?
What matter of intrigue brought you and {PlayerName} together at this hour, Uncle? A table... are we speaking of a splendid card game, then?
Your timing is most unfortunate. Our little chat just finished.
Pity. I didn't think you'd pull {Male=him;Female=her} aside for a private word, especially after all Rover and I have been through together.
But since you've finished, would you excuse us now?
Carlotta, you stay. I have more to discuss with you.
Meet me at the <color=yellow>rendezvous</color>. Beware the "eyes."
A gun is a powerful tool, but only in the hands of the worthy.
I understand, Uncle. I've never forgotten where my privileges come from, nor will I covet what's not mine.
The Black Shores, the Carnevale... my sole principle is whether they benefit the Montellis.
I will execute any command that strengthens the family, and crush any threats to our standing.
...Very well. Keep your words in mind.
Uncle, about Benett... have you heard?
That family thief stealing from the vault? Why, are you suggesting I failed my duties?
Not at all, I just happened to overhear someone talking about it in passing...
You or Carlotta, what's the difference?

Standing before you is Capollo, Carlotta's uncle, son of the Padrino, and the next head of the Montelli family.
While expressing gratitude for your cooperation, he warns that your deep involvement may destabilize the family's delicate balance and disrupt future plans. Capollo offers to take Carlotta's place as the family's representative in your alliance but makes it clear that, if you decline, you should avoid meddling further in Montelli affairs.
As the tension escalates, Carlotta intervenes, leaving you a cryptic message, "Meet me at the rendezvous. Beware the eyes."
Seeing you off, she brings up the recent betrayal involving Benett, the family's vault manager, who was caught stealing from the vault.
Whether you want to look around or head to that shelter, the choice is yours.
Hey, {PlayerName}. Good to see you again.
It's been a while.
You're looking cheerful today.
Well, I owe that to you and Carlotta. Thanks to your efforts, we've been able to restart our cooperation with the Montelli family, along with others whose ties had been severed.
The Reserved Terminal is still a sensitive subject in public, but at least now, people here are free to explore in the wild and gather Echoes as they please.

Honestly, I was shocked when Carlotta asked if I'd be interested in joining your plan. I never imagined you'd outmaneuver the Order and strike a deal with Capollo, forcing him to hand over the core data module.
But in hindsight, trusting you, Carlotta... and Benett's judgment turned out to be the right decision.
Capollo's been removed and dealt with by the family. Carlotta's busy managing the aftermath alongside Padrino while also focusing on charting a new sea route.
A new sea route? Where to?
Looks like Montelli's ambitions are growing.
The exact route hasn't been finalized yet, but it's rumored to span three or four countries.

Carlotta told me it was your brilliance that made this possible. Your performance at the Carnevale was so inspiring that more and more people are rallying behind Montelli, eager to explore a bigger, grander world.
We're still figuring out what ventures to take on and what we truly want to achieve. This time, I'm determined to make the right call too.
{PlayerName}, just sit tight—we'll bring you some good news soon!
Do you think someone will find out what we're doing?
That's the sixth time you've asked in three minutes. Just breathe and calm down. No one's going to find out.
But… this is the Order we're dealing with, and it's strictly forbidden by Padrino.
Exactly, which is why we just need to ensure Padrino doesn't find out. Once the deal's done, it'll all be behind us.
Besides, Capollo is Padrino's own son. Following his lead is bound to benefit us in the long run.
I know, but still…
What's the use of worrying now? Everyone involved knew the risks going in.
It's almost time, but why did the Order suddenly change the location and schedule?
This isn't just any ordinary deal. The Order is notoriously cautious, always looking over their shoulder. They were probably worried about a leak.
The Montelli member before you is deeply immersed in his work of safeguarding, observing every movement around him. He impatiently waves at you, signaling that he has no time to deal with you.
You decide to check other areas of the trading venue.
The Montelli member before you stares blankly at the entrace. A flicker of hesitation and conflict flashes across his eyes, and his finger unconsciously tap lightly.
It's clear that this Montelli member, caught in his own emotional turmoil, won't give you any further response. You decide to check other areas of the trading venue.
Stop messing around.
The deal hasn't started yet. Get back to your post.
Once this is over, I'm getting myself a new codename.
A new codename? Why? I thought the one you have now suits you.
Why you suddenly want to change your codename? Did you get yourself into trouble?
Trouble? In our line of work, trouble is part of the package. Look at this mess…
*curses* Why is this city such a nightmare? Problems everywhere! Seriously, who cares about the Order or Fisalia?
Anyway, I'm not retiring yet, but I'm burned out. A new codename and a new environment might give me a fresh perspective and keep my passion for my career.
Ah, I see. Sounds like someone's having a midlife crisis. By the way, if you're changing your codename, I'll change mine too. Let's make it a team effort.
What?! I'm not having a midlife crisis!
Sure, sure. Oh, and I hear Septimont is short on people. Maybe we could...
Coming up with new codenames is tough. I'll leave that part to you.
Oh no, look at the time... Sorry, but I've gotta head home for dinner.
Seriously? Come on, don't be a buzzkill. Your mom's not gonna lose it if you eat out just once.

Maybe not, but she made it clear: no matter what I'm up to, I have to be home for dinner every weekend. If I don't, she'll "break my legs with a spatula and stuff my head into a bowl of spaghetti." Her words, not mine.
By the Sentinel, Gustavo, a Montelli, scared of his mommy! How interesting!
Hey, watch it! I'm not scared of her—I'm respecting her. Family comes first, always. No matter what.
Returning here once again, you finally understand the deeper meaning that Francesco had not directly stated that day.
"They say in art, we glimpse pieces of our own soul... True artistry lies not only in what is painted, but in what is left unsaid."
Glory in Decay is the name of the painting, as well as the motto this elder man has gifted to himself—he feels honored by his own exit.
Passing by Benett's former residence, you discover a bouquet quietly placed at the door.
Looking at the bouquet, with the signature "DC," you almost instantly realize who is mourning Benett—Duncan, the man who had chosen to leave, yet still returns for his dear friend.

He helped deliver the false message about the schedule and location change to the Order and helped you successfully infiltrate the trading venue... In your and Carlotta's plan, he was an important piece.
Now, for his own safety, he must temporarily leave under Carlotta's arrangement.
But no matter when, no matter in what indentity, as long as he chooses to return, Ragunna and Montelli will always welcome him with open arms.
"The rain poured relentlessly, cloaking the world in a shroud of gloom, stripping away its pretense of grandeur to reveal its barren core."

"Under the storm's shadow, people were fighting at each other's throats—fragile yet ferocious, like... like beasts cornered in a cage." No, no, Tornatore, that's far too trite! Think, man! You can craft something better!
You're the playwright of this drama. Give it an ending that lingers, and echo that won't fade!
"As she fell, her trembling hand raised the gun. The old acquiantance, a traitor to his ideals, stared down the barrel. One last shot. Addio." Hmm, does that come across too... passive?

Ah, I see. Rumors, ripe and waiting, a wellspring of inspiration at my fingertips. Let's see... "Can I really trust {Male=him;Female=her}? She wondered. Yet instinct urged her forward. She clasped {Male=his;Female=her} hand firmly, then turned her back, offering it wholly to her new companion." Yes, yes, that has promise!
The creator in front of you is completely consumed by the tale of storm and betrayal he's spinning. Perhaps it's best to let him remain in his trance.
Kirsch, whiskey... and cherry tomatoes? Does it mean revenge?
Hmm, blood orange, gin... that drink you have there is quite rare. Would you mind telling me what it means?
You will know it when you need to.
It's a secret too terrifying to speak of...
Ah, a riddle cloaked in mystery! You don't want to share, hm? Ha... Sorry... I am simply enthralled by symbols and codes.
Wait, wait! Maybe I'm not ready for this. Ah, forget it. I don't want to know!
Imperator above! I am but a humble man obsessed with the secret "code" of drinks! I shan't risk my neck over this...
What grand schemes occupy your time?
Uh, I-I've been exploring how drinks might encode numerical values, through alcohol content or vintage, perhaps. But lately I'm starting to wonder if the drink itself even matters.
The key to any language lies in the shared rules and agreements between both parties.
With that in mind, the same drink, or even the same object, can be given countless meanings… much like how my people and I sometimes improvise codes with whatever's available.
For an instant, you feel a gaze from where you got your drink, but it vanishes as soon as you turn to look.
Sounds like you've been at this "code" research for quite some time. Mind if I ask you a question?
Do you know when the bartender started his shift today?
(Is Carlotta suspecting the bartender?)
Let me see... I got here quite early, and he was here about the same time. Probably around eight o'clock in the morning?
Thank you. That's all I needed.
Anything else I can get you? Or is there a problem with the drinks?
No, it's you we have a problem with.
No, we are here for you.
As expected from a Scarlet Velvet informant, you are smart. In a place like this, a bartender is the perfect cover, the least noticeable but with the best view.
You mix every drink and pass every "code." You might not understand all of them, but nothing of importance ever escapes you.
So, this Scarlet Velvet Ribbon... is meant for you. Am I correct, sir?
Well, well... it finds its way back to me at last. A drink of trouble, I'd call it.
Contact has been made, and by the rules, a conversation should follow. But Scarlet Velvet has decided there will be no further dealings with the Montellis.
The partnership is broken, and whatever bond you had is all but gone. If you do meet up, Lady Carlotta, aren't you afraid things might turn ugly?
There's no need to fight when we can talk.
We're here to solve problems.
It's rumored that Scarlet Velvet's decision to end our partnership has something to do with a vault keeper named Benett.
Surely you don't believe that nonsense?
Then what is the truth? Benett was recently found dead in the wild... The dead are silent, but you are not. So let's talk.
Wait, Benett is dead?
So there was a connection after all.
Seems like the news hasn't reached you.
That complicates things, I'm afraid.
I'm not sure if trusting Montelli is a wise choice, but in memory of Benett... If you truly are as noble as he believed...
Go to Whisperwind Haven after dusk. I will inform Scarlet Velvet.

You and Carlotta quickly deduce that the bartender is the contact for Scarlet Velvet. Though he may not understand all of the cryptic messages, nothing of importance escapes him. While the bartender is not optimistic about your meeting with Scarlet Velvet, he doesn't stop you as you followed the rules and found him. It also seems that he has heard of Carlotta's character from Benett. Therefore, he promises to arrange a meeting for you with Scarlet Velvet at Whisperwind Haven at dask.
Benett... where could I dig up more of your secrets?
Oh, it's you. What happened? Need my help?
About that rainy night...
About you and Benett...
What's your plan?
That's it for now.
Ask about something else.
Everyone's got things they'd rather not share. For me, it's that rainy night. Not now, not with you. All I'll say is that the night was bitter cold, and the rain—merciless.
Rain like that reeks of rust. It poured down in torrents, smothering cries for help. Convictions we thought unshakable blurred like ink on waterlogged parchment.
Ask about something else.
Ha, it's just a cheesy story.
Benett and I—we were partners. Missions, mischief, even a dog we shared. We knew each other's families. It's the kind of story you hear about anyone who's faced life and death together.
If our roles were reversed, he'd have done the same for me without a second thought.
I'm old, but I've still got a few strings to pull.
Whether it's a casual contact from years ago or the family's next head, I've got to try my luck.
Ask about something else.
Ask about something else.
Terminals are divine artifacts from the Sentinel, brought to Rinascita by the first Primus.
What you possessed were nothing but privately made replicas, existing solely by the grace of the Primus. How dare you defy our cleansing of such blasphemy!
We never stopped asking the Order for permission to wear the Terminals, but every single request is denied. You won't even tell us why!
You've controlled the Terminal supply, and the family stopped trading with us... These are all we have left. Why should we hand them over?
I can sense your fervent desire for the artifacts and the blessings from the Sentinel... But whether you are worthy of the terminals is for the Order to decide.
If you willingly part with your wealth in devotion to the Order's divine cause, the door to forgiveness might still be open.
But should you persist in your defiance... we'll have to escort you to the Penitentiary for judgment.
People are quarreling there.
The Order and the commoners... it must be Scarlet Velvet causing the stir.
The Order's arrogance is known, but such blatant actions... Is it because we're far from the heart of the city?
Let's first address their troubles, and then we'll have a proper talk.
Ah, the Montelli's second daughter and this year's Laureate. I suggest you tread carefully and avoid crossing the Order and the Sentinel, especially not for the sake of mere commoners.
Must I remind you again? Trading Reserved Terminals is a breach of the discipline.
I didn't see anyone trading Terminals here.
All I see is you taking what's rightfully theirs.
We paid good money for these. If you're taking them, you owe us a refund.

Yet the very <color=yellow>traders</color> who took your money have seen the error of their ways and reported your dealings. They have sworn to repent for their illicit production and cease all trade with you.
(Illicit production, traders... Is he talking about the Montellis?)
How sad, Ms. Carlotta. Such loyalty to your family, only to be left in the dark. No one bothered to inform you, did they?
Oh, please. My ties with the family are not so fragile as to be shaken by mere words.
The fact that we are having this conversation at all means that you cannot ignore my status, wouldn't you agree?
The Sentinel and the Primus have declared free trade as our undeniable right. Scarlet Velvet is always entitled to trade as they please, regardless of their previous partnerships.
You preach the doctrine, yet fail to adhere to it yourself. If I were you, I'd be on my way to the Penitentiary. Willful transgression... is the worst blasphemy one can imagine.
Mark my words! The day Montelli is brought to its knees by the Order and Fisalia will be the day you beg for the Sentinel's mercy.
When that day comes, all shall be under the Order's control. And it will not be long in coming.
The Acolyte departs with his entourage. Scarlet Velvet signals the others to leave and assess the damages.
Ernesto, the bartender, said you needed to see me.
You may have just defended us, but you heard it—your family has left us in a mess. Frankly, I don't see the point in having this conversation.
But since Ernesto said it's about Benett, I'll give you a minute, for his sake. Speak quickly.
What you heard could be another lie from the Order.
What if the Order is trying to turn us against each other?
Regardless of the bigger picture, your side ended the deal. We were informed on short notice to stop all trade.
And it's not just the Terminals—no more "jewelry," "perfumes," and all that nonsense. You saw what happened today.
Not to mention I haven't seen a Montelli for nearly two weeks.
Where were you when we were fighting against the Order and the Fisalias?
Montelli has been dealing with its own troubles lately.
There was a slight issue of a traitor in the vault, so our hands were tied.
You sure don't beat around the bush.
A direct approach works best at times. Actually, what that Acolyte claimed is news to me. Surrendering control and ceasing trade... are not in the Montelli's vocabulary.
The Montelli creed has always been family first, and a pioneering spirit second.
With your grandfather, maybe, but he won't be around forever. When Capollo takes the helm... you won't have a say.
The real question is whether we can get our trade back on track. Can your family still be trusted? What I need is a solid promise from someone in charge—can you do that?
One thing's for sure, I don't want to see the family who first broke the monopoly to trade with us commoners end up defending it.
I'll speak with my uncle and grandfather to see what happened with our cooperation.
You know what? This is supposed to be your family's business. Why am I saying this to you... Excuse my earlier words.
So... Ernesto told me Benett's gone. What happened? He seemed fine the last time we met.
Some say he got what he deserved for stealing from the vault.
And there are rumors that you helped him fence the stolen items.
Of course, we think there's more to the story.
Good judgment there! The rumors are nonsense… Fencing stolen goods? Please. Benett used to handle our shipments for the vault, but everything was above board.
Come to think of it, he did stay there for a while the last time we saw him. Asked us to stash something too. What was it he said… "Hope we don't need to use it."
It seems Benett may have anticipated the trouble ahead.
There's <color=yellow>an entrance along the coast</color>. Go straight down the road and you will see it. What's your business there, anyway?
(So Benett left something behind on purpose...)
Nothing shady, okay? He knew his stuff—never took advantage of us, never budged on prices either.

For him, it was always business first, friendship second. When he was running late, he'd stay up that <color=yellow>hill</color> sometimes. We even set up a shelter there after it happened a few times. That's all.
I wonder if you might show us to the shelter? We'd be most grateful.
To test our hypothesis and see if there's anything of importance hidden.

Realizing that retrieving the Reserved Terminal is impossible, the Acolytes attempt to further sever the relationship between Scarlet Velvet and Montelli before departing.
According to Scarlet Velvet, it is not her group that severed ties but Montelli themselves. The family revoked their rights to purchase Reserved Terminals and weapons, as well as their protection. This revelation surprises Carlotta, as it contradicts Montelli's philosophy of proactive expansion. She asserts her stance to resume trading and assure that Montelli, which once broke the monopoly, will never become a supporter of it.
Regarding Benett, Scarlet Velvet denies the possibility of him stealing from the vault and reveals that Benett foresaw his own death, leaving something behind at the coast, hoping it would never come into handy.
You share the clues and items you found with Carlotta.
...Something is strange here.
There seems to be a connection here.
"Thy eyes guide my course in the tempest," the woman in the painting here seems to stand in the gloomy rain, but her eyes remain bright.
This line refers to the letters ML and CL in the eyes.
Like the secret "code" in drinks, what matters is never the objects themselves, but the shared rules and agreements between both parties.
Now, the book. It appears to be about winter, which is likely related to the second line, forty winters...
Forty winters... try page 40.
You flip the book to page forty, and there, written in large numbers, are 1, 9, and 0.
The last one is a rotor device, the planet...
Revolves right twice and a half.
You and Carlotta rotate the device two and a half times to the right. With a click, a slip of paper pops out, showing numbers 4, 6, and 8.
<color=yellow>MLCL190468</color>? That format—It's a vault storage code.
Of course it is. Benett was a vault keeper. But what was he trying to convey in such a cryptic manner?
<color=yellow>Four letters</color>... the highest clearance level in the vault. Could it be...
Carlotta? Uh... you asked me to keep an eye out for Benett's Terminal. Well, I've found it.
Amazing. Where did you find it?
That's for me to know and you to wonder.
But... it was not in good shape after what it went through. If you can use it at all, the data and records inside might need to be recovered.
Understood. I'll have someone pick it up for restoration.
Wait, wait... n-now? You're not even... gonna check?
Why are you stuttering?
Isn't it a good thing that we've found the Terminal?
Oh, it's nothing, really. Just worried it might be too tricky to repair.
Alright, we'll inform you when there's more to share.
What now, shall we go get that Terminal?
We're returning to the Montelli Quarter first. The Terminal will be fixed there. As for the codes, we'll figure it out once we arrive...
{PlayerName}, you might not know this, but Benett was never granted the highest clearance in the vault.
Isn't that a good sign? It means Benett might not be guilty after all, just as you suspected.
But it's replaced by another suspicion, one I am reluctant to entertain but am... forced to consider.
Only <color=yellow>Grandfather, Uncle, and I</color> have the highest clearance.
Liberty Square, our proximity, the vault's security clearance, a traitor among the top brass... the indifference toward the stolen goods, and the authority to end dealings with Scarlet Velvet...
There's someone all evidence points to... Were I to entertain it... it all starts to makes sense. Uncle...
Now, all that remains is to see what the code reveals. It might clear our doubts... or confirm it.
There's only one way to find out.
Whether it will clear our doubts or confirm it...
I'll be with you no matter what. So let's see where this leads.
Hold on.
But if it was truly him—the heir to our family—who betrayed us, wouldn't that be utterly absurd?
These items aren't exactly rare, but they're not everyday objects either. They seem out of place here. Looks like Benett left them deliberately.
Indeed. But what I find strange is... these items, don't they seem familiar?
Do you recall those three lines from the anthology? The ones Benett sent to me in the photo?
Or see what item the code represents?

Deciphering the wine code, you and Carlotta piece together the cryptic message Benett sent on the night of his death. The message points to a collection requiring the highest level of authority in the vault. At the same time, you also receive good news from Duncan—he successfully retrieved Benett's Terminal, though it is severely damaged and requires repair. 
A chilling possibility begins to form in Carlotta's mind: all the suspicious details seem to be pointing to Capollo. To uncover the true traitor, you need to return to Montelli headquarters, repair the terminal, and locate the collection indicated by Benett.
You can tell someone was here, look at the mess. Perhaps Benett deliberately arranged it this way as a cover.
We'll each use our sensors to search, then let's gather and analyze the clues we find.
It's so quiet here... It seems like nobody has set foot in here ever since Benett left.
Stay vigilant, {PlayerName}. We're in the wilderness, and anything could happen while we investigate. Promise me you'll take care—I don't want to have to worry about you.
