You notice a slightly faded oil painting. The woman in it wears a serene and enigmatic smile.
As you look closer, you see the pencil marks of the letters "ML" and "CL" in the woman's eyes.
You come across a tattered book. As you flip through it, nothing seems out of place.
Maybe this is what Benett left. You decide to take the book and inspect it later with Carlotta.
You spot a small, delicate rotor device, but you have no idea how to open it.
You decide to take the device and inspect it later with Carlotta.
My people just reported some initial progress on the Terminal repair.
Let's go. Our meet-up spot is right up ahead.
Lady Carlotta, we received a Terminal addressed to you, signed <color=yellow>"DC."</color>
("DC"... It's from Duncan.)

The initial restoration is almost complete, but some data is <color=yellow>overwritten</color> or <color=yellow>isolated</color> due to the extensive damage... We were only able to recover certain sections.
Our evaluation suggests that a full restoration might not be worth it. But if you insist, <color=yellow>Mr. Pierre</color> at the headquarters is an expert in this field.
Good, make sure to contact him. Now, please project the restored sections.
Absolutely, one moment.
Carlotta's agent takes out the damaged Terminal and projects the restored data before she leaves.

As you and Carlotta review the projected data, you notice a pattern of movements between Margherita's, Benett's home, and the vault with only two deviations—<color=yellow>Liberty Square</color> and <color=yellow>a dock</color>.
Liberty Square... I was there not long ago.
Yes, that's where I was investigating that night. Seems like the intel was right—Benett did go there.
And the other location... I think it's my uncle's private dock, primarily used for storage, not shipments.
Capollo again? That does sound fishy.
Should we head over after this?
Hmm, reviewing the records hardly proves the connections between these locations.
If time permits, we should take the Terminal to Mr. Pierre. He is an old friend of Grandfather's, and is an expert in this field.
There may be <color=yellow>other useful information</color> in the Terminal.
But first, let's put that code to use. It could help us narrow down the range and provide better clues.
Follow me. This is why I suggested we return here. Our vault holds everything—family property, valuable items for trade, and prized possessions entrusted to us by clients...
...The complete inventory and access records can only be found here, accessible to those with the proper clearance.

Benett's Terminal is severely damaged, so only basic data are restored. The recovered data shows  Benett's movements, and you notice two suspicious coordinates: one points to the Liberty Square that Carlotta previously investigated, and the other is Capollo's private dock.

What seemed to be an unremarkable ornament blending into the Quarter turns out to play a crucial role. After navigating multiple codes and biometric authentications, a holographic screen finally appears before you.
(Carlotta warned me about eyes... So she probably wants me to avoid unnecessary attention.)
(Not sure why, but staying under the radar is never a bad idea.)
Someone extracted the core data module... It's empty now.

This must be what Benett was trying to tell us before he died. Someone with access to the vault has broken their oath and leaked the data module. Now, only Uncle, Grandfather, and I have the clearance to retrieve it.
So that clears up all the questions.
I see. But what can he gain from it?
In Rinascita, the Order maintains control over Terminals, unlike other countries where they are freely traded. My grandfather learned to modify them during his early ventures in the New Federation.

Our lantern-type Terminal is a modified model. It may look purely ornamental, but it houses the tech modules we've developed. As Scarlet Velvet said, aside from our art dealings, we've been supplying these Terminals to Resonators at fair prices as part of our discreet business.
By doing so, we've broken the Order's monopoly. We've given more people the means to protect themselves in their ventures, giving them choices they didn't have before.
As a result, no family member would ever divulge our Terminal secrets, much less allow the modules to fall into the wrong hands. What exactly are you planning, Uncle?
No, we must find the core module...
Carlotta, where are you?
Uncle, may I ask you something first? Before the Carnevale, the Priest showed me your pendant. How did he come by it, and what led to your capture?
Does it matter? All you need to know is that it's handled, and I'm in the clear now.
Were you mistreated? Did they coerce you into doing something against your will?
Heed my words. Whatever you've uncovered, put it behind you, and all will be as it was. No grudges, no consequences, only family.
Now, we've had some trouble with a shipment over at Septimont. As the rightful heir, I'm giving you a new order. Take care of it, and I'll pretend none of this ever happened.
I refuse.
Excuse me?
I said I refuse! I can't act as if nothing happened. I won't let a family member die unjustly, or see our modules fall into the wrong hands.
Don't trouble yourself with the module. Yes, our family's ambition has led us far, but it's exacted a price paid in blood and tears. What harm is there in choosing the safer, easier path?
I can't believe you just said that. So, you're refusing to tell the truth and reveal the module's location, is that it?
Why do you insist on tearing everything apart? Have you ever thought about what Padrino would say? What others will think of us? I've given you an out, all you need to do is accept it.
Then so be it.
Your course is set. As is mine. But mark my words... I will stop you, Mr. Capollo.
I'm sorry you have to see this side of our family.
It's okay to be a little less perfect with friends.
Well, wallowing in emotion won't solve anything. Our priority now is to recover the data module. Every moment it's missing puts our family at greater risk.
We need to adjust our strategy. My conversation with Capollo will have alerted him. He's likely to move the module sooner than expected. I need to inspect the dock for any clues.
The Order is aware of our discreet business, but they turn a blind eye as long as we don't openly challenge their authority. The hefty taxes we pay maintain this... delicate understanding.
It's messy, but still manageable.
Really? I just wish... No, I did promise I'd try to drop the pretense with you.
I may need more time to come to terms with all this. I don't regret uncovering the truth and exposing the traitor… I'm just saddened that my uncle is the one behind it all.
We were meant to be the guardians of our family's ideals, to carry the torch forward. And yet, now…
The core module is difficult to carry around. They must have hidden it... The dock Benett visited, used for storage... Could it be there?
We may restore more data in this Terminal.
There could still be other possibilities.
Indeed, but time is not on our side. If Capollo acts on this, I might lose my window to secure the module. Our sole advantage now is that we're operating as a pair.
I need you to take this terminal to <color=yellow>Pierre</color> at the bank. If the dock turns out to be a dead end, we will need other leads.
What's your next move if we find the module?
I know that securing the module alone won't suffice. I must uncover Capollo's true motives...how it will affect our family. I'll figure it out, I promise.
According to the plan, you and Carlotta part ways. She heads alone to the dock she mentioned.

The collection the message points to turns out to be the family's custom-made Reserved Terminal, and all clues suggest that Capollo was the one who removed the core data module from the Terminal, and Benett was framed for embezzlement.
During communication, Carlotta rejects Capollo's proposal to move past the matter, unable to ignore Benett's death and the hidden threats within the family.
Time is pressing, so Carlotta quickly decides to split up, with you taking Benett's Terminal to an expert named Pierre for a thorough repair, while she heads to Capollo's private dock to find out more clues or retrieve the missing core data module.
(I'm more entangled in the Montelli family's schemes than I ever realized. When I went after the traitors... No, when I decided to help with the Carnevale, the game was already in play.)
They call it a dock, but no ships ever come. Uncle has concealed what he took from the vault here—a secluded place entirely under his control.
For a secret trove of such value, the lack of security is strange. There was little resistance on my way here. This can't be right.
Wait, I sense an energy fluctuation nearby... Time to investigate. The size of this place is manageable. I should be able to trace the source quickly.
You track the energy fluctuation, sifting through the gaps between stashed goods and looking for its source.
A storage box catches your eye. Inside, a stunning handicraft adorned with jewels sits in stillness. It's exquisite, but not what you seek.
You trace the energy fluctuation to the piled goods and start looking for its source.
On the left, a delicate aroma of wine fills the air as you spot bottles of golden osmanthus wine. To the right, carefully folded custom-made clothes catch your eye with their luxurious fabrics.
But none of them are the data module you seek, nor do they seem connected to the mysterious energy fluctuation.
(Nothing so far... Was I wrong? Maybe this place doesn't hold what we were looking for? Why did Benett come here, then?)
(Or am I too late... Did Capollo get here first?)
(And the energy fluctuation... it was going off and on... No, I couldn't have been imagining it.)
(Such a big mirror... Why is it here?)
(It doesn't seem to be made of common glass, but some kind of crystallized energy... Oh.)
(Will I find the data module on the other side...)
(Or was all this just a trap...)

Carlotta arrives at the dock as planned. Following a strange energy fluctuation, she finds a stained-glass mirror buried under cargo. At that moment, a hand adorned with a blue-black ornament suddenly reaches out from the mirror, pulling her inside—the coordinates are a trap in disguise.
Hello again.
Hello again, Carlotta's grandfather.
You must be Francesco, the current head of the Montelli family.
Should I call you Padrino like the rest do?
It would be my honor if you do.
You don't seem very surprised to learn who I am.
Carlotta told me Mr. Pierre always follows her grandfather around. My instincts weren't wrong when I saw you together.
It also explains why you seemed familiar when we first met.
Was our previous meeting really a coincidence?
What's the term for it... A destined encounter? The universe brought us together, and I happened to take the initiative. It's almost poetic, wouldn't you agree?
That's it, I doubt you want more chit-chat. I know you're here for that Terminal.
Let Pierre inspect it for you and we can resume our conversation.
You knew I was coming.
And you knew why I'm here.
Remember that painting we discussed earlier?
In a fragile equilibrium, the smaller piece is forced to repress its true nature. It's confined to a seemingly flawless structure, stripped of its autonomy. I don't want the same fate for her.
But I can't simply impose my path upon her, expecting blind obedience. She must find her own path, with a partner she can fully trust.
As for those who betray their own blood, there will be no leniency. Even my own son is not exempt from this.
However, before I intervene, I want to see her plan take shape. My hand should only be played as a final measure.
The old give way to the new, that is the way of the world. But for us Montellis, the courage to break from the past matters far more than clinging to it.
So, I ask you this favor. When the time is right, give this to her. She will need it.
It's a little tricky... but you're lucky to have my expertise!
This Terminal is defunct, but I've retrieved all its data, even the overwritten and isolated bits.
You mean, data was erased from it?
The Terminal has been tampered with, but nothing was intentionally erased. It seems they wanted to overwrite the data to avoid detection.
I can show you. Do you have a Terminal? I'll send over the data so you can see for yourself.
These records...
I assume you've taken care of Benett's body?
We... dumped him in the Tacet Discord zone overnight. We'll claim he was killed by those monsters tomorrow morning.
Sir... are you sure? Are we really going to work with the Order... after they made you kill one of our own?
We're in too deep now. Handing over the data module to the Order will cement out position as an ally of the authorities. We'll replace the Fisalias! The other Resonators in the city are irrelevant.
And Benett... I would have taken care of him regardless.
He knew too much. He deserved it for pursuing the Scarlet Velvet matter. Anyone who gets in my way shall meet the same fate.
Y-Yes, sir...
Unbelievable. What is Capollo even thinking? Killing one of our own... It's a complete betrayal of our family! I must record all this madness with something...
My Terminal? No, it's too risky. Wait... I have Benett's body... Nobody's going to pay attention to a dead man's Terminal.
I'll record it, then overwrite with new data.... I have to keep this record well... In case I also...
We all stood together on that stormy night, each one of us losing someone dear. And we all share the desire for our family to find an easier path forward.
The best way to avoid sacrifice isn't fighting, but aligning ourselves with superior powers and knowing when to yield.
You may have left the family, and I should expect no more favors from you. But I ask this of you one last time. Please, put this Terminal in Carlotta's hands.
What's in it? Carlotta.. What will happen to her?
Nothing, save for the standard location tracking data every Terminal holds.
In three days, I'll be negotiating on behalf of the family with the Order. I just want to make sure Carlotta doesn't interfere in the meantime. She'll be given a chance to join our side, I promise.
Think about Benett. If you take care of this, I will overlook what he stole and let it be a thing of the past. I know you care more about your late friend than you're willing to admit.
That Terminal... It was part of Capollo's schemes!
They set a trap in the docks...
Carlotta... Tsk, I can't reach her now.
I must go check on her immediately.
A trap? Wait, sir... Wouldn't Lady Carlotta be in danger? I don't think that is part of your plan. Are you really letting her face this by herself?
She's already there, so why bother? I trust Carlotta and our esteemed guest. It is a trap, but also an opportunity for her to mature.

Standing beside Pierre is the elderly man you once saw admiring the painting—Francesco, the current head of the Montelli family, also known as "Padrino." His words are not just about the painting but also about Carlotta. Rather than relying on his own plan, he hopes that Carlotta and her companions can offer their own solution.
Then he entrusts you with a crucial item to be given to her at the right time.
After fully restoring the Terminal, you uncover hidden data—it turns out that Capollo deliberately handed this Terminal to Duncan to lure Carlotta into the trap at the dock.
With Carlotta now missing, you must rush to the location to save her.
W-what is that...
The family will shield you
In the meantime, Carlotta is seeing fragments of her past in a mysterious space.
(Carlotta's not here yet. Guess I'll have to wait.)
(Whoever was following me seems to have left.)
(Is he one of them?)
(There's something distinctive about his attire and demeanor...)
Might I trouble you for a light, young {Male=man;Female=lady}?
Sorry, I don't have one.
Ah well, a cigar without smoke... My granddaughter told me Ragunna's rain is a bad omen. Can't argue with that now, can I?
(Is he here by accident or design?)
(I can sound him out a bit.)
You've been looking at this painting for a while. Anything special about it?
Oh, did it capture your interest as well? Or are you simply passing the time until the rain ends?
Just happened to see you studying the painting.
You could say I'm waiting.
Haha, it's only the investor's nature in me. I find myself irresistibly drawn to items of unique value.
(So he's an art investor...)
Then it seems you will have to put up with me for a while.
(So he's waiting out the rain...)
The Montelli family prides themselves on their eclectic taste in art. Any style by any artist can find its home within their quarter.
Art knows no boundaries of time, place, or the mind. Here we stand, united by the rain, drawn to the same painting.
They say in art, we glimpse pieces of our own soul.
What do you make of this piece? Care to share your thoughts?
You step closer to study the collage.
Small, irregular shapes nest within larger circles, their edges melding together to form a delicate harmony.
This balance, however, feels precarious, as if two opposing forces are on the verge of collision.
The large circle completes itself by absorbing the small pieces.
It's too abstract for me.
Maybe the artist is seeking some kind of change.
You have keener eyes than I expected. Seeing essence beneath the surface.
Hahaha, it is typical of symbolism to conceal ideas in a play of colors and forms... But sometimes, simplicity is more powerful.
Indeed. True artistry lies not only in what is painted, but in what is left unsaid.
I share the same view, except that I'm somehow saddened by the part that forsakes its character to achieve balance.
...Perhaps chosen by the artist for its uniqueness.
Now is not the time to cling to the existing balance, but to embrace the unknown, seek change, and carve out one's path... just as she once did.
Seek change? You mean this painting?

You arrive at the rendezvous before Carlotta and notice Montelli members, dressed in the family's attire, quietly departing one by one. Left behind is an elderly man who is appreciating a painting.
When you approach, he reveals himself as an art-loving investor, simply waiting for the rain to stop. 
He explains that now is not the time to cling to the existing balance, but to embrace the unknown and seek change... You feel there is a deeper meaning behind his thoughts on the painting.
"Glory in Decay," the impressionist Pasoli's latest piece... Didn't know you had such refined taste.
I was discussing it with an old gentleman.
He left soon after the rain stopped.
I dodged those pesky "eyes" the whole way here, worried you'd been kept waiting too long. But it seems you've kept yourself entertained.
So the old gentleman was simply hiding from the rain, was he? I see... The Montelli Quarter does attract art enthusiasts. Anyway, I'm glad prying eyes didn't follow.
When it rains in Ragunna, surprises are as common as puddles. A delay is only a small splash.
Calling you here with little explanation and a word of caution... I can only imagine your confusion.
It's taken me by surprise.
You and your uncle both...
The Montellis enjoy their intrigue, don't they?
The Montelli's path is not always paved with roses, but with thorns as well. As the heir apparent, my uncle bears many burdens.
Seeing me work with you on the Carnevale under Grandfather's orders might have unsettled him, leading to a hasty, misguided move.
How do you feel about this?
Will this change your plans?
In truth, I haven't thought about it, and my opinions hold little weight.
The current plan has proven effective. I believe it's wise to trust Grandfather's judgment, as I always do.
Besides, I now have more important duties to fulfill.
The shark in our midst has finally made its move.
Recently, several of our partners claimed to have found a superior seller and ended their dealings with us.
Meanwhile, Benett, our vault keeper, was reported to have embezzled and sold vault assets. It's said that he tried to flee but was killed by Tacet Discords outside the city.
So Benett betrayed the family as well?
I am not so sure... I've worked with Benett before. He was principled, bold but not reckless, not one to easily betray. And...

The night he died, he sent a photo to my Terminal—a blood-stained page of an anthology, marked with three phrases. "Thy eyes guide my course in the tempest," "When forty winters siege thy beauty," and "The planet turns right, twice and a half."
That's rather cryptic.
Okay, but... it makes no sense.
The meaning is yet to be revealed, but he is clearly conveying a message.

The Montelli family is a symbol of liberation for Ragunna. We uphold freedom and equality for all. Our vault is the heart of our family, and if it's corrupted, it threatens not only us, but risks plunging the city back into oppression and isolation.
As much as I hate to suspect family members, I cannot rule any of them out.
You, however, are different. As an outsider who has aided us in capturing the initial traitors... I hope to not be proven wrong, but I feel that I can trust you.
So you're asking for my help.
I suppose this is when I volunteer to help.
My uncle's words were clear. Only those at the table can play the game. To engage with my family, one must have both standing and purpose.
So, I offer you a new identity in our upcoming inquiry—Cat's Eye, a provisional member under my patronage.
But I'm not truly a member of the family.
This... is obviously a lie.
If you wish to join, you must undertake the final assessment and pledge your loyalty to the Montellis.
Oh, don't worry, we aren't harming anyone. It is but a subtle adaptation of the rules.
Why Cat's Eye though?
When it comes to family matters, we like to use codenames, each tied to a unique token. Mine, for example, is Opal.
Opal recommended Cat's Eye. It has a ring to it, don't you think?
Also, have you looked closely at your own eyes? They share the same luster as Cat's Eye gems.
Well, you recommended me, so it's your call.
We must prevent this threat and bring peace to Ragunna.
I want to uncover the true identity of this lurking shark.
I understand decorum is important to the Montellis. But among friends, can't we be a bit more... informal?
What made you say that?
You're always one step ahead. How about we slow down and savor the present?
Hmm, you're curious who I am beyond my role, is that it?
Hmm, I just might entertain that thought.
But for now, my agents just sent me the address of Benett's residence. While his body has been found, what he left behind is still out there.
Let's try our luck at his residence.
All evidence points to Benett being the key to uncovering the shark lurking in our waters.
Now, Cat's Eye, will you stand with me to catch the traitor within our family and avert this looming threat?
As the rain finally ceases, the elderly man who had been admiring the painting quietly departs, leaving you alone to contemplate the painting's deeper meaning.

When the rain stops, the elderly man quietly leaves the scene. Freed from the watchful eyes, Carlotta successfully meets with you.
She apologizes for Capollo's rudeness and confesses that she has no interest in becoming the family head. Her true concern lies with the traitors lurking within the family. She reveals that Benett, the trusted vault manager, was caught embezzling and subsequently killed by Tacet Discords outside the city. However, on the night of his death, Carlotta received a cryptic message from him.
Once again, Carlotta asks for your help to uncover the truth as you are an outsider that once aided her in capturing the initial traitors. To avoid alarming your targets, she offers you a new identity: Cat's Eye, a provisional member under her patronage.
Believing that Benett's death holds key to unraveling the truth, you decide to investigate his residence.
It seems someone has acted faster. Those two... They're my uncle's agents, Sage and Acorn.
Codenames?
Those are not real names.
Yes, we address each other by codenames—handy identifiers in a crowd.
I'll keep you updated on the family members' codenames we encounter, along with any other details you might need.
Seems like they are looking for something as well.
It's only natural my uncle wishes to retrieve the lost items... but my presence might raise a few eyebrows.
I'll go have a little chat with them to see what they know.
You can find a way around them and continue the investigation.
Yes, you try and loosen their lips. If memory serves, they are senior members, having served under my uncle for years. Regulars at Margherita's.
Talk business with merchants, and wine with drinkers... Engage their interests, and their words will flow like a river. As for the rest...
I'll improvise as needed.

Outside Benett's residence, Capollo's subordinates, Sage and Acorn, are searching for the stolen items on his order, as Capollo is in charge of the vault.
After some discussion, you and Carlotta decide to split up: she sneaks in through the back, while you confront them for information.
You tell Carlotta what you learned from the recovered Terminal data.
I see... so Duncan was in the dark about the real cause of Benett's death. He simply wanted to protect his friend's reputation, and Capollo used that.
Duncan gave us a rigged Terminal to cover Benett's "debt", clearing his name.
I can empathize with Duncan, even to some extent Capollo. They are driven by a desire for safety and stability—a tempting future even for me.
But we will never achieve that by surrendering ourselves to the Order.
From the very beginning, our paths diverged. To yield to them now means giving up even more, and once we lose our grip, we'll no longer have the luxury of refusal.
Grandfather and the others have already paved the way. I will follow their lead and chart a course towards a brighter tomorrow. For our family, and all of Ragunna.
An all-out war with the Order isn't a wise move. Rather than blindly tailing Capollo in search of a hidden data module, let's take control and have him come to us.
Scarlet Velvet mentioned they need a formal reply, and we can deliver that.
{PlayerName}, care to help me give them an unforgettable response in two days?
We're taking the initiative. I like it.
Have him come to us... That makes things interesting.

Capollo <color=yellow>couldn't have tampered</color> with the Terminal data himself, or he would have found the information hidden beneath the overwrites. He simply laid a trap at <color=yellow>the dock that Benett visited</color>.
Wealth and power will safeguard our freedom, while freedom, in turn, will nurture wealth and power.

The Montelli family is set to break the Order's suffocating hold and lead Ragunna towards a wider horizon—embracing Septimont, Huanglong, and other countries. And through it all, we will never forget who we are.
The family exists to accomplish what one cannot and withstand the winds of fate. This is the future I envision for the Montellis.
What do you plan to do next?
Like I said, we seize control.

It would be unwise to directly confront the Order, but staying passively behind Capollo and aimlessly searching for the core data module isn't a reasonable choice either.
You and Carlotta decide to force Capollo into handing over the item by giving them an unforgettable response in two days.
Acorn, Sage...
Hey, that's you they're calling.
No, that's both of us. But I don't recognize this person.
Neither do I. Listen up.
Acorn, Sage...
Okay, you got the names right. Must be family. Who are you?
I'm Cat's Eye, new to the family.
I'm a Montelli.
Cat's Eye? Doesn't ring a bell... Probably one of those new recruits after the Carnevale.
Heh, we are all Montellis here. Remember, when someone asks, use your codename.
Oh, it's Cat's Eye.
A rookie, huh? Learning the ropes with contacts and all. No wonder you look unfamiliar.
So, what do you need? We are just about to wrap up and grab a bite at Margherita's. Still got a lot on our plate today.
(Strike up a conversation about being a newcomer.)
(Strike up a conversation about Margherita's.)
Say, I've heard whispers of your skills. Seeing you here, it's clear you're on an important mission, aren't you?
I haven't faced a true challenge since I got here. Would you accept my help? I'm sure I'd learn a thing or two.
Easy, haha. We've just finished up. So, nothing more to help with.
But here's something I can tell you. Someone tried to steal from the vault recently.
Oh, Margherita's! Nothing quite like it, hm? And the pizza... Oh, it's a favorite in my circle, too.
Ah! Always a solid choice when on the move. Perfect spot for a bit of catching up.
You know, the last time I was there, I heard talk about a thief stealing from the vault. Is that true?
Well, cat's out of the bag now. See that house right there? That's where the thief lived. We came to search for clues.
Did you recover the stolen goods?
No, not yet. We've looked everywhere but found nothing.
To be honest, I doubt we'll ever find them. The thief has probably sold everything off by now, and we are short on manpower. That's a needle in a haystack if you ask me.
Isn't your boss worried?
Boss doesn't seem too worried... is there a plan B?
Well, our boss is the Padrino's son. He has his methods.
Our job is to follow orders, not to ask questions. Just do what we're told and do it well.
That's right. If you spot anything unusual, keep an eye on it. Could be your big break. With a bit more time, I think you'll do just fine.
(That should do it.)
(Time to meet up with Carlotta.)

You successfully gather information from Sage and Acorn, learning they found nothing in Benett's residence. They express little hope of retrieving the stolen items as Capollo didn't allocate enough resources for investigation and they also believe that Benett had already sold the items off for quite some time.
Just checking your location, have you reached the spot, my clever accomplice?
Everything's going according to plan.
Perfect. Remember to be stealthy. Scarlet Velvet and my operatives are positioned in all the streets around the venue. Should anything go awry, I'll set Plan B in motion.
The venue only has one entrance. I've arranged for a handler to get you in. You'll go in first and then help me slip in without drawing attention.
Ahem. Can you hear me?
The upstairs parlor is off-limits, reserved for a private event.
We gave you the heads-up before.
Boss wanted a batch of gifts for our business partner.
Hmm... Now that you mentioned it, yes, they did tell me about that. But weren't you supposed to arrive half an hour later?
Half an hour is enough for me.
What was that?
Oh, I mean, I thought it was good to come here half an hour early.
We can get ready sooner this way.
You do have a point, but it's a special day. I need to confirm everyone's identity. What's your codename? Show me your token.
(A token?... Tsk, I don't have one.)
(Where's the promised handler? He should be here by now...)
Hey, Tulip! Why are you still standing there? Come here! Boss just asked for you.
The visitor slyly palms a Tulip coin, hiding the gesture in his shadow. You discreetly accept it and present it as proof of identity.
Ah, Tulip coin... Oh! I remember you. You work at the vault, don't you? We had a drink at Margherita's.
Don't tell me you've already forgotten me?
No wonder you arrived early. You people at the vault are always one step ahead.
Yeah, yeah, we can talk after getting the job done. Now hurry up, we'll deliver the gifts together.
Huh? Uh, well... Yes, it's been awhile!
With the help of a mysterious figure, you disguise yourself as a family member delivering a gift for Capollo and successfully escort Carlotta into the venue.
Have you made it inside?
This area is under surveillance. On either side of the main stage, you should see something that looks like a control panel.
Operate it to disable the cameras, then place the "gems" I made with my Forte into position.
How did it go? Any issues?
Everything's fine. Just got to the place we agreed on.
The front of the hall. Done.
Main hall, five o'clock. Done.
Blind spot, done.
Back window, done.
The setup is complete, and the time we planned is drawing near.
How's it going on your end?
I'm out of the mirror, and the jammer's set up. Capollo actually inspired this plan, otherwise we wouldn't have been able to infiltrate.
The Order's agents have taken the bait and are at the location. "Blue Rain" and "Retriever" are primed for action.
We'll head out at the chime of the hour.
Your guests won't be showing up today.
Ha, Carlotta… Looks like you've pieced together the whole story. So it was your crew who tipped us off about changing the time and place for the deal yesterday.
Let me guess. You fed the same line to the Order, didn't you? Playing both sides, setting yourself up nicely… But something doesn't add up. You couldn't have pulled this off alone.
Capollo's promises of safety and comfort are nothing but a sham. He has been <color=yellow>using our family as pawns</color>, making them pay the ultimate price. Benett was just one of his victims.
He didn't fall at the hands of Tacet Discords but to Capollo himself. His body was disposed of outside the city's limits... The truth is, Benett never betrayed us.
The path of the Montelli family is one of unity. We stand together, leaving no one behind.
I can't promise there won't be more losses, but I will prioritize the welfare of every member. I do not take sacrifice lightly.
Now, will you continue down this path? Or will you align with our cause for Bennett's sake and your own?
Trust built on deception always comes back to haunt you. You're getting what you deserve.
…You're right, I've crossed a line. But I can still salvage this if I take you out here and reclaim that data module.
Now that you've lost both the goods and your trading partners… this is your last chance to bow out gracefully.
Bow out gracefully? Do you think I still care about saving face at this point?
My only regret is not being ruthless enough… I should've cut you loose earlier, making you pay the price like the others who crossed me.
You've betrayed your family's ideals.
And what of it? You'll never understand!
We lack the power to protect everyone, so what's wrong with seeking a powerful ally? Why not align ourselves with those who share my true goal?

Trust built on deception will eventually be shattered by reality. You, Carlotta, and Duncan, who decided to help you, change the location and time of the deal without Capollo noticing. Even though both the trading partners and cargo are lost, Capollo refuses to back down. The two Montellis, now on different paths, finally arrive at their confrontation. The key to winning this duel lies in the whereabouts of the core data module.
Fall for me, will you?
Everyone, capture them!
Time to leave.
Copy.
Then let's fall together!
You rendezvous with Carlotta after her investigation and share the information you gathered.
So, they found nothing, but assumed Uncle wasn't concerned?
That makes no sense. Everything that happened recently ties back to the vault. If Uncle wished to protect his position, he'd be quick to retrieve the items and resolve the situation.
Maybe he's hiding something.
Maybe he's in control all along.
Things don't add up.
Curiously, Benett was last sighted in the vicinity of <color=yellow>Liberty Square</color>, where you met Uncle.
Last night, I was investigating the area before I happened upon your private meeting.
That explains why you were there...
But when I brought this up to him afterward, he didn't seem privy to any details.
As for my search of Benett's home, nothing of note turned up, just as the two agents reported.
I found no spoils, not even the faintest trace of them being stored or moved... Everything about his living space fits the profile of a typical junior vault employee.
I've also asked around about Bennet after our previous collaboration. He was ambitious, but never greedy. I was even told he refused the bribe offered by a business associate during an operation.
The Montelli family is ever generous with wealth and opportunities, welcoming all who aspire to make their mark in Ragunna. Mere profit would never make him betray us.
The family protects its members.
Members bring the family glory.
For now, more evidence is required. The entire matter might need to be approached from a different angle...
Shh, hold still... See that man over there, the one that looks like a gray dove?
Without making a movement, you follow Carlotta's line of sight. Not far away, a man, partially hidden, is frequently glancing in your direction. He seems to be observing you and Carlotta.
Noticing your gaze, he immediately starts running.
After him, quick.

Sharing this information with Carlotta, you both notice some suspicious aspects: when Carlotta brought up Benett's betrayal, Capollo had remained calm, but the series of recent family troubles seem to be all linked to the vault he directly manages. If he is eager to secure his position as the next family head, he should have put more efforts in resolving these incidents. Besides, Benett was not a man who would be easily swayed by greed...
While discussing these points, you notice an elderly man observing you from a distance. Realizing he is exposed, he immediately flees, and you pursue him.
Scarlet Velvet's people have secured Duncan and will bring him to a safe house. He'll return after everything's settled.
Regarding the Order, I tasked "Blue Rain" and "Retriever" to <color=yellow>pose as Capollo's agents</color> and declare the cooperation null and void.
No data module, no explanation or any follow-up... Capollo is already a lost cause. The Order will realize this soon enough.
The rain's back. I remember telling Grandfather how I hated the rainy season.
I once saw rain as a bad omen in Ragunna.
When it rains, it's easier to wash away blood stains. That's why acts of revenge usually happen on such days.
But today's rain feels different. As it falls, the troubles of yesterday are washed away. I feel calm, like I've found my true self again. My present and my future are now in my own hands.
Well done, Carlotta. And thank you, {PlayerName}.
My girl could not have accomplished this without your assistance.
She personally invited and vouched for me, after all.
She is capable enough in her own right.
I had faith in you two, but you surpassed my expectations.
It appears I underestimated the potential that you possess when working together.
What he just said... Looks like someone has been keeping secrets from me, huh?
I've been curious, you entered that Sonoro and delivered his gun to me. How did you earn my grandfather's trust so soon?
That's a story between the two of us.
I'll tell you next time.
Hm, the nerve... Fine, since we make such a good team, I'll let it slide for now.
Capollo and his lackeys will face the consequences of their actions. Our code is simple—vengeance for blood, death for life. No one is exempt.
There's a lot at play here. It will require some effort and a true Montelli at my side to handle it.
I see. I'll take care of the rest.
But before that...
Are you leaving?
Yes. What, miss me already?
Of course not.
Yes, I'll miss you. Who knows when I'll see you again.
Well... maybe a little.
"No need to feel sad about parting, for each goodbye brings us closer to the next hello."
That's my favorite way to think of it—a countdown to our next reunion.
With Capollo ousted, the family needs someone to fill his shoes. I must assist my grandfather through this tumultuous transition. There is no one else to do it.
Thank you, {PlayerName}. As my grandfather said, things couldn't have gone so smoothly without your help and support.
Now that the dust has settled, you no longer need to stay with me as Cat's Eye of the Montelli family, but still... I want you to have this.
As I said, every member gets a token that matches their codename.
Though you already have a pair of Cat's Eyes, please accept this as a token of my appreciation. No, this gem wasn't crafted by my Forte. I chose it just for you.
I know someone like you won't stay just for me, and joining the Montelli family might not be in your plans just yet.
But I'll keep this codename for you, Cat's Eye—the first and only member to receive my personal invitation.

As the evening rain falls, washing away everything from the past, Carlotta tells you that today's rain brings her peace. She has finally found her true self and feels in control of both her present and future.
When the rain stops, Carlotta bids you farewell. To build a new, true Montelli, she needs to handle the aftermath of Capollo's betrayal. Before parting, she hands you a Cat's Eye brooch, telling you that the codename "Cat's Eye" will forever belong to you, as you are the only member she has ever recommended.
Nowhere to run. Now it's time for a proper chat.
Hah... These old, creaky bones of mine.
Did I offend you? Or are you just chasing down every passing soul... Never thought the Montellis would grow so aggressive.
No running, no chasing.
Just a glance and you can tell we're Montellis?
He had no choice but to run, to escape his past and sever any ties with the Montellis.
No one knows the family's ways better than its members, even though... he is no longer one of us.
Right, Old Duncan?
Ha, hahaha... I must admit, you have an annoyingly good memory.
It's remarkable that someone of your rank would remember a man such as myself.
I will never forget that <color=yellow>stormy</color> night, nor any of the members who were caught in it.
Sadly, I've no desire to be remembered. To me, Montelli is only a name of the past.
There were moments of joy, but they cannot make up for my loss... now I only feel tired.
If that's true, why are you here?
You say one thing, but do another.
Why go back to what you claim to have left in the past? Unless there's something you can't ignore.

You were standing across from Benett's doorway, and your clothes are still damp from the rain... You weren't simply passing by, you were watching. What were you looking for? Or should I ask, what did you hope to find?
I don't know.
To grieve for my last friend in the family? To blame him for being so reckless and greedy?
Or to figure out how this fool ended up in such a mess, hoping to find the lost items and settling his debts, so he may rest in peace?
I tried to persuade him to leave with me, but failed. In Ragunna's game, the Montelli family has only two options.
We either play to win, or are forced to leave with nothing.
Every Montelli has a chance at their desires, but what's the price... They stake everything they hold dear—family, love, faith, principles, and even their life.
Now... his ambition and greed have cost him everything.
But you can decide when to leave the table.
Is that why you left the family?
Most people find acceptance easier than change, as change demands the bravery to face uncertainty. No great endeavor is without its perils.
So yes, if the Montellis are to drive the change and push past current barriers, the path ahead will be anything but easy.
The family exists to withstand what an individual cannot, and accomplish what might otherwise be unattainable.
But within the family, each Montelli still enjoys the freedom of choice. Your leaving is a testiment to this, is it not?
If you're willing, there is still much to be done for Benett. His Terminal, the alleged stolen goods... everything but his body remains missing.
Given your familiarity, you might help us in locating these items...
Benett's death may not be as simple as it looks.
We were also looking for more clues in his home.
...In that case, you might want to speak to Scarlet Velvet.
Who is this Scarlet Velvet?
The leader of a network of commoners seeking freedom in Ragunna City. They had close ties with Benett. If he was really stealing, I'd wager they were complicit.
That said, with their recent fallout with the family, I can't guarantee you'll find them, let alone talk to them.
We have little choice but to try.
Now... let's go, {PlayerName}. We're off to the most reliable source of information in Ragunna.

Carlotta identifies the man as Duncan, a former member of the family who had long left. Duncan attributes Benett's death to insatiable lust and ambition. He shares that like Carlotta, he experienced that "stormy night" and believes all those who inherit the Montelli name are doomed to lose everything.
Carlotta respects Duncan's views, but she also sees through his inner conflict—though he wishes to sever ties with the Montelli family, he returned to Ragunna after hearing Benett's death.
You confide in Duncan about your doubts regarding Benett's death and ask him to join your investigation as his friend. After some hesitation, Duncan agrees and provides you information about Scarlet Velvet and her possible connection to Benett as the recipient of the stolen items.
This is the place.
The best place for information... is a pub?
I don't think Scarlet Velvet would hide somewhere so public.
She may not be here, but I have my ways of reaching her people.

Was the Echo performance hosted by the Montellis?
...I see.
Sorry to keep you waiting. That was Mr. Alberto from the Montelli family. Also my employer.
Come to think of it, that Echo... it was looking at you. It seemed to target you.
You've got sharp eyes.
Hmph, I won't pry into my ward's privacy. I only remember what I need to get the job done. Anything else I accidentally overhear just slips my mind.
My orders are to guard and to guide. I do my job. Nothing more, nothing less. So if you want to investigate, I'll stick with you until you're done.
Thank you.
You're very professional!
Don't thank me, thank the family who hired me. Their generosity is beyond what you can imagine.
Thank you for trusting in my abilities.
So, what's our next move?
Let's find that Vitreum Dancer first.
It was complete chaos, but I spied the direction it fled… We can try our luck at the Pioneer Association.
I know someone there whose Forte might help us uncover some details we missed.
Sure, let's head to the Pioneer Association first.
Good. Let's go this way. It's right over there.
Well, I think we'd better work the scene first.
No problem.
I want to find out what caused that Echo to lose control.
Yes, it was. The Montelli family has been promoting the use of Reserved Terminals and Echoes.
As far as I know, the Montelli family has been promoting the use of Reserved Terminals and Echoes.
Most Ragunnesi use Common Echoes and don't know much about the Reserved ones. The Montellis spotted a chance and started researching Reserved Terminals.
They push to bring back the Carnevale so they can showcase their Reserved Terminals, prove the quality of their Echoes, and attract both customers and investors.
Oh sorry, just a minute.
Yes, Mr. Alberto. An Echo was...
Zani recounts what happened to the caller. Moments later...
He extends a sincere apology for what just happened. They too are at a loss to explain what caused the accident.
He told me that the Montelli family would investigate further. Please rest assured.
Did the Montellis really have no answers?
No... After all, such an incident only hinders their promotion of Reserved Terminals. They have no reason to rejoice over it.

During the Carnevale rehearsal, one of the Vitreum Dancers suddenly loses control and charges into the crowd. Amid the chaos, your mind connects with the Dancer's and you hear the voice of the Sentinel. They ask for your help in bringing the Lost back to the earthly realm.

After pondering these words, you suspect that Imperator, like the Sentinel of Jinzhou, might be in a vulnerable state, relying on Echoes to communicate. But all your questions could only be answered by that Vitreum Dancer.

You ask Zani about the Dancer and the rehearsal. She explains that it's not a Common Echo, but a private one owned by the Montellis. They're pushing the use of Reserved Terminals, and this Carnevale is their opportunity to promote them. The incident with the dancer could cause a major setback for them.

The Vitreum Dancer you connected with has already escaped. Zani suggests finding a Resonator from the Pioneer Association if you want to track it down. But if you'd like to investigate the scene first, she's happy to help.
An Echo attacking humans? Right before the Carnevale? That’s wild…
Rumor has it, the Montelli family's Echoes are "filthy"—none of them have been purified by the Order...
Yeah, I’ve heard whispers, but those Montelli Echoes have been helping out around the city for ages without a single issue… until now.
The real problem isn’t the Echoes but their Reserved Terminals!
Oh? Isn’t all that Montelli tech based on the Genesis Nexus? They always insist it’s completely safe.
Come on, that's just their sales pitch. When has a business ever told you the downside of their product?
They’re even planning to push more Reserved Terminals during the Carnevale. That can't be more suspicious...
But isn’t the Montelli family hosting the Carnevale this year?
Doesn’t matter. They’re businesspeople. Who knows what they’re really up to.
Keep blathering on about this without a shred of evidence and you could end up before <ano=The Secular Court> the Order's Tribunal</ano>.
Ugh, fine, I’m just saying…
Dear Sentinel above…
Excuse me, do you know anything about the Echo that lost control?
Oh, the Sentinel is in a great rage! They are warning us, reminding us of our follies.
We shouldn't have forgotten... Ten years ago, it was our unbridled indulgence that brought about divine punishment!
We should have heeded Primus Fenrico's words…
What do you mean?
What happened ten years ago?

Oh, dear visitor from afar, you may not know. Ten years ago, the Carnevale angered the Sentinel and brought forth divine punishment. Primus Fenrico foresaw the shadow beneath the revelry and halted its spread!
Simply put, many terrible accidents happened during that Carnevale, like Echoes losing control. Since then, the Primus ordered the Carnevale to stop.
Most Ragunnesi don't like to talk about that tragedy, so it's understandable you haven't heard of it.
Echoes are messengers of the Sentinel. They lost control and attacked people because they were corrupted, reflecting our transgressions against the Sentinel!
This year, the Order has approved the Carnevale. We will return to our traditions… Dear visitor, please join us in praising the Sentinel. Only then can our misguided souls be forgiven…
How will that Echo be handled?

It may be a divine blessing, but it has committed an assault against the Sentinel's people. The corrupted will be purified under the holy light of the Genesis Nexus. As for the one that escaped, the Order will retrieve it as soon as possible to prevent further harm.
In other words, the Echo will be reset in the Data Bank. That's how we Ragunnesi usually deal with malfunctioning Echoes.
We deeply apologize for the disturbance caused by that undisciplined Echo… Now, please excuse me. I have other matters to attend to.
The Acolyte leaves while murmuring to herself.

She may not have given us anything useful, but she did remind me of one thing—that Vitreum Dancer's behavior was different from those Echoes that went wild in the past. It seemed to have a clear goal and a sentience.
The Echoes are connected with each other, so usually if one loses control, the others will be affected too. However, we haven't received any reports of other Echoes losing control.
If it wasn't the Sentinel's punishment, it could have been…
…caused by someone.
Let's pick up the pace and find that Vitreum Dancer still at large.
You're right. We need to catch it before the Order does, or we won't be able to get the information we need.
Here's to a world of discoveries and wonders! Welcome to the Pioneer Association!
Ms. Zani! It's been some time! Have you finally decided to join us?
No, I'm here for something else. This is Mr. Fulmine from the Pioneer Association.
Oh, hello! You've brought a new friend! Pleasure to meet you. I'm Fulmine, head of the Wutherium Film Studio under the Pioneer Association in Ragunna. How should I address you?
Nice to meet you, I'm {PlayerName}.
Your name rings a bell… Oh! Y-you're the legendary Rover?!
Savior from a foreign land, the dark thunderbolt streaking across the world… I've longed to meet you! By the Sentinel, let me seize this extraordinary moment!
They're just titles, not worth bragging about.
Let's get down to business.
Wait, you're actually some kind of celebrity?

Ha, indeed {Male=he;Female=she} is. Ragunna's routes have only recently opened, so {Male=his;Female=her} feats haven't made it here yet. Should you perform a great deed, trust me to ensure your name echoes throughout Ragunna!
I had a nagging feeling I've met someone important... But let's get back to what matters.
We're here to ask a favor. We're investigating a Vitreum Dancer who caused a scene around Trattoria Margherita.
It fled in this direction, and we're wondering if you can recreate the scene for us.
Ah, I know the one you mean. Saw it streaking out of the city with a few Order fellows in tow.
As for recreating the scene… C-MOSS, my friend, it's time to get to work!
Hmph.
Alright, where is it? My memory of that Vitreum Dancer… Ah, I've found it!
Mr. Fulmine's Forte is Celluloid Chronicle. He can convert events into film, recording all that happens within a span of time.
His partner, C-MOSS, uses a "Memory Projector" Forte to show these captured moments.
There it is! Take a look!
So it did leave the city… This complicates matters. The area beyond is too vast to search effectively. Plus, Tacet Discords are hampering our investigation. We can't start searching just yet.
(Abby, can you sniff it out?)
(…What do you think I am? Not a chance! And I'm too sleepy to help, just wake me if there's any progress…)
I'm sorry. I can only record what is plain to the eye.
Don't be hard on yourself, Mr. Fulmine. You've been a tremendous help. At least we're not flying blind anymore. But {PlayerName}, we need a new plan.
Can you think back carefully?
Was anything unusual?
…Give me a moment. Ah, yes! Look at this!
How could this be...
His garb suggests he's from the Montelli family. Could they be involved in this turmoil?
It's too soon to tell.
He wore an unusual mask.
Indeed. But it's rare to wear a mask before the Carnevale. He must have wanted to hide his face.
Speaking of, the mask is not the typical Montelli style, and wearing it now is unusual.
With their eagerness to promote Reserved Terminals, the Montellis would be the last to invite trouble now. If he's tied to the disturbance...
Then perhaps we should seek Ms. Nyarla's expertise. She's known for her intricate masks, and this one seems custom.
Good idea, but nobles are secretive. Direct questions might lead to unwanted attention.
I have a plan.
I'll arrange for a custom-made mask myself.
Ah-ha, Excellent. Let's make for the Masked Reverie.
Thank you for your assistance, Mr. Fulmine.
Good luck!
We're here to ask a favor. We're investigating a Vitreum Dancer who caused a scene around Trattoria Margherita.
He may be a spy or in disguise.

Fulmine from the Pioneer Association has a unique skill: he can turn his memories into special film reels, and assisted by the Echo, C-MOSS, he can project those memories for others to see.

In one of Fulmine's memories, you see someone dressed in Montelli attire, wearing a mask and lurking suspiciously behind the Vitreum Dancer. Since the Carnevale hasn't started yet, it's odd for someone to already be masked up—as if they're deliberately hiding their identity.

With this clue, you decide to head to Masked Reverie, a mask shop, in search of leads…
Has the perfume, compact, and jewelry set arrived?
Yes, they have. Would you like them now, or shall we deliver them to your residence before tonight?
Tonight… No, I'll take them now.
…Of course. I'll have someone fetch them immediately. It won't take long.
Welcome to Masked Reverie. From masks to elegant garments and splendid stage props, we craft it all to order. How may I help you today, my dear?
...Who's there?
Hehe, so eager to skip the pleasantries, are we? I'm right here. Do I seem invisible, or are you simply ignoring me? I am... right behind you.
Madame Nyarla, I saw you. Your mask gave you away.
Hehe, don't spoil my secret so soon. It's not every day I get such a charming visitor.
Besides, only by "hiding" oneself can the true beauty of a mask be revealed, don't you think?
But scaring the guests is just your twisted sense of humor, isn't it?

I hope this didn't bother you. <ano=Ombra Elusiva>Invisibility</ano> is Madame Nyarla's Forte. Madame Nyarla, this is the distinguished guest invited by the Montellis, {PlayerName}. {Male=He;Female=She} is very interested in Carnevale masks.
Yes, I'd like a custom-made mask.
You elaborate on the mask design you saw in Fulmine's memory to Nyarla.
Hmm? That's quite a detailed description, even covering the smallest intricacies... I admit, I'm surprised.
Not long ago, we customized a mask just like the one you've described.
If the Carnevale is a dream shared by all Ragunnesi, then a well-crafted mask is the key to it.
When faces are hidden, souls break free from the shackles of everyday life. That's why we love balls and plays, eagerly awaiting the Carnevale.
Masks liberate our spirits. We believe they reveal what lies within. It is our honor to help our customers express their innermost selves.
So, are you certain you want to custom order this particular mask?
Well…
(She's suspicious... Will I be forced to reveal my hand...?)
That's a very fine mask.
If I remember correctly, the one Mr. Gilberto picked up last week looked very similar. If it's your first mask, a unique design might be more fitting?
You have an impressive memory.
I'll be on my way now.
Ahem, we spotted a fellow on the street with a mask that caught our eye… I didn't expect it to be Mr. Gilberto from the Fisalia family.
The Fisalia family?
Yes, they're one of the oldest families in Rinascita. Their ancestors once ignited a war here, but they were defeated and driven out of Ragunna.
The Fisalias are a mixed lot—while some hold honor, others bring disgrace to the name.
They show new ambitions. Lately, they've taken to more prominent roles in the city, flaunting their mining ventures and acting with increasing arrogance.
Speaking of which, I revised Monsieur Gilberto's mask twenty-three times…
I see why it's left a deep impression…
Anyway, given your standing with the Montellis, I'd advise against this design.
Why's that?
Rumor has it the Montellis plan to push for Reserved Echoes at the Carnevale. It's stirred tension with the Fisalia family. Best avoid any association.
That incident with the Montelli's Echoes going berserk... Unfortunate timing. Who knows how this will affect their promotion.
I see…
So, the trail leads to the Fisalia family.
Thank you for the lead, Madame Nyarla. Oh, and we will reconsider the mask's design. Thank you for your time.
Hehe, you're too polite, Mademoiselle Zani. You're my special guest, after all.
Isn't it interesting how a small mask can both hide and reveal? I can't wait to see the "face" you'll choose to show.
I look forward to your next visit. This splendid reverie is always open for you.
We need to look into the Fisalia family.
The Fisalia's residencies are near the Cathedral of Mercury. We could stop by the Order for more information.

At Masked Reverie, you pose as a customer interested in bespoke designs, hoping to gather information about the mask you saw earlier. The shop owner, Nyarla, quickly sees through the ruse. Just as you consider revealing your true motive, a noblewoman steps in to assist you.

You learn that the mask in question was commissioned by a member of the Fisalia family—a man named Gilberto. Rumor has it that the Fisalia Family has been at odds with the Montellis family over issues related to Reserved Terminals.

Since the Fisalia estate is near the Cathedral of Mercury, you decide to pay them a visit and stop by the cathedral to gather further insights from the Order.
Ha, Antonio, surely you know how things work here. It's always about who pays more. Is there a problem?
Do you Fisalias even honor contracts?
Ha, since when do Montellis fret over such trivialities?
Instead of whining, maybe focus on cleaning up the mess your Echoes caused. Ha ha ha...
The Fisalia man walks away, leaving Antonio fuming.
And you are…?
Greetings, Sir Antonio. I'm Zani from the Averardo Bank.
This {Male=gentleman;Female=lady} here is a distinguished guest of your family, {PlayerName}. {Male=He;Female=She} was attacked by a rogue Vitreum Dancer while dining, and we're investigating.
Ah, so you're… Please accept my apologies! It's a relief to see you unscathed. We're as puzzled as you are about the Echo's behavior.
It's okay, but there's something else I want to know.
Miss Carlotta asked me to hold nothing back, so ask away.
Tell me about Reserved Terminals and Reserved Echoes.
Well, before I do, a little context first.
In Ragunna, the Order controls all Terminals for Echo use. They store Echoes in their Data Bank and only grant access after thorough screening.
Only a select few Resonators are permitted to carry a Reserved Terminal.
You see, most Ragunnesi rely on the Genesis Nexus and Common Echoes, with little need for the special access types.
However, things have changed with Ragunna opening up to the greater Solaris. People want to travel, making Reserved Terminals essential for safety outside the Order's reach.
You see why demand is up. The Montellis saw an opportunity and started to develop them. After all, necessity is the mother of invention, hm?
It should be celebrated, but some think we disrespect the Order's authority or even the Sentinel by doing this. The path forward has been... resistant.
Heh, if you ask me, I suspect the Fisalia family has been spreading slanders about us.
We back the Carnevale to showcase our Reserved Terminals to the people. It's our chance to prove their worth and attract investors.
And the Fisalia family has been standing in your way?
Sigh… The Fisalias have coerced our miners to break their contracts, seizing our largest vein and cutting off our Terminal supply.
And it gets worse. With the Carnevale nearing and our Echoes malfunctioning, the family's Executor might have to step in.
The Carnevale is at risk. While we hope it brings fortune, the festival itself is what truly matters to us, just like the rest of Ragunna.
We must uncover why the Echo lost control. We cannot let the Fisalias use this to tarnish our reputation any further!
I can help you with the investigation.
That would be good for us, but it hardly seems proper to involve our esteemed guest in our troubles...
I have my own reasons.

Ah, understood. Thank you! But I'm afraid we can't spare any of our own to assist you. Rest assured, the Montellis are always generous. Here's an advance. Once the matter is resolved, you'll be well-rewarded.
Take it. In Ragunna, if you want help, you must offer a reward and one only declines a reward when they refuse to help.
Yes, that's right. Please accept it. If that's all, I must be on my way. There are many matters to attend to...
Antonio departs with a sigh. The weight on his shoulders seems heavier than before.
From what we know, the Montelli family has no motive for such incidents. They've been anticipating the Carnevale's arrival.

But the Fisalia family is another story. They've been against the celebration from the start, perhaps they could be behind everything? But I don't understand, what could they hope to gain by stopping the Carnevale?
The mystery continues.
Maybe it's related to the Sentinel?
Why do I feel like I've gotten myself into something above my pay grade…
You... have a hunch, hm?
They say the Fisalias have been seen frequenting the Cathedral of Mercury. They must be in league with the Order. How else would they dare to seize our mine so boldly?
Only investigation brings us answers.
You're right. Let's go.
Ciao, we need to get to the Cathedral of Mercury.
Got it! Please, come aboard.
Andreas... That ship... No, no, I must stop that ship!
...Have you gone mad? You can't stop the Pilgrim's Sail. The Order will arrest you!
Ah, you just don't understand...
We are now in the Fisalia Residencies territory. We should... Wait, look over there…
He looks like the man we saw in Mr. Fulmine's memory. Isn't that Gilberto?
Let's follow him.
Legends say the Sentinel quelled the storm and stilled the waves, sparing countless lives at sea.
To show their gratitude, people place candles around the statue, keeping them lit both day and night. Every boat that passes pays their respects.
It may seem fanciful, but it's best to show respect as we pass by.
So is this the statue of the Sentinel? Why does it feel weird...
As you reach the upper level of the Cathedral of Mercury, you spot Gilberto just ahead, slipping inside…
Ah, more seekers. What brings you to these halls?
We're here to visit Sir Gilberto.
Sir Gilberto...? Oh, Gilberto from the Fisalia family.
A pious soul, frequently here in prayer. But not today, it seems.
I've heard whispers of you. An Acolyte mentioned your desire to meet the Sentinel. I assume you must be interested in following Their path.
But I don't think you truly understand the significance of the Carnevale. Allow me to explain.
I'm interested.
If you must.
You've probably heard about the connection between the Carnevale and the Sentinel, but do you know why the Carnevale hasn't been held for years?
I have a general understanding.
Is it because of the accident a decade ago?
In the last Carnevale, a sea fog shrouded the entire city. Echoes paraded like lost souls, a dragon roared above, and a beast in the sea stirred up towering waves…
It was sent as punishment and warning against our indulgence and division.
This is our Primus, Fenrico, the Enlightened One.
Amidst that chaos, he stepped forward and quelled the Sentinel's wrath.
Ragunna's greatness was forged from its battles with the sea. It inspired a common goal in all our hearts.
Without everyone working together, land cannot be cultivated, islands cannot unite, and dams cannot be built. A nation's strength lies in its unity.
You see, this is why we preach restraint and control over our desires. Only through rituals can we strengthen our resolve, our unity!
This is why we must banish those who stray from the right path and impose restrictions on those who threaten the common good.
We've dedicated ourselves to this cause.
It seems like you disapprove of holding the Carnevale.
Hehe, you misunderstand me.
I simply mean that the Order's actions are always made with great deliberation.
Guided by the Sentinel, we strive to unite and lead the people. We hope to build a kingdom on high, a land of the blessed… As it was in the beginning, and ever shall be.
I trust you'll have faith in the Order's judgment. We handle all matters that come to our attention.
...What did you say? How could the Montelli family...
Forgive me, I must attend to pressing matters.
If you have further questions, seek answers in the cathedral. We are always open to those in search of truth.
But I remind you to keep your distance from the sacred relics and honor our customs. Otherwise, we will have no choice but to address any act of disrespect.

At the Cathedral of Mercury, you're welcomed by Priest Alessio. He denies any connection to Gilberto and instead tells you about the events of the last Carnevale ten years ago: the city was shrouded in thick sea fog, the Vitreum Dancers acted like ghosts, a dragon's roar echoed through the sky, and giant sea monster stirred the waves.

The Order believes it was "divine judgment" on the Carnevale—a warning against people's selfish indulgence. It's clear they don't want you getting involved in the Montellis' recent Vitreum Dancer incident.

Just as you're left uncertain about your next move, news arrives that the Montelli family is making a move. Alessio steps out, leaving you alone in the cathedral…
What's got him so rattled that he'd leave us like that?
He's hiding something. We saw Gilberto enter the cathedral with our own eyes. He couldn't have vanished into thin air.
Could there be a hidden chamber or secret passage within the cathedral?
Now that you mention it, something's not sitting right.

Since Alessio has granted you the freedom to explore the Cathedral, you decide to take full advantage of this rare opportunity.

With Zani by your side, you begin investigating the cathedral, searching for leads...
I didn't expect the Order to have such a grand garden hidden here.
But where could Gilberto have gone? Let's split up and see what we can find.
Step forward.
What burdens weigh upon your soul?
I carry no burdens.
Bless me, for I have transgressed.
Are you certain? Search your heart.
Truly, I have nothing to confess.
What do you wish to confess?
I sleep too much, eat too much, and squander my days in idleness.
May the Sentinel grant your absolution. Go in peace, and transgress no more.
Now, I shall open the path to your ascension.
I confess that my remarkable good looks have stirred envy and discord.
Looks like they're slowly finding their way.
No need to rush—I, too, am curious to see what truths await them.
The grand revelry draws closer and closer...

Zani's clues lead you to the cathedral gardens where there is a room that resembles a confessional. To gather more clues, you enter the room.

Meanwhile, Phrolova, the mysterious Overseer of the Fractsidus quietly watches and waits for you to uncover "the path to ascension."
Hello there! Need a lift to the city? Hop on this Gondola right here.
This boat is... an Echo?
Yes, please. Thank you.
Correct! In Ragunna, we sail in Echoes. They are trusted and reliable helpers, gifts from divinity.
A third of a Ragunnesi's life is spent on a Gondola. Pretty amazing, right?
This little one will get you there safe and sound.

At the dock, you plan to ride the Echo boat "Gondola" into the city.
Maybe you'll see a whole flock of Echoes like Abby along the way!
That was so scary! I really thought Bakie was gonna lose control just like that Vitreum Dancer…
Anyway, you really shouldn’t have had to go through such a rough experience on your first visit to Ragunna.
Here, take these dishes—they’re on the house! Hope this keeps your day on the bright side!
Did he head that way?
At the end of the garden… is that a confessional?
Are you alright? It's strange. Why did that Echo suddenly lose control…
I'm fine. Something's off with those Echoes. Let's try calming them down.
Gilberto, how are things progressing?
Your trust means a lot, Priest Alessio. The "Flower" has been quite... effective.
A word of caution. Don't overstep. We can't afford unwanted scrutiny.
I know what I'm doing.
Our sanctuary isn't infinite. Some murmurs are getting harder to quiet.
I understand. That's why we seek "unity" and "integration."
Our beliefs are already one. This is also the destiny They intend.
Within the Cathedral of Mercury, you see Gilberto secretly discussing something with Alessio, a Priest from the Order…
Forgive me, honored guest… In our eagerness to share the faith, we may have caused you some discomfort.
Ragunna is a city rooted in devotion, and to us, Imperator, our dear Sentinel, is the guardian over all of Rinascita.
This is something every native knows well. Yet we forgot that you come from afar, unfamiliar with our traditions.
Therefore, please accept my sincere apologies, and do enjoy yourself in the city. Should you have any questions about Ragunna, Acolyte Phoebe will gladly help you.
May the Sentinel bless you.
Would you like to look around? I'll be here.
O revered Sentinel...
Thank you for gifting us "the source of light," and for gracing us with "kind Echoes."
So, this is Ragunna's Genesis Nexus? Magnificent...
It looks so different from those Nexus we saw in other places...
Identity confirmed… Does this mean I now have access to use the Common Echoes?
Yes. Please remember that these Echoes are the Divine Envoys of the Sentinel and must be treated with utmost respect. Any transgression will result in disciplinary action.
All security measures checked?
Yes. We're inspecting everything every few hours.
All security measures checked? The Carnevale is only days away.
Yes. We're inspecting everything every few hours.
Good. We need this Carnevale to be absolutely perfect.
Of course. Holding the Carnevale is a wish we Montellis share with the people.
Indeed. Joy has been absent in this city for too long...
By the way, sir… do you believe in the Sentinel's existence?
Well, the Order speaks of Their grace, how They graced us with this land for shelter and provided us with countless blessings.
While I’m grateful for all that the Sentinel represents, I believe humanity is meant to shape its own future. Whether They exist or not, we each have a role to play in this world.
Grandpa, what’s the Carnevale like?
Well, there are so many stories about the Carnevale…

At first, it was a festival to thank the Sentinel. Back then, people had just escaped the sorrow of the Lament. They’d lost their homes and felt a deep respect for the Sentinel, so the ceremonies were always very serious.
One day, the Sentinel’s voice came down from the heavens:
"Solemnity is not the only name of gratitude or remembrance." The Sentinel wanted people to build a future with joy and hope, to honor the past by living fully in the present.

Since then, everyone began following the Sentinel’s guidance. They put on their fine clothes, sang their favorite songs, and put on plays. Gradually, the Carnevale turned into the celebration we know today.
Every year, the Sentinel chooses the best performer and gifts them the Laurel as a sign of encouragement.
One of my old friends was actually a Laureate, hehe...
For kids like you, this festival is a time to hang out with friends and eat all kinds of special treats.
Wow! So… does that mean I don't have to do homework as well?
Hooray! Carnevale! Why can’t we have it more often, Grandpa?
Ah, that's a bit complicated, dear. But don't worry, Grandpa will explain it all to you one day…
A traveling troupe? Never heard of a group like that around Rinascita...
Oh, come on! The Guinizello Troupe is gonna win the Laurel at this year's Carnevale for sure!
Heard the news? The Order's bringing in a "Conductor" for this year's Carnevale!
A Conductor? Yeah, I bet they just want to control the whole thing again.
I didn't know all the ships in Ragunna are Echoes. That troupe isn't as special as I thought...
Now I can't even imagine what kind of Echoes we might see in the city.
Maybe we'll come across some that look like you, a whole pack of them.
You're kidding me... Even in the Land of Echoes, I, Abby, will always be the most special one!
Hic!
...Approved. Welcome to Rinascita.
Excuse me. First-time visitors must cooperate for inspection.
Is this... a Reserved Terminal?
Reserved Terminals should be declared upon entry. May I see your declaration form, please?
...I didn't know about that.
I didn't declare it.
These are the rules. I'll need you to cooperate.
Forgive the inconvenience. By the Order's decree, all visitors must undergo customs clearance to ensure safety...
...Or, do you have a guarantor?
(Show the invitation letter)
Someone invited me here.
Ah, I see you are a guest of the Montelli family. You are granted permission to bring your Reserved Terminal into Rinascita.
We apologize for any trouble caused. All Echoes, even those in Reserved Terminals, are seen as Divine Envoys. Once they are baptized, they too will receive Imperator's blessings.
Does that mean I can see the Sentinel in person?
I don't have any plans to do that.
Naturally! We are all "united" under the Sentinel's influence, free from "division."
The Sentinel is with you, me—all of us.
Their presence is eternal in our hearts, guiding us always...
Rest assured, for our Sentinel embodies peace, justice, modesty, and mercy. Laud Their name, and you will find solace!
Their presence is eternal in our hearts, guiding us always...
Preach with respect and patience, lest you induce doubt and confusion.
Acolyte Phoebe.
I'll take it from here. Greetings, esteemed guest. I am Phoebe, an Acolyte of the Order.

The city of Ragunna welcomes your arrival. Many visitors are here for the upcoming Carnevale. To ensure everyone enjoys the festival safely, the Order has tightened the customs procedures and added new regulations...
Some information might be overlooked on your declaration form. Please accept our apologies.
It's okay. Rules are rules.
Can we enter the city now?
Thank you for your understanding. Please follow me.
Certainly. Please follow me.

Before entering the city, you go through The Order's customs checkpoint. It seems they have additional regulations for Reserved Terminals. Fortunately, the Montelli family has already arranged a guarantor for you.

During the inspection, the Order members' elusive words confuse you, until Acolyte Phoebe arrives to clear up your questions.

With her guidance, you finally step into the city of Echoes.
Carnevale, delicious Carnevale…
Oh wait, I mean gelato…
Carnevale, delicious Carnevale… Oh wait, I mean gelato…
Hey there! First time in Ragunna? Well, let me tell you this—Carnevale isn't just for partying! It's our big chance to make enough money to last us all year!
Plus, what the Laureate says about food can totally be a game changer!
Take the Laurus Salad, for example. It used to be just a plain ol' salad, nothing fancy.
Then, one day, a Laureate casually mentioned that the Sentinel liked it, and bam! It became the most popular dish in town!
They say the Sentinel's always watching over us, especially during Carnevale. Who knows, maybe They'll even show up as one of us!
And if They try our gelato… well, it might be just the thing to hit the spot!
Hmm... something's wrong with that Vitreum Dancer...
An Echo lost control? H-how could that be possible?!
Someone call the guards! Hurry!
What… just happened? How could a Common Echo harm people like that?
A Divine Envoy doing this… it doesn't make sense…
Wait, is that one of the Montellis' Echoes? I heard theirs aren't exactly considered "Common Echoes"…
Alert the Servitude Hall now! We need that Vitreum Dancer under control!
We must get security tightened around the Montelli Quarter.
Nooo! My pizza! I didn’t even get a bite! D-do you think the Sentinel’s gonna punish me for wasting food…?
Oh, don’t be silly. It was just an accident. No way the Sentinel would care about that...
O Sentinel above... Is this your fury? Are you trying to warn us...
Follow this road and you'll reach the Nexus.
To the Ragunnesi, the Sentinel is the Divinity, a holy beacon guiding our way.
We hold the Sentinel and all Their gifts in the highest reverence, especially the Echoes, which bear profound significance to both the Order and the people of Ragunna.
(...You've been hiccuping for a while. Do Echoes get indigestion as well?)
(H-how am I supposed to know? I haven't had anything to eat since we left for Rinascita. So hungry...)
Bakie! Are you okay?
Beep beep!
Thank goodness you're alright...
An Echo attacking humans? Right before the Carnevale? That’s wild…
Rumor has it, the Montelli family’s Echoes are "filthy"...
So the Montellis are behind this mess? Ha! Now that would be top-shelf entertainment!
Hmph, isn’t the Montellis the one pushing this whole Carnevale? And they can’t even control their own Echoes? A Vitreum Dancer show? Really, that’s their big idea?
They keep saying it’s for the people, but who actually buys that? It’s all about the money, fame, and power for them.
Ignoring past "truths," shrugging off the Order's warnings, disregarding public safety!
