But this isn't the section I oversee. Why am I here... Why are you here?
Lady Carlotta has tasked us with a special delivery. May I see your ID, Ms. Lily?
I only have this card.
Thank you. Hmm... Confidential Researcher? The vault does have that position, but a researcher shouldn't be in this section.
The ID is real—the anti-counterfeit features check out.
She doesn't look like she could be a thief's accomplice, either.
That thing you're carrying seems to disagree.
The Order's relics are kept a secret from everyone, including an Acolyte like myself. I can't say what it's reacting to.
But... I do have a strange feeling about Ms. Lily.
We shouldn't leave her here.
We should bring her with us.
She could accidentally trigger something dangerous if left alone. That's the last thing we need.
Agreed. And if she is somehow involved, we'd save a lot of effort by taking her with us.
I'm sorry, ma'am, but you'll need to come with us.
I understand your hesitation, but with the vault sealed, you'll be safer with us.
Alright, I'll come with you.
Good. Time to use your clearance, {PlayerName}. Let's find out what's really going on in this vault.
You encounter a vault employee who claims to be Lily, but she can't remember why she is there. Although you find Lily's identity suspicious, for her own safety, you invite her to accompany you.
More guards are gathering.
The longer the vault stays in lockdown, the more defense systems and Echo guards get activated.
Someone's hiding over there!
Ma'am, does the name "Ash" mean anything to you?
Old Ash? He used to say he wanted to sleep among the Echoes to study their behaviors. What a stubborn man.
So the real Ash did exist. As for that man hiding over there... he might have stolen Ash's ID and gotten stuck here.
Ash's ID was stolen? Outsiders couldn't have done that—we've been in here for at least twenty years. Even with my fuzzy memory, I know that much.
Twenty years?!
Is this a vault or a prison?
Twenty years in this vault... Sounds like a living hell...
If it were me, I could maybe last... Well, ten years tops.
But... no one should be working in such awful conditions, Ms. Zani.
Yeah, well, personally I just hope to live long enough to make the most out of my retirement someday. Anyway, we've got an imposter on our hands posing as "Ash."
Let's take the train to the Echo depository. We must find this thief and retrieve the security module. After that, we can decide what to do next.

You use your access to review the surveillance footage, while learning from Lily that she has been working at the vault for at least twenty years, and the "Ash" you encountered earlier was actually an imposter with a stolen employee ID.
In order to recover the security module, you decide to take the train to the Echo depository.
Stay alert, everyone. During training, I was told to avoid the Echo Depository unless absolutely necessary.
Each Echo is unique, and trust me, you don't want to know what happens if one gets damaged.
Don't worry about us, {PlayerName}! Just focus on operating the train Echo!
Hold tight! It's just the safety mode kicking in!
Are you alright, Ms. Lily?
I'm fine. Be careful.
Ha... I didn't expect this fella in the vault.
Thank goodness, everyone's safe.
Mmhmm, I see. You've done a great job—
Oh, {PlayerName} and Ms. Zani! Nice to see you again!
Hi there, Phoebe.
Hello again, Acolyte.
It's been a while. Mind if I ask what you were doing just now?
Oh, we're just chatting. They seemed lonely. Not many people talk to them.
This train Echo? It's been running since the vault was built. It chugs along, doing its thing in silence.
But I do believe your company has made its day.
But if I remember correctly, you are not the representative the Order informed me of.
Yes, it was supposed to be another Acolyte. But she's busy with the Order's work, so I volunteered.
Huh. Did the thought of working with the Montellis scare her away?
Perhaps, Ms. Zani, but I'm sure she'd think differently if she met a Montelli employee like you.
Seeing as the Montelli family and the Order are both blessed by the Sentinel, our paths were bound to cross eventually.
...I'm glad you see it that way. Now, do you have it?
Certainly, as you requested, the escorts carried an empty case while the relic stayed with me.
Thank you.
What's inside?
What exactly is this thing?
It's an important relic entrusted to the Montellis. That's all I know.
Same here, but it doesn't matter. Lady Carlotta gave me this job. I just follow orders, no questions asked. That's how you work for the Montellis.
Our top priority is to get the job done, nice and clean.
By the way, {PlayerName}, the device from Lady Carlotta should have top security clearance, so you'll be able to operate the train Echo. I hope you enjoy driving.
You and Zani head off to meet the representative from the Order. To Zani's surprise, it is Phoebe, the Acolyte who joined your adventure before.
Tsk, the imposter just ran away.
There's a book. What is this...
It looks like a letter sent to his grandson. And this paper... was it torn from a book?
The book you just picked...
It must be from this book.
Hmm... I can't understand a word.
I can make out a little. It seems connected to cryptography.
It's an Echo book, young lady, and it seems fond of you. You think you're reading it, but it's actually the book communicating with you.
An Echo book? Incredible.
Yes. It doesn't speak, but it responds to the questions you ask. The more time you spend with it, the more you'll understand it.
Old Ash carried this book everywhere. I heard it even helped him design a coded lock for the vault.
That letter you saw is indeed a page from this book. I remember Ash tearing it out in a fit once. We all made him clean the bathroom as a punishment, hehe.
So, Ash left this letter to tell his grandson about that mysterious "secret cache." Turns out it really does exist.
Then the "Ash" we're chasing now...
He probably found out about the cache from the letter and is attempting to steal it.
Exactly. It's just like Acolyte Phoebe said. He triggered the lockdown to get to the depths of the vault without interference.
If he'd acted like a professional and stuck to the plan instead of messing around, we wouldn't be in this mess.
We need to find him before he puts himself or others in danger. Plus we need the security module to leave. Let's head to the lower control room and check the surveillance cameras.
Since this book belongs to the Montellis, I'll hold onto it for now.

You find a note left behind by Ash for his family, mentioning a treasure deep within the Averardo Vault. You make the assumption that this is where the imposter obtained clues about the "secret cache."
You must get to "Ash" before he can trigger more defense systems.
A mask? Is this also an Echo?
Let me check... It says the wearer can see their true self through the mask's eyes and bring it to life.
Its last owner was rumored to steal other people's "desires" at will.
Hmm... but why did I only see myself?
This is...
Just a strand of hair. Nothing special.
The label says, "A strand of hair that once made a contract with the devil."
What does that even mean...
Watch out! It's fast!
Ha... what a pain in the neck...
The Echo Depository is in complete disarray. Make sure to keep your distance from all the Echoes.
The security clearance should give us control over the defense systems… I'll figure it out.
Look! He's there!
Okay, let's sort out the clues.
The lockdown is still in full effect, triggered when "Ash" removed the security module. To escape, we need to retrieve the module and use our clearance to reach the vault's depth.
On top of that, thanks to him, we're stuck dealing with the defense systems.
So, for both his sake and ours, we need to catch him as soon as possible.
How about we do it the other way around?
What if we approach this from another angle...
There must be a smarter way to go about this.
He's running blind, getting more desperate as the lockdown escalates. But there's only one way he can go.
And only one thing that can take him there.
The train Echo!
Makes sense. He has no choice but to go to the train Echo's terminus. So...
We beat him to the vault's depth and wait.
We wait for him at the final stop.
Without us chasing him, he'll follow the main route and trigger fewer defense systems.
That would save us a lot of trouble. I can help manage the security systems. With the clearance, I should be able to override some defenses and open shortcuts.
That should work. {PlayerName} and I will go retrieve the clearance. Ms. Lily, could you stay here and assist Ms. Zani?
Of course.
Let's do it.
Seeing there's no end to this chase, you decide to use the vault's defense systems to guide "Ash" towards the Echo train terminus and intercept him there.
I'm amazed it's so steady on tracks this steep!
Perhaps your earlier encouragement did wonders, miss.
Don't worry, {PlayerName}. I'm here for you!
No need to rush, {PlayerName}. Take your time.
{PlayerName}, can you hear me? The room to get the clearance is right ahead... Wait.
I see a group of Echoes heading your way. I'll operate the controls and try to block them.
Mind your step—research value aside, these are worth a fortune. Breaking one could land you a hefty bill from Lady Carlotta.
Besides their worth, I'd rather we handle this without hurting them... Watch out!
They just keep coming… We need to stop them.
I'll do my best to block them. Acolyte Phoebe, are you with us? This isn't the time for prayers!
It's finished. We can get the clearance now.
Are you okay?
Need a break?
I'm fine, really. It's just like hauling the Codex around back at the Order... But, uh, {PlayerName}, why are you staring at me like that? Is something wrong?
Stunning work, miss. If I hadn't seen this myself, I'd never believe your staff was meant to be used like that.
Yes. Very impressive.
Striking with an appropriate level of force clears the mind, enhancing one's purification.
Well, well... since when did our Acolyte start cracking jokes? Looks like {PlayerName}'s humor is rubbing off on you.
Uh... I wasn't joking.
Ahem. Maybe you should grab that clearance before they wake up.
This should be the place.
Great, it's working now. One moment... Okay, take the nearby shortcut to the train station. We'll meet you there.
That was close! Are you alright, {PlayerName}?
Nice moves! Don't worry about me. I'll keep up.
What's this?
Zani, what happened?
I smell trouble.
The vault's security mode has been activated. Someone touched something they shouldn't have.
Thieves?
Unlikely. All personnel were sent home at the start of this assignment. The highest security protocols are in place too.
Should we ask for outside help?
We can't, not while the vault's security Echo is there. It's capable of sensing danger.
Once it detects a threat, it locks down the vault, jams all signals, and activates a bunch of troublesome Echo guards.
Ha, a triple whammy.
That means there's no way out and no hope for backup...
Any backdoors? The Montellis must have designed one.
There is, but it's a bit tricky. Anyway, we need to access the security room first. Your clearance might come in handy.
Don't worry. Keeping you safe is part of my job.
Alright, let's go.
Everything's under control now. The vault schematics show the next stop is the terminus. That man has nowhere to hide.
But I'm not sure where the terminus is exactly. The Employee Manual only states that the Echo Depository is located at the vault's depth, without any further information about the station.
My memory is hazy... I do remember something dangerous out there, but that's all. I'm sorry.
It's alright, Ms. Lily. May the Sentinel guide our way.
Whatever it is, we have no choice but to move forward.
Right. Let's get this done quickly, {PlayerName}.

You manage to find "Ash," but he jumps onto a train before you can grab him.
Still, everything is going as planned. The train runs on a single rail, and the final stop is where you will catch him.
Ugh, it's getting more ferocious.
Don't worry, {PlayerName}. We're all here with you.
Well, Sentinel above, if you can hear this, please keep us safe.
Phew... Is everyone alright?
Thanks to the train Echo, we're still in one piece, though I have no idea where we are now.
There should be other train Echoes available, right?
We'll need it to get to the terminus.
Please wait... Ma'am, are you hurt?
She seems lost in her thoughts.
Did you remember anything, ma'am?
I'm fine, child. This place feels so familiar. It's like I've lived here for a long time.
Any details you can remember would be useful. Since employee training didn't touch on this area, we'll be going in blind in search of the exit.
Hmm... this place. I've been here before with many others, but their faces are a blur...
Yes, we rarely left this place, but I do remember taking the train somewhere very dark...
You've been here before?
Somewhere very dark?
Don't be nervous.
Are you suggesting that people used to live in the vault?
Yes, if I'm not mistaken, a group of scholars made a home for themselves here.
It seems the vault's structure is more complicated than we thought.
I take it that this "very dark" place you mentioned is the terminus.
"Somewhere very dark"... What kind of place could that be?
We'll be just fine. Ms. Lily, take your time remembering. We'll take it slow.
Plus, we need time to find the exit.
Let's get going. We need to retrieve the stolen security module. That's our key to getting out.
You unexpectedly arrive at an unmarked area on the map. Here, Lily seems to recall some memories.
"In memory of those who persist in the dark to keep the light. Though our names shall be removed from history, the truth we seek will one day dawn on Ragunna."
So, people actually lived here before... Ah, Ms. Lily's name is on it, and the name "Ash" too.
These look like diaries. It's not very polite to read them without permission—
"When the green leaves turn red, everything will be back to normal."
Ms. Zani!
We need to be thorough. I'm sure the Sentinel will forgive my intrusion. Anyway, it's just some person's diary.
Your conclusion might be a bit far-fetched, Ash.
Far-fetched? For the Sentinel's sake, I've been in the Echo Depository for seven straight days gathering data!
Even so, incorrect is still incorrect. Here, take a look at this control group...
Acolyte, should we bring these Reverberations back to the Order Tribunal?
I think your misunderstanding of the Order runs deeper than you realize, Ms. Zani...
My apologies. But why is that thing in your pocket still flickering? Did I say something wrong? Or is it because I haven't prayed to the Cathedral in three months?
It's just flickering, not burning or reacting in any other way. It should be fine, I think...
When will all this end? Any ideas, Ash?
I suggest you ask those artists. The day they stop tearing up drafts, we can finish the research.
I'm not talking about the research. I mean us—when will we finally get out of here?
And you're believer, right? Why not just ask the Imperator when we can leave?
...Until the Sentinel gazes upon Their land again.
It won't be long. I've heard the situation is improving. The Montellis even promised to send letters to our families.
Are you available now, Lily? There's a problem with the results you gave me.
Lily? Are you there? Lily?
Lily...
Ms. Lily...
I'm all right child. We shouldn't dawdle here.
Bad news. I know nothing about deciphering passwords.
You might want to try the Echo book. It's an expert at this sort of thing.
It's nothing but riddles to me.
Ms. Zani, the book says the password is "0622," those numbers refer to...
The date when an innocent truthseeker was wrongfully convicted by fools. I remember, but the memories hurt.
They never hesitated to sacrifice for the truth. They shouldn't have had to carry such a burden.
Faith tells me that the truth you sought will eventually come to light, Ms. Lily.
Perhaps, but for now we must stay focused on what lies ahead.
This vault... feels suffocating.
I find it comforting. There's no idle chit-chat here—just work, plain and simple.
Can you pray to the Sentinel on my behalf, miss? I'd rather not run into any more trouble.
With you and {PlayerName} here, there's no need to worry!
Be careful, it's on alert now! You need to force it to stop!
Be careful!
Are you feeling alright, Ms. Lily?
I remember it all now... Yes... I'm no longer...
Well, Mr. Criminal, thanks to your actions, we've had to wreck these priceless artifacts.
If you stole anything else from the vault, I advise you to surrender it immediately.
Hmph, you Montelli dog! I couldn't care less about that so-called "secret cache"! I just want this place destroyed for good!
Open your eyes! This isn't a vault. It's a nightmarish prison!
You locked up my grandfather, and now you want to do the same to me!
You must be the young Ash. I've seen your picture, child. Old Ash spoke a lot about you.
As for this vault... Yes, it's nothing but a prison.
Ms. Lily...
But we chose this imprisonment—not just our bodies, but our very souls. Freedom was never an option.
We had to erase every trace of our existence to survive, to discover, to create.
...What do you mean?
We followed in the footsteps of our predecessors, but one day, we unexpectedly uncovered a hidden chapter of the Order's history.
They hunted us down in the name of preserving stability, stripping us of our rights as researchers and artists.
The Montelli family took pity on us and came to our rescue. They feigned loyalty to the Order and locked us in this vault, but in reality, it became a refuge for outcasts like us.
Five years, ten years, twenty years...
We've been trapped here for far too long. None of us have returned home.
Ash thought of you till his last breath, my child. He asked the Montellis to send you the letter he wrote on his deathbed, hoping to impart a will to thrive.
As for that "secret cache"... If you have the chance, you should go and look for it.
We are counting on you now.

You defeat the Echo guards and corner "Ash." Lily now remembers everything: She, along with many researchers and artists, had been imprisoned by the Order and were deprived of their rights to research and create.
The Montelli family built a sanctuary deep within the vault to protect them. They lived their final moments here.
Lily's soul can finally rest in peace. Before leaving, she urges "Ash" to check the vault's secret cache.
So, the Montellis didn't imprison Grandpa... he chose this path himself...
That thing he mentioned in the letter... I...
Please cheer up, Mr. Ash. Everyone was blind to the truth as you once were, but now, we know everything thanks to you.
Very touching, but I'm not as forgiving as our Acolyte. You have a price to pay for breaking into the vault.
The exit is open. You're free to go now. I'll stay to tie up any loose ends.
Thank you for helping us again, {PlayerName}. I thought this would just be a routine job.
I'm used to it.
You're welcome.
Here's the reward Lady Carlotta promised. Naturally, she did not forget to include a little "overtime pay" for your efforts.
By the way, miss, I'm sorry but I'll need to take that relic from the Order. Don't worry, the rules still allow you to come and go as you please.
Of course. I need the Sentinel's enlightenment on certain matters... but I'll still be around if you need me.

Ash learns about his grandfather's fate and the truth about the vault's secret cache. He will now bear the consequences of his actions.
The path has been opened. It's time to leave.
The secret cache... So this is it... Grandpa's true wish...
So, you managed to find this place, {PlayerName}.
We sifted through all the documents on old Ash and the vault before finally locating it.
Here it is. This tree—the one where "the green leaves turn red."
When the persecuted entered the vault, they would take the elevator to the upper levels for a background check before continuing.
For them, the last glimpse of what could be called "scenery" was just this tree on the island.
But this tree, fed by barren soil and still waters should never have been able to turn red.

By the way, the Order is still up to no good. That relic the young Acolyte brought was a bomb. It reacted to the Reverberations here in the vault... Ha, looks like I'll have to investigate the matter myself. If this keeps up, I might never retire.
You discover that the "secret cache" is actually a tree, and the item the Order requested the Montelli family to transport was a bomb that would react to the Reverberations in the vault.
Are you praying for them?
No... not really. Just bidding them farewell.
A resolute soul needs no guidance. I simply want to understand the future they've paved the road for.
You've been a great help. Thank you. Lady Carlotta mentioned she left you a special bonus downstairs.
I have other matters to attend to. Until next time.
She will find the path worth her devotion.
Greetings. The Averardo Vault is in lockdown. Please proceed to the train Echo station and take Line 1 to evacuate the vault.
We need to go to the evacuation site. When will the train depart?
We won't be taking the train for now.
Understood. Current train Echo passengers: 0. You may depart at a time of your choosing.
Perfect. Do we need anything to board the train?
We won't be taking the train for now.
To depart on Line 1, please present your employee ID, or temporary ID, and a valid emergency pass issued by the security room.
(Present the clearance device.)
We won't be taking the train for now.
Verifying now. Please wait.

Please present your emergency pass to board the Averardo Vault's train Echo. Running on a specially designed track, the train Echo ensures an evacuation that is both efficient and convenient. We wish you a pleasant evacuation.
How can we get this emergency pass?
We won't be taking the train for now.
Please demonstrate lawful vault entry by presenting an emergency pass issued from the security room located in the next depository. It may be accessed by the train Echo.

Once you obtain an emergency pass, you will be authorized to board. Running on a specially designed track, the train Echo ensures an evacuation that is both efficient and convenient. We wish you a pleasant evacuation.
Hold on...
We won't be taking the train for now.
Are you seriously telling me that I have to go deeper into the vault to get out of here?
Processing... Please present your emergency pass to board the train Echo of the Averardo Vault...
I've had enough!
...It seems I won't be taking the train.
I ought to take you to the scrap yard.
What are they, Ms. Zani?
Not sure, but we'd better take them down.
Active security mode means all the main routes inside the vault are sealed. But with your device, we should be able to override their protocols.
Keep an eye on the surveillance cameras—they're all interlinked. Guards will be summoned if you're detected by one for too long.
Watch out! It's starting to move!
Take them. They're the "personal bonus" Lady Carlotta arranged just for you.
These Echo guards are controlled by the security system. You can also command them with your clearance.
The higher your clearance is, the more obedient they become.
You actually fixed it. What a genius move, miss.
Oh, that's nothing. If they relapses, I'll be back to perform more percussive maintenance.
Be careful, {PlayerName}! Something's coming our way!
It's a special Echo guard. Tsk, I didn't expect it to follow us this far. We gotta lose it!
Once we activate the clearance, we should be able to access the elevator.
Security lockdown… That's odd. The Employee Manual says this mode can only be activated by...
Um, miss. If I may, what are you doing?
Me? Oh, this Echo seems to have a headache. I'm trying to help.
Wait, even if it is malfunctioning, you shouldn't hit it with your—
Beep... Bleep...
Depository One security module malfunction. Lockdown detected. Emergency pass override activated. Line 1 temporary access granted. Please evacuate via the nearest exit.
What the?!
Is something wrong, Ms. Zani?
No... never mind.
Perhaps it can help us deactivate the alarm.
I'll give it a try...
Somehow, the silent Echo seems to respond to the gentle mumbling.
They're willing to help us!
Here it comes again. Watch out, its attacks are getting faster.
Hold tight!
Interesting. It's labeled as a donation from the Order, but the cabinet is empty.
"The air collected before the Lament."
Ha, it might have some research value if it's real.
Please note that no Echoes were harmed in this quest.
There are several tracks reserved especially for us. Just switch over when you see the sign.
The security control room in this depository is right ahead. You can put your device to good use there.
Each depository has its own security room. Just verify your device here to obtain security clearance. It's only valid for this depository, though.
Sounds complicated.
Necessary for the vault's security, but yes, it's a hassle.
We're stuck here for now, and the only way out is to get clearance from each of the depositories. That means going deeper into the vault.
How much deeper?
Beats me. The security room only controls the depository it's in and grants access to the next.
So, aside from a handful of senior members of the Montelli family, no one knows the full layout of this vault?
I don't know. Maybe a handful of people who've worked here for over thirty years might.
Let's get clearance first. It might help us avoid most of the defense systems triggered by the lockdown.

After finally arriving at the security room, Zani informs you that to leave the vault you must use your clearance to access its deepest area.
She suggests you utilize the vault's cameras to avoid any possible defense systems.
Attention all staff. Please cease work at once and leave the vault. We wish you a pleasant day.
Don't worry, it's already been approved by the higher-ups. They see this as a valuable opportunity to work with the Order and as such requested your assistance.
Sigh...
Are you alright, Phoebe? Do you need a break？
No, no, I'm okay!
"A mysterious scroll painting that leads to a secluded retreat."
I heard a tiger ironsmith wielding a greatsword lives inside this scroll.
I see.
Okay, leave it to me.
Is this the right way to do this?
It worked! Let's go, shall we?
The door is open!
Now we need to find the train Echo station. Once we reach the depths of the vault, we'll catch that fool.
What the hell is this thing!?
Ugh, clumsy.
Watch yourself. It's coming at us.
Do the Montellis have a love for building labyrinths?
Not really. It's all for the security of the vault.
With top clearance, you should be able to disable some of the cameras. Give it a try.
Maybe we can make a detour from this side...
Wait... something's off with this thing. Has it been tampered with?
Let me see... Tsk, someone removed the hidden security module.
Check the log file with your clearance... There it is, it was taken by "Ash." The name rings a bell...
Yes, the Employee Manual mentions an old employee named Ash who designed most of the vault's security features. But he passed away.
This is only speculation, but what if this "Ash" stole from the vault and took the security module? That would explain why a complete lockdown was triggered.
What's a hidden security module? Is it like a key?
Pretty much. It's the monitoring core that powers this entire depository. If we don't get it back, we'll be stuck here for good.
A vault employee could easily access the module, but nobody would dare steal it. Everyone knows that'll trigger a lockdown of the entire vault.
But what if that's exactly what they want?
Think about it. There's no one in the vault except for us, and all comms are blocked. It's the perfect opportunity for a thief.
Don't tell me they're searching for... Never mind, we need to catch this rat before they cause us more trouble.
It seems this "Ash" also had access to the control room. Could it be... that old woman?
Let's go find out.
After reviewing all the surveillance footage, you discover that a person named "Ash" might have taken the vault's security module. You'll need to find Ash to leave.
Why are we getting a day off all of a sudden? What about the meeting today?
Woohoo! A day off! I heard Margherita's just put out something new on their menu. Perfect timing!
Great idea. And since we're getting off this early, there won't be a line, right?
Right, I do have some time off now, but there won't be an extension for the deadline, which means I'll have to take the rest of my work home. So...
So... we don't have to work anymore?
Initiating self-diagnosis... Self-diagnosis canceled by default...
Security lockdown activated. Please evacuate immediately!
The Echo train experienced an accident and fell, but fortunately, no one was injured. While the train Echo itself seems to have sustained only a minor scratch, it is now unable to move...

Sails of the departed drift on and on, souls above the clouds, hearts claimed by the sea...
Oh, hello, {PlayerName}.
Is that one of your new songs?
It is... this one came from a rather unusual experience.
Tell me, {PlayerName}. What do you think of the sea?
Why do you ask?
Someone once said the sea is a city of the dead. You can hear the endless cries of the wind and waves, but never the voice of anything living.

When you spend days, weeks, maybe even years adrift, loneliness creeps in and twists despair into something monstrous. And yet, when you see a flicker of light out there—something you dare call "hope"…
That's when people stop thinking straight.
Is this from someone from the Fool's Troupe?
No, it was someone who's long gone now.
He died ten years ago in a shipwreck. I wasn't there to see it happen, and his face has almost faded from my memory. But...
But?
On my last voyage, I saw him. He was on another ship. A lively one if I might add. I could hear the laughter and clink of glasses.
Hold on. Didn't you just say it's rare to see anything living on the sea?
Exactly. That's what makes it unusual. When I saw him, he looked just as he was all those years ago, not a single day older. And in that moment, everything I'd forgotten about him came rushing back.
Are you saying… he might still be alive?
Surviving ten years on the sea, without even a scratch? What do you think, {PlayerName}? How likely is that?
Almost impossible, right? My thoughts exactly.
Yet when the light of "hope" is right in front of you, you can't help but chase after it. No matter how violent the waves or impossible the odds, you have to see it for yourself.
Sadly, when we got closer, Battier and Brant reported back the waters were teeming with Tacet Discords.
If another ship were to stumble across that area…
It would end badly. No doubt about it.
That's why I need your help, {PlayerName}.

I'll admit, this seems more of a personal request from my side. But when you're out there dealing with those Tacet Discords or trying to find the man, regardless of the results your safety comes above all else.
What does this man look like?
He had the same blue hair and eyes as me. He used to call it the color of the sea, a blessing from the ocean itself.
After he died, I stopped believing in nonsense like these. Most sailors still prefer to hold onto their superstitions though, as a way to boost their spirits before heading off to sea.
{PlayerName}, I wish you safety... and the best of luck.
{PlayerName}, welcome back. How did it go out there?
The place was overrun with Tacet Discords.
So it's already…
I didn't see the man you mentioned.
Ah, I see... Thank you for trying, {PlayerName}. Can you tell me more about what you saw?
You describe what you saw to Levito.
Sea fog, never-ending tides of TDs, distant voices on the wind... {PlayerName}, it reminds me of an old story I heard as a child.
Sailors, weary and broken after battling storms and endless waves, find their minds playing tricks on them. As I said before, loneliness can evolve into something unbearable.

In those moments, if a door appeared before them. Bright, warm, and inviting. Even if it led straight to death, many would still choose to walk through it. All for a glimpse of happiness that feels so real they'd gladly give everything for it.
So these waters… is a trap. The TDs are luring people in.
I believe so. And the longer those monsters are left unchecked, the more lives they'll claim.
I'd like to ask another favor of you, though I understand you've got plenty of other tasks to tend to...
I do have a lot going on.
But it's not like I can't make time.

I've learnt about your reputation of being quite a busy person. So don't feel pressured in taking on the task. Feel free to come by whenever you have the time to spare. I'll think of other ways to handle it in the meantime.
That said... I do prefer that you make use of that time on some relaxation.
Are you planning on a reward for me?
Of course, if that's what you hope for. I do not want anyone else to have to experience the loss of hope any longer.
Don't worry. I've made my peace with the idea that he did die ten years ago. Maybe that's not such a bad thing after all.
Ten years have passed for me, but for him? He'll stay forever young. I think there's something beautiful about that—it's the kind of ending that belongs in a song.
Thank you, {PlayerName}. I'll leave the rest in your capable hands.
However, if you do lend me a hand, I'll make sure you're rewarded properly.
The TDs have been growing in numbers lately. I'd be grateful if you could lend me hand when you have the time, {PlayerName}.
A strangely shaped wooden handicraft, with a seashell carved at the top.
The introduction mentions that this artifact was salvaged from an ancient sunken ship from Ragunna. The seashell on it likely represents the Ragunnesi's past beliefs in the seas.

Subject: Averardo Vault Tour Guide (Underground Depository Zone)
 
Welcome to Averardo Vault! We hope you have a wonderful and unforgettable time here.
 
The main areas of the Underground Depository are as follows:
 
1. Precious Metals and Artworks Depository
This section primarily stores valuable metals and rare artworks. Some of the items are displayed to the public on a rotating basis. Below is a partial list of recommended exhibits for this month:

Stern's Ceramic Jar
The beloved ceramic jar of the famous comedian Arthur Stern! After receiving the Laurel, he retired from the stage to focus on the art of pottery. This jar is one of twelve masterpieces he personally painted.
Recommendation Rating: Five Stars!

"Deepening Stars"
The painting of an anonymous artist, depicting the starlight reflected from beneath the abyss. Critics have debated the theme of this piece for years, making it a highly controversial and discussed piece.
Recommendation Rating: Three Stars!
 
2. Echo Depository (Currently Closed)
This section primarily houses Echoes.
Important: The Echo Depository is no longer open to visitors.
 
3. [Data Deleted]

[Work Log]
 
8:30 AM: Clocked in. Today's task is to perform an inventory check of the artworks inside the depository. Great, let's get to work.
 
12:00 PM: Lunch break. A new guy tried to ask me about the rumors surrounding the "secret cache." It's honestly surprising how long these baseless rumors have managed to stick around. Even if there was some secret cache, it's not like that's something we Level 1 folks are supposed to care about.
 
5:30 PM: Work is wrapping up for the day. On the Echo Train ride back, Jason thought it'd be fun to spook the newbie with one of those corny old ghost stories. Something about a mysterious, unmanned train that only runs at midnight and takes passengers to the Vault's "underworld." There, spirits of the dead rip apart anyone who dares trespass in their domain. I've heard enough of these kinds of stories. If there really were any mysterious trains, I would've seen one by now.

Whoa... It's a meteor shower!

Don't mention it. It was the right thing to do.
Come on. We should make a wish!

Well, then...

With you as the matriarch, the Fisalia family will surely have a new future.

Let us simply admire this wonderful performance.

Upon seeing you, "Sparky" dances back and forth before scurrying off in a flash of light...
Hey, wait up. I know it's happy to be free and everything, but geez, what's with all that excitement? Didn't even give us a chance to say goodbye...

(Night of Remembrance? Is that another special event in Egla Town?)
(And this message… Is it a prank? Or is there more to this?)

Ew, why do I still smell it down here? Wait, this weird frequency… It's coming from that message!

Hehe… Things have returned to normal, it seems. How delightful.
It's late… Would you care to come to my castle and rest for the night?
I'd love that. I could use a good rest.
It will be my pleasure. Let me walk you home.
Cantarella's lips curve into a gentle smile, her eyes, calm as the ocean depths, rippling with a hint of warmth.
She knows you're stronger than her, but her instinct to care for you remains, as natural as the breath she takes.
Oh, the pleasure is mine, my dear.
With you here, this castle feels… warmer. Your presence may have dispelled the chill that used to linger.
The Fisalia family...
The Divine Trials...
Our family's purpose has always been clear—to resist the Threnodian's spiritual interference and hold fast to our faith in the Sentinel.
The cruel trials were designed to find a Maiden with an unbreakable will, someone who could withstand the Threnodian's whispers and fix her eyes on the true light.
Yet, in pursuit of that "noble cause," innocent lives were sacrificed without question.
I can't accept the so-called "necessary sacrifice," one that tramples the will of others in the name of duty. It's nothing but living off the weak.

After all, we are more than just firewood.
So, you chose to offer your own strength...
So, you sought a different way...
Yes. When I took up the Sword of Divinity, I felt a <ano=Fleurdelys>presence</ano>, someone far more capable, more suitable. A new possibility emerged.
I asked the Sentinel to transfer my Second Awakening power to that girl.
The Sentinel had always wielded the power of separation, but instead agreed to my proposal to combine our strengths. With that power, she confronted the Threnodian.
We triumphed, for the moment, but the Threnodian proved to be more difficult than we expected.
To stop the brutal Divine Trials and secure us the final victory, I chose to become the family head, drawing on every resource available to achieve our goal.
I pretended to align with the Order to keep the Threnodian off guard, all while searching for a way to fully liberate the Sentinel and end the Threnodian once and for all.
And then... I found you.
So that's why you took me straight to the Sword of Divinity.
You must've gone through a lot.
Hehe… I have been watching you from the moment you set foot in Rinascita.
Now, I daresay I know you inside out.
Just as you chose your path, I've chosen mine. I will see it through, whatever it may cost.
Besides, compared to what you've endured, my hardships aren't worth mentioning.
You defeated the Threnodian in the Inverted Tower, saved the people of Rinascita, and freed those young girls... and me as well.
The girls are now back home, and the Threnodian's whispers have finally faded from this castle.
And with the Order's concessions, the shadows over Rinascita are vanishing. Peace has come to us once more.
Thanks to you, the days of pain and sacrifice have ended. A calm life… that is the miracle you've brought.
As the head of Fisalia, I must offer you a fitting reward for all the efforts you made.
An elixir for eternal youth, perhaps? No, judging from the power of your Awakening, it seems you may already possess that.
Then, let it be the elixir that turns stone into gold.

That's too much.

Hehe, this is "our" home now.

Here, a special elixir I've prepared with Albizia flowers—their gentle, lingering fragrance can waft through reality into your dream.
Now, close your eyes... and rest. Good night.
Hi, {PlayerName}!
Thanks to you, we're finally back home, safe and sound!
And Jojo's fully recovered, too.
Ms. Rosemary at the Apothecary gave me this special medicine! Just a tiny dab, and the pain's all gone!
She said it was from Ms. Can… something… Oh, I can't remember. Grown-up names are always so hard to keep straight!
Anyway, it's from a very nice lady!
And anyone sick can use it, too! Yay!
We survived, but at what cost? Is it a blessing? Or is it just more to carry?

But if you die, you lose everything. No more chances. No paths ahead.
Besides, as survivors, who are we to say whether the dead found peace?
Just being here, with thoughts and worries and even fears… That's its own kind of happiness.
How marvelous! I hear the sounds of birth and doom, of everlasting mountains and seas, and the fierce pulses of life!
This is life's symphony, each note threaded by the loom of time, more alluring than any Siren's call!
As promised, here is the first riddle: The Siren's Song.
"Long ago, a group of girls followed the Siren's call out of town. They journeyed to the 'crown' atop the mountain and to the waterfall that cascaded into the depths."

So Annis is just a legend?

Oh, no, child. Annis is as real as hope itself.

If you're strong enough to hold on, Annis will come to you.
I've conducted over a hundred visits and interviews, traveling between Thessaleo Fells and Egla Town. Finally, I think I have a theory...
It seems that these regions are experiencing a phenomenon—mass hypochondria, if you will.
For example, many people claim to have seen an ancient knight they believe is still alive.

Yet, after combing through records over the past few centuries, I have yet to find any concrete evidence for Annis's existence.
Medically speaking, it seems more likely that these are hallucinations brought on by intense mental strain.
When someone is under severe stress or endures deep trauma, the mind might create an external figure to ease the pain, like a survival mechanism.
Think of the pressures of strained family ties, the toll of years of competition, and hallucinations induced by toxins...
In extreme cases, one's own identity can fragment, conjuring up an imaginary figure.

I never imagined life could feel this carefree.

Well then, might I suggest we collaborate to secure this reward?

Without exceptional insight and unparalleled courage, all you'll end up with are mere scraps.

Cantarella gives you a reassuring glance.

"The girls lined up for their apples, each one in a vivid, glistening red… but why would apples appear in the deep sea?"
Whether it brings "luck" or "misfortune," taste it and see for yourselves.

Heads up signifies good fortune, a sign of following the sacred path. Tails up, however, invites misfortune, a mark of defiance against the Divinity.
The front of the coin features a doll in a red hat, while the back shows one in blue. The coin has an unusual appearance, with uneven, ribbed edges.
Are these dolls blessed or cursed?
Perhaps the last riddle will give us a clue.
Hmm, which is the most beautiful among these dolls?
This one has bright eyes, that one has a nice nose, and that one there has red lips… Wait, this one's gotta be a bit less pretty. Can't let it outshine me!
Ugh, so frustrating. They're all gorgeous, but none quite live up to my standards!
Now tell me, what do you think? Which doll stands out the most?
(Pick the doll in a red hat)
(Pick the doll in a blue hat)
(Look for help from Cantarella)
They all look the same to me.
The lucky red hat! Exactly! Following the divine will is always a wise choice.
Defying the divine will is a reckless gamble with your very life at stake—one I wouldn't advise.
Without waiting for your response, Invidia hands you a doll with a red hat.
Cantarella's gaze seems to reflect a stormy sea, veiled in layers of mist that hide her feelings. After a moment, she picks up a doll with a red hat.
If we obey the divine will, does that really bring us luck?
Haha, I like your honesty! Yes, they're all pretty much the same, aren't they?
Here, take this one.
Invidia tosses the red-hat doll your way.
Wonderful! As long as you follow the Divinity, luck will surely be on your side!
Now, for dessert, I present you with fortune cookies.
This is the last riddle: The Round Hat.
"A girl dons her red dancing shoes and wears a scarlet hat, ready for the final act of her performance."
Now, all the riddles are in your hands! Whether the answers will rise like bubbles from the witch's cauldron, well, that's up to you.
As you hold the doll, its features suddenly sharpen and become lifelike. Its delicate brows, bright eyes, and elegant attire seem to come to life in the blink of an eye.
Bells chime, spirits awake. Mask up for the ghost parade! Welcome, dear guest. Are you here for the Night of Remembrance?
What is the Night of Remembrance?
Yes.
It's the only night in a year when the lost souls return to the mortal realm! Wear your mask and blend into this special gathering. You never know who or "what" might be hiding behind the mask…
Well, well, that's a plain reaction. Can't scare you, huh? Alright, let me explain it properly.
The Night of Remembrance is an annual festival in Egla Town, dedicated to honoring those who have passed. When night falls, people dress up like ghosts and join in a variety of activities.
And… Er… Oh dear, can't quite remember the rest.
Ahem! Anyway, to satisfy your curiosity, why not see for yourself? All you need is a mask.
Fabulous! All you need is a mask.
(Take out the mask.)
Like this one?
This is… the mask of the Laureate! What an honor to meet the new Laureate in person! Yes, this one will do perfectly!
The Laureate enjoys the same privileges as the host of this festival, so please, enjoy yourself tonight!
Now all the riddles are here, like fish returned to the sea. However, they are entangled in a maze of seaweed.
How would you free them from the maze?
Analyze the keywords of each riddle.
Find the connection between these items.
The Siren's Song, the Red Apple, the Red Shoes and the Round Hat…
Among the tales of Rinascita, all these three end bitterly.
However, with the Laureate's aid, we may see a different ending tonight.
Since all stories are rooted in reality, perhaps we should take a closer look at the three items we've collected.
Let's see... A dusty broken music box, a cog-like "lucky coin," and a doll in a red hat.
Let's see... A dusty broken music box, a cog-like "lucky coin," and a doll in a red hat.
They're all out of production now. None of the music boxes these days use this kind of cog.
Looks like these little trinkets are relics from the past.
They can be assembled into a ballerina music box!
How about we put them together?
Good catch. As a girl, I used to while away those endless, quiet hours in the castle by playing with such things.
Perhaps some part of me still remembers what to do… No, I'm certain I still do.

Cantarella places the doll on the music box's pedestal and slides the cog-like coin into the slot. Click—the missing cog clicks back into place. Just like that, the fish breaks free from the maze of seaweed.
It seems all we need is the Laureate's performance to breathe life back into this old relic.
The show begins.
The melody evokes a sense of familiarity, reminding you of that place—<ano=Castle of Fisalia>Porto-Veno Castle</ano>.
It only strengthens your suspicion that the "ghost girl" must be connected to the Fisalia castle.
A sharp headache interrupts your thoughts, the distorted frequencies intensifying. Through the pain, you find a reason to visit the Fisalia castle.
Ugh… what was that…? My head… This pain's getting worse. I need a break somewhere…
You've been under this influence far too long, especially in a place filled with spirits. I should have warned you sooner.
You need a proper rest… and we're not far from Thessaleo Fells.
Come to my castle. I have potions there that can help ease the strain.
Hope this can help you feel better.
Thank you. What's this?
Smells good. What's this?
This potion is crafted from freshly crushed Barnacle Leaves, mixed with the sap of Violaca, Sea Okra, and Sea Apple, all fermented in a glass vial.
Each of these lovely plants is cultivated here, hand-picked, sorted, and blended by my own hands.
As the poisonous ingredients entwine, their toxins soften over time, like nightmares transforming into the sweetest dreams.
Don't worry, it's perfectly safe and even delightful. Drink up, and rest a while.
Though I may not be able to lift the "curse" binding you just yet, I can certainly help tame it for now.
Ah... Excuse me for a moment. It's time I tend to the flowers.

The potion eases your headache, bringing clarity to your mind. 
With renewed focus, you try to explore the castle for more clues.
You find a young girl hiding behind a plant, peering at you with wide, timid eyes.
Her round red hat draws your attention, a striking resemblance to the one worn by the dancing doll in the music box.
Sensing that her presence here is no coincidence, you brace yourself to ask her some bold questions.
Excuse me. Who are you?
What are you doing here?
Are you one of the "ghost girls"?
Do you know where Cantarella is?
The girl attempts to speak, but all that escapes is unintelligible mumbling.
The girl nods decisively before running off to another area.
Are you playing hide-and-seek with me?
Are you trying to show me this plant?
The girl shakes her head and then points at a crimson plant nearby. Its shape resembles an apple, yet it seems more like a peculiar marine creature.
The girl nods. The crimson plant resembles an apple, yet it seems more like a peculiar marine creature.
Apple... apple in the sea... Sea Apple!

Sea Apples are known to be poisonous. This clue must be key to solving the riddle of the Red Apple. 
Before you can ask the girl anything more, she has already run to another spot.
The girl nods. The plant resembles an apple, yet it seems more like a peculiar marine creature.
Jellyrose... Round hat...
Could the round hat worn by the girl in the riddle actually be a poisonous Jellyrose Medusa?
If that's true, then the "ghost girls" indeed have a connection to the Fisalias.
I need to discuss this with Cantarella.
The girl nods decisively before running off to another area.
You find Cantarella finishing a dance under the moonlight. Her graceful movements seem meant to regulate certain frequencies.
Ah, you've made it here. I'm glad to see you're feeling better. Now we can finally have a proper conversation.
Did you come all this way for me, or are you in search of the secrets slumbering in the deep?
I come for you.
I come for the secrets.
Both.
Oh, I'm flattered… Don't worry, with someone as precious as you here in my castle, I'm not going anywhere.
Hehe, clever little fish… Have you figured it out? The answer has been right here, waiting to be discovered.
Hehe, such greed… Rest assured, I'm here to unravel the secrets with you, as I promised.
What exactly are the Sea Apples and the Jellyroses in the garden used for?

The crimson Sea Apple, also called "the alluring reaper," is a dangerous plant. A single bite can lead to paralysis, suffocation, or the excruciating pain of a burnt throat and torn organs—ultimately bringing its victim an agonizing death.

As for the Jellyroses, their blooms will transform into Jellyrose Medusae. These little ones can produce a neurotoxin that induces intense hallucinations, and in extreme cases, causes the body to seize and twist in a violent, uncontrollable dance of death.
The two lethal plants have been meticulously nurtured by generations of the Fisalia family, flourishing within the gardens of Porto-Veno Castle for centuries.
So my guess was correct. The "Red Apple" in the second riddle refers to the Sea Apple, and the "Round Hat" in the last riddle points to the Jellyrose Medusa.

As for the first riddle, "Siren's Song," the "crown atop the mountain" and the "waterfall that cascaded into the depths below" clearly points here—a crown-like castle that sits atop a jagged cliff, with a waterfall rushing down.
It seems the girls in the riddle were lured into the Porto-Veno Castle.
The strange frequencies coming from the music box probably reflect the suffering of the "ghost girls," who were poisoned and tortured in the castle.
But why? Why would the Fisalia family do this?
I don't believe you'd engage in such senseless cruelty or take pleasure in others' suffering.
There should be a reason behind this… Wait, there's one Fisalia tradition that might explain it. The Divine Trials.
It's a ritual to select a maiden of extraordinary willpower, a Fisalia who can withstand the Threnodian's whispers. I assume such extreme methods were needed for the trials.
Well… I never imagined you'd solve the mystery so quickly. You never cease to amaze me.
The truth behind the "ghost girl" riddle is none other than the grim secret of the Divine Trials.
The blood and tears shed in these trials throughout the years have seeped into this castle and concocted what we now call <ano=Sonoro Sphere>the Sea of Ghosts</ano>.
There, past and future intertwine, and Fisalia's ancient secrets cling to the cracks of time like grotesque scabs.
With you by my side, I would relive that trauma, and unfold the layers of forsaken time for a closer look.
And if… you find these scabs have somehow crept unto my very flesh and feel the need to cut them away, I'll place my full trust in you and leave it in your hands.
Why do you trust me so much?
Can I trust you?
Ever since I guided you to the sanctuary… you've seen through me and all that the Fisalia family conceals.
I've witnessed you cleanse the chaos of the Inverted Tower, restoring order to the heavens and seas. If you are the one to pass final judgment on me… it would be the highest honor.
Absolutely. Remember my promise? Whether it's elixir or poison, I'm ready to explore it with you.
I, Cantarella Fisalia, value every promise I made to you and vow to see them through.
Now, the answers we seek lie in the depths of fierce undercurrents… Will you join me and dive into the deep sea?
Sure. I'm good at swimming.
Of course. I've seen it all.
Yes. We must free those ghosts.
Yes. I have to remove the influence on me.
Then let's dive in together.
You're like a pearl from the deepest sea, but… I'd never let such a flawless gem endure even the smallest scratch.
I knew you'd say that.
Your wisdom, courage, and kindness… no matter how deep the waters, always shine through.
Mmm, the strange frequency you carry is indeed from the Sea of Ghosts.
That message with the distorted frequency is no doubt a creation of this Sonoro.
I don't know why it reached you, but the answer is hidden within. After we uncover the truth, its influence on you will fade.
Once we enter the sea, I'll be right by your side, tightly. No poisonous creature shall harm you.
For you are the one I've chosen.
I think I'm ready to go now.
I need some time to get ready.
Excellent. Together we dive into the Sea of Ghosts.
Of course. It's wise to ready yourself before diving into such perilous depths.
I'll be waiting for you in the garden, whenever you're ready.
So, prepared to set out?
I'm ready.
I need a moment.
Excellent. Together we dive into the Sea of Ghosts.
Take your time. I don't mind lingering here a little longer with my beloved Violacas.
Would you like to proceed, honored Laureate?
Yes, please.
I need a moment.
Perfect! Please, follow me.
Of course. Please take your time. I'm here to assist whenever you need me.
What a pleasure to meet you again, {PlayerName}.
So, what brings a distinguished Laureate to this ghostly place?
Tired of heavenly views, are we? Hehe, are you here to savor the underworld's wonders and dance with its spirits?
What brings the head of Fisalia here?
Why not? What harm could there be in a ghost of the deep reveling among spirits?
So you're also a ghost of the deep.
"Also?" What are you implying?
You show the strange message to Cantarella.
On the Night of Remembrance, it's only natural that the departed return to the mortal realm for their unfulfilled wishes.
Still, it'd be best if they didn't stir up trouble for the living.
In my humble opinion, lost souls find peace only when their wishes are fulfilled. Then, perhaps, they'll stop haunting people.
Since fate has brought you here, why not offer your aid to those poor, restless souls? I'll join you, of course.
I don't usually do ghost work.
Why would you offer to help me?
Ah, the familiar confusion of a first-timer. But fret not, for I will be your guide through this unforgettable night. Step by step.
Shhh, no need to jump to conclusions. Who knows, it might actually be you doing me a favor.
Every Night of Remembrance brings its own theme. And this year, it's the "Ghost Girl."

Imagine this: an innocent girl lost in the dark sea, fear ripping her apart as her soul drifts away, while her body sinks ever deeper into the abyss. Despair consumes her, bit by bit, until she transforms into a monstrous phantom.

A thrilling story, don't you agree? Like savoring a medium-rare lamb chop served with oysters. One tender slice, and the crimson juice spills, adding just the right flavor to the already exquisite dish.
I like exquisite things, too.
Not sure I love it.
You're making my skin crawl.
Huh… So we share similar tastes. How wonderful.
Oh, really? Then consider it a simple "appetizer" for tonight.
Oh, is it too much for an innocent lamb like yourself? Hehe, my apologies. I hope this doesn't dampen your spirits.
Offer your soul, surrender your flesh. Give all you have, call the lost from their rest...
That sounds uncanny.
Oh, sorry. Forgive me if it unsettles you. It's an old folk song about the Night of Remembrance. They say its eerie melody has a strange frequency that can draw the attention of ravenous "demons."
Ah… I can feel it now. There it is—the first stall.

Cantarella steps forward with unwavering certainty, her movement ethereal, drifting like a ghost. At this moment, she seems capable of summoning demons herself. Without hesitation, you follow her lead.
Will the lost souls truly return home?
It's been nine years...
Sometimes, it feels like they actually return to us on the Night of Remembrance.
Yes, but only on this special night...
Look! It's the new Laureate!
My oh my, but who's beside her? Looks like some kind of noble lady.
I'd say she's no ordinary noble. Such grace and maturity… she's got to be from a prestigious family.
Hmmm, the nearest land with a noble house is Thessaleo Fells, which belongs to… the Fisalias?
Just look at her dress! Such elegance! She's not even eclipsed by the Laureate. She must be someone of great importance.
I've heard the Fisalias are super secretive. Never thought we could actually see one here.
I know, right? How lucky are we to meet them both tonight!
Wait a second… If people like them are showing up, could the rumor about the elixir actually be true?
Yeah, that makes perfect sense!
Blue and purple clothing inspired by the sea… Is she a Fisalia?
Fisalia? Ancient nobility, known for their fondness for poison, power plays, and their ties to the Order. One of their own even made it to Primus, if I'm not mistaken.
Wait, how do you know all this?
Novels, of course! Mysteries brew imagination, you see.
I'm not a noble myself, but I can definitely read about them. Just think of it as a fun tidbit.
But the Fisalias aren't just any nobles to gossip about… What if they poison us?
Relax! They can't know who we are with our masks on...
It doesn't matter if you're wearing a mask or not. With just a wave of their hand, they can unleash a deadly smog and finish us off!
Seriously? You're joking, right? Even those novels didn't mention anything like that!
They've allied with the Order to control the Common Terminals. Plus, they might have tricks up their sleeves we can't even imagine! We'd better watch ourselves!

You receive a strange message from a "ghost girl." The twisted frequency within it affects both you and Abby. 

To uncover the mystery and lift its effects, you decide to attend the Night of Remembrance in Egla Town, as mentioned in the message.

The guide briefs you on what the Night of Remembrance is. It's an annual festival in Egla Town, dedicated to honoring those who have passed. People dress up like ghosts at night for various activities.

The guide tells you to wear a mask for the event, and you show him the mask of the Laureate, which works perfectly.
I am after a particular elixir myself.

Cantarella tells you that three riddles entwined with the tale of the "ghost girl" are hidden among the stalls set up for tonight.

Whoever solves all three riddles and uncovers the mystery of the "ghost girl" can ask the host for an elixir that grants any wish. You're skeptical, but Cantarella seems intrigued. You decide to join her.

Mammon, the owner of the first stall, says he will only give you the first riddle if you exchange something precious.

As the new Laureate, you offer a performance, which he gladly accepts.

Impressed by your performance, Mammon reveals to you the first riddle: The Siren's Song.

"Long ago, a group of girls followed the Siren's call out of town. They journeyed to the 'crown' atop the mountain and to the waterfall that cascaded into the depths below."

He also offers you a music box.

As Cantarella tinkers with the music box, you notice its shape resembles an apple.

Inspired by your observation, she solves the first riddle and leads you to the second stall.

The owner of the second stall is Beelzebul, who asks you to pick the freshest apple in the stall. After you find the correct apple, Beelzebul gives you a "lucky coin" and reveals the second riddle: The Red Apple.

"The girls lined up for their apples, each one in a vivid, glistening red… but why would apples appear in the deep sea?"

The coin isn't perfectly round, with its edges ribbed and uneven. The front of the coin features a doll in a red hat, while the back shows one in blue.

Cantarella picks up on the clue and leads you to the third stall... But, isn't collecting these riddles going a bit too smoothly?

Dolls wearing red and blue hats are placed in the third stall. The owner, Invidia, asks you to pick the most beautiful one. But no matter which one you choose, she insists on giving you the doll in the red hat, claiming that the red hat symbolizes divine will and brings luck.

She then tells you the last riddle: The Round Hat.

"A girl dons her red dancing shoes and wears a scarlet hat, ready for the final act of her performance."

You realize that the music box, the cog-like "lucky coin," and the doll in a red hat can be assembled into a ballerina music box.

Cantarella puts the parts together and you perform once again. This time, the music box plays.

After reading the strange message you received, Cantarella explains that the Night of Remembrance is centered around ghost-related themes. Tonight's theme happens to be the "ghost girl."

She senses the effect on you and invites you to join the event, promising that you'll recover once you solve the riddles prepared for tonight.

As the music box plays, the red hat doll materializes and dances, only to abruptly stop. You realize it was all an illusion, but the music reminds you of Porto-Veno Castle. A fleeting shadow crosses Cantarella's usually calm face.

A sharp headache interrupts your thoughts, the distorted frequencies intensifying. You seize the moment and ask Cantarella if you can rest at her castle, and she agrees.

The girl points at a crimson plant nearby. Its shape resembles an apple, yet it seems more like a peculiar marine creature.

You realize it's a poisonous Sea Apple, which may be the key to solving the riddle of the Red Apple.

Before you can question the girl, she runs to another part of the garden.

The girl points to a jellyfish-like plant, its crimson bloom resembling her own round hat.

Could the round hat from the riddle be a poisonous Jellyrose Medusa? If so, the "ghost girls" are tied to the Fisalias. You need to speak with Cantarella about this.

The girl seems to understand and runs off, gesturing for you to follow.

Cantarella lets you rest in her garden and brings you a potion to ease your nerves. You feel much better after drinking it.

Cantarella then leaves to attend to other business, giving you a chance to search around.
You spot a girl wearing a red round hat among the bushes. She tries to say something but can't speak, instead gesturing for you to follow her.

You follow the girl to the corner and find Cantarella dancing, her steps seemingly regulating certain frequencies. 

You share your thoughts with her, and she admits that the "ghost girl" refers to the cruel Divine Trials of the Fisalia family. The blood and tears from these trials have twisted Porto-Veno Castle into the <ano=Sonoro Sphere>the Sea of Ghosts</ano>.

To uncover the truth and lift the "curse" binding you, you must dive into this Sea of Ghosts.
You prepare to send the girls back to their homes. Before you leave, they say their final goodbyes to Cantarella, thanking her for everything she's done for them over the years.

The Night of Remembrance ends smoothly, and the girls return to their homes. The lingering influence over you and Abby is lifted, and everything returns to its usual calm.

It feels like nothing ever happened, as if it was just a fleeting night's dream. But you know it was real, because Cantarella stands right beside you.

She acknowledges that you're stronger than her, but that doesn't stop her from instinctively caring for you. She invites you to rest at her now peaceful castle.

It's just you and Cantarella in the castle now. She opens up to you, sharing her thoughts.
 
The Fisalias have always fought to resist the Threnodian's spiritual interference and hold fast to their faith in the Sentinel. The cruel trials were designed to find a Maiden with an unbreakable will, someone capable of withstanding the Threnodian's whispers.
 
Cantarella can't accept the so-called "necessary sacrifice" that strips others of their free will, but she understands it's the only solution. Therefore, she transferred her Second Awakening power to find a solution where no one else but her would be harmed.
 
She pretended to align with the Order to lull the Threnodian into complacency, all the while searching for a way to liberate the Sentinel and defeat the Threnodian once and for all.
 
And then, she found you. Alongside Cantarella, you shaped this peaceful, happy ending, a miracle born from both of you.
(Cantarella? What's she doing here?)
In the bustling event, you spot Cantarella in the crowd. She smiles at you from a distance and signals you to follow her.
Let me think… the switch should be in the other room.
Light floods the room again, but your keen senses tell you something is different.
We've scoured every inch of the backstage, including every shadowed corner.
It seems the Round Hat isn't here.

Various paintings pile up in the art room, their pigments emitting a gentle glow. They all appear to have been painted recently. But... does someone as busy as Cantarella have the leisure to paint them?
Round Hat... for you.
Take them.
The doll thrusts a Round Hat into your hands with no further explanation.
The red velvet of the hat gleams, as if coated in a girl's shimmering tears. It's like a maraschino cherry on a frosted cake. Sweet, yet bitter.
The doll thrusts a Round Hat into your hands with no further explanation.
At long last, the final performance.
Dance! And fight!
The Maiden's crown will soon appear—
And rest upon one among you.
Round Hat. Thank you.
Odd… but, thank you.
The final performance. Begins now.
Go. The front. Closer… clear… reassured.

The doll's broken words seem to suggest you step closer to the stage for a clearer view. 
But "reassured"… Who should feel reassured? You? Or the doll? The answer may lie ahead, once the performance begins.
The doll thanks you for bringing her the Round Hat and invites you to the stage for the final performance.
Show time. Need light.
The doll's face is expressionless, yet its gaze lingers unmistakably on the lamp in your hand.
Light. Lamp.
The frequencies... are in such a disarray... It will be hard to switch between worlds now...
The frequencies... are too chaotic...
No worries. We'll try again.
(Strained breathing)
You must be Annis.
And also Girl A, who couldn't speak but managed to send me that message.
You want me to find her, right?

You figure out who this girl with a red round hat is. She must be Annis, the silent Ghost Girl A who sent you that message. But why hasn't she aged over these years? There's no time to dwell on this question now. After all, saving Cantarella comes first.

Annis offers to help. She closes her eyes and holds the lamp. A brilliant light appears, reigniting the lamp's glow, yet Annis vanishes in its wake.
We'd better watch ourselves! They might have tricks up their sleeves we can't even imagine!
How dare she show up in the town after everything they did!
Will the lost souls truly return home?
So... painful...
Ergh...
The Cantarella I know is unbreakable.
She will never falter even if you drown her with all these malicious whispers.
And you certainly won't shake me, either.
All those years of lying and scheming, and what have you gained?
A tarnished reputation? You could have walked away from this, Cantarella.
I still remember the little you. The youngest, the most neglected of all the Fisalias. You always lingered by your cauldron, and only smiled when a bird fluttered past the window.
You despise this place, don't you? But the blood in your veins... it binds you, holds you prisoner in this endless nightmare.
You loathe our rules, yet they have already seeped into your very existence.
Tell me, have you ever considered leaving? Let go of this burden that crushes you, and you'll be free as air, free to live the life you've longed for.
My dear lord, I've already gifted you the sweetest of dreams. But why do you still cling to this earthly burden?
You watched with satisfaction as I climbed over the fallen, ascended the steps to glory, and wore the thorned crown... Was that not enough for you?
Illusions are no match for poison, Cantarella. False bubbles burst, and here we are—the end of it all.
Well, you see, illusions can also lead to true beauty.
Your obsession, corrupted by whispers, has become a shadow over the castle… A deluge of delusions that shouldn't exist in this world.
I can feel the pain those whispers inflicted upon you. Allow me to free you from them... once more!

Years ago, Cantarella used illusions to deceive the late head of Fisalia, seizing his position and ending the cruel trials. But his remaining obsession, corrupted by the whispers, has lingered in the castle and turned the place into the Sea of Ghosts.
 
Together, you and Cantarella set his lingering will free.
The abyss may reside in shadows, but even the deepest darkness cannot endure the touch of light.
Your trust strengthens the lamp. It now burns brighter.
Now is the time. Let the light shine brighter.
Now! Free him from the Threnodian's whispers.
We haven't fully banished the whispers. Watch out. The twisted obsession is returning to the shadow.
My lord, I offered you the sweetest of dreams and safeguarded your legacy when you departed.
I have entrusted Fisalia's true faith to one most deserving, and the Threnodian's deceptions in the Inverted Tower have been laid bare.
No more whispers shall haunt us. Our children are freed from the cruel burdens of those trials.
Now, you too shall find release from the Threnodian's whispers.
They aren't ghosts, are they?
So, this is the answer?
Heh, nothing escapes your eyes, does it?
We're here, alive and well!
In that hellish duel, Cantarella shielded us with illusions.

As the lingering obsession of the late head of the Fisalias fades, the Sea of Ghosts vanishes.

With the hymns rising around you, you find yourself in the sanctuary, where the girls who are supposed to be dead stand in front of you, all safe and sound.
It all started
with a false hope
An elixir to grant any wish
was said to be here
We dived into darkness
Choked down fear
Nothing's here but the deep... and ourselves.
The elixir
was our blood and tears

gave us sweet dreams
At last
