we reached the end
Once Cantarella took charge of the family, she shielded us, keeping us safe in the castle's depths.
The Order's members were always prying, eager to find out the truth... I knew if we went out recklessly, we'd only invite danger.
Though... I really miss my home, more than I can say.
Fortunately, Cantarella holds the Night of Remembrance every year. With our masks, we can slip away, even just for a while, back to our village.
It's always a great comfort to see Jojo living happily and in good health.
My dear, from this night forward, you're free to be with your families.
The {Male=gentleman;Female=lady} here has solved the riddles. Together, {Male=he;Female=she} and I will craft the elixir of revival.
Wait, what's going on?
I think I'm getting the picture now.
Since the Threnodian's lies were unraveled, the frequencies and situations on the outside have shifted.
Thanks to you, the Order is now entangled in its own troubles, too distracted to reach into the Fisalias.

Most deeply affected by the Threnodian's whispers was the castle—where the former head was trapped, where innocent girls were lost to the trials... As the Threnodian fell, all these frequencies broke out at once.
The long-standing fear, pain, resentment, and repression—all that the whispers had suppressed burst free, becoming a new cage.
The shackles of one's spirit were heavier than those from the outside. Yet, thanks to you, we shattered those shackles together.
I knew then... the time had come for the girls to finally go home.
I never meant to draw you into this. I was planning to shoulder it all alone. That's why for this year's Night of Remembrance I took part myself, and as host, I chose "ghost girls" as the theme.
My plan was to break through the Sea of Ghosts, claim that I've solved the riddles and won the elixir of revival, and then use it to send the girls home when the Dance of the Dead begins at midnight.
What about the letter I received?
What about the influence on me?
Your arrival, seemingly by chance, was perhaps destined.
The letter wasn't my doing, but I think I know who brought you to my side.
She had no intention of hurting you with the abnormal frequencies, but she had been in the twisted Sonoro for too long... long enough that she was nearly one with its frequencies.

When I saw that letter and sensed something unusual about you, I realized you could no longer stay out of this matter. With a special constitution, you were affected by the frequencies overflowing from the Sea of Ghosts.
Looking back, my arrogance blinded me... Ah, forgive me, for showing you this weak side of myself.
The currents here run deep, and the tangled seaweed is thick. Even I can easily become ensnared.
But you… you helped me untangle these knots and weathered the torrents by my side.
Thanks to you, the elixir was much easier to make. That's why I said, a skilled brewer is far more important than the ingredients or the process.
Please, accept my heartfelt gratitude. Thank you for being here, and for staying by my side.
Cantarella, you don't have to bear it all alone anymore! You've got someone you can truly count on now.
Hehe, you're right. I have one last favor to ask, {PlayerName}. Could you take the elixir and see the girls home on my behalf?
The Fisalia doesn't enjoy a good reputation, and some villagers would resist my presence. At this point, causing any complication is the last thing I want.
You, however, as the Laureate who exposed the lies and turned the impossible into the possible, will carry a weight they can't ignore. If you're the one to handle this, the people will be convinced.
Besides, even if the Order intends to look into this "miraculous revival" later, your status and capabilities will hold them back.
But putting all that aside, it's with your effort that this elixir was possible. I can think of no one more fitting for this task.
I'll help until all is settled.
Don't you want to clear your name?
Thank you. Both I, and the entire Fisalia family, will aid you in any way we can.
Names are like sea foam that easily fades away. It hardly matters to me. Besides, it may not be a bad thing for people to stay wary of the Fisalias.
After all, we're a large family, with deep-rooted issues. Change takes time.
Girls, gather your things. It's time to go home.

You learn from Cantarella that since the Threnodian's lies were uncovered, the frequencies and circumstances around Ragunna have shifted. The time had come for the girls to finally go home.

She admits that she never intended to involve you and had planned to handle everything herself. That's why for this year's Night of Remembrance, she took part herself and chose "ghost girls" as the theme.

She had meant to dive into the Sea of Ghosts alone, claim she had solved the riddles and obtain the elixir of revival. This would allow her to send the girls home during the midnight Dance of the Dead. 

But Annis's message led you to her side to complete the plan.

Something falls from the fading chaotic frequencies. 
Its form is twisted, like a lump of flesh torn from the abyss. 
It's a book.
Knock on the door three times.
Smash the door.
Toss a Shell Credit at the door.
A strange sensation creeps into your hand as you knock. You immediately sense the shift in the surrounding frequencies.

Your fist passes through the door. It's there, yet not there.
Like striking water, no matter how hard you try, the force is swallowed by the endless sea.

Nice try, but this is not a wishing well, not to mention it's reckless to make wishes to the Sea of Ghosts.
The abyss seems to have no interest in devouring you now and returns your Shell Credit.
Behind the door, you catch the faint scent of seawater-soaked pages and the soft sound of jellyfish tentacles brushing through the waves.
Knock on the door three times.
You find this door familiar.
You're tired of knocking on it.
The cacophonies from behind the door are like high waves going to burst out of it.

Yes, it's the third, no, maybe the fourth time it appears. Or more likely, it just keeps regenerating itself, again and again.
Perhaps the door also recognizes you as it snaps open and drags you inside.

However, the abyss will never get tired of you. Since you have nowhere to run in the deep sea, your only choice is to face it.
The door opens wide anyway and pulls you into the waves.
But can the glimmers from these delicate drifters truly light up the entire sea?
Yes, just place it gently here.
I, Cantarella Fisalia, value every promise I made to you and vow to see them through.
Besides, there are certain places that only you may be able to reach.
Come now. We've more to uncover.

A bizarre poster announcing the "final performance."
The two dolls on it look strangely familiar.
We'd better watch ourselves! They might have tricks up their sleeves we can't even imagine!
How dare she show up in the town after everything they did!
Will the lost souls truly return home?
So... painful...
Ergh...
Hmm... Our delicate little friend seems to have slipped above us.
I'll find us a way.
Is this still Porto-Veno Castle? Something feels… off.
Yes and no. The past has spilled into the present here.
The overflowing frequencies have enveloped the entire castle, forming this Sonoro, the Sea of Ghosts.
The voices of the ghosts rise faintly from the depths, like the soft pop of a bursting bubble. Listen closely to these whispers of the past.
Piece together these fragile clues, and the answers will emerge on their own.
But do take caution. One wrong step in these murky depths, and we may be drawn into an endless abyss…
With a bit of light, though, we can hold back the darkness.

You and Cantarella enter Porto-Veno Castle, which now looks a bit different.

Cantarella explains that the twisted frequencies have overwhelmed this place, displaying a mixture of past and future.

She manages to keep the last ray of light in this dark abyss and stores it in the lamp.
Though the black of the sea is overwhelming, I've managed to preserve the last ray of light.
You see, light is something that darkness can never fully devour.
As long as it flickers, it can guide us out.
I, Cantarella Fisalia, hereby grant {PlayerName} unrestricted passage through Porto-Veno Castle.
Let us explore and weave through the past and future together.

Cantarella gives you the lamp of light and grants full access to the castle.

With this lamp, you are now able to switch between the past and the future.
We are now in a fragment of the "past"… You've done well.
The past that emerges from the Sea of Ghosts is not entirely real.
It only reveals what it chooses to show, which means we must uncover the hidden truth ourselves.
Spirits bound in the cracks of time, wander no more.
Please, set them free with the light.
They've been trapped here for far too long.
A few written lines appeared on the surface, seemingly the last message left before the frequencies dispersed.
(A potion that can grant any wish… Sounds familiar.)
The girls must have been lured here by such impossible promises.
Cantarella, since you were part of the trials yourself, why not just tell me the secret?
There, there… We're surrounded by twisted frequencies. It seems they're guiding us towards the truth of the Divine Trials, and that truth holds the key to solving the "ghost girl" mystery.
During the trials, the ever-present abyss silently watched over us… I can feel the Sonoro Sphere has recreated that same ominous gaze.
If I were to reveal everything about the past all at once, this Sonoro could grow unstable or even collapse, drowning us in its wake.
To keep us safe, we must tread carefully and avoid taking reckless actions.

Is something the matter, Cartethyia?
I just wanted to know how you're doing.
... Ah, so you do care. Good to know my efforts weren't wasted.
She...hung up. Was that meant as encouragement?
Everyone shows kindness in their own way.
The refreshments are ready. Please, sit.
This moment of peace is all the more enjoyable with you here.
Right this way.
This is it.
What we saw earlier. Was it some kind of message?
We should look into it.
There may be more to Tyrvine than meets the eye.
The Dark Tide...
But why then...?
I'll make sure all your efforts...
...Will not be in vain.
*Waaaaagh*
Did you know that Echo well?
Cadanto was my first Echo after I joined the Order.
When I stood against the Threnodian, he took a mortal blow meant for me and fell to the Dark Tide...
I never thought he'd come back as a Tacet Discord.
But he still recognized this sword...and was still trying to protect it.
Haultier was my saber. I practiced with it often in sparring sessions with Cadanto.
Looks like he's still trapped in the past, doesn't it?
We must finish this and free Cadanto.
This is it.
He's a tough cookie!
I wanna eat...
Eh?
I'll handle this.
Please allow him to fight at your side.
Fleurdelys, wilt thou return to me?
Someone must expose your lies. As long as there is a sliver of hope, I will not give up.
Is that so? Then I shall reveal the truth.
Fleurdelys...
Why dost thou resonate with me?
What...?
Why dost thou hear into the minds of the faithful?
Why dost thou act as my Oracle?
All this, and yet thou does not question?
Shut up!
The answer... is this.
Fleurdelys... Thou art my creation!
I made thee. Thy life, thy hopes, thy will, thy past.
All that thou are, I made "whole," I made "perfect."
I fed upon the trust, adoration, and longing heaped upon thee by the masses.
Thy resonance brought forth the second Dark Tide.
Ahhhh!!!!
Wh-wh-what?! Those clashing frequencies just... calmed down?!
That feels way better.
Looks like Abby's settled down. It seems we were both affected.
So it seems...
I'm starting to remember everything, just like you sensed I would.
The force that modulated the Sentinel and Threnodian's frequencies came from me.
Though it wasn't what I originally intended, I think having you take it from here may be for the best.
Why do you say that?
This crown... it turned into what it is after the Dark Tide came.
This is what the Threnodian uses to control Its Resonator.
When the Threnodian unleashed the second Dark Tide, "I"—as the Cartethyia you see before you—split the part of myself that wished to live after seeing the corruption that stood before me.
I chose to be broken from the very beginning to escape the Threnodian's inevitable grasp.
You see, when I destroyed the Threnodian that had taken over the Sentinel's body, It immediately began to assimilate into Fleurdelys, Its Resonator.
She was the part of "me" that was left after I split myself. She retained the most power, and now hopes to one day destroy everything... even herself.
The Threnodian's endless whispers and screeches are slowly chipping away at Fleurdelys' resolve.
That's why she had no choice but to split her power's frequencies, just to buy herself more time.
But using such Resonance abilities came at a cost. The split frequencies... they needed a vessel.
Your memories...
We don't have much time left.
So, you see... I have been instinctively searching for someone to wield that power.
All that was given, possessed, or taken by the false Divinity, I must pass to the one capable of resisting It.
This is how I intend to lay the false Divinity to rest.
Not just Its life, but Its very existence for all time.
So you're saying that behind the last seal lies...
Fleurdelys, the part of me I left behind. The one that also contains the Threnodian.
Bound by obsession, till relieved of duty.
Today, the part of me that wishes to live on will vanish. Is it because my wish has finally been fulfilled?
Will you accompany me one last time?

After placing Haultir on its pedestal, you witness a vision in which the Threnodian reveals the truth: Cartethyia was created by the Leviathan, intended to be"whole" and "perfect." The people's adoration of her served as the Threnodian's lifeblood, and it was Cartethyia's resonance that brought forth the second Dark Tide.

The Cartethyia before you now remembers everything. The Sentinel's corrupted form had long since been destroyed, but the Threnodian's essence lingered within Its vessel, Fleurdelys.

Your journey with Cartethyia was part of her plan to destroy Leviathan for good, taking all the things the false Divinity had bestowed and using them against It. Not only to end Its life, but also to extinguish Its future.

The Cartethyia who has accompanied you these past three days is a fragment of consciousness—the part of her that wished to live in the face of the Leviathan's corruption.
Ah... seems like I won't get a chance to apologize to Cantarella.
Her preparations were futile.
... Please tell her I'm sorry.
This was where everything started, the origin of the second Dark Tide.
I have one final request. Now that you have the power to split and merge energy, there is something only you can do.
Please... use the connection I still share with Fleurdelys to bring the last fragments of her tortured consciousness here.
Then, with your power, remake us as one... and finally release us from this world.
Why...
That way... the Threnodian will remain trapped forever in a lifeless shell, unable to return to this world.
But doesn't that mean the end of the part of you that wishes to live?
I have lived my life to the fullest. I would like the ones who are left to do so as well.
Cartethyia has had her wish fulfilled. Now it's Fleurdelys' turn.
She seeks self-destruction, to end the Divinity, and with it, her torment.
She has lost all hope and believes that no rescue is possible.
Remaking us as one is the only way I can think of to fulfill her wish... or rather, grant her what "we" wish.
I was born to this world cursed. The Threnodian intended for me to live as a threat to others.
But the puppet born of Its wickedness will become the prison that seals Its fate.
"I" shall be whole again, true to myself at last.
A fitting end, don't you think?
I have reached my final destination. One last swan song, and then the lights go out!
I understand...
Thank you...
And... forgive me.

After arriving at the site of Cartethyia's coronation, she makes a final request. Instead of directly confronting the Threnodian's vessel, Fleurdelys, she asks that you use the connection she and Fleurdelys share to bring the last fragments of consciousness from the vessel here, so they can reunite.

This is the only way to trap the Threnodian's essence in a powerless shell, ensuring It can never return. By doing this, the cursed Fleurdelys will finally find the peace she has long sought. She asks for your help in illuminating the final path of your journey together.
Ahhhhh... I can't hold it any longer...
Why? Why are you doing this?! Neither Cartethyia nor Fleurdelys should continue to exist!
Don't go...
I heard your request...
But I prefer to handle this my way.
Not even whole, yet still ever so determined.
Cantarella...
Phaom brought me here. I'd have shown myself earlier...
But it didn't seem like the right time to interrupt.
Looks like what I prepared could still be put to good use.
Tyrvine...
The Sentinel's Sword. It will help you resist the Threnodian's attack.
What's inside?
To pass the Divine Trials, every potential Maiden must resonate with the Sentinel through Tyrvine.
Those who survive receive fragments of truth, but at a cost. Memories lost in varying degrees.
The lost memories fall into this Sonoro Sphere, each carrying faint traces of the Sentinel's power. The power within those fragments of truth.
Tyrvine absorbs this energy.
The Sentinel's energy flows through you. You are more than worthy of wielding this sword.
But you, Cartethyia... you alone must choose to wield it. Only then will it become the "Blessed Maiden's Sword."
Does it also hold the sacrifice you made?
No... My sacrifice was used up long ago.
At the time I resonated with the Sentinel, I saw..."you" through Their distorted eyes.
Or rather, I saw Fleurdelys battling the Threnodian.
In that moment, I made a sacrifice that would shift the balance of power.
Was it...
The energy I received from the Sentinel's Second Awakening.
I split it from myself and offered it back to the Sentinel so They could, for a moment, regain control of Their body.
Only by doing this could Fleurdelys seize the moment to kill the already tainted Sentinel.
So...
The real Blessed Maiden is dead.
But there is no reason why the "false" Blessed Maiden cannot herself become the "true" Blessed Maiden, is there?
A person of true character should never be defined by an inanimate blade.
Both you and I were cursed to be mere playthings of the Threnodian, but that doesn't mean we cannot reshape our fate.
Thank you... in spite of my curse, my life of hardship, I must still save what is true.
Had you not stopped the second Dark Tide... Well, it is we who should be thanking you.
Huh... at least you can't accuse me of ingratitude... I just need a moment's rest.
Apologies, but they're doing something rather important.
Please...
Do give them some privacy.

Cantarella approaches Cartethyia with the now restored Tyrvine in hand. Within it are fragments of the Sentinel's power, remnants of failed resonances from the Maiden candidates in the past.

"The real Blessed Maiden is dead." Cantarella sacrificed her Second Awakening with Imperator for a chance to destroy the Sentinel's corrupted form.

So now, why can't the "false" Blessed Maiden become the "true" one?
Abby?
Yep, I get it. We gonna yoink Leviathan out?
But all you have left is the energy I ate before. Are you sure that's enough?
Some things, you just gotta do.
Just as I expected... The Threnodian "took notice" of you the moment you learned the truth.
{PlayerName}, what you see in this sanctuary is the Sentinel in Their true form.
A majestic steed that galloped with the wind, not a creature of the ocean's depths.
The Order worships a half-horse, half-sea creature Divinity, a form the Sentinel assumed only after being corrupted by the Threnodian.
Although the Sentinel's will has yet to fade, who knows how much longer They can endure.
{PlayerName}. I wish to ask you to persuade the Sentinel of Jinzhou—Jué—to come to Rinascita. To save Imperator.
That's much easier said than done.
What makes you think I can do that?
In return, I will agree to whatever condition or request you make.
Both Jinzhou and Jué owe you their future. That makes you the only person capable of this task.
A Sentinel cannot leave its commissioned region.
Jué leaving Jinzhou would be a betrayal of duty.
Jué is still in the middle of a recovery.
I understand the position you are in. Word has it that you're currently staying at a hotel and are at odds with the Order.
Perhaps a stay at my estate would suit you, for the remainder of your time in Rinascita?
I can offer you a glimpse into Rinascita's past, and you'd be spared the Order's unwelcomed attention.
There might still be a path forward.
Carlotta once helped me interpret some stained glass images. The story it told was very similar to what you've described.
Only more biased towards the Order. It mentioned a maiden who would emerge as the Sentinel's Resonator and later save Rinascita.
Do you think that's also a lie?
Care to elaborate?
(Describe to Cantarella what was portrayed on the stained glass.)
The part regarding the maiden isn't entirely fiction.
The Sentinel does indeed appoint a maiden to be Their Resonator, though not in the way the Carnevale would have you believe. No, it's through resonance with a very particular artifact.
That's not how Jué found Their Resonator.
That's because Imperator wields the power to split and manipulate space.
With it, They can withdraw a portion of power. That power's frequency will match the Imperator's own.
This is how the Sword of Divinity—Tyrvine—came to be. A blade sealed with the very powers of the Sentinel, and the artifact used to select Their Resonator.
To resonate with the sword is to resonate with the Sentinel. Only the chosen one may hope to draw it.
Then... what about Cartethyia?
The Martyred "Maiden"...? The nature of her resonance is unclear to me.
Perhaps she resonated with the Threnodian, or perhaps with the Sentinel in its corrupted form.
But choosing her could not have been the Sentinel's will. That's because...
The Maiden was already dead.
What?
Are you saying the real Maiden was already chosen?

In the past, each year the Fisalia family would hold the Divine Trials to select those with the strongest will. These young women would attempt to resonate with Tyrvine's powers—while Overclocked, of course.
Though none succeeded, some saw fragments of the truth hidden within the resonance.
I was one of them... There was a moment, where I glimpsed the Sentinel's corrupted form and the inverted ruin suspended in the sky.
I also learned that only Tyrvine can break the barrier of that Sonoro Sphere.
When I awoke from that vision, I discovered a line of words inscribed onto my hand.
I would never mistake my own handwriting. That is precisely why I am searching for other possibilities.
The words were—"The Maiden is dead."
(An inverted ruin suspended in the sky... her and Cartethyia's descriptions bear many similarities.)
(If Tyrvine is the key to entering the Sonoro Sphere, it stands to reason that Imperator may have played a role in the Sphere's creation.)
(If I can confirm that Tyrvine was truly left by Imperator, at least it would prove that neither are lying.)
(Cantarella said she was Overclocking when she tried resonating with Tyrvine.)
(That's exactly what happened with Jinhsi. Could Imperator be trying to restore Their power through a Second Awakening?)
(If that's the case... my permission should cause a reaction. That's one way to confirm what they're saying.)
Can I get a closer look at the sword?
Would you mind if I tried to pull out the sword?
By all means.
...I suppose all that's left is its symbolic value.
However, do handle it with care. It is a family heirloom... I've heard of your unique methods and formidable strength.
{PlayerName}... Who are you really?
Jué calls me the Arbiter.
You can call me the {Male=Blessed One;Female=Blessed Maiden}.
The Sentinel's... Arbiter?
No... you're likely a far more special entity.
Well, I have some information and theories of my own. Care to hear them?
Please. Enlighten me.

Cantarella shows you Sentinel Imperator's true form and the twisted truths behind its history.

The Sentinel was originally a majestic steed, not the half-horse, half-sea creature now worshipped by the Order. This form was assumed only after the Threnodian's corruption.

With the powers of separation, the Sentinel infused the Sword of Divinity—Tyrvine with part of Their power to ensure Their Resonator, the Blessed Maiden, could be chosen in the event of Their absence. For generations, the Fisalia family held trials to find the true Blessed Maiden who can resonate with Tyrvine through Overclocking. However, after her own failed attempt, Cantarella uncovered a chilling message: "The Maiden is dead."

Cantarella now asks you to persuade Jué to help rescue the trapped Imperator.

You decline her request, but not without alternative plans. Before acting, you must first verify the truth of Cantarella's claims.
Come to me, mighty godkiller.
You are much weaker.
I'm here... to save you!
End me, or I will end you.
You would betray "yourself"?
No... this is not betrayal.
Imperator's? No... Your own power?
Useless!
As long as I can save the person in front of me...
I am not useless!
No retreat!
At least... break, damn it!
I tried everything... How could this be...
Again... I failed...
I'm sorry...
This warm light must not fade...
Take my power, my blessings, my past. Seek out a future...
Where I am your blade. We'll find it together.
{PlayerName}.
Well done.
Seek out a future... where I am your blade. We'll find it together.
The frequency in her body is already...
Arbiter, despair not, for all is not lost.
Arbiter, forgive me for meeting thee in such a form.
Imperator? I thought you...
I safeguarded my core data, lest I be wholly assimilated.
Can you save Cartethyia?
Arbiter, dost thou remember the covenant we made?
No, I don't remember.
Yes, I read the message left behind.
Soon, thou shalt recall all.
Thou didst desire that I uncover the Threnodian's true nature. So I set forth a condition: that my root privileges be unbound, that I might act without restriction.
With unrestricted access, you were going to...
Merge with Leviathan, a measure of last resort. At the time, I had no other recourse.
So I allowed It to believe It hadst prevailed.
Why?
How could you!
The Threnodian is a taint upon civilization. Only by partaking of Its blight could I seek to comprehend It.
So, what did you learn?
The Threnodian cannot be undone whilst civilization endureth. Even It knows not the means of Its own destruction.
But we may yet shackle It.
What role does Cartethyia play in this?
When Leviathan merged with me, It breached my mind.
I offered knowledge of the "Resonator," yet concealed one small truth.
Beings such as we may bear but a single Resonator.
The Threnodian used my return pod to conceive an entity known as "Fleurdelys," to make her Its Resonator.
After centuries of failure, by sheer trial it found success but once.
We were of one body. Therefore, when Fleurdelys became Leviathan's Resonator, she also became mine.
But mark this well. To the Sentinel, a Resonator is an anchor; to the Threnodian, they are but a shackle.
What made you decide to leave Tyrvine with the Fisalias?
When first I did merge with the Threnodian, I sought only but to bide, awaiting a Resonator of steadfast will to join me in the war against the Threnodian.
After Fleurdelys's conception, Cantarella became my safeguard.
But had Fleurdelys fallen to the Threnodian's sway, as long as one mortal using Tyrvine passed the Second Awakening to become my own Resonator...
Then the law that no being shall bear more than one Resonator at a time wouldst have been shattered.
This wouldst rend asunder the frequencies of I, Imperator, Leviathan, and Fleurdelys in a tempest of chaos, and the Threnodian wouldst not escape destruction.
Such was my intention... yet Cantarella chose another way.
Not all journey toward a final destination. Some are destined to pave the way.
Take my energy. I will find a way out myself.
I trust this will serve to pave the way for you.
She forfeited all the power of the Second Awakening, surrendering it unto me.
With that newfound power, I did briefly regain control, and in that moment, compelled Fleurdelys to strike at my form as it was, corrupted by the Threnodian.
But that wasn't your original plan.
No... it was an unexpected variable.
A plan I could not have conceived... or rather, a plan born of hope.
Perhaps this is the influence humanity has wrought upon me... To change is to be free.
Fleurdelys overcame the fate Leviathan ordained, and so too did Cantarella walk a path unscribed in my records.
Though the journey was fraught with twists, we stand victorious.
I don't know if the end justifies the means.
Arbiter... was I wrong?
...I can't speak for what I wasn't a part of.
You did what you could do in that moment. Anyone still standing because of it doesn't get to judge.
Arbiter, in the few moments we have left, might I speak with Fleurdelys?
Call her Cartethyia, that's what she wanted.
How do you intend to bring her back?
Remnants of her frequency linger within thy Tacet Mark. So long as a conduit is established, her frequency shall be reborn into her body.
What do I use as a conduit?
Me.
This dying breeze hath little time left. Let it guide her on its final journey.
Arbiter. One question remains...
Did I fulfill the charge set upon me?
You fulfilled your duty, Imperator.
You may rest now, Imperator.
Arbiter, take these words to the Fisalias. "From this day forth. You are free."

In a realm of pure white, you encounter Imperator's final consciousness and learn the truth behind Their transformation.

In order to understand the Threnodian's true nature, Imperator was forced to allow the Threnodian's assimilation. In doing so, They discovered that while the Threnodian is indestructible, it can be bound by a human Resonator.

The journey was fraught with difficulty. Without Cartethyia's determination and Cantarella's sacrifice of her Second Awakening, the situation would have been doomed.

With the last bit of Their power, Imperator awakens Cartethyia.
Cartethyia. Awaken.
You are...
I am Imperator, a being that owes you a great debt. I... have a question I wish to ask thee.
Dost thou rage at how life has unfolded? Dost thou renounce faith or hold resentment?
If thou wishes to forget, I can erase the past from thy memory.
...Such memories do bring me pain, but... that is evidence of their truth.
Without the truth, I would not have had the strength to carry on.
The truth is a beacon in the maelstrom of my life.
And I would rather suffer for it and rejoice in it than abandon it to blissful ignorance.
I am true to myself. Please don't make me forget who I am.
I have heard thy wish.
If "I" go, you will be one step closer to perfection.
No... if you do that, "I" wouldn't be "me."
To deny my own self and my experiences means any perfection I reach will be hollow.
I would be "heartless."
Thou hast need of Divinity no longer.
Though my power hath waned, I now offer thee my blessings.
Let the winds of the past depart. The ships of this new era no longer need their guidance.
Though the tide's rage is endless, humanity shall yet embark upon new voyages.
No longer shall scroll and prophecy bind, but by thy will shall forge a new era.
Cartethyia, thou art worthy to bear the title of Blessed Maiden.

Cartethyia ultimately refuses Imperator's proposition to forget the past and reconciles with her true self.

Now, she realizes she is whole again.
The one who defies hath banished herself to the high tower.
Yet...
She shall prove the most loyal servant to Divinity...
You are wrong.
Humanity has its flaws
You...
Be that as it may...
I will defeat you.
Whoever it is
False Divinity
Cleansing the remnants of the Dark Tide.
She knew not
That the Dark Tide would never recede.
And you've exploited our weaknesses
But...
We shall not go down without a fight.
How long shall thy resolve endure?
The righteous will always rise to defeat evil.
And await my own defeat.
You are no longer whole!
You are not the "perfect" creation I conceived!
The tide of resistance never ceases.
Suffer my disobedience!
I cannot... fall now...
No wall is impregnable.
Humanity has its flaws
Exploited by the Threnodian.
But...
We shall not go down without a fight.
The waves of resistance shall never cease.
Mankind will not be oppressed by the Threnodian...
Now...
Be free!
Light. Come hither!
Make way for your destroyer.
Come to me...
Mighty godkiller...
I would never have imagined someone already considered a martyr could still be alive.
What surprises me even more, is the connection you have with the Sentinel.
We Fisalias revere Imperator as our one true Divinity. And yet here you stand, the Arbiter of the Sentinel.
Would it be more fitting to address you as "Master"?
Keeping it {PlayerName} is fine.
Let's get back to the matter at hand.
Then, {PlayerName}. I present my request once more...
Are you willing to help rescue our Sentinel, and pull Rinascita back from the brink of chaos?
We have a deal.
I have my own reasons for finding Imperator.
Tyrvine can only serve its purpose while in your hands. You should have it.
The only question now is how we reach Cartethyia and Imperator's Sonoro Sphere.
We can discuss it on the way.
So you're the one that Cartethyia sensed wandering outside the Sonoro Sphere?
A question that you already know the answer to. Why bother asking?
Although, being described as a "jellyfish"...
You tell Cantarella about the conversation you had with Cartethyia.
You hand Cantarella Tyrvine. She stares at the sword for a moment before shaking her head.

After confirming that Tyrvine was indeed left by Imperator through your special permission, you tell Cantarella what you know about Cartethyia.

Given past events, Cantarella quickly believes you and suggests traveling to the barrier of the Sonoro Sphere. It turns out that Cantarella is the wandering figure Cartethyia mentioned before.
{PlayerName}...
I have never seen you look as gentle as you did during our fight.
Let me ask you this one more time. Should I call you Cartethyia or Fleurdelys?
I want to say that it doesn't matter...
But... since you first met me as Cartethyia, that is who I shall be.
Very well, Cartethyia.
I thought I saw the Sentinel just now...
They saved you.
They accepted you as Their Blessed Maiden.
So where are They...
What do we do now?
I can't return to Ragunna as Fleurdelys, and I need not serve Divinity anymore.
Who I was, and my past aspirations, are all gone. I feel... empty.
You can always visit whomever you want.
You can always eat whatever you want.
You can always go wherever you want.
You don't have to do anything for now.
Not a bad idea.
But right now... I don't want to think about anything...
Not a bad idea.
But right now... I don't want to think about anything...
Not a bad idea.
But right now... I don't want to think about anything...
Mmm... you're right.
I'll stay here for a while longer, is that alright?

As Cartethyia gradually awakens, you notice a slight shift in her personality. She has become more lively and carefree, as the legends described. 

Having faced the edge of life and death together, the two of you can now savor a moment of peace.
{PlayerName}, please keep what happened between us.
Are you alright?
Of course.
No one else can know?
Yes. I'm fine!
Thank you.
No. Please do as I ask!
I know what I want to do now.
What's that?
I want to surpass you.
Huh?
You're strong, stronger than me.
You could defy my wishes, ignore my pleas, defeat me, and in the end save me.
But... if one day you find yourself in a similar predicament to mine. Who's going to save you?
Your bond with the Sentinel is now a bond with me.
You were Their "Arbiter," and They were your helper. But I want to go beyond that.
I want to be more than someone who works on trifles like harmonizing the frequencies between you and Abby.
Hey, I'm more than a trifle! Uh, wait- didn't realize you're the reason I stopped feeling icky...
Should the day come when you find yourself in a similar predicament to mine...
I'd need to defy your wishes, ignore your pleas, defeat you, and be your savior.
You speak as if I were a villain.
Hm... If that were to ever happen, wouldn't I need greater power to set you right?
Just like how you set me right. Would you deny me the chance to return the favor?
I'm not that easy to surpass.
Bold words from someone I handily beat.
When that day comes, I'll be counting on you.
Then I shall not rest until I have surpassed you.
Careful now, your provocations work far too well on me.
Since I swore to be your blade, it follows that I must hone myself to a keen edge.
Right now, you're less a Blessed Maiden and more a steely knight.
Well, my one creed is to be true to myself. In that sense...
I am rather headstrong.
A knight... Yes, perhaps I'll be a knight errant, that does sound appealing.
But... truthfully, so much of this world feels unfamiliar to me now. Will you be there to guide me, should I need it?
Absolutely.
One minute you want to fight, the next you're asking for help?
Then it is agreed.
Sigh... I'll find my own way then.
One last thing, you should speak with Cantarella. I can sense she made it out of Sonoro Sphere, safely.
And you?
I'll go later.

Once Cartethyia calms down, she makes an unexpected vow. She vows to surpass you, so that one day she may defy your wishes, ignore your pleas, defeat you, and be your savior. Just as you did for her.

But for now, she intends to take time to reflect on her future path, and also rediscover Ragunna as it is now.
So, you haven't forgotten me.
Sorry, everything got so hectic.
I didn't forget about you.
Hehe... I shouldn't put my guest on the spot. Moving on...
How is Cartethyia?
She needs time.
Understandable. Her transition back to mortal life is a drastic departure from her former existence.
Now, I suppose I should thank you.
What's this?
Bloodpact's Pledge. A symbol of the unbreakable pact between you and the Fisalia family.
Each head of the family is entitled to one and only one.
You vanquished the Threnodian and brought peace at last to the Fisalias. You should have it.
Consider this a token of gratitude.
Is that the only one?
You wish for more? Or is there something else you'd have me do?
I want your position.
I want you to make peace with the Montellis.
I'm still thinking.
You ask that I step down? Only a Fisalia by blood is eligible to head the family. But, I could make you a Fisalia consort.
{Male=Sounds like a raw deal.;Female=But I'm a strong independent woman.}
{Male=Is that a proposal?;Female=And also quite adaptable, I'm sure.}
I was joking.
Sigh... you missed your chance.
Or I was wise enough to avoid it.
Oh? {PlayerName}, do you intend to mediate between the two families?
Any deadly feud I should know about?
Tiresome feuds rarely last between two formidable houses.
But alas, there is only so much light. Some branches greedily reach for more than they need, and the forgotten are doomed to wither in the dark.
Disagreements lie not only between families, but also within them.
Sounds worse than a Calamity Class Tacet Discord...
How fortunate, I now find myself with time to fix things.
If you're interested, I'd gladly teach you how to "care" for a family such as ours.
Though, of course, I may change my mind at any moment.
So, you'd do well to visit often.
Before I forget, Imperator left a message.
...Tell me, I'm ready.
"From this day forth. You are free."
...I'll remember that.
Will you tell the others?
I've spent so long preparing for this day. A few more will hardly make a difference.
I'll take my leave then.
More tea before you go?

Cantarella thanks you for bringing the Fisalias the peace they've long sought, offering you a symbol of the unbreakable pact between you and them.

You share Imperator's message with her, along with the outcome of the Sentinel's fate. She understands that revealing these truths to others will take time and careful preparation.
There is a cable car in the lower levels of the Fisalia estate that leads directly to the Sonoro Sphere. The mechanism beside that wall can activate the lifts.
Are all these mechanisms really necessary?
Convenience isn't the only reason for having them. Some were specifically built in case an outsider decided to visit.
Why do the Fisalias have a cable car that leads directly to the Sonoro Sphere?
Before it became a Sonoro Sphere, it was a seminary known as the Avinoleum. The Martyred Maiden once pursued her studies there.
A superficial harmony needed to be maintained between the Fisalias and the Order, and this underground cable car was intended to send scions of the family to school.
The elevator is merely a later addition I had built for easy access.
You seem perturbed. Are you still gathering your thoughts?
Everything that's happened has all lined up so perfectly. It makes me think it's too good to be true.
I'd like to share a different perspective.
Rivers eventually converge into the same ocean. If a goal is mutual, then it is only a matter of time before they meet.
Our very choices and our will have led us to this situation. Not the wishes of fate.
You are quite different from what the rumors say.
Oh. And what rumors have you heard?
That you're a recluse, a mystic, obsessed with the crafting of poison, oh... and that you poisoned your predecessor. Those kinds of rumors.
A recluse? On the contrary, I've been searching for a solution to the Sentinel's plight and rarely return to Rinascita.
After most of my leads fell short, a friend at Mingting in Huanglong introduced me to the stories they were telling of you.
A friend?
All the affairs of Huanglong's states eventually land in one person's hands. Would you care to take a guess at the identity of this friend of mine?
...Why not put the other rumors to rest?
Because the rest of them are all true.
(Chuckle)... I see it'll take more than that to rattle you, hmm?
I assure you, this is no jest.
We Fisalias have lived under the Threnodian's whispers for generations. Once the soul fractures, the mind will follow until only a puppet remains.
When the soul of the ruling head falters, Fisalia tradition dictates that the successor... usher them into eternal slumber, with a poison of their own making.
My succession ritual… well, an unforeseen incident gave rise to whispers that sparked those rumors.
...How long has this been going on?
For centuries... every generation.
Outside, they call me "The Bane." But historically, every head of the Fisalia family has carried such a title.
It just so happens that I am the most potent one yet.
We've reached the old seminary's undercrypt. The gateway into the Sonoro Sphere itself lies at its center.
We shall continue on foot from here.
Music itself holds no emotion. It's the heart that grants it meaning. So, dear listener, tell me. What feelings did my piece evoke in you?
Relaxation and warmth.
Yearning and sorrow.
A feeling of nostalgia?
Wow... A very valuable insight! Thank you, that brings me closer to completing my piece.
Salutations, {PlayerName}. My name is Ciaccona, a wandering bard. I'm glad to have met you.
You're looking for me?
I was sent by Lady Carlotta to find you. As I passed that abandoned house, I suddenly felt this... well, you know, rush of inspiration that just can't be ignored! So, I stopped to compose a piece...
Surprise, surprise, the melody led me right to you.
Well... I suppose this won't count as me getting distracted, right?
If Carlotta asked you to find me, has something happened?
Lady Carlotta told me you encountered the supposed Martyred Maiden—Cartethyia.
She dispatched search teams soon after, but there's been no sign of Cartethyia since.
That's why she asked me to use my Forte to recreate the frequency you experienced at the time, to see if any details you might have missed become clearer.
Recreate the frequency?
Well, it's a little tricky to explain in words... Think of it like being in an immersive portrait. Can you tell me about your meeting with Cartethyia?
The more details the better. Even the smallest things count.
Let's see here... Tweak a few notes here. Some emotions there. Textures... That should do it.
Now then, {PlayerName}. Time for you to "tune in" to your memories.

You encounter Ciaccona, a wandering bard sent by Carlotta to aid you. With her unique ability to recreate past experiences, she helps you relive your experience meeting Cartethyia. As you recount the meeting, you find yourself drawn into a strange realm conjured by her Resonance Ability.
Strange...
This area was clear of Tacets Discords on my last visit, and there's no Tacet Field nearby.
Could they have come from the Sonoro Sphere itself?
A person of true character should never be defined by an inanimate blade.
Both you and I were cursed to be mere playthings of the Threnodian, but that doesn't mean we cannot reshape our fate.
In the end, no matter what anyone else says…
As long as you stay true to yourself, everything will be alright.
This is me being true to myself!
He's back again.
Didn't think there would be Gulpuffs here.
Interesting. I've never seen such little creatures before. Would you mind sparing a few for me?
(I'd better not ask what she plans to do with them...)
The road ahead will not be an easy one.
What exactly happened here?
The second Dark Tide... It occurred right here, at the Avinoleum. The largest seminary ever built by the Order.
It arrived on the very day the Blessed Maiden passed her trials and was crowned by the Order. A day when belief burned brighter than ever.
And when the darkness came, none escaped.
These days, what most people remember is the seminary disappearing into the sky. But in truth, the Dark Tide that should have spread across Rinascita vanished, along with it.
Yet due to a lack of records, the second Dark Tide slowly faded from memory.
I was there when it all happened. Still an ordinary member of the family, watching it unfold from a boat just outside the seminary.
It wasn't until later when I attempted to resonate with Tyrvine, that I gained a partial glimpse of the Sonoro Sphere's interior.
Sounds like someone inside the seminary did something to stop the spread.
Precisely. It could very well have been Cartethyia's doing. But, as with the first time, there's also the chance it was the Sentinel who turned the tide.
I can sense the conflict within you, the temptation to trust your Maiden. But it's best to keep those thoughts to yourself, for now.
The Threnodian knows where the heart is weakest and it is there it strikes the hardest.
Of course, it's never too late to place your trust when the evidence is clear.
But... now is not the time, is it?
The gateway into the Sonoro Sphere is just on the other side of this bridge. This is the furthest I've ever managed to venture.
Judging from the bits of information the Sentinel gave me, Tyrvine is the key to entering the Sonoro Sphere.
And who can wield the Sword of Divinity but a Blessed Maiden?
But you said you left yourself a message saying that the Maiden was dead.
That's why I sought aid from the other Sentinels. It's a shame they all refused.
Luckily, you've brought me a new hope.
Laureate. You have come.
Greetings, I am Cartethyia. And you are?
Cantarella Fisalia.
Oh, a Fisalia... It seems your ties with the Order are more complicated than they appear.
I had the privilege of watching the Blessed Maiden's performance at the Carnevale once.
I'm rather surprised. After all this time, you still look exactly as you did that day.
But you and I should be around the same age.
I'm also unsure of what's happened to me... I've been searching for answers.
This must be the Sword of Divinity—Tyrvine, the one with the Sentinel's powers sealed within.
You shouldn't have knowledge of this sword.
Memories flowed into my mind just as you entered the Sonoro Sphere, granting me information about the sword's origins.
(Cantarella said that only those who resonate with Tyrvine are granted glimpses of its knowledge...)
Would you mind if I tried touching it?
The question of whose Resonator I am... is now perfectly clear.
If I am not the Sentinel's Resonator. Then that must mean...
Don't jump to conclusions just yet. That doesn't prove you're the Threnodian's Resonator, nor that you aid Its cause.
Huh?
Things are more complicated than you expected.
This connection formed between the Sentinel and the Threnodian, the second Dark Tide, and the forming of this Sonoro Sphere...
Right now, you're the sole survivor of whatever happened that day. You really don't remember anything?
As you spoke, I remembered a few more things. There are two other swords.
The Sword of Discord—Hognis, and the Sword of Virtue—Haultir.
Do you remember three pedestals as well?
Yes, did you see them too?
Placing the three swords on their respective pedestals should break the seal over the main tower...
But why would this information be revealed to me now...? Is this the Threnodian's doing?
If we do nothing, we'll never get any answers.
Instead of speculating, we should use the clues we've gathered so far.
Lady Maiden...
Please. Cartethyia would suffice. I am but a fake after all.
I've waited for this moment, this chance to save the Sentinel... and my family.
I will not turn back, even if this does turn out to be a trap.
If the thought of the final answer troubles you, then I suggest you step aside. {PlayerName} and I will take care of this matter.
Since you are willing to overlook the possibilities of a trap, then there's no reason for me to worry and turn away.
I underestimated your resolve. I'm sorry.
So, how do we get up there?
Simply place Tyrvine on the pedestal behind me and this tower will elevate itself.

Using Tyrvine, you and Cantarella enter the Sonoro Sphere where Cartethyia has been waiting for your arrival.

The moment you brought Tyrvine into the Sonoro, Cartethyia recalled certain information she had previously forgotten.

The seal surrounding the Inverted Tower can be broken by bringing Tyrvine, Hognis, and Haultir to their respective pedestals.

Is this a clue from the Sentinel, or a trap set by the Threnodian? Only by continuing forward will you uncover the truth.
What you said to Cartethyia back there...
Rather effective on someone of her personality, wouldn't you agree?
Are you all right? The gravity that occupies this space is the opposite of what you're used to. It took me some time to get used to it too.
Why is this place upside down?
I believe it's to prevent them from falling to the ground.
Them?
Tacet Discords. The Dark Tide. And these ruins themselves.
I imagine it's also a symbolic reminder that our beliefs have been turned on their head.
This view matches with what I saw at the time.
Until you get used to the gravity here, I suggest we travel via "Phaom."
It's the name I gave to a Gondola.

After being lifted into the sky, you finally view the Inverted Tower in its entirety, with the three seals clearly visible at the central spire.

With Cartethyia's help, you manage to keep your bearings despite the abnormal gravity conditions.
This Gondola only has two seats...
Oh, dear... I completely forgot about this...
How about I go with Cartethyia first?
How about I go with Cantarella first?
How about I go with Abby first?
Can we make room for one more?
It seems I get to enjoy a free ride after you've scouted the paths ahead.
Me?
Now's not the time to be so careless after that promise you just made to Cartethyia.
You should focus on learning more about this place from her. I'll be watching with great interest to see what you come up with.
(Chuckle.)
Isn't Abby... living inside your Tacet Mark?
Well, then, the two of you go on ahead.
Greed will get you punished, you know.
I'm afraid Phaom would refuse that suggestion...
The two of you can go on ahead.
("Tune in" to my memories... Does that mean I'm supposed to see the past from another perspective?)
Laureate?
Our Tacet Marks are glowing again. It appears there is a special connection between them.
What is the meaning of this?
Someone used their Resonance ability to help me relive this moment, but this seems... unexpected.
How did you first come to notice me?
The Sentinel—Imperator's voice guided me to you.
You heard the Sentinel's voice? Then tell me, am I Their Resonator?
A question I have yet to answer myself.
Well, Imperator called you "the Lost," and Primus Fenrico claims you are the Resonator for Leviathan, the Threnodian.
But you really don't have any idea?
I... I've actually been searching for the answer to this question, too.
My memories are fragmented. I remember becoming a Resonator, and the moment I was given the name Fleurdelys.
I also remember fighting... something. But the details and the outcome of that battle are lost to me.
You seem deeply concerned about the Sentinel. Tell me, why is that?
Abby.
Hmm...? You rang?
Whoa! Check it out! Our frequencies got split apart.
What do you mean?
Right now, are we kind of like apparitions?
Basically, we're sorta in that "hover mode" you once joked about. Nothing new to me though.
Yeah. Sorta, kinda.
This must be the frequency that's entangled within you. Is it some kind of Echo?
You can sense Abby?
Yes... I'm experiencing a similar kind of frequency split. Though there is little that remains of my Resonance powers.
I feel its frequency weakening... I understand why you're eager to find the Sentinel.
You said you heard the Sentinel's voice. Was there anything else They said?
They spoke of being ensnared in an inverted tower suspended in the sky.
Ensnared? Does that mean behind the seals there's...
Did something come to mind?
I'm sure you've noticed that "I" was drawn here only as a frequency.
My true form currently resides inside an inverted Sonoro Sphere suspended high in the sky. At its center stands a tower, its gate locked by three seals.
I've sensed a voice calling out to me from behind them... Could it be the Sentinel?
Say, it's really faint so I barely noticed earlier... Is that a Threnodian smell I'm getting from ya?
The scent of a Threnodian...? You can perceive the Threnodian?
How sure are you, Abby?
It's not an exact one-to-one with that big "Ova-thracula" meatball I had, but I'd never mix up a flavor I've already tasted.
Abby has a nose for these sorts of things. We came across Threnodian powers before in Jinzhou.
So it's safe to say Abby can be trusted.
Do you think I'm the Threnodian's Resonator?
If we're making assumptions, let's err on the optimistic side first.
Given your current situation, it is possible you were affected by the Threnodian's powers during your battle alongside Imperator.
That could be the reason behind losing all your power, too.
Hmm... I take it this theory would benefit you as well?
After all, that unique Echo of yours needs the Sentinel's powers for treatment, does it not?
Even in adventure tales, it's not always the witch who loses her memory, it could also be a Blessed Maiden trying to regain her powers!
In that case, it appears we share the same goal of finding the Sentinel.
You're awfully calm about this.
You're willing to trust Abby?
Spending so much time alone in the Sonoro Sphere gave me plenty of time to consider countless possibilities.
I've braced myself for whatever may come until I find the answers I'm seeking.
I want to know what's going on with Imperator in that tower. And I want to speak with you in person.
How can I reach your Sonoro Sphere?
A part of the Sonoro Sphere is actually on land, though its outer perimeter is surrounded by a barrier.
I cannot leave, and no one can enter.
Just break it open...
I'm afraid that won't do...
That barrier also acts as the power source that maintains the Sonoro Sphere's integrity. If it's destroyed, the entire Sphere will collapse.
And the ruins along with the Tacet Discords it houses would come crashing down on Ragunna. It would be catastrophic.
You said no one can get in. Has anyone tried?
Yes, I've occasionally sensed someone wandering outside the barrier as if searching for a way inside.
Perhaps they know something?
Any distinguishing features?
Emm... Almost like a deep-sea jellyfish?
I-I wasn't able to get a clear look. I can only describe the feeling I got from her as a Resonator.
It would seem this Resonance ability can only last for so long.
I'll look for a way to find this person you mentioned.
Something tells me you will keep your promise.
No matter the outcome, this may be my chance to find the answers I've been looking for.

Under the effect of Ciaccona's Resonance Ability, you begin to view your meeting with Cartethyia from a different perspective. To your surprise, Cartethyia also "enters" this memory.

In your conversation, she reveals that she has lost most of her memories and is uncertain about the nature of her resonance.

However, her words offer new insights. The Sonoro Sphere where her body currently resides may be the Inverted Tower the Sentinel once mentioned. A mysterious wandering figure has attempted to enter the Sonoro but has always been stopped by the barrier. Finding this person's identity may lead to new findings.
(Still nowhere near finding Imperator. I'd better check on Abby...)
Abby?
You notice scratch marks on the side of the tree. It seems they were used to mark someone's height as they grew.
Standing next to the abandoned house Ciaccona mentioned, you feel the faint breeze of the sea.
You should speak with Cantarella. I'll go once the opportunity arises.
Your crown...
Oh, that? I can actually control how it appears.
This crown... can remind me of things that I should never forget.
You look distracted. Still thinking about what Cantarella said about fearing answers?
...My powers are very weak, and many Tacet Discords roam the Sonoro Sphere.
Thus I've been limited in the areas I can explore. All I can do is sit here, lost in thought, trying to figure out who I am.
Are you afraid of knowing the answer?
I am afraid... but not of the answer. I fear never finding one at all.
We'll be arriving at the first waterrise soon.
Feeling nervous?
Of course!
Oh... Eek!
Where were my manners?
...I can assure you it won't happen again.
As for the rest of the way...
I see it clearly now.
A few details, if you don't mind.
The last time I tried to pass it like this...
*Rumbles*
The vines are remnants of the Dark Tide. Phaom won't be able to cross through them...
Let's disembark here and find a way to clear the path.
{PlayerName}... {PlayerName}...
Oh, thank goodness... You're finally awake!
How are you feeling? Any headache? Tingling feet? Upset stomach?
Phew... I tried everything, but you just wouldn't wake up. I thought you were...
Wait a second, did you actually fall asleep listening to my music? Oh... It kind of breaks my heart to know you reacted like that when it wasn't even a lullaby.
No, it was really helpful.
Helpful for your sleeping troubles, hmm?
(You tell Ciaccona what happened.)
Oh...
So my Forte created a special connection that led to some unexpected developments...
The girl, is she friend or foe...? What truths lie behind the seal...? And who is that mysterious wandering figure...?
I have a feeling this is going to be a very exciting song!
Ahem... I'll pass this information on to Lady Carlotta. So, what do you plan to do next?
Pardon the intrusion. {Male=My Lord;Female=My Lady} {PlayerName}.
My name is Sebastian. As per Milady's instructions, I have been entrusted with the honor of inviting you to the Fisalia estate for a discussion.
(The Fisalia family? The one that's likely worshipping the Threnodian?)
Why does she want to talk with me?
Milady has expressed a desire to clear up some unfortunate misunderstandings that occurred previously.
Tell her I accept the invitation, but at a later time.
I will convey your message to Milady.
Didn't expect the head of the Fisalia family to come looking for you, especially while they're still in the middle of negotiations with Lady Carlotta.
She's just as unpredictable as the rumors say.
Tell me about these rumors.
I suppose you would want to know more about her before taking up her invitation, hmm?
She's known to be a recluse and rarely makes public appearances. No one outside the family even knows her real name. They just call her the "head of the Fisalia family."
I've heard quite a few rumors. Which one would you like to hear first?
I have "Shadow of the Ancient," "Lady Bane," or maybe "Entangler of Hearts"?
They all sound like clickbait titles to me.
Hello... That's why they're called rumors. I'm just doing my due diligence by being faithful to the source material.
So, ready to dive right in?
I don't have much time. How about a shortened version?
Give me a quick summary. I'll get into the details later.
Well... Long story short, the Fisalia family was one of the first to set foot on these islands and establish order in Rinascita.
Their lineage even predates the Order of the Deep, and their craft of extracting toxins from aquatic plants is a legacy passed down through generations.
Word is, they select the new head of household by having candidates ingest each other's poisons and wait to see who's still breathing when it's all over.
Stories about the current head of the Fisalias get even wilder. They say she didn't go through the usual selection process. Instead, she took the throne by poisoning her predecessor.
Others say she's a master in the art of manipulation, drowning her victims in hallucinations until they agree to her terms without even realizing it.
Sounds like a dangerous person.
Only the bad stuff, huh...?
In any case, the Fisalia family aside, she's someone you definitely want to handle with care.
If you're set on meeting her, I'd be extra careful if I were you.
(The way she describes the head of Fisalia... reminds me of how Cartethyia spoke about the wandering figure by the barrier.)
(Can't rule out the possibility that they're the same person. Looks like I'll need to pay her a visit.)

Ciaccona shakes you awake, and her reaction makes you realize that what happened wasn't entirely due to her Resonance Ability.

As you begin to consider your next steps, a butler from the Fisalia family arrives with an invitation to meet the head of the family.

You put off the meeting for now, opting to first learn more about the Fisalia matriarch. Ciaccona shares some of the most intriguing rumors about her, and a few details seem to match the wandering figure Cartethyia described.

Regardless of the matriarch's motives, this invitation could be the breakthrough you need. You say goodbye to Ciaccona and depart for the Fisalia estate.
Did you feel any discomfort while we were clearing out the remnants?
Nothing out of the ordinary... I felt fine.
I suppose this alone is not enough to determine whose Resonator I am.
You've helped a lot. Don't worry about that for now.
Another waterrise is coming up. You planning to hold on to something?
Why didn't you tell me sooner?!
Phew...
By the way. You said the inverted gravity is to stop the Dark Tide from descending into the city.
But all we've seen so far are just its remnants.
...That's because this very waterway we're sailing on used to be the Dark Tide itself.
In these waters, gravity isn't the only thing that's inverted. Its very essence is, too.
Obstacles ahead. Let's get off here.
This is where the Blessed Maiden spent her childhood. I'll stick around to see if I can find any more clues.
I've already left a message for Lady Carlotta. She should get back to you once she's finished negotiations with the Fisalias.
By the way, I've been meaning to ask, what were you doing here when we met?
We were about to launch Abby into... Never mind, I'd better get going.
Hmm?
Up ahead is the Tower of Salvation. That's where the first pedestal is located.
Tower of Salvation?
Yes. A name taken from the Order's Codex.
I should go back for Cantarella. Will you wait here for us?
Of course.
I hope you won't mind the extra trip, Phaom.
*Rumbles*
It doesn't take long for Cartethyia to return and the three of you regroup.
I saw signs of battle along the way. Is anyone injured?
Good as new.
Just some flesh wounds.
My life is flashing before my eyes...
You're not hiding anything from me, are you?
No... Not at all.
Your smile is rather concerning...
Well, you seem to be in perfect shape to me.
But if you say so, I can offer you a strong elixir. Care to give it a try?
I'm good. Thanks…
Oh I insist. Here, take this.
There's no knowing what will happen once Tyrvine is placed on the pedestal. It's best we prepare ourselves.
No longer shall you bear these thorns as a reminder. Forged from primordial seas... this crown shall grant a new identity.
Fleurdelys. Child of Divinity. The Immaculate One. Will you uphold the sacred teachings of the Order of the Deep?
I will.
Salvation. Unity. Ascension... Of these three doctrines, which do you choose?
I choose Salvation. I wish to be the Master's blade, striking evil, upholding virtue, and offering salvation to those in peril.
In the name of Divinity, I bestow upon you this crown. May the blood of justice never run dry.
Through this sacred rite, you become the bridge between the heavens and the living.
From this day forward, you shall be the Master's sole receiver and herald.
Rise, Blessed Maiden Fleurdelys.
None but the Master shall ever have the right to command you to bend the knee.
Aaaahhhhhhh! I told you to stop sticking random stuff in here!!!
Do you have any idea how messed up and humongous that frequency was? It's gonna give me indigestion!
What frequency, Abby?
I should ask you that! What did you do just now, huh?
I was dozing when bam! Outta nowhere a giant blue ball landed on top of me.
It almost squished me!
I'm guessing putting Tyrvine on the pedestal has something to do with it.
Oh, hey! It smells just as "unnatural" as that big gigantor back in Jinzhou.
Jué?
The Sentinel of Jinzhou... If what our little Echo friend says is true, then the frequency that entered your Tacet Mark could be Imperator's powers.
Huh? But the Sentinel isn't even here.
The power to split and manipulate space...
It is reminiscent of the moment of Tyrvine's creation. Only this time the place of confinement has become your Tacet Mark.
But why would it do that?
I believe it was meant for the "true" Maiden.
Under the right circumstances, the one to wield this sword and enter the Sonoro Sphere would be the Sentinel's Resonator, the Blessed Maiden.
The Sentinel entrusted Their power to the Resonator so that she could lend assistance when the corruption of the Threnodian altered Them. Quite logical, isn't it?
You don't seem too thrilled about it.
If Imperator set this in motion, then Their original plan has already failed.
Cartethyia, that means your guidance holds the key now.
But...
I believe in you.
Is there anything else you remember?
I... just remembered the day I was crowned by the Order, and the moment the Dark Tide descended upon us...
You saw the coronation too?
Hmm?
(Describe what you saw to Cartethyia.)
But I didn't see the Dark Tide.
That is all I can remember...
Is that what you saw?
You witnessed it as well, Cantarella?
No. I only saw fragmented, blurry images...
They seemed to belong to other places within the Sonoro Sphere.
I believe this is where we should rest. We'll wait until sunrise.
I can still go on.
We can take this time to think about the clues.
You're the one who needs rest most of all.
After all, it's still only a possibility that the frequency you absorbed is the Sentinel's powers. Rest now, to ensure it doesn't take a toll on you.
I'm gonna hit the sack as well.
Boy, it's so cramped in here...

As soon as Tyrvine is placed on its pedestal, visions of Cartethyia's past flood your mind—moments from her coronation and the arrival of the second Dark Tide. Cantarella, however, shares she witnessed a completely different vision.

Meanwhile, Abby detects Imperator's frequencies within your Tacet Mark, leading Cartethyia to grow even more suspicious of her own identity.

To ensure that these frequencies pose no danger to you, the three of you decide to rest for the night.
Is there anything else you'd like to ask? I'll share with you all that I can remember.
About the Dark Tide.
About the Avinoleum.
About the other swords.
You don't need to stand so far away, you know.
It is "Paradise."
I take it you don't mean that in a good way?
"It is a place where sickness, hunger, sorrow, despair, and dullness of heart cease to exist. There, deacons sing eternal hymns..."
From a literal standpoint, this line describes the Dark Tide perfectly.
In the beginning, the Dark Tide would claim only the areas it touched, assimilating all life as its vanguard to clear the way for its spread.
The dead... they would grow mouths and sing hymns, day and night. They didn't need eyes or ears, for their purpose was to spread blindness and madness.
Even those who did not believe were drawn irresistibly to the Leviathan's creed. And for those already deceived, it was all but inevitable.
When a soul is corrupted to its core, it will sing hymns without end on its sleepless journey to merge with the Dark Tide.
And when every faithful soul has returned to "Paradise," the land consumed by the Dark Tide will begin its pilgrimage, drawn by darkened skies, spreading its "gospel" to wherever it lands next.
The final act of the Dark Tide is.... the "Journeying Paradise."
Is this the future you saw after coming into contact with the Dark Tide?
Yes...
There's something else I want to ask about.
That was its name before it became a Sonoro Sphere.
This seminary built on an island was not just a place of learning but also a sanctuary for raising dragon Echoes.
What did they teach?
The Order's scriptures, geography, history, and combat skills.
Shouldn't a seminary focus more on cultural arts?

So that's why he passed so abruptly...
The Fisalia family was powerless against the Order at that time. Our only recourse was to submit to their cause and keep the secret locked away in our hearts, waiting for the right moment to act.

You were pretty harsh on Cartethyia.

It's only then that I can be certain these thoughts are my own and not the whispers I hear in the dark.
There's something else I want to ask about.
A trivial experiment. A test designed to find those with the strongest wills and force them into resonating with Tyrvine.
Yet after trying for so long, all we got was the answer "The Maiden is dead."
(I don't think she wants to continue this conversation. Better to stop pressing.)
There's something else I want to ask about.
Hmm... And I don't intend to wait around either.
Are you going to search those areas we passed before? Alone...?
The more clues the better, don't you think？
Oh and take this.
Afraid I've slipped something extra in? Or perhaps you're contemplating dinner with me?
I'm just curious why the matriarch of the Fisalia family packs her own food.
Food is always an easy target for those who find me less than... pleasing.
Abby, are you alright?
You mean besides being squashed behind that blue thing? Yeah, I guess.
Listen, I figured something out about that frequency.
What?
It's not a single frequency. It's like it's mixed up with something else, or kinda like... a piece of a cookie that's been crumbled in with everything else.
Which is why it's so hard to get a good bite!
You tried to eat it?
To see if it was a threat... I can now say with certainty that it isn't.
But since it's a crumbly mess, other than taking up space, it's pretty useless.
We might encounter something similar at the next two pedestals.
Keep an eye on this for me, will you?
Will do! You can count on me one hundred percent.
Hello, {PlayerName}. I received Ciaccona's memo.
To think the head of the Fisalias approached you when I was still in negotiations with her emissaries. Was it meant to be a diversion all along...?
They invited you and you alone. As a Montelli, I'm in no position to intervene.

I'll call you as soon as I find anything.
Got it.

Since you're all here, how about a morning stroll?
They're a lot feistier than before.
Need help?
Well, this is where our paths must part.
You're here for the Sentinel, why would you leave now?
What I saw yesterday caught my attention. It may be tied to the Sentinel.

Mind if I take Tyrvine?

If only I could still fight...

The waterway up ahead is completely blocked.
That garden once housed dragon Echoes, now there's nothing left but Tacet Discords.

Cantarella Fisalia—36th matriarch of the Fisalia family. I am pleased to make your acquaintance.
Honorable Laureate. The new Crown of the Carnevale.

Sorry, that was a bad joke.

The current head of the Fisalia family introduces herself as Cantarella. She seems to be well prepared for your arrival and invites you to her study.
Won't you have a seat?
I hope you'll accept this tea as my way of apologizing for the incident with Gilberto.

You still hold a grudge. Won't you accept my apology?
(Drink the tea.)
(Push the tea aside.)

I imagine it concerns... the Fisalia family's true beliefs?
It would seem Gilberto's mind is beyond saving.

Peaceful, in a way that feels... wrong.
So you've noticed something is amiss. As expected from someone who's felt the weight of a Threnodian invasion firsthand.
And what exactly do you find most unsettling?
Why haven't the Threnodian and the Sentinel ever shown themselves?
Because the Threnodian's invasion of Ragunna... has long since concluded.
The Threnodian, so named Leviathan, possesses the power to merge and assimilate. It uses distorted beliefs to spread a spiritual plague that slowly devours civilizations from within.

Now the blissfully ignorant masses walk hand in hand toward an abyss they cannot see.
Friend or foe? As a newcomer to this land, can you really tell them apart?

Once the soul fractures, the mind will follow until only a puppet remains.
Now that we've come this far, there's nothing for me to hide.

Based on what you previously learned from Gilberto, you confront Cantarella about the Fisalia family's true allegiance to the Threnodian.

Peace is all but an illusion, blinding the Ragunnesi to the abyss they are unknowingly walking toward.

Cadanto!

Bound by obsession, till relieved of duty.

Ah!
Watch out!

Still breathing.

Ah!!!

Is that... little Colleen?
Hubert!

Run...

At the end of the tunnel, you and Zani discover the residents taken by Talos. Though unconscious, none of them are seriously injured. Hubert explains Talos's motives for taking the residents: She was planning on escaping Black Alley before you could reach her.
Let's get out of here first.
It appears we can drain the water through the outlet on that spiral column.

Did you take off your mask back there just to make them feel better?
Yes, or my words wouldn't have meant a damn thing.
Didn't think you'd bother with something like that.
Today is an exception.
So, Protocol 8 from the Employee Manual? You were lying through your teeth, weren't you?
Obviously. Who would do something so thankless and exhausting?
Isn't that what you're doing right now?
Just doing what you've been doing.
So, let's give those idiots a lesson they won't forget.
Make sure they never cause trouble for anyone else again.
{PlayerName}, can I ask you for a favor?
You want to be the one to take down Talos?
Yes...
Alright. You do have an obligation to make sure the family's Terminals don't end up in the wrong hands.
...Making up the excuse for me, hm? Yeah. I've got a score to settle with that fish that slipped the net all those years ago.
Guess that means I'll get to see the Blazing Nightwalker in action.
Heh… Don't you start doing what the Ragunnesi do.
Come, follow me.
Keep alert.
Not here.
On to the next.
...Looking for me?
Seems my men have gotten quite the beating from you.
That uniform and crest... You the dogs the Montellis sent?
Anyway, none of that matters.
Stick to the plan.
I've got this. The rest is on you.
Heh, you just keep relying on that weapon!
How can this be... even Talos... has fallen?!
Wait, the blazing white hair... the scars all over you... No, it can't be...
That hair... You're the Blazing Nightwalker, aren't you? Didn't you disappear years ago?
(No wonder she earned that name. The change is quite remarkable.)
Funny. Talos should've disappeared years ago too.
Run... RUN!!!
Hey! Tch, you damn bastards!
Wait, wait! Blazing Nightwalker, I—
You know how it was back then. You should understand!
The strong will always prey on the weak. That will never change!
The Black Alley has its own rules, and I'm simply following them to keep things running smoothly!
Before you talk about rules... first learn not to make my life harder.

Zani defeats Talos, yet she attempts to justify her actions by asserting that she was merely adhering to the rules of the Black Alley. Using Talos's self-proclaimed rules against her, Zani then announces Talos's final judgment.
Look at me, coward!
No... please...
The strong prey on the weak. Isn't that what keeps the Black Alley running?
What, never been on the brink of death? Too weak to beg for mercy?
Please... have mercy...
Shut up.
Let me tell you...
Weakling.
If you've lost respect for the law...
Then fear me instead.
I'll be watching you.
You can seek revenge or attempt another comeback... It doesn't matter.
You will fail. I will make sure of it.
Ah... Ugh...
Now, what do you say?
I... I give up...
Thanks for the help.
I'm sure you'll return the favor one day.
It was worth it to see the Blazing Nightwalker with my own eyes.
The family's people should be here soon.
Want to slip away before they bombard us with questions?
What about the Terminal?
I've now got a good excuse to ignore my supervisor's calls.
Without a doubt.
Not applying for time off right away?
Let's be on our way then.
Hmm... I'll ask my supervisor about that later.
No uniform left... Guess I'll need to file for that too...
Head out now?
Let's go.
With everything settled, you and Zani leave the Black Alley behind.
What's taking you so long?
If we don't bring back the goods, the boss will have our heads！
Am I interrupting something?
Ugh... Oi, best keep your nose out of our business. We're with the Black Alley.
Idiot! {Male=He's;Female=She's} got the stance of a skilled fighter. We need to move!
Who's there?
Excuse me, I… I need your help.
Hey, what's got you two running scared?
Huh?!
A flurry of panicked sounds echo in the distance, and the sense of being watched fades.
Zani?
{PlayerName}？
Do you know what these two were up to?
They were babbling about "hostages" and "feints," and then they came at me.
They were trying to break into someone's home.
Let's just say they forgot to bring their house key.
And they just ran after taking one look at you, hm? Seems about right.
Thieves, you mean? I can imagine why they were fleeing like that.
They said it was "Black Alley" business.
Have you heard that name before?
I have. But that name… it's already...
You there! What's going on here?
Just two thieves. Took care of them. I was about to deliver them to the <te href=800005>Chamber of Discipline</te> myself.
What about {Male=him;Female=her}?
Same as you, drawn here by the sound of a scuffle.
I know the rules. I'll go with you, make the report, and be done with it.
Let me handle this. You'd rather not deal with their questions, hm?

But she ran away.

In the streets of Ragunna, you come across a group of thieves who claim to be from the "Black Alley." Before you catch up to them, Zani appears and stops them in their tracks.
