Which one should I pick?
Hmm... I'll take all of them. One of each, please.
A bit hard on digestion, no?
Ah, {PlayerName}, you made it. Let's sit over there and talk.
I wasn't sure what you liked. It was too hard to choose, so I just got one of each flavor.
I took you for more of a coffee person.
Work is bitter enough as it is. Why drink something bitter on top of that?
Things not going well?
Those two thieves give you more trouble than expected?
I thought they promised you a vacation?
Yeah... Still about the stuff from last time.
Actually, a lot of the family's staff have been running into the same kind of trouble as that night.
They're not anything special on their own.
What matters is... a lot of the family's employees have been running into the same kind of trouble as that night.
A vacation is like an ad. Only the ones dishing it out have the power to make it real or fake.
And recently, a lot of the family's employees have been running into the same kind of trouble as that night.
Guess my vacation will just have to be postponed again.
What if I help you apply for it next time?
Hmm... Maybe that could work.
So, where should we start?
First, tell me what you need help with.
As I mentioned before, many people working for the Montellis have been victims of attempted thefts, like last night.
The family has tightened security, but just sitting here waiting won't solve anything.
As for the ones we caught... they haven't been chatty. Plus, they've only committed a few small-time crimes.
So it would be tricky to use... more extreme methods on them. If we do, it could give the wrong people a chance to twist the situation.
You mentioned someone asked for your help earlier, right?
You want to locate her?
We've been trying but haven't found anyone who matches her description yet. She's probably keeping a low profile.
But right now, she might be the only lead we've got.
So, might I ask you play your face card one more time?
Seems it's up to me again.
For the ice cream, I guess I can't say no.
Much appreciated.
Maybe some more then?
We'll do it tonight. It will be in your hands.
Feel free to rest until it's time. I've already made arrangements at a hotel.
You know what. I'll be here for a while. If you have any questions, just ask away.
Do I need to prepare anything?
Everything is taken care of.
You ordered too much.

You meet Zani near the ice cream cart in Ragunna. She shares with you that many of the Montelli family's staff have previously run into the same kind of trouble as that night. Zani asks for your assistance in locating the help-seeker, which is crucial to resolving the deadlock in this complicated case.
(Should I head straight for the hotel, or dig a little deeper first?)
Something you wanted to talk about?
Ask about the Black Alley.
Ask about Talos.
Ask about the Blazing Nightwalker.
That will be all.
Ragunna once went through a hell of a time. The Order was hit with major losses, including many of their best. The chaos lasted for quite a while.
You mean... the Second Dark Tide.
Yes. The Order is by no means above reproach, but you cannot deny they keep Ragunna stable.
The Black Alley was born when that stability fell apart. Criminals from every corner banded together, and law-abiding citizens paid the price.
To make things worse, they forced a lot of vagrants into their ranks, using them as tools for their dirty work.
Their eyes and ears were everywhere. The Order tried several times to wipe them out, but each time they came up empty.
Then one day, the Chamber of Discipline managed to catch the ones pulling the strings—they were found tied up and served on a platter. That's when the Black Alley taken down.
As for the Blazing Nightwalker... and Talos, that's the names the Black Alley gave them.
I have another question.
Talos... that was what the Black Alley called their leader.
Word is, Talos might not even be a single person. Whoever is on top gets the title of "Talos."
There must have been quite a few "Taloses" over the years.
That's right. They had a brutally efficient way of picking the leader. Whoever was the strongest got the crown.
But this title should have died with the Black Alley.
I have another question.
The Blazing Nightwalker was just one of many dramatic titles around Rinascita.
Ragunna once went through a hell of a time. The Order was hit with major losses, including many of their best. The chaos lasted for quite a while.
Back then, nights weren't as quiet as they are now. There were always some poor civilians getting hassled by criminals.
Then someone elusive gradually caught people's attention. They took down those criminals and disappeared right after saving the civilians.
They never revealed their name, so the people started calling them the Blazing Nightwalker.
The last time anyone saw them was when they took down Talos and the rest of the Black Alley higher-ups.
I have another question.
Best to get some rest now. Work starts later.
Before getting some rest in, you decide to inquire Zani for more information about the case. Seeing that she has experienced past events, she might help you piece together some parts of the puzzle.
Hello there, {Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}
Ms. Zani has already reserved a room for you. Ready to check in?
Have you heard of the Blazing Nightwalker?
I'm ready to check in.
I have other matters to attend to.
You've come to the right person.
I was once saved by the Blazing Nightwalker myself. Ragunna wasn't nearly as peaceful back then as it is now.
I was heading home later than usual when I ran into some Black Alley brutes.
If it hadn't been for the Blazing Nightwalker, I'm sure they would have robbed me blind.
I had an entire month's earnings on me!
What does the Blazing Nightwalker look like?
Well… It all happened so quickly, and it was dark, so I didn't get a proper look.
All I saw were a pair of blazing eyes. Guess that was where the name came from, eh?
I see.
Very well, I'll show you to your room.
Of course. You are always welcome to stay with us.
Any nibbles you're hankerin' for today?
Have you heard of the Blazing Nightwalker?
Oh, I've heard some of the patrons talkin' about em'! Sounds like someone who can really give a good thrashin', eh?
But those who got a beatin' were bullying thugs, taking the weak for a ride. Honestly, they probably had it comin'.
But that's all from ages ago. Ye know, they say the Blazing Nightwalker only frequented the dodgy areas anyway.
Since the city's been safer, I don't hear much about 'em anymore.
Honored Laurate, may I be of service?
Have you heard of the Blazing Nightwalker?
Ah, yes... I remember the stories from long ago.
Back then, the Order had yet to recover from the devastation of the Second Black Tide, and our peacekeeping forces were stretched thin.
In those neglected corners of the city, crime took root and chaos spread like wildfire.
That was when this righteous figure first made their presence known.
The Chamber of Discipline received criminals bound and left at our doorstep every day. However, the Blazing Nightwalker vanished without a trace.
I suppose, once the situation improved, they faded into the shadows. May the Sentinel bless them.
You seem to hold this figure in high regard.
It was a special time in the city's history. What the Nightwalker did still stirs debate to this day. Everyone has their own theories.
Some of my brethren believe their actions overstepped the bounds of the Order's teachings.
But when you look at the results, they clearly align with the Sentinel's will of salvation.
So, you leave the hotel and decide to wander around before the operation starts.
{PlayerName}? It's not time yet. Aren't you going to rest a little longer?
Aren't you?
Can't sleep anyway.
I am resting, alright?
I'm afraid I can't help you with that.
Insomnia and I go way back.
I have a few questions.
What about?
The family's approach this time.
A lot of people were targeted, but in the end, they only sent you to handle it?
If we send too many people, we risk tipping our hand.
Why not tell The Order?
Well, the Chamber of Discipline did catch a few perps, but they're not quick to act without solid proof.
And... some of the higher-ups in the Order might just be happy to see the Montellis having a little trouble.
The biggest issue I find is...
You actually volunteered for extra work?
Really? That's the biggest issue you find?
There's probably something you're not telling me, isn't there?
Alright, alright... You've got sharp instincts. Spending too much time with you, and I'm running out of secrets.
I was the one who delivered Talos and those Black Alley leaders to The Order.
What?!
I knew it all along.
The Blazing Nightwalker... So is it the Rinascitan tradition to have a moniker?
Yeah, that's me... the Blazing Nightwalker. But honestly? I really don't want to keep repeating that name.
By tradition, shouldn't you have revealed your true identity at the end?
Oh, you're talking about the stories where, after a lot of hardship and misunderstanding, one side lets the truth out with their last breath, leaving the other to regret it forever?
Where did you read that?
I've got my own ways to keep entertained.
Hiding my true identity got old fast. Since you were curious, I might as well just tell you.
After all, you're not someone I can't trust, right?
Well, as you have already known, I am the Blazing Nightwalker... though I really wish I didn't have to keep repeating that name.
Honestly, it's a bit of a burden...
Oh, and by the way, after you became the Laureate, they're giving you all sorts of monikers too.
The family sent me to handle this, partly because they didn't want a big operation to stir things up, and partly because... well, it was a strategic move.
Hard for me to imagine you all fired up like that once.
I have to say it again, I never called myself that.
Back then, I was just doing what needed to be done. Never planned on picking up a fancy nickname.
It's hard to imagine that name suiting you now.
What happened?
Did work change you?
You seem to have lost a spark.
Well, that's what work does to you...
Do you think this "Talos" is the real deal then?
...Not sure. Could just be the same old story repeating itself.
Let's call it a cleanup job.
If things go smoothly, maybe we can grab a late-night snack after, hmm?
I'll go all in then.
I don't think this is serious enough to give it your all.
Just do enough to get it done. But keep some of that enthusiasm for the snacks later, hm?

You wake up in the middle of the night and find it difficult to fall back to sleep, so you decide to take a walk. To your surprise, you run into Zani, who also struggles to fall asleep. You take some rest in your room. By the time you wake up, you realize you haven't slept much.
It's almost time. Let's split up and prepare for the ambush.
Let's see if we can catch them in the act.
(Zani is clearly doing more than just "enough to get it done," but I'll hold off on mentioning it for now.)

I'll watch your back and keep an eye out for anyone trying to shadow you.
You wait on the roof for some time. As you anticipated, several suspicious men begin to appear.
(While I wait for Zani, maybe I should search the area where that voice came from. )
Figured someone was waiting for us. But you walked right into it, didn't ya?
Alright, boys! Let's put 'em down!
Need a hand?

Stop resisting. Just surrender!
Well, my boss gave me this—!
Zani.
Let's move in. Now!
Blimey, how the hell are you movin' so quick?!
*Beep*—*Beep*!
Put Bakie down. Now!
Stop this pointless resistance!
Not a chance! It's my hostage now... This is an Echonapping, you hear!
Ha! Ain't no way you'll do somethin' stupid while I'm holding this Echo!
Beep! Beep!
Hey! Don't be causing trouble for folks who need their breakfast bright and early.
Alright, start talking. Where's your hideout? Who's the one really calling the shots?
Looks like we'll have to drag him back. We'll get answers sooner or later.
A shame this one's only good for squealing. He's not the one we're after.
Is it... me you're looking for?
My name is Colleen... Please, help me and my friends.

After defeating the gang members, one manages to escape and takes Bakie from Trattoria Margherita as hostage. Just when the situation seems dire, Zani arrives in time and takes him out. And the mysterious help-seeker finally reveals themselves.
Before we go any further, shouldn't you explain who you are first?
I'm from the Black Alley...
So you are one of them too?
You don't exactly look like you're in the same business.
No, no, no... The Black Alley is more than just the gang! It's the place too.
The entrance to the Black Alley is shut. It's done.
You're right, Talos destroyed it. But there's another way in...
It used to be a home for vagrants like us. A few scraps, a couple of jobs... just enough to get by.
But then she came, and it all went up in smoke...
What did she do to you?
She came in claiming this place was hers since they owned it before.
Told us, if we wanted to stay, we had to follow her rules. No other choice.
Steal, lie, cheat, rob... same as the old days. Give her your tribute, or... or you get a beating.
A fish that slipped the net...
Sounds just like how the Black Alley ran things... But do people actually accept her as the acting Talos?
Some people did. They wanted to, you know? The ones with the dirty hands already. They were easy.
But the main reason is that no one can stand up to her...
Is she that strong?
Why?
Colleen doesn't answer your question, instead she looks at Zani with a conflicted and wary expression.
I'll wait outside.
No.
{PlayerName}？
Colleen, if you can't trust my friend, then I can't offer you my help.
Trust goes both ways. You can't ask for help with one hand while holding a knife with the other.
The operation is a wrap. Bring the ones we caught in and then everyone can call it a day.
Got it, Ms. Zani. Any leads on your side?
No, nothing to report.
Ah, looks like we'll have to try again tomorrow.
It's just us now. Anything else bothering you while I'm at it?
A Terminal... Talos also has a Terminal. It lets her transform into a powerful Echo.
So that's it. You are worried the Terminal was supplied by someone from the Montelli family, aren't you?
That's why you doubt us and prefer to put your faith in a wayfaring Laureate, hm?
I'm sorry...
There's no need to apologize. You're a victim in this, with every right to be suspicious.
So then, {PlayerName}, what do you think we should do?
What's your take? It's your job, after all.
I can't ignore someone who's asking for help.
I want to see how powerful this Echo really is.
*Sigh*... Who told everyone to call it a day again?
As an employee of the Montelli family, I have an obligation to stop any Terminals from being misused.
I'll just have to ask the boss for double overtime pay and an extra vacation after this.
Great, but have you spent the vacation you got last time?
Are you really bringing up something so depressing now?
Thank you, thank you both!

The mysterious help-seeker, Colleen, admits she is from the Black Alley, a place that was once home to the homeless but is now seized by Talos and her gang. Colleen warns that Talos possesses a Terminal of unknown origin. You and Zani are determined to stop Talos from exploiting its power.
Talos has us blindfolded whenever we leave the Black Alley. Keeps us from knowing the new entrance. A runner takes us to the meeting spot.
I'll take you to him.
That's his hideout. Over there.
He's a slippery one. One wrong move, and he'll be gone, off in a Gondola before you can blink.
We can use that to our advantage.
Looks like we're thinking the same thing.
I'll cause a distraction up front. Leave the show to me.
And you'll move to checkmate.
Following the plan, you move to the rear of the hideout. You signal Zani to initiate the operation once in position.
Same as usual. Just another day's work.
Wait, wait! Wait, wait! You're after the Black Alley's entrance, aren't you?
I haven't said a word yet...
I know my value to people.
Now that you've got me, no point in resisting. The longer I hold out, the more pain I'm asking for.
Smart people know when to give in. It's how I stayed alive.
{PlayerName}, have you got him?
Yeah, and he's already talking.
So we won't need to "help" him talk after all.
Once he coughs up the entrance location, we'll head straight there from here.
The family is almost on site. They can handle the cleanup.
With the description the runner provided, you find the Black Alley's entrance.
Might be a bit late to ask, but… Colleen, you did what Talos asked, didn't you?
I didn't...
Did you forget what {PlayerName} said? Trust goes both ways.
I… I didn't have a choice! If I didn't, they'd... they'd...you know, hurt me!
Then when the time comes, make sure you tell the Chamber of Discipline everything. No lies.
But… but I…
Don't excuse yourself by saying you were forced into it. Can you do that?
Fine... I get it.
The Blazing Nightwalker is no joke.
Giving someone a lecture? Are you sure you're Zani?
Ugh, don't call me that.
Believe me, I'd kill to be in a bed right now instead of standing out here.
Let's get this over with.
I'm praying it doesn't reek in there.
Please don't point that out right now.
Don't worry. It may be an underground waterway, but it's been abandoned for a long time now.
It's not exactly clean, but it's livable. We did some work on it.
The pipes are a maze, though. They split up the territory by rank...
Talos is holed up somewhere deep in the waterway.
"Demons always live in hell, like the Primus always stays in the Cathedral." Yeah, that's about right.
Oh, and {PlayerName}, masks on.
The mask makes things a lot easier.
It's better if neither of us gets recognized too easily.
Fair point, but...
H-hey… I'll pretend I don't know who you are!
Guess I don't need to spell it out for you.
Following the runner's route, you locate the hidden entrance to the Black Alley and confront Talos to put an end to this once and for all.
(Looks like they left by Gondola...)
(The trail's gone cold. I'll wait for Zani to return.)
Here. Sorry to keep you waiting.
Mmm... those Chamber of Discipline folk are as difficult to deal with as ever.
How did it go?
Well... you know how they are with the Montellis these days. No surprise they didn't share any interrogation details.
I told them the thieves claimed to be with the Black Alley, but the Chamber doesn't bother with rumors without solid proof.
What exactly is the Black Alley?
A gang made up of criminals, although how many joined willingly is anyone's guess.
A lot of vagrants were pressed into their service. Pawns in a game of crime.
The leadership got wiped out a few years ago by someone working solo. The leftovers? They were screwed. Some are still rotting in prison.
Do you think those two were just a few stragglers?
Maybe. Or maybe they just wanted to spook you... but they picked the wrong person to mess with.
You're still thinking about that person who asked for help, huh? Got any leads?
(Tell Zani what you discovered.)
You think she's in the same boat as those vagrants in the past? Forced into something they didn't choose?
Ah, {PlayerName}, you're the type who can't turn your back when someone asks for help.
It's not too late. Got time for a detour?
Is it far from here?
The old entrance to the Black Alley.
If they're crawling back from the ashes, we might find a clue or two at their old haunt.
I've got time to spare, so where are we going?

You uncover some clues, but none lead you to the mysterious help-seeker. You decide to wait for Zani to return before continuing. After her return, she shares stories about a lone hero who single-handedly wiped out the Black Alley, a known criminal gang. This makes you suspect that the person might be connected to the Black Alley.
This is it. Just hit the right spot, and the trapdoor should open.
What's on your mind?
How come you're so familiar with this?
You're not quite the same as you were during the daytime.
Mmm... I have some past experience...
After all, it's not work hours now.
Let's focus on what's in front of us first.
Protecting the rich...
Is not exactly the work I find meaningful.
But I get to slack off
Nothing to complain about...
Late again...
Help!
Heh heh heh...
You're all out of luck, sweetheart!
Hey.
Thank you! Thank you!
"Thank you"...
Have I ever thanked anyone so earnestly before?
What was I thinking back then?
Wishing someone would stand up for me...
Right?
...I'll walk a little longer.
Who are you?
Mind your own damn business!
It was you yesterday...
Err...
Have you heard...
About that one?
The Blazing Nightwalker...
How overdone...
Huh... time to work again.
Anyway, that's the real story behind that ridiculous name.
I thought it would be a more elaborate story.
Not everything needs to be turned into some grand tale.
In this city, it's mostly the same routine every day.
How long can I snooze before I'm late...
Which time's best to line up to get a fresh wrap...
How to sleep without lying in bed for hours...
These little routines are fragile. One bad move and they're gone.
But likewise, just one bold move is enough to bring them back.
Most people got it wrong, slapping that big name on me.
It's just part of my routine. Like snoozing, eating, or keeping my hair and horns in check.
So, is taking down an entire gang also part of it?
I was alone back then. I didn't even bother hiding who I was.
And that's when the trouble started to find me.
I thought, why wait for it to get worse? Better to finish it quickly.
But of course, I made it worse... Too fast, too soon.
So how did you deal with it back then?
The Montelli family reached out to me and offered to clean up the mess. Even said they'd back me up in the future.
So, I changed jobs. The work is the same. No difference.
Disappointed?
Your instincts came from a good place. A fist might not be as sharp as a blade, but it can still break through deeply rooted problems.
And up close, it's gentle enough to protect what's important.
So don't let today bother you.
No, I'm not letting it bother me.
Cleaning up simple scum doesn't weigh on me.
So what you said back there...
Just reliving some old memories, that's all.
But you're right about something...
What you said just now applies to you, too.
The difference, though, is that you are a blade. A weapon that can break the cycle.
But you don't seem to realize it. Seeing you has brought some old feelings back to me.
Don't you see? Ever since you helped make the Carnevale happen, Ragunna's been different.
Things are busier now. There's more work, more opportunities.
I told you before that these routines are fragile. One bad move and they're gone, right?
So... a stable environment is the only way to reduce the bad moves. That's the way we get to keep our routines.

Ha... I see you've been waiting for me, Cartur.
He was my manager back in the Bough of Legions. Has a gift for knowing exactly what to say to anyone, though that's his flaw, too.
For a manager, isn't the skill of speech always a gift?
Domina Julia Silva hoped you'd behave and return home. She bid that I reason with you at the earliest opportunity.
But... it seems you've found yourself a new ally. I daresay her hopes are dashed.
And? What's your point?
How disappointing. Not even a hint of charm when there's no crowd around to impress.
Feeling confident about this new team of yours? What do you think your chances are of winning the championship?
With me and {PlayerName}? One hundred percent.
Enough, Cartur. Spare me the games and empty chatter! I have one question for you...
...Are you involved in the Silvas' match-fixing?
No. I do love money, but I don't stoop to that level to get it.
Fair enough. You may leave now.
Tut, tut, dangerous question, Lupa. Think carefully. The Silvas may have made you a star, but they can just as easily snuff that star out.
I've never doubted your talent, but these are the rules of the game.
I know the rules well enough.
...I just wonder if Domina Julia truly understands who's making the rules now, and where she stands in this game.

Lupa's former manager, Cartur, waits for her by the road, but it's clear Lupa has no intention of returning to fight for her patron House. 

The power struggles between Septimont's noble Houses simmer beneath the surface as the Great Agon unfolds.
Is this Cartur also from House Silva?
Not exactly. He's a free man, though he's handled Bough of Legions business for the past few years.
Look, {PlayerName}. Once we cross the Hero's Way, we'll get to the Capitoline Hill district.
For centuries, countless Gladiators have walked this very path to Colosseum Olymdos... just as we are now.
Are you ready for the Gladiator's Agon?
Yes, I'm ready.
I need a moment.
Happy hunting, Gladiators!
Of course. I'll be right here waiting.
Fierce attacks. Shame it's only exposing your weaknesses.
Hahaha! Great work! Your skill is fueling my bloodlust, {PlayerName}!
(Cartethyia... standing on the water?)
(That abnormal sensation came over me again when my sword struck the contender's Echo. )
(All the Echoes in Septimont seem to exhibit unstable power. Something is definitely off.)
(But it seems like no one else has noticed.)
Contender Lupa isn't in the Bough of Legions anymore... what a shame.
Just two days before the finals, as well! It's unfair to her former teammates and her fans.
Is it about the money? She's changed teammates how many times now? As for that newcomer next to her...
Without the Silvas' patronage, there's no way a gladiator from the outskirts could rise to fame so quickly.
Quiet down. Where are you hearing these rumors? Open your eyes, Lupa has never once thrown a match!
Hmph, everyone thinks they know the real truth. But consider this, it's a fact I know to be true...
Let's go, my fellow warrior.
It's all going as planned! Let's get you settled somewhere comfortable, then tomorrow, we head to the Colosseum Olymdos for the semi-finals.
I've been meaning to ask, is there a body of water in the city? I think Cartethyia might've passed through there.
A body of water? Yes, but it's been abandoned for years. That elevator can take you to the upper city, though.
If you want to try looking for her, we can start there!
Thanks. And…
Yes?
Those people just now… they talked about match-fixing. Don't you want to challenge that?
I didn't have time to gather enough proof before I left. Besides, this isn't the right moment.
Once we win the Great Agon, I'll make everything public. In Septimont, only the winners get to speak their truth.
Doesn't it bother you?
Their slander gets under my skin.
Hehe, I'm fine. High praise leads to harsh words. It's always like that.
Heh, a strong warrior with a kind heart... Rare traits for a hunter.
Honestly, I don't care what people say. This kind of thing happens every day in Septimont. If you can't handle it, you won't last.
Tarnishing rivals' reputations is one of their usual tricks. I cut off their betting profits, so it's only natural they'd be upset.
Besides, now I have a reliable warrior by my side. That's all that matters.
No worrying about whether my teammate can keep up, no dealing with petty politics... just the thrill of the fight.
Thank you for that, {PlayerName}.

After your victory in the second Agon, you sense Cartethyia's presence by the waters of Septimont, just as you notice the strange energy affecting Septimont's Echoes.

Meanwhile, Lupa's departure from House Silva sparks retaliatory rumors, but she appears unaffected, focused on helping your search for Cartethyia.
Beware of the Kerasaurs lurking below. Those Tacet Discords will ambush anyone who falls into the water.
Are those the city's ruins down there?
Yes, remnants of the Old District.
We rarely use this route since it's too dangerous. But some thrill-seekers come here to hunt Tacet Discords.
Speaking of which, this area is actually under Silva jurisdiction. I used to play here as a child.
You said Cartethyia might've been here. Do you have an idea where she passed through?
I think… somewhere over there.
Ah, that's where the statue of Tercules is.
This is the place. I'll look for Cartethyia's traces here.
How?
Through... the connection we share.
Alright then. I'll wait here. Good luck!
You call upon the power of Imperator, calling for the one who shares its essence.
The unique frequency pulses through your blade and spreads across the water in ripples. But the connection weakens, fading into the distance.
Cartethyia isn't here.
How's it going? You look... frustrated.
I just feel uneasy.
I'm okay. We still have the lead on Arsinosa.
Don't worry, we can follow the lead on Arsinosa.
That's right! I'm sure you'll make progress by the finals.
Tercules… His statues once stood tall on both sides of the street, watching over the heroes of Septimont as they set out to hunt.
Back then, the chimes drifting up from the city were the finest sounds of glory.
You arrive at the waters where you felt Cartethyia's presence but still find no trace of her.
Cartethyia...
I've never heard that name before, but it feels strangely familiar...
Look! A wingray right here!
It can give us a lift.
(Someone's still alive.)
Are you okay? You seem like a local… are there any other survivors?
I'm managing. I-I can still move, but I'm exhausted. I've walked for so long, for so far... but I still can't leave this city.
The white <te href=850161>Tidal Blight</te> follows me wherever I go.
(Tidal Blight… could she mean the Dark Tide?)
What's your name?
I… don't remember.
That's alright. Memories can be recovered, and so can your name. I've been through something similar myself, and someone helped me find my way back.
I've only just arrived here. All of Septimont is cloaked in mist. Would you mind sharing with me what you still remember?
Who… are you?
My name is Cartethyia. I'm Ragunna's…
I'm a wandering knight from Ragunna.
A wandering knight… ah.
Don't worry, I'll take care of them.
Come forth, and face my blade.
Who are they...?
Oh, some minor noble houses that didn't make it into the Agon.
But in Septimont, strength and power go hand in hand. Nobles get more, but they better prove they're worth it and pull their weight for the city.
The Agon isn't just about fortune. It's a way to find the capable. For nobles, the ability to command and control Echoes is a basic responsibility.
If the heir of a noble house isn't strong enough, it signals that the house is unfit to hunt down Tacet Discords or protect Septimont.
So... if a noble's been living it up, they'll end up broke and thrown out of the city after paying high patronage fees for a gladiator who doesn't even make the cut.
Makes sense.
Sounds harsh.
"Strength is everything." That's how it works. You've fought your battles too, or you wouldn't be here.
Might not work like this everywhere, but here in Septimont, with the Dark Tide breathing down our necks, it's our survival code.
For most Septimontians, the Agon isn't just an event. It's the training ground nobles and commoners alike have to fight in.
The victors show no mercy to the defeated. People here despise weakness, worship strength, and crave glory.
Where you come from don't matter. Prove yourself, and the crowd will scream your name. The spotlight's yours, the arena's your stage.
But if you can't can't keep up, if you're not chosen... you'll be left in the shadows.
Welcome to my city, Gryphon's Fortress of Capitoline Hill!

After coming to Septimont, you learn from Lupa just how important the arena is to the city. It can elevate someone to the heights of power or cast them into obscurity. 

Meanwhile, in a side of the city unseen, Cartethyia walks beneath the shadowed skies of Septimont and meets the Nameless One.
Hmm, my heart's racing like crazy...
Do you feel sick?
Not really, I just have this uneasy feeling.
Uneasy? Did you sense something dangerous in Septimont?
I don't know how to put it. It's strange, like things are all tangled up somehow...
Abby, we've arrived. How do you feel now?
Abby?
(Nothing from my Tacet Mark. Is it sleeping? Or is it...)
(Cartethyia helped with Abby's symptoms before... I could really use her help now.)
(We share the same thread of Imperator's power. I could try using that to sense where she is.)
(What's that creature she's facing? A half-human, half-lion Tacet Discord? Or a special Echo?)
(She was here before.)
(I'll follow this same path and see if I can find someone to talk to.)
As your fingers touch the cold statue, the whispers of fallen heroes ring through your mind.
The clash of weapons mingles with battle cries and hearty laughter. Amid these sounds, the <te href=850166>Hero's Legacy Armor</te> murmurs its late master's eternal longing for glory...
(That armor might be an Echo.)
(An Echo... that awaits a true warrior.)

Since arriving in Septimont, Abby has remained silent within your Tacet Mark. 

You try to sense Cartethyia but are confronted with an unbelievable vision—Cartethyia facing a half-human, half-lion creature.

Following her tracks, you head toward a sculpture beneath a stone wall where you find the Hero's Legacy Armor.
(It seems happy. Is it because I'm reminding it of past battles?)
(Looks like I've made my first friend here.)
There are traces of a Resonance Energy discharge everywhere...
What a MESS! This place looks like it was just bombarded!
Yep, that's definitely Cartethyia's residual frequencies. Where did she go?
The traces will guide you here, {PlayerName}.
And, when the time comes, you'll bring this story to its rightful end.
The scent of seawater... It's right ahead.
The next qualifier is just ahead. Once it's over, we can take the cable car to the upper city!
On an autumn day, the view as you ascend and the breeze on your face can truly lift your spirits.
Why would the place you mentioned be abandoned?
Because of the first Dark Tide in Ragunna… Oh, you know what a Dark Tide is, right?
Yes.
Due to certain safety concerns at the time, the main city district was relocated further up the hill.
{Cus:Var,VarType=Global Key=main_team_name} versus Vulcan Mining.
Let the Agon begin!
So… this is Septimont.
{Cus:Var,VarType=Global Key=main_team_name} versus Blue Furies.
Let the Agon begin!
Kerasaurs here. Let's take them down!
What set off this huge energy surge? There are traces of Cartethyia's Resonance Energy discharge everywhere...
What a MESS! This place looks like it was just bombarded!
(Sniffs) Yep, that's definitely Cartethyia's residual frequencies. Where did she go?
(Its frequency is similar to the Echoes in Ragunna. Could it have originated from Imperator's power as well?)
(But it's unstable, as if something else is interfering... Strange, it's just like Abby said.)
(I can feel its source close to the city, but can't pin down where exactly.)
Boss, you're looking so serious!
And you are...?
Me? I'm a traveling Taoist from <te href=850154>Mengzhou</te>. Just call me Buling.
Exorcism, talisman divination, fortune-telling... you name it, I "bling" it! So {PlayerName}, you want to try your luck fah?
How did you know my name?
Heard about you from an old friend. You know Jianxin? Pretty sure you met her in Jinzhou. She trained with the same master before me.
We've got history. Last time I went up to the mountain to see her, she mentioned you.
So I hear you're looking for someone? Tsk, not so easy, not so easy. The feng shui in Rinascita is not good.
The Qi is trapped underwater, not good flow. No luck now, bad sign. You should be careful, Boss!
You show up and the stars change... I was betting on who could break the deadlock, so I'm glad I caught you first.

You encounter a young Taoist girl named Buling, who claims to be from Mengzhou.

She seems to have sought you out deliberately, but after a few cryptic exchanges, she vanishes without a trace.
The semi-finals are tomorrow, yeah? Wonder who'll claim the title this year…
Beasts Beneath. They're the safest pick.
Can you two shut it already? You're drowning out the broadcast! I can't even hear Breen's commentary!
What that odd little girl from earlier said sounded like a load of nonsense, but it felt...
Felt like it might be true, right?! I swear, it's like she could see the outcome! Just like one of our Priestesses!
She said she was from Mengzhou, didn't she? People from Huanglong do have some strange tricks up their sleeves...
Too bad she just vanished like that. I was about to ask her about my family next.
The teams in the top ranks now… match pretty close to that piece The Gladiator ran a while back.
The Blue Furies, Beasts Beneath, Vulcan Mining, and the Bough of Legions are all top of the leaderboard. No real surprise.
Speaking of the Bough of Legions... I've heard some whispers lately.
Bet it all, didn't I... If I'd known earlier, I wouldn't… Oh, to the Tide with it!
I told you! That friend who pulled you into the underground betting was setting you up from the start!
I.. I... (Sobbing)
After a long, bumpy ride from Chongzhou, I've lost count of how many times that damn ship's turned...
Wide open skies… Ah, Septimont. I just hope this year's Great Agon doesn't leave me disappointed.
Heh, after the Carnevale, finally something that piques my interest again.
The one who claimed the Laurel took my family by surprise. I wonder who'll claim the Champion title here...
If we'd booked tickets six months ago, we wouldn't be stuck camping out here!
Who knew the Leonidas Hotel would be this packed? I can't even call in to book a room… Wasn't this hard last year.
And those prices… Let 'em stay if they want to, but I'm not paying that. What's wrong with a tent, anyway?
This is the Great Agon, after all! Ugh, fine. It is what it is this time, but next time, you'll follow my lead.
I just saw Lupa heading into the arena with some stranger!
The Bough of Legions is backed by House Silva. Didn't you notice how often Lupa's partner changes?
House Silva only sees her as their golden goose… It's a good thing Lupa's finally breaking free.
Troubled by how difficult it is to wrangle a bottle of Heartpour? Fret not, we've got a few bottles tucked away here!
What a beautiful hotel... The package I bought was worth it.
Septimont is a fine place. The scenic views and amenities alone are perfect. No wonder people all over Solaris come to watch the Gladiator's Agon.
Mama! I want to go to the baths right now!
We'll drop off our bags at the hotel first, then we'll go, okay?
Look at that hairtail fish! What a projection, I can't believe it's broadcasting across such a wide range...
Septimont's Echo conversion tech is something else. There must be a genius behind this.
Exactly. I'll need to put in a request with the Ephor's Palace and try to meet with the researchers here.
House Silva has been expelled from the city!
The fall of a family as entrenched as theirs will spell unrest for the Ephor's Palace and the Senate.
Who knows, maybe this year Arsinosa will give her blessing to the winners of the Great Agon...
You think so?
No harm, right? I'm already an old man, power doesn't mean much to me anymore.
Arsinosa... our Iudicis. It'd be good to lay eyes on her more.
Every time I do, it takes me right back to the matches I fought years ago...
...Bough of Legions, you sun-forsaken lot! I want my money back!
They lost! Why didn't anyone tell me Lupa switched teams?!
How much did you bet this time?
Ah, you're the one who won the title with Lupa, aren't you!
You two were somethin' else! Perfect teamwork, I was hooked from start to finish!
That match was spectacular! You earned every bit of that glory.
Hope Septimont's sights live up to your expectations, Champion!
Didn't head out with Lupa today, eh?
Aye! Next time, come with us. I'll buy you both a round!
To earn Arsinosa's blessing means you're a warrior of the highest caliber, no doubt.
Real glad to see the title of Champion go to folks like you and Lupa.
Rats and mud! The whole city's run dry, save for that greedy merchant hoarding it all for a pretty penny.
Look at the price... twenty times the usual cost.
You don't understand, I have to try Lupa's endorsed drink!
What say we teach this pig a lesson? Let's steal his stock of Heartpour...
Contender Lupa... look at that smile.
I hope she and her new partner win the title!
I hope that smile never fades from her face.
So that's Lupa's new team, huh?
Interesting. Let's see if they can live up to the hype.
The entire city is holding its breath for that final showdown...
No… that can't be her lover, can it?
I fabricated the story for The Septimont Tribune. Did it somehow come true?
But... I've never even been in love myself. Did I depict it in the right way?

Phrolova offers a faint smile that carries a hint of some unknown expectation.
It feels like you've fallen into the velvety embrace of a Lycoris. When you open your eyes again, the bustling noise of the Great Agon surrounds you.

Lupa speaks with you a little longer before leaving. The flood of new information leaves you weary, and you quickly fall asleep.
When the sun rises, the day of the finals arrives.
Come to think of it, we haven't had anything to eat since those two matches.
Right, I know just the thing I want you to try!
Oh, I can already smell it, can almost taste it...
Fulvia! Two large platters please, with two bottles of <te href=850151>Heartpour</te>!
Ohh! It's Lupa!
I heard she left the Bough of Legions...
That's enough, folks. You know the rules, no gossip outside the arena.
Just dig in!
Still got that fire, huh, Fulvia?
You should talk. Finally cut ties with the Silvas, eh? With the way they handled the share of profits, you should've left sooner!
Haha… well, back then a strong backer was exactly what I needed. Can't say it was all bad.
So, this is your new partner. Hmm... Looks like you can handle yourself.
You can tell just by looking?
The most dependable one in all of Solaris, at your service.
Can't keep a tavern running for long if you don't have a good eye.
Well, well, you better prove it in the Agon then.
By the way, Heartpour is sold out today. Guess the celebrity branding really worked.
What? Oh, come on...
What's Heartpour?
A drink I endorsed. Most of the drinks I promoted were... Ahem. But this one's actually really good.
What about the others?
If my name's on it, you don't have to worry about quality. It's just that the taste... well, let's just say it's "meh" at best.
Anyway, I'll get you a taste of Heartpour later. For now, let's enjoy the meal!
So, fellow warrior, any stories to share? There is still much to learn about each other.
Hey Lupa, got a message from Old Appius. He said the new batch of restored footage just arrived, including those about Contender Mya.
Oh thanks! I almost forgot with everything going on lately.
Restored footage?
Recordings of major matches or famous contenders. Helpful for those who want to learn from them.
Ephor Augusta's are the most popular. Four years ago, she became the champion and a household name by crushing every single opponent. From there, she worked her way up into the Ephor's seat.
But I prefer watching Contender Mya's matches over any of the past champions.
I think she's... got real heart.
You can feel it, even through the recordings. The way she threw herself into every fight.
Do you think we'll face her in this Agon?
Ha, not likely. She disappeared during a Great Agon years ago.
Some say she got tangled up in illegal betting scandals. Others think the pressure from her manager drove her to leave Septimont... There are plenty of rumors, but no one knows what really happened.
Still, it's frustrating! To just disappear halfway through...
If you fail to make it to the end, people will see you as nothing.

You and Lupa go to a restaurant, drawing the stares of many.

Lupa mentions a former Gladiator she admires, Mya, a true competitor. However, Mya's career was cut short during the Great Agon two decades ago when she vanished under mysterious circumstances.
Solis never disappoints! Their dishes hit the spot every time! Now that our bellies are full, time to relax.
To Leonidas Hotel! It's the best place for travelers in Septimont. I've got a long-term rental there myself.
Ta-da! Welcome to your new spot! It's a lifetime suite, and it's yours anytime you need it during your stay in Septimont.
It's gorgeous. Thank you.
A lifetime suite? It must've cost a fortune!
Speaking of which, I own a room in the Black Shores too.
Don't mention it! The hotel owner sees us as future champions. Supporting us is an investment that'll pay off, of that I am certain.
Ha, I've been a name in the arena for years now. I'm doing alright. Besides, it didn't hurt that the hotel owner gave me a nice discount.
The Black Shores, huh? I'd love to see it one day. Maybe when the time's right, I'll venture beyond Septimont and explore the world out there.
You know... gladiating means everything to me!
I really, really love it... I know I'm lucky. I know what I want and I'm doing what I love.
Compared to those drifting through life, I've already been given so much. But sometimes...
But sometimes...?
You don't look happy, Lupa.
Well, sometimes, I feel a little... afraid.
Haha, well, I'm not unhappy!
I was born for this. But the more I embrace it, the more I fear losing it.
I can't help but wonder... What is it that fills me up when I'm under those lights? My passion for the fight? Or the favor it brings me?
If one day I lost that favor... would I be more helpless, panicked, and heartbroken than those who never had it in the first place?
If that day comes, would I still be able to say, "I love this life?"
You would if you truly love it.
Even if you wouldn't, you shouldn't blame yourself for it.
That's something only you can figure out.
You're right... I hope that love never fades. Not until I'm buried in the Vale of Glory.
Thank you. You're kind. I'll try not to dwell on it. Still, sometimes I feel... guilty. Why should I be so lucky when others aren't?
Haha! Well said. It's my life to live, my path to walk. If I don't make my choices, who will? That's how you live without regrets.
Tomorrow is the semi-finals. We'd best get some rest, {PlayerName}.
Night, my fellow warrior.

Lupa books you into her lifetime suite. Now, no matter when you return to Septimont, you will always have a place to stay.

She confides her worry: Is the joy she finds in the arena due to her passion for it, or because of the favor it brings her?

As she says goodnight and leaves, you see her suddenly transform into another young woman. It lasts only a moment, like a fleeting illusion.

You lie down in the soft bed, the phonograph beside you lulling you to sleep.
As the foreign yet familiar melody plays, you drift into a deep slumber...
(Words? Lines of them, all around me...)
(...And music coming from above.)
This is but an illusion. One of the night, one of dreams. Not like the spectacle you saw in the glimmer of the Carnevale.
Here, I am not your foe, nor can we harm each other, should we so wish. Lay your blade to rest, if only for now. Tis' a pleasure to see you again, {PlayerName}, on this special stage.
A city wild and beautiful, chasing endless glory... Tell me, does Septimont please you as much as Ragunna once did?
Let's cut to the chase. You're connected to Cartethyia's disappearance.
Has the Fractsidus's hand already reached Septimont?
Ah, so it is she you seek. It appears this special Resonator has you rather captivated.
When one wrestles against the torrents of fate, every signpost is an anchor guiding you toward the infinite horizon.
Let's take our time. I would like our talk to be pleasant. No one will bother us here.
I have an associate who adores the heroic tales told throughout this land.
For this reason...  the missing girl you seek and the anomaly you sensed in Septimont, they are indeed threads in his tapestry.
You could call it... an obsession of his.
Stop beating around the bush. Tell me what you really came to say.
Tell me what the Fractsidus is planning.
Every hero's tale begins with a trial.
Your wisdom and courage, your compassion and resolve, your hope and madness... Will they be strong enough to carry you through the trial? To make you the hero of this story?
Read it. I hope this story speaks to you. The answers you seek lie within these pages.
If we continue to meet as foes, the symphony grows monotonous. I confess I find it... rather uninspired.
I'll ask again, Phrolova. What are you doing here in Septimont, and why give me this?
I'm giving this story a little nudge.
As of now, you and that Blessed Maiden from the tower are deeply interwoven in the fate he has spun.
So you're not the only Overseer active in Rinascita.
Scar, your nameless ally, and you... The Fractsidus seems to revel in the company of those with twisted obsessions.
It's not as you imagine. You've already met my associate, you see. He trusts what he sees, not the words of others.
(I've already crossed paths with him since arriving in Rinascita…?)
As a creator, he always hopes his characters will craft twists and turns that he himself cannot foresee.
He believes that the closer one stands to the protagonist, the greater their influence over the tale.
But the true lead of this story has yet to emerge.
I gave you this <te href=850153>play</te> so you can see the ending. That Gladiator girl will be the harbinger of the Dark Tide in Septimont.
All glory will be consumed, and the pride of heroes will dissolve within a blackened maelstrom. Such is the finale "she" holds most dear.
This is a short story, {PlayerName}. One that only lasts three days. When the final match concludes, so too will this story.
You could claim the spotlight by ending her life before the curtain falls. Change the ending, and the tragedy is averted.
But should you falter, or worse, warn her of what's to come, the consequences will spiral far beyond anything you can imagine.
What you're proposing I do... Tell me, what reason do I have to trust a word you're saying, Phrolova?
You don't need to trust me. Let my words slip from your thoughts, if you wish. As I've already said, the story will unfold as my associate has written it.
The choice lies with you, {PlayerName}. It is a freedom we all hold.
Even the wildest imaginations draw from what already exists.
So it is with this story. It follows a template, and even its creator cannot escape its confines.
Choose wisely, {PlayerName}. Time is still on your side, for now.
I look forward to your performance in this grand finale.

In your dreams, you see Phrolova floating in the air with pages swirling around her.

Phrolova gives you a play that contains an account of the future. You don't believe her, but she seems indifferent. 

She tells you that Lupa will be the one to trigger the Dark Tide's surge in Septimont, and it will happen within three days.
Morning, {PlayerName}!
...Hmm? You don't exactly look well rested.
(Phrolova may not have told the whole truth, but there's no denying the anomaly here in Septimont. And neither Lupa nor the others here seem to notice.)
(And that fleeting image… Lupa turning into that unfamiliar girl... I need more clues before making any decisions.)
I'm fine. Just a bad dream. Let's get going, our next stop is the Colosseum Olymdos, right?
You got it! Let's get going!
As expected, the Silvas chose to face us in the semi-finals. The news spreads quickly.
You knew this was coming?
Of course. To them, it's a provocation... and to forfeit would be a disgrace.
Domina Julia must be here. She wouldn't miss a moment like this.
She's shrewd and exceptionally capable but arrogant to the core. She's convinced that she's always right.
She doesn't believe in talking things through, thinks it's for the weak. So we'll show her we don't need rigged matches to win. We'll win with pure stength!
Four years have passed, and I stand before you once more. Not as a Gladiator, but as a witness to the start of this grand event.
You all know well that Gladiatorial combat is the lifeblood of our ancient and mighty city.
"Seize power, and fight for victory."
Once, we fought to survive on the seas. That same instinct courses through our veins today. The instinct to face fate head-on and defy it.
Remember, those who cling to glory without the strength to defend it will see it slip through their fingers.
Warriors! By the eternal sun, may your courage honor Septimont and prove your loyalty to its spirit!
I look forward to the rise of new heroes in this Agon.
Let the Agon begin.
Come, my fellow warrior! Victory is ours for the taking!

You and Lupa face House Silva in the semi-finals.

Ephor Augusta gives a stirring opening speech. Now it's time to prove that true victory should be won by strength alone.
Are you ready for the Gladiator's Agon?
Couldn't be more ready.

And promise us now, don't be causin' us worry. Let us know you've made it there safely, okay?
…I will. And I'll bring back the applause when I return. On that day, I'll stand by her side, apologize, and tell her everything.
But for now… Mrs. Leah, it's time to set out!
Excuse me, is Phrolova going to a concert?
Sorry, who are you?
I've come looking for a Gem.
A Gem? What are you talking about?
Maybe Phrolova knows.
Me? I've never heard of it… Sorry, but you must have the wrong person. We haven't met before, have we?

Alright, no time to dawdle! We should head off now!

Well now... I can't say for sure.

Phrolova, you're here!

You meet Phrolova in her past self and some others who know her. You try to ask them about the location of the Threnodian's residual energy, but you are a complete stranger to them, and they have no idea what you are seeking.
(No one here knows about the Gem… I should look elsewhere.)

(...Could this be her home?)

(But what does "a new anchor" mean? Who is she using… and who is using her?)
None shall stop... the final cadenza...
Phrolova?
(That was her voice, I'm sure of it… But why can't I reach her?)
(I won't find any more answers here. I should check somewhere else.)

(Why are there so many Tacet Discords now…?)
(Where is everyone? Are they hiding in their homes?)
Did you... forget something...
RUN! Run... This place will soon be devoured...
(Tacet Discords that can talk, but don't attack humans?)
We can't escape... No...
What are you talking about?
What are you running from?
Let's... practice... the performance... Yummy...
(Why do these Tacet Discords sound like the people from earlier…?)
(Could they… be one and the same?)
(It can't be possible... They looked indistinguishable from real people. I didn't notice anything off at all…)
(Wait, Phrolova said there's no divide between humans and Tacet Discords, and their frequencies could merge.)
(Merge...)
(I see now...)
(She wants to use the Gem to fuse the bodies of Tacet Discords with human consciousness, bringing them back to life. She's trying to fulfill the desire that's always haunted her.)
(That's… insane.)
(Given their unstable nature, these Reverberations have never truly become human again…)

The people you just encountered have transformed into TDs, still repeating the same words. You finally realize that Phrolova is attempting to use the Gem to fuse the bodies of Tacet Discords with human consciousness, hoping to bring them back to life and fulfill her seemingly impossible obsession. However, her attempts have yet to succeed, and these Reverberations have never truly become human.
Why do you keep alone?
Phrolova?
Of what sorriest thoughts do your companions make, clinging to what should have died with them?
All life in this world... has already died...
No, this isn't irreversible. I won't simply succumb to it.
I searched everywhere… but why can't I find it?
Tell me... have you found it?
Found what?
My violin...
Violin...?
My ambition. My companion. The most precious Gem among all that I have...
I can't lose it… But where could it be? It must be waiting for me.
(The most treasured Gem?)
I won't leave without it.
(Looks like this place isn't entirely under her control…)
(Could that violin be a sign she left behind?)

In your search for the Threnodian's residual energy, you meet a mirage of Phrolova. She seems overwhelmed by conflicting emotions but eventually manages to get a grip on herself. She mentions her violin, something that holds special significance to her. It is her ambition, her companion, and the most precious Gem among all she has. You can't help but wonder if her words hold a hidden clue.
{PlayerName}, I've been informed of what happened at the Fabricatorium of the Deep.
I'm afraid I have another favor to ask of you regarding this matter.
Head to these coordinates if you've got time. A friend of mine there will fill you in on the details.
On behalf of the Montellis... No. On behalf of the people of Ragunna, I thank you.
Ready to begin our investigation?
All set. Let's go.
I need some time to prepare.
Your assistance is much appreciated.
Don't worry. Someone's already thanked me.
Absolutely. We'll depart whenever you're ready.
Strange. The melody of this place has gone back to normal. The Echoes shouldn't be behaving like this.
...It seems you haven't reached the deeper truth. This place is more than just a factory for Echoes.
The new research data I gathered indicates the Order has been secretly pushing experiments on Echo consciousness control in the facility.
In other words, if things had gone according to the Order's plans, the Echoes would become mere puppets and watchdogs entirely under their control.
But... we should've led with faith, not attempting control through force.
If all we have is sand slipping through our fingers, no matter how tightly we grasp, nothing would have mattered. Why, Primus Fenrico, why must you do this...
Ah, apologies, I tend to talk to myself sometimes... Let's move on and document this place.
This is...
The Lost Beyond.
(Did she take this photo before finishing her work?)
What is the Lost Beyond?

I've heard of such an organization... But how are they involved in all of this?
This is where Fenrico collaborated with the Fractsidus.
Collaborate? The Primus understands their kind better than I do. Why would he do such a thing? This Lost Beyond, does it pose a threat to Ragunna...
No, the Lost Beyond has nothing to do with Ragunna.
It's only about someone with an obsession, and a distant, deluded dream.
Sounds rather dangerous.
Quite the opposite. That was likely her final show of weakness.
The Lost Beyond is no longer here. Don't worry, it won't interfere with the Fabricatorium's operations.
Noticing your expression, Luther paused for a moment, then handed you the photo.
Very well, the families placed their trust in you, then I have no reason to doubt. Here, you should take this photo.
If I'm not mistaken, you must know the person related to this photo. It seems more fitting for you to have it.
Sure.
Hmm... Let me see here. We've completed the data collection, which confirms the Echo experiments we mentioned earlier.
As of now, the energy devices are nearly automated, we just need people to monitor them... Alright, done. Let's move on.
These Echoes have less stable consciousness than ordinary Common Echoes. The experiment here is truly a chore.
It's not wise to hold everything too tightly. Sometimes, letting go brings greater rewards. An experiment that does only harm may not be worth continuing...
As it stands, Ragunna still needs a place where the Echoes can call home...
There's one last thing I need to tell you.
This is the control hub of the entire Fabricatorium, overseeing all of its areas. Each region has a similar device that reacts to every change.
I've noticed and recorded an image of it.
Someone once told me that everything is made of frequencies, melodies can bend the rhythm of existence, and by orchestrating their essence, we reshape their very nature.
The key to Fabricatorium's operations is a melody. Keep this melody, make sure it plays well, and the Fabricatorium will remain stable.
If you want to make a change here, you'll have to adjust the melody. No way around it.
Do you remember the melody?
I do.
You hum the melody softly, and its tune echoes throughout the tower.
If not for seeing it with my own eyes, I would've never imagined such grandeur was hidden right beneath the land we've been walking on.
The sea nourishes us. In ways we least expect.
A place this intricate is difficult to fully comprehend in such a short time. You seem to know this place like the back of your hand. Have you done some research prior to your last visit?
Not really. A lot of it came from... the person that was with me at the time. She was one of the founders of this place.
I see. One moment, I'll add a few final notes here.

The Fallen Grave relies heavily on frequency decomposers. Only a small number of Echoes maintained their operation, and no personnel appeared during the course of the investigation. Future management may require fewer staff.
Evaluating and handling anomalies in the Common Echoes requires further revision. They should be offered a choice, rather than helplessly be sent on a conveyor belt for disassembly and smelting.
What a beautiful song. As if I can almost hear a story from it.
I have it recorded. Seeing how focused you are, I took the liberty of capturing your image.
It's fine, as long as it helps you.
Your guidance has been essential to my understanding of this place. Trust me, we will make this place better.
The age of lies is behind us now. Now that the shadow over the Order has lifted, I'm sure the brighter days will come.
Hmm? Why are you looking at me like that?
There's ambition in your eyes.
Heh, isn't that good? Ambition, or you might call it, a desire for the better.
The Order of the Deep needs change. Ragunna deserves a better future, but who will lead that change, I'm not sure.
Luther gave you a calm and meaningful smile before bowing deeply in gratitude.
Alright. I've gathered enough information. Shall we move on to the next area?
Let's go.
Give me a moment.
No problem. I'll be here waiting.
Carlotta's coordinates are outside of the Cathedral of Mercury.
So the Montellis have already talked with the Order about this...
We need to document this place too, right? Let's take some pictures ahead.
Yes, please.
Is everything set? Shall we go to the next area?
Let's move.
Give me a moment.
No problem, I'll be here waiting for you.
Shall we proceed to the next place?
Let's go.
Give me a moment.
No worries. I'll be right here.
Is that... Primus Fenrico?!
Ah, Righteous One. You must be here for the deep, yes?
Luther, at your service. I've been expecting you.
Does the Order know about the Fabricatorium?
No need to worry, the events that occurred haven't been made public yet, and we've decided to keep it so after thorough discussion.
Discussion?
Not long after you brought the news, a private meeting was held between the Order of the Deep and the Montelli and Fisalia families.
So rarely do these parties find common ground, especially under such circumstances.
An agreement was made to keep the incident under wraps for now, to prevent unnecessary confusion and fear among the citizens. Meanwhile, we'll need a thorough investigation.
Common Echoes have become a vital part of Ragunna, and it would be unrealistic to remove them entirely. Thus, the fate of the Fabricatorium would be decided once we all fully understand it.
The Fisalia's expertise in Echo control, combined with the Montelli's Terminal technologies will aid in the smooth transition of the Fabricatorium's operations.
Once everyone is ready, the truth will be revealed to all of Ragunna.
You need me here because...
You are the only person who's been to the Fabricatorium and returned unscathed. We couldn't think of anyone who can lead this investigation than yourself.
I'll be responsible for documenting any findings. It'd be most helpful if you could be my guide and explain along the way so our investigation can be as detailed as possible.
Just the two of us?
Yes. Since Acolytes mostly station the Fabricatorium, the Order and the families have decided that I am best suited for this task.
Alright, let's go.
I need some time to prepare.
Your assistance is much appreciated.
Don't worry. Someone's already thanked me.
Absolutely. We'll depart whenever you're ready.
Are we now inside the Fabricatorium? This area is...
We are in the Fallen Grave.
It's a deeper part of the Fabricatorium.
Coldness and death litter these obscure corners.
Only a few straggler Echoes remain, watching their own kind being fed into the "furnace" one by one.
We've always regarded Common Echoes as gifts from the Sentinel, never caring about their birth or death. But here lies the dissolving and decaying truth behind the miracles.
The frequency will be recycled once broken down.
You're saying frequency energy can be reused? You mean there's a way for these abnormal Echoes to be reborn after meeting their end?
Where does that energy lead? Do the reborn Echoes retain their past consciousness?
Let's keep moving. The depths will answer your questions.
You speak in riddles. I suppose I'll have to take notes more carefully.
(Why am I starting to talk like this too...?)
I noticed something in the files earlier. This is the area where Common Echoes are brought to be incubated, isn't it?
Yes, those devices you see still running are Echo Brooders.
Hundreds, if not thousands, of Echoes are being incubated. That explains why there's heavy security and so many researchers.
The pipes transport frequency energy.
The recycled Echoes from the Fallen Grave feed the creation of new ones...
Pieced together from innumerable broken frequencies, these newborns bear no relation to the past.
How do you know?
I used to be a researcher of frequency studies. One look at the readings is enough to know that every trace of the old data is erased...
You seem concerned.
Years in the lab can numb one's mind. Eventually, you stop seeing the subjects as living individuals.
I keep reminding myself not to go down that path. But here, it feels like everyone sees the Echoes as expendable tools, not living beings.
Is this not a betrayal of our faith?
I've heard it phrased differently before.
What is it?
Someone once told me, it's vibrancy in the ruin, an opus of eternal life.
You mean, this cycle is the immortal, unbroken unity of life?
No, that is a fallacy. Our "unity" must never be built upon the sacrifice of self-awareness.
Sacrifice of self-awareness?
Like these poor Echoes...
The amount of energy stored here is astounding.
Energy Hub serves as the central energy storage.
The data shows two types of energy being stored here.
One of them matches what we found in the Fallen Grave. Recycled Echo frequencies must be stored here before being distributed to the incubation areas.
The other energy source appeared on devices we saw before. It seems to be the power source that supports the Fabricatorium's operations.
But why is it giving a low energy level reading...
Must be because of the explosion.
Explosion?
We had to detonate some of the energy to escape from underground.
So there's an underground section of the facility. And that's where the energy storage area is located?
Yes, but I'm not sure if there's still a way down there.
Let's go take a look.
Looks like the path is sealed. We'll need someone to repair the underground levels first.
Hmm? What are these?
Seems like someone managed to salvage some files from below.
They are not entirely about Echoes. And the data seems to be from another era.
No, wait, given the age of these records, the conclusions about the Waveworn Phenomenon were far ahead of their time.
Mind if we look over this again? I want to make sure we don't miss any critical information.
My dear {Male=brothers;Female=brother and sister}, you who have come here will be the strength that shall save Rinascita.
Oh? Thank you. I didn't expect to see so many...
Let us join together to spread light to all, and face the Divine Ordeal in unity.
Divine Ordeal...? I'm not sure I follow.
They can't communicate with you normally.
Why is that?
To save Rinascita and withstand the inevitable "Divine Ordeal" is a road paved by many.
They're victims of the Order's pursuit of salvation, willing martyrs in their attempt.
This is unheard of...
Might be because Fenrico is keeping the cost of failure in check.
After countless failures, their minds are filled with chaos, unable to live a normal life.
The ones who survived the darkness could only cling to their faith.
This place has nothing to do with production or the experiments. It's just Fenrico's last refuge for them, where they can live peacefully away from the rest of the world.
I understand. Then these people will remain under our care.
But the chaos and darkness you mentioned earlier...
Let's keep moving. You'll soon see the truth for yourself.
Is that... Primus Fenrico?!
He can't hear you.
I beg of you, tell me everything that's happened.
Do you know about the false Divinity?
Yes. Soon after I was chosen for the Fabricatorium's investigation, I received a letter from the Fisalias revealing the truth about the Sentinel and the Threnodian.
Your place in the Order must be quite significant to be shown secrets like this.
Fenrico must have known about this earlier than we ever expected.
But he forgot, or to be more precise, his thoughts were muddled after being eroded by the Dark Tide.
With the Threnodian rooted in his mind, he had to record fragments of the truth with his last remaining sanity and keep them buried in the depths of the sea.
He and other Acolytes once sought ways to save Ragunna, until he realized that only by attempting it himself could there be hope of success.
But he forgot one important thing: he was the Harbinger of the Dark Tide.
The Threnodian's residual energy almost slipped back into the Dark Tide. Fortunately, the lantern awakened him, and he gave everything to stop the spread of the Dark Tide.
The Threnodian... that explains it.
Explain what?
Many years ago, I had a few exchanges with the former Privy Councilor.
He mentioned that back in the Seminary days, Fenrico was a different person before becoming Primus. Even as an old fellow classmate, he felt like a complete stranger.
He never understood why, even when he was sent on the Pilgrim's Sail. I suppose what you've told me is the reason.
Let's go.
Give me a second.
No worries. I'll be right here.
Wait, no... How do I open it...
What's going on?
I'm collecting Sacred Salt for future needs.
There is no room for errors in the work of a Steward. I must take great care of the Acolytes' welfare.
The martyrs sacrificed everything for the cause of saving Ragunna. Even in failure, they are entitled to live out their days in peace...
So the Sacred Salt is for them?
Yes. For they hold onto the belief that anything untouched by the Sentinel's grace on this blessed land could be potentially tainted or cursed by the Threnodian.
That's why I would perform cleansing and consecration rites with Sacred Salt on all provisions before their eyes.
To lead them into thinking they're taking the Divinity's nurturing meal, drinking holy blood that grants enlightenment. So they have no reason to refuse.
But lately, we are running short on Sacred Salt. As an Acolyte of the Ministry of Holy Rituals, I...
(He seems a bit unsettled too... Best not to push him. We should figure out a way to help.)
Did the Order anticipate this situation?
Ah, yes. We've set aside some Sacred Salt in the Fabricatorium for times like this. It's kept in the Triptych Chests and other places...
If you happen upon any, bring it to me. I'll offer you plenty in return. What do you think?
It's a deal.
Thank you for your help and devotion. Please, take a look and see if anything catches your fancy.
May the Sentinel always bless you.
Like this? No, that's not it... How...
Another Orchestration Altar?
Orchestrate using the flower she left behind and see what happens.
Is this how the music used to control the sea depths was made?
I wonder what these unused melodies are for. I’ll keep a record of them either way.
This... this is the real prayer...
Relax, I'm here. You won't forget how the real prayer goes.
Look, I've written everything down. We'll put our trust in this book. Do you need this book?
I don't need it.
I do need it.
Oh-ho, so you trust your memories. Just you wait, the need will arise.
Of course, you need it. Everyone needs it here. Now, how will you prove you'd be a worthy owner?
(Show him your wealth)
(Make a gesture of prayer)
(Do nothing)
I see. You value money above all else. You have strayed far from the path. Take this book and return to the fold.
I see. Your prayer lacks finesse. This book will help you remember how best to pray. Here, take it. You're welcome.
I see. Your resolve is unshakable and your faith is immovable. This book will let you ascend to greater piousness. Please take it.
Over here? Or there? It's going to appear again!
No. There is no corruption or blight here.
The darkness that swallows all light will creep into every corner. We must be careful at all times!
Look! What is that blackness over there? It's coming. It's here!
Is it under my feet?! It will swallow me whole. I can't breathe in there!
This sacred land is under the protection of the Divinity. No defilement shall come to pass.
Cleanse your soul... Let unharmonious words be banished from this place of peace...
Those things must be lying in ambush. Help me look over there.
May the Divinity help you...
We are all connected. Our souls are aligned. We shall become one.
Paradise... I long for the Paradise...
I venerate Thee. Yea, I do believe. Please guide me upon Thy path.
What do I gain... by worshiping here...
Impenetrable... mire... Suffocating... confinement.
False light... cold... I won't go... Don't make me go...
I venerate Thee...
Venerate...
Guide me upon Thy path.
Guide me...
They're almost in my grasp... I can get them out soon!
Just a little more... Help ... is near...
A stranger, eh? Now that's a rare sight!
Folks don't often find their way to Ostina. You bringing good news, I hope?
Good news?
Yeah. Is Phrolova making any headway with her work? Are we getting back to the real world?
Don't reckon I've seen you around. A friend of hers? Or one of them researchers she works with? Sure don't get many like you out here…
I'm neither.
She's still researching.
That so? She must trust you plenty, or she wouldn't have told you about us.

You're the only one besides her who can travel between the two realms. You must be powerful.
I hope you can help her... Ah, sorry, that was selfish of me. Spoke without thinking again.
Well... truth is, we're all counting on her. She must be worn clean out by now. It'd be good if she had someone to share the load, someone who gets it like she does.
So you support her plan?
Of course. If she says it's possible, then it's possible. I believe her.
I don't get all the fancy details, but hey, who doesn't want to live longer?
So what do you think?
Yawn...
Don't be indifferent. Now listen, a normal welcome-back party is boring. We should throw a surprise party. The youths do like surprises.
There's a fine line between surprise and jump scare.
Hehe, she's braver than you. Maybe she's into that kind of thing.
What are you talking about?
Oh, it's you. Phrolova is out performing, and we're discussing how to organize a party for her return.
You act younger than the youths of today. Try not to overexert yourself. Oh, you seem tired, child. Care for a glass of water?
Hey child, do you like my idea? If we throw a surprise party, maybe they'll let me be the main organizer.
It's a good idea.
Why do you care so much?
Hahaha, I most certainly know what the youths want. What have you got to say to that, Leah?
Sigh...
Uh... haha, we saw them grow up. Those young'uns are like family to us.
Besides, I need to be important to them. If they enjoy my company, they won't forget to visit us from time to time.
Unlike our own ungrateful brat... He never....
Okay, that's enough.
Won't you at least consider my suggestion?
I have some spare cash on hand. You can borrow my money and pay me back later.
Thank you for the offer, but I can't accept this. I've also returned everything Phrolova's given me.
It's infuriating. She bought her first violin by herself with savings from her job. Does she think I can't do the same?
I'm sure that's not what she meant.
But I'm not angry, really. I only want you all to trust me. Even though it'll take a while, I want to buy a new instrument on my own.
Still... I'd like to help.
Then you can accompany me to the city and help me pick out an instrument after I've saved enough.
Alright, it's a deal!
Who was the first to skip the class?!
Rote practice is an essential part of studying music. If you do not master the fundamentals, you cannot create great pieces.
I shall inform your parents if you ever skip class again!
Sigh... Kids are getting harder to teach by the year. Just look at you all...
And look at Phrolova, only a few years older, and yet she's doing extra practice. She even plays me music she writes herself.
Yes, we know, Ms. Searle. You've told us a million times already!
Yeah, no matter how hard we try, we don't have her talent...
Well, I don't expect you to be exceptional, I simply want you all to... Hang on. Caleres, where is your textbook?
Lost.
Lost! That textbook belongs to Phrolova. I borrowed it from her for you so you could read her notes in the margins! Go find it!
Urgh! I'm seeing red...
Triiiiiiisss.
Where did Triss run off to... That child's always darting about. If she could just stay where I could see her.
Phrolova and I were meant to go to the city... Maybe I'll send her to look for Triss when we get back. Triss will listen to her.
Why?
Eh, how do I put it... She has some kind of aura that inexplicably makes people respect her.
I see.
Oh? Tell me more.
You know how I found out?
When we were younger, she once stopped a large brawl between kids.
Even though I'm older than her, I couldn't take charge of the situation. Maybe the adults thought it wasn't a big deal, but I saw the aura in her eyes.
Her powerful and pervasive presence compelled many to follow her lead.
When I heard her say she wanted to be a conductor, I wasn't surprised at all. Controlling an orchestra wouldn't be very difficult for her.
Lalala...lala....
Argh! You scared me!
What are you up to?
Practicing songs.
My singing seems to sound better here. So I come here to build confidence in my voice. Hehehe.
Well now, don't interrupt a star singer in the making. I'm in the groove right now!
You really don't want to go?
I want to stick close to home this week. I walked too far with Betty last time, and my feet are still sore.
Oh dear, I forgot you went out not too long ago.

To be fair, it's a nice skirt. Must've taken you ages to find the right one.
Hehe, naturally. We're both excellent shoppers.
I've never seen Betty so picky. As if nothing on display was good enough.
I spent ages trying to get her to make a decision. Otherwise, we'd have had to walk even further to find more shops.
I thought Betty didn't want Phrolova to perform. The poor child was so upset she almost ran off from home.
That's just something Phrolova said out of frustration. She's too stubborn and doesn't want to rely on anything, so she's always ill at ease.
Ahhh, I don't know if that's a good or bad trait...
Be careful, and come back early.
Don't worry, I'll be back before sunset.
Did you buy the event decorations and snacks?
Yes. Everything's here. We're waiting for you to begin preparations.
Is the stage big enough?
It's quite a large orchestra. We might have to make the stage bigger.
When can I go out?
What's it like outside now?
So you think the Primus is...

There is only one possible explanation… He took the final step into the darkness. The crisis draws ever closer.
