I'm sorry, but the fewer people who know, the better.
That said, we do need to initiate the procedures in that dusty old security plan.
So it's serious, huh? That security plan is supposed to be activated only when Ragunna is in the gravest of crises.
Doing so transfers the Primus's authority in his absence to us members of the special decision-making group.
You mean to imply that the Primus is...

You do not tell us the truth, and yet you expect our help?

We still do not know exactly what happened. The people are not ready. Tell them the Primus went out to sea on official business and isn't back yet.
Right, best not to fuel speculation.
Have you discovered any promising team in this qualifier?
No, I'm still observing.
Pity! I told you that team's strategy was way too defensive!
Humph, they should have fired their coach ages ago.
You... How did you get in...

The energy portal outside wasn't your invitation?
You're right. I'll leave.
Obviously not.
You will gain nothing in this bygone realm. Must you cast your gaze here?
Bygone, but cozy.
How much of what you said is true?
Anyone who comes here should experience a simple sense of joy... It seems we share similar feelings about this place.
Is that why you've returned? How unexpected.
(I'd like to immerse myself in melodies of the past)

You wish to listen to past stories? Ah... It seems I have an audience for the songs I've collected throughout history.
Go ahead. Every song kept in this room is at your disposal. There's a seat by the window.
The people here are of no use to you. Don't try anything. I will protect this place.
To the end? With your life?
Heh, an empty and graceless threat. After all, you are not one to harm commoners.
They're not commoners.
I alone am enough to bear all your hostility. Stay away from this sacred land. Whatever you do, I will accompany you to the end.
A foe's weakness is worth preserving.
What exactly are you here for?
(To watch what my foe is doing)
I will return here often to watch them and you. Even if you're not personally here, that should be sufficient.
Holding us under your vigilant eyes... Looks like I'll never be able to fully rest here. How cruel.
See yourself out.
I shall go into the darkness. I will save everyone's faith.
If it has so been ordained that someone must fall into darkness, then let that person be me. The Divinity will see my devotion, and that will be enough to bring me back to the land of light.
I will bring back your souls, and return everyone to their true selves.
I will not descend into madness. Please let me on the ship. I have already sacrificed everything for this.
Perhaps you already tried.
I tried... I'm back now... The impregnable darkness... Argh, my head!
I will not fail... I must... Their voices call to me, clear as day...
Please let me go. I will save everyone. The darkness shall not take our home... never...
Wrong, everything's wrong! It's all wrong!
Nothing is right! Nothing! Not the Divinity's statue, nor the prayer, nor the people!
This isn't right... You, you're not right! You're not a true believer!
And I'm not a true believer... What is it that I believe...?
Heaven and earth aren't right... It shouldn't be dark... It shouldn't be blue...
Wrong! Everything's wrong! Ah ha ha ha—
There are missing notes in the music sheet. Must pinpoint their location first.
No, it was the <color=Highlight>wrong</color> Orchestration order.
Was that it?
A perfect cadence is still missing.
This will do.
Maybe we try that again? Can you do it?
...Yes. I can manage.
I wonder... Perhaps give this a try?
Let me give it a try this time.
Please do. I look forward to your creation.
No, the Orchestration was <color=Highlight>wrong</color>. It should be...
Wait. Let me give it another go.
Very well.
It worked.
It is not over yet. Stay focused.
Did I miss something?
A perfect cadence is still missing.
That was easy.
One's sensitivity towards music will not so easily decline...
What's next?
Connect the scales labeled by numbers in <color=Highlight>ascending</color> order.
Perhaps I should...
Just one more try
As you wish.
I get it now. Is this how you do it?
An interesting approach to Orchestration, I must say.
No, it was the <color=Highlight>wrong</color> Orchestration order.
The melodies sound fairer to the ear now.
Indeed. We should finish Orchestrating the remaining ones.
Was that it?
A perfect cadence is still missing.
Good. The music has been restored.
Maybe we try that again? Can you do it?
...Yes. I can manage.
I wonder... Perhaps give this a try?
So much distortion...
Pretty much the same as the last one. An Orchestration should do the trick.
Yes.
(Patience. I will move when their gaze turns elsewhere.)
(There. My way out.)
(When the melody beckons, their eyes may turn away...  and in the hush, the shadow slips through.)
(Well then... Show me how you conduct your symphony.)
(Heh... The more watchful the eyes, the louder their fear sings to me.)
(Shall we let the music begin?)
Phrolova, in a bit of trouble, hmm？
Don't show yourself with her face, Grand Architect.
Oh? But you used to like it when "I" was like this.
Why are you here?
"I" promised you, didn't I? To let the Elegy from the Beyond sing here, and see "us" reborn again.
The frequency in your eye... It hurts, doesn't it? So many voices, so many cries, all echoing in your head...
"I" know you can bear it, just like you always have. With your half-human, half-Tacet Discord body, can anything even hurt you, or kill you? But your mind? I don't want you to feel all that pain.
And now... the game has changed. After what happened in Septimont, Augusta's made her move.
"Disdaining fortune, with Its power clutched in our grasp before Its fall, we shall wield It, and call forth every forgotten soul." That was your promise to me.
But without Leviathan's power of Unity, I can no longer grant them all a rebirth within the Beyond.
Oh, but you still can. You're saving "us" now!
"I" just want you to finish Cristoforo's plan first.
The seabed is in chaos. Now isn't the best time to bring "us" back.
Merging Reverberations with Tacet Discords, keeping "our" consciousness alive while creating new vessels for "us"... Don't you want more time to make it perfect? A true revival, done the right way?
Even if I agreed to help you first, {PlayerName} would never allow it.  {Male=He;Female=She} would fight to the end to stop us.
The Beyond is merging with you. Once you gain the strength to open that gateway, you can keep {Male=him;Female=her} there. With "us." Forever.
Oh? You're hesitating. Is that moment you two shared really more important than "us"?

You misunderstand. A seat in the Beyond has always awaited {Male=him;Female=her}. Trapping {Male=him;Female=her} now changes nothing. In the end, {Male=he;Female=she} will fulfill {Male=his;Female=her} promise to me there.
Hehehe... Hurry up, Phrolova. The Beyond is holding onto you tighter and tighter. I'm scared you won't have much time left.

While searching for the sheet music, Phrolova encounters the Grand Architect of Fractsidus, who has taken the form of Triss. The Grand Architect suggests that with the unexpected turbulence in the sea depths, plans for the Lost Beyond should be set aside for now. Instead, trapping you to secure the Threnodian's residual energy has become the new priority. Phrolova considers this and then accepts the Grand Architect's command.
The stars never blink... The sun never sets...
When can we leave?
No, I can't do it... I can wait, but when can we...
(Silence. I need silence...)
Phrolova, when this piece is truly complete, I'll come back.
Is that a promise?
Yes. No matter where I am, I'll return.
Every promise matters. Once I make one, I'll see it through, no matter the cost.
Phrolova, don't forget! We're off to the neighboring city tomorrow!
Phrolova, could you tell us the story behind that tune you're conducting?
Phrolova, we made a promise. Friends forever, through thick and thin. Neither of us will ever leave the other behind.
Phrolova, Reverberations from human death are destined to disperse or distort. If they become Tacet Discords, they're no longer human.
What I couldn't do back then… I can make happen now...
Your bones will no longer be marrowless. Your blood will no longer be cold...
Phrolova, keep living… We long to be by your side…
Phrolova, I've faith that the melody you weave with your baton will change the world one day…
Yes, it will...
The world is but a symphony of resonating frequencies. Humans may fall to be Tacet Discords, and Tacet Discords may rise again as humans... There is no divide between us.
I have long erased that line. So can everyone else.

The Lost Beyond's influence on Phrolova intensifies. Visions of people from the past and promises fill her mind... Some voices urge her to yield, but she refuses to give in. Out of stubbornness, she believes the world is but a symphony of resonating frequencies. Humans may fall to be Tacet Discords, and Tacet Discords may rise again as humans—all are but vessels with no true boundaries.
(When did {Male=he;Female=she} come?)
(That chaos clouded my mind. Did I just...)
Am I orchestrating the right way?
...You have a talent for it.
Did you touch something? What caused the explosion?
Fenrico tied the music piece to the security system.
Heh. He'd blow up all the energy here just to stop us. He's really putting everything into this.
May he enjoy the music we prepared for him.
An explosion blocks off the elevator to the upper floors. Phrolova instead decides to use her ability to amplify the blast, creating a greater shock wave to propel the two of you upward.
Here, as we agreed.
You return Phrolova's baton to her.
Can you still orchestrate?
Of course.
After a short deliberation, Phrolova hands you all the music pieces.
I'll leave the rest of the Orchestration to you.
Why?
"Are the changes here truly coming from the shifts in the melody?"
"Are there hidden plans woven into these pieces?"
For all your little doubts...
Taking the conductor's baton yourself is the only way you'll believe in what's unfolding here.
And that's how we move forward.
Alright, I'll wrap up the Orchestration then.

You return Phrolova her baton, and in turn, she hands you all the sheet music pieces and entrusts you with the Orchestration. Taking the conductor's baton yourself is the only way to believe in what's unfolding in this place and decide how you both will move forward.
That was precise...
We should be landing around the Gem's location, right?
Correct.
From what the Order's pursuers said, Fenrico will have his men guarding it.
Even the most unpredictable story will one day welcome its conclusion. And when that moment comes, we must act.
That will also be the time when you can turn your blade against me.
On your way to the Lumen Tower, some interference makes you stray from the correct path. You find yourself in somewhere unknown.
This device looks the same as the ones I saw earlier.
We can adjust the water level and get out from the passage above.
Come on, we need to find the music piece.
What music piece?
It's a long story…
Alright then, I'll keep an eye out. Just make sure you fill me in later!
Intruder alert. Intruder alert. Engaging intercept protocol.
Target location locked. Initiating Eradication sequence.
Target location updated. Entering Advanced Eradication Mode.
Detecting frequent target location updates. Entering Super Advanced Eradication Mode.
Target leaving engagement zone. Activating Ultimate Eradication Mode.
We can't take the elevator. We need another way up.
Then let's make the quake spread further, shall we?
We'll descend from here. The path ahead should be safe.
Safe, really?
...I didn't expect this either.
It's a mess here. How are we supposed to find the movement pieces?
Try to think from the perspective of the one who concealed them.
Echo Brooders, in here?... Stay on guard, just in case they break out and attack.
They won't. They're not fully developed yet.
Oh? What was that you said?
We should each go our own way.
You want to act alone?
Fenrico likely hid the two music sheets separately to stall us.
You're wondering if this was all a setup to trap you.
I can't be sure what's happening in the Lost Beyond.
The timing is too convenient.
Heh… Now I'm even more certain. Fenrico wanted us separated.
If he could craft a snare for us to walk into, why wouldn't he?
Searching together wastes time, but if we're separated, the fragile trust between us could crumble in an instant.
Doubt, dispute, hesitation… such ruinous trappings follow us disquietly to our graves. That's his plan.
But I won't let him win. Will you?
What do you mean by this?
It's tied to my power and the only support I have in my weakened state.
Even if we're apart, you'll still hold my fate in your hand.
You'd trust me with this?
Staying here will get neither of us what we want.
Don't keep me waiting.

An accidentally triggered security system separates you and Phrolova. She proposes splitting up to speed up the search. You worry that this might be a trap set by her and Fenrico. To ease your doubts, Phrolova hands you her baton, which holds her remaining Resonance Energy, her only support in her current state. After some thought, you accept her baton and go your separate ways.
An ambush?
Ha, as expected.
Pointless.
It's a bit tricky without a guide...
Not if I'm here!
Did you sleep well?
Mhm! Feeling great!
But where are we now? So many twists and turns, it's making me dizzy...
Let's figure this out together.
Roger! Roger!
Hah, that wasn't so tough. See? We made it out.
You were about to pass out.
No way! Something like that ain't ever taking me down.
Check out all this stuff! We might find the music piece here.
"Tacet Discords generated by the Dark Tide consist of fragmented frequencies intensely fused together."
"These subjects lack self-awareness. The collective consciousness formed through fusion is entirely shaped and controlled by Leviathan."
"The Dark Tide cannot sustain or preserve original human consciousness. Research terminated. Recorder: Phrolova."
"The frequencies in <te href=851024>Retroact Rain</te> are essentially purer and more stable Remnant Energy. This shows potential."
"The human consciousness retained within the rain is too weak, resulting in only brief, repetitive fragments."
"Retroact Rain is unpredictable and cannot independently form Tacet Discords or Echoes capable of maintaining human consciousness on a large scale. Research terminated. Recorder: Phrolova."
"Artificial Sonoro Spheres have a short duration and are unstable. Additionally, the influence of Fortes can cause unintended changes to them."
"Creating a large, stable Sonoro capable of sustaining a reality for all, would entail significant costs. Additionally, the process would demand the sustained application of my Resonance ability."
"This research direction has gained solid support and will continue. Recorder: Phrolova."
These records all link to the Waveworn Phenomenon.
Why did Phrolova even study this?
There's a pattern here... She was searching for a way to preserve human consciousness.
And if Fenrico's recording is real, who exactly was she trying to save when she created the Lost Beyond?

You come across old research files on the Waveworn Phenomenon, which appear to be Phrolova's work. Your investigation reveals that she was searching for ways to preserve human consciousness, though you can't tell whose.
Why are there so many Tacet Discords?
She can't defend herself. We need to clear the way for her.
Wait, why would you even… Ugh, whatever. Maybe trying poking these control devices?
Whoa, this can distract them!
Look, this can take care of them!
She's probably safe for now. Let's go.
Huh? Is that Phrolova?
She's talking to someone… but I can't tell who.
Anyway, let's keep going.
Are these guys guarding something?
Looks like the music piece is nearby.
Here it is. We should bring it back.
Back? What do you mean?
We need to rendezvous with Phrolova.
I don't know what's going on between you two, but maybe you should do this yourself.
Why?
Her frequency smells… off.
Off?
It's safer for you to stay in my Tacet Mark and keep watch. This place is unstable, and the Threnodian is still at work.
Copy that. Be careful out there.

You find a piece of sheet music and prepare to meet up with Phrolova, but Abby warns you about her strange frequency. Given the unpredictable dangers of the underwater environment, you tell Abby to return to your Tacet Mark but to stay alert.
Phrolova's perspective.
(I didn't expect you to act...)
(More guards... and watchful eyes...)
(I must find another way.)
Phrolova, this is your debut in this city. Are you sure about this? Taking the stage in a dress of mourning… and playing an elegy?
I am certain.
I want my melody to sink into the very bones of this earth, so that they hear my return, loud and clear.
…Alright. I respect your decision. Time's almost up. I'll inform the orchestra.
The Blessed Maiden, unable to fully govern herself, still becomes a thread in your grand tapestry.
Manipulating reality behind her back, reviving the Threnodian's lingering power within her through the progression of a tale... That's now nearly impossible.
Ah, but at the very least, we have affirmed her resilience and stability after the merging. That alone offers invaluable insight into our research sample.
If we allow the story to unfold, we may have the chance to further destabilize Cartethyia and mold her into the Threnodian.
Do you not hear {PlayerName} on our heels? And you're willing to gamble everything on a mere "chance" to deliver what the Grand Architect desires?
Heh, so eager to witness the Beyond's completion at the seabed.
Why not nudge Septimont's plot just a little? Use your original plan to mask our true purpose.
The Resonator's Second Awakening, the attempts to merge with the Divinities... These are but advancements for individuals. Why not place our wager on ordinary souls instead? The moment is ripe.
Worry not. Whatever the Grand Architect promised for your plan, I've already accepted. Your actions aren't at odds with our ultimate goal.
We need only ensure that the Threnodian's lingering power remains firmly within our grasp.
Cristoforo hands the script he holds to "you."

In a flashback through Phrolova's perspective, you experience her conversation with Cristoforo back in Septimont and realize why she handed you the script: Cartethyia's intervention had made their plans to overwrite reality almost impossible. To maintain control of the Threnodian's power, they made a last-minute adjustment, shifting their focus to this underwater location ahead of schedule. Giving you the script was a way to leverage your power to progress the story until the power could be separated from Mya and returned to their grasp.
The two Divinities have been entwined for centuries. To sever Them is no simple task.
Without Them, the Lost Beyond will fail to take its destined form.
Their power is bound to faith. Only by deepening the people's beliefs can we ensure a successful separation of the Divinities.
Yet, I have devoted much time assisting with your endeavor. Tell me, what will you offer in return?
Primus Fenrico, there's no need for pretense before me. You have already gained much from this grand design, have you not?
Speak freely. What is it that you desire?
Fenrico hands "you" a guest list for the Carnevale.
Travelers from far and wide, a grand celebration upon us... Such a convergence invites chaos, and I fear for Ragunna's stability.
Heh, I see your concern. Very well, allow me to lend a hand.
Oh? Are these outsiders also intolerable to you?
No. I simply noticed a new variable on the list.
Perhaps, this is no misfortune at all. If my understanding is correct, no one would be more determined to sever those two "Divinities" than {Male=him;Female=her}.
{Male=He;Female=She} may be the final cadenza heralding a new chapter for this world.

The second flashback of Phrolova. This time, you find yourself talking with Fenrico in Ragunna, revealing the true reason for the Fractsidus's involvement in the Carnevale: Deepening people's beliefs helps Leviathan gather and amplify Its power, paving the way for a successful separation of the Divinity, a shared goal between the Order and the Fractsidus. The Order has invested far too much to see it fail, and having the Fractsidus ruin the Carnevale would only solidify the Order's rule. When Phrolova saw your arrival, she realized they could use you to help complete the Divinity's separation.
The Threnodian's awakening has slowed. Could the Midnight Rangers have caused this?
Soft cries will never command its attention.
The ceaseless tolling of funeral bells, the restless wails of lost souls... How could it continue its slumber?
It's only a matter of time before its eyes open.
Oh? So, {Male=he's;Female=she's} made {Male=his;Female=her} move.
No wonder...
{Male=He's;Female=She's} in the Gorges of Spirits. Care to witness it firsthand?
No need. For now, {Male=he;Female=she} has nothing to offer me.
I will remain here and listen to what the "people" have to say.
Hmm... Staying behind to merge Reverberations with the Tacet Discords' bodies? Don't you need Leviathan's power for that?
Just a few simple orchestrations. I alone will suffice.
What Leviathan shall carry is all that stands behind me.
Hah. Well then, I'll go see what this big shot is really made of.
Don't underestimate {Male=him;Female=her}. Excessive improvisation will disrupt the original composition. You do remember your task, don't you? What we seek lies in the depths of Jinzhou.

In Phrolova's third flashback, you see her and Scar in Jinzhou, standing before a hatching Ovathrax. Her presence in Norfall Barrens was mostly for personal reasons. Despite the Grand Architect's orders, she cared little about Jinzhou or you. She was more there for the countless Reverberations of the dead scattered across the battlefields. Experimenting with merging Reverberations and Tacet Discords there could offer valuable insights for the ultimate success of the Lost Beyond.
Hey! Phrolova's back!
How were your performances? All smooth, I hope?
Look over there! What's that?
Triss... Melissa... Granny Leah...
The music you conducted was sensational! It was so graceful and ethereal! Every note was pure magic, striking deep into the soul!
I was so lucky to attend this concert. Ms. Phrolova, I'm already one of your biggest admirers!
Thank you.
Ms. Phrolova, mind sharing the story behind that piece you conducted?
I hear there's been talk about some ancient, forbidden compositions discovered recently, supposedly written by a musician who shared your name.
Wouldn't you know, there are all sorts of strange rumors about those pieces.
Word is, they were so depressing they'd drag anyone already on edge right down to despair. They were condemned as luring people to their ruin... That's why they disappeared from history, they say.
So, any chance this composer might be related to you?
An interesting story, sir. Unfortunately, interesting stories aren't of concern to someone like me.
You didn't clap.
Perhaps a silent mourning is more suitable for such a depressing piece.
You're the first to say you've found sorrow in it.
So, what were you mourning for?
For... the fragility of life? The tribulation of survival?
That's too general. The sorrow it conveyed is more than that.
What makes you think that?
It felt uniquely authentic. Like it came from something real.
Do you know how this concert hall came to be?
It was built upon the remains of an ancient town.
An ancient town?
Yes, an insignificant one. A tiny grain of sand in the long course of history.

No divine blessings. No kindly fate. Only desperate hands clinging to life. Despite their struggle, this town was swallowed by a disaster, erased along with the entire civilization in the blink of an eye.
Those good people's lives expired before the flowers in their caps, dying before they sickened.
And the land beneath our feet turned to ashes, bereft of its former laughter and joy.
Sighs? Groans? Shrieks that rend the air? No, nothing. That was the way the world ended. Not with a bang but a whisper.
However...
For some reason, one person survived.
She drifted through the ruins, searching for signs of life, only to find none. On and on she walked, yet no matter how far she strayed, she could never escape that pit of death.
Tell me, do you think this lone survivor suffered more than the dead?
Maybe...
Beneath this concert hall lies the story that gave birth to this melody. I wove her burden into the composition to release it for her.
I still remember the words she could never let go of, "Why is our world like this?"
This pain might be the seed of a new hope.
What do you mean?
If this world can't be changed, then maybe it's time to take a different path... even if it's nothing like before.
Just like how I chose to change myself.
You changed yourself? What kind of change was that?
I started over.
Hmm, that sounds intriguing.
I wonder if each of us can change in that way...
I've gained more than I imagined from this performance.
I'm lucky I heard such a good piece of music.
But it's still not good enough. I want to include the voices of the past, making that history a true part of it.
When this piece is truly complete, I'll come back.
Is that a promise?
Yes. No matter where I am, I'll return.
Every promise matters. Once I make one, I'll see it through, no matter the cost.
Alright, I'll be waiting for you then. I'll save you a VIP seat next time. Besides, I also want to hear more stories about how you "started over."
"This tour led me to a friend. {Male=He;Female=She} understood the true emotions woven into my music..."
(So the friend she mentioned...)
(Was it me?)
(And the one she's been waiting for... is also me?)
(No, that doesn't seem right. Did we really meet at this concert?)
(It could've been an illusion she created on purpose, not something that really happened...)
(With the Gem at stake, this could be her attempt to throw me off...)
I hope this special day brought you happiness.

The fourth flashback takes you back to your first true meeting with Phrolova in the concert hall. You sense the sorrow from the music, listen to her story, and can't help but offer her suggestions, inspiring her. After the conversation, you wonder if the path Phrolova chose was influenced by your words. Had you inadvertently led her astray? You begin to suspect you are the "friend" she mentioned, yet at the same time, you wonder if any of this truly happened.
Thank you. I'm happy. This reunion is an unexpected surprise.
Today was just grand! We sailed together, watched a play, and even had our own little concert by the road!
Yes… It was just like the old days.
Phrolova, did you notice...
How many people... were cheering... for us...
I'm sorry, but I cannot let her remain for too long.
I once bowed before the divine, a servant in its name, offering my faith in return for those I loved. Yet the divine remained silent, watching as fools took my abilities as a free elixir.
I once sought science, surrendering my own flesh and blood to prove resurrection was more than a dream. But I was deceived, used as a mere material in their pursuit of immortality.
I once turned to the people, asking if the Waveworn Phenomenon had ever cradled life. But I was cursed, branded a harbinger of doom by the terrified.
So I begged no more. I sought in silence. Again and again, failure upon failure, loss upon loss.
Until today. Until you let me see Triss.
A fleeting moment, yes. But this is only the beginning.
You seek to "start over," don't you? Then make full use of your power. Survive. Be bloody, bold, and resolute. Laugh to scorn the power of humans.

Make her last longer than she did yesterday. Tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow. Time will creep forward, to the last syllable of recorded time. Until the day she's more real, more joyful than ever before.
Until the day Leah drives with you to another concert. Until the day old Aeschylus rehearses by your side once more.
Until the day...
You voice the apology you denied your mother all these years.
Even a fragile civilization deserves the right to grow. And you, Phrolova, will be the beacon of that hope.
The road ahead will be long. Grueling. Such is the nature of any righteous cause.
Fear not. We will walk it with you. The resources, the knowledge, the technology, all will be yours.
You have met the others. Though our pasts differ, our goal remains one and the same.
Then from this moment on, I walk with you.
I will spend endless years. I will pay the heaviest price. I will silence all distractions. I will wield everything at my disposal to bring back the light.
Welcome to the Fractsidus.
You're too sharp.
A shift in melody means a change. That's what you taught me.
You're truly one to leave mixed emotions.
You're fully recovered, aren't you?
From operating the Orchestration mechanism, to wielding Tacet Discords at will, to opening the gateway to the Beyond by yourself...
It seems that your recovery is in sync with the merging between you and the Beyond.
And yet, there's no reason for you to raise your blade against me. Not now. The Gem is no longer in the Beyond. If we are to retrieve it from Fenrico, we must work together.
After you just tried to trap me?
The modulated melody failed to play its part. And so once again, the choice is yours.
That piece... Did I really hear it before?
Whether it's real or not, it changes nothing.

In the last vision, you witness Phrolova's conversation with the Grand Architect of Fractsidus, who appeared as her audience. By briefly shifting to Triss, he showed Phrolova a glimpse of rebirth, thus persuading her to join the Fractsidus. Having endured countless failures, Phrolova accepted. As you watch this past version of Phrolova move toward the darkness, you try to stop her from going down the wrong path. Suddenly, the present Phrolova reveals herself. You notice something is off and stop her plan to trap you. You question whether what you just saw was real, but she refuses to answer, only replying that there is nothing you can do to change the present, whether it was real or not.
Where should we go next?
To the top.
Ambush.
What is it this time?
(More enemies here. We must be close.)
That is...
Hurry.
I am the first, yet shall be the servant of all.
Is that... the Dark Tide?
It didn't work...
I remain here to guide the lost and bring true peace to Ragunna.
Fenrico can summon the Dark Tide creations?
"From among the faithful, a powerful Harbinger shall arise, bringing both life and annihilation from the Dark Tide into this world..."
He's the Harbinger!
The Gem's power grows.
Salvation, Ascension, and Unity. This will be the one true path.
Dry bones, hearken unto my words. I shall cause spirits to enter thee, and thou shalt live again.
Hark, O breath of the winds! Bow thee down and yield, ye lost souls!
Thou shalt walk in my statutes and keep mine ordinances.
The faithful shall not falter. By faith shall their souls be preserved.
Fenrico, stop! The Threnodian is using you! You are the Harbinger of the Dark Tide!
Absurd! I stand against it. How could I ever be its puppet?
O Sentinel! Return the souls in darkness to this world! Let all wills be made one!
The Gem… is fleeing into the Dark Tide?
Your plan won't work.
Says the one who hasn't witnessed the years, the failures, the countless attempts I've made. What gives you the audacity to pass such judgment?
You've already tried everything! Can't you see? The path you're on only leads here, nowhere beyond.
Among thousands of paths, surely one will lead me back to them.
And even if I'm wrong... I fear not starting over. I've done it time and time again.
What meaning is there in chasing something that's neither realistic nor attainable?
I know they're there.
I saw them in the Beyond.
Those fading Reverberations did not, and cannot, return to life. No matter how long you hold onto their frequencies, the result will be the same.
The villagers are dead. What you've created are Tacet Discords. If you continue turning the entire town into that... you're not creating a paradise. You're creating a hell.
"The villagers are dead..."
So, you saw them in their human form.
Then how can you claim my goal is unattainable?!
Your goal is the one the Fractsidus gave you.
It's what they forced on you. And the Triss you saw? Fleeting, unstable, an illusion. And yet, you still believe everything they say can become real?
The Fractsidus showed me a way forward.
Even if they have their own motives, even if we're only using each other... I care not.
If they can help me take this step, then another step may follow. And another. No matter how steep the price, I'll pay it, step by step, until I reach the end I seek.
Love? Sincerity? Compassion? Trust?
What you and your cronies hold dear is but a jest to the Fractsidus. No bond lasts forever. Without true loyalties, there can be no betrayal, no deceit.
I no longer buy into such illusions.
After all, even if you believe with all your heart, even if you wait patiently at a crossroads...
The one you're waiting for may have long since forgotten you. Forgotten the promise they swore to keep.
I waited. For a long time.
I won't wait anymore.
What was once an unforgettable encounter between us can now be the thread that weaves a paradise for "them."
You've gone too far.
Heh, you're one to talk. How amusing.
You, with your long life and its endless possibilities, still choosing to start over, even at the cost of all your memories?
The irreplaceable bonds, the emotions that make us human, are the brightest lights and most precious treasures in our fragile existence.
What madness, what cruelty, what impossible goal would drive you to cast them all aside?
You've gone further than I ever could.
Perhaps you believe more than I do that only in endless time can true, eternal perfection arise. That only then will a brave new world arrive.
We walk different paths, yet in the end, we are both driven by the same madness. Why argue who's fallen further?
The only difference is that... you've forgotten it all.
You never understood the true value of human life.
Nor have you stepped beyond the boundary that death has placed upon the human soul.
Our cooperation ends here.
Hehe...
So, this is our finale.
My predecessors... What you taught... I...
"The path born of injustice must be fortified with further transgressions…"
Hah, no, even with the body perished, hope and salvation shall endure.
Righteous One, please, save Rinascita's souls from the Paradise...

Fenrico is awakened by the visions of his predecessors appearing in the lantern's light. After regaining consciousness, Fenrico exhausts his powers to seal the gateway to the Journeying Paradise, blocking the Dark Tide. With the Threnodian's residual energy separated, you and Phrolova both race for the Gem. You tell her that the dead cannot be brought back and she should abandon her fantasies. Phrolova scoffs at your words, calling you the stubborn one and scorning your inability to step beyond the boundary that death has placed upon the human soul yourself. Unable to convince each other, the rivalry between you and Phrolova continues.
I'm sorry.
I've come home.
(Fenrico spoke of a... Paradise. What does it mean?)
(And "save Rinascita's souls"... Was he pointing to the source of the anomaly in Rinascita?)
I heard curses... not loud, but deep... I deserve them.
Soon, It will gather enough strength to herd the people and drown Rinascita beneath the Dark Tide.
Fenrico?
The Gem isn't the true heart of the problem. The false Journeying Paradise has created an illusion of everlasting peace, hiding the real source of the catastrophe.
What will you do?
I will remain here to stem the Dark Tide's spread.
Now, I can sense it clearly. The fluctuations from the Paradise are not in Ragunna, but in Septimont...
I cannot reach that far. I must rely on you to go, find, and solve the crisis there. Only then can those who abandoned their faith save their homeland.
Phew, that was exhausting...
I can't believe it! That gate sent me to some lab so, so far away!
Finally made it back... So? What happened after that? Did we win?
The Fractsidus got away with the Gem.
What? What should we do now? Let's track them down!
Not now. There's something more important.
Huh? What's the bigger deal?
We were after the Gem to find the source of the anomaly in Rinascita.
Now we have a better lead—the Journeying Paradise.
That might also explain why the Fractsidus took the Gem and what they're really after.
We'll head to Septimont to uncover the truth.
Maybe it's time we spoke with the Ephor.
Oh... Alright. Are we heading back now?
We still have to tie up loose ends here.

In his last moments of consciousness, Fenrico reminds you that the Threnodian's residual energy isn't the real problem. Rinascita's woes lie in the "Journeying Paradise." He hopes you can prevent this impending calamity and save Rinascita. With this new information, you cease your search for the Threnodian's residual energy and instead plan to return to Septimont for further investigation. As you take one last look at the Fabricatorium of the Deep, wondering what to do with it, a Lycoris suddenly catches your eye.
Even with the body perished, hope and salvation shall endure.
"Once I dreamt that we were dear to each other."
"I woke to find that we were strangers."
Salvation, Ascension, and Unity. This will be the one true path.
Dry bones, hearken unto my words. I shall cause spirits to enter thee, and thou shalt live again.
Hark, O breath of the winds! Bow thee down and yield, ye lost souls!
Thou shalt walk in my statutes and keep mine ordinances.
The faithful shall not falter. By faith shall their souls be preserved.
Such leniency... is not your style.
Why did you save me?
Where is this place?
I need you alive to explain this.
You're welcome.
Answer the question.
The depth beyond reach, where secret treasures often hide.
Remember the story you experienced in Septimont? The one of the girl lost to the sea?
A soul in defiance of itself, its essence seeping into a brilliant Gem. It drifted here with lingering whispers of resentment.
Enchanted, the faithful of the deep followed its call, seeking to claim the divine power as their own.
This is a twisted movement in the symphony, and to play it again, your strength is necessary.
(The Threnodian's residual energy in the sea came from Mya... and it crystallized inside a Gem?)
You already know what I'm here for, don't you?
Nothing but this deserves your stay in such barren waters.
This is just the beginning. Wandering this unfamiliar sea alone will lead you nowhere, and you'll have no defense against the Order's zealotry.
Are you proposing a cooperation?
Thought I heard something over there!
Search every corner!
I'll take care of the Order's guards first, then we'll discuss the Gem's whereabouts.
Of course. Even if everyone here stood against you, none would truly rival your power.
Alas, time slips through our fingers. Were I granted the luxury, I would wait for my injuries to heal and reclaim everything myself, rather than risk it all to save you.
You might find the right path on your own, but listen closely... Hear those distracting footsteps? They will never cease pulling you astray.
By the time you finally silence the noise and find your way, what you seek may already be lost.
The choice is yours.
Think you can turn the tide with words alone? Nice try.
Nothing there!
What about over there?
(Agree to cooperate.)
(Try to search for another way yourself.)
Glad you made the wise choice.
Remember, it's just for now.
Be my guest.

You find yourself in a strange place beneath the sea, realizing it was Phrolova who had saved you. Though critically wounded and hunted by the Order, she risked her life to rescue you. She then reveals that Fenrico has the Threnodian's residual energy and offers a deal: since both of you seek to reclaim it from the Order, why not work together? Time is running out. With Phrolova injured and your surroundings unknown, cooperation seems to be the best option for both of you. The pursuers are closing in, and Phrolova is waiting for your answer...
(No, forcing my way through won't work.)
(I should try my luck elsewhere.)
(Is this the right way...?)
(Push it.)
The door doesn't budge.
(Push harder.)
(Look for another way.)
The door doesn't budge.
Even if you opened it, you'd find nothing but a dead end.
(Look for another way.)
(Fabricatorium of the Deep... It belongs to the Order.)
(Is Phrolova an intruder or the Order's accomplice? Is she after the Gem as well?)
No other way out. Only one choice left...
Lost your way?
There is still one path you've left unturned.
I agree.
Say again, please?
I agree to work with you, for now.
Shall we?
Everything is made of frequencies. Once the melody is distorted, its rhythm is skewed. No blunt force can ever rectify it.
Unless one orchestrates its essence anew.
After you.
You encounter a distorted door. Phrolova uses her Orchestration ability to briefly change its state as she explains how her ability works.
The same door again...
Time your moves carefully.
That way, you can shift its state at will.
They're here!
Noisy...
Take them down!
You, open that gateway...
Out of the question.
What's this about?
Even if you don't... the Primus will be there... You'll never get the Gem...
Fenrico wants the Gem for himself?
This is... the only way!
We should leave.
Leave them be. They won't wake.
How do you know?
Mismatched rhythms, twisted frequencies. Both are signs of the Gem's touch.
How vexing. After all this time chasing me, they still haven't learned to let go.
Is that where you got your injuries?
I'm just surprised the Order dared to target you. I thought they'd behave before the great Laureate.
Spare me the commentary. Fenrico wants the Gem, and I intend to stop him. That's all that matters. Now, lead the way.
I will clear the mist and reveal the path before you.
The blades of ignorance and chaos are yours to shatter.
Orchestrating here should get us through, right?
Yes.
(This is much faster.)
(But how long can she keep this up?)
(Why are Fractsidus members here?)
Finish them.
Are you sure?
I am.
You're stone cold.
Why did they attack you?
Those ensnared by the discordant melody only strike out blindly.
No use to me, no reason to spare.
Is this how our cooperation will end?
Why? Are you afraid?
There is nothing to fear. The worst that awaits is simply death.
When we joined the Fractsidus, we accepted that this day might come.
Me, them, every one. We're all the same.
Not sure if that's absolute loyalty or sheer indifference to life.
Indifference, you say?
The closer you come to death, the sharper the weight of life cuts to expose what you truly desire.

Phrolova doesn't even bat an eye at the death of her fellow Fractsidus members. You start to question how working with her will end. Phrolova, however, explains that every Fractsidus member has been braced for death since the day they joined. While some might see this as disregard for life, she sees it as truly understanding life's value—by facing death, they discover what they truly desire.
It will be faster this way.
Didn't expect to take this route.
Transport channels aren't just for goods.
The Order has tried every possible way to block us.
I'm sure you've learned how to handle it by now.
What's wrong?
...Nothing.
...What a cacophony.
They shouldn't be here, right?
Yes, but given how twisted the melody is, anything could happen here.
Is this the Gem's doing?
It's Fenrico's.
We must return to the tower before Fenrico finds it.
What exactly are your people planning here?
My... people?
You know this place too well, and the Fractsidus have a heavy presence here.
Don't tell me you have nothing to do with all this.
Why do you care?
Now I'm intrigued. Tell me, if death were closing in, what would be your final thought?
A person? A memory? Words left unsaid? Or perhaps, regrets too late to mend?
That's not your concern.
You still haven't answered my question.
Ah, that look. You thought of something just now. A desire unfulfilled, yet still haunting you.
But what if I told you that even the most irreversible fates could "start over"?
Start over?
Ah, how careless of me... I forget I'm speaking to someone who chose to wipe their own past...
Here, we shall witness the advent of the Lost Beyond.
A land of serenity, harmony, and perfection... A sphere beyond the reach of time... A new world never to be marred by tragedy.
You mean a Sonoro Sphere?
How crude. That name strips it of its poetry and warmth.
I composed it, note by note. And within the tower, it opened its arms to the world for the first time.
It is my chance to mend what was broken, to fulfill every wish I could never make true.
Yet for the Lost Beyond to truly endure, for its melody to bring joy, it still needs a divine "texture."
The Gem.
Yes. Only with the texture can each movement resonate in perfect harmony. Only then will this new symphony truly come to life.
But Fenrico smothered its first breath before it could even cry out. I won't let him twist its melody to serve his own ends.
Where's the Gem now?
Deep within the Lost Beyond.
With the last of my strength, I cast it into the depths and sealed the gateway leading to the tower.
If I cannot claim it, no one shall.
If it's hidden in the Lost Beyond, why are you worried?
Sealing an entire realm drained my power. When my strength failed, the Order's betrayal was no longer a mere sting, but a blade, heavy and sharp.
But with every strike, I saw things more clearly... Yes, I could not resist the pull of the next blade.
But I cannot fall. The immortal Divinity within grows and writhes. It will not remain caged forever behind that gateway.
The Lost Beyond will return.
So you're saying the Order might get to the Gem before us?
Without the full picture, I can't trust you so easily.
Heh, trust...
How absurd, to speak of trust between us.
There is only one Gem.
No matter how this unfolds, we'll see which of us walks away with what they desire.
Where should we go next?
This path is a shortcut, but difficult to pass through.
That one takes longer, but may be smoother.
In truth, either will take us...
The shortcut, then. I'll handle whatever comes.
Don't act like my choice doesn't matter to you.
Heh... if you insist.

Phrolova points you toward the Lost Beyond, where the Threnodian's residual energy lies. She reveals all she has done here and tells you about Fenrico's betrayal and his plot against her. Their broken alliance with the Order forced her to temporarily seal the Threnodian's energy within the Beyond. It significantly diminished her power, leaving her vulnerable and thus injured.
A harmonious tune shall unveil the path forward.
But along the seabed, the melodies have been distorted, tangled beyond recognition.
Restoring them will take time.
Steel yourself for the twisted hymn.
How do you know what lies ahead?
The area before us is vital to the Order. Fenrico wouldn't leave it lightly guarded.
Ready your blade.
More guards, just like you said.
They're all yours.
The frequencies of these Order Echoes feel unnatural.
The Order created them. They know how to warp them just as easily.
What is this place?
It is where the Order of the Deep crafts Common Echoes.
Are we supposed to pass through here?
Yes. The Orchestration Altar is there.
However...
What's the problem?
Keep your eyes sharp. The mist is another trap they've set for us.
So let's avoid it. Which way is faster?
The left one.
Still in doubt?
The right one seems closer and safer.
Suit yourself.
(Take the left way.)
(Take the right way.)
You reach the key area where Common Echoes are created. Phrolova warns you to avoid the dangerous mists, but the two of you disagree on which path to take.
Made up your mind?
(Go left with her.)
(Stick with going right.)
Let's proceed.
That was close...
(This way's blocked, and the rail's out of order. Looks like I'll have to go left after all.)
See, doubt made the hand on the dial move two more ticks.
This is...
Remember, the essence of all things can be altered.
What are those?
<te href=851022>Echo Brooders</te>.
What's their purpose?
To create Rinascita's Common Echoes from the twisted fragments of Tacet Discords and Echoes.
Born in chaos, yet shaped to be amiable and useful. How interesting.
A touch of vibrancy woven into ruin, an opus of life that lasts for an eternity…
The art of reshaping frequencies is far more fluid than one might think.
And... brimming with vitality.
You find the Echo Brooders where Common Echoes are being incubated. Phrolova explains how it all functions.
How did you know they would emerge?
I heard the restless discordance.
Sharp ears… I didn't catch a thing.
There are whispers that reach me beyond these…
(It hurts... Phrolova... I don't want to be here...)
(Take us away... Only you... Only you can...)
(Don't leave us... Don't leave us here...)
You question how Phrolova knew of the Echo attack in advance, to which she explains she heard a restless discordance and much more. Fragmented whispers echo in her ears.
We should be able to take the rail here, right?
Hm? Ah, wait a moment, I'll activate it first.
(She clearly drifted off just now. What was that about?)
(Is this… really the right path?)
(I need to stay sharp and quickly get a handle on this place to be sure of my way forward.)
If I time it right, the way forward might reveal itself.
Here it comes again…
The same trick should do.
Well then… seems we'll have to do this together.
Very well.
Phrolova, you're back.
You don't look well, child. Did something happen?
Nothing to worry about. {Male=He;Female=She} will take care of it.
I heard your murmurs just now… You didn't seem this frightened the last time we met, Leah.
Frightened? Heh, nothing gets under my skin at this age.
What about... death?
Ah, now there's a true demon. Always unwelcome, always reminding you of the shortness of our days and the regrets we can't mend.
How I'd love for this merry life to last forever, for things to never change, and for no one to take their leave.
That's not right! If I've fulfilled my one true purpose, then death could never scare me!
Oh, not this nonsense again, Triss! Come on, dinner's ready!
Phrolova, it's time to go home for dinner! Your parents must be waiting for you!
My parents... waiting for me...
Haha, Triss's words remind me of myself fifty years ago. Wouldn't you say, Leah?
Aye, she spends far too much time with you…
What do you think now?
Now? I just want to watch a few more sunrises with my Leah.
My, my. I thought the meticulous Rover was supposed to be flawless in battle.
And I thought you would never doze off before an enemy.
…A crack has appeared on that gateway.

Just as Phrolova tries to use her ability, a sudden hallucination shatters her focus. Visions of close people from the past fill her mind. She realizes that the Threnodian's residual energy she sealed away is now causing disturbances in the Lost Beyond.
This one also needs...
I'll activate it.
How did you know the gateway had cracked?
I felt the disharmony within the Lost Beyond.
That was fast...
How pathetic that most will overlook the smallest of fractures... but for now, time remains on our side.
Almost there.
Just like before, you'll handle the Orchestration.
Mmm.
I see you're prepared.
No—!
Wake up, my love! It's me! Can't you recognize me?
Phrolova, it's happening again...
It's time for the rehearsal… I don't want to go… No… Don't go…
I'm here.
I've found the way. Soon, I'll bring you all back.
Don't leave me... Take me with you...
My child, no one can escape death. Let go of what we've told you. In the end, we're all bound to face it.
…And perhaps the only thing left for us is to accept it.
Aeschylus, over all these years, each of you has spoken to me in contradictions.
Words of surrender, of perseverance, of fear, of pleading…
Fate is fickle, ever ready to devour. Death comes swiftly, without warning...
...And in its shadow, I have seen you at peace, in fear, in sorrow… and in madness.
But worry not, for I am here.
I will always be here.
Phrolova, my poor child...
(How many times has it been? How many times has he tried to let go, only to tighten his grip again?)
(Life is as fragile as trembling leaves caught in winter's breath, their quiet cries swallowed by the wind.)
(The more fleeting, the harder to judge if our choices were ever right. To find meaning in them, one must first walk a path that stretches into "forever.")
(With a soul reaching toward the world's end, like mine... and like {Male=his;Female=hers}…)
(Even when lost at a crossroads, there's no need to despair. No matter how far you've gone, you can always turn back and find your way home.)

Phrolova suffers from another hallucination while using her ability despite her injury. This time, she is shown the chaotic, desperate minds of people from the past facing death. She comforts them, and after a brief moment of pain, she quickly recovers to continue the search for hope.
(Everything is but a frequency. The living and the dead, Tacet Discord and Echo… In Solaris, they are one and the same.)
("My" existence stands as proof.)
Careful now, my child. Watch your step.
Time to switch the rail.
Got it.
(She seemed to have just noticed it… strange.)
The escaped samples have been corrupted by the twisted melodies.
They're too hostile… No choice but to take them out.
The melody has returned to its proper rhythm. This place is beginning to restore itself.
Soon, it will recover too.
I knew we'd make beautiful music together! Another perfect rehearsal!
Hold on, you played ahead of the beat. I heard it!
Ahem... Well, Phrolova, your playing and Triss's improvisation were completely in sync! No wonder you're our best violinist!
It's only because... I've played this piece countless times before.
Oi! Don't be changin' the subject now!
I've heard tell you've been asked to perform far from here? I'm sure you'll amaze them all, just like you always do.
That performance...
Are you alright, Phrolova? You look a bit pale...
Plans have changed, but it's nothing to worry about.
I see... When you can, come back and rest, will you? You've been workin' so hard!
I remember you said this is the only place you could truly rest. But you're always busy, and sometimes things here get a bit... messy.
I'm here with you.
Triss, do you want me to keep going with my plan?
Of course! I wanna sing and sing forever!
Even though this isn't the home we once knew?
I know it's not. I'm not the same as I was either. I died in an accident, hundreds of years ago.
But I still feel me inside, and I can still laugh and sing. It doesn't feel any different.
I know you can do it, Phrolova. You'll bring everyone back, and I'll be right here waitin' for ye. I'll wait for that day.
By then...
By then, you will stand on an even brighter stage.
(I'll be here. "Always.")
This time... Will death be real...?
Am I... finally going back...?
But you can't, Phrolova. You can't simply die. Didn't you promise to bring them home?
Phrolova... Phrolova... Wake up...
Phrolova... Phrolova!
Losing that much blood and not even trying to treat it... If you really wanted to die, I could've made it quicker for you.
You deliberately teeter on the verge of death. Are you that desperate to see what you truly desire?
We should move.

Phrolova's Orchestration has restored the area, but overusing her ability plunges her exhausted mind into more hallucinations. She finds herself beside her loved ones, playing music and sharing laughter as they accept her every word. Phrolova then faints, thinking the long-awaited death has finally come for her, but you bring her back.
An audio recording here.
Fenrico's goal isn't just the Gem.
Or, more precisely, this man of authority has already sunk deep into the mire of his own confusion.
(This feels a lot like what Cantarella described before.)
(Is the Threnodian's power driving him toward something?)
Why did you create the Lost Beyond?
Because... I made a promise long, long ago.
A long-lost friend once told me that every promise matters. Once you make one, you see it through, no matter the cost.
How long is "long, long ago"…
Well, nothing like what you'd call "long ago," I suppose.
But you're still human.
And?
Maybe it's about keeping a promise. Or maybe it's your own stubbornness.
Heh...
Resonance abilities are tied to emotions. If your stubbornness drove you to create an entire Sonoro, then I'd call it an obsession.
Perhaps.

You find recordings that reveal Fenrico's scheme to seize the Lost Beyond and the Threnodian's residual energy, which seems to contradict his previous commands. Fenrico appears to notice his abnormality. When Phrolova points out that Fenrico is in disarray, you suspect he has fallen under the Threnodian's influence. You then seize the moment to ask Phrolova about her true reason for creating the Lost Beyond. She simply replies that it was but to keep a distant promise and satisfy an obsession.
Primus, Phrolova has reached the final stage.
The foundation of the Paradise is complete. It is time to purge those who have strayed.
The souls trapped in darkness need a temporary dwelling. For that, we need her work.
But Primus…
You hesitate. Why?
This is... different from what you told us.
You said our goal was to return the divine power within the Gem to the holy sphere. You never mentioned this part.
Has the plan changed?
Primus? Should I continue the recording?
Recording... When did I ever... I see. No, continue recording.
This wasn't part of the plan, was it?
No. Someone interfered. I've never been here before.
Then we'd better find a way out quickly.
Dear brothers and sisters, you who stand before us shall be an irreplaceable force in Rinascita's salvation.
Let us join together to spread light to all, and face the Divine Ordeal in unity.
Are you one of Fenrico's Acolytes?
Come, join us! Offer your prayers to the holiest sacred land!
Amidst your endless research, do not forsake your faith! Never forget! They are always watching!
(There's no light in their eyes. Just emptiness… and blind devotion.)
These fanatics can give you no answers.
Why are there so many ensnared Acolytes here?
Let's check out what's happening.
Agreed.
Brothers and sisters, if your resolve is firm, step forward. The sacred pilgrimage awaits.
Remember! Only the devoted shall receive Their blessings.
These Acolytes seem more fervent than the last group.
To find the exit, we must play along.
How about a simple disguise, dear Acolyte?
Let's do it.
Give me more time.
With no way out, Phrolova points out that disguising yourselves as Acolytes is the only viable option.
I didn't expect the Order's rituals to be this elaborate.
Elaboration fosters reverence.
Fair point.
How do we lead people to worship You?
We guide them closer to Your boundless grace.
How do we lead people to believe in You?
We let them touch Your very soul.
Come closer.
Reach out your hand.
Until you walk with Them.
There's an inscription on the altar.
"I am no longer Them. I will lead the people forward."
Imperator's statue is gone… Is this Fenrico's ambition?
The next line reads...
"It reminds us that the Sentinel walks with us, illuminating our path with wisdom."
The Sentinel… Could this lantern be the very one Napoli the Second used? The one imbued with the Sentinel's power that allowed him to repel the Dark Tide?
You follow a group of Acolytes to a statue, where an altar holds the lantern of Napoli the Second. Upon touching it, you are suddenly teleported into an illusive realm.
(That lantern wasn't real... Where am I?)
(Where's Phrolova?)
Take the red gate.
He wants to trap us here forever.
Phrolova?
I'm here. Do what I said.
The flickering lights show you the way forward.
If time works against you, then change it.
Leave the Orchestration to me. You just open the red gate.
Was that reality or an illusion…?
Does it matter? Let's move forward.
A secret space with no visible exit. That can only mean...
There must be hidden pathways.
Is this another Orchestration Altar? It looks different from the one before.
The principles should be the same.
I'll check the surroundings for clues while you handle the Orchestration. It'll be faster that way.
Sure.
You come across an Ochestration Altar. You suggest Phrolova handle the Orchestration while you search the area for any useful clues.
Perfect timing.
Wait, we just unlocked something.
I'd really like to see what secret is kept in such a place.
("Unity is the sole deliverance from the Divine Ordeal." That's why Fenrico fought to keep Ragunna from falling into discord.)

(The record says darkness has long shackled the Ragunnesi's subconscious. Only by defeating this <te href=851025>Harbinger</te>, descending into the depths of darkness, and bringing back all trapped souls can the Dark Tide be resisted...）
(So that's why he's after the Gem and the Beyond. He intends to use them to house the Ragunnesi's subconscious and fend off the Dark Tide.)
(The Acolytes we encountered... They were probably the martyrs who tried and failed.)
(...Could he really have come up with this solution entirely on his own?)
(Gathering everyone's consciousness and keeping them in some sanctuary...)
(But when I compare this to the information I found before, the handwriting is the same, but the viewpoints contradict each other.)
(That recording I found earlier also mentioned Fenrico giving conflicting orders to the Acolytes at times.)
(He doesn't strike me as indecisive. He must've noticed these inconsistencies himself. That's why he left these notes and the lantern, as reminders to himself.)
(What other force is at play here? The path of salvation he's chosen might not be as perfect as he thinks...)
From among the faithful, a powerful Harbinger shall arise, bringing both life and annihilation from the Dark Tide into this world.
This Harbinger... Who does that refer to?
I don't know. Nor do I care.
Alright, let's move on. There's an opening below. We might find a way out there.

Reading through the files you found, you uncover a hidden truth: the Dark Tide has long shackled the subconscious of the Ragunnesis. Only by defeating the Harbinger and bringing back all the trapped souls can it be resisted. Fenrico's pursuit of the Threnodian's energy and the Lost Beyond is actually an attempt to use them to house the Ragunnesi's subconscious and fend off the Dark Tide's invasion. But who is this Harbinger? Something seems to be hampering Fenrico's plans. Could there be other hidden risks to his actions?
O sinful dream, why do you disturb this tranquil slumber?
The weeping child lingers no more.
Instead, she raises her hand and claims that vaporous drop.
Heh. No exit. Only a dead end.

Are you alright?!
I... Ugh, I'm fine!
Aim for the ankle on its right leg! That's its weak spot!
Aeolus leans weakly against the stone. Only a faint flicker of life remains in his eyes.
This scene is all too familiar. Heartbreakingly so. A "gift" from fate, carefully prepared for those who dare to defy it.
Listen and honor its weight in silence.
I've always been… a coward…
I feared Augusta, so I lost my will to fight her the moment we crossed blades…
I feared the Lion Beast, so I ran back to camp...
I feared death, so I turned away. Left Master Cato behind to face that hopeless end alone…
I… I keep having the same dream… In that dream, I still lose to Augusta... I never earn Cato's approval. But…
I also dream… of standing right in the swarm of the Dark Tide's creatures. Master Cato is behind me, and I'm holding my ground, fighting with all my might…
Would Master Cato smile... and say he misjudged me?
Heh… just a dream... but this… this isn't so bad either…
To take the Corrosaurus down with me… Ha, who said I didn't have a sense of humor…
Thanks a bunch for the help! Gramp's back has been acting up lately. If it were just the two of us, who knows how long we'd have been stuck out here.
By the way, I'm Rolla. What's your name?
...You're the Champion of this year's Great Agon, aren't you? Name's {PlayerName}?
Whoa, I never thought I'd run into the Champion in person!
Fighting people and fighting Dark Tide beasts aren't the same, but you've got the skills for both. Born with the gifts, I'd say?
Years of practice.
I learn from my opponents.
Hah, you're good at talking crap too.
Haha, don't mind him, Champion. The old timer's a bit grumpy these days. He roasts everyone.
Someone from the camp is looking for you.
Because of the Corrosaurus, right? We were sent to track it down! Gramp actually spotted it a while ago!
Let's head back.
Tell him about Aeolus's death.
Aeolus... he was truly a great Gladiator. I will make sure his story lives on.
He could've avoided that Corrosaurus.
He could've survived.
I understand your sorrow for Aeolus. But Septimont doesn't measure one's sacrifice by whether it was "necessary."
If you can't understand Aeolus's choice, then think of it this way:
He was a Gladiator. That's all there is to it.
Tell him about Aeolus's death.
What kind of joke is this, huh? A prank? If I fall for it, is he gonna jump out and mock me?
Aeolus, you old fool... You think I'd find this funny?!
Damn you Gladiators... Damn the Dark Tide... Damn it all!
…I'll tell Rolla later. Just—just give me a moment. I'll see you around.
Did you build this?
Uncle Gren helped too. He's probably off slaying more Dark Tide creations. Been cursing nonstop.
…I recently had a dream of my childhood.
I dreamed of Dark Tide creations attacking the village. No reinforcements. Just two Gladiators holding the line. When the monsters were about to kill me, a Gladiator picked me up and ran.
His face was covered in tears. He kept saying sorry. Called himself a coward.
...Why did you say that, Gramp? You've always been my hero.
He was crying, holding me tight, running away from the battlefield... from his companion.

To Gladiator Lord Aeolus,

I have received your withdrawal request. It is hereby denied. The glory of Septimont shall forever shine upon you—a true Gladiator.

Also, Master Aeolus, you were the seventh formidable opponent I faced on my path forward. Your swordsmanship and keen battle instincts left a deep impression on me. I will carry your blade, your ideals, and everything you stood for, and lead Septimont forward.

Please, bear witness.

Highest regards,
Ephor Augusta of Septimont
Aeolus stands before Cato's grave in silence. He tries to hold himself upright, but you can still see the stoop in his posture.
Time hasn't treated him kindly.
(Say something.)
(Remain silent.)
I don't know much about Septimont's culture, or you. But I respect your choice.
Should we return to the Hunter's Den or Gren's camp?
You don't know much about the Gladiator before you, but it's clear that fate has taken much from him.
All you can do is offer him silent respect.
...{PlayerName}, Champion of the Great Agon.
I, Gladiator Aeolus, hereby challenge you to a duel.
It won't prove anything.
I refuse.
Draw your blade.
Without holding back, you finish this match in just a few seconds.
...I lost.
{PlayerName}, bring the Corrosaurus's intel back to the Hunter's Den. Tell them I'm sorry and I won't be going back.
...Right. There's no point in challenging you. What was I even doing...
{PlayerName}, bring the Corrosaurus's intel back to the Hunter's Den. Tell them I'm sorry and I won't be going back.
You go first. I'll stay here for a while.
This doesn't seem the way back to the Hunter's Den.
Nope, we're heading back to our camp.
Thanks, Aeolus. Any anomalies?
If you mean the Corrosaurus, no. It hasn't found this camp yet. But there's a Kerasaur sneaking around.
Tsk, that thing's roar is ear-splitting. If we're not careful, it could draw the Corrosaurus right to us.
Shame to abandon a camp like this with such perfect terrain. Look at it. Hills for cover, water all around—
By water, you mean the Dark Tide, right?
…You really are a mood killer, Rolla. Can't you tell I was trying to lighten the mood?
Are you Gladiators as well?
We were.
Not to brag, but back in the day, we were household names. Until we got fed up with the sponsors and nobles. That's when we walked away.
You must have heard the name Gren back in Septimont City, haven't you? I even endorsed drinks once.
That was forever ago, Coach. This here is {PlayerName}, the newest Champion of the Great Agon!
Seriously? And I thought that Lupa girl was already something. Now there's another one?
No kidding! Ask Aeolus!
I'll handle the Kerasaur. We can't let it get any closer.
Alone? But you're still injured!
I'll go with you.
At least patch yourself up first.
No need.
So, should I take this as your official acceptance to join our team, Aeolus?
I'm going to deal with the Kerasaur. That's all.
Then take Rolla with you. It's about time she fights one herself.
And to make sure she comes back in one piece, {PlayerName} should go too. Sound fair?
…Don't think this earns you my thanks, Gren.
What, are you trying to crush Rolla's spirit, Gladiator Aeolus?
Hmph. Fine. I'll patch up. Then we move.
Are Kerasaurs really that dangerous, Champion?
Coach Gren always said he could take one down single-handedly in his prime… But Gramp's always going on about the "nine rules" of fighting a Kerasaur.
I can take a Kerasaur with just one finger.
You have to give it your all against any opponent.
Aha, now that's the Champion talking! One finger, huh? That makes you, like, five times stronger than Coach!
You sound just like Gramp...
Hmm… now I'm curious what Gramp was like when he was younger.
You don't know? I thought you've always been together.
Nope. He only showed up after we set up this camp not long ago.
Before that, I was roaming the Plateaus with Coach Gren and the others, scraping by wherever we could find shelter. But we always avoided Gladiators.
Why?
Coach used to say they were a bunch of stiff guys who'd do anything in the name of "a brighter future for Septimont." He's not a fan of people with no sense of humor.
But Gramp seems to know Coach Gren well. He's always looking out for me... Wait—don't tell me he's actually my real grandpa?!
You know, that "Gramp" Aeolus is actually about eight years younger than me. Hard to believe, right?
Let me tell you the secret to staying young: keep your sense of humor! I heard you're from Huanglong? People there have a saying... hmm, what was it again—"Laugh more, live longer"? Haha!
Anyway, I'll leave Rolla in your care. It's been years, and Aeolus's skills haven't improved one bit. That stubborn old man...
Why don't you go with them yourself?
You're more than capable of keeping them both safe.
Ah, no can do. Not this time.
It takes someone as strong as you to make Aeolus drop the whole Gladiator thing.
I bet you've got a lot of questions on your mind right now—"What's your relationship with Aeolus?" "Why did you try to stop him from being a Gladiator?" "Is Rolla really his family?"
Well, I'm afraid those answers are yours to uncover on your little journey.
Why, did you carve them on stones along the way?
I'm not that nosy...
Pfft, you've got a sense of humor, eh! Didn't expect someone your age to crack better jokes than me. Wait… don't tell me you're actually older than I am?
You can return to the camp now. Tell them I'll bring back the intel soon.
I promised Gren I'd keep an eye on Rolla.
It won't take long to hunt a Kerasaur.
Oh, come on, Gramp! Why so stubborn today? Let's just go!
Those are its footprints. It's larger and heavier than normal ones. The stride is steady. No signs of injury or irregular movement.
No traces of battle with other Dark Tide creations along the way either...
Looks like its frequency alone was enough to scare off the others. Could it be... a special variant?
Damn the Dark Tide...
Tsk... Just shut it. Count yourself lucky you're still breathing. Don't let any of that dark slime get on you, or you'll be twisted into a mindless monster.
Let's see if you'd still have the strength to complain then.
Teeny, Arctos, and everyone got away... no one hurt...
Chunkie can go home now...

Chunkie's frequency fades along with the Dark Tide, as if it has never existed.
The Dark Tide erases its mind and body, leaving behind nothing but a single feather.
This feather... It's from my old helmet.
When the Dark Tide struck our old camp, as a former Gladiator, I stayed behind to cover everyone's retreat. Chunkie and Teeny also stood with me.
We thought it would be a glorious hunt, but little did we know, we were the ones being hunted by the Dark Tide.
In the end, as the corruption crawled up my helmet, it was Chunkie who charged to save me, knocking aside the tainted helm and pushing me out of harm's way.
But Chunkie...
Chunkie let the Dark Tide take it instead... To protect me and Teeny...
Arctos, Teeny hears Chunkie's voice—
Teeny, Arctos, and everyone got away... no one hurt...
Arctos grasps the feather tightly.
Yes, Chunkie. Let's all go home now.
Chunkie can go home now...
Thank you, {PlayerName}. My children have all made it home.
Woo ta, woo ta ta, ta—
Our new camp has been rebuilt as well.
No matter how many times the Dark Tide tears it down, as long as one of us remains standing, it will be rebuilt.
I added the feather Chunkie left behind to the Hornett's tail.
A Hornett's tail is made from the plumes of Gladiator's helmets. Now, I finally understand the significance.
The Dark Tide may erase our minds, our bodies, but it can never erase our courage to fight back and push forward.
Chunkie was a Gladiator worth honoring.
And no matter how many times the Dark Tide returns, we will rise to meet it, until the applause of triumph echoes through this land once more.
That's what Chunkie would've wanted.
May applause greet this world again.
Hold a moment, young warrior...
It shames me to ask this of you, but… I don't know who else to turn to.
Could you help me find my children?
The Dark Tide ravages everything in its path. So many innocent lives lost. And the ones who went mad turned the camp upside down.
See the claw marks around camp? My friends, fallen. My children, missing. And I... I can't lift a sword with these injuries.
Sometimes I hate these old bones of mine... I don't even know whether it's the Dark Tide or just the weight of years that's made me this useless.
I'll help you find your children.
Don't worry. Leave it to me.
Thank you. Young people like you always have such courage.
Before I fainted, I last saw my children running toward the iron gates.
Hmm... There's something familiar about that monster.
Doesn't matter. I'll take 'em down just the same once the horns go off.
Ugh, it hurts...
Woo ta... Woo ta ta...
Woo ta! Woo ta ta ta—
As you push the huge stone aside, a brownish shadow darts out.
A tuft of fur left behind catches your eye.
Ta ta ka!!!
Woo... hmm, t-thank you, ta!
That's a serious wound. You shouldn't be fighting like this.
T-to bring Chunkie back!
Teeny wheezes softly, clearly injured. But its wounds don't dampen its spirit. It looks ready to charge forward again.
Easy now. Just head back to camp and get patched up first. You'll need your strength to do what you came here for.
Woo… Okay. Teeny knows where Chunkie is. Teeny should see Arctos first!
Did you hear about Arctos's children? Such bravery.
Indeed. The Hornett's been blaring louder than ever.
Every time I hear it, it strengthens my resolve to protect those around me.
The new Hornett sounds amazing! It really gets the blood pumping!
No matter how many times the Dark Tide returns, we will rise to meet it, until the applause of triumph echoes through this land once more!
Hey, don't get too eager. I'd prefer the Dark Tide never return!
Still, that Hornett really does set you up in the mood for work.
Yeah! Let's rebuild this camp together!
Woo ta ta... Woo ta... Ta ta!
Abby, Echo interpretation service, please.
Roger that! Your five-star Echo interpreter, at your service! Ahem... Let's try out my new emotional-adaptive mode!
Beep—loading complete! Standing by for interpretation request...
Thanks to Abby, you can now understand what the Wootter is saying.
Woo! Danger ahead!
I'm looking for someone.
Have you seen any children come this way?
Abby relays your words to the Wootter. Its chubby face scrunches up in confusion.
Woo. Wootter sees no one. Very dangerous out there. Big monster!
Wootter and friends protect camp and search outside. Wootter hurt. Must stay here.
But Wootter's friends ahead. They help you!
The Wootter plucks some fur from its body and offers it to you.
Follow the scent. It leads you to them!
I sense something dangerous...
What happened at that camp over there?
I can sense it. Something dark, filthy, and dangerous...
It feels urgent, but I've still got things to take care of here...
Don't worry. I'll go check it out.
Hmm... looks like the danger has passed.
Looks like the danger has passed. Did you take care of it?
Yeah, that was me.
I'm just a passerby lending a hand.
Thank you so much.
You're too modest.
I see everyone working hard to rebuild the camp.
They look full of spirit.
That puts my mind at ease. Now I can focus on guarding this place.
Judging by the tufts of fur scattered on the ground, a fierce fight must've taken place here.
Sensing the urgency, you press on without delay.
Woo!
Ta! Ta ta!!
Ta ta ka!!
Interpret that, please, Abby.
Interpreting—
Woo! So scary!
Thank you!
Whew... If Dark Tide monsters hurt Wootter... Wootter will turn scary too...
No! Wootter no want to turn into big scary monster!
Excuse me, have you seen any children around?
Children? Human children? Wootter sees no children.
Only Wootters and monsters here. No human children.
Too dangerous. No human children would play here...
Woo ta ta ta—! Teeny! Where's Teeny?! Teeny not with us!
Teeny... Arctos's Teeny? Did monsters get Teeny?!
Save Teeny! Help us! Pleeeassse!
(They said they didn't see any human children. Could this Wooter "Teeny" be one of the children Arctos is looking for?)
(Only one way to find out.)
Okay, I'll go find Teeny.
Thank you, woo! You a good human!
Are you alright, Teeny?
No worry, ta! But... Chunkie still out there...
It's okay, Teeny. I'm just glad you made it back safely.
So this is one of the children you were looking for?
Yes… But as long as "it" is out there, this isn't over.
Teeny found Chunkie! Chunkie looks strange… hiding in the cave behind big stone.
Young warrior, would you be willing to search this cave with us? I should handle this alone, but both Teeny and I are injured...
Just leave it to me. You two stay here and rest.
No… I must see this through and end it with my own hands.
Back at the camp, Arctos notices Teeny's wounds and tends to them.

A massive Hurriclaw stands in the cave, its body covered in dark, writhing growths that burst from its back.
Its mind is corrupted. It stumbles, groaning in delirium. The cave walls bear the marks of its frenzied claws.
Wake up, Chunkie!
The Hurriclaw sees Teeny and Arctos, and a spark of awareness flickers in its cloudy eyes.
Arctos... Teeny...
Chunkie... I'm sorry. I couldn't protect you from the Dark Tide... If only I'd been stronger...
Chunkie... wants to go home... with Arctos... and everyone... But Chunkie... can't control... Ngh—!
Chunkie looked for camp... but camp gone. Chunkie went to where Teeny, Arctos, and Chunkie played... but also gone.
Gone! The dark thing came... and all gone!
As if recalling the painful memoriees, Chunkie begins to thrash and roar in anguish.
Aaarrrghhh—! It... hurts! AAAARRHHHHH!
It hurts... so much... Help Chunkie... End this...
You glance at Arctos. He meets your eyes and gives a gentle nod.
You wander around the camp for a while. Seeing the imposing Tetragon Temple, you decide to head up and take a closer look.
The Ephor's Palace is just ahead.
