You're right. With the Black Shores' tech, we might be able to outwit our unseen enemy.
I'll contact them as soon as we're back.
There's a friend of mine who… well, she knows a lot about Imperator. She might be able to help solve this mystery.
More importantly... her powers are unique. The Earthrender's holding back the Dark Tide for now, but those sudden outbreaks and the way it's fixated on you… it's not just a coincidence.
If anyone can put an end to the Dark Tide's threat in Septimont, it's her.
Sounds like someone worth meeting.
Do introduce me later. I'm curious what kind of person she is.
But one thing I'm sure of, she must be a formidable opponent and a figure to be respected, like you.
You two share a lot in common, actually. I think you'd get along.
I'll reach out to her once we're back. She wasn't able to travel before due to some unavoidable reasons, but now, I think the timing's right.
Alright. Let's set all this aside and enjoy the victory we've earned.
There's probably a bonfire roaring at the encampment by now… {PlayerName}, it's time to return to those waiting for us.
We won this battle, but the war is far from over. The road ahead's still steeped in blood and thorns. But with you, and everyone who stood beside us, the banner of Septimont will never fall.
With the eternal sun as my witness, the name of hero belongs to you all.
Meanwhile, in Murmurstown, Cristoforo finds the Holmleaf Medal lost by Avidius. The Playwright's work is not yet finished...
What a beautiful ending, my near-perfect protagonist. I must confess... even I didn't see this coming.
Should this be your final act? No. No, allow me this small indulgence, as your creator.
The quill of fate may be sharp and cold, but still, I want to see how far the soul I created can go.
After all, it's the stories that sink deepest into the mire that stir the heart most, don't you think?
It's been a while, Rinascita.
What prey do we hunt this time?
...The Threnodian.

Somewhere in Rinascita, a mysterious woman walks alongside a Dark Tide creation, her gaze fixed silently on the distant horizon. She turns to the creature and reveals the purpose of her return to this land—to hunt the Threnodian.
You take the upper area, {PlayerName}. I'll take the lower one.
If you spot any signs of the Sovereign or run into trouble, let me know right away.

To speed up the search for the False Sovereign, you and Augusta split up. When you contact Buling for help, she explains that the Sovereign has absorbed Murmurstown's chaotic frequencies to mask its own, making it impossible for the Tethys System to locate it. To fix this, you and Abby set out to find a sample of pure Dark Tide frequency.
This place is too quiet. No trace of the Sovereign anyway...
Hey Buling, can you help me track down the Sovereign?
You got it. Gimme a sec to scan things.
Emm... Sorry, Boss. The frequencies around you are all over the place... I can't get a clear reading.
This Sovereign's a slippery eel, eating up every little frequency like it's popcorn. Now the Tethys system's got nothing to work with!
Hmph... it's playing hide-and-seek with us on purpose. What trouble.
Hold on. What if you bring me some pure Dark Tide frequency samples?
Maybe Tethys can use it to track down something with a similar frequency, like the Sovereign itself or the original Dark Tide. Could give you a better lead.
Understood. I'll do what I can.
Abby? Abby? Wake up.
...Whaaat's going on...?
I'm sooo sleepy... Ugh, that dark spooky stuff I ate earlier is still gurgling in my belly...
Sorry to hear that. But if my clever, brave, stylish, and sweet Abby could help me out, that'd be amazing.
Aww, you're making me blush! Okay, okay, your best buddy Abby's on the job. Go on!
So... that thing we tangled with before has gone into hiding around here.
I need your help to sniff it out.
Easy-peasy! You know I have a good nose for searching!
(Sniffs the air)
Find anything?
Ugh... the whole place smells like a dumpster fire. And that monster... I can't tell where it is exactly... The scent's all muddled...
There's something weird over there!
Is that... a <te href=750020>Waystone</te>?
I've seen those back in Septimont City. They're like signposts for outlanders.
Alright, let's check it out!
This the one?
Yep! This is it!
Its right arm is missing. Isn't it supposed to be pointing in that direction?
I guess. It wouldn't be a Waystone if it didn't show the way, right?
Hey, something just flew by that way!
It's that muddled scent again! C'mon, we've gotta catch it!
...It's gone.
Is it hiding among those strange statues over there?
Wait... are they singing?
They must be the Hollow Figures Augusta mentioned... And that song…
No... I can't get any closer.
(Maybe I can split off the Dark Tide's influence...)
It worked...
Ugh, nope! That troublemaker's off again!
Look, {PlayerName}! It stopped over there!
Darn it! It flew away again!
Gotcha!
Tacet Discords are gathering… Need to take them out.
Watch out!
Now it's hiding inside a Tacet Discord? Boo!
Don't worry, we'll flush it out.
Great, it's found another one to cling to!
...It's making that Tacet Discord even stronger. We should handle the others first.
Aha, your hide-and-seek game's over!
Time to finish it.
A piece of cloth… Looks like something from a Gladiator's gear.
But why here...
Hmm... its frequency is something else.
Is it that same muddled scent you mentioned before?
Well... it's got a bit of that smell, but the fabric's frequency is even stronger. It's not giving in…
Kind of like... a brave Gladiator fighting a monster!
I see...
...That Waystone with the missing right arm had a sleeve that was torn.
Why don't we take it to the statue? Maybe it'll unlock the next clue!

Elsewhere, Augusta stands before a withered oak. The Whispers tempt her to enter Oak Hollow and accept "Divinity's" power and become the prophesied Hero of Heroes. But past memories flash through her mind, and she firmly rejects the Whispers' temptation. Immediately after, she receives your signal and moves to regroup.
You long to become the one true ruler of Septimont, the one to end the unending tragedy of your people. Is that not your true desire?
And yet, you remain but a fragile mortal, unworthy of the greatness you seek. How can such a weak soul claim its place among the gods?
Deny it not, sweet child. Your heart is bare to us...
Take one more step. Grasp it. Feel it. Embrace it. Awaken this power through your Forte, and shed the weakness of your pitiful shell.
Come to us. Let Divinity crown you in glory and might...
Answer our call, and Septimont shall stand eternal, rising above all, with you as its one true sovereign...
Angel...
A power granted rather than earned... Could never truly be mine.
If this power strips me of my will, how can I be sure where my sword will strike?
Heh. I reject such a "gift."
Augusta, I've got a lead.
Location's on your Terminal. I'll wait for you there.
Copy. On my way.

You bring the "light," a cloth scrap carrying the lingering frequency of a fallen Gladiator, to a Waystone. It opens a portal to a Sonoro Sphere giving off frequencies similar to the False Sovereign's. After reuniting with Augusta, you decide to enter it together.
...The clash of battles long past is proof of my unyielding will...
Travelers who have braved the path, press onward. Step into the dark,  where forsaken truths and forgotten words slumber.
This is... a Sonoro!
Huh? That muddled smell makes sense now!
A Gladiator who fought the Dark Tide in Murmurstown to his last breath. His frequency still lingers to carry on the fight...
Thank you for showing us the way ahead.
Augusta, over here!
Is this... a Sonoro?
It's a bit more complicated than that...
Alright, time for Abby's rundown! So... {PlayerName} and I were tracking that shadowy monster fella.
And I followed its scent right to... eh... this Sonoro.
Well, kind of. It's not the exact same scent. It's just really close. It's also kinda muddled.
Right. The frequencies the Black Shores detected in both Murmurstown and from the Sovereign are unusually complex.
To track the Sovereign, we'll need to help by isolating a pure Dark Tide frequency.
I wasn't sure where to start, but Abby's been a big help.
Ahaha, don't mention it! Easy peasy, lemon squeezy.
...I assume this is your Echo friend who saved us in the Asphodel Barrens?
You have my gratitude.
No biggie!
You don't seem surprised.
The level of power it showed is indeed questionable for an Echo... but I trust it as much as I trust you.
No need for explanations between allies.
Hmm... did you hear that?
"Through me, walk the Path of Glorious Ascension... Through me, enter the City of Eternal Bliss... Yet all who enter must first forsake all Hope."
Sounds like a song... Those lyrics are pretty intense though...
Sonoro... what do you want to show us...
Let's enter it, {PlayerName}.

Following a mysterious "light," you and Abby reach a group of Hollow Figures chanting a haunting "hymn." You use the power of separation to resist the Dark Tide's influence and search for the hidden "light." Your instincts tell you it's tied to the pure frequency you're after.
Something's not right... Be on your guard, everyone.
The ground is collapsing! Watch out!
Over there...
Getting excited are we, Tyrannos?
Watch out for those molten rocks. Use the pillars for cover. Move!
Cunning bastard.
Everyone under the ledge. Now!
Phew. We're almost at the hunting grounds.
Victory is still far from reach. We're not in the clear yet.
Rocks above!
Say something, anything
Say something, anything
Say something, anything
This path will take us to the first anchor point.
Due to the High Tide, Tacet Discords in the hunting grounds have become more aggressive than usual.
Maintain your focus.
Tacet Discords...
Hmph. Just in time. My sword's had enough of waiting.
Such carnage...
These tricks do not surprise me.
Avidius, take a response team and get that Anchor Obelisk functioning.
{PlayerName} and I will provide cover.
As you command, Your Excellency.
Avidius's team should be almost done, Augusta. I'll head over to join them.
Of course. See that it's done.
Your aid couldn't have come at a better time.
We were just about to insert the Anchor Stone into the Obelisk.
Excellent work, all.
Filthy... spiteful... shadows...
Its shadow...
Inside these hunting grounds, the hunter can become the hunted at a moment's notice.
Think that beast is running away? Heh, just a trick to throw us off.
Let Augusta humor its little performance. Beasts who think they've won are always the first to die.
Let her handle the Corrosaurus for now, {PlayerName}. We have more important matters to take care of.
What brings you here, Iuno?
Oh? Surprised to see me?
I've already shared my interests with you. It wouldn't kill you to remember a few things I've said, would it?
But fine. Since it's you, I suppose I can let you in on the secret.
The Corrosaurus is just an appetizer. I've got bigger fish to fry.

The hunting party works together to activate the first Anchor Stone Obelisk. The Whispers alert Augusta to Tyrannos's surprise ambush, and she gives chase. You prepare to follow her, but Iuno arrives in time to stop you. She explains that you still have more important matters to attend to, and that it's best to leave Tyrannos to Augusta for now.
The next Anchor Obelisk is on the other side of the plateau.
Impeccable timing, my dear Priestess.
Consider this a privilege, would-be Hero.
Wingrays are here too, huh?
Does that surprise you? Augusta and I prepared it all well in advance.
Ride the winds, {PlayerName}, and let's soar over these cliffs together.
We've lost sight of Augusta and the Corrosaurus.
Let me see your Terminal, {PlayerName}.
You give Iuno your Terminal.
What for?
There. Try using the Sensor.
These are traces of the Dark Tide.
You catch on quickly.
My Resonance power can reveal hidden traces of the Dark Tide for a short time. With these markings, be it Tyrannos or a Tyran-whatever, nothing can escape my eyes.
Aren't we supposed to find the Obelisks?
Yes, you're not wrong. But the beast also has its eye on <te href=750014>them</te>.
A sly enemy like this won't play by the usual rules. The more cautious we are, the better.
Ha, so it is heading for that cave. The second Obelisk is also in that direction.
Come. Let's go have a little fun with our friend.
This is it.
The second Obelisk should be at the other end of this cave.
Mind the Tacet Discords.
I'd be more worried about yourself, would-be Hero. Try not to slow us down.
Watch out! Tch... How did it manage to get here?
There's an opening in the floor, {PlayerName}. That's our way out!
I'll keep it busy. Now's your chance, go!
Make no mistake, your fight is with me!
Augusta!
My apologies for the delay.
Be warned the Corrosaurus could return at any moment. We should leave.
Careful of the rocks!
Here it comes!
Tyrannos will not rest until we are corpses.
But since it hasn't shown itself yet, we should use this moment to catch our breath.
These formations seem solid enough for a quick pause.
Up there, to the left! That stone seems loose.
Pull it down, {PlayerName}!
It's the Obelisk. Leave it to me.
Splendid! Let's keep up the momentum!
Tch... You again.
It just left...
It should be the Anchor Obelisk doing its job.
Or perhaps it's up to something more insidious.
The direction it's heading... Is it planning to destroy the final Anchor Obelisk?
Heh. Persistent. I suppose that makes you a worthy opponent.
This fog...
...It hinders our vision. We could be walking into a trap.
Makes for a fun challenge, don't you agree, Avidius?
Stay vigilant. In due time, Tyrannos will learn that Gladiators always keep their blades sharpened.
{PlayerName}, the Obelisk is right over there!
Good. You did well not to disappoint.
Augusta, Tyrannos is heading for the Asphodel Barrens.
The net has been cast... It's time to reel in the prize.
Looks like the oration they mentioned.
Huh… I thought for sure it'd be Iuno at an event like this.
Eh, well. Guess I'll catch her later.
...Yes, I fear that until Grandmother Lillibet finds a gifted successor, we shall not glimpse further into <ano= Septimont's Auguries>Septimont's future</ano>.
By the light and fate above us, we are but apprentices carving insights into stone, passing their words along.
(Gifted successor? Shouldn't it just be Iuno?)
(Is Iuno no longer serving as Priestess?)
Once, fate flowed like a thread. It guided reverent seekers to glimpse Septimont's end...
Under the Tide's surge, all was overturned. No soul was spared.
Until the Unwritten One arrived from afar to join forces with Augusta.
With the Corrosaurus as bait, {Male=he;Female=she} cut through the Dark Tide's miasma to reveal the truth.
With the False Sovereign's blood, a new ruler was crowned. The prophesied end was averted, thanks to Augusta and the Unwritten One.

From now on, fear no longer grips me. The Dark Tide retreats into the forgotten night, and countless souls drink from pure waters again. The new Hero of Heroes, Augusta, shall lead Septimont into a new age.
Thus, the present now aligns with the prophecy Grandmother Lillibet once foresaw in Septimont's Auguries.
Prophecy of the end, and how we managed to lure the Sovereign out... The order and the story are right, but something's missing.
You speak of me and Augusta, but what of Iuno?
Who is... Iuno?
Iuno is Iuno, what do you mean?
Is this supposed to be a joke?
Unwritten One, you leave me baffled.
Are you suggesting that my recounting missed... someone named Iuno? I don't find the name... familiar.
You're not just forgetting her in your story.
You speak like you don't know her at all.
Hmm. I should know this... Iuno, you speak of, yes?
Iuno is a Priestess, just like you.
More than that, she wielded the Moon Bow and fought alongside me and Augusta in the hunt. We defeated the Sovereign together... Don't you all remember?
Impossible. As a Priestess myself, I can tell you with certainty that none among us bear that name.
And, I must remind you, we rarely take part in hunts. Our place is with the <ano=Sacred Flames>flames</ano> in Tetragon Temple.
The hunt for the Sovereign involved many. Perhaps you are mistaken and confused her for someone else?
No, this can't be.
I don't know what a Priestess is supposed to be, but I do know what Iuno is like. And I'm certain... she's a Priestess.
You mentioned cutting through the Dark Tide's miasma. Tell me, if Iuno wasn't there, then who shot the Moon Arrow?
Who shot the Moon Arrow...? What do you mean? You were the one who dispelled the miasma.
It was... me?
Yes. On the cliffside, you struck with your sword to cut through the Dark Tide. Don't you remember, Unwritten One?

After distributing some petals, a Priestess's oration catches your attention. Surprisingly, for a ceremony of such significance, Iuno isn't the one hosting. In fact, she isn't mentioned at all. Dispelling the Dark Tide's miasma, her role in the hunt, everything... The Priestess's oration of the battle attributes all of Iuno's contributions to you. No one seems to find this strange. It's as if all memory of Iuno has been erased from the world.
May joy also be upon you, {PlayerName}.
The Sovereign is dead. Now we pause in our victory to honor the Hero of Heroes, and all those who stood by her side.
I am Bruno, Master of Ceremonies for the occasion. I had hoped to greet you alongside Augusta.
But she was called away... The Senate insists on wasting her time with their trifles.
We wish to bestow upon you the honor of Rosebearer. Roses symbolize our glory and triumph, to be shared with all who are gathered here.
Rosebearer?
Yes, it's a ceremonial role. Don't worry, it's pretty simple, and you won't be handing out too many.
At the height of the celebration, everyone will toss their petals into the air. We will all shower in the flowers.
Your task will be to distribute the petals beforehand. You have been chosen by the people, for you are held in the highest regard.
The people of Septimont gave their all on the battlefield. Now, after fighting side by side, we'll share honey and wine beneath a rain of petals.
You are our first non-local Rosebearer. But I believe you were already chosen the moment you cut through the Dark Tide's miasma. Without you, the Sovereign's defeat would not have been possible.
Eh? You're saying I did that?
Yes... Oh, I hope you won't decline. This is not only Augusta's wish, it's the people's too.
When Augusta arrives, she'll join the other Rosebearers. I'm sure those who partook in the hunt will be honored to receive petals from you.
I'll give this local tradition a shot.
It would be my honor.
Sounds like a good way to soak in the atmosphere.
Very well, I'll leave it in your capable hands.
As for who you choose and how, trust your instincts. It's just like a toast, or a Priestess's oration, all part of the celebration. No need to overthink it. Now, enjoy!

With the Sovereign slain, you attend the victory ceremony by invitation of Ceremonial Officer Bruno. The celebration honors the new Hero of Heroes and those who stood by their side. As part of the celebration's highlight, countless rose petals will be thrown into the air in a shower of glory. You accept Bruno's offer to become the first non-local Rosebearer and distribute petals to your allies in tribute to victory.
To Septimont! To peace after the storm!
Yes! To the Hero of Heroes, to you, to me, to... Wait, is that {PlayerName}?
(Give petals to the Gladiators.)
Good. When the time comes, I'll hurl the <ano=petals>glory</ano> high and let the wind carry it far. Let the world see our triumph!
Since you're here, anything you want to drink? Speak up. Theseus and I will take care of it.
I'll drink with you when I'm done.
Thanks, but I'm off to see what else is going on.
Alright, we'll catch you after you finish.
Right to the point, huh? Fine. Enjoy yourself. The night's just beginning.
If you're interested, you should go listen to the Priestess. Her orations are one of the highlights of the celebration.
Who's leading it this time? It's not Lillibet, is it?
I already have an idea of who's leading the oration.
So that's why I haven't seen her yet.
I... I'm still worried. The Paradise was stopped, right? But the Dark Tide isn't gone for good. The Sovereign is gone, but what if something worse is waiting for us?
You're hopeless. So what if tomorrow's uncertain? Does that mean tonight doesn't matter?
We've earned a breather. At least for tonight.
Don't stress about tomorrow. Who knows what's coming anyway?
That's the spirit. Tonight is for those who've bled for it. All of us!
Speaking of which... {PlayerName}, you're here early. Got a little something for us?
(Give petals to them.)
Knew it! You were always going to be one of the Rosebearers.
Ah, the fragrance really makes the glory linger... Thank you. Be sure to save some for those who've fought by your side.
Ha! If I were them, I'd gather petals from every bearer, then, when you least expect it... give you a <ano=petal shower>small surprise</ano>!
Augusta wouldn't do something like that.
But Iuno might enjoy it.
Huh? Iuno?
There's not much left. I'll hand some out over there.
My apologies. I should've been here to receive you, but some Priestesses ran into some trouble... I had to step away.
What trouble?
Simply put, aside from what's already been verified, we can no longer see any other of Septimont's Auguries.
The full scope has always been out of reach, but this feeling of being blocked by an impenetrable white barrier is something I've never encountered. It's as if there's nothing there at all.
All the Priestesses' abilities have failed?
Can you still make prophecies?
Well, there is a silver lining. Septimont's Auguries concern Septimont's future, but as for smaller, individual futures... we can still see those.
For instance, I saw Avidius making a commotion not long ago.
But let's talk about why you are here first. Augusta mentioned your situation and said you might come looking for me. You seek help in finding a Priestess by the name of Iuno.
Iuno once lived and breathed in this world.
Everyone's forgotten her. Except for me.
I wish she were a figment of your imagination. A product of your proximity to the Dark Tide. That would make things much simpler.
Because I did find a record of a Priestess named Iuno.
But according to the record, she died three years ago. Buried where the Dark Tide swallowed the spring basin.
How did she die? And why?
A death that shouldn't have happened. Is that a coincidence...
The record didn't say, but...
You must understand, "death" and "disappearance" are two different concepts.
If Iuno truly died three years ago, then she couldn't have been your companion three years later, let alone have existed up until today.
In other words, if Iuno disappeared today and was erased from the memories of Augusta, myself, and everyone else, then the death three years ago must have been a fabrication.
Can you say that again, but in simple terms?
What does it mean if her death was a fabrication?
It means her death three years ago and her disappearance today cannot both be true.

If someone has truly disappeared from this world, do they need a fabricated death? Likewise, when someone dies, they no longer exist in a way that others can feel. These two causal chains should be clear, but they crossed paths with you, the unknowable void.
Although I hate to admit it, Avidius was right... Since you still remember Iuno and thus hold onto that last connection between her and the world, you've essentially "anchored" her.

This has caused the causal chain to become tangled. The ending is still unwritten. Right now, she is but a specter, stuck reliving her past in the Chaos between life and death, between existence and non-existence.
And I can choose which causal chain to keep.
What if I enter the Chaos myself...
In theory, yes. You could forget her, let her disappear entirely. Or, you could forget her and let her die for good.
Is there really no other way?
What if neither of those work for me?
I believe insight into fate is not to tempt one's defiance. It will move according to its intended end.
Besides, it's already granted you a rare gift—two options. More than most ever get.
Then I'll make my own deal with fate.
I refuse to let fate dictate my choices.
So you wish to use yourself as a vessel to anchor the memories, feelings, and connections with Iuno in the Chaos, manifesting her back into existence?
Anchor, manifest, whatever you want to call it. All I know is Iuno's not gone because of me. So why shouldn't I be able to bring her back?
If I can tangle the causal chain, why can't I create a new possibility?
Your thinking is... bold, to say the least.

But do you really understand? Chaos isn't just disorder. It's the aggregation of all things. A web of cause and effect, the convergence of infinite possibilities. If you end up lost within it, you risk being consumed, never to return.
Even ones such as we, guided by fate, can only pull small insights from certain shores of destiny. What if you enter only to find that you cannot bring Iuno back?
But you didn't say I can't enter.
So just tell me how to do it.
Chaos isn't a place in the usual sense. The key to entering isn't about where you are, but what's happening and what you do in that moment.
I suspect that three years ago, this Priestess must have done something that defied fate, which set the course for her inevitable disappearance.
If you can get close to that inescapable knot in the causal chain, maybe you'll find a way in.
Then I'll go to the place where the record said she died.

Lillibet reveals two important truths. First, Septimont's future is now veiled behind a white barrier. For the first time, none of the Priestesses can see any of Septimont's Auguries. Second, after hearing from Augusta about your unwavering belief in Iuno's existence, she uncovered a single record: a Priestess named Iuno who died three years ago. But death and disappearance cannot both be true. Your lone memory of Iuno has disrupted the causal chain, creating a reality suspended in limbo. Refusing to accept this ending, you resolve to bring Iuno back from the Chaos between life and death, between existence and non-existence, by using the same method that once gave form to Avidius.
Even with no certainty, you're still heading toward that deathtrap...  {PlayerName}, you've made up your mind, haven't you?
Yes, let's go. The quicker the better.
I still need a moment to prepare.
I understand. One must try at least... Very well, I'll accompany you there.
Of course. But if you truly are to face Chaos, no amount of preparation will ever be enough.
We're here.
This is where the record says she died, three years ago.
Nothing here... Well, that's okay. You tried, {PlayerName}.
No. We've already come this far.
Did we take the wrong path?
Guided by the light of fate, we walk the web of futures. Many seek prophecies to follow or to break free from... all in pursuit of harmonious completeness.
I've never doubted your judgment of Iuno. But if, as you say, she knew what would happen and still chose this path... could it be that this was the closest she could get to true completeness?
If you refuse this ending, how can you be certain that you can create a better one?
A life with all its experiences and feelings, shredded, scattered, and thrown into the realm of Chaos... What you find there may not be beautiful. It will be filled with pain and emptiness.
Even if you do find a way in, your time together may be brief.
With so much uncertainty, do you still feel that you must go?
If there were any doubt, now... Now I'm sure.
Wait, you—
I'm not rejecting the ending Iuno wrote. I just want to fix the regret she left behind.
This is not about her, but me.
Because this ending wasn't fair.
Because I don't want her to go like this.
This isn't the ending I'm happy with, that's all.
An unnecessary death traded for an unforetold victory... She gave everything for Septimont only to be forgotten.
That's a fate no one should suffer. Not her, not anyone.
We've only just begun our story. The future I want... is one where she's there with all of us.
Forgetting may be easier than remembering. But let that be the choice of someone alive, not one who's already gone.
Right now I... don't want to lose anything I still have.
The secret to anchoring, lies in connection and its manifestation.
If you can find what remains of her in the Chaos, and she responds to you...
Then follow her guidance. For that will be the only fragile rope connecting you, her, and this world.

The realm of Chaos isn't entered by location, but through a causal "knot," a specific intersection of circumstance and action. You and Lillibet travel to the site of Iuno's recorded death three years ago, but find nothing unusual. Just as doubt begins to creep in, you notice the corrupted moon above. Once again, a trail of moonlight appears, guiding you toward a specter of Iuno—and deeper into the Dark Tide. You don't hesitate. Though uncertain of what you're seeing, Lillibet knows she can no longer stop you. She offers one final piece of advice: "If you find what remains of her in the Chaos, follow her guidance."
Endlessly cycling... shattering futures... Is this Chaos?
Unsalvageable, fractured into pieces... This is Chaos!
Countless possibilities, both true and not true... This is Chaos...
...Until every Anchor is revealed, laid bare in the light.
(Their accounts are all true, except when it comes to Iuno. How they react to her name is completely wrong.)
(Could this be possible? This distortion in perception? Is it a remnant of the Sovereign's power? Or is this the work of the Fractsidus again?)
I heard what you said to the Priestess, {PlayerName}.
You remember Iuno?
No... I've never even heard of her.
You should know, I've been stationed in this camp longer than most. Memory ain't bad, either.
Been thinking... Maybe the Dark Tide's crawled into your head. Could be you're suffering from dissociation, a side effect of all that exposure.
Dissociation?
Word is, people who get too close end up seeing things. Hallucinations, delusions, the works.
Some of 'em go as far as thinking they see the dead. Or worse, some start calling themselves Tacet Discords.
The Sovereign was built from the Dark Tide itself. Who knows what it swallowed before it came for us? Could be worse than what you're used to. You must be in its grip.
Do you mean to say I'm the crazy one?
I never heard of this dissociation side effect before.
Ah, don't get too worked up. It ain't that bad, not yet anyway.
See, the thing is, it's not like there's one solid name for it. Happens in all kinds of ways, different for each person. And…
At any rate, dissociation is just a problem in perception.
How are you feeling? You need to rest up a bit? ...Oh, looks like Augusta's finally here.
She's been through it too, faced the Sovereign just like you. If you're still doubting, maybe talk to her. Could help.
(Everything she did, they attribute to me. They're not just forgetting. It's as if Iuno never existed to them at all.)
Some folks let it eat at them for life. Others know what's real and what ain't. They keep away from the Dark Tide, and before long they start feeling alright.

Your mind swirls with questions, but no answers come. An elder at the camp notices your unease and gently explains that what you're experiencing may be a side-effect of prolonged Dark Tide exposure—hallucinations, confusion, delusions. He reassures you that these symptoms aren't permanent, and simply avoiding the Dark Tide should let you recover. He suggests speaking with Augusta, who went through the Dark Tide alongside you and might offer some clarity.
{PlayerName}, you've come.
Bruno has already filled you in on the Rosebearer matter, yes? How are the celebrations treating you?
I have something more pressing to discuss with you.
Augusta, do you remember Iuno?
Iuno?
Yes, she was often by your side. The one with the bow like the moon. She joined our hunt for the Sovereign...
Everyone has forgotten... No, that's not it. Everyone says they've never even seen her before.
But you, you remember her. You remember everything that happened. You are certain she is real and cannot exist in your memories alone.
I know what you're feeling, because I've felt it too.
The Dark Tide's frequencies twisted my perception as well. Made me see things that weren't real.
The Sovereign's whispers dogged me for decades, tempting me to accept its gift.
But that's all in the past. I know now that to find peace, I must see through the deception, fight it, and conquer it.
How can you be sure it's deception?
Because of my sword. It reflects everything that happened in Murmurstown.
Existence always leaves a trace. Beyond feeling, memory, and perception, is there anything that can prove this "Iuno" isn't an illusion?
This bracelet... Yes, this bracelet!
I tried to return this to her once...
After this, I shall likely sleep like I've never slept before.
Say, I heard the Montelli family imported some device that aids sleep. It's all the rage... Augusta, I trust you will acquire one for me? I wish to try it myself.
Scented candles are fine, though the scent of the forest is most pleasing. As for pillows and bedding...
That's enough. I allow requests... but only three.
Hmph. Apologies, but I need my rest if I'm to be at full power. Do bear with it. It's for your own good, after all.
And you, {PlayerName}? Were I to indulge in a bit of selfishness, you'd forgive me, wouldn't you?
Saying that in itself is rather selfish.
Depends on how selfish you get.
No, I wouldn't.
Oh? Didn't think the great "Unwritten {PlayerName}" would be so stingy.
Well, lucky for you, I'm feeling generous today. Now, what brings you to me?
You can have this back.
Really? You traveled all this way just to return what I gave you, is that it?
Was it truly such a burden for you?
If one day this bracelet becomes meaningless to anyone else, I hope you will remain the exception, Unwritten One.
But... perhaps in that distant future, forgetting might prove far easier than remembering. Never mind. In any case, you are not to return it.
It's something I've carried with me ever since I was bestowed the title of Priestess. Keep it for me, if only as a keepsake.
For how long must I keep it?
Well, until we meet again, I suppose.
This bracelet belongs to Iuno.
Quite the unique design. Like a crescent moon. But still... I'm sorry.
I wish I could offer you the answer you seek, but to me, it's just an ordinary bracelet. Nothing about it stands out.
When you mentioned her name, I tried to recall any trace of her in my memories.
But there is nothing. What has passed is clear... and she feels like an extra piece to a puzzle, one that doesn't quite fit.
How can this be? You spent the most time with her.
Iuno?
{PlayerName}, wait...
What... did you see?

Knowing how close Augusta and Iuno are, you look to her for confirmation. But what she says shocks you. She believes your memory of "Iuno" is a product of the Whisper's deceptions, a false memory to be resisted. You try to prove Iuno is real by showing her Iuno's Lunarum bracelet. During the hunt, you had tried to return it to Iuno, but she insisted you keep it as a memento. Did she somehow already know she would be forgotten? Just then, light spills from the bracelet to form a specter of Iuno. But Augusta sees nothing at all.
Wait... Why is it only me?
Where's Iuno?!
(The way into Chaos has closed. Lillibet's not here either. Did the Anchoring fail? Or is it not over yet?)
(But Iuno and I made it to the very end. Does this mean... this is the new ending I created?)
For a moment, you can't quite tell...
Were those times with Iuno real... or just a dream?
(I don't see Lillibet anywhere. I'll ask those Priestesses over there.)
Don't you think it's odd...
Grandmother Lillibet also said...
Don't you think it's odd? Even if we can't see the next part of Septimont's Auguries, it still shouldn't be such a white blank?
Grandmother Lillibet also said that for the first time, some of her records in Septimont's Auguries were rewritten...
Seems like some things changed, after all.
Yes, it's like there's a whole new part to the story... Huh? Wait, aren't you who they call the Unwritten One?
This is our first time meeting you in person.
I'm looking for Grandmother Lillibet.
Do you know where Grandmother Lillibet went?
She returned not long ago. She was here just now... Oh, I think I know where she went. Underground.
I don't know why, but things just keep happening today.
Apparently, that Avidius locked up below overheard the Priestesses talking about some prophecy and escaped, just like that.
I think Lillibet must've gone to handle the situation.
No, that's not it. Avidius wasn't being locked up. He chose to stay here. If he wanted to leave, Lillibet wouldn't worry about him.
I think she was called away to the celebration?
Ah yes, I saw a girl with two blue... or was it black, ponytails. Grandmother Lillibet went to the celebration with her.
That makes sense. It must've started by now then! Before the oration ends, Lillibet would definitely need to be there.
(Ponytails...)
(Did Iuno make it back?)
Do you know... who Iuno is?
Iuno? I don't think I've heard that name before. Do you mean that's the girl we're talking about?
Apologies, I didn't have a good look at her...
We've only just become Priestesses. There is much we still don't know about this land. Maybe she was Iuno?
If it's important, perhaps you might try looking for her at the celebration?

Upon returning from Chaos, you discover some records in Lillibet's Book of Prophecies have been overwritten, proof that what you did made a difference. After hearing the Priestesses in discussion, you're certain that things have changed. They mention a girl with two blue ponytails. Could it be Iuno? Following their suggestion, you step into the celebrating crowd to search for her.
Drinks, fine food, orations... The Rosebearers milling about... Yes, everything is just perfect! Hm, {PlayerName}?
I was just saying how the celebration is nearing its most glorious part. You've come here... for more petals to hand out?
Or would you like me to recommend another interesting part of the ceremony?
Neither, actually. I'm looking for someone...
Do you know a girl called Iuno?
Have you seen a girl with dark blue ponytails?
Ah... the name has a lovely ring to it, but I'm afraid I don't.
Ponytails, dark blue... My apologies, but I don't think I have.
I see. Thanks, I'll try my luck elsewhere.
In a celebration this grand, it's easy to get separated... I'll keep an eye out for her for you.
Oh, it's {PlayerName}, eh? How've you been holding up?
Since you've kept your distance from the Dark Tide, how're things? The bow, the girl... those daydreams of yours get any better?
Kept my distance? I even went right back into it.
Daydreams? You still don't seem to remember Iuno.
Have you seen a girl with dark blue ponytails?
Hmm, let me think. Plenty of fresh faces here. But dark blue ponytails... Ah, I think I saw a girl like that!
She walked like a cat, as nimble as they come... Seems she was looking for someone, too? She was just over there...
I'll head there now!
Come on over! Toast!
Let's drink till we drop!
We should just live in the moment and enjoy what we have now...
That's more like it!
Come, triumphant rain of petals...
Make it even grander...
(Didn't you tell me we would meet at the very end? Then why can't I find you...)
I could hear your voice from a distance, "Iuno, Iuno!" Wasn't that it?
Seems like you're in an awful hurry to find someone.
You little... Do you know how worried I was?
Back to cracking jokes. Guess we're good now.
I thought you'd like this, us slipping back into our old, familiar rhythm... Now you know I'm still me. And yes, I really am back.
Exactly. See? I come right away and stand before you, in the flesh.
Okay, now's the time to talk.
It's just like you saw at the end of the Chaos. Three years ago, at the end of the spring basin swallowed by the Dark Tide, I, as a Priestess, made my choice.
I was so done with just being dragged along by the moon's whims... So I defied fate, severed the path, and became the arrow that struck at destiny itself.
After that, I lost the ability to see clear visions of the future, but in return, I gained the power to anchor the Dark Tide's creations.
With that, the last prophecy I saw changed slightly. In a squad doomed to fall, one survived—Harelius.
If I can do it once, then I can do it a second time, then a third... Perhaps one day, I can overturn more destined futures.
Since fate didn't prepare a Hero of Heroes, we decided to eliminate the need for one by taking on the disaster at its source—the Sovereign and the Paradise.
This is the plan Augusta and I made, though I did hide the teeny tiny cost.
Anyway, all the Septimontians who were supposed to die are still alive. The end I once foresaw has changed. The meaning of this has already transcended my own existence.
So then, even if every trace of my "existence" was erased, who can say that the altered fate I left behind isn't proof of my existence?
More importantly, I had the privilege of standing by your side to witness what lies beyond the end. The void. An unwritten... void. Perhaps it signifies the unimaginable possibilities yet to come.
Let's make sure there's no next time.
Why, sacrificing myself? Or just trying something I'm not sure about?
Do the people remember you now?
But, at least... you still remember me. You pulled me from the Chaos and brought me back to existence. That's enough.
Oh, I'm certain Augusta and I, along with the rest of them, will be thick as thieves again, this time creating new futures. You really shouldn't underestimate my charm!
Oh yes, and this bracelet...
This is the second time I've given this to you. Never mind the first time, but I wouldn't refuse a second time, if I were you.
Being the second time means there's been a change... Now, it's a testament to our secret little interactions. I've Anchored the world, and you, you've Anchored me.
As for any matter pertaining to me... What you saw in the Chaos and what transpired, do not breathe a word of it to another soul. Understand?
Feeling bashful all of a sudden?
It will be our little secret then.
That so? I'll keep it in mind.
Hmph, bashful? Hardly! If you blurt it out, it would cause quite a stir. All that explaining would be too much hassle.
Besides, to them, I am... quite the anomaly. If the truth came out, the first reaction would be shock.
You think so too? Okay. Good. I'm most relieved.
You think so too? Okay. Good. I'm most relieved.
Well, then again, this is a perfect opportunity to start anew.
In Septimont, it would be a crime to miss the height of the celebration.
Your disappearance.
Just like you, bringing unknown possibilities to Septimont... and to me.
Come now, you know me... I follow my whims. And the more I trust someone, the harder it is to keep my impulses in check.
I'm not one to make promises I can't keep, but I'll promise you this... if there is a next time, you'll be the first to know.
And when I do, you'll get the full story. No holding back.
I've run into a few friends since being back. Not one of them recognized me.
Guess the memory of the Iuno they once knew is just... the price we had to pay.
After fighting side by side, we share honey and wine under a rain of petals, drinking to our hearts' content... Surely you've heard of this little tradition of ours, haven't you, Unwritten One?
Come on, let's go. Together... to be drenched in those rose petals that smell of glory and triumph.

You search the crowd, but she's nowhere to be found... A flicker of doubt crosses your mind. Didn't she promise to "meet you in the very end"? Then, under a beam of moonlight, a hand gently taps your shoulder. In that familiar, playful way, Iuno greets you. She's back, whole and real, and she begins to tell you everything—what happened three years ago, and what brought her here now.

She explains that as a Priestess, she grew tired of simply watching. She broke free from fate's decree and became the arrow that defied it. Her disappearance was just part of the cost to anchor herself and rewrite what was meant to be. Now, you've given Septimont a future unwritten, and given her one too. 

As a gift, she gives you the Lunarum bracelet you returned once again. Besides you, the world may still have forgotten her, but she still has her present and her future. And that's enough. As the celebration reaches its peak, Iuno takes your hand and leads you into a glorious shower of petals.
(Accept the bracelet and put it on.)
(Accept the bracelet and put it away.)
Iuno.
Of course, only you would be the exception.
So you've known this all along...
A death that shouldn't have happened, traded for an unforetold victory. A fair deal.
Now... I am but a fading sliver of moonlight.
I'm sorry, but...
Even I fear being...
Forgotten...
Huh? The Unwritten One is back here too?
So you noticed it too. We're not the only ones who returned to this world… it is back as well.
You mean… the Lunarum Bough?
But I'm pretty sure I cut it down.
Yes, but since we managed to get the stalled flow of causality moving again, bringing a broken branch back to life can't be that hard, right?
I've got this feeling that with it, we can jump into a new kind of Chaos again and again... one that we Anchored and manifested into this world.
For a while, the old Chaos realm was the only place where I could put my past to rest. Honestly… it kind of makes me want to go in and try again.
Hey, {PlayerName}, you alright? You've been standing here for ages.
So Iuno's really gone? Just like that?
You still remember her too?
Duh! Even though I was snoozing on and off... I still remember everything that went down, crystal clear!
Yeah, totally! We had so much done with her during the hunt trip.
She even invited us to Tetragon Temple to check out the murals. Oh, and we caught that giant blue spiky TD, which led us to that big bad stinky thing...
Yep, and I'm pretty sure she was the one who took that Moon Bow and blasted the Dark Tide wide open! Not you, not anyone else!
And that bracelet, she gave it to us to lure out that nasty big fella... Even asked us to keep it for her...
Iuno said she traded her life for our victory...
Iuno said only I would be the exception...
Iuno said she didn't want to be forgotten...
Iuno once said she glimpsed the end, where she would be the last one standing. But now, this end never came... and Iuno is dead.
Is this the cost of changing destiny? Did she know she'd disappear, but accepted it anyway?
Why am I special? Why has everyone forgotten everything about Iuno except me?
But if I'm the exception, if I'm the only one who still remembers... does that mean there's something I can do about it?
She didn't even get to finish her sentence. What was she thinking? Why did she do it... If this is the end, maybe I'll never know.
Yeah, I know what you mean... Like, we didn't even get to have a proper goodbye!
I can't accept this as the end.
I need to know how it all happened.
I don't care if Iuno foresaw her fate and chose this path for herself.
All I know is I won't let it end like this. Not with her fading into oblivion.
Why did Iuno choose this? Did she truly believe this was the better ending?
I'm the one she entrusted with her bracelet. The exception. So it's on me to find the answer.
Like Augusta said, everything that exists leaves a trace. Since she's a Priestess, I'm sure to find traces of her in Tetragon Temple.
A lead could be the breakthrough I need.
That's the spirit! Look at ya, {PlayerName}, snapping out of that funk! Knew you'd be back at it soon enough!
You told me the first time you met Iuno was in the arena, right? She scared the toga off that other team with just a few words. Intimidating stuff. But when I actually met her, she was...
She only seems like she has an attitude.
She's unexpectedly open and straightforward.
We faced the Sovereign's ambush together, too.
So it doesn't matter whatever anyone thinks, or... or what happened to her. You remember her, and I do too! It wasn't some made-up crap!
I still got some kinks to work out before I'm in my Super Echo Abby form, but you can bet I'll be here...
Remembering everything that happens. We'll figure something out, whatever it takes! Even when I'm just riding along, I'm in this with you, pal.

You're unable to accept Iuno's disappearance, but doubt flickers through your mind... Was it all an illusion? Now that even Iuno's last sliver of moonlight fades, your memories are the only proof she ever existed. Abby reassures you that it also remembers everything about Iuno and all the moments you shared. As the only exception left, you refuse to accept this ending. You decide to search Tetragon Temple for any remaining traces of her.
(Strange... Lillibet and the other Priestesses aren't here. The Temple seems empty.)
(Hmm? Iuno's bracelet is shining? The light is... pointing at a wall?)
Where could this lead?
You stand in silence before a wall covered in markings. Like a shore shaped by the rising tide, it bears the brushstrokes of fate.
Guided by the light and fate above, the Priestesses of Tetragon Temple share the futures they've glimpsed, be it through carvings, scrolls, or spoken word... through every means imaginable.
Huh? The mural changed.
You pause facing a wall covered in markings.

At first, the room is dim. The Priestesses sit quietly, troubled by something unseen. But as you draw closer, whether by your presence, your touch, or something else, Iuno appears on the wall, resonating with the moon.
Light spills forth. The prodigy from prophecy leaves behind a glowing revelation for the Priestesses.
Is this rewriting what was, or revealing what should have been?
You pause, facing a wall covered in markings.

At first, the image is faded and hard to read. But as you draw closer, whether by your presence, your touch, or something else, Iuno's figure appears in place of the Priestess delivering the prophecy.
Now you see the False Sovereign corrupted by the Dark Tide, the new Hero of Heroes, and the blank, unwritten space spreading from the center.
Heh, heh heh... trapped in your own pathetic shell, and you still think you're the king of the world...
Who? Who's there... Is it you? Show yourself! Yes... Yes! I've been waiting for this moment!
Tch. It's you.
The person I need to lure fails to show, and now you're here to mock me, is that it?
I don't care for punching down.
How did you end up like this?
You speak so innocently, as if my being here...
Wasn't all your doing.
You brought me to Tetragon Temple to try to erase me from the story. All so you could summon the one behind it all.
I played along... I agreed to be "watched" here because I wanted to see him. Wanted to look him in the eye.
But now it's clear we'll both be disappointed. I am fate's discarded pawn, and he couldn't care less what happens to me.
Are you saying this was our plan?
Ha, there's no one else here. No need to put on an act.
(He doesn't look like he's lying, but this is the first time I've been here. Priestesses, Tetragon Temple... Could this be Iuno's doing?)
(For Avidius here, Iuno has also never existed. Whatever she did in the past is now my doing. That's why he thinks I'm behind all this.)
I was just testing you.
I thought you might have more to say to me.
Ha... Hahaha... At this point, what do I have left to hide?
I always thought I was the hero who conquered Manes Deep. The one more worthy of ruling than even Augusta.

Until the day I led the charge to Murmurstown, determined to stop my comrades from falling to the Dark Tide and prove I had what it took to be king. I walked to the door I had passed a thousand times only to find—
Did I even come here before? When did I conquer this place, and with whom?
At that moment, I realized so much was blank. Disconnected dots, scattered and meaningless.
How pitiful everyone knows my deeds, yet no one can explain how. And I can't find a single soul who's actually witnessed my so-called exploits.
It makes no sense, but everyone takes it for granted.
It's like someone implanted fake memories into your head.
Yes, so I tore through my memories until I saw a hand holding a feathered quill. It wrote everything about me from the moment I was born.
And I realized an undeniable truth. Existence is anchored in connection, feeling, and memory. They are its very manifestation.
If someone uses their Resonance ability to fabricate a memory of the Hero of Heroes everyone expects, and convinces them it's real... does such a fabricated person really exist?
And what of you, the one they call the Unwritten One？
An undefined, unknowable void that can anchor unimaginable connections. Imagine the existence that could emerge!
Anchoring and manifesting existence? What are you...
Enough. You arrogant fool. I did not allow you to stay here so you could defile fate with your delusions.
Please excuse this disturbance, {PlayerName}. Whatever you need to say, we'll discuss it back in the hall.
A dead end. Nothing was ever there.

You don't expect to meet Avidius in the depths of Tetragon Temple, but he seems unfazed by your arrival. It becomes clear that Avidius, too, has forgotten Iuno, convinced that the plan she once shared with him was actually between you and him, devised to draw out the hidden Quillbearer. Avidius, as it turns out, isn't a person in the usual sense, but a being created by the Quillbearer's Forte to resemble a Hero of Heroes. If connection, feeling, and memory were enough to anchor Avidius into existence... could the same be done for Iuno? Just then, Lillibet arrives to interrupt the conversation.
Still here? You'd really rather walk beside a fabrication like me?
Or... did my words inspire you? I hope you act on them. I am most eager to see how that ends.
Why keep saying things you don't mean?
But you hate what those hands did to you.
Am I supposed to forget everything? Join your little celebration, play the perfect noble again, and act like I was ever real?
Once you've seen the line between what's real and what isn't, you cannot go back. Don't you understand that?
You let Avidius's words hang in the air. You have no answer to give, not yet. But at the mention of the celebration, you remember the petals Bruno gave you to hand out.
(Offer the petals to Avidius)
(Decide not to give Avidius the petals)
Heh… What is this? You know I can't… I'm not…

You don't offer the petals to change his mind. But maybe he'll understand what the gesture means—the celebration was never about any one person. It's for everyone who joined the hunt, Avidius included.
It's better not to give him the petals. This might not be what he needs, and it's not your place to decide that for him. Maybe when he's ready to face what comes next, you can talk again.
Iuno, or perhaps her specter yet to fully return, finds you lost in the Chaos.
Once again, she reaches through the unknown to pull you from the tides of uncertainty. She places the rope that binds you two together back into your hands.
You can't quite understand how she does it... but somehow, once again, she finds you.
Maybe this Chaos isn't that unbearable. After all, you know she will always find you and lead you where you need to go.
I can't see where it ends. Can't tell where I am, either.
Is this the Chaos between life and death, between existence and non-existence?
That's Iuno in the center!
Iuno, are you...
Iuno? You're... calling me? Are you here for me?
Why... would someone be looking for me?
(She looks the same as she did when she faded away... a sliver of moonlight. How long has she been lost in this Chaos?)
I'm sorry. I've come late.
I'm here for you. Everything is going to be okay.
Do you... still remember me?
I know you.
You are... Unwritten. A blank...
An unwritten... blank.
Your new nickname for me?
You can call me whatever you want.
Mmm. Unwritten.
Do you...
I will guide the <ano=you>Unwritten</ano> with the moonlight.
To find more of... me.
(She responded to me... Now she's guiding me.)
(Even if it's just a trace of her, I found her. Now that fragile rope connecting her, me, and the world... is already in my hands.)

Iuno's specter takes shape before you in the Chaos. You don't know how long she's been lost here, but it's clear she's no longer whole. She calls you an "unwritten blank" and reaches out her hand. You're unsure how to anchor Iuno back into existence, but the moment your hands meet, you know it has begun. You've found a trace of Iuno, and now she's guiding you to find the rest.
Guided by the light of fate, we walk the web of futures. Grandmother Lillibet has already prophesied her successor. Iuno, born in a lunar eclipse, will become a "prodigy" Priestess.
Wait, Sibylla's Iuno? I know that girl... wild and dramatic. She's just won a handful of matches.
Do you think she'll really come to Tetragon Temple? Her mother is a former Gladiator champion, and her father a famed blacksmith. She's already from a highly respectable family.
And she is skilled with a bow. Maybe she'll just want to be the next champion, you know? She is spoiled for choice...
The prophecy can't be wrong. Grandmother Lillibet's already seen it!
She'll resonate with the moon's phases... That's a huge honor! Not just anyone can see fate's patterns, and she'll be able to see it more clearly than the rest of us.
It's our duty to share visions of the future to guide Septimont and its people forward. Such glory... She won't refuse, and she shouldn't.
This is the past. Where my existence left its mark.
I see. Grandmother Lillibet said that the key to Anchoring lies in connection and its manifestation. Let's try to find more.

You and Iuno's specter journey deeper into the Chaos, seeing memories of her past unfold around you. From whispers among the Priestesses, you learn of a prophecy tied to her birth. Lillibet once remarked that Iuno, born during a lunar eclipse, was destined to be a prodigy among Priestesses. Whether she would rise as the next great champion or follow the fate written for her, one thing was clear: the bold, willful Iuno was never bound to a single path.
Where are you taking me?
Mmm... Just don't let go of my hand.
I can't see it! It's gone after that... Gone forever... Hah! Just one desecration is enough for the ordinary...
I just wanted to understand! To look at it! To see the blinding flames! I was so close to seeing the outcome, to tracing back the cause!
You... you must be smarter than me, stronger than me... Tell me... Did I do it right?
Staring at the sun, burning with pain for that truth... Tell me, have I gone mad? Is it me who's... gone mad?
Could this be another mark of Iuno's existence?
Let's go before Chaos catches up to us.
We're nearly there.
We were this close to killing that <ano=Dark Tide creation>Tacet Discord</ano>! But then it touched the Dark Tide and just dissolved back into it.
All of 'em are part of it. Wherever the Tide shows, they crawl right out with it. But the second they're spotted, they melt right back in.
You can't track 'em, can't lock 'em down... The only thing that barely reveals them is the moon... What the hell are we supposed to do?
You can't track 'em, can't lock 'em down... The only thing that barely reveals them is the moon... What the hell are we supposed to do?
We keep moving. No matter what, we move forward. Until we can't anymore.
Alexandros, you're not falling here. Not now!
Fighting the Dark Tide is the mission you were born for. The one you should be proud of.
Fear not, Andrius. The Priestesses already spoke of our victory.
They can't see everything, but when they do, they're always right.
We found a way to handle the Tacet Discords through their prophecy, didn't we?
Sibylla, wait!
Spare me your words! The entire western defense rests on us. Do you have a better plan?
As for death... Of course I want to live. I fight not with death in mind, but victory!
Yet, if glory and death come hand in hand, so be it. Let the bells toll, and mourn me when the time comes.
Until that moment, I will not stop.
Are you crazy? Charging off alone is walking to your death! Think about your daughter, she's still waiting for you!
Do you want to say something to her?
So, Sibylla's Iuno, am I correct?
What's happened is done... It can't be changed.
Is this... how it was...?
Or... is this just my imagination?
Those who closed their eyes never truly saw... So, this isn't really her.

Your anchoring with Iuno continues. In another memory, you witness a female Gladiator charging into a battlefield corrupted by the Dark Tide. From her name and title, you sense her connection to Iuno, but when you suggest approaching her, Iuno's specter refuses. These visions in the Chaos aren't entirely real—they're shaped by Iuno's own memories and perceptions. For someone who once kept her eyes closed to the truth, she can neither see things as they truly were nor change what has already passed. You see deep pain in her eyes.
Thank you, Unwritten.
Stay close to me.
Mm, I won't let go. I don't want to let go.
Iuno!
Is that...
Ah, there you are. Been waiting for you, Iuno.
...Iuno?
You can see her?
What's the surprise? You're Iuno, aren't ya? Been hammerin' away at this bow for you long enough. If I couldn't call you by name now, well, that'd be a proper surprise.
Her? Is there anyone else besides you here, Iuno?
(Maybe it's because I'm Anchored to Iuno?)
(Here, I really am Iuno.)
So, you came for the bow I promised you, eh? Still want it?
Why wouldn't I want it?
Should I want it?
Is the bow really that important?
Ha! Right you are. Why wouldn't you want it? But once you take it, what then?
That's not a question for me. That's a question for yourself.
What truly counts as "important"? Even the finest bow or sword... is just a weapon. Doesn't matter much if you don't use it in a fight.
I reckon you've heard Lillibet's prophecy, haven't you? What do you think?
I can't picture you as one of those serious Priestesses in the Temple... stuck in there with your scrolls and your candles and your tablets. Doesn't seem right for someone with a spirit like yours.
And if you really did become a Priestess... well, this bow wouldn't be of much use, would it? No time for it.
But you've got a gift that other Priestesses could only dream of. Such a shame to waste it... And the warriors of Septimont need their Priestesses, so do Septimont's Auguries.
Lillibet and the others still fail to foresee the entirety of the coming disaster.
(Of all times, Iuno chooses now to go silent...)

Aye, well, it's not my place to say. You make up your own mind, and that's all that matters. As for me? I make weapons. If you still want the bow, I'll forge it for you. But the materials... Well, you'll have to gather those yourself.
Materials? What do you mean?
Heh, forgetful today, are we? Didn't you say you wanted to craft a bow from your favorite Lunarum Bough?
Truth be told, making a bow isn't all that different from making anything else. You learn as much as you can, repeat it often enough, until you've shaped it just right.
From nothing to something, to its final existence... that's how it's always been, eh? But like I said, if you still want it, you'll need to gather the materials first.
When you've gathered enough Lunarum Bough, you'll get your bow.
And if you're not sure where to look for it...
There, see it? Just head that way and you'll see!

You continue forward and meet a blacksmith who mistakes you for Iuno, perhaps a result of the anchoring. He asks whether you still plan to become a Priestess or choose another path, but offers no advice. Instead, he reminds you of the bow you once asked him to craft. Like anything else, creation takes knowledge and the right steps to take form. He tells you that if you can gather enough Lunarum Bough, he'll forge the bow for you, and then opens a path deeper into the Chaos.
Lunarum Bough... that's what the blacksmith mentioned. Looks just like what was used for your bow.
…Mm.
Up ahead, it looks like... two chairs?
Sitting just like that, huh? You're still just as... spontaneous.
Shh, Unwritten.
It's time for a rest. Come sit with me.
We rest to manifest what we've already found.
I've never said it properly before, and I don't know if you fully understand it now... but now that I've found you, I will bring you back. I won't stop until I do.
Because you said it, I believe you.
"Come on! Don't bore me this quickly. Show me what other tricks you've got up your sleeve."
"Victory? That's the only befitting outcome."
"Getting whatever she wants, doing whatever she sets her mind to... Are you talking about me? Very well, I'll prove you right."
"That... that was..."
You look like you're recovering.
Exactly. After manifestation, this is how I can absorb more.
Only then can I find… a more complete me.
Manifest? How?
So after experiencing and feeling all that, you need to rest... among Lunarum Boughs, to make what's Anchored become a part of you?
Unwritten, you... are a clever one.
"Now spare me the words. I know I'll be first."
"This is only the beginning. Soon... I'll be an even greater warrior than Mother ever was."
"Prodigy, you say? If you want to call me that... I'll gladly take it."
"But why are you so certain... that who you see is me?"
"Huh? They're gone now..."
"...Because this is fate's will. It has favored me more than others."
"...Because I can see what others cannot. Only I can see farther... But..."
Chaos won't disturb us here.

You reach a shallow pool and sit down to rest beside Iuno's specter. Her bracelet begins to glow, releasing memories of the past: A young Iuno celebrates a victory gladiating and runs into her mother's arms, only to see her consumed by the Dark Tide. She wonders why fate chose her, and what the cost truly was. The memory ends suddenly. From the pool, golden Lunarum Bough begins to grow, and Iuno's specter becomes a little more whole. Anchoring her back into existence is working.
Follow the foretold fate
"As the prophecy says, I cannot waste my talents. I will not turn a blind eye to misfortune. Since only I can do this, I'll be the one to see it through!"
"A Gladiator or Priestess, what does it matter? I'll face fate and see just how far I can go!"
"Let's go. Forget the prophecies, forget being a Priestess. Let's do what we truly want. If the future is a question, the answer's never in what others define."
"If we don't want to walk a determined path, then let's steer clear and try something we've never even seen before."
Ignore the foretold fate
Anchoring cannot continue.
There are countless possibilities, but what's done is done. Only one past can bring you to the present you seek.

The light from the bracelet leads you to two doors. To accept the fate that was seen, or turn away from it. To face a predetermined path, or hide from it. The possibilities are endless. But like Iuno once did, you know you must make a choice.
We can't continue the Anchoring.
The past folds over itself, leaving behind a faint trail of wrong choices on the shoals of Chaos.

What's done is done, yet you still have the chance to begin anew.
This time, you've turned away from a wrong choice.
(Follow the foretold fate.)
"As the prophecy says, I cannot waste my talents. I will not turn a blind eye to misfortune. Since only I can do this, I'll be the one to see it through!"
"A Gladiator or Priestess, what does it matter? I'll face fate and see just how far I can go!"
Back then, it seems you didn't mind giving prophecies. The people were much closer to you than they are now.
Over there. That was my divination altar.
They're waiting for the Priestess's words. I must... go and deliver it.
The Anchoring is still working. This looks like a memory from when you became a Priestess.
Isn't that... the agora in Aeterna Square? I think I'd like to see it.
There's no one by that altar...
Isn't the Priestess supposed to give us a prophecy there?
I'm dying here!
I need to know what happens!
But... I'm also afraid of what that will mean...
Every Priestess has her limit.
But this one seems to see everything...
When I see her, do I just hand her the focus item?
Huh, you look unfamiliar. Not from Septimont, I take it?
Iuno... have you returned to your true form?
Not bad. You even bothered to learn my name.
An outlander coming all this way, seeking the most gifted Priestess—me—just to beg for answers about the future.
Hmm? What's this about? How dreadfully complicated... But I suppose I can't fault your luck, finding your way to me.
They say a Priestess can't see everything, but when she does, she's always right. But I'm different. I can see everything, and I'm always right.
Even when I'm not in the Temple bathed in flame, I've more than enough power to see your future. So far, nothing's happened that I didn't already foresee.
Now, hand over whatever item you've brought. I'll see what's been bothering you.
I didn't bring anything.
I don't have time for this. I'm trying to...
Oh? That's alright. I hope you're okay with me freestyling it then.
Shh, quiet please... And don't you dare look away. I'm about to...
What? I see... a void?
I can't see your past. I can't see your present... and your future... How can this be?!
Like you said, I'm the Unwritten One.
You can't see everything now, can you?
Unsurprising, considering we're not technically alive.
The Unwritten One. Why is that familiar... Who exactly are you?
You! You... No, it can't be. Let me try again—
Think you're funny, hmm? We're both sitting here, perfectly normal. If this isn't alive, then—
{PlayerName}? You... why are you here? Isn't this... Aeterna Square?

Did something happen in Septimont? Is it Augusta or the others? No, that's impossible... I should've disappeared by now. Why do I feel so tired? Like I'm walking the same path, over and over again without end...
Why do I see so many memories from the past? My mother, the other Priestesses... and you. You've done something for me, haven't you?
Yes. We're in the Chaos now.
But you shouldn't be here. Neither should I. Why haven't I disappeared completely?
Why did you sacrifice yourself? Why did you just leave without a word? Was this really the outcome the most gifted Priestess chose for herself?
Because this was the best I could do for Septimont.

Destruction, failure, oblivion... the Dark Tide devours everything you can imagine. The Gryphons can't escape it. The Gladiators can't defeat it. In the blink of an eye, before we could even react, it had already enveloped everything.
I knew it from the start.
I knew three years ago, I would turn everything I am into the Moon Arrow that would pin down the Sovereign. I just didn't know when that day would come, or if it would be enough...
Until I saw you. You, the one who stood between me and the manipulating hand behind everything. Just like the faint light I once saw in the future.
I finally understand. My defiance, my sacrilege... it was all worth it. Now I... I found the answer.
So you're just giving up?
Let me show you what a better outcome looks like.
Whether it's because of the void I carry, or whatever else it may be, I still remember you. Your place in this world isn't over yet.
I'm taking you out of this realm of Chaos.
You...
Seems like I missed something. Something I didn't foresee. So, the Unwritten One from the future isn't happy with the ending I've changed and wants to rewrite it...
The battle's still undecided. The war isn't finished yet, is that it?
Yes. You traded your existence to alter the prophecy. But I'll Anchor your existence and rewrite your ending.
If I've ever guided you before, then now, let me guide you one more time.
Really?
I'll entrust myself to you, then.
But be careful, {PlayerName}. Don't get lost in the Chaos. And I shall put my best foot forward as well... We shall meet at the very end.
Wait... Am I Iuno now?
Ah. You're still not fully recovered...
More like I've come to beg for answers about the past.

The moment you sit at the divination altar, everything around you shifts. You find yourself in what appears to be a moment of the past, face-to-face with a living Iuno who's caught in a looping memory. She reaches for your hand to read your fate, but the instant your fingers touch, her lost memories come rushing back. Why are you here? And why hasn't she vanished from existence?

Realizing you entered Chaos to help her, Iuno chooses to go along with your attempt to rewrite her ending. She promises to meet you again at the very end. As her voice fades into the air, your vision shifts once more. This time, it feels like you have truly become Iuno.
Hello, Priestess. Uh... I've got the item here with me. I hope you can take a look for me.
What do you want with Iuno... I mean, what is it?
I can't promise anything, but show it to me.
My squad and I were once ambushed in Cassos. A monstrous Tacet Discord never seen before appeared in the Dark Tide.
I seek guidance on what comes next. Will we have the strength to battle it?
(Are these the types of visions Iuno sees?)
(The broken horn, the spear piercing through the eye... Victory, cheering, you... and the other Gladiators... There's blood, but they all survive...)
(Objectively recount what you saw.)
(Consider the potential possibilities.)
(A Priestess would probably relay her visions as they were, without any omissions or additions.)
(Seeing the outcome gives new information. Now, their future is both certain and uncertain. Knowing it ahead of time lets them prepare, and with that, gain the upper hand.)
...The beast falls, and we are cheering. Its eye is pierced by a spear, its horn is broken... So that's its weak spot. Is that the key to our victory?
Thank you, Priestess Iuno! Your words put my mind at ease.
Can I... come see you again once it's all over?

As Priestess Iuno of the past, you sit on the altar offering prophecies to those who seek guidance. 

The first to come is Harelius, a Gladiator in search of strategic insight for his squad and their mission to confront a monstrous Tacet Discord never before seen in the Dark Tide.
The second to come is Samara, a lovestruck woman holding a bracelet. She...
The third to come is Nikolas, a noble youth desperate to outwit fate. He...
The fourth to come is Maia, a young, innocent girl. She..
Phew... Oh, Priestess, is it true that if I give you the right thing, you can see everything?
(Reply confidently. Iuno would do the same.)
(Reply cautiously. Insights depend on the situation.)
Wow, you're amazing! I can tell you're different from all the other Priestesses!
You look so serious... but everyone says you're the most powerful Priestess. If it's not you, I don't know who else to ask.
Look, Grandpa made this bottle. Can you see where he went? And what did he turn into?
I want to find him quickly. He left so fast... he must've forgotten to tell me!
(It's dark... Nothing but darkness. I don't see anything. What does it mean?)
(Recount what you saw truthfully.)
I see. The Priestesses at the Temple said they saw the same thing.
They said when someone dies, their light goes out... and everything left is just pitch black, nobody can see anything anymore.
So your grandfather is already...
Yes. Grandpa was really sick and he... died.
But it's okay! He made me promise that if he ever wasn't here anymore, I'd put all my tears in this bottle.
One day when the tears dry up, we'll see each other again!
So I don't cry anymore. I'm worried it'll take a really, really long time to see him again... Just how long exactly? What will Grandpa look like then?
I can be forgetful sometimes... What if I don't recognize him, what then?!
(Tell her a kind lie wrapped in the illusion of prophecy.)
(Tell her the real truth beyond any prophecy.)
Wait... I see a flicker of light in the dark. It's one of your favorite things... it's...
A butterfly! I love butterflies!
Yes. When your tears dry, your grandfather will return to you as a butterfly. When he does, you'll know it's him.
Thank you! Priestess, I knew you could do it... Even if nobody else believed me, I just knew there would be someone who could see!
...I don't believe it. I don't believe you! Grandpa didn't lie to me!
Grandpa wouldn't lie to me... I must've given you the wrong thing. Or maybe you're just not as powerful as they say you are!
I believed in all of you Priestesses, that's why I came! But you... don't believe me. It doesn't matter if you can see or not! I'm not giving up!

As Priestess Iuno of the past, you sit on the altar offering prophecies to those who seek guidance. 

The fourth to come is Maia, a young, innocent girl carrying a glass bottle filled with tears over an impossible promise made by her ailing grandfather. Will you comfort her with a kind lie, letting her believe he will return when the tears dry, or tell her the harsh truth that he's gone?
I have a little trick I'd like to pull off, regarding a life. That's why I've come to you, Priestess Iuno. I'm curious if your prophecy can confirm whether it's possible.
A trick? A Priestess's visions don't deal in trivialities.
Let's hear it. What do you want me to do?
Don't be so hasty to dismiss me. What if the trick I wish to pull off is against fate itself?
Have you never questioned whether it could be deceived or defied?
I speak of fate, of course.
These figurines I brought were crafted by my family for me and my brother, as a rite of passage. They're made in our likeness.
We're twins, but we walked two very different paths. Me, books and knowledge, and him, weapons and strength.
By chance, I learned my brother's fate in Tetragon Temple. Destined to die this summer at the hands of a Tacet Discord. They couldn't see my fate, so here I am now.
I want to see whether fate will once again lead me down a path opposite my brother?
(An older, more aged Nikolas... peaceful... Dead at fifty? No, at least sixty...)
(Recount exactly what you saw.)
(Probe into his intentions first.)
...So I'm right! Hahaha, see! Kyrion, my brother... What did I tell you!
...We were born identical, after all. I know him well. If I wanted to imitate him, even our parents wouldn't be able to tell us apart. But fate? What would it do?
You've shown me my end. I will live to become an old man. That means this summer I won't die.
What if I take Kyrion's place in the battle? And he plays the part of Nikolas, sailing across the seas? I'll confuse the whole world, even fate itself...
Let me try. I'll use fate's prophecy to overturn another, and trick death with the undying!
Bold. I don't hate it.
Who knows, it might work.

As Priestess Iuno of the past, you sit on the altar offering prophecies to those who seek guidance. 

The third to come is Nikolas, a noble youth desperate to outwit fate. Another Priestess has prophesied that his twin brother will die at the hands of a beast this summer. But you foresee Nikolas living to old age. He wonders: if he takes his brother's place in battle, can he cheat death? Can one prophecy cancel another?
The fourth to come is Maia, a young, innocent girl. She...
Priestess Iuno? I'm here with a bracelet my betrothed gave me.
I feel like it best captures his feelings for me.
Perhaps... our future together will be one of true love? Where we grow old together?
(Pain or conflict... confusion, shattered hopes... They don't look that old. Not much time has passed... Is that their child?)
(It's not as clear as the last one. All I can tell is that their love doesn't end well. But it's obvious she's hoping for a better ending.)
(Speak the truth about what you saw.)
(Offer hints to leave space for her to choose her path.)
(A happy ending gives peace. A painful one serves as a warning. Both hold meaning. The rest... is in her hands.)
...You're saying we won't be together forever? That it ends... badly? Are you sure you're not mistaken?
