We met at the academy, how could we drift apart? I... I don't believe it. Surely there's some explanation?
You said we had a child. Maybe he was just going on a trip. Maybe it wasn't a permanent separation.
(If a Priestess's vision is never wrong, then telling her won't change a thing. But what if it's the act of telling her this prophecy that causes that ending?)
(She should decide the path she wants, regardless of the outcome. I'll just let her enjoy the present.)
...So, not much else to see? You want me to focus on the present... Well, we are very happy now. I... feel very lucky.
I really never thought we'd end up together. We've known each other for a long time, but we're both so strong-willed... I came here because I was worried about our future.
What matters is that we're in love now. Whatever comes, I don't want to let him go.
And thank you, Priestess Iuno. No matter what, thank you.

As Priestess Iuno of the past, you sit on the altar offering prophecies to those who seek guidance. 

The second to come is Samara, a lovestruck woman. She presents a betrothal bracelet from her fiancé, hoping you can foresee whether their love will endure forever.
The third to come is Nikolas, a noble youth desperate to outwit fate. He...
The fourth to come is Maia, a young, innocent girl. She...
We followed the prophecy, and we won. But when I see Borde's shattered leg, I can't shake the thought... Was there another way?
If we hadn't followed the prophecy, or if I'd chosen someone else to wield the spear, would Borde not have gotten hurt?
As the prophecy foretold, I cut the Tacet Discords' retreat. And as the prophecy foretold, I will never return to my homeland again.
You who watch fate unfold, do you know the weight of life and death?
For three weeks, I removed everything that could catch fire! I couldn't have been more careful!
Damn that leak, damn that peddler... The fire still started, just like the prophecy said...
Thank the mercy of fate, and thank that Priestess. I'd already... let go of hope.
But she saw the path that would lead me to my lost child. She was there, in the forest, by the spring.
"I... I understand. It's because I understand that I hope I can make a difference."
"What is meant to happen will happen. There's no avoiding it. There is no such thing as a perfect prophecy, nor is there... true completeness."
"Is that so? Then all is well. If what I see can help even one, then I will keep my eyes open, until the very end."
Let's rest here, one more time.
Anchor these memories and connections. Make them a part of you.
I can see further than anyone else. I can see things no one else can...
So why... why, at the moment I should've seen the clearest, did I close my eyes and shut it out?
After that, I decided to keep my eyes wide open, no matter the cost.
I'll sit at the crossroads of fate. I'll stare into what's to come and not flinch, be it joyful, tragic, rebirth, destruction...
Until I see it all. Until I know everything.
Because I'm stronger than anyone else. This is something only I can do. But—
"If the Priestess's prophecies were really perfect, we could avoid all misfortune..."
"If there is such a thing as fate, then misfortunes cannot be avoided..."
"Just because you know the outcome, doesn't mean the journey isn't worth it!"
"If life is destined to follow a predetermined path, does it even matter if we know our fate?"
After all I see... could I ever answer what they hope of me?
Does glimpsing one's fate really matter?
I understand why you stopped offering prophecies.
You weren't sure if seeing the future alone was really enough.
Unwritten... You are as sharp as ever.
Seeing is simple. But facing what you see isn't.
In your eyes, I see my past self. I also see my present self. Together, they overlap to create a more complete version of me.
I've seen things others can't begin to imagine.
I was so close... If I hadn't... closed my eyes...
I would've learned the causal chain, and I could've stopped it.

Light streams from the bracelet. You've learned how to draw out Iuno's memories, and you wait as they reveal more of her hidden past. The girl who should have watched her mother's death unfold instinctively chose to shut her eyes. After losing the chance to change anything, she vowed to see everything from then on, no matter the cost. That vow led her to become a Priestess. But after countless prophecies, she began to question whether "seeing" truly meant understanding. The Lunarum Bough continues to grow, and the Iuno beside you slowly becomes more whole.
I know Grandpa won't come back. When you die, you die. Some things can't be changed, no matter how much we want to fight.
The tears in the bottle have dried, and I'm not that little girl anymore.

Kyrion set sail across the sea only to meet his end at the hands of a Tacet Discord, and I... believing in my own prophecy, took his place in battle. I was gravely wounded and now am but a living corpse.
The prophecy said I can live to 50 or even 60, but now I have to spend all those years in a broken shell of a body. Those who think they can cheat fate will find themselves thoroughly deceived.
Gustavus left me and little Chiani... Hah, I knew it all along, didn't I? Who ever really has forever, anyway?
But at least I had those moments with him, so full of passion. I've learned to live in the now, even if now means feeling the sting of his loss.
Still giving prophecies, Iuno?
Like the first time we met on the plains, you told me you saw a glory as bright as the sun. One that would earn me respect.
Truth be told, I didn't think much of your words back then.
When I want something, no one's permission is needed. Nothing could stand between me and my goal.
When the prophecy came true though, I found it... unsatisfying.
Imagine thinking you are the master of your own fate, only to learn, for better or for worse, everything you are is part of fate's design.
It's as if fate chips away at the untamed part of you, turning you from a wolf into a caged rabbit.
And you... you saw it all so easily. Truths as clear as the moonlight. Bright, yet distant and cold.
If that's the case, why did you seek out the Priestess?
I know you are not one to believe in prophecies.
Don't mistake me. I don't dismiss the value of prophecy.
No, quite the opposite. I do recognize the Priestesses' abilities.
Seeing the outcome gives us insight. Prophecies allow us to envision the future and find better ways to face it.
In every one of Septimont's Auguries, the Priestesses foresaw disasters that would befall the land, but also the hero who would rise up to face it.
Like the people of Septimont, I too have been blessed by prophecy. But in the end, whether disaster is averted or who the hero is... those choices are never ours.
If we are nothing more than fate's puppets, what difference does it make if we can see its hand?
If fate one day wills our annihilation, with no way to change it, what then is the role of a Priestess?
Are they merely fate's mouthpiece, bowing to its will? Or... are they pioneers, seeking to shape what's to come?
Is this about Septimont's Auguries?
Be straight with me. What really brings you here?
Last night, Grandmother Lillibet told me another Septimont Augury had emerged. This one revealed a future unseen, a warning long overdue...
An unknown disaster that would bring about the end of Septimont.
The vision was unclear. The Priestess couldn't discern the cause of the disaster, nor could they see the hero who would rise up to stop it.
The Senate prefers to wait, believing the solution will reveal itself in time. But I must consider the darker possibility.

I know that you'd rather be out there dealing with living, breathing people than confined to the Temple to await some grand future. You, too, are tired of the Senate's rules and the Priestesses' chains.
But as a prodigy in prophecy, you should see further than Lillibet or any of the other Priestesses.
Would you dare, with no direction, no clues, and not a single focus item, gaze upon Septimont's end and trace its cause?
Agree to Augusta's proposal. Search for Septimont's ending.
Reject Augusta's proposal. Wait for time to reveal more insights.
"So be it. I'll make this prophecy's ending my answer."
"End or future... If I can break through the maze and find the Hero of Heroes they could not, I won't need to worry about the meaning of what I see. I will be the meaning I see."
"Countless souls have come to me for prophecies, and I've never held back. But in the end, all I do is relay what I see, down to the smallest detail."
"Whether I intervene or not, what's destined to happen will come to pass. If we are but fate's puppets, what difference does it make if we see the future?"
Anchoring cannot continue.
There are countless possibilities, but what's done is done. Only one past can bring you to the present you seek.

You encounter Augusta in the Chaos who mistakes you for Iuno, like the others you've met. She poses a difficult question: when fate offers no solution and only promises annihilation, what then is the role of a Priestess? Would you dare, with no direction or clues, gaze upon Septimont's destruction and trace its cause? You understand your answer doesn't matter. What matters is how Iuno would answer that question.
We can't continue the Anchoring.
The past folds itself, and in it, you see yourself bidding Augusta farewell before stepping into the wrong choice beside Iuno.
But, just like last time, you now know where you should go.
Once again, I repeat Iuno's past choice.
Would you dare, with no direction, no clues, and not a single focus item, gaze upon Septimont's end and trace its cause?
(Agree to Augusta's proposal. Search for Septimont's ending.)
"So be it. I'll make this prophecy's ending my answer."
"End or future... If I can break through the maze and find the Hero of Heroes they could not, I won't need to worry about the meaning of what I see. I will be the meaning I see."
Over there, it looks familiar... Perhaps we can stop to take a breath and rest, if only for a moment.
You think there are Lunarum Boughs?
I don't know, but something about it is different.
I must've been there before and done something... something important.
None of the other places felt like this.
But why is it so ruined, so silent? There should be people, and more light, like how it was when it all began...
Let's go find out why this place feels important to you.
It's Chaos. It found us.
Those things... are manifestations of Chaos.
Be careful, they're closing in.
Huh... it really insists that I stay.
I... I remember now.
This place is where it all began.
It's also where it ended...
It's okay... Run...
Go there...
Is that another one of Chaos's tricks?
Don't get in my way.
Got to hurry. Running out of time.
Now!
That way!
(Manifestations of Chaos... Where is it taking Iuno? How can I find her?)
(Iuno wanted to come here... What did she remember? What's different about this place? When she said it's where it ended... does that mean it's the way out?)
(Did Iuno leave these lights to guide me?)
Go there? The Dark Tide is starting to surge...
Have to get there before I'm swallowed too.
"Those cursed creatures! If it weren't for the Dark Tide... we would've killed them all already!"
"We couldn't activate the Anchor Stone before they destroyed it. Now it's over, everything's ruined..."
"Harelius, we shouldn't have come here. We've lost everything. The Priestess saw it all... What in bloody skies made her insist on coming with us?"
(This calcification is severe. Such corruption... the Dark Tide's surge just now wouldn't be enough to cause this.)
(Could this be connected to the important event Iuno mentioned before she was taken?)
"First David and Lilian, then Ari, Vincentius, Perla... Now even Anassa. Please, Iuno, weren't you able to help us before?"
"Just like when you told us to use a spear against the Tacet Discord, help us see something again! You must be able to see something..."
"All of us, doomed to die? If that's true, why did you come with us... just to watch us die?!"
"No, the Dark Tide's corruption is spread too wide. It's covering their retreat, we can't catch them. The moonlight offered us some illumination, but—"
"Now it too... is being swallowed by the Dark Tide!"
Looks familiar... A Priestess's candelabrum？
How did it get so damaged?
Fate unveils itself to the Priestess.
Beyond a doubt.
No other choice.
She sees no Hero of Heroes.
Heads fall.
Whimpers fade.
She sees no Hero of Heroes.
Variables added.
Visions expanded.
She sees no Hero of Heroes.
The Priestess is never wrong.
For her success is Septimont's defeat.
Why... is it always defeat?
"If fate one day wills our annihilation..."
"If we are nothing more than fate's puppets..."
When that time comes...
Septimont will be no more.
Nothing will remain.
Only she who foresaw every death still lives.
Following its guidance.
She reaches the end, again and again.
What good is a Priestess?
Foreseeing its conclusion.
But she despises her own truth.
Why? Why... why?!
Hundreds of days and nights spent in fate's embrace, staring at the end.
I tried to see everything, missing nothing... but not once did I see a single future where Septimont still stands.
So, this is the answer you give me—
Yes, I saw it. A clear, undeniable future. I know... all I need to do is convince myself this is the final answer...
But... how could I ever accept it?
How could I be content?
With our very existence being denied like this?
Who are you to decide Septimont's fate?
Certainty... is just the narrow boundary fate sets for us. The immeasurable, the free... That is where our dignity lies!
A mouthpiece, a silent witness... Heh, if this is what you expect of me...
I'll raise my bow and turn fate into a storm of possibility!
If, just once, I can prove you are not fixed, then will this so-called "end" even—
Wait, Priestess Iuno... Are you really going to stand with us against the Dark Tide?
You've already... seen how it ends, haven't you?
Of course.
I'm doing this because it's what I want.
The answer I seek is one only I can give.
Priestess, what more do you hope to achieve?
Priestess, what more can you do?
Haven't you... already seen it all, plain as day?
Haven't you seen it countless times already?
Haven't you already viewed the answer?
To know our inevitable doom, then tell the people of Septimont to wait for it, accept it, and even be grateful?

After countless days and nights of divination, not a single prophecy showed Septimont surviving. Still, Iuno refused to accept that fate. To her, human dignity lay in defying what was predetermined. When Harelius returned seeking guidance, she cast her candelabrum into the Dark Tide and walked toward the unknown beyond Tetragon Temple. By joining Harelius's squad in battle, if she could prove fate could be changed, even once, then Septimont's fated destruction would no longer be absolute.
The Lunarum Boughs have grown strong. You've done well with your Anchoring.
How did you know I was doing that?
Who are you, really?
Look at you, a mortal from the real world stumbling into Chaos. What else would you be here for, if not to take something back with you？
Also, with that thing on your wrist there... Isn't it clear? That's how she's been connected to you all this time. Only Anchoring explains that.
As for your second question, that's even stranger.
Along the way, you met the Priestesses, Gladiators, and many others chasing prophecies... Did you ever stop to wonder who they were?
You gave me a strange feeling, so I asked.
You're the only one who doesn't clearly belong to any past.
You seem to know a lot more than you're letting on.
What is it you expect to hear then, mmm?
I'm a blacksmith, long dead. Once a forger of weapons.
A father to a daughter.
A reflection of her past in the Chaos.
So you can tell that I'm not really Iuno.
Aye. But just like the question of who I am, that's not the point.
What matters isn't me, but you. Isn't that right?
You noticed, didn't you? The more you rested near the Lunarum Boughs, the more memories and connections manifested into reality. Iuno's specter became more real, and the Boughs grew.
But now, Chaos has that specter. After all, it was never truly Iuno, was it? But the Lunarum Bough, that's what the two of you built along the way.
There'll be no more doors to choose from. You can keep the Bough and take it back with you. Find a new specter to follow. As long as you have it with you, that should be enough.
Heh, still choices to make, but more intangible.
Aren't you asking me to make a choice now?
We were gathering Lunarum Boughs to forge the bow.
Just like... I came here only to Anchor her and bring her back.
If you cut it here, all your previous Anchoring will be for nothing. You might have to start over many times, with things going even less smoothly. Are you willing?
Not to mention, being trapped in Chaos for so long... There's a chance she's already forgotten her will to fight.
Are you sure you want to throw away all the certainty you've built, just to gamble on a possibility?
Isn't that what I've done from the start?
If I start over, maybe I'll do it better next time.
I'm sure. I have to try.
Forgotten... to fight? I don't know who you think she is, but the Iuno I know is not someone to give in so easily.
She promised we'd meet at the end. As long as Iuno needs a bow, I'll be the one to carry it for her.
Ha, I always thought you followed the light's guidance. Now I see, you reached this point because the light followed you.
How could I forget? The greatest archery isn't about hitting the target every time. It's about letting the arrow choose the mark. Wherever it lands, that's where destiny awaits.
I've said it before. I forge weapons. If you still want it, I'll forge the bow for you.
Come then. Let's do it.
Or... do you still want to forge it into a bow?

You return to the now fully grown Lunarum Bough and talk with the blacksmith again. While there's clearly more to him than meets the eye, what matters now is that the Bough's growth has strengthened the anchoring of Iuno's memories and connections. Even though Iuno's specter you've been trying to make whole was taken by the Dark Tide, as long as the Lunarum Bough remains, there is still hope to find another trace of her in the Chaos. 

Remembering your promise to Iuno to meet at the very end, you decide to gamble everything on the chance of finding her again in the Dark Tide. You ask the blacksmith to fulfill his promise of making the Moon Bow to give to Iuno.
This again... My head's spinning, my arms and legs... It's like I'm underwater. So heavy...
I saw {PlayerName}... at the divination altar at the agora... And then...
Priestess Iuno, we're already indebted to you for accompanying us on this journey.
But you've seen how it ends. Our squad is doomed... The others and I are fated to fall here. There's no need for you to risk your own life any longer.
Return to Tetragon Temple. That's where you should be. I too... will go where I should be.
This place must be... where I gave my last prophecy three years ago. At the end of the spring basin, where the Dark Tide surged!
Harelius? What are you doing here? Didn't Chaos just take me?
This is...
Go back, Priestess Iuno.
...Words fit for the abyss. Don't you dare underestimate me.
Where to go, what path to take... That's something only I decide!
Iuno... Priestess Iuno...
Cough...

After being taken by the Dark Tide, Iuno awakens alone at the edge of Chaos. She finds herself standing on the battlefield from three years ago. Having foreseen Harelius and his squad wiped out, she had decided to stop being a passive observer of fate and instead fight in their battle against the Dark Tide.
Are you... the Priestess Harelius spoke of?
Thank you... Back there, closer to the surge... They need...
Don't push yourself. After what you've just been through, it's enough that you're still on your feet.
Treat your wounds first. Leave the backup to me.
Thank you...
Th-Thank you...
I feel much better...
For Septimont, for our honor!
Everyone, together now!
Cough... cough... I can't die here...
Th-thank you... I feel much better. I can still—
Definitely not. You're too wounded. Before worrying about them, make sure they don't need to worry about you.
I know what you're planning. I'll go in your stead.
Septimont… my beloved homeland… the heart of all I hold dear.
If I die tonight… if I never make it back… will anyone bury me?
Will anyone remember my name… and weep for me?
Ugh... Cough, cough... Priestess Iuno, thank you...
You... And all of us... Have done well...
I will not let you fall!
This is pure torture... How can I let it end like this again...
Cowardly, blighted bastards! Always hiding in the Dark Tide...
Then I'll send you right back into it!
Again, as always...
But why... Would I just stand by and watch you, accept you, complete you?!
No. Even if the end is here, unavoidable, I still have the right to refuse.
The Lunarum Bough has grown strong...
From now on, I need no one's guidance—
Because wherever I choose to aim is my true destiny!
Look closely. Before you isn't a moon the Dark Tide can devour...
It is a moon I command!
I made myself the arrow so you will answer to me! No escape. No retreat. No way out!
I told you I'd rewrite the ending you changed!
You look... completely restored.
Yes. We've come out of the Chaos between life and death, between existence and non-existence.
There aren't any guiding traces, no visions of fate's hand. It's just you and me and... our own grasp of what's to come.
An unwritten void.
Yes. Stretching as far as the eye can see, an infinite... void. More vast than what I saw within you, or anything I glimpsed in the future.
So this is what our changed ending looks like?
No longer an indeterminate chaos, or a singular answer given by someone... but an infinite sea of possibility awaiting choice.
It seems like there's nothing, but in truth, there's everything. So this is the true meaning of a void.
Now... it's time to leave this place.
Compared to before, now what we see is...

The dust settles after that final moment of the battle. No more Chaos. No more Dark Tide. All you see is Iuno standing before you, framed by an infinite white void. Is this the changed ending? Did you really unlock infinite possibility? You can't be sure, but within the vastness of this blank void, Iuno tells you it's time to leave.
These TDs are scuttling about again...
I'm gonna need some help with this.
May applause greet you!
Ah, warrior... Do I know you from somewhere? Did you participate in the Great Agon?
You've got the wrong person.
You're looking at this year's champion.
Is that so? Hold on, you must... There it is, you're the champion of this year's Agon!
Aha, so it's you! Thought you looked familiar.
I've been out here in the hunting grounds for longer than I can remember, so do forgive me for not recognizing our beloved champion at first glance.
Nevertheless, I am deeply grateful that it was you who showed up.
How so?
The thing is, we've run into a bit of trouble.
The High Tide's drawn in so many TDs, and even after it receded, plenty of those bastards still refuse to leave.
Can't just leave them running around the place.
That's a potential risk.
Do they not count as targets for a hunt?
Exactly. A true warrior should always keep their blade sharpened, even after a hunt.
The hunt this round's already wrapped up, and these TDs are just scattered breadcrumbs that can't even make the list. Yet, they still pose a threat.
The surrounding terrain is complex, so you'll need to keep a watchful eye before the real action starts.
A TD hunter must have eyes as sharp as an eagle's, and the explosive prowess of a lion.
Are we just tracking them down?
TD tracking is a skill-demanding work. A slight lapse in judgment and your prey will slip through your fingers.
However, I notice you've been probing the nearby traces ever since you arrived. I take it you've got some experience in this?
I may know a thing or two about hunting.
I've already gotten approval from the Hunter's Guild.
Haha. My hunter's instincts are still as sharp as they were.
Approval from the Hunter's Guild? Is that something new they're doing now? Goodness, I've been here for too long.
Well then, without further ado, let the hunt begin!
May glory be with us, my friend!
Ha! You even took care of the biggest and baddest TD out there!
And just like that, we can enjoy some momentary peace in the Sanguis Plateaus.
Looks like I don't have to worry about TDs for a while. I think it's time I go do something else.
Something else, as in?
It's incredible how a young champion like you came to be during my years here at the hunting grounds. This must be a revelation of fate.
I intend to step outside for a bit. See the world. Come back when the next High Tide arrives, and have a good brawl with those TDs myself.
Until next time, fellow warrior!
Oh no, what should I do... Can anyone help me?
You're… the Champion? Looking for my Ma? She just passed away recently.
...Sorry for your loss.
It's nothing... I don't really care anyway...
What the...? Did this Echo just pat me on the head? How rude!
Sorry. We're just helping it deliver a song to someone who lives here.
A song? Heh, weird. Well, since I'm the only one left in my family, I guess I'll give it a listen.
The Aria Mummer hands the stubborn girl a Melody Box and begins to play a song. She falls silent after the last note fades.
…Did my Ma ask you to bring this here?
Is your mother the master of this Aria Mummer?
No. I've never seen her with an Echo like this before.
This song must be for her. I heard an accordion. Ma used to love playing the accordion.
Are you alright?
Did you and your mother not get along?
I... I don't know.
Not get along? It was worse than that. We had a big argument before she left for the Den.
She barely came home, and whenever she did, she'd yell at me for not living right and for not preserving her glory by becoming a Gladiator.
But this song… she used to play stuff like this for me. Songs that made me want to be a musician.
You did nothing wrong by following your own dreams.
I know. It's just...
I wish we hadn't had that argument that day… I… I should have wished her "Happy Hunting"…
It's okay to cry.
...I'm not crying! I just want to know who wrote this song.
Do you have any idea?
There are plenty of Gladiators who enjoy music, but none would carry an Aria Mummer around.
But… I remember Ma once mentioned a musician friend she met at the Hunter's Den. Maybe that's who you're looking for.
Got it.
Thank you for bringing me this song. I'll... treasure it forever.
The third recipient lives here.
They're quite a renowned family in Septimont. Their eldest son, Galba, is a veteran of the Hunter's Den.
I sent them a message to let them know we were coming, but they never replied… Please don't tell me this is going to be like the last two recipients...
You know, that big mouth of yours is gonna get you in trouble sooner or later.
Don't you worry. Journalists move fast and are hard to hit.
Wait, the door's opening. A medic. I'll go talk to her and see what I can find.
Greetings. Is Mr. Galba home?
Oh... you're here to see him?
Yes. He's an old friend. I came by to visit him.
I'm sure you're aware of the recent unusual High Tide. His team came under devastating attack by Tacet Discords.
Galba was seriously injured, and he barely made it out alive. He's currently in a coma...
That's terrible… May the Sentinel bless... Ahem, may fortune favor him and bring him back to us.
What about his family?
You mean Mr. Cratus? He's probably hunting Tacet Discords outside the city.
Thank you. That's where we'll be going, then.
The Aria Mummer's frequency is fading… We need to find Cratus quickly.
On it… Hold on. Is that a person in the middle of that group of TDs?
Roarrrrrrr!!
Ha... thank you so much for saving me.
Ohh! You're the Champion!
May applause greet you! I'm Cratus. You here to hunt TDs as well?
(Tell him why you're here.)
The Aria Mummer hands Cratus a Melody Box and begins to play a song.
The melody is bold. The trombone, bright. This must be a song for my brother.
My brother was like the trombone in this song: proper, forthright, and admired.
Thank you for bringing us this beautiful song. Did you compose this?
I'm just carrying out someone's request.
So far, it seems the recipients are all members of your brother's team…
Could it be Pulkara? I remember she loved playing the accordion.
Based on what we know, the composer is likely a Ragunnesi lady who enjoys singing and has an Aria Mummer companion…
She sent a song to Ms. Pulkara as well.
My brother once mentioned in a letter that his team had a member from Ragunna who loved to sing and dance.
Aha! At last, a clue. Do you know her name? Was it a woman?
A woman, yes. But my brother never mentioned her name.
There was also another survivor on the team besides my brother, called Aleus.
Maybe he knows something about her.
Aleus? Hmm, he's actually the next person on the list.
Thank you. Looks like we're getting closer to the answer.
You're welcome, {Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} Champion! I still have much to learn, but I'll meet you in a duel in the arena someday!
So... you made it out.
Haha… other than our comatose Captain, it's just you and me now.
Are you here to reprimand me? I failed Strozzia. If you want to punch me, go ahead. I deserve it.
Strozzia? That's a Ragunnesi name.
Seems like we've got our answer, {PlayerName}!
Tell us what happened, Aleus.
…I was in Galba's team. We were stationed near the Hunter's Den, keeping tabs on TD activity during the High Tide.
We wrapped up a hunt that day and held a celebration feast at camp.
But something was nagging our Captain. After the feast, he ordered us to patrol the camp's perimeter. I had too many drinks, so I stayed behind.
When I heard the alarm go off, I rushed out, only to see waves of TDs rushing toward camp...
I ran to my team as fast as I could... I only found Strozzia, severely wounded and shielding the Captain with her own body…
She said she couldn't make it and told me to get the Captain out.
Why did I drink so much that day? I should've been out there with them… revelling in that glorious last stand.
And Galba would have died.
But if I'd gone with them… maybe… maybe they'd all still be here…
Wait, Strozzia sounds like someone who couldn't fight. Why was she on your team?
She was our support. The Captain approved it himself.
They say she was from Ragunna. Her story was that she couldn't make a name for herself there, so she came to Septimont for inspiration to create songs no Ragunnesi had ever heard before.
She couldn't even play a proper tune when she first got here.
Honestly, I thought she just wanted to act out some romantic story of sacrifice. Typical Ragunnesi.
Hey, watch your... Forget it. Go on.
Over time, Gattuso, the cheery one on the team, started helping her, told her all about Septimont. Even invited her over to his place while off duty and introduced his little brother to her.
Pulkara was all tough at first, but she eventually warmed up to her. I often saw them playing the accordion together, with Grisoni as accompaniment.
Strozzia's music changed. I could tell she's grown to truly love Septimont.
So when she asked to stay on the team as our support, I voted yes. She earned it.
I taught her how to hold a sword and the skills needed to defend herself. She said she wanted to write a song for each of us, not for fame, but to commemorate our time together...
…She must've followed the Captain out of camp in search of inspiration that day.
If you hadn't taught her how to hold a sword, she might not have been able to bring Galba back.
…Is this the song she wrote for me? That clarinet… Such a clear and elegant melody…
Is this how she saw me? Was I ever like that?
I'll be honest with you, brother, drowning yourself in remorse isn't a good look.
There are still things you can do.
Don't let Strozzia's song go to waste.
…You're right. There are things I must do.
I need to recover the weapons of my comrades. I'm the only one left who still recognizes them.
Thank you all. And thank you, Grisoni. The melody of this song will forever be engraved in my heart, as a reminder of the person I am meant to be.
This Aria Mummer... Are you Grisoni?
That makes the final box. Anything else you wanna do? Let us know.
Hmm… It says it wants to go back to its master's home and meet her brother, {PlayerName}.
But its travelled with its master for so long, it's not sure if its master's family moved some place else or not…
Strozzia… Strozzia… Now that we have her name, it makes things easy. I know basically everyone in Ragunna.
You're smarter than you look. Shocker!

Perhaps... What I carry is rage. A rage... for vengeance.

Born from the fury that courses through the earth, rage cast my spine, and slaughter forged my chest...

I've torn through countless souls, rained fire on fields, slept to the wails of a thousand dying cries... They remember me as "Nemean," the name of the land I reduced to ruins. A name forever seared into their hearts with terror.
But Leviathan... Its treachery dragged me into the Dark Tide. It twisted my frequency and forced me into an abominable union with the frail Goat and pathetic Serpent. We were merged into one...

Sounds like you were a villain.

If Leviathan based this underworld on the old tales of Septimont, then this must be Kharon, the ferryman of the dead.

The accursed shore awaits all who fear not Divinity. If your heart harbors unfinished desires, and you fear not death... then come. Step aboard.

...Please ferry us.

I believe in all of them...
...Just as they believe in me.

Alas, this interlude must end here. Leviathan stirs from Its slumber, and with Its wrath comes Its gospel.
Now then, show me... Show me that humanity can rise against the divine. Prove your will is your own. Prove you are worthy to pen your own fate.
But if humanity cannot cross the threshold of the divine... then we shall be the ones to write its fate instead.
By now, you must have realized that Rinascita's fate was forged by the Sentinel.
Never paused to wonder why it grows dizzy each time it absorbs the Dark Tide? You do already know what the Dark Tide really is...
Tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow...
Creeps in this petty pace from day to day, to the last syllable of recorded time.
All our yesterdays are but... faint glimmers lighting the road to the grave.
Life is but a walking shadow, a poor player that struts and frets their hour upon the stage...
And then, in the blink of a moment, is heard no more...
I believe in them... just as they believe in me...
Hehe... of course. You've always been the protagonist of our play.
But what if, the one we speak of, "the one meant to end Leviathan"...is not you?
What...? So your true target is...
The special scene between her and our Grand Architect must not be disturbed.
For now, take a brief rest. The stage is nearly set for your finale.
Not long ago, by the Styx Lake...
So… I was your true target all along.
Indeed. Another stalemate awaiteth {Male=him;Female=her}. And you, the revenant returned from the Dark Tide... You are the one chosen to end Leviathan in our script.
I know the power you wield. Left unchecked, it unravels the fabric of our play. And so, I must still your steps here.

Yet I confess, Galbrena... Your growth hath far outstripped what I foresaw.
How many Tacet Discords have you devoured to stand here now?
...Heh. Do you count how many gemberries you've eaten in your life?
For one with a lifespan like yours, surely you know more than most. So go on. Take a guess.
You risked all to save those who share no bond with you.
To choose to protect is one thing, but to do so wielding power not born of mankind... That, you should never have done.
You must have felt it. The cold stares of those you saved. No gratitude, only fear for that which they cannot understand.
So what? I chose this path, and I'll follow it.
Your frequency now intertwines with the Tacet Discords. The moment you crossed that threshold, the mortal world... ceased to be your home.
My offer still stands. Join the Fractsidus. You, too, have crossed the veil that parts life and death. Among us, you shall find haven and purpose.
Ever since I got these wings, I've found freedom in the open sky...
I don't need a haven or titles to cage me. I am what I choose to be.
Shoulds you crave power, we shall grant it, even that of the Threnodian. Should you seek to help, we shall guide mankind toward a future beyond all comprehension.
Sounds like something a hypocrite would say.
Mortal sight is too narrow to fathom our path.
So you think you stand above humanity, huh? Whatever, I don't give a damn about you or your grand ideals.
I only need one reason to take you down. You're in my way.
The Tacet Discords within you are gone. Now, tell me. What remains of you?
I've heard enough of this crap.
You hide behind borrowed faces. But me? I've never once doubted who I am.
I've risen from blood and inferno a thousand times, faced the monsters that lined up to devour me, and fought back, without mercy...
I broke Harpyia's razor wings and tore out Balor's demon eye. Not even Dullahan's iron hooves could bring me to my knees. The Dark Tide cursed me long ago. I should have been dead, but here I stand.
And you think one of your clones can stop me?
Still clinging to hope? A sharp tongue may spark your courage, but it shall not change your end.
Then so be it. Forsake all hope of ever beholding Paradise. I shall guide you to the other shore, into eternal darkness... into hell.

By the shores of Styx Lake, Galbrena faces <ano=Grand Architect>Kharon</ano> alone, bloodied and spent. She realizes she has been the Fractsidus's true target all along.

Condescendingly, Kharon questions and tempts her: After devouring so many Tacet Discords, she has long since crossed the threshold of what it means to be human. The Fractsidus is where she can belong and find purpose.

Galbrena answers with scorn. She strikes again, but her bullets freeze in mid-air, her flames cannot reach him, and the Tacet Discords within her are torn away. Even so, she gets back up and charges in a final, desperate strike.

This time, Kharon does not hold back. A shadowed claw pierces straight through her chest. Galbrena only smiles faintly, as if this was her plan all along.
…This blood. It should be enough.
My flames could never reach you before.
But now… it's time you paid for your arrogance.
The hunt begins.
Your flames… they purified the corrupted frequencies?
Bullseye.
May the flames light your way home.
You never cease to surprise...
And here I thought you knew me well. A good hunter turns nature to her advantage.
I wasn't referring to that. I was surprised to see the spirits rise at your command, forming as Cetus the Tidebreaker...
I didn't command them. They chose it of their own will. When disaster strikes, humans unite.
A hollow being like you wouldn't understand.
...Even if you absorbed the corruption in their frequencies, it will not last. That Kharon is but one mask the Grand Architect wears. The spirits will not restrain him for long.
I know. That's why we have to move and find {Male=him;Female=her}.
There was a battle near the Journeying Paradise. Its aftershock blocked the main path. Which way do we go?
Left. It's a shortcut.
There is no path on the left.
Then I'll carve one out myself.
Or did you misunderstand? I didn't become strong because of any of you... I was strong. That's how I broke you.

Kharon's shadowed claw pierces through Galbrena, but this is what she had been waiting for. Her blood, tempered in the depths of this hell, splatters on Kharon and sets him ablaze. Forced to sever his arm to survive, the predator becomes the prey.

As they clash, Galbrena's flames purify the lake's corrupted frequencies. The souls of the dead gather into the form of Cetus the Tidebreaker and drag Kharon into the burning depths.

After bidding farewell to those freed souls, Galbrena turns and rushes to find you once more.
You just made a path swarming with enemies.
Which means it's the right one.
Ah... a path of slaughter, then?
No needless bloodshed.
Tch… we will paint a trail in blood.
Leviathan's presence is growing stronger. Flamewing won't last much longer in the air... Heh...
(The Beholder's mark is set. With Shadow Fiend's power, I can throw the Feather Blade to move to the target location.)
Prey marked. Time to end it in one shot.
(I'll use the Feather Blade to weave through 'em while shooting. That'll speed things up.)
(That stone... Looks like I can pull it loose.)
(I'll pull that stone loose. That'll clear a path.)
Sorry, I'm in a hurry.
The hunt continues.
All set to die?
Those I slay... stay dead forever.
Hah, the path is hidden. To another dimension then.
Hiding yourself, huh? To another dimension then.
Chimera! Tear the space apart!
Stay sharp.
Through here.
Sweet, sweet slaughter… I shall feast to my heart's content!
Slow down. I must savor the exquisite taste of their agony...
Almost there...
...{PlayerName}!
You are too late. The purest Dark Tide has swallowed {Male=him;Female=her}, and the stairway to the Paradise lies in ruins.
Run all you like, your chance to save {Male=him;Female=her} is already lost. Such is the nature of fate.
If I believed in fate, I wouldn't have made it this far.
You think that little flame can burn this Dark Tide? You drown in delusion.
I know it's not enough. What if... I add some of this?
...You intend to unleash the Tacet Discords within you.
Those savage frequencies alone will destroy you before the Dark Tide even gets a chance.
I tamed them once. I can do it again. It's just a matter of... what I'm willing to lose.
If saving {Male=him;Female=her} means we still have a shot at taking down Leviathan…
I'll risk it all. My will, my everything.
...Lunatic.
Let's see whose fire burns hotter. Don't tell me you're getting cold feet now.
Everything you have fought to keep will burn to ash.
Then let it burn!
Time to make a choice again. Hunt with me, or die with me. If you still want to see Leviathan destroyed with your own eyes… this is your final chance.
Either way, I've already made my choice.
…I called on you time and again to unleash your true power… And now, of all things, this is what gets through to you?
You would risk everything for a sliver of hope?
I would. No matter the cost.

At the stairway to the Paradise, Galbrena arrives only to find you already engulfed by the Dark Tide. To save you, she unleashes the Tacet Discords within herself to burn the Dark Tide with hellfire. Yet against the purest of Dark Tides, even her flames fall short.
 
So she chooses to ignite her own "life force," setting herself ablaze, all for the sake of a single hope.
Just as I foresaw, she arrives to save you from the abyss.
A fleeting spark, kindled by all she once had… burning for a hopeless stand against the furious tide.
What awaits you is your end.
Now, roving outlander, don that exquisite mantle once more...
And step onto the deserted stage you are destined to face.
How much time has passed...
No path to take... No way to go...
Wait... what's that ahead...
Before you, countless pale lights converge into an ancient stele, standing in austere silence.
You reach out, fingers brushing the surface. A faint line of script emerges at its base.
"Here lies Carlotta Montelli."

After being engulfed by the Dark Tide, you awaken in an unknown space.

On a pallid shore stand countless gravestones, each bearing the name of a companion…
Death is a divine gift bestowed upon humanity.
Those you cherish now... a lucky few had their names carved into this ancient stone.
But far more, those who once stood by your side, you've already let slip away. Like raindrops into the sea... lost to the depths.
One day, even this stele will follow. Swallowed by the tide of your fading memory. Just like the rest.
I will not forget them.
...You've changed from who you once were. Still stubborn, as always... But now you fear losing what you have.
And that... has made you weak.
Go on, then. Your destination lies just ahead.
Here lies Tern Brant
Here lies Roccia
Here lies Zani
Here lies Phoebe
Here lies Cartethyia
Here lies Ciaccona Toccata
Here lies Cantarella Fisalia
Here lies Lupa
Here lies Iuno
Here lies Augusta
Here lies Galbrena
Abby's condition was written into our script long ago. Even if you strike Leviathan down, Abby can no longer serve as the vessel to seal Leviathan's essence.
Only one variable slipped past our design. Her, the revenant returned from the Dark Tide. She could have bridged your failing forces and brought Leviathan to Its end.
But the moment she gave up, your downfall was written. Hope, scattered like ash.
Oh, Harbinger of the Dark Tide... you can save no one. What follows in your wake is ruin, and ruin alone.
No... this is not the end...
Hmm… Not fond of how the story ends, are we?
Well, fortunately, you are not like the rest. Your fate rises above the masses. You... you still hold the power to choose.
You've always wanted to be the savior. Now, that chance lies before you. The one... you've known was coming all along.
Shut up, you noisy pest.
You don't buy his nonsense, do you?
Galbrena... Is that you?
In the flesh. Took a few tricks, but I made it in.
What is this place?
That voice said this is the "truth" I cannot escape.
This is your Mindscape. Leviathan drew it from the deepest layers of your mind using the purest frequency of the Dark Tide.
Everyone has a Mindscape. Some say when countless seas of consciousness flow together, they make the essence of Solaris.
I've seen many places, but nothing quite like this... It must mean a lot to you.
...I think so.
Is this... where it all began for me?
But I saw Carlotta, Brant, everyone... and you. You were all just like in that illusion I had before...
Leviathan preyed on your deepest fear of losing the ones you care about and turned it into these gravestones.
The ones who seem the strongest often fear loss the most. That's how Leviathan slips in, by exposing our pain to the light.
If you let it take hold, you'll never break free. In the end, your mind and body will be devoured, dismantled, reshaped, and assimilated. It's no better than death.
So, you could say this place hangs between life and death. Your friends are here too, each of them fighting their own demons. But...
Can you feel this?
Yes... it's warm. And real.
There. Look up.
When I hunt, I often travel through the night.
The darkness is thick, but faint stars hang above to guide me.
But those stars don't shine for me. Long before I even looked up, they'd already been watching over the sky.
Leviathan has underestimated human resolve. To me, these gravestones... they're signposts left by the "living" for those still fighting.
Like stars destined to burn out, they refuse to stop shining until the very end. There's always someone in the dark, giving their life to light the way and pass hope to those who follow.
That's why... you and I, we don't stop moving forward.
Sometimes, all it takes... is the first step. That's enough to light the way for others. And maybe one day… they'll be the ones lighting the way for you.
This story was never mine alone.
My fate is bound to others.
That's what this journey has always been about.
I don't know your past, but I do know the future you want isn't one of death.
Being scared of losing someone just means you're human. But the people you love, the ones who love you back... They'd never let you face the end alone.
This isn't where it ends. If you want a path to open... Remember all the people you helped Anchor to a future. Now, it's time to Anchor yourself.
But before that... take a look behind you.
You've come a long way. Changed a lot of lives. That's your past, but it's also your strength. So use it. Hope... is still out there, waiting for you.
This path lies right before me.
No more fear. No more doubt.
Just keep going, right?
Take this spark with you...

Through the mist, a familiar vision takes shape. Cristoforo's whisper claims this is the truth you cannot escape. On destiny's stage, only you will remain for the final bow.

He claims your plan was doomed from the start. When the Discord Slayer fought to her last breath, your final hope turned to ash. As the Harbinger of the Dark Tide, you already know the only way to change the ending. A sword waits in front of you.

But Galbrena's voice pierces through the mist. She descends, alive and well, shattering Cristoforo's lies. She tells you to look to the sky, where the starlight dispels your doubt. What you must do now is take the next step.

She places a spark in your hand, a flame to carry you forward. Now walk. Through darkness, into the light.
Take the step... through darkness into the light.
When the bustling stage quiets, all who played a part in your fate will take their leave. Only you remain for the final bow.
From beginning to end, you've always walked alone.
That.. is the "truth" you cannot escape.
I... no, we will be right behind you.
Ah, new allies born from the perils of the high seas! What better way to begin an epic story?
Good people have their wishes fulfilled, heroes appear in a time of crisis, justice triumphs over evil, and united friends are undefeatable.
The Codex reminds us, "It is not the lighthouse that guides us through the storm to safety, but our own eyes fixed on the shore."
The difference, though, is that you are a blade. A weapon that can break the cycle.
Like I said, we seize control.
Music itself holds no emotion. It's the heart that grants it meaning.
A person of true character should never be defined by an inanimate blade.
Even if one day you meet defeat, remember this. Those you've helped will never let you face it alone.
I've been thinking... our final fate might already be written, but how we walk that path is up to us. We, as humans, are meant to carve our own way forward!
A civilization's glory is forged by generations of brave souls. It was never meant to be one person's medal of honor.
The waves of resistance shall never cease. Mankind will not be oppressed by the Threnodian...
The power to write our fate has always been ours...
Even without guidance, even when Divinity falls silent... Civilization will find its own way...
You have no role in Rinascita's destiny!
You have no reason to carry on this fight.
We carry the Dark Tide's memories.
We command both light and shadow.
Did you really think you could stand against us alone?
Steel yourself...
Defy the prophecy. Rise above fate again.
If the road ahead is dark, then let this soul—
—Be the spark that lights the night.
Well said!
You're not alone.
Because we are here. With you.
Where the dark night ends lies the blazing sun. We all made it, {PlayerName}.
I'm back!
Is everything alright on your side?
Has anyone seen Galbrena?
Worry not, Herald of Hope. "We" have shielded them from the Dark Tide.
...Don't worry, it's just a scratch. Glad to see you're alright.
As for that Grand Architect, heh... The spirits will guide him to the other shore.
Are you really alright...
But you don't look well...
She burned her own life force to help you. Only by Overclocking was she able to break through the Dark Tide's illusion.
Her true Forte has always been inside her. As her blazing will became Overclocked flames, that seared away the corruption of the Tacet Discords and the Dark Tide. It awakened her Forte.
I took on some of the cost of her Overclocking... I admit her insolent gamble paid off again.
She saved me, but you saved her.
Maybe it wasn't really a gamble this time. I knew you wouldn't stand by and let me die.
...Hmph. Then slay Leviathan and prove I was right about you.

You awaken from the illusion. Your companions are by your side once more, and Galbrena returns atop the back of the Dragon of Dirge.

To reach you, she ignited her own life force, Overclocking her power to tear open the Dark Tide's illusion. Chimera bore part of the cost for her. Meanwhile, when Septimont and your companions were engulfed by the Dark Tide, the Echoes responded to humanity's hope and resolve. They came together in their strongest form to aid. Though the Anchor Stone was destroyed, your companions still followed a different beacon. You, the "Anchor of Hope."

Through the Dark Tide, all of your memories connected. They have learned of Galbrena and Cartethyia's plan too. But Abby can no longer bear the burden of the Gem. Galbrena offers to use her power of devouring to seal the Gem within herself. It is for this very reason that the Fractsidus made her their target.

Cristoforo believed his script to be flawless, but underestimated what small hopes, when united, can become. Now, before the gate of the Paradise, you and your companions stand together. It is time to break it open and cast down the false Divinity that waits beyond.
Finally recognize me, Augusta?
I almost didn't. You've changed a lot. But the warmth in that Resonance ability... That, I could never forget.
Glad to see we both stayed true to who we are. But we can catch up later. For now... How did you all make it here?
Just as we were about to take the potion and enter the Dark Tide, the Fractsidus triggered its surge. Leviathan pulled us into Its illusion.
But... the Echoes swallowed by the Dark Tide protected us. They bought us the time we needed to drink it.
Leviathan can mimic our form, but never our "soul."
We heard your call, strong and full of resolve. So we came, every one of us, to stand by your side.
The Echoes of Rinascita can sense human frequencies. When we reach out in hope, they answer us with hope.
But even with their help and the potion, we're still far from our goal... We fought through the illusions, but we still need an Anchor to open a path to the Journeying Paradise.
I have an idea! If Leviathan found Its <ano=Harbinger>Anchor of Reality</ano> to summon the Tidespawn into our world...
We follow suit and find an Anchor of Hope to find a way out of the world of the Dark Tide!
And who better for that… than you, {PlayerName}.
Even in the depths of despair, you held on to hope... That unwavering faith makes you worthy of being our Anchor of Hope.
And the <ano=bond>unbreakable tether</ano> we share is what led us to you.
I won't let you down.
I'm here because of all of you, too.
The Dark Tide showed us your memories… We know that Cartethyia planned her own "death" to plant humanity into Leviathan…
Her mind is asleep inside Leviathan's anchored body. If we can wake her, our chances of beating the Threnodian will grow.
Let Abby rest for now. When the Threnodian falls, use your power to "split" Its essence from the Gem. And I'll use my "devouring" ability to seal It inside me.
…So that's the real reason the Fractsidus was targeting you.
Yes. But now, I've got backup. Neither they nor the Threnodian can stop us.
Cristoforo thought his script was flawless, but he missed one thing. Even the faintest spark of hope can ignite a blaze when we stand together.
Defeating the Threnodian is what we all seek. That is what unites us here!
Leviathan twisted our memories and emotions into this fake Paradise, hoping we'd surrender to Its will, and let It harvest our civilization…
But now, the fate It's forced upon us is ours to shatter!
Together, we'll bring Leviathan down.
Everyone, with me to battle!
No throne lasts forever. Even Divinity can fall.
As long as we hold on to our shared faith and hope, Leviathan will never win.
It's time to break open the gate... and burn this false Paradise to the ground.
…That's the Threnodian's Chrysalis, Leviathan's gestation pod. It's expanding the rift bleeding into our world.
Temporal distortions! Watch out!
It thought dividing us would make us easy prey.
Then It thought wrong.
Everyone, pay attention to those Cocoons summoning monsters.
They are linked to the Chrysalis above. Destroying them will weaken the Threnodian's hold.
Copy that!
Leave them to us!
All Cocoons cleared on my side. How's it looking for you?
Mission accomplished, Captain!
Quickly and swiftly.
That? Pfft, child's play. We handled it ages ago, obviously.
Careful! The platform is collapsing now that the Cocoons are gone!
...Lorelei?
She just stabilized the distortion. Let's move.
What about the others?
We're good! The Lioness of Glory caught us! What a sight to behold!
The Dragon of Dirge lent its aid as well.
Alright. Let's all meet up ahead.
We will finish the remaining threats.
Go and fulfill your mission. Defeat Leviathan.
Mortals must seek salvation... Mortals must follow a uniform creed...
Now... Righteous One... open the gate to ascension.
...You are not her.
Reveal yourself, Leviathan!
I am the Beginning, and the End; the First Breath and the Final Sigh... I have ever been Rinascita's sole Divinity.
By my Gospel alone didst thou arise, United and Reborn. And now thou dare lift thy hand against me?
Fleurdelys… once more, the crown is thine. Return to my embrace.
Now, faithless heretics... Kneel and receive thy judgment.

With the aid of Rinascita's Echoes, you reach the heart of the Paradise. The Dark Tide surges, surrounding you. Leviathan attempts to sway your resolve with Its whispers, but you see through the deception and fight on. At last, Leviathan reveals itself in the likeness of the Blessed Maiden, Fleurdelys.

The moment you have fought so long to reach has arrived. Now, brace for Leviathan's judgment.
Imperator's power is mine to command.
Behold how it ought truly be wielded.
So long as we stand, we can still bring Cartethyia back.
Let our hopes reach Cartethyia!
...A vain struggle.
Come forth, lost souls. Draw near, and face the depths of thine oldest, most primal fear.
Tch... You soil our memories with your filthy touch, and now you want to assimilate our Resonance abilities?
Despicable. Is there anything left within It that's real?
Only one truth remaineth. Thy despair and thy terror.
Hear my decree...
This... is Imperator's power of separation?
Fleurdelys?! You... dare...
It's Cartethyia... she's awakening!
Now, {PlayerName}!
...It's reaching for the Chrysalis to restore Its frequencies!
I'll handle it!
How can this be…?
Coward! You hide in the shadows playing tricks from afar?
Thou art unworthy to stand against me.
Hmph, how insulting...
This vessel carries the frequencies Leviathan split from Its body. Every blow we land here wounds Leviathan Itself.
We need to evade Its attacks while waiting for the right chance to strike.
Hah, this is barely a challenge!
Thank you, everyone...
It worked...
I'm back!
Fleurdelys... wilt thou cast aside thy godhood once more?
I stand here in the name of "humanity."
If my "humanity" alone can't sway you...
Then we will defeat you together!
Thou dare pit mortal will against the divine?
Then behold...
The deepest abyss of despair!
People of Rinascita, please hear my call...
Unite... with all your will and hope!
Feeble resistance...
The fate of Rinascita is mine to decree!
Even the Threnodian's Chrysalis, turned into a weapon. So you're ready to take a final stand. Too bad... that won't bring us down!
The light of hope has pierced the Dark Tide. Leviathan, your doom is inevitable!
Every crime you've committed will be answered in full.
Our tomorrow isn't yours to shape.
No matter how great your power, do not presume to claim our future!
False Divinity, we will tear your delusions and drag you down from your hollow throne!
In the name of Imperator, be gone!
My power... my strength...
Your form is shattering, and your fate is sealed.
This time... fate will flow to the future we have Anchored!
Leviathan, now it is your turn... to drown in despair.
...My Gospel shall resound across the tides for eternity!
Stand in our way… and we'll slay even the divine.
Watch closely, Leviathan! This is the will of humanity!
Count me in too, {PlayerName}!
Let's knock It's lights out for good!
Time to end this once and for all.
Leviathan, prepare for your final reckoning!
Brave the tide, {PlayerName}!
Still trying to corrupt us with your "whispers?"
Wait... it's the people of Rinascita! They're singing for us!
Even in the depths of despair, the song of hope echoes. Hear it well, Leviathan! This is your requiem!
No matter the suffering, our courage carries us onward! This is the hymn of humanity!
Insolence! My will suffereth no defiance!
This is my kingdom!
We'll burn your false Paradise to ashes!
Leviathan, may you now be bound...
By the weight... of humanity's hopes!
Abra... Abraxas! Why hast thou betrayed us?
...It's trying to absorb the Dark Tide!
Time to finish this.
Our paths were never truly opposed... One day, they shall cross again.
Remember this... We were once your "Waystones."
Righteous One… Raise the lantern in your hand…
Within it lies the will of every Primus of the Order, from Napoli the Second.
To my own resolve and atonement...
Let its light banish this final darkness.
Rinascita will surely know... a lasting dawn.
I'll split the Gem from Its physical form.
...Heh.
You came.
Yup.
Chimera showed me the way.
Not a bad shot, am I?
Hope I'm not too late?
Not too late, not too early. Right on time.
One side each?

The mists lift, revealing Galbrena locked in battle with the Tidespawn at the path's end. Her guns are knocked away, but she holds her ground with nothing but skill and grit.

You pick up her guns, fire a shot that turns the tide, and rush to her side. As promised, you meet again in "hell." With your backs to each other, you face the encroaching swarm. No words are needed. Together, you fight, each guarding one side.
The Guardian of the Dark Tide, a Mortarch... We meet again.
I tried to clear the path for you, but that thing got in my way.
You handled all the monsters along the way by yourself?
More or less. Too many roads led here, and I couldn't be sure which one you'd take.
So I wanted to make it easier, whichever way you chose.
You've already helped more than enough.
So have you. There were things I couldn't have done alone.
As for the rest... Let's deal with what's in front of us first.
"Shining with your love... We stand united in devotion..."
"With hearts full of joyous loyalty... we rise from the sea... guided by your light..."
The dead grow tongues and sing praise day and night. That's what becomes of those consumed by the Dark Tide.
If the Journeying Paradise reaches our world, everyone in Rinascita... will suffer the same fate.
Heh… Look at them. Lining up to flatter their Divinity, groveling for Its grace.
Without Leviathan's "wisdom," feeble minds like theirs are fit only to be devoured.
Ceaseless worship, stripped of meaning or soul. From this shore to the next, from Paradise back to our world...
All to gather more "believers," to be drawn into the Paradise's maw. Then they'll go claim their due from Leviathan.
Even with the tape's help, we can't stay exposed to these "hymns" for too long... Chimera.
I don't take your orders.
Silence, wretched souls! There is no place for you in Paradise. Burn in your ruin and rot in Hell.
Seems Chimera still commands some authority here.
Hmph, coming back here feels like coming home. By blood, they ought to call me... Forefather.
Leviathan was right about one thing. Fear is the most ancient and enduring truth in all living things.
Fighting through more enemies, you and Galbrena finally reach the "gates of hell."
We're here again...
The Styx Lake. A myth once whispered in Septimont, now carved into reality by Leviathan.
Those touched by the Tidespawn often begin to see things. Hallucinations... and this lake is usually the first they find.
Anger, sorrow, pain... Leviathan reads the depths of our hearts. And from them, It births this river of memory.
What you see here is a part of you. The river mirrors what you fear most.
That's why I saw those terrible visions. But why were you there too?
My mind can walk between reality and the Dark Tide. I've crossed this lake many times, trying to guide the lost home.
Oftentimes it isn't Hell that people fear. They fear fear itself, and that creates Hell.
No passing!
Worry not. You are safe with me.
Not while I'm watching!
Let my melody join yours!
Stand tall! Your captain's got your back!
Time for an interlude!
Anchor aweigh, it's showtime!
Your turn, Augusta!
My blade calls.
Careful! Stop... right there!
O light of hope, shine upon us once more!
Well, that's unexpected...
Heh. Is this supposed to be a mockery?
Ugh, ridiculous imitation! Disgraceful!
The Ephor's swordplay... and even my flames?! Oh, you filthy thief!
Our proud craft will not be defiled by the likes of you!

On the final path leading to the Paradise, Cristoforo once again blocks your path.

He reveals the Fractsidus's goal: to become beings equal to the gods themselves, and to rewrite "humanity's fate."

No matter how noble their reasoning, you cannot condone their methods. Still, Cristoforo extends an offer: to make you the "Quillbearer," granting you the authority to write the fate of humankind.

But humanity's fate belongs to no one but humanity itself. You make your stance known. Cristoforo, however, has already seen through your plan. Because Abby still carries the frequency of the Ovathrax, if it attempts to absorb the Gem, Leviathan may merge with that power and complete Its rebirth.

Your strategy is exposed, but you refuse to abandon hope. Cristoforo steps aside, and in the next instant, Leviathan's wrath descends. Let your free will rise against the divine. Let it prove you worthy to seize the right to write fate with your own hands.

Cristoforo's voice continues, seeking to shatter your final hope: What if the one meant to end Leviathan... is not you? What if whoever is capable of doing so is far stronger than even Cristoforo himself?

The Fractsidus's endgame begins to dawn on you. At the same time, the stairway to Paradise begins to crumble. Just as you near the end, the Dark Tide surges and pulls you under.

Rest for now. The final act of your story awaits.
I would. No matter the cost.
You and your companions enter the Journeying Paradise, but temporal distortions scatter you onto separate platforms.
Move aside.
Stay back.
I see you.
Next.
Could be faster.
One down.
Another one bites the dust.
Show me all you've got.
Yes... unleash your fury! Kill with abandon!
Magnificent… their terror drives them into the shadows...
At last... Galbrena, this is who you are...
Another dimension... within the Civilization Capsule.
But why does it open up now? Was it when Avidius and I made contact?
Arbiter...
Is that Imperator's voice? Imperator... do you have more to tell me?
Arbiter. This moment was always foreseen. Now, it comes to pass...
Imperator... is that really you?
Arbiter, I grieve to say... I am but a message, set to activate in response to the presence of an Initiator.
Time, in this place, flows near still. A moment remains for us to speak.
When I merged with Leviathan, It seized a fragment of my mind... and with it, a trace of my power to separate.
I knew not the fullness of Its design. As a safeguard, I split elements of my core data into this space... the Civilization Capsule.
It records the origin and birth of the Rinascitan civilization, preserving their most ancient memories.
Arbiter, heed me now... let me unveil... Rinascita's beginnings...
Once, we drafted the first <ano=fate>Blueprint</ano> for these seaborne kin. Now, I have entombed it here.

Amidst the chaos, the Civilization Capsule is accidentally opened through your <ano=resonance>contact</ano> with Avidius, pulling you into its inner space.
 
There, you finally hear Imperator's last message about Rinascita and the origins of Leviathan…
In the beginning...
Life rose and fell with the tide
The displaced and wandering
did follow My guidance
They journeyed unto the archipelago
There, I did leave <ano=Genesis Nexus>Knowledge and Technology</ano>
that they might walk the path to freedom
Your light blesses us...
We follow Your will...
To build our republic...
"Unity"
became the bedrock of civilization
But Leviathan seized upon mankind's "longing for Unity"
to manifest the civilization's shadow
It spoke in My name
Wrought false miracles
Forged hollow grace
Feeding on stagnant, obedient minds
From the founding of civilization
It had invaded their spirit and beliefs
We are blessed by the sea...
By You, we are "unified"
By You, we are "born"
From the sea we came
and to the sea we shall return
I rose against it
Only to unleash the Dark Tide
It scarred Rinascita beyond measure
I... began to question
all I had done
In truth... We were no different
Those who truly walked the land
were never granted the right to choose
Civilizations are bound with Threnodians
No eternal solution doth exist
Have I the right...
to choose their fate?
The shaping of a civilization
must belong to its people
The Threnodian doth steer Rinascita's fate
and I too, once guided Rinascita's course
We both sought to mold civilization after Our own will
What followed, thou already knowest. I allowed the Threnodian to exist. I chose coexistence, using Myself to shackle It. I partook of Its blight, that I might comprehend It.
Once, I did seek thy counsel. Thou granted me... the freedom to choose.
I would do the same thing again.
You've done more than enough. Let me handle the rest.
I just have one question... Why did the Civilization Capsule need the Threnodian's power to open?
When Leviathan and I were one, I split a sliver of Its frequency... a "memory." That memory I sealed here.
The Capsule was ever meant for thy hands. My design was that it should open only in the presence of thou and the Resonator bearing both My power and that of Leviathan.
What if... that Resonator became the Threnodian's puppet?
If that came to pass, then Rinascita hath already fallen. And the truth within this Capsule would cease to matter.
But if she standeth with humanity, then this truth is hers to know. And thine.
If the Rinascitans... wouldst walk a path "free of Divinity," they must face their past and "the most primeval fear." They must overcome the "shadow born of civilization."
The opening of the Capsule shall stir the Rinascitans' oldest memories. Leviathan shall seek, through the Blueprint we created, to lay claim to Rinascita's fate anew.
Arbiter... the hour of farewell hath come. Go now. Gather every last hope... If all unfoldeth as it should, Rinascita shall be free of Divinity henceforth.
When the shadows of the soul are at last dispelled, Rinascita shall welcome a true dawn. And humanity... shall have a future beyond any I could foresee.
The true faithful believed in Imperator. So too did Imperator believe in humanity.
(Draw your sword.)
(Keep your sword sheathed.)
You killed the Blessed Maiden before my eyes. Ragunna's disasters are tied to your actions... Now, tell me what I need to know.
...If I told you I acted to save Cartethyia, would you believe me?
This place is protected by Imperator. For now, Leviathan can't hear us. This... is for you.
{PlayerName}, trust her. And trust me... Everything we've done... is to... defeat... Leviathan...
That is her frequency...
I need you to accept this. Cartethyia is "dead," but she may still "return." For that to happen... we need to kill Leviathan.
Kill Leviathan? Didn't she absorb It when they merged?
Now... Leviathan is on the verge of "rebirth."
It stole some of the Sentinel's power. During your battle with the Blessed Maiden, It split off a trace of Its frequency and hid it in a Gem. I'm sure you've seen it.
That Gem ended up in the Fractsidus's hands. Their whole play in Rinascita? Use it to bring back Leviathan.
It's always that group of lunatics...
I didn't think Leviathan would be that insidious...
So the Fractsidus has been incubating the Threnodian... How long has this been going on?
Perhaps longer than we can imagine. Even your clash with Cartethyia may have been scripted. A setup to give Leviathan a shot at slipping the Sentinel.
You know about that? Just who are you, Discord Slayer? I can't imagine Cartethyia keeping something that important from me.
Think of me as what I am... an avenger hunting Leviathan. As for the rest...
The next Harbinger of the Dark Tide has surfaced. Until we find him or her... we keep this quiet to avoid the worst-case scenario.
Our first priority is to find them. If we don't, the Dark Tide can overwhelm Ragunna again at any moment.
You're saying this Harbinger is behind all the Dark Tide creations we're seeing?
Not all. The Harbinger resonates with Rinascita's darkest emotions. Those emotions act as Anchors, pulling horror into form and speeding the tidespawn.
If the emotion is strong enough, and the Harbinger is near... Those things "evolve." They feed off the Harbinger's thoughts and memories to become more real. Some even start to look... human.
You've noticed it. The Tidespawn in Ragunna are starting to mimic us. Which means...
The Harbinger is in Ragunna.
We may be close to the Harbinger.
Exactly. I've always hunted the Dark Tide's creations—each one shares slivers of thought and memory. I kill them, and I take what they know.

They've been watching you. They want the Civilization Capsule. So... I followed you. Tracked your movements, figured if I stayed close, sooner or later I'd find the Tidespawn's "core." Maybe even the Harbinger.
The Capsule only unlocks with both the Sentinel and Threnodian's power, and it opened the moment you and that Gladiator touched it, so...
You think it's Avidius? But you carry the Dark Tide's power too...
Caution is a virtue in a hunter. You're right. The Dark Tide is in me... But Leviathan stopped counting me among the living a long time ago.
And this power... It's mine now. Who I turn it against is my choice.
When calamity strikes, I trust... you'll know exactly where to point your blade.
I'll trust you. For now.
I trust Cartethyia's judgement.
Heh... good. Then hunt with me. Until we give Leviathan a death worth talking about. Loud, messy, unforgettable.
The Sentinel's frequency is gone. I guess the time for talking is over. Leviathan's power is spreading, and this space is about to collapse. We need to find a way out.
Leviathan was born from the dark side of mankind's "longing for Unity." Their fear of the sea shaped Its likeness as a great sea creature.
Even at civilization's dawn, It had already tainted mankind's hearts. A primeval shadow lurking within the soul.
You're welcome to try and stop me. But me? I'm not stopping this hunt any time soon.
Only the people can decide where their future must lead.
You killed the Blessed Maiden before my eyes. Ragunna's disasters are tied to your actions... Now, tell me what I need to know.

The Sentinel reveals the origins of Leviathan and Rinascita. After long contemplation, They entrusted humanity with the right to decide the course of civilization, sacrificing Themself to become a shackle to bind the Threnodian. What followed, you already know well...

After Imperator's voice fades, Galbrena appears. You confront her, but she simply tosses you Cartethyia's pendant. Resonating with it, you confirm it is real, but the message embedded in Cartethyia's frequency only deepens the mystery: everything they have done is for one purpose—to defeat Leviathan.

Galbrena explains that Leviathan is on the verge of rebirth, incubated by the Fractsidus using the Threnodian's Gem. To prevent their plan from falling into the wrong hands, she cannot reveal more. She asks you to accept one truth: the Blessed Maiden is dead, and only by defeating Leviathan can she be "resurrected."

The priority now is finding the new Harbinger of the Dark Tide. Galbrena already suspects Avidius, but you still harbor doubts about the Dark Tide power she carries. She responds by saying that whether you trust her or not, her hunt will go on.
 
As the Sentinel's frequency fades completely and the space begins to collapse, you choose to form a temporary alliance with the Discord Slayer.
...If I told you I acted to save Cartethyia, would you believe me?
This place is protected by Imperator. For now, Leviathan can't hear us. This... is for you.
These things... They're all Tidespawn.
The Civilization Capsule was tainted by the Dark Tide. That's how I got in... followed the corruption straight through.
So you can enter the Dark Tide. No wonder we couldn't find you.
Yes, but the frequencies there are chaotic. I locked onto yours and followed it through the storm.
You have access to core data. But Avidius, he might've been swept into the frequency vortex. Hard to say where he's landed.
We need to move fast to find him. Figure out who he really is before the next wave of Tidespawn hits.
The exit is at the end of this wind trail. Stay on it.
The collapse is accelerating. Our way out is closing fast...
Faster. We're almost there...
Permissions detected—Arbiter.
Lifting imposed restrictions...
First Instance initiated. All probabilistic futures now revealed...
Outcome verified. Blueprint compiled. Advancing to Phase Two.
Commencing simulation. Attempting civilization fit: Rinascita...
Long time no see, Ragunna!
Mmm—mmm—! Can you smell that? Sweet o' Margherita's Restaurant. C'mon, c'mon, let's go stuff our faces already!
Let's take care of important matters first. You'll eat well soon, I promise.
Yeah, yeah, I know. We're here to find Cartethyia!
I still can't believe Tethys couldn't unlock the Sentinel's Relic we found in Septimont...
At least now we know it's called the "Civilization Capsule." It probably holds key legacy data left behind by the Sentinel.
Like some ancient data recorder, right? But Tethys said to unlock it we'll need... the Leviathan's power.
If it's really from the Sentinel, why do we need the Threnodian's power for that?
Maybe because they fused together at some point...
Oh well, guess that's why we need to find Cartethyia. Maybe she'll know a workaround...
The Black Shores warned that the waters in Ragunna are acting weird again. Gotta be extra careful.
And you know... something feels off in the city too. It's not as cheerful as when we left it.
I think things do feel more tense.
Might just be the weather.
There is a sorrow in the air...
Yeah, and they just threw a huge Carnevale not long ago too...
Hmm... you might be onto something.
Uh... since when did you get all poetic?
Amid howling winds, rising storms, and ghosts adrift, I heard the captain's call—
Look! Over there! Isn't that Brant and Roccia? Wow, the Troupe of Fools is putting on a show!
Hoist the sails, O humanity! The abyss and the summit have entwined. Your only path now is forward, bold and uncharted!
You stand on the precipice. Now is the hour to decide your fate—to plant the seed of your highest hope and watch it bloom into tomorrow.
Captain, why do you burn alone in your own flames?
If you do not first become ashes, how will you rebuild?

Embrace your fire. Embrace your grief. Go into your solitude! I love those who dare to create, who strive to transcend, for in doing so, their old selves are destroyed. Yes, so they might reach the shores of a new life!
To journey onward is perilous. To stand still is perilous. To look back is also perilous. To tremble and falter... is perilous.
Now, I begin to understand what truly makes a hero great. It is to stand before humanity's deepest sorrow and its highest hope.
Oh, how I love those whose souls remain rich and vast, even when wounded. Even when the smallest risk could spell doom, they leap without hesitation into the unknown.
Should you stand alone, suffering in the endless dark... Today, may you hold fast to every last ember of courage and hope!
Bravo! Bravo!
Life... is but a walking shadow.
A poor player, who struts and frets his hour upon the stage... and then is heard no more.
It is a tale told by fools, full of sound and fury... Signifying nothing.
