On your earlier journey through Septimont, you recovered the Sentinel's Relic from the Earthrend Wedge. To unlock it, you returned to the Black Shores seeking Tethys's aid. Its analysis revealed it to be the Civilization Capsule, likely containing the Sentinel's legacy data. But for reasons unknown, it requires the combined forces of both the Sentinel and the Threnodian to open. With no clear solution, you return once again to Ragunna, hoping to find answers from Cartethyia in the Inverted Tower.

Back in Ragunna, however, the atmosphere is thick with a strange tension. The only splash of color comes from a Troupe of Fools performance. As you and Abby pause to watch, Cristoforo's whisper slips into your ear...
"Slowly they join the crowd pilgriming toward the kingdom rising in the dark waves… Those blessed by the sea are ever doomed to bear its curse."
He cursed the Ragunnesi with a broken sonnet. No, more than that... He cursed all of Rinascita! Now, his curse is coming true...
Is he alright...?
Hello, {PlayerName}! Haven't you heard? Lately, the Ragunnesi have started having "nightmares." That's probably what he's referring to...
In my dreams I saw things... monsters I've never seen before...
Maybe it's because I've had my nose buried in that "mysterious playwright's unfinished draft"... those hobgoblins, banshees, and beasties are all carved into my mind now...
I thought it was just a dream. Just… <color=YellowD>imagination</color>. But then… one day, in the wilds… By the Sentinel, I saw one. Every infernal detail exactly as I dreamt it!
The playwright conjured illusions with words. Summoned ghosts, stitched nightmares into verses, turned phantasm into flesh! These are HIS verses... HIS CURSES!
Think about it! Monstrous fiends once trapped in myth and sonnet are now strutting on stage! He planted the seeds... centuries ago...
That mysterious playwright...
Mmm… sounds like a perfect premise for a ballad. I wouldn't mind meeting some of these storybook monsters myself.
Miss Ciaccona… you… you're not afraid of them?
Our souls are as eternal as theirs. How could they possibly harm us?
Besides, if the play is still unfinished, then the ending is ours to write, isn't it?
Finally, we made it…
...Where did those monsters come from?
Nothing's left… it's all ruined…
Hey, be glad we're still alive…
Papa… Mama…
Where are you…?
Miss Zani… I'm so sorry. I'll head back right away…
No worries. If you're feeling low, it's good to step out and get some air.
Ah, buongiorno, {PlayerName}. If you're here for banking... you'll have to wait.
Did something happen to her?
Thank you for your concern... I just had a vivid dream... about my grandmother who passed away some time ago.
When I woke up, I could still SEE her, sitting right beside me. Her smile was gentle... just like when I was little. She used to sing me to sleep with lullabies…
I told her how much I missed her, and she listened quietly, just like always. Then she stood up and said goodbye.
I saw her walk through a door. I tried to follow, but she stopped me. She said, "Don't follow me. And don't go gently through those gates." Then I woke up... again.
Was it a dream within a dream? Or was it a vision pulled from a <color=YellowD>memory</color>? But her face, her voice... it all felt so real...
...Capisco. I get it. I'll handle your desk. Go home. Take the day to rest.
Thank you, Miss Zani. But I think... my grandmother was trying to tell me something. That I can't stay trapped in grief and the past.
So I'll keep going with today's work. Sorry to worry you all.
Acolyte Phoebe, "Paradise"... It really exists...
But...
I saw it in my dreams. It was a revelation from the Sentinel...
A revelation from the Sentinel...?
Oh, hello there {PlayerName}. May the Sentinel's grace be upon you.
{PlayerName}... you're the Laureate of the Carnevale! That means you've heard the Sentinel's voice too! You can help me prove it, can't you?
My dreams must be divine revelations! I saw it all, the "City of Eternal Bliss" and "Path of Glorious Ascension." It was so clear...
That kingdom is the <color=YellowD>afterlife</color>. They told me that to gain entry, one needs only forsake all hope and call Their name...
But surely not everyone can enter the "true Paradise"...?
…You're right to remind me. We mustn't forget the Sentinel's teachings to live righteously here in the mortal world.
Acolyte Phoebe, let's hold fast to that. We will reach that "Kingdom of Eternal Bliss."
I've always believed "Paradise" was real, but...
If it is truly sacred and beautiful... why ask us to "forsake all hope" to enter?
Is that... Cantarella up ahead?
{PlayerName}? What brings you back to the Inverted Tower so suddenly?
Something's come up. I need Cartethyia's help to deal with it.
Did something unusual happen here?
I've only just arrived. For now, everything appears to be in order. I didn't come because of any disturbance.
There are matters I, too, need to discuss with Cartethyia...
At the Inverted Tower, you come across Cantarella, head of the Fisalias. Before you can ask her why she is there, the sharp sound of shattering windows pierces the air…
BANG—!
Cantarella...?
How could this happen...
...It all happened so fast.
...I'll make her pay. Blood for blood!
That woman...
Leviathan, I will deliver you... "her death."
(Why… Why does this scene match what I saw in that dreamland?)
Her Tacet Mark... Look, it's flickering! Cantarella, she's...
...No. Something's wrong. It's strange... I can't sense any frequency from her, and yet...
She is still resonating with... something.
A Resonator's frequency is usually gone when they die, right? This doesn't make any sense.
There's something even stranger...
Cartethyia's sword.
The shattered stained glass.
The shell casings on the floor.
None of this is adding up.
Cartethyia had her sword in hand... With her strength, how could she fall to an intruder like that? And... it doesn't look like she even tried to resist.
The Sword of Divinity, sealed with a portion of the Sentinel's power... Could what we're seeing be a result of that power of separation being awakened?
…The Inverted Tower itself is a sealed Sonoro. Only the Fisalias know it exists. So how did she find it?

And she broke through the stained glass from the outside. Physically, not by tearing through the Sonoro Sphere. But Cartethyia has complete control over the Tower. If someone had intruded, would she really not have noticed?
Spent casings... These traces, could they be from the Dark Tide?
You bet they are! I'd know that stench anywhere. And I caught the same frequency on that freak who jumped out earlier.
...Cantarella, you never did get to say what brought you here.
Cartethyia reached out to me with an urgent matter to discuss. She gave no details, only insisting that I come at once.
With the strange phenomena stirring across Ragunna, I feared it might be linked to the Dark Tide. Or Leviathan.
(Was what I saw... really just an illusion? I saw this... her death, exactly as it's happening now.)
(That woman... she was using Dark Tide energy. Could she be another Harbinger?)
...Whatever the case, we need to find the one who did this. I want answers.
Leave Cartethyia to me. I'll bring her back to the Fisalia estate and keep her safe. The rest… I entrust to you.
Abby, can you track the killer's frequency?
Abby, can you track the Dark Tide's frequency?
Heh, this nose? I could track the Dark Tide blindfolded! Let's follow the stench and hunt down this killer!

The strange woman you saw in Cristoforo's "illusion" suddenly appears and shoots Cartethyia right before your eyes. She then summons an unfamiliar Tacet Discord that blocks Cantarella's attack before vanishing. You want to go after her immediately, but instead choose to stay and try to revive Cartethyia, clinging to a faint hope... But Cantarella tells you that her frequency has completely vanished.
 
Rage flares within you. You realize that the scene matches what you saw in the "illusion."
 
Just then, Cartethyia's Tacet Mark flickers, sparking a glimmer of hope. Cantarella senses that although Cartethyia's frequency is gone, she is still resonating with something.
 
After steadying yourself, you uncover more anomalies within the Tower. To protect Cartethyia's body, Cantarella takes her to the Fisalia estate, and you and Abby set out to track down the killer.
That's weird. The trail ends here, but... Ugh... My head's starting to spin again...
It's the Dark Tide's energy messing with you again. You can rest, I'll search the area.
Abby? Asleep already... That drowsiness should've worn off by now. Another side effect of the Dark Tide?
Since leaving the Inverted Tower, Ragunna's sky... what happened to it?
Spear of Glory... pierce through!
Slipped away again.
By this spear, I vow to protect my allies and crush the hearts of the evil.
Avidius? What are you doing out here?
What any Gladiator of Septimont is born to do—hunting.
But you, Your Grace… You vanished without a word. What brings you back in such a hurry?
After what happened before...
Tell me what you're doing here first.
That's a long story. Let's speak of more pressing matters. Are you after the Thundering Mephis as well?
No. I'm tracking someone else.
(Describe Cartethyia's killer.)
Silver hair and violet eyes... cloaked in cursed, shadowlit flame. So you seek the one they call "<ano=TD Hunter>Discord Slayer</ano>."
Discord Slayer? Sounds like you know something about her.
Yes, she's on my radar. I suspect the recent Tacet Discord outbreak in Ragunna City is tied to her presence.
Wait, Ragunna City was attacked by a TD Outbreak?
Your Grace hasn't heard? It struck not long ago.
I had gone there in search of the "Quillbearer." While gathering information, the city was suddenly overrun... To be precise, they looked more like "spawn of the Dark Tide."
The outbreak has since been contained, but the Genesis Nexus was damaged. Without it, Common Echoes can't be used, and Ragunna is no longer secure.
The Montellis and the Order agreed to evacuate all civilians to Averardo Vault, where Private Echoes can still be deployed. It's the only way to protect them.
(A TD Outbreak, right after I left... But while I was there, I didn't even sense a ripple.)
The Thundering Mephis has fled! The path ahead is safe!
Thank you for your help, Gladiator! Averardo Vault isn't far from here. We can handle the rest of the journey!
Now, about the Discord Slayer you seek. The townsfolk shared some troubling whispers.
She may call herself that, but witnesses have seen her alongside swarms of Tacet Discords, leading them like troops into battle.
What's more, many have confirmed that the unrest across Ragunna coincides exactly with her appearances. The time and place match perfectly.
I even crossed paths with her on the road to Ragunna. I sensed a malicious frequency we both know well—the Dark Tide.
That very frequency is what led me here.
Of course. Even if she didn't cause the outbreak in Ragunna City, the connection is undeniable.
The Dark Tide is Rinascita's ancient enemy. If you're hunting her, allow me to join you and lend my aid.
Do you have any leads on her whereabouts now?
If I'm correct, the Thundering Mephis we encountered is also a Dark Tide creation. This frequency it left behind…
We can track it, and from there, draw out the Discord Slayer herself. To that end, we'll need this.
An Anchor Stone? You brought that all the way from Septimont?
Ha... A habit picked up on the hunt. You're no stranger to its use either, Your Grace.
Looks like I'm fortunate to be hunting alongside you again, {PlayerName}.

The killer's trail suddenly vanishes, leaving you no choice but to land and search the area for clues. Since leaving the Tower, the skies above Ragunna have looked distorted. As you ponder this, a Thundering Mephis ambushes from above. A spear knocks it away just in time. It is Avidius, your old comrade from Septimont.

You tell him about your hunt for Cartethyia's killer, and he tells you that soon after your departure, Ragunna City was attacked by Tidespawn. They destroyed the Genesis Nexus, making Common Echoes unusable. The Montelli family, after consulting with the Order, has begun to evacuate civilians to Averardo Vault. Avidius was escorting villagers from Egla Town through this area when he heard rumors about this killer. He, too, once crossed paths with her and sensed the Dark Tide's frequency within her. Together, you decide to hunt the Dark Tide's "Thundering Mephis," hoping it will lead you to the killer, the so-called "Discord Slayer."
Take note. Enemies ahead.
...Dark Tide creations. Grant them the oblivion they deserve.
What a hollow existence. Who "scripted" your delusions?
You mentioned you left Tetragon Temple to search for the "Quillbearer" here in Ragunna, right?
I grew weary of waiting. When I heard rumors of his presence in Ragunna, I came to find him myself.
No trace of him yet, but I've learned this much—Here, no verses were ever penned about me.
Then perhaps here in Ragunna, I am free to write my own story. Free to define my own "existence." Free to create a reality of my own.
This... this matters more than finding him. I will break free from his narrative and become the master of my own destiny.
Well said.
Now you're starting to sound like a true ruler.
I prefer you like this, honestly.
Your fate is what you want it to be. No one else gets to decide who you are.
No one has the right to dismiss your efforts and dreams with some absurd idea of destiny. You'll find your own Truth. I know it.
You honor me. I hope to prove worthy of that belief.
If my former "existence" was just a fabrication, an idea of some Hero of Heroes crafted to "Septimont's expectations"...
The Ragunnesi know not my name, past, nor the prophecy I once carried. Here... I am a completely blank page.

During your pursuit of the Thundering Mephis, you learn that Avidius originally came to Ragunna in search of the Quillbearer. But along the way, he discovered something far more meaningful, a chance to be the master of his own destiny…
The Anchor Stone is holding strong. Let's push forward.
Our destination is up ahead...
Where... am I?
That was Cristoforo's voice just now... Is this another one of his illusions?
Buling's bronze mirror isn't responding... Abby?
...No answer. This isn't like what happened in Septimont. Guess I can only keep moving and find out why.
Is that an entrance to a Paradimensional Tacet Field?
Ragunna's geographical records haven't documented this...
Do you feel that? That ominous energy... the Anchor Stone confirms the Thundering Mephis is hiding here.
Let's prepare to enter it.
That's our best lead right now.
Very well. I stand with you. Whatever comes, you have my sword.
Together, you and Avidius follow the trail of the Dark Tide and discover a Paradimensional Tacet Field that shouldn't be there. Seeking the truth, you step boldly into it…
What happened? Where's Avidius? We crossed inside at the same time.
It's the Thundering Mephis.
...Open... the gates...
So you just barrel in without thinking...
That voice... the Discord Slayer? Is this her trap?
Another illusion...
Focus. You are in an illusion. It's weaponizing your combat instincts.
Steady your resolve. Do not let its whispers sway you.
The pain and hallucinations are fading... Is she helping me?
Good. See that Cocoon in the center? The Thundering Mephis is just bait. That right there is the core of this domain.
Destroy it. Then the monster and this illusion will unravel together.

Within the Paradimensional Tacet Field, the illusion returns, disrupting your battle with the Thundering Mephis. From the darkness, the Discord Slayer's voice emerges, revealing a way to break free.

After breaking the illusion, you call out to her, but she doesn't seem to be there at all. Still, her words reach you: to prevent an even greater calamity, she too is searching for the Harbinger of the Dark Tide.
It worked... But—
Who are you?! And what did you do to Cartethyia?
...Now is not the time for stories.
But I'll tell you this. I'm here to kill the Harbinger of the Dark Tide. To stop a greater calamity.
I can't hear her voice anymore... Time to leave this place.
{PlayerName}! Are you unharmed? You vanished the moment we entered the Tacet Field.
I'm fine... So, it's gone? Avidius, did you see anything after we got separated?
The Thundering Mephis was nowhere in sight. But I did observe a peculiar figure.
I couldn't see his face clearly, but I heard him call himself... Caligula.
Caligula...?
Caligula was a tyrant feared throughout Septimont's history. Notorious for his cruelty that defied reason, the world remembers him as the "Mad King."
Legends say he wielded a vile black Resonance energy, and the worst calamities ever stirred by the Dark Tide all began with him.
He didn't fight it. He embraced it. Commanded its abominations. Bent them to his will. In the end, the people rose against him... and struck him down.
But not before he left a curse: "I shall become the very history and memory of Septimont. So long as fear lingers in your hearts, I shall return."
(The power to command the Dark Tide's creations... Only a Harbinger could do that.)
(That Discord Slayer said she's hunting a Harbinger to stop a greater calamity. If that's true, then everything happening across Ragunna might be tied to the Harbinger.)
(She pulled me from the illusion. If she's the cause of this chaos, why help me?)
(This isn't making sense. Harbinger... who are you, really?)
{PlayerName}, traces of the Dark Tide's frequency still linger where the Paradimensional Tacet Field collapsed.
The Anchor Stone is useless now. The signal is blocked by some sort of spatial layer.
Augusta said the Dark Tide spoke to her when it swallowed her whole. Maybe... I can learn something that way.
My telepathic ability should give me a way in.
Telepathy? Your Grace is versed in many arts. I don't doubt your abilities, but this is the Dark Tide. Reckless contact could—
I don't want to see... another tragedy like what befell Septimont.
Let me at least try.
It's just a meeting of minds.
I won't make direct contact.
We're falling behind. The Discord Slayer knows far more than we do. We need to find her, and fast.
I'm not letting any leads slip past us.

You reunite with Avidius after leaving the Paradimensional Tacet Field.

Though you entered together, what he saw within was the figure of Caligula, a tyrant reviled in Septimont's history, said to have wielded the Harbinger's power and brought calamity to the land. According to the Discord Slayer, the strange anomalies plaguing Ragunna are also tied to the Harbinger.

But who is the true Harbinger? The mystery only deepens. To uncover more clues, you turn to your telepathic skills to seek the Dark Tide's next move...
I can't see anything... I'm only getting jumbled voices.
Focus. I should be able to hear something.
Okay, everybody listen. Don't panic. Take the lift. It will bring you to safety...
The prototype Echoes in the depositories... Activate them all...
Those voices... Zani and Carlotta?
They're in Averardo Vault. The Dark Tide creations could be appearing there.
It's currently sheltering a large number of civilians...
Let's not waste time. We leave now.

You attempt to connect telepathically with the Dark Tide's traces. No visions appear, but you hear the voices of Carlotta and Zani, hinting that Dark Tide creations may be appearing in Averardo Vault, where countless civilians have taken refuge.
Zani, status of the evacuation?
Eighty percent of Ragunna's residents have been relocated.
But... the Troupe of Fools hit a storm while ferrying people from the Riccioli Islands. Rough seas out there.
Trust them to see it through.
Miss Carlotta! We've cleared the depositories as ordered. Ready to receive incoming supplies.
Good. Rinascita's greatest treasure has always been the people who built it. The next Cloudpuffer Express is due at any moment. Be ready to offload.
Understood, ma'am!
{PlayerName}.
Anything unusual happening here?
If you mean the incident in Ragunna... You've likely already heard. A hoard of Tacet Discords has overrun the city, and Common Echoes are out of control...
Evacuation here is still on track. No anomalies detected in Averardo Vault… yet.
Your assistance is appreciated, Sir Avidius. The residents from Egla Town have all been accounted for.
I am simply fulfilling my duty.
(Strange... I clearly sensed the Dark Tide's presence around here. So why does everything seem normal?)
BANG—!
Gunfire. We've got intruders.

You and Avidius rush there, only to find most civilians already evacuated, with no signs of Dark Tide creations. Just as doubt begins to set in, the sound of familiar gunfire echoes through the Vault...
These Tidespawn... They've evolved fast. Mutation? Or...
And sure enough...
Entering a restricted zone armed, without triggering a single alarm...
Be careful. Her abilities... are not normal.
...All this? By her hand?
All this in broad daylight? Brazen.
Let's not jump to conclusions just yet.
Fiction and reality are starting to blur. Don't put your faith in appearances.
That... is what they really are.
The Dark Tide can corrupt, and you carry its power. What proof do we have this isn't your doing?
You don't. Believe whatever you want.
By the sacred statues of the Divinity, evil shall know no peace. Only the righteous may taste eternity. Wickedness shall be purged by the blade, and those who consort with calamity shall fall...
Galbrena, demon wrought from ruin! You are not welcome here.
(Fenrico...? Why would he be here?)
You have slaughtered my flock and ushered in ruin. The Sentinel's wrath is already upon you. I will cast you back into damnation myself before your carnage spreads any further.
You should be howling in the Styx's depths, your soul aflame in the pit's cruelest fire... forever.
If you're offering me a shortcut back to hell, I'd honestly appreciate the favor.
Your heart holds no reverence for the Divine. Only... desecration and scorn.
Demon, your sins are ripe for judgment. By the Highest Will's command, I shall strike down all that you have wrought. Justice shall be done!
(She could've dodged that... but she took the hit to shield a civilian?)
(And Fenrico... he knew innocents were here, but didn't hold back at all...)
Righteous One, I come to cleanse Rinascita of a traitorous demon and avenge the blood debts of my people. Why raise your blade against me?
Rinascita teeters on the edge of collapse. Now, more than ever, we must uphold the tenets of Unity and Salvation.
The path to deliverance lies within the Civilization Capsule. Entrust it to me. By the authority bestowed upon me, I will open... the gates to the divine Paradise.
You shouldn't be here, Fenrico.
I never told you about the Civilization Capsule.
They might not know, but I do. You're the Harbinger.
Unless... You're not Fenrico at all. You... Who are you? What do you want?
...Bloodshed cannot be avoided. Blood must pay for blood. The path born of injustice must be fortified with further transgressions.
My goal is pure. Singular. All I've done, I've done so Rinascita survives the Divine reckoning and rises as a land free from sorrow.
No understanding is needed. Only faith. When all hope seems lost, I... no, we are the beginning and the end. The absolution. And the grace.
Hand over the Civilization Capsule.
...So the Civilization Capsule is your goal after all. Lost your patience, have you?
Death is the fruit of transgression. To resist it is to defy the will of the Divinity.
You? You and your Divinity cannot end me...
And these Dark Tide shams... Today, you face your reckoning.
I am the Enlightened One, anointed by the Divinity and crowned by Fate itself.
Huh, so you're the "core" of these abominations. Took long enough to hunt you down. Still pretending that mask isn't cracked?
Mocked by fate, whispering poison, a demon reviled by all! You wield the Dark Tide's power, yet you dare judge me?
It's too bad I'm not the one judging. If the Dark Tide's power isn't enough to convince... How about we try this?
"The Envoys declare the guilt, but Imperator is the only true judge…"
By the Light of Imperator... REPENT!
It's... the Light of Genesis?
Looks like the judgment is clear.
These <ano=Tidespawn>hollow existences</ano> don't need your mercy.
Protect the Civilization Capsule. That's what they're really after.

Following the gunshots, you witness what appears to be the Discord Slayer firing on civilians, only to realize these "civilians" are actually Dark Tide creations, Tidespawn, in disguise. Avidius accuses her of corrupting them with the very Dark Tide power she wields... 

Suddenly, Fenrico, meant to be stationed at the Fabricatorium of the Deep, appears. He calls the woman "Galbrena" and unleashes a devastating assault. Galbrena takes the blow to shield the civilians behind her. When "Fenrico" demands that you give him the Civilization Capsule, you begin to doubt his true intentions.
 
Tensions erupt. Though pierced by Fenrico's sword, Galbrena "rises from death." Dismissing his words, she hurls her lantern-like Terminal into the air, where it detonates, scattering the Light of Genesis. The burst reveals more disguised Tidespawn as battle erupts…
How were they able to disguise themselves as humans?
I've never heard of any possessing such abilities...
Their fangs are bared now. Don't hesitate. Let's end them all.
The one mimicking the Primus is the heart. Take it down, and the rest will collapse with it.
It's calling in more of them... We'll need to clear the rabble while waiting for our shot.
That which cometh from the sea... Shall walk upon the land...
It shall work great wonders and mark the flesh of Its faithful...
All who have ears to hear... Let them hear...
Avidius, you have received the blessing of my Master. Serve... your true Divinity.
I shall never...
Back down!
{PlayerName}, now!
Mistaking rebellion and recklessness for glory, like an inferior gem made precious only by how it glitters. Yes, even the castoffs of lesser branches can earn admiration if they shine bright enough.
She couldn't control the monstrous family legacy, so she turned to bravado. An armor crafted to hide her naivety and fear.
Fragile. False. But oh, how brilliantly a gem shines... in the instant it shatters.
{PlayerName}! Good... looks like you haven't run into too much trouble.
How long was I gone?
What happened when I was gone?
It hasn't been long since you disappeared into the rift. Once that thing masquerading as Fenrico was slain, the other Tidespawn didn't last.
That was the last one. With the family's Private Echo arsenal backing us up, we held the line just fine.
Surely you didn't think we'd fall apart without you? We Ragunnesi are made of sterner stuff than that. We handled those creatures just fine.
This Feilian Beringal... When the "core" was destroyed, the other Tidespawn lost their form. For now, the Vault is secure. At least until the next wave spawns.
I'd set up Order Terminals around the perimeter though. They'll detect humanoid mimics and prevent new Tidespawn from forming here.
Might I ask...
She's an ally for now.
You can trust her.
Where's that Gladiator from Septimont?
Sir Avidius made it out of the rift before you.
But... he didn't look great. Kept muttering about needing to "stop the crisis," then off he went, like a man on fire.
We need to track him down.
That one really knows how to pick his moments...
...Give me your hand.
I left a mark on Avidius during our fight earlier. With <ano=the Tacet Discord "Beholder">Balor's</ano> power, I can tap into his sight. We'll find his trail.
I must... move quickly...
Silence, you maddening whispers!
No... I'll be damned before I accept a fate like that...
There must be something left I can still do...
I won't let the same tragedy... happen twice...
...He's headed for Thessaleo Fells.
We've lost contact with Cantarella. The Beacon on her end appears to have been destroyed.
Dark clouds are gathering over Thessaleo Fells... Something is definitely wrong.
The two of us will go reinforce her.
You stay and protect the civilians here.
...Very well. We'll hold the line. Zani, call in the family's transport Echoes. We'll assist {PlayerName} where we can.
Don't complicate things. Put those Echoes toward supply runs instead.
Stay close. We're taking the sky route.

Escaping the Civilization Capsule with Galbrena, you learn that the Averardo Vault crisis has passed, but Avidius has vanished.

Using her abilities, Galbrena tracks his location, and together you ride her wind trail toward Thessaleo Fells.
Manipulating the air to form a wind trail... Is that your Resonance Ability?
One of them. I have the Tacet Discord <ano=half-bird half-woman>Harpyia</ano> within me.
Not an Echo, but a Tacet Discord itself... So you can absorb them directly?
You can say that. Balor is one of many.
One of many... Now I'm really curious about you and your abilities.
If we live through this, maybe I'll tell you. But right now...
We need to find the Harbinger. Do you know how we can identify them?
First things first, they'll be corrupted by the Dark Tide. But the signs aren't always so visible.
We'll have to look for associated side effects, and prepare for what they might bring.
We've entered Thessaleo Fells. I can already sense the Tidespawn up ahead...
That's... a Fisalia member! We need to help him!
Ah, it's {PlayerName}! Thank the Sentinel!
What happened here?
Dark Tide creations swarmed without warning. We were overrun before we could—
Move aside. We'll clean up.
Thank you! Lady Cantarella is still on the frontlines fighting. Would you please help to reinforce her position?
It's too late, my Lady... My mind... can't be fixed. Save your potions for those who still have hope...
I only beg... don't let me die a monster. Don't let me become Leviathan's puppet...
GhhhaaAAAAGH—! I see it... The End Times... Paradise... descending at last! AHAHAHAHA!
{PlayerName}... She is... Why are you with her?
Trust me. I'll explain later.
Let's handle the crisis first, and I'll explain later.
...The Fisalia bloodline's ties with Leviathan run too deep. Their ancient fears were the first to be awakened.
This is the true horror of the evolved Dark Tide. It feeds on human despair, warping that frequency to form Tidespawn.
Your family's "antidote" can still cure those lightly infected. But for those whose corruption runs deep, like him... Their frequencies cannot be reversed.
All we can offer is the dignity of dying as a human.
My Lady... don't let me burden... those who still have hope...
Matriarch of Fisalia, I understand the cruelty of such a choice. If you cannot strike the final blow... allow me.
...Fisalia blood must be ended by Fisalia hands.
Thank you... May glory return to the Fisalias...
Gilberto...
Cantarella...
The dead rest. The living march forward... The Fisalia will never forget its fallen sons and daughters.
Cartethyia remains secure in the Fisalia estate. But the Divinity's statue began whispering in our minds... Then came the Tidespawn soon after.
It was Leviathan's voice. Something has... awakened It.
It's very likely Avidius. Right now, everything is riding on us finding him.
That Septimontian Gladiator... Our scouts saw him advancing into the depths of Thessaleo Fells.
Lady Cantarella! {PlayerName}! Reinforcements have arrived!
Thessaleo Fells... It's already... Attention! Deploy all Acolytes to set up temporary Resonance Beacons. Scattering the Light of Genesis will hold back the Tidespawn!
Acolyte Phoebe! A cluster of Tidespawn is marching toward the depths of Thessaleo Fells！
{PlayerName}, Avidius is our mission.
I'll use my Forte to diffuse the family's antidote. It should help to mitigate the Dark Tide's influence.
We'll triage the wounded and fortify this position. The Order's Acolytes will clear a path for you. Please, you have to stop this!
Whether the Sentinel comes or not, we are Their will made flesh! We protect Rinascita!
O Light of Genesis, shield us! As we were at the dawn, so we stand today as the Sentinel's soldiers!

Tidespawn have already swarmed Thessaleo Fells. There, you witness the true horror of the Dark Tide. Facing Gilberto, who is on the verge of becoming a Tidespawn himself, Cantarella makes the painful choice to end his suffering and preserve his humanity in death.

The departed may rest, but the living must carry on. Avidius has already set out toward the depths of the Fells. Meanwhile, the Acolytes of the Order arrive in time to clear a path for you.
The Order's Acolytes are holding off the other Tidespawn. This is our chance to go straight for the source.
Ah... it's you...
Forgive me... that you have to see me like this...
What happened to you, Avidius?
Why has Thessaleo Fells become like this?
When the Civilization Capsule opened, I was dragged inside. A black frequency took hold of me. Swallowed me whole.
I saw Rinascita's beginnings, and the memories of... so many of its people.
I saw him too—Caligula. His face was like mine... He was my past, and the future I am meant to inherit...
...Leviathan used the Dark Tide's frequency to force those memories into him.
You said you'd become the master of your own destiny!
No one gets to decide who you are!
Yes, I once said... that I would write my own story... define my own "existence"...
But after I left that space, I suddenly felt the Tidespawn's movements. They were converging on Thessaleo Fells. I still wanted... to do something, anything, to stop the devastation.
But once again, I stepped blindly into the <ano=Fate>churning river of Chaos</ano>. The Fisalia's oldest memories awoke ahead of time. Because of me...
Countless Tidespawn emerged in my wake. I tried to drive them back, but I... overestimated myself... and was corrupted by them.
My hopes and dreams... all of it was real. So why? Why did it all come to this?
From Septimont to Ragunna, the blame lies with me. Perhaps this is the fate I could never outrun. Caligula's fate... It's calling to me!
Damn it. His mind is being consumed by Caligula's memories.
This is the role Fate wrote for me. Fate decrees I become the Mad King. So why... why should I reject its crown?
I am the one who glimpsed "Fate" itself... And now, I will reveal it to the world...
But who can truly know the mind of Fate... That is why I will become it. I will wear its face... that foolish, divine mask no mortal can comprehend.
I am the King... bearer of extraordinary power, risen from the dark tides. I shall quiet the waters and still the tempest...
I shall be crowned in glory... with the blood of the old king.

In the depths of Thessaleo Fells, you finally find Avidius. But he has already been implanted with Caligula's memories and deeply corrupted by the Dark Tide.

Sensing the stirrings of Tidespawn, he came here intending to stop the disaster. But his arrival awakened the Fisalias' oldest memories, calling forth countless Tidespawn...

Fate's cruel joke breaks his spirit. He descends into madness, becoming the Mad King Caligula, and raises his blade against you...
Avidius...
Unwritten One, I have no need for your pity.
From the deepest dark, I rise against your purest light. Let us see which is worthy of a true ruler.
If you believe he was once an honorable Gladiator...
Then fight him. Make him remember who he truly is.
I can write my own fate. And rewrite theirs.
I can quench their hunger... Or ignite their fury.
I will tear down this wretched, false world... and ride the only Truth that endures for eternity... Death.
I once scorned the weakness of others. Now I see... My own heart trembles just the same. How pitiful...
…His attacks are slowing!
His will is stirring within the Dark Tide. Don't let up!
Your memories. Your emotions... They weren't all lies. Reach for them. Find what was your Truth.
He's stopped... It seems…
Avidius! Remember who you are. Remember the man you wanted to become!
I am... human. Not one of these monsters...
This will be... my final glory...
Ah... He plays the role of captain. I have a theory. Tell me, do you think a performer will ever realize that he is part of a grander play?
He mistook his role for his true self, blind to danger and death alike. In the end, he led his crew... straight into the abyss.
Burning passion is but a beautiful kind of madness. When the curtain falls, he'll stand trial before the flames of his own arrogance.
Avidius! Remember who you are. Remember the man you wanted to become...
Fate lies within the Dark Tide. No one escapes the net it casts.
Wield the Dark Tide's power... And it will consume you in turn.
Come back... Come back to us.
I am... nothing like you...
Heh. You... How do you plan to resist us?
There must be a way...
That girl... Was she devoured by the Tide too?
Wait! If you keep going, the Dark Tide will swallow you completely!
I know... the Dark Tide devours everything. Assimilates everything. If I can't escape it... then I'll use it...
It's already flowing inside of me... So why can't I turn it against them? Why can't I... be the one who devours them?
These "false frequencies" need me to "survive." If this power... doesn't want to listen to me...
Then I'll show it who's the real boss.
Fate... It may be loud, but I don't think it's that strong. I... don't believe in it.
A memory left behind in the Dark Tide...?
She's right... In this war against Fate...
I still have a move to make.

Avidius's consciousness has sunk into the Dark Tide, struggling desperately against its whispers.

A girl passes before him... He sees that she, too, has been tainted by the Dark Tide. He moves to stop her, but watches as she turns the Dark Tide's power against itself, absorbing the surrounding Tidespawn.

The girl turns toward him. Before Avidius's eyes, she slowly merges with the image of Galbrena, then fades away.

While only a fragmented memory, it reminds Avidius that even in this war against fate, there is still something he can do...
I want it to be a story that gives people hope.
By my spear, I vow to protect my allies...
And crush... the hearts of the evil.
I will absorb all of the Tidespawn...
Kill me, and the calamity ends here.
Avidius!
There's no time, {PlayerName}.
Discord Slayer, I saw your past in the Tide. I know what you seek to do...
Take my power... And finish it.
That too is my wish.
I promise I will.
Give me all your bitterness.
We will... make them pay.
Now, why greet our reunion with animosity?
Before the tides of fate, we are all but… players on a stage.
Pathetic as he was, in his final moments...
He outran his fate.
A truly moving scene. A pitiful, doomed soul struggling to reclaim his fate in the final hour.
...Alas, his script was written long ago. In this scene, he was always fated to exit.
The Quillbearer finally takes the stage.
Avidius was your creation.
A lie told often enough becomes the truth. Weave memory, history, experience, and you can craft a man who "exists in the minds of others."
But to become truly "real"... that path was still far off. I merely gave him form, a mask of flesh and blood, fit to walk the world.
In the end, the breath that could give him life... was his alone.
Oh, a being born of lies, grasping for meaning in a world that offers none! Such a pursuit demands the courage to question the meaning of one's existence. Yes, it demands pain...
As creators go, you're rather heartless.
Have you no compassion for your own creation？
Did you not see? I did. His intentions, his ambitions, his darkness, his weakness... To lay a soul bare is not always an act of cruelty.
Humanity is Fate's plaything. I simply showed them the strings. I lit the fire, the hunger that might ignite their free will.
Through contradictions and conflicts, pain brings metamorphosis. Tragedy breeds transcendence. Only then may a soul rise beyond itself... and touch the gates of "immortality."

Should you still insist on my cruelty... well, high praise indeed. At the very least, it proves this story has stirred your pity and fervor. That alone earns you the right to read through to the final act.
Go then. To Septimont. The curtain is drawing. There, I shall rewrite Rinascita's fate... with the Dark Tide as my ink.
Will you suffer in silence beneath Fate's poisoned arrows, or rise to defy this world's endless trials? I, too, await your final answer.
You brought ruin to Rinascita. You think you're just walking away?
My stage lies elsewhere. In this scene, I am but a herald.
But since you're so eager, I'll leave you with one final clue. I've never had much fondness for overwrought dramatic irony.
The Dark Tide has already tainted the Civilization Capsule. It no longer requires the Threnodian's authority to be opened… Just a single drop of the Tide's nectar will suffice.
So tell me, how could an existence born of the Dark Tide ever serve as its "Anchor of Reality"?
Be forewarned. When dark waters recede, the truth beneath the surface... shall come to light.
I hope you understood what he meant.
Wait, so Avidius wasn't the Harbinger?
The Harbinger of the Dark Tide is the Anchor of Reality of all Tidespawn. That means it must be a real, existing person.
When I was absorbing the Tidespawn, I felt it. Avidius was also born of the Dark Tide.
Then why didn't the "Light of Imperator" reveal his true form?
Because his intentions and words were real. He may not have shone as brightly as the sun, but in walking beneath its light, he still caught its glow.
And that unshakable resolve not to become a pawn of the darkness, even unto death... That created his own Truth.
That's why he played right into the Quillbearer's hands. A scapegoat, the perfect "sacrifice" to bury the truth. All his noble wishes were twisted. Such cruel irony can rot for all I care...
He still stopped Ragunna from falling to the Dark Tide.
He still succeeded in changing his fate.
That playwright is the true culprit.
Avidius shouldn't have had to bear such a fate... I will carry on his fight. I'll keep writing the story he believed in, the story that gives people hope.
Yes. As he wished... we must stop the greater tragedy that's coming.
Let's return to Cantarella and check on the wounded. If Avidius wasn't the Harbinger, that means we missed something...

In the end, Avidius sacrifices his life to stop the Dark Tide outbreak in Ragunna. At last, the hidden Quillbearer, Cristoforo, reveals himself. He invites you to step into the final act and leaves you with a cryptic riddle.

Galbrena hands you the paper crane Avidius left behind. Although she sensed Avidius was a creation of the Dark Tide, the Harbinger itself must be "a real, existing person," which means the true Harbinger is someone else.

The Light of Genesis never revealed Avidius's true form because he had already created his own Truth—one defined by his humanity. You mourn his fate and vow to keep his belief that fate can be defied alive...
The Tidespawn have fully retreated. The situation around Thessaleo Fells is improving.
Seems like the Order has already transported most of the wounded to Averardo Vault.
But... as for the rest... the scars Leviathan left on their minds still need time to heal.
It has returned... Just as before...
We can't... we can't defeat It...
Believe in the strength of humanity.
There's nothing we can't overcome in this world.
That's what Leviathan wants you to think.
You are... I know you... Yes, you've defeated It before!
The whispers... the whispers disappeared once. I heard what you did in Jinzhou. You helped them drive away the Threnodian there...
Yes, Threnodians are powerful, terrifying even... B-but not invincible.
You're right. Now is not the time to give up...
Damn it... Is this all I can do? Just stand here... and watch my friends die in front of me?
...{PlayerName}, thank you. Truly. But... if I may, can I ask you something?
I understand why they chose to resist the Threnodian, even if it meant death. But after everything I've seen... Tell me, how do you carry on in the face of so much loss?
What keeps you going? What is it that... What is it that you hold onto?
I mourn their sacrifice too, but...
To honor their sacrifice, we have to keep fighting.
To build a world without sacrifice, we have to keep fighting.
So that's what you believe... Thank you for sharing that...
You're right... My friends wouldn't want to see me like this, so hopeless and defeated...
Even if I'm dragged into the Dark Tide itself... I'll make damn sure I tear a piece out of the Threnodian first!
Cantarella went inside to prepare that "antidote"... She should be finished now. Time to find her.
I... I'm so scared...
Everything's okay, don't worry.
Ah, it's you, the great hero {PlayerName}!
...But... You can't save everyone...
Don't go... Don't leave... Don't abandon us...
...Cartethyia?
Mortals need salvation... Mortals need unity...
Righteous One... open the ascendant gates for me...
This world doesn't belong to you, Leviathan.
Chimera!
How are you feeling, {PlayerName}?
But, Lady Cantarella, we all saw it… just now—
Enough. I told you to stand down. You've withstood the "whispers" before. Will you forget your loyalty to your comrades in the face of fear?
I'm sorry, Lady Cantarella... and {PlayerName}. We... We lost our composure...
Leviathan is a master at finding the cracks in one's spirit to tear it asunder. Go do what you must. I'll handle this.
What just happened...?
Certain emotions between you and the others resonated. Your Tacet Mark opened a "portal," pulling you into another illusion.
That "portal" fed on your presence to spread malice and fear... But before it could fully take shape, I broke into your illusion and shut it down.
I saw Fenrico, Mya, and Cartethyia... They all passed through that gate. What exactly lies beyond it?
That's the realm Leviathan created. The Journeying Paradise.
If those gates opened because of me...
Then does that mean—
Avidius was Cristoforo's decoy. He planted that decoy in Septimont for years... When the waters recede, the truth shall come to light...
{PlayerName}... you are the new Harbinger of the Dark Tide.
Stand down.
I said, stand down. Fall back.
Cantarella told me stories about you. She said you're just like the heroes in the adventure tales. Brave and determined...

You and Galbrena make your way back, checking on the wounded along the way.

While comforting a little girl, your Tacet Mark suddenly flares with an ominous glow. The girl transforms into a Tidespawn, and everything around you freezes. A whisper from Cartethyia brushes against your ear, and a vast gate appears in the distance. Galbrena breaks from her stillness and erupts in flames, firing a bullet at the gate while summoning a Tacet Discord named Chimera to strike at you—

You snap awake from the "illusion" to see the terrified and hostile faces of the Fisalias before you.

Cantarella calms them and explains that your emotions resonated with those around you, causing your Tacet Mark to open a "portal" that dragged you into the illusion. This "portal" fed on your presence to spread malice and fear into the real world. But before it could fully take shape, Galbrena broke into the illusion and stopped it.

A chilling realization strikes you. If that "portal" opened because of you, then it can only mean one thing. The Harbinger of the Dark Tide... is you.
This is the family "antidote," made to suppress Leviathan's spiritual corruption. Take it now.
I've learned about Leviathan's current state from Galbrena. The Fisalias have resisted the Threnodian for a century. Its whispers aren't undefeatable. We will defeat It.
So this is the worst-case scenario you warned me about.
You must have suspected something for a while now.
I still find this hard to accept.
Leviathan needs a Harbinger with enough influence to spread Its "gospel." You're the Laureate of Ragunna and the Hero of Heroes in Septimont. That's more than enough to be Its first choice.
Your path overlaps with Avidius. The Tidespawn are shaped by the Harbinger's thoughts and memories. Neither the Thundering Mephis nor the Feilian Beringal are native to Rinascita. So...
You once said the Harbinger had to be corrupted by the Dark Tide. But I still don't show any signs of corruption...
I suspect... the one corrupted might not be "you."
Phew... the Dark Tide, huh? I ate some back at the hunting grounds. It tasted kinda funky... made me super sleepy. Ever since then, I've been having the weirdest nightmares...
Abby must have absorbed many other frequencies. So while the Dark Tide's frequency lay in wait... it was masked by the others.
It makes sense. You two share life and energy. As the primary in this bond, your frequency has been overriding Abby's... Leviathan planned for this.
{PlayerName}, did I... did I do something wrong?
You've always done great, Abby.
It's not your fault, Abby.
We made a call when it mattered. I asked you to absorb the Dark Tide. We couldn't have known what it would become. You didn't do anything wrong.
I see... I-I can go hungry if I have to, but you, {PlayerName}, you better not get hurt...
The real threat is Leviathan. If we want to end this for good, we kill It and destroy Its Paradise.
...From what I know, Leviathan manifests Its kingdom by flooding Rinascita with the Dark Tide. That's how it turns the real world into the Journeying Paradise.
But we've already secured Ragunna and Septimont. The Fabricatorium and the hunting grounds are both stabilized... So why is this Paradise still there?
Everything you've done has slowed down or maybe even sealed off some of Its pathways. That's why Leviathan is resorting to Its "final plan."
This so-called divinity is more devious than humanity realizes... The Paradise you saw is not of this world. It stands... within the Dark Tide.
Matriarch of Fisalia, you have guarded this truth for over a century. Now... we need your insight.
I couldn't see the truth until the Threnodian's whispers finally quieted. Only then did those ancient records, once twisted beyond recognition, begin to make sense again.
Leviathan... was born from the shadows in our hearts. From our longing to connect and belong. It took the shape of a sea creature, because nothing frightens us more than the deep.
It used faith to spread a spiritual plague. All the while, it has been feeding on our pains. Fear, despair, sorrow...
Our ancestors believed Leviathan survived by absorbing these emotions. Little by little, it burrowed into Rinascita's collective unconscious.
They said the Dark Tide is that subconscious made real, an ocean of shared trauma. That's why... they called Leviathan the "Master of the Deep."
I heard them. All those voices in the Dark Tide. And before I touched the gate... I felt it. Fear. Sorrow. Like it was pouring out of the people.
The stronger the conflict, the deeper the emotion it stirs. That's what shapes our memories and subconscious...
That's why the Playwright kept forcing Rinascita into conflict. Every tragedy, every struggle... it wasn't random. It was all to keep feeding Leviathan.
The End Times are drawing near. The Ragunnesi cling to hopes of a blissful afterlife. Septimontians have long believed in "another world" that begins after death...
Leviathan may have drawn from these subconscious beliefs, "aligning" with those desires to fabricate a false future and afterlife within the Dark Tide—the illusion of the Journeying Paradise.

If that's true... once the people's belief in the End Times reaches its zenith, their consciousness will align entirely with Leviathan's vision. Like Gilberto, and the others who were fully corrupted...
Its power of assimilation will grow stronger, until the line between imagination and reality vanishes. The Journeying Paradise will descend upon the world, just as before.
...When it does, every soul in Rinascita will be unified under Its control. No thoughts. No will. Just blind devotion... No different from the Tidespawn.
...So how do we fight Leviathan?
You saw it in the illusion. It cast aside the Sentinel's form and took on Cartethyia's. That means... The first step in her plan is complete.
Leviathan is still watching the real world. Because of the "Mark of the Dark Tide," It can read your thoughts. So for now... we can't share the full plan with you.
But you must have sensed it by now. Your connection with Rinascita runs deeper than I, or even you, ever imagined...
You're not just the Harbinger of Despair... You've become a vessel of Rinascita's hope.
So go. Gather every last flicker of it. This is a "hunt," yes. But it's also more than that. It's a war of spirit. Of light against shadow. Hope against despair.
To take Leviathan down, our belief has to be unshakable. If there's doubt in your heart... then stop. A new path won't reveal itself unless you're ready to walk it.
For now, the Dark Tide in Ragunna is under control. And I think... I've figured out what It plans to do next...
Before the bells of Paradise ring, I'll buy you time. When you're ready, head to Septimont.
Just like the Playwright said, when the moment comes, everything—fiction and reality, past and future—will converge there.

As long as we can identify the problem, there's a way to fight back. You carry the Sentinel's power within you. That's keeping the corruption at bay for now. What's left... are the hallucinations and whispers.
Abby does... carry the Dark Tide's frequency...

Even after drinking the Fisalia's family "antidote," your heart remains unsettled.

Galbrena's words help reveal that it is Abby who has been corrupted by the Dark Tide. Because you share life and energy, the corruption passed to you as well. Now, the only way to reverse it is to defeat Leviathan and destroy Its Paradise.

From the Fisalia's ancient records, you learn that the Dark Tide is the "subconscious ocean of the Rinascitans' shared trauma." You also uncover Leviathan's final plan to bring Its Paradise to the world. Galbrena and Cartethyia have a plan to stop this, but because you bear the Mark of the Dark Tide, Leviathan can read your thoughts. For this reason, they cannot reveal everything to you. Yet throughout this journey, you have felt the trust others have placed in you. You are not just the "Harbinger of Despair," you are also a vessel of Rinascita's hopes. In this war of spirit, only an unshakable resolve can stand against Leviathan.

Galbrena spreads her wings and takes flight. With the Dark Tide in Ragunna contained, it's time for the next step. You prepare to head to Septimont. Everything will come to a head there.
Members of Fisalia will relocate to Averardo Vault. When I meet with Carlotta and the others, I'll relay what we've learned about Leviathan.
As for the Harbinger matter... I'll keep that confidential to prevent further panic. That's likely why the Discord Slayer has kept it quiet.
From what I understand of Leviathan... It chose you not because It can control you, but to hinder your progress.
But looking into your eyes, I see... no matter the obstacle, you won't stop moving forward.
I have some questions I wanted to ask you.
I'm preparing to leave for Septimont.
I still have some matters to attend to.
Mmm. There are still some ancient records I have yet to fully decipher. If you're interested, I'll share what I can.
About Leviathan...
About the Dark Tide...
About the Harbinger of the Dark Tide...
About Cartethyia and Galbrena...
I'm preparing to leave for Septimont.
I still have some matters to attend to.
The records say that since the dawn of civilization, Leviathan, under the guise of Imperator, wormed Its way into the Rinascitans' faith and thought.
When discovered by the Sentinel, Leviathan hastily unleashed the first Dark Tide, attempting to harvest the civilization.

In that battle, the Sentinel was assimilated by the Threnodian. But in doing so, Imperator bound Leviathan, entrusting <ano=the "lantern" filled with Their power>the First Relic</ano> to the First Primus.
The calamity was quelled by Napoli the Second, but Leviathan's "poison" left deep scars on Ragunna and Septimont.
Since then, every Primus has upheld the "Oath of Silence" to hide the truth—the people once worshipped the Threnodian.
And yet... even in chains, Leviathan used "twisted faith" to spur conflict. Suffering, turmoil, and struggle that followed all continued to feed It...
The "Dark Tide of this world" was a calamity wrought by Leviathan's hand. But the heads of our family have long suspected that Rinascitans have always harbored a "spiritual Dark Tide."
It takes root in the shadows, deep in the valleys of our fears. When the Threnodian draws forth enough anguish, It may call a Dark Tide into being. And in the terror of calamity... It feasts.
The "whispers" once planted an idea in our minds: the Dark Tide is fate, and Leviathan its keeper. In hindsight... perhaps it was not so far from the truth.
Our collective subconscious flows endlessly through the Dark Tide, by day and by night. Leviathan lies hidden in its depths, weaving unseen changes, delivered to us through our dreams.
When those altered bits of us rise to the surface, they slip into the waking mind. Our choices and actions were then guided by a will without form.
I fear Leviathan has reclaimed full control over the Dark Tide. Our every thought and feeling... may now fall beneath Its gaze… and bend to Its will.
Galbrena and Cartethyia hesitated to reveal their full plan... and perhaps this is why. As she said, only an unshakable will can stand against Leviathan.
The Harbinger of the Dark Tide is chosen by Leviathan, an Anchor of Reality that summons the Tidespawn. A vessel, too, for spreading Its "gospel"… and gathering Its "sustenance."
The Harbinger is condemned to wander the Dark Tide's illusions. And as the corruption seeps deeper, the boundary between dream and reality begins to unravel.
In time, they may mistake the living for monsters… or even strike down those dearest to them in illusion. Tragedies born of confusion...
To others, and even to themselves, they may come to embody "malice and fear" itself. If they surrender to that fate, the Dark Tide will devour them whole... leaving behind nothing but a puppet.
The records speak of Harbingers who resisted until the end. To spare others from greater harm, they each made the same choice... To take their own lives.
{PlayerName}, you... No, there must be another way. We must bring an end to Leviathan.
Cartethyia's condition... can only be described as "death." For now, we must accept that truth.
Galbrena confided in me, though only in veiled strokes, her intentions. In truth, I know no more of her than you do.
I only know she bears the rare ability to move between this world and the Dark Tide's illusions. It was through that gift she was able to pull you back.
What I saw in her eyes... was unwavering focus. The kind of resolve found only in those who have truly stood against the Dark Tide.
But in those depths, I also saw a blackened will... Absolute, heedless of means or cost. I wonder… what crucible of blood and fire shaped it.
Thankfully, those flames are not aimed at us. Her sights are clear. She simply waits for the moment to pull the trigger.
To us, she is an ally worthy of trust. Should danger arise… you may trust her with your back.
I understand Septimont calls for your aid even now.
As Galbrena said, we must gather every last flicker of hope. We will stand with the Montellis and the Order to face the crisis in Ragunna. This front is ours to hold.
If your strength wanes... do not overburden yourself. Safe travels, {PlayerName}.
Gentleness born of delusion. A beautiful, sorrowful fantasy. She tried to confront an ancient curse with blind devotion and silence...
But fear has eaten away at her soul. Illusion stripped her of freedom. And her tears have long since left her nowhere to hide.
What she needs is not light, but a long, dreamless sleep.
A pure heart blindly devoted to a deity on the verge of extinction...
Yet the true eternal Divinity embraces all. It washes away everything, be it joy or sorrow or hope or obsession.
She realigned her faltering faith, and in doing so, claimed her "redemption."
The phases of the moon wove her luminous gaze, yet she insists on using that light to peer into fate's menacing face.
Her eyes were destined to be burned. All who overstep cannot escape its wrath.
Now, neither she nor her moon will ever be whole again.
A valiant and determined ruler... On the battlefield where life and death collide, a faint ember lingers. Flickering, barely alive.
Conquest and slaughter walk hand in hand. Sooner or later, she will be consumed by the very sun that nurtured her.
Beyond her throne lies nothing but withered bones. If she cannot endure such loneliness, then she must learn to descend her own steps and enter "their world."
Amid the endless cycle of surging tides, she plunges into fate's swirling maelstrom once more.
Soon, she will wear a new crown—one ordained by fate, never to be defied.
Her fate was written long ago. What remains is but a fleeting moment of stolen peace.
What you see before you... is fate itself.
And now, with every step you take, you stir the tides into motion.
Is it fate that rules over man, or man who commands fate?
I await your answer to this question...
Cristoforo... He won't sway me. I've got to keep going.
What is this place?
Through me, walk the Path of Glorious Ascension... Through me, enter the City of Eternal Bliss... All who enter... must first forsake all Hope.
(These Tacet Discords... why aren't they attacking?)
Harbinger... Open... The gates of Paradise for us...
You'd better leave. This place... isn't leading to any "salvation."
Leviathan, I will deliver you... "her death."

Cristoforo's whisper pulls you into unconsciousness. When you awaken, you find yourself in a mysterious realm.

Visions of fallen companions appear along the path as Cristoforo's whisper continues. Fighting the unease, you reach a lake where in the distance a vast "Paradise" hangs above.

As you stand in disbelief, several Tacet Discords emerge behind you, not to attack, but to chant the title "Harbinger." Then, from the darkness, a strange woman steps forward. With a single demonic arm, she unleashes a surge of flame that casts you from the realm. Her final words: "Leviathan, I will deliver you... 'her death.'"
{PlayerName}... {PlayerName}!
We could try this... "Nightmare Awakener"—
I'm up, I'm up!
Good, you're all okay...
I think I saw Paradise...
You're finally awake, {PlayerName}! One second I'm fine, the next my head's spinning and you're face-down on the ground...
I'm fine. What I saw, though…
(Recount what you saw)
Hmm... Sounds like the same thing happening to the people here.
From what I've heard, many Ragunnesi have been having peculiar dreams lately. Even some of our Troupe members too.
The details vary, but they all end the same way... the fall of Rinascita.
And it's not just in dreamland either... {PlayerName}, I'm not sure if you've heard, but there have been strange rumors appearing across Rinascita lately.
Even in Septimont, folks claim they've seen Tacet Discords not of this land in the wilds, or the ghosts of their ancestors.
Thanks to all these oddities, the mood in Ragunna has gone sour.
The Troupe performed today because Brant thought a new play to lighten the mood might give the people some hope.
But here's the odd part. Only Rinascitans seem to be having these dreams. Visitors are spared... the same should be true of you.
Have any of you had similar dreams?
Have you seen other anomalies like this?
I'll get to the bottom of what's happening.
Well... Not Brant or me. But someone in the Troupe has. They said they dreamed of sinking into an enormous, black ocean...
The Tacet Discords in the Stormy Sea have been more restless lately. And the "siren's" songs? Well, they've started sounding an awful lot like the Order's hymns...
We'll keep gathering intel on our end. Might be worth asking around the city to see who else has been experiencing this.
Rinascita's tides don't lie. Watch your back, {PlayerName}.
(What were those Tacet Discords whispering about? Gates of Paradise... and the word "Harbinger." Could they mean the "Harbinger of the Dark Tide"?)
(The only "Harbinger of the Dark Tide" is Fenrico. But he should still be sealing the Dark Tide at the Order's Fabricatorium...)
(That figure I saw... and Cartethyia's murder...)
(I came back to find her, so I should look for her first. She might know what's at the root of all this.)

You regain consciousness under the Troupe's care. What happened feels like an "illusion," but the Troupe members tell you that many in Ragunna have suffered similar "symptoms." Meanwhile, across Rinascita, anomalies have begun to appear.

You recall what you saw in the "illusion": the chanting Tacet Discords, the strange woman, and a vision of Cartethyia's murder. Maybe you can search the city for clues... or maybe the answer lies with Cartethyia herself, the very reason you returned to Ragunna.
A few of our friends are already in the city. Seems they're digging into these incidents too.
I'd suggest having a little chat with them first. We'll gather more intel on our end as well.
Keep moving! Stay in line and follow instructions. No dawdling. I promise... we will return soon.
Well, well. Is that you, Unwritten One? So you did decide to grace us after all. Thought maybe you'd forgotten about us.
Let's get back to business.
Still the same Iuno, I see.
Now's not the time for teasing, Iuno.
Did you come straight from Ragunna?
I did. Has it begun here too? I see you're starting evacuations.
An unannounced High Tide. But that term doesn't even begin to cover it.
No signs. No patterns. The Dark Tide's spawn are surfacing at random... even outside the City of Septimont.
It doesn't make sense. The Earthrend Wedge is still holding back the Dark Tide at its depths... At any rate, Augusta's already led a team to the Sanguis Plateaus to investigate.
As for me, I'm helping out here. Someone has to stop the panic from turning into a stampede.
It's not just Septimont. Ragunna has been hit too...
(Brief Iuno on Ragunna's situation...)
I see, Ragunna too… And Avidius... He never bent the knee, never played by the rules. Why is it that fate always strikes hardest at those who dare to defy it?
People still don't remember you?
You still can't give new prophecies?
I'm just a helpful, ordinary person now, helping the Temple with the evacuation. No more restraints from the Tetragon. No prophecies... I admit, I've never felt freer. It's just...
It's not just me. No Priestess can see Septimont's Auguries anymore. In our visions, it's all gone. Just blank.
The last prophecy ended with, "The Dark Tide will erupt and engulf all of Septimont." After that... nothing. And with this abnormal Dark Tide behavior, people are starting to fear the end is upon us.
But maybe… that doesn't mean the end is near.
A blank future could mean a new beginning.
Nice thought. If only more people shared your hope.
But in the face of something this vast and unknown, fear is only human. We can't blame them for trembling.
Aquila, any word?
…The Dark Tide has been spotted at the Three Heroes' Crest.
How bad is it?
Bad. It's the highest point in the Sanguis Plateaus, well beyond the Blightcloud's reach. The Dark Tide has never touched it before.
They call it the Three Heroes' Crest for the three Heroes of Heroes who once stood there. Many believe their blessing has kept it one of the few sacred places the Dark Tide cannot reach.
If even that place isn't safe... We need to see it with our own eyes.
Worry not, Honored One. The Senate will oversee the evacuation. Please, go assist the Ephor.
We may lack your strength, but we will not stand idle. We will do everything we can to hold the line!
We were born in Septimont. Resistance runs in our blood, and we were raised beneath the shining legacy of heroes. You think we'll sit back and let ruin claim us?
We're counting on you, Honored One!
That's why I'm here.
For Rinascita!
I won't shame the title of Hero of Heroes.
I hate to admit it, but the current Senate's grown a backbone. Cowards wouldn't last long working under Augusta, anyway.
Come on, {PlayerName}. Let's find her.
But Septimont still needs us too...

After parting ways with Cantarella, you set out alone for Septimont City.

By the time you arrive, the city is already preparing for war. At the gates, you encounter Priestess Iuno helping to evacuate civilians. You recount what happened in Ragunna, and she tells you that the Priestesses can no longer deliver new prophecies. Because of this, many people now believe the apocalypse is nigh.

Griffrex "Aquila" brings unprecedented news from the Plateaus: the Dark Tide has erupted near the Three Heroes' Crest. Named after three Heroes of Heroes, the peaks have been one of the few sacred places in Septimont untouched by the Dark Tide. You and Iuno decide to head to the Plateaus to meet Ephor Augusta, while the Senate stays behind to oversee the evacuation. In this time of crisis, everyone is doing everything they can to hold the line.

Now, mount the Griffrex with Iuno and fly toward the battlefield.
Traces of the Dark Tide are everywhere...
The Tidespawn always shows up where we least expect them and never slow down. Our warriors are stretched thin just trying to hold the lines.
Even though the Common Echoes here don't depend on the Genesis Nexus, they're still breaking down due to the Dark Tide's corruption.
Don't wear that face. These are Septimont's warriors. They don't fall easy.
There, the Three Heroes' Crest. Looks like they just finished a battle.
Let's pick up the pace. You fought beside Augusta before, and you once led the battle to defeat the Sovereign. Your presence will rally them.
Look! It's {PlayerName}, the Honorable One!
My fellow warrior! You came!
It's been a while, Lupa.
My fellow warrior! It's been a while.
May applause greet you!
Feels like just yesterday we were fighting side by side in the Colosseum. And now look at you, "Hero of Heroes" and all. Didn't see that coming!
{PlayerName}, your arrival is appreciated.
Oh, let me introduce you. Augusta, this is...
Iuno. We know each other.
What? When?
Did... everyone's memories recover?
A lot happened while you were off adventuring. You missed some fun.
Recover...?
Ahem, never mind that. Didn't I say before? Never underestimate my charm.
It is strange… From the moment we met, it felt like we were cut from the same cloth. Like we'd known each other before. She might seem unmoored, but when the storm hits, she holds fast.
Alright then, Augusta. What's the situation?
Theoretically, the Dark Tide flows here from the Blightcloud above the Plateaus. High Tides have always followed its movements.
But this time, nothing. No Blightcloud anomalies. No frequency fluctuations near the Three Heroes' Crest.
We always knew the Earthrend Wedge was a stopgap as we continued to search for a permanent solution. But this... eruption without warning defies everything we thought we understood.
We repelled the first wave and set up an Anti-Corrosion Ward using Anchor Obelisks.
Have you discovered anything?
The Fractsidus is incubating the Threnodian...
The Threnodian is on the verge of rebirth...
The Fractsidus, always scheming in shadow. Its wicked ambitions know no end.
Your Excellency! Another outbreak! Tidespawn heading straight for the camp!
Heh, Leviathan won't spare us any time to breathe.
Let's go. My sword is ready.
I wouldn't miss this fight.
It's been too long since we stood shoulder to shoulder in battle.
Warriors! The battle horns sound once again. Let those who defy Septimont tremble at our fury and fall before our valor!
What?! But... I thought the Sovereign's death would sever the root cause of the Paradise's descent. But Leviathan's rebirth… This is a whole new thread of fate...

From high above, you and Iuno witness the Dark Tide's onslaught. Yet the warriors of Septimont stand unbroken. Their unyielding spirit stirs hope in your heart.

The Griffrex dives, bringing you swiftly to the battlefield. There, you reunite with Augusta and your old partner, Lupa. Iuno, once "forgotten," seems to have rekindled her friendship with Augusta as well.

Augusta explains the abnormal Dark Tide surge at the Three Heroes' Crest. To hold it back, they've set up Anti-Corrosion Wards using Anchor Obelisks. You share your own intelligence, but the Tidespawn strike again before more can be said. As Septimont's Hero of Heroes, you leap into the fray without hesitation. Inspired by your resolve, the warriors rally behind you. It's time to show the enemies once more the fury of Septimont.
Oh, it's {PlayerName}...
I heard you ran into a rough storm at sea...
We did right by the trust they placed in us. We got all the folks from the Riccioli Islands to safety.
Compared to what you're about to face, that storm was nothing.
Sailing into the unknown is never easy. Sailing through the Dark Tide? Even worse.
Pero stocked up on gadgets. You can take whatever you like!
I like gadgets!
Bring me a few more Training Swords!
This is all we can do for you right now… Please come back safe, {PlayerName}.
Pero, Pero...
Oh! Take these Shell Credits too. They're lucky charms, or so the old sailors say. Take as much as you like. A little luck never hurts.
To us, {PlayerName}, you've always been the protagonist. Never forget that.
…It's not being the protagonist that makes you brave. It's your courage that gave you that role to begin with.
We trust you, so trust us. No matter how dark things get, we'll always be here when you need us.
It's not a matter of "knowing how to resist" the Dark Tide's corruption, is it? You've already been corrupted.
Sorry, but under the circumstances, I think this is the most rational choice.
You know how I am.
Are you mad at me?
…Whatever the case, I respect your decision. But even so, let me say this one more time—
Do not overburden yourself. Do not carry this weight alone. We are here. Always.
Take these potions. My people and I will begin crafting the full batch. Once you activate the Anchor Stone, we will follow into the Dark Tide and meet you there.
Thank you, Cantarella.
Thank you all for your effort.
You, above all, have borne the most. Be safe, {PlayerName}.
Hmm… So this is how Septimont's Common Echoes operate. But I see some similarities with our Sentry Constructs...
How are things holding up at Averardo Vault?
You actually brought this many echoes along…
Grandfather is overseeing Averardo Vault, and the Black Shores are holding the line there as well. No need for concern. Besides, the Montellis' cache of Echoes is nothing to underestimate.
But really, such "technology" is our family's proudest "asset." Naturally, we brought what we could with us.
Septimont's Common Echoes use a different configuration than Ragunna's, but the underlying logic is compatible. Our tuning technique will still serve us well here.
Just don't forget to take breaks.
Looks like you'll be working late again.
…If working a little longer means you'll carry a little less, then I'll stay up as long as it takes.
I don't care about overtime in this case... If working a little longer means you'll carry a little less, then I'll stay up as long as it takes.
Besides, Ms. Carlotta hasn't rested properly in days.
In times like these, we cannot afford even a sliver of carelessness. We must do everything within our power... so that you can focus on what lies ahead in the Dark Tide without distractions.
These items will strengthen your Echoes. Even without us by your side, they'll be reliable allies.
...We won't let you walk this path alone for long.
{PlayerName}! It's been a while!
It has. I haven't seen you around lately.
As a wandering bard, I couldn't just sit idle while everyone else played their part.
So I did what I do best: played the loudest tune Ragunna's ever heard! With it, I called back every last soul still lost out there.
But now, just as we reunite… you're setting off again.
Music can be a weapon too. So take my song with you!
Winds blow, rains weep, but light will always follow. Look up, and you'll see the stars. Their quiet twinkling is proof you'll never be alone.
This entire world listens when you sing. Every bold, bright note will follow in your wake... And so will I.
Ah... {PlayerName}. I'm sorry, I didn't see you there.
Many of these warriors fell under the Dark Tide's corruption in battle. The Sentinel's light can help to purify their wounds… but the scars on their hearts are much harder to heal.
I know Septimontians don't believe in the Sentinel, so… I wanted to try, in my own way, to comfort those who've suffered...
You've changed, Phoebe.
Your faith shines brighter than ever.
Thank you... {PlayerName}.
The Sentinel's form of Unity is one of shared faith, without stripping away individual freedom. It's nothing like Leviathan's... forced "oneness."
I heard you... you're going into the Dark Tide. To lead the way for the others.
I know blessings alone won't be enough to protect you. What matters now is action. Real tangible aid.
Please, take this protective gear with you.
"Though you walk in the valley of the shadow of death, fear no evil... for we are always with you."
When the time comes... I'll follow the others to find you and fight by your side.
Ha! Your fire blazes strong, my fellow warrior. Now I can breathe a little easier.
You seem confident, Lupa.
You seem almost hungry for it, Lupa.
Confident? By Septimont's blazing sun, you better believe it!
Septimont's Gladiators live for the challenge. The bigger the threat, the fiercer we fight!
But I know this Leviathan we're facing is tougher and more complete than what we faced at the Gladiator's Agon. I will be cautious.
But I won't lie... I am worried about you going into the Dark Tide all alone.
Still, when the heat's on, better to slap your back and shout "You've got this!" than to doubt.
We've overcome a lot together. The Dark Tide... Pft, just another beast to break.
You've got your fight, we've got ours. While you open up a path, we'll hold down the fort here.
I'm with you all the way. Roll with the punches, right? And here, I got this for you. Hope it helps.
We all believe in you, my fellow warrior. Now it's time you believe in us. Soon enough, we'll storm the battlefield right by your side!
Your Excellency, fortifications are advancing ahead of schedule.
Most warriors, thanks to the healing efforts of the Order and the Fisalia, have been restored to fighting strength and are already deployed at their posts.

Additionally, with the Montellis' technical support, the damaged Common Echoes are fully operational again. They've also contributed a significant number of Private Echoes, greatly boosting our forces...
A timely reinforcement indeed... Understood. Continue to watch enemy movements in our vicinity.
What's the Dark Tide's current status?
Its fluctuations remain unstable, but so far, the Tidespawn have yet to show any signs of offensive action.
I believe that "Discord Slayer" is holding Leviathan's moves in check within the Dark Tide. What do you know of her?
Only that she slays Tacet Discords.
I only know she's on our side.
Is that so... She stirs a curious sense of familiarity in me. And she's knowledgable about Septimont's affairs, almost as if... She's lived here before.
Regardless, our priority now is to concentrate our forces, hold the line steady, and capitalize on the time she's buying us.
The Fractsidus lurks in the shadows. We must remain vigilant against them.
Before the moment comes for you to brave the Dark Tide, rest well, {PlayerName}. The battle ahead will demand everything of you. I trust these will serve you well.
And know this, you do not fight alone. Wherever you turn, you will find us standing with you.
{PlayerName}, Ephor Augusta has already departed for the Anti-Corrosion Ward.
She and Lady Iuno prepared some supplies for you. Please, take them.
