O Rover guided by the tides, you have climbed the peaks of Jinzhou and listened to the waves crash against the Black Shores. You've braved tempests, heard the dual nature of Ragunna's faith, and tasted the glory in the arenas of Septimont. Now, the path to the frozen frontier unfolds in Honami City. It's time to set forth to Lahai-Roi.
As the tides receded, a new world and an unexplored adventure awaited you.

In Jinzhou, you joined hands with Jiyan and the other Resonators to quell the Tacet Discord outbreak in Norfall Barrens. You also met "little Abby." You ultimately triumphed over and absorbed the Dreamless.
Under the guidance of the Wayfinder Changli, you resolved the Temporal Disruption at Mt. Firmament. And Sentinel Jué passed the Temporal Mandate on to Magistrate Jinhsi.
When you sought the truth of your own past, you met Shorekeeper in the Black Shores and reclaimed your duty as the organization's leader.
In search of a solution to Abby's deteriorating condition, you crossed the Stormy Sea and arrived in Ragunna, a port city in Rinascita.

You met Carlotta of the Montelli family, who vouched for your entry into the city. Yet beneath Ragunna's splendor, the Order of the Deep was guarding a grave secret, one tied to the Sentinel of Rinascita, Imperator.

When the Order conspired to sabotage the Carnevale, you and your companions calmed Lorelei's rage, defeated the Dragon of Dirge, and joined forces with the Troupe of Fools to bring the Carnevale to life.
But amid the cheers of the celebration, the Fractsidus's Overseer, Phrolova, appeared. Together with your companions, you defeated her and claimed the Laurel of the Carnevale.

After the Carnevale, the Primus of the Order spoke to you of the Sentinel, the Threnodian, and a Blessed Maiden of legend. All clues pointed toward the Fisalia family, which has long been entwined with both the Sentinel and the Threnodian.
At the invitation of the Fisalia head, Cantarella, you traveled to Porto-Veno Castle. From her, you learned that the Threnodian "Leviathan" commands the power to merge and assimilate.
For generations, the Fisalia family's mission had been to resonate with the Sentinel's true remaining power and find Their Resonator, the Blessed Maiden.

The current Blessed Maiden, Cartethyia, awaited you in the inverted Avinoleum Theological Seminary. With your help, she finally uncovered the truth behind the Sentinel and the Threnodian—that she herself was a creation of the Threnodian Leviathan.

The Sentinel's corrupted body had long been destroyed, and what remained sealed away was a vessel bearing Leviathan's will, "Fleurdelys." Cartethyia wished to end both the corrupted "Divinity" and its vessel.
Eventually, you and Cartethyia defeated the Threnodian's vessel, Fleurdelys. There, you saw the final consciousness of Imperator, who, with the last of Their will, awakened Cartethyia.
With the fall of the Sentinel, Cartethyia, now a wandering knight of Rinascita, chose to live by her own will.
Not long after, you sensed Cartethyia's abrupt departure from Avinoleum and followed her trail to the city of Gladiators, Septimont.
In Septimont, you met the young Gladiator Lupa and teamed up with her in the arena.
As the truth came to light later, you discovered that Lupa's fate had merged with the Threnodian's failed creation, Mya.
But the Threnodian's Gem on Mya's helmet was taken by the Fractsidus Overseer, Phrolova.

To retrieve the Gem, you set sail from Septimont, only to encounter the Order's Primus, Fenrico. He summoned colossal waves that dragged you under. As you sank into the deep, it was Phrolova who came to your rescue.
She revealed that Primus Fenrico had already taken the Gem and that she had been hunted down and gravely wounded by the Order. You agreed to a temporary alliance to reclaim the Gem.
As you pursued Fenrico, you came to understand Phrolova's true target: the power of assimilation hidden within the Threnodian's Gem.
And in her endless waiting, she finally set down her violin.

When you and Phrolova left the Lost Beyond, you confronted Fenrico, only to find that he intended to use the Gem for his own design: to draw the collective subconscious of the Rinascitans out from the Dark Tide, liberating Rinascita once and for all from the Threnodian's control.

But Fenrico himself had long since fallen to the Threnodian's corrupting influence. In his final moment of clarity, he gave his life to stop the Dark Tide's spread, entrusting you with Rinascita's future and with the task of preventing the descent of the Journeying Paradise.

As Fenrico turned to stone, the Gem slipped from his hand. You and Phrolova fought once more, but the Gem was eventually seized by the Fractsidus Overseers. Phrolova, wounded by your blade during the battle, fell into the sea and vanished.
Following the clues Fenrico left behind, you traveled to Septimont. There, the Ephor, Augusta, extended an invitation to you.

In the Sanguis Plateaus, you met Avidius, a rising Hero of Heroes recognized by the Senate. During the final pursuit of the Dark Tide creation known as the Corrosaurus, Augusta prepared to execute her original plan—
To turn the tide, Iuno sacrificed her very existence to forcibly manifest the Dark Tide, giving you and Augusta one last chance to strike down the False Sovereign. Against all odds, you prevailed.
Guided by the bracelet Iuno left behind, you finally found the girl only you remembered, just before she faded away in a sliver of moonlight.

Determined to bring Iuno back, you traveled to Tetragon Temple in search of clues. Through Avidius's story, you came to understand that existence itself was the sum of memories, feelings, and connections. You decided to Anchor Iuno back into existence through those bonds.
You made yourself the Anchor and held Iuno's spectral hand as you traversed her memories. Piece by piece, you reconnected her memories and emotions, until she was brought back into existence.

After retrieving Imperator's relic from the Earthrend Wedge beneath Septimont, you returned to Ragunna and set off for the Avinoleum Theological Seminary to seek Cartethyia's guidance on unlocking its secrets.
To track down the killer, you joined forces with Avidius, who was pursuing the "Quillbearer." Together, you found the mysterious woman called Galbrena.

After witnessing Avidius's tragic fate, the truth finally emerged: you were the new Harbinger of the Dark Tide chosen by Leviathan. To confront both the Dark Tide and the looming Journeying Paradise, you and Galbrena set out once more for Septimont.

Near the Three Heroes' Crest, you and your companions battled the Dark Tide head-on. To end its corruption and prevent the descent of the Journeying Paradise, you ventured directly into the heart of the Dark Tide.

After crossing the Styx Lake and a fabricated Mindscape, you and your companions manage to shatter the gates of Leviathan's Paradise. Together, you defeated the divine husk Leviathan had reshaped in the image of the Blessed Maiden, Fleurdelys.
With your journey in Rinascita concluded, you returned to the Black Shores. There, a rift near the coast pulled you into a Sonoro Sphere containing the ruins of the once-prosperous Honami City.

To end the Lament's destructive loop, you and Chisa made your way to Neon Tower, the heart of the disturbance. After clearing the last of the Lament, you helped the city residents' Longings find their way home. You and Chisa returned to the Black Shores and Honami City finally saw the light of a new day.
You guided Chisa through her doubts about the future, and together you reopened Shashou Cafe. For a while, you and your friends shared a rare time of peace.
Leviathan has even corrupted and merged with the Sentinel Imperator, and through the long course of history, twisted the faith of both Ragunna and the Order of the Deep.
Soon, you sensed that something was amiss in Septimont. At times, Lupa's figure blurred into that of another Gladiator girl.
In the end, Cartethyia and Lupa joined forces to bring down Cristoforo's scheme. Peace finally returned to Septimont, and Mya was finally able to rest in peace.

With this power, she hoped to merge the souls of those she'd once known—the townsfolk who perished in a great calamity—into the bodies of Tacet Discords, granting them new life in her Sonoro Sphere, the Lost Beyond.
Hoping both to find the relic left behind by Imperator and to suppress the spreading Dark Tide, you accepted the invitation and joined the great hunt.
With the Priestess Iuno's aid, she intended to lure out and destroy the False Sovereign, a humanoid embodiment of the Dark Tide. However, the Fractsidus intervened, and the plan failed.
During the post-hunt celebration, you realized that everyone had forgotten Iuno's existence. Even Augusta believed she was merely a hallucination caused by your exposure to the Dark Tide.

Defying fate's ordained ending, you both returned to the day of the celebration. Iuno once again stood as the blue-haired girl the Priestesses talked about. She had broken the arrow of destiny itself, and you delivered an unwritten future to both her and Septimont.

But at the Seminary, you witnessed a mysterious woman—someone you had seen before in a vision—suddenly break in and shoot Cartethyia before your eyes. Across Rinascita, strange phenomena began to spread.
She claimed she'd been searching for the "Harbinger of the Dark Tide." Yet, in your mind, the Harbinger, Fenrico, had long since perished beneath the sea.
Within the Dark Tide, you saw Galbrena's past struggles against the Tide and came upon a mysterious member of the Fractsidus who stood in your way.
At last, Rinascita welcomed a dawn that belonged solely to its people, an era no longer defined by Divinity.
As you explored the city, you met a girl named Chisa, who had been fighting ceaselessly within the Lament's time loops. You also encountered a talking capybara named Namipon...

But soon, you began to experience a loss in your frequency. According to Shorekeeper, your frequency was being drawn toward the region of Lahai-Roi. To resolve this mystery, you must now set out once again…

16.2.1 Emergency Procedure: Ice Rescue

Should you become stranded on ice after a slip or fall, do not attempt to stand up on your own, as concentrated ground force may cause the ice to fracture below you, or you may suffer injuries from falling a second time. Instead, remain prone and use your hands and feet to push along the ice, gradually moving your body toward the edge. Only attempt to stand once you have reached the edge.

If others are nearby, have them use a rope to pull you off the ice. Under no circumstances should you venture into a hazard area prior to a careful assessment of the conditions of the ice.

Researcher's annotation: Given the correct posture, you can remain steady even on slippery ice. The key is to keep your center of gravity as low as possible, keep your upper body upright, and use both hands to balance… All right, this might not sound very intuitive, but you'll probably get the hang of it after one or two falls. Ah, there it goes again. Can't manage to spook you even for a little. Turned out he simply left his bedtime music on, and it had woven its way into his dreams.

Anyway, I'll keep improving these waffles. Maybe make them a little sweeter and crispier, then add a drizzle of maple syrup and some freshly diced fruit on top. I have a feeling this would make it better. Next time you can...
Dr. Herssen! Someone just fainted at the celebration!
Seems like we'll have to cut our tea time short today. I'm so sorry about that, especially since I was the one who invited you.

We should stop trying to catch it by force. That might stress it even more.

Doctor, any more waffles?

I'm trying out these lunch boxes. A reminder to eat, packed with most of the vitamins they're missing.

Why don't you have lunch here? I'd love to get your feedback.

In many cases, a simple, good meal works better than any extended therapy session.

Well, just make sure you're getting enough exercise. Though I doubt that will ever be a problem for you.

You stroll through the campus with Luuk Herssen. Sharing this moment is a slice of warmth in your day...

The rhythm. The power...

Connect through music. Support the Overtonic Society!
Drop by and see how we mash the screams of mushrooms on the grill into a remix!
My body. It's moving on its own! I feel on top of the world!

Check out my new album, "The Pulse of Startorch." Have a listen!

Check out my new techno album. I named it "The Pulse of Startorch." Have a listen!

Baldur-felagi, you came! I hope you enjoy this ceremony!
Make sure to stop by our exhibit!

While you all waste your time in the wrong spot, I'm gonna take the prize for myself!

Stop whining, there're still 32 sites to go after we're done with this one!

Try out TARD-E's "Triple Workload Crunch Plan" to quickly bring you up to tip-top shape!
No, thank you! Unsubscribe! Thank you very much!
I really wish this ceremony could go on forever...

Just forget everything you know about up and down. Relax. Keep hovering. Practice makes perfect.

Energy gel for meals and minimal sleep...

Psychological suggestion?

 She didn't say a word. Just walked toward the swarm. The snow swallowed her fast. I heard the "ding... ding..." of her blade against the ground a few more times before everything fell silent. When I looked again, both she and the Discords were gone.
 
I didn't think. I just ran. When I got back to camp, my colleagues  looked at me like they'd seen a ghost. Turns out I'd been missing for four hours. I told them everything. They said it was a hallucination.

Alright—Starting now!
Having someone cover my back like this... Hm, not too bad.

After examining the mysterious device disguised as a calibrator, Lynae discovers it can store and amplify Void Storm frequencies, triggering malfunctions in any creation connected to the Exostrider. The maker is likely someone inside the Academy, capable of remotely activating it at any moment. Handing it over to the authorities might just return it to the Fractsidus mole. To stop this, Lynae decides to overwrite the device's permissions and take control of it herself.
Quick and clean.
It's been overwritten. Don't have to worry about it being remotely controlled. Glad we pulled it off in time…
You look nervous.
Your hands are shaking.
Hah… You got me. It's been a while since I've done something like this. Gotten a bit rusty.
Stay in your comfort zone too long and you start to slack off without realizing it... Back in the day, I would've handled this in 28 seconds flat.
That precise?
Not necessarily a bad thing.
Because… the longest reboot time for the Auto-Defense Array is 28 seconds.
...You think?
Ahem... sorry, back to the topic. While digging through the database, I noticed something.
The Academy's mechs and the <te href=700014>Voidmatter Barrier</te> security logs show unusual access. Someone used admin-level protocols.
Also, the device's data has three frequency waveforms. One from Hyvatia. The other two are... unrecognizable.
How do you know that's Hyvatia's waveform?
Um... Heh, just by, uh... browsing the Academy Forum.
Mm, alright, I was once tasked to hack into the Institute's database and tamper with Hyvatia's calibration data.
But I didn't change anything. Just threw in a few emojis and left a note telling them to upgrade their encryption.
That backfired though. Got me flagged.
So that's how it happened.
Back to those waveforms… If one is Hyvatia's, then the other two are likely the targets for the next experiment.
I think you're right. Next, we need to figure out what those waveforms correspond to. Maybe we'll find a clue in the Lahai-Roi ecological studies.
Let's head to the Spacetrek Archive then.

With you providing cover, the overwrite is successful. During the process, she finds evidence of admin-level access to the Academy's mechs and the Voidmatter Barrier security logs. The device contains three frequency waveforms. One belongs to Hyvatia, and the other two are unidentifiable.
You both decide to investigate the source of these waveforms at the Spacetrek Archive.
So it's true. The Dark Thunderbolt has enrolled at Startorch! Can you walk us through that epic battle with the Voidworm?
Dark... Thunderbolt?
One of my many titles.
How did that title catch on so widely?
At any rate, your actions were legendary!
Sorry, guys. I need to report the Voidworm incident to the Academy first.
Once that's done, I'll tell you everything you want to know. Promise.
You must know why we're here, Miss Lynae.
I do. I'm not a Startorch student anymore. Rules are rules, and I should return to the New Federation.
That's it, right?
We've reviewed everything. No matter what happened, the Academy is grateful for your bravery. Truth is, we never should've allowed our students to face danger like this.
Our duty is to keep you safe while you're still learning how to protect yourselves, not throw you into the fire.
Like you said, Miss Lynae, you're not a Startorch student.
Yeah. I know.
So if you want to be a student here, you'll need to pass the entrance exam.
What?
Of course, you'll need to enroll under your real identity this time.
That means... you're coming back to the Academy.
Indeed. But we must conduct another inquiry before admission.
An inquiry? Sure. And the entrance exam? No problem.
Very well, Miss Lynae. Please follow me.
Thank you.
I'll see you later.
Good luck with the exam!
Yeah, see you!
Gosh. Never thought I'd be this happy to take a freaking exam.
The Academy convenience store's specials are really good.
When I become a "freshman" at Startorch, let's go grab a bite together, okay?
...Protect the sun.

You and Lynae are surrounded by excited students and reporters. Amid the questions, Lynae, normally so unflappable, shows a rare, nervous smile. Just then, an Academy officer approaches. Prepared for expulsion, Lynae is instead met with a decision that fills her with joy: due to her bravery, the Academy will allow her to take the entrance exam under her real identity. Lynae accepts, and you watch her cheerful figure depart. Just then, a faint, familiar voice whispers in your ear: "...Protect the sun."
It seems the crisis is far from over.
Whew… the Academy is safe. Thank goodness.
Whoa... so many people here.
It's them! They're back!
Ahem, allow me to introduce Miss I.R.I.S. She's—
One of Startorch's Seven Great Mysteries?
That's right! She's the Archive's administrator, responsible for indexing all the data here. A very reliable senior, you could say.
Hello, I'm I.R.I.S., the retrieval AI of the Spacetrek Archive.
Miss Lynae, and… {PlayerName}, what can I help you with today?
You look beat. Everything okay, Miss I.R.I.S.?
The Archive experienced a data leak recently, so I'm running system maintenance in the background. But don't worry, routine queries are still available.
We want to look up info related to this waveform data.
Searching now. Found 3,281 matching entries. Should I list them all?
That's a lot… Add these keywords: "Void Storm" and "Exoswarm Contamination."
Understood. Narrowed down to 324 results.
Add "Threnodian" too?
Down to 3 results now.
A big improvement. Let's split up and review them.
Locations for those files are marked. Need anything else? Maybe… some tips on your school life?
Sure, I'm all ears.
Maybe next time.
Never call Mr. S.I.G.M.A. "Traffic Illuminator," unless you're up for a 10-minute, non-stop high-speed chase.
...Hmm, pity.

At the Archive, with help from the AI administrator I.R.I.S., you search for information tied to the waveform data. The search eventually narrows to two keywords: Void Storm and Exoswarm Contamination.
"Determining Exoswarm Contamination Thresholds via Synchronous Accelerators: Tensor Renormalization of the Void Storm's Frequency"
Looks like it's a paper studying the impact of the Void Storm on Exoswarm.
Can't understand a word.
But if I match the waveform Lynae found with the data in the paper...
It's a Voidworm's.
"Voidmatter Storm Surveyor Amplifier Module Manufacturing Manual (v3.12)"
This is the original manufacturing record for the device Lynae found.
Could be useful.
"Can the Voidworm Be Eaten?" Chapter 2: Edibility Assessment of Symbiotic Organisms
As one of Lahai-Ro's persistent regional hazards, the Voidworms consume what is left of Exoswarm that were consumed by Void Storms, using this as "food" to grow in size year by year.
Through repeated field sampling and lab analysis, this study must first emphasize an undeniable fact: the Voidworm itself is entirely unsuitable for any form of dietary incorporation.
Although the Voidworm proper proved biologically unrewarding, our team discovered a suspected parasitic organism within its active zones, tentatively named the "Exoshell Leech."

...Preliminary culinary experiments have determined that rapid, high-heat searing optimally develops its flavor profile. The creature's thick, shell-like exostructure, while resistant to Void Storm corrosion, is inedible. Searing promotes rapid surface charring for easier removal, while the interior transforms into a resilient, gelatinous substance. The finish carries a subtle minerality, yielding a surprisingly complex and notably addictive palate.
Evaluation Result: Dangerous. Rejected.
Comment 1: Third revision. I'm staking my pride as a Huanglong native on this one...
Comment 2: It's already been shot down by the advisor. Just give it up...
Comment 3: Can we meet in the middle? How about "The Impact of Voidworm Activity on Lahai-Roi's Dietary Structure"?
"A Study on the Recent Abnormal Periodicity of Void Storms"

Abstract: Recent observations indicate that Void Storm activity has significantly deviated from established patterns over the past two months, with both frequency and duration exceeding historical averages.

A comparison with historical waveform data reveals that some minor Void Storm zones exhibit a degree of regularity and consistency in their structure, suggesting the possibility of non-natural, artificial intervention or modulation.
Concurrently, Voidworm activity has also intensified. In the most extreme case, we detected their presence less than a kilometer from Sundermere—a previously unprecedented occurrence.

This paper synthesizes these anomalies to propose two preliminary hypotheses: either the phenomena stem from anomalous Threnodian activity beyond the Stridergate, or they are the result of deliberate human intervention. Further investigation is urgently required to verify the mechanism, assess potential risks, and formulate contingency plans.
How's it going on your end?
What I found were mostly things we already knew. Abnormal Void Storm cycles and the Institute's equipment acting up for no reason...
(Tell Lynae what you found.)
A Voidworm? Could it be...
They're planning to use the device to trigger a Voidworm's rampage? If so, then their target could be...
The Research Institute.

That's the most likely target. With the <te href=700012>Greatsword</te> there, Voidworms usually steer clear of the Institute. But before Hyvatia lost control, I saw a lot of contaminated Exoswarm remains nearby.
Looks like the contaminated Exoswarm and Hyvatia were just tests and rehearsals before the main event.
Whatever their game is, the real goal is to control a Voidworm to attack the Institute.
Voidworms spawn under the influence of Threnodian energy. In other words, as long as the Void Storm and the Threnodian exist, they can't really be destroyed.
This isn't a problem we can fix with a quick solution.
We need to warn the Institute right away.
I'll leave that to you. As for me... there's one more thing I have to do.
What's that?
The Department of Engineering's Crafting platform runs a mass production line. The Fractsidus must have more of these devices.
If they activate them to lure a Voidworm toward the Institute, we'll need a backup plan.
With the manufacturing manual you just found, I can boost our device's power two to three times. That way, if a Voidworm shows up here, we'll have a stronger bait.
The Spacetrek Collective has defense systems and restraining devices in active Voidworm zones. If we draw it there, we can keep it from attacking the Institute.
That's too risky.
Like I said, it's only a backup plan. Once you warn the top brass, they'll have countermeasures ready.
Besides, with the permissions overwritten, I'm the only one who can control the device... that ties me directly to Hyvatia's malfunction. So yeah, I'd rather not use it.
Hmm, is that the time? Trouble's just about to roll in.
What do you mean?
By now, they've probably noticed I've overwritten the device's permissions.
This "contact" of ours isn't going to just let it slide.

Based on your findings, you conclude that the Fractsidus intends to use the device to trigger a Voidworm rampage, with the most likely target being the Research Institute. You decide to alert the Institute immediately. Lynae chooses to stay behind and prepare a backup plan to boost the device's power, thereby luring the Voidworm toward the Spacetrek Collective's defensive systems. Unbeknownst to you, her overwrite of the device has already been detected by the Fractsidus "contact."
If, as Lynae said, the Fractsidus have infiltrated the Academy, I need to be careful who I alert in the Institute.
For that... I need someone I can trust.
Looks like I'll have to visit the infirmary again.
(Heavy Breathing)
We don't need to rush into this.
Are you alright?
Mm-hmm... Yawn...
Oh, I'm fine.
It's just... thinking about going back to the Academy kept me up all night.
Is it nerves or excitement?
I get it. Same here.
Both, I guess. It's been two decades since I was last there. I wonder how the Academy looks now. My teachers, classmates, and my parents...
No. I can't waver before setting out.
You too? Yes... I can imagine.
Never mind. Whatever happens, I'll face it head-on. You taught me that, remember? That means you should relax too.
Darn it. It's charging up. Hang tight!
(Sniff sniff. It's that guy!)
(It stole your frequency! I'd know that stink anywhere!)
(Now isn't a good time for a face-off. We'll settle the score later, Abby.)
(Fine, but it's not getting off easy!)
So this is what everyone here fights against.
The Academy's got a defensive barrier for the Void Storm. Once we're there, we're safe!
What a pain.
This isn't good. We need to wrap this up before it makes more of a mess.
Tch, still on us.
Gotta slow it down.
Sharp turn ahead! Hold onto your lunch!
Careful! It's closing in from the back.
Got it. Hang on. Full throttle!
Let me see. Great, all set!
A desk in organized chaos. Several spray cans in various colors sit in one corner. They were clearly used for spraying designs on models.

The room is a comfortable mess, where you can almost see vignettes of its occupant's life—curled up with a soft pillow, diving into studies or hobbies with bright-eyed focus, chasing down every curiosity, big or small, or weathering the occasional speedbumps of frustration over grades and credits.
She lives every moment of her Academy life in earnest, just like any other student here.
The Terminal shows several letter drafts, each heavily marked with revisions.
"To the esteemed Academy leadership and faculty: I am writing with a heavy heart and sincere remorse to submit this formal statement of accountability."

"This month marks the third time I have performed a full, borderline-non-compliant custom wrap on my vehicle, alongside unsanctioned performance modifications. I also swapped the horn for the Academy's class dismissal bell and took the vehicle for a test drive during class hours..."

"I now fully grasp the severity of my actions. I promise to immediately remove all non-compliant parts and restore the vehicle to its OEM-spec condition. I will study the traffic regulations again, and I solemnly swear that no such violations will occur again..."

"The teacher was right. The Academy roads serve as our means of transit, not as a proving ground for the Department of Engineering. Under no circumstances should they be used for vehicular dynamics experiments..."

"<s>Regarding the "Rainbow Exhaust Trails" modification, given how effective it is in alerting trailing vehicles to maintain a safe distance...</s> (Don't include this. It will just sound like I'm making excuses...)
...The subsequent drafts contained similar content, just dated differently.
"...Such behavior violates the Academy's rules and sets a bad example for the student body. It is most definitely unacceptable!"
A meticulously preserved Startorch Academy acceptance letter. It seems to hold extraordinary significance for her.
An assortment of "limited edition" snacks sits on the desk: "Mint Current" Flavor Squeezy Jelly, "Herald of Yore" Canned Cake, and pies with mysteriously sourced ingredients.
It's hard to imagine what state of mind led her to purchase these... unique flavor profiles.
First up... Name. Just input it right there.
Your class will be assigned automatically. New students usually start in the Preparatory Program, but since you passed the Synchronist Test, you'll be placed straight into the Rabelle College.
Next... contact address. You can fill in your home or guardian's address.
Jinzhou City Hall.
The Black Shores.
Leonidas Hotel.
Sky for roof, earth for bed. Home is wherever I roam.
All set? Then it's time to take your ID photo!
Do I need a school uniform?
Since you're joining mid-term, a lot of things aren't ready yet. That's what happened to me too.
Don't worry! Those will come later.
Hello there. Can I help you with something?
Hi, I'm here to see Lynae.
Miss Lynae? She's not in the dorm right now. Would you like to leave a message?
Wait... are you {PlayerName}?
Yes.
Miss Lynae asked me to tell you that if you're coming to see her, just wait in her room.
Do you know where she is?
Not really... She got a sudden notice from the Academy and left without saying much.
It's rare to see her so down. Whatever's going on, I hope it works out for her.
By the way, here's her room number.
Thank you.
What happened?
Wait... the barrier! It's failing!
Don't get any closer! Get back!
Go! Now!
Let's go.
Mm!
Warning: Voidmatter Barrier not fully activated.
The Academy has reviewed the incident, Professor Warren. While we share your concern over the Institute's loss, blaming a single student...
What were you doing when Hyvatia lost control, Miss Lynae? Why were you at the Institute during class hours?
I was escorting {PlayerName} to burn {Male=his;Female=her} Cassette at the Institute.
On my way back to the Academy, I noticed abnormal frequency spikes and contaminated Exoswarm near Sundermere.
Before I could act, I was surrounded. I tried to contact the Academy, but the Void Storm blocked communications.
Exoswarm remains should still be there. I assume... you are already investigating them?
No such remains were found, Miss Lynae. Making things up won't help you.
That was quick.
What about the surveillance cameras? They're equipped to handle Void Storm interference. They should've captured the Exoswarm before things escalated.
They didn't. And in fact, you aren't in the footage at all. I wonder what you were doing at that time. Avoiding the cameras, perhaps?
What if the footage was tampered with? Her presence could've been erased.
Possible. But only if she and the Exoswarm were truly there.
Since neither side can confirm that, how about we start by verifying if the footage was altered?
We should expand the scope of the investigation. Remember the security breach in the database? There might be more compromised than just today's feed.
You mean the breach that exposed a flaw in the system? Fair enough.
Do you have anything else to add, Miss Lynae? Don't worry, we're here to help you.
Then please remain on Academy grounds until the investigation is concluded.
One last thing, Miss Lynae. You're from the New Federation, right?
What do you mean?
Nothing. I just noticed you stay at the Academy even during breaks. Never thought of going home?
Thanks for asking, Professor. I keep in touch with my parents whenever I can. If you're implying I have some secret agenda, you'll be disappointed.
Not at all. I simply wonder if you don't want to return.
I don't think that's something you should concern yourself with, Professor.
Let's not waste any more time, Professor Warren.
Phew...
Thanks… for speaking up for me.
Why not tell them the truth?
What was that device you had when Hyvatia went berserk?
Straight to the point, huh? I thought you'd let it slide, like they did.
Highly unlikely.
Good... you're still you.
What's your real purpose?
Let's talk somewhere else. This place is suffocating.

Back at the Academy, Lynae is questioned by Warren and other faculty. She recounts the Hyvatia malfunction, but you notice she omits any mention of the "liaison." Warren points out that her testimony about the "contaminated Exoswarm" doesn't match the scene investigation or surveillance footage. He questions her motives, especially in light of a recent security breach in the Institute's database. Although you and Voss speak in her defense, Lynae cannot explain the key inconsistencies.
After everyone leaves, you ask her directly why she didn't tell the whole truth. After a pause, she asks to continue the conversation somewhere quieter.
You're not just a student, are you?
I've always wished I were just an ordinary student. But… well.

Ever thought about throwing everything away? The responsibilities, the secrets you can't share, the constant weight on your shoulders… just letting it all go, and living a carefree life like the rest of them?
Heh, just a passing thought. I know it's not something you'd admit to, whether you've ever wished for it or not. Not someone like you.
But we're not the same. I just… really want to be like the other students here.
Wanna grab a bite first?
Bet the line's gonna be insane right now...
Yeah, let's just chug a Nutri-Pack for now.
Eww...
Quit being such a stickler! Live a little, think bigger!
Are you winging it?! That's not how the manual says to do it!
You don't need to follow every exact step, you know!
Guys... chill out...
Respected advisors, professors, hello. So my thesis is on...
So, uh, my research focus is basically about... the, uh...
Why so nervous? It's just the proposal.
So about the notes you lent me... Some of the numbers were off, so I just marked 'em up. There's also a...
Oh, thank you! I totally missed that.
Wait, uh... maybe just open that later...
Hey, isn't that...?
Go for it! Shoot your shot!
Um, I don't want to be a bother...
Dark alleys. Hushed whispers. Greedy eyes hiding behind masks...
That was everyday life for a mercenary.
I used to wonder, what if the sky above me wasn't always black?
What if there really was another life I could choose?
Even if the price would forever haunt me from the shadows...
...I'd still take the deal. No question.
Every day at the Academy has been more than I ever let myself hope for.
The bright halls. Charging into the unknown with people who had my back. Eyes locked on the edge of the world. Those "good mornings" at dawn...
Moments that don't just shine, but burn.
Now I know that living, really living, has colors I didn't even know existed. So bright... you'd bleed to hold onto it.
But just like the stories in all those old comics...
Stolen time always comes knocking.
"Is it really okay... to run away?"
Oh my, oh my, the day's finally here.
The coordinates have all been calibrated. A smooth landing, guaranteed!
The tunnel is stable, but only wide enough for one person at a time.
I see. Then please let me go first.
Namipon, Shorekeeper... thank you. For looking after me during this time.
Oh, don't get all serious! You can visit during your holidays.
...Alright. I promise I'll visit often.
Well then, {PlayerName}, I'll see you at the Academy.
See you there.
The tunnel is stable. She'll arrive safely.
I'm ready too.
You are fully prepared. I see.
{PlayerName}, safe journey.
Alright. Time to go.

The spatial tunnel to Lahai-Roi allows only one person to pass through at a time. After thanking Namipon and Shorekeeper, Chisa goes first. You bid Shorekeeper farewell and leave under her watchful gaze.
Ha... this place always brings me peace.
You want to know who I really am so you can connect the dots on that incident, right?
I can tell you... but only if you promise me one thing: Let me stay here. At the Academy. As a student.
Is it really so important to you?
...Yeah. More than I can say.
I'll take your silence as a yes then.
So, you've heard those old "pulling a switcheroo" stories, right?
HQ... this is Lynae...
Sorry Overseer... we were... ambushed...
Don't worry... I'll make it to Startorch Academy in Lahai-Roi in time...
I'll complete the mission... assigned by the Grand Architect...
Spoiler alert: their mission wasn't completed.
Overseer...?
The Fractsidus...?
Professor Warren knows I'm from the New Federation, but not exactly which part.
It's called the Lawless Zone. Let's just say... you'd see blood spilled every three days, on average. That's where I grew up.
I had talent, and the New Fed saw it. Put me to work. Off the record. Dirty jobs.
Then that day happened… It was an accident, but I saw my chance.
...An admission letter to Lahai-Roi's Startorch Academy.
So that was your "switcheroo."
I found that recording I played you on the real Lynae's liaison at the Academy.
So I quickly learned she wasn't just a regular student from the start.
Even so, I came to Lahai-Roi.
Everything here… It's nothing like the New Fed. People don't question themselves when they wake up, brush their teeth, and look in the mirror. They just know who they are.
And you want to be one of them.
Look, as far as I'm concerned, the Fractsidus threatens my school life. They're your enemy too.
We have shared interests. That's a solid basis for us to cooperate.
...A "student" wouldn't talk like that.
Even if we solve this, do you think you'll be able to look at yourself in the mirror afterward?
That being said, I do know what matters most now.
I stood up to Warren for you because I chose to trust you. And I'll own that choice.
Ha... you know, sometimes you really do sound like a teacher.
Alright then, let me rephrase.
I like this school. I've met good people here, people who treat me like their friend. People worth protecting.
That's why I hope you'll help me find out why the Fractsidus are here in Lahai-Roi, {PlayerName}.
Let's do this. Together.
I've been holding in these words forever. Ahh.. Feels good to finally get 'em out.
As for our first lead...
Any ideas?
What we do know is... Hyvatia's malfunction and the contaminated Exoswarm are definitely connected to this device I found.
It looks like Academy tech... maybe the Department of Engineering's lab can shed some light.
But why would the Academy allow something this dangerous to circulate freely?
Maybe its appearance is just a disguise. Or maybe it means its maker had free access to the Department's resources.
After all, that "contact" who's been feeding me orders might still be inside the Academy.
Makes sense. Then we start with the Department of Engineering.
If you're ready to start making moves, I know a shortcut.
How short?
Right this way!

Lynae finally reveals her true identity: she is a former government-hired mercenary from the New Federation's "Lawless Zone." During a mission, she found an admission letter in one of the dead's belongings. Seeing a chance to escape her old life, she took on the dead girl's name and identity to enroll in Startorch Academy.
What she didn't expect was that the dead girl, the real "Lynae," had been a Fractsidus plant, sent to infiltrate the Academy. Wanting to stay in the place she's come to call home, she asks to work with you to uncover the truth and thwart the Fractsidus's plans.
She then takes out the device that caused Hyvatia's malfunction and prepares to investigate its origin in the Department of Engineering.
Speaking of which, by enrollment year, I guess that makes you my "Senpai," huh?
...What?
Th-that's not how it works...
Miss Lynae, the Academy requires your presence for a follow-up inquiry concerning Hyvatia's malfunction.
I'll answer any questions you have, but this has nothing to do with {PlayerName}. {Male=He;Female=She} only enrolled today.
Very well then. Please return to your dorm and wait for further questioning. Leaving without authorization during this period will count as a breach of Academy regulations.
(Sorry... I'll count on you for the rest.)

Also, we've received an anonymous report alleging that a criminal record and prison history under the name "Lynae" closely matches your identity. This raises concerns about possible falsification of your admission documents.
Please cooperate with our investigation.

The Academy teacher finds Lynae again for a second round of investigation about the Hyvatia incident. They present an anonymous report accusing her of falsifying her admission records, linking her to a criminal record under the name "Lynae." Lynae calmly accepts the investigation and is placed under dormitory confinement. Before she is led away, she secretly passes you a message, entrusting the next phase of the plan to you.
Ah, what a rare visitor. I assumed the Void Storm, those Voidworms, and your admission would've kept you too busy to drop by.
The Fractsidus have contacts inside the Academy. They're planning an attack on the Research Institute.
That's... certainly surprising news.
And what do you need from a school doctor like me? Or... should I say, why come to me at all?
Because I'm still new to the Academy. Professor Mornye isn't around, and I have no way to judge if I'm passing the message on to the right person.
And you trust me?

You gave me a hint when we first met, didn't you? Saying "Welcome back," and recognizing me as a Black Shores' Bloom Bearer—that's not on my official record. Your knowledge of me goes beyond the paperwork.
Besides, Chisa mentioned I left the Academy in a hurry, so someone must've helped to erase my trail.
You didn't exactly act like that was our first meeting either.
Hm, interesting theory. Though I'm not sure I fully understand it. What I'd like to know is... what do you want me to do about it?
(Not going to admit it, huh... Fine, no time for games with an emergency looming.)
(Brief Luuk Herssen on your investigation and suspicions.)
I see... pests inside the Academy, then.
A Voidworm attack on the Research Institute... It must be part of a bigger play. Hyvatia's malfunction, the abnormal Void Storms... I fear it's all connected.
Don't worry, I'll handle things with the Institute. Whatever you discover or whatever course of action you choose, I won't interfere.
I'll provide support when the time comes.
Now, go do what you must.

You seek out Dr. Herssen and share your suspicion that Fractsidus agents have infiltrated Startorch Academy. Surprised by your trust, he doesn't confirm your theory outright but promises to liaise with the Research Institute and support your investigation.
Well, look who's here! How's everything going?
I've informed Dr. Herssen and Professor Mornye about the situation. Once the Institute gets the warning, they'll prepare accordingly.
The Fractsidus's plan is still unclear, so it's best not to act rashly. Any investigation, leave that to me.
Mm, nothing urgent for now. But since you're here, maybe we could talk a bit.
Sorry about this mess. I really should've cleaned up.
You know, back in the New Fed my room was just a bed, a chair, a desk… and my weapons.
Mercenaries? We don't know what a "real life" is. We only know survival. That's why we never settle down. Everything that isn't gear or a weapon is just dead weight.
But… the more "dead weight" I pick up here, the more I realize how much this place means to me.
At first, I only saw the Academy as a way to outrun my merc past. Didn't care about the cost. I took the chance, no hesitation.
Startorch Academy... It's really important to you, isn't it?
Yeah, every day here is a blessing! I get to splash color around, cruise under the sun, and learn stuff I never even knew existed.
This place may be buried under frost, but it feels brighter and freer than anywhere I've been.
About that anonymous report on "Lynae's" criminal records and prison history… Who are they really talking about?
The Fractsidus's "Lynae."
Mercs in the New Fed are essentially government contractors. After I took her identity and faked my death, they wiped all my merc records clean.
Now that I think about it, it's kind of funny… I can't even prove who I really am anymore.
...Whichever "Lynae" I am, I don't belong here.
But still… I truly appreciate what you've done for me.
Thank you. For speaking up for me, more than once. And… thank you for trusting me.
It's rare to have trust unbound by contracts.
Isn't it a bit early to give up?
The Fractsidus won't quit just because you walk away.
I'm not a student here anymore.
The Academy let me know the result of their investigation.
They're kicking me out, sending me back to the New Fed. Then it's either back to the old work... or spend my life behind bars.
Not like I'd choose either one of those.
