(Aemeath said someone lifted her from the lake when she was a child. That's when she lost her talisman.)
(It wasn't my past self who saved her, it was me. Right here, right now.)
(My failure to save Aemeath… has it already become part of Lahai-Roi's chain of cause and effect?)
You emerge from the water. In your palm is the talisman the young Aemeath once thought she had lost. Because of you in this moment, all causality finally closes its loop.
(Aemeath is on the other side of the Stridergate. I'll just go through it and bring her back.)
(Someone has to pilot the Exostrider, open the Stridergate, and deal with the Threnodian anyway.)
(I'll do it.)
(The odds are slim, but they're not zero.)
(It touched the talisman then ran away. Is it trying to lead me somewhere?)
(That direction, it's the Synchrolink Training Grounds.)
What's wrong? The simulation pod won't open?
Seems so. It bugged out with an emergency error and just... locked down. Maintenance is on the way.
But it's showing it's occupied? Class just started. No one could have gotten in yet.
Aemeath?

The Soliskin touches the talisman in your hand, then runs toward the simulator cockpit. You push through the crowd to find Aemeath, who once died in that very cockpit years ago, now sitting in the pilot's seat.
You joyfully grasp her hand, only to realize her eyes are empty, staring into a quiet, blank nothingness.
The results are in. It's what I had expected.
This "Aemeath" isn't exactly human, nor is she a Reverberation. She's closer to an Exoswarm, with only a trace of her original frequency remaining.
As your friend, I wouldn't suggest you think of her as the girl you knew. That would cause unnecessary pain.
As for the Exostrider plan you asked about, we can go over the details at the infirmary when the time comes.
Stay strong, {PlayerName}.
She just left the recovery pod and is headed to the transport dock. If you want to see her, that's where you'll find her.
This is... her paper plane.
You can keep it, if you'd like.
I know you're not Aemeath. You're only a piece of what she left behind, kept alive by this talisman.
But if you exist, it means she's still alive, too. Doesn't it?
Otherwise, the Soliskin couldn't have brought you back.
So... it wasn't for nothing. If I hadn't gone looking for Aemeath, I never would have found this talisman.
And you wouldn't be here at all.
Luuk told me you're a piece of her. A thread that might still tie her to this world.
If I follow it, maybe I can find where she is.
He might've only said that to comfort me. No one has ever seen what's beyond the Stridergate. It's all just guesswork.
How long has it been for her since she was pulled into that chaos?
Is she still alive? And if she is, how much longer can she hold on?
...I don't know.
But I will hold on to hope.
Because the world she saved is so full of it. So peaceful, and so beautiful.
It's... strange seeing "Aemeath" so quiet like this.
I will cross the Stridergate and bring you home.
Wait for me, Aemeath.
Don't... be sad...
A gentle breeze whispers the beginnings of spring.

You arrive at the station, where the Exoswarm shell resembling Aemeath sits quietly. You speak to it, hoping the real Aemeath, far beyond the Stridergate, can hear your vow: you will bring her home.
Under the spring breeze, the world she saved remains as peaceful and beautiful as ever.
I'm Aemeath. The Academy's star. A Synchronist. A savior.
<ano=Don't look for me>Please, look at me!</ano>.
This mission has become an eternal shackle.
Why...
It hurts...
What should I do...
(This looks like a projector.)
Are you alright, Aemeath?
All good. Inside the Exostrider, I'm the one in control.
Go home.
I'll destroy Sigillum. So, just go. Stay away from it, okay?
Please, I'm begging you.
Aemeath?
Why refuse?
It's clear Aemeath wants you to stay as far away as possible from Sigillum. Her speech slowly becomes laced with aggression and instability.
So lonely.
Open the Stridergate.
Go.
Home.
I said—
SHUT UP!
THAT IS NOT HOME.
I won't allow anyone...
Go home.
Shut up!
To harm {PlayerName}.
You look at "Aemeath." She sits there, silent, her face an expressionless mask.
Following her gaze, you take in Lahai-Roi's scenery carressed by the soft breeze.
Students laugh as they always have, sharing dreams and plans for the future. Professors quietly discuss their latest findings, a steady hum of thought and discovery.
Everything under the sky pulses with life. Calm, familiar, and heartbreakingly beautiful.
Aemeath...
Don't worry. It will end soon.
(There's still a way. I can't give up here.)
What exactly are you hiding from me?
You don't need to know, {PlayerName}. I will protect you.
Aemeath, haven't you noticed you're not yourself right now?!
Did you forget your own homeland?
(Aemeath and Sigillum are gone.)
(A poster of Fleet Snowfluff's fan meeting.)
The poster is neatly stuck to the wall, but the bottom-right corner hasn't fully adhered. You lift it gently and see something scrawled messily on the back.
"I'll do anything. Guess that means I don't really care about anything."
"Singing, piloting the Exostrider… It's all the same. I don't care."
"But saving the world… will I ever see the day?"
(A photo album.)
You open the album to photos of Aemeath with her classmates.
You can tell she's a girl of many passions: ice-fishing in the frostlands with friends, splurging at markets, battling it out in the arcade…
But away from the camera's focus, Aemeath seems elsewhere. Quiet. Lost in thought.
At the very bottom, you find a photo of you with her as a child. Its edges are soft, creased, and worn from handling.
(Is this Aemeath's old dorm? Since she can resonate with the Exostrider, even after her body was destroyed, her frequency must have merged with it.)
Piloting the Exostrider... Heh, it doesn't matter to me.
But if this is what it takes to lighten {PlayerName}'s burden, and ease {Male=his;Female=her} pain…
Saving the world... Heh!
Nothing but a pair of shackles. Heavy, eternal shackles.
No, {Male=he;Female=she} can't ever know this.
I must... keep this secret. Bury the truth deep.
Inside Aemeath's mind, her sorrows are scattered like fragments.
(Luuk texted me to go over the Exostrider plan at the infirmary. Better get going.)
The "Golden Serum" developed by the Novialle Group. But I prefer its other name—<te href=750042>Ichor</te>.
My father started it as a medication for rare diseases. But as research progressed, it came to represent something far more ambitious—the "drug of evolution."
Evolution? Sounds like something the Fractsidus would like.
Well, on paper, it worked. I became its Resonator, so it would be unfair to say it was entirely useless.
But I was a rare case who survived. All it cost me was excruciating pain and my color vision. Most test subjects like me didn't make it.
It wasn't until I met you that I realized there was more to the story.
A vial of "Golden Serum," an "evolutionary drug" developed by the Novialle Regenerative Group, owned by Luuk's adoptive father, which drew the Fractsidus's attention.
The entire Lollo Logistics carrier was already blown to smithereens by the time I recovered this page.
I managed a quick glimpse before the fire consumed most of the page. Hehe, it is a report from an Overseer.
A Fractsidus Overseer's report on its way to the New Federation?
Yes, tucked away in a Lollo Logistics delivery box.
The recipient is "Eris" in the New Federation.
A scorched report from a Fractsidus Overseer, meant to be sent to "Eris" in the New Federation.
My brother Rhein drew this picture.
We're not related by blood. Father took us both in after his own children passed away from a rare illness long ago.
For a while, I tried to be the perfect son Father wanted. It never worked, so eventually I stopped trying.
It only got worse from there. What Father tried to do to Rhein was unforgivable. And then came that accident...
I thought what my father did was a rather mundane story. A cliché, someone trying to atone for past guilt, only to cause greater harm.
Until your hints made me suspect it was someone's staged finale. So I had my father's grave exhumed. It was empty.
Rhein never could handle pain, but he was easy to cheer up.  Whenever the grown-ups would give me candy, I'd save it all for him.
(So that's why he always has candy with him.)
A child's drawing inside a picture frame. A family portrait drawn by Luuk's younger brother, Rhein.
A niche edition of "The Minimalist Approach to Cat Psychology," a magazine that the infirmary has a subscription to.
The subscriber doesn't own a cat. Rumor says he's not even good with them. Others have seen him late at night, holding a copy and staring into space.
It was Rhein, Luuk Herssen's younger brother, who loved this magazine series. The good doctor took over the subscription after him and, even years after leaving home, has never canceled it.
Luuk Herssen gathered this dirt from the "place where he rests."
Few know of its significance, yet Luuk places it in the sunlight every day. No one knows why he studies and measures this frozen mound of dirt that never thaws.
Those three items you just showed me... Did the Fractsidus get into <te href=750043>Novialle's</te> work after learning about the <te href=750042>Ichor's</te> potential for "evolution"?
They didn't just "get into" our work. They went a step further—replacement.
Have you ever met the Fractsidus's Grand Architect?
The "thousand-faced survivor." We met near the "Styx Lake" deep within the Dark Tide.
Wait... Does this mean your father was...?
Yes. My father was just another face the Grand Architect borrowed. Though, looking back now, I can't recall the moment the real him was taken.
I think the Grand Architect sees life and death as a game. I wouldn't be surprised if "Father" was even smiling in his coffin as we buried him in that downpour!
So, that's your answer. Why did you choose me? Because I have a very personal reason to go after the Fractsidus—hatred.
Hatred... Even now?
Now, it has become something of a habit.
Continue this train of investigation and you'll see for yourself what they are. But before you do, there's something I should share.
My friends in the Black Shores told me you've already had a few run-ins with certain Overseers. Is that right?
Three: Cristoforo, Phrolova, and Scar. Plus the Grand Architect you mentioned.
Ah, those names do ring a bell. Phrolova is codenamed Hecate. Cristoforo? Arachnos. Intriguing, isn't it? The flair they have for their own branding.
But it's a telling detail. A codename can reveal its owner's style, personal tastes, and even ambitions.
Think about it. A powerful Resonator who causes chaos at random leaves no trail to follow. But give them a preference, a pattern, and we can start to build a profile from the pieces.
I've been compiling reports on the Overseers for years. Allow me to share what I've learned so far.

Luuk explains that his father's identity was also stolen by the Fractsidus's Grand Architect. Hatred was his initial motivation for pursuing the organization, and the very reason your past self chose him for this task.
I've reactivated your access. You'll find the door controls right over there.
The Fractsidus is loosely organized. Most of its members have only undergone basic, artificially-induced body modification. They're not terribly difficult to neutralize.
But if you encounter Artificers with more... creative modifications,  you're likely looking at the handiwork of "Hydra."
Hydra is their leading mind on human evolution and body modifications. Whoever they are, they often work in tandem with "Siren."
In other words, if you spot one, be on guard in case the other is lurking close by.
Zashiki-warashi won't require much of your attention. This Overseer primarily operates in Ashinohara, a region that's been largely destroyed by the Lament.
Ashinohara... I've heard of it somewhere before.
The girl we had in the infirmary for a while, Chisa, I remember? The city that trapped her, Honami, is part of Ashinohara.
Now, on to two key pieces of the puzzle.
I did say the Fractsidus was a loose organization, but even the most scattered cells still need funding to function.
Remember that report from earlier? It's only a matter of time before you go to the New Federation. And based on the intel I've gathered...
That's their most critical base of operations, and where you'll find "Eris."
How critical? Do they operate in the open?
Not exactly. But in a place where money talks, they must have members in the highest echelons of government and business. Key members.
Their foothold in the New Federation has given them immense leverage. With that endless stream of wealth, the Fractsidus operates with impunity across the planet.
Speaking of which, Startorch Academy is also heavily funded by the New Federation. To be blunt, they're the Spacetrek Collective's single largest donor.
Eris, huh? Duly noted. I'm assuming the other key piece is the Grand Architect?
The Fractsidus Grand Architect. Their true name is unknown. They only appear through borrowed identities: Real people, legendary beings, and even the phantoms of the dead from others' memories.
I did brush shoulders with them once. It was a shame I had no idea at the time and missed my shot.
This pen was the only thing I brought back from that great fire.
I have yet to discipher the lettering, but it shows one thing for sure: the Grand Architect has been around for a very, very long time.
It's a pity you called me to Lahai-Roi. Otherwise, I would've continued following that trail. But you always have good reason. Right?
You uncovered all this by yourself?
More or less. I did have some help along the way.
To get your hands on one of the Grand Architect's personal items. You did more than just follow a trail. You infiltrated them.
Playing along with them isn't that difficult once you get the hang of it. Like I said, they are a loose organization.
Knowing the Fractsidus, stealing all that intel on the Overseers is risky, no matter how loose they are. Each infiltration will only be more dangerous than the last.
Luuk, how can a doctor who doesn't value his own life save anyone else's?
You know, this is the second time you've said those words to me.
They got away again.
(If I hadn't been so cautious, I could've "taken care" of them this time.)
(I should send today's findings to {PlayerName}. It's been two years. I suppose I'm due for a report.)
Good, you got the intel. Would've been a shame if I got myself killed for nothing.
You want me to go to Lahai-Roi? Why?
There's evidence of their activity in Lahai-Roi. I need you to keep an eye on things. And frankly, you need a break.
Now is not the right time.
You've already drawn enough attention. Do we really have to wait for you to get killed to decide it's "the right time"?
How can a doctor save anyone else's life if he doesn't value his own?  Keep pushing like this and you'll be no different from them.
Not pulling any punches, are you?
Trust me, that's only the warm up. Lahai-Roi is a nice place, Luuk. Bright, passionate students, beautiful snow. Perfect for slowing things down.
Listen to me on this. Come.
Very well. As you wish.
So I've led a leisurely life in Lahai-Roi ever since. No need to worry, I know my limits.
Let's set aside the Fractsidus for now. We should discuss the Exostrider plan. But first, tell me what happened to you and Aemeath in the frostlands.
(You briefly recount to Luuk the events in the frostlands.)
I see. Aemeath, she... No wonder you're in such a state.
I understand her reasons. She was fighting for her dream, for Lahai-Roi, in the only way she knew how. And I respect that. The fate she chose for herself.
But I won't accept it. There's more I haven't tried. I'm not done fighting for her.
Of course. I wouldn't expect you to give up so easily.
Now, about the Exostrider... It started with the Spacetrek Collective finding a "giant Soliskin root network" in Bjartr Woods. They identified it as the "lid" sealing the Stridergate, so to speak.
It keeps the Threnodian's fractured forms sealed on both sides of the Stridergate. Break it, and these forms will reunite. That wouldn't just spell Lahai-Roi's doomsday, but the entire world.

But the Collective still yearned to open that gateway, to explore the unknown. So, they created the Synchronists. The idea was to use Augmented Resonance to amplify the Exostrider's power, hoping that would keep the Threnodian suppressed.
But lately, the Threnodian's attacks on the seal have been increasing. I'm afraid the Fractsidus is also getting ready to make a move.
With the Reactor Core returned, all you need now is a little patience. Wait for the Exostrider to awaken. Then we can focus on how to use it to find Aemeath.
You were a Synchronist in the Academy once before. I'll speak with Lucilla about getting you piloting access.
Then I'll wait for your news, Luuk.
Certainly. But our immediate priority should be the Fractsidus. I have a feeling they're planning to sabotage our plans for the Exostrider.

In a secret workspace, Luuk introduces you to the wealth of intelligence he gathered while infiltrating the Fractsidus. His apparent indifference to his own life or death raises your suspicion. He promises to speak with Lucilla to smoothly advance your plans with the Exostrider, which entails you piloting it beyond the Stridergate to retrieve Aemeath.
In the past, Luuk once teetered on the edge of darkness, holding the Grand Architect's pen amidst burning flames. Your past self called him to Lahai-Roi, preventing his fall and ensuring he did not become the very enemy he hunted.
(Nivora... Has she been staying here to recover?)
Ha... haha...
I-I brought the student! Just like you asked! You... Where are you?!
Lahai-Roi was just a minor setback! I'm still useful! I still have work in the New Federation, I still—
Stop hiding! Say something!
ARGH! YOU! That doctor who's always watching.
You've reached a dead end, Warren. Don't you see that?
Hehehe... AHAHAHAHA!
It's your dead end!
Nivora lies unconscious on the ground. Warren, desperate and on the brink of madness, lunges at Luuk.
(SkyArk's data room. There must be a reason.)
(Was that just impulse... or perhaps...)
How are you recovering from your injuries, Nivora?
Oh, i-it's you, {PlayerName}. Uh, yes. I'm feeling much better.
Dr. Herssen took very good care of me. I just did what he said and rested for a few days here, and I barely feel any pain now.
Are you here to visit him?
Yes, we have something to discuss. Is he here?
He's in the counseling room next door. Um... My friend Sigrika is in there. It might take a while.
Thanks. Take care of yourself.
No!
Oh... Dr. Herssen... Warren, is he—
He's only unconscious. Everything's okay, Nivora. How are you feeling?
Ugh... I'm... fine. It's just that he struck me in the back of the neck. It really hurts.
I'm... really scared.
It's okay. Don't force yourself to hold it in. After a shock like that, it's much better if you let it out. Keeping it bottled up is stressful in itself.
Take your time. Tell me what happened when you're ready.
Okay... I'll try... I just... I need a moment...
Then rest here for now. I'll go check on Warren.
I fell asleep on the hospital bed. When I woke up and opened my eyes, Warren was pointing a gun at my head.
He was frantic. Grilled me non-stop about SkyArk. And when he found out I'd been to the station before, he forced me to bring him.
Wait! Those researchers by the door—
One of them didn't make it. The other two are still alive.
I see. As for what else happened, I don't really remember.
That's alright. I've already formed a rough theory about his motives now. You should rest, Nivora. We'll handle things from here.
Is that so? Then, Dr. Herssen, care to share your theory?

After rescuing the unconscious Nivora, she claims Warren coerced her into guiding him to the station. Luuk comforts the shaken girl and begins checking Warren's condition.
Nivora trembles as she stands, then begins to approach Luuk from behind.
Oh, Doctor...
I'm afraid "identity theft" is not in the curriculum.
Isn't that right?
Since you insist on playing the student, I'll offer a lesson.
It takes two to play a game.
How mean. Is that any way to treat a student?
Grand Architect of the Fractsidus.
My, my. Played me for a fool, didn't you?
I was going to kill you for a little one-on-one time with {PlayerName}. Shame.
Regrettable, that you evaded what was meant for you.
But it's okay. Uncle Warren's dead. Nice and clean!
Being caught out in the open, and still he thought he could just vanish from Lahai-Roi and get away with this fiasco? The naivety is remarkable.
Anyway, I got back what I wanted too, so I'm a happy girl.
On my way here, I kept wondering why you acted so quickly. It didn't fit your usual style of staying in character until the very end.
Just as I thought... You were after this pen.
Ah, yes. My precious. I couldn't find it anywhere! So it was you who took it from me.
This is the first time someone's taken something from me! Oh, I almost forgot to ask, when did you begin to suspect?
If you must know, my suspicions began to deepen during our last visit to the space station. When you feigned that injury.
Your "acting" had been flawless, Grand Architect. But even you cannot mimic what you don't understand.
Death itself.
To an immortal like you, no matter how many times you die, it's just another lost identity. And I happened to have "seen" <ano=my father>you</ano> die before.
Oh? Is this why you've had your eye on me all this time?
Let me think... Hmm, whoops? Can't seem to remember. My bad.
My real favorite things are the ones that are really old and far, far away.
But you... you're something special, Dr. Herssen! You're the first person in forever to ever come this close.
Without you, the game in Lahai-Roi would be so boring! So, you get prizes!
And I promise, it's right up your alley.
Now, for the first one. At the upcoming New Solar Celebration, among all the lovely students, stands a member of the Fractsidus.
I'm so looking forward to that child's performance!
Telling us this doesn't do your spy any good.
But that's what makes it fun! It's a cat-and-mouse game. The mouse needs to know the cat is coming, or how else will it run fast enough on its little wheel?
To win, you just have to be the hunter.
And if you do end up catching that child, that just proves they were useless anyway!
That was only the first. What's the next one?
The next prize is right here in this data room. You're so smart, Dr. Herssen. I bet you've already figured it out, no?
Let's be sure to have more fun like this in the future. Until next time, you two!
I wish you a pleasant past, present, and future!
I had so much fun on this little trip to the SkyArk. So, {PlayerName}, how did you feel seeing the Etheric Sea?
Oh, home, sweet home! Your faraway home, the one you can never, ever go back to!
Mmm! Leading you there wasn't all for nothing. The look on your face was the sweetest treat.

Nivora, the Grand Architect of the Fractsidus in disguise, openly confesses "she" revealed herself early to reclaim an old pen. In a mocking acknowledgment of Luuk's efforts, "she" casually informs you that another Fractsidus member hides among the students during the upcoming New Solar Celebration, and that what Luuk seeks is in the station's data room.
This entire SkyArk incident was "her" setup, and she hints at knowing the truth of your origin. In the next moment, "she" vanishes.
Why did you stop me? You think we couldn't have stopped her here?
Yes. My goal was to gather intelligence, not apprehend the Fractsidus's Grand Architect.
The Grand Architect may appear to act on a whim, but in my observation, that playfulness is just another layer of disguise. There's a purpose behind it.
When N.A.N.A. called earlier, something felt off. Warren is a researcher himself. Why would he need to take a student hostage to investigate a debris field?
Even if he did, breaking into the infirmary and letting N.A.N.A. send a distress call was a sloppy strategy. Of course, I'd be the first person she contacted.
I did hear Nivora say you've had her in the infirmary all this time. You were keeping an eye on her, then?
I was waiting for her to show her hand. Until then, it was all speculation. I needed to see her end the "act" to be sure.
Immortal. A thousand faces... We've managed to gather quite a bit of intel on the Grand Architect.
If I'm not mistaken, there should be something more important hidden in this room.
Otherwise, she wouldn't have called it a prize.
When we dug up my "father's" empty grave, I realized that it is no simple feat to find an immortal who leaves no trail.
So that's why you called me afterwards.

Luuk's contact with you on his way to the space station made this joint strike against the Grand Architect possible. For now, he believes you lack the means to truly eliminate this "thousand-faced individual," and that gathering more intelligence is the current priority.
These are... the personnel files from the SkyArk Space Station.
This lettering—
Do you recall the lead researcher on the Etheric Sea Initiative, {PlayerName}? The one we saw in the hologram during our first visit.
Professor Junxi?
Yes. During his lecture, he mentioned a scholar who had just joined the project, Weiying. But his introduction was cut short.
I've found that scholar's record in the system. And her name.
The letters of this name are a perfect match with those engraved on that pen.
Are you saying that scholar is the Grand Architect?
According to these records, the Etheric Sea Initiative was stalled due to a lack of funding until she joined. Then it was pushed back on track.
Her involvement influenced the <ano=Court of Savantae>CSC's</ano> decision on this project.
But everything else about her birthplace, employment history, or academic background is missing.
Sounds like another identity borrowed by the Grand Architect.
Indeed. It seems we've just traced this thousand-faced individual back to an even earlier point in Solaris's history.
These records also show Weiying took great interest in the CSC and Etheric Sea Initiative during that period. That must be why she infiltrated the SkyArk Space Station.
The universe… What secrets is it hiding, behind all those infinite stars?
I really want to know.
And about that footage—No, no need to explain. The fewer people who know about your secret, the better.
It just occurred to me that this wasn't a coincidence. If her goal in the past involved you, then it's something to keep in mind on your journey ahead.
(The Etheric Sea. That might've been my entry point to Solaris after leaving my distant homeland.)
(Weiying was interested in the Etheric Sea before its planet-wide spread. Did she want to use it as a medium to reach somewhere beyond?)
I will. Given her nature, it's only a matter of time before we meet again.
The more she appears, the more she gives away. If she enjoys "playing games," then it means she'll follow some rules at least.
Otherwise, she'd die of boredom.
Hah, exactly. And as I've said before, sometimes style, personal taste, and ambition can be more revealing than intended.

The Fractsidus has more than one base in Solaris, and I'm far from the only one with a grudge or an interest in their activities. Until now, the Grand Architect has been like a reflection in water. "She" never appears as her own person, only by the faces of the already dead.
But now, her fascination with what lies "beyond all those infinite stars" is a thread we can pull. We can start identifying which schemes bear her signature.
I'll be cautious. Before Nivora, did you find any other traces of this Grand Architect in Lahai-Roi?
Yes. There is this one thing. But it's only speculation.
About how Aemeath disappeared, from what you told me, she died from Overclocking trying to stop the Threnodian over a decade ago.
After that incident, the Academy detected cracks on the Threnodian seal in the depths of Bjartr Woods. The damage seemed... intentional.
You mean...
I believe it was the Grand Architect who damaged the seal. And that led to Aemeath's death.
Lucilla's people will handle things here now. We should leave, {PlayerName}.
To where?
Let's go clear our minds. You shouldn't sit with this alone.
And the Court of Savantae... since our Grand Architect has taken interest in them before, a trip to Mengzhou may be worth a visit.
The Court of Savantae was active in Mengzhou?
Just a rumor. They say a city was built there under their direction. There may be clues there.
As for the New Federation, you'll likely end up there eventually if you plan to counter the Fractsidus's operations in the future.
But not now. Things are too complicated over there, and they handle Resonators differently. Even with the Black Shores' backing, going in unprepared would be serious risk.

Inside the data room, you learn the Grand Architect once worked at the SkyArk Station, promoting the Court of Savantae's research on the Etheric Sea—she showed intense interest in it. Connecting the Etheric Sea's link to you and its potential as a gateway, you begin to form theories.
Then Luuk reveals his suspicion that the Grand Architect was the one who sabotaged the Stridergate seal, triggering the Threnodian's breach. To save Lahai-Roi, Aemeath Overclocked forcing a resonance with the Exostrider to stop it. Fresh, burning fury consumes you. Seeing this, Luuk sighs and quietly invites you outside to walk.
Penny for your thoughts?
There's too many to count.
Feel like talking about it?
Maybe a little.
I keep wondering if the choices I made in the past were the right ones.
I still don't know why I chose to erase my memories. That one decision cost me my grip on everything. It made me leave so many people behind.
You, Aemeath, those at the Black Shores, and probably more I don't even know or remember now.
I pulled everyone into my grand plan to "save the world," and when it mattered most, I wasn't even there.
If we can't save Aemeath, she'll just be... forgotten. Left to drift in the void forever.
Even if that hadn't happened, your path was always destined to diverge from most of ours.
You know your lifespan is immense. Barring some accident, most of us will leave this world long before you.
Death and goodbyes are a final lesson no one escapes. But for you, it's a question that lingers... for an exceptionally long time.
You're right.

This has never happened before. I've got a bad feeling about this.
Like a gut feeling?! Well, let's just steer clear of riddles for now then...
Where did Denia go? I need her help for something.
She's probably off napping somewhere.
Lynae's fingers fly across the controller, racking up an impossibly high score. She's completely immersed in the game, seemingly oblivious to your presence...
{PlayerName}, there's a matter regarding the New Solar Celebration I'd like to discuss in detail.
If you have a moment, come find me at these coordinates.
And keep this in mind: When the one from afar touches the "truth," the door of dreams will appear.
How do you feel, {PlayerName}?
I'm fine.
My head hurts.
Glad to hear it.
It's nothing serious. Don't worry.
A strong frequency cut the signal soon after you entered the Dark Side. What exactly happened in there?
(Tell her what happened.)
Tacet Discords… they have no business being in the Dark Side. It seems the situation is even more delicate than we thought.
And that student you met—
Sigrika. The Reflections mentioned her name.
What kind of person is she?
She's considered to be a "future Heliodic Six successor." An A-list student, brilliant in deciphering runes, and passionate about every aspect of Academy life.
Never one to hesitate to lend a helping hand. That kindness has earned her many friends.
Including Nivora.
I've seen them together several times. Nivora's Reflection also spoke of her.
We both know who Nivora really is.
You think Sigrika might be the one the Grand Architect was talking about?
She may have just entered the Dark Side by mistake.
Still… <ano=the Grand Architect>Nivora</ano> could have influenced her more than anyone else.
Besides, I'm curious about the riddle she received. She said it's some kind of rune picture.
I've reviewed every registered riddle for the New Solar Celebration. None fit that description.
Then we'll have to speak with her directly.
My thoughts exactly. The New Solar Celebration holds great importance for the Roya. You'll likely find her at the event venue.
Contact me if you need anything, {PlayerName}. I'll assist however I can.

After returning to the real world, you report everything to Lucilla. She identifies the girl you met as Sigrika, a successor to the Heliodic Six. 
To gather more information about the recent changes within the Dark Side, you head to the celebration venue in search of her.
Dr. Luuk and I will speak with the students you saw appear in the Dark Side.
As for Sigrika, I'll leave her to you.
If you need any help with the investigation, come find me. And, {PlayerName}—as a student yourself…
Do take some time to relax and enjoy the celebration.
Huh, {PlayerName}? Hey! Over here!
Long time no see, {PlayerName}! How's it going?
It's great to see you, Lynae.
All good. And you?
Oh, come on! Don't get all formal on me.
I'm great. Just swamped with Academy business lately. Ha, how I miss the days I could just take off whenever I wanted to.
But look at you! Still full of energy, I see.
People seem so out of it these days. Like they've all just crammed for a month of exams in one night.
Anyway, what brings you here? The celebration, I guess?
(Ask Lynae about Sigrika.)
Sigrika? Sure, I know her. We were in the same year. She saved my butt in Royan Cultural History. I never would've passed that exam without her.
Now she's, like, my senior or whatever.
She actually came asking about how we dealt with that Voidworm a while back.
Said she wished she could've been there to help out.
Oh, and she's planning to get your autograph, too!
Since you're looking for her… oh, right! Let's go ask Denia!
She's a friend of Sigrika's and is in charge of the celebration's entrance tickets. She might know where she's at.
Ah, there she is!
The <te href=800031>New Solar Celebration</te> and riddles… Hm, sounds like a blast!
Here I was thinkin' we could use this chance to relax, but that Architect guy from the Fractsidus mentioned it too…
Yes. The Grand Architect treats everything happening here in Lahai-Roi as a game.
Without you, the game in Lahai-Roi would be so boring! So... you get prizes!
At the upcoming New Solar Celebration, among all the lovely students... stands a member of the Fractsidus.
A Fractsidus agent is hiding among the students, biding their time to strike during the celebration.
Maybe that's what President Lucilla wants to discuss.
Makes sense! But what's with the "one from afar" bit?
Probably a riddle.
Let's go see the President and find out what she's planning.
She's not here. Probably off solving riddles again.
That's alright. To be honest, I don't think I can keep doing this anymore. Just... tell her I said thank you.
Made your decision? Well, no one's going to blame you. Not everyone's built like Sigrika.
How does she manage it? No wonder they call her a future Heliodic Six successor...
Your guess is as good as mine. Leaving? Hm, see ya.
Hi, Denia! You know where Sigrika's at?
Here for her help too? You'll have to get in line. She's been running herself ragged with all these riddles lately.
She's after "<te href=800034>Minerva's Treasure</te>" too? But isn't her sorting exam coming up? How's she handling all that?
You'll have to ask her. She's the one who has to live up to the whole "Heliodic Six successor" thing.
Personally? I'd just let it all go. Life would be way easier that way.
Yeah, but then she wouldn't be Sigrika anymore.
Heh. Just wait here, you'll run into her soon enough. She's been in and out of the Dark Side all day. Those portals can open anywhere.
Who knows? Maybe she'll just fall out of the sky.
...Like that.
...Oh, Denia. Did Isla come by?
She did. Said to thank you. Looks like she figured things out on her own, so she doesn't need your help anymore.
Also, you've got visitors.
Upperclassman Lynae! You're back! I'm so glad! And this is… huh?
You're the upperclassman now, Sigrika. {PlayerName} and I are just lowly freshmen.
M-Me? But I...
By the way, this is {PlayerName}, the one I told you about.
Nice to meet you, upperclassman.
Hello. I'm a freshman here.
Wait—you're the {PlayerName}?! I can't believe you're still a freshman…
It's so great to finally meet you! I'm Sigrika. Lynae's told me all about you. I can't believe you're the one who took down the Voidworm!
So, what can I help you with?
Mind if we talk in private?
In private? Uh-oh, sounds serious. You'd better help {Male=him;Female=her} out, Sigrika!
It's nothing serious. I just have a few questions.
Okay then, we should find a quiet spot...
Go see the Divinator. I'll get you tickets.
Good idea! I can pick up the new riddle while we're there. You're the best, Nia!
It's Denia.
Alright, alright. Let's head to the Divinator's place. See you later, Lynae!
Yeah, I'll get back to work! Bye, {PlayerName}. And check your messages when you get a sec.
See ya!
Upon Lynae's suggestion, you meet a girl called Denia. Not long after, you witness Sigrika falling from the sky.
Now off you go. Bye-bye.
...*Yawns* What's up?
About the New Solar Celebration...
About Sigrika...
About you...
Nothing. Thanks.
A celebration of the new sun. For the Roya, it's like... the grand finale of a thousand-year duty.
But duty is just a fancy word for the chains you put on yourself.
Not a fan of responsibilities then?
I think life feels better without the extra weight.
Just ask her whatever you want to know. She'll help you, no doubt.
That's just the kind of predictably boring person she is.
Huh?
Let's get to the venue, Senior.
Interested? This is the Mind Dive Arcade. The games here are so immersive you can easily lose a whole day.
Would you like to try one?
Okay.
Maybe later.
Then let's go see the Divinator first.
Let's go find the Divinator first.
It looks like Sigrika's diary, better not read it for now...
Such a high score… How did you do that?
You'll have to show me your secrets sometime!
I heard the student who solves the most riddles gets a wish granted by the Academy.
What's your wish?
Um... Well... I'd like to get a clear photo of a bird. Yeah!
(She sounds hesitant. Is she trying to hide something?)
No wish greater than that?
Sounds like you just made that up.
This one's good enough for me.
Of course not...
Denia said this year's theme is all about Royan culture. As a Roya myself, it'd be a shame not to take part.
A good friend of mine loved this event too. We used to solve riddles together.
I don't know where she is now, but I want to keep going, for her sake, until she's back.
I think she'd be happy if I did well!
Look, Sigrika just passed your score.
That's a Heliodic Six successor for you. It's only natural.
It would be more of a shock if she couldn't solve them.
Let's go.
Despite earning herself a top position in the event's leaderboard, it's clear that something is bothering Sigrika.
When I met you in the Dark Side yesterday, I didn't realize you were the one in Lynae's stories.
She said you're very determined. You always do whatever it is you set your mind on.
I think that's amazing.
This is it. Denia found this spot. It's quiet, and not many people come here.
See? Perfect for a chat.
Senior, you... wanted to talk about what happened in the Dark Side, right?
(Until I know where she stands, I won't mention the Grand Architect.)
(I'll see what she has to say about the other topics first.)
Denia said you've been busy solving riddles lately.
Yes. It's great fun. I'd like to solve as many as I can before the celebration ends.
Notice anything unusual while you were in there?
Well, everything in there is unusual.
You know how they say the Dark Side reflects people's truest selves?
Once, I saw a black cat that wished to go home. It was a brilliant cat, with black wings to fly.
Another time, I talked for hours with a ghost. I couldn't see her, but I could hear her voice.
Did the black cat find its home?
What did this ghost say?
No, it disappeared in a hurry. Thinking about it now, it was probably someone's delusion.
She said she had to go somewhere far away to do something really important. That she wouldn't see her family for a long time... so she was feeling a little lonely.
But she was so determined... it warmed my heart. I never forgot her.
Such strange, but fascinating experiences. I could spend an entire day in the Dark Side, leaving all my worries behind.
But the disturbances in there lately... You must have heard about them too.
So those things we saw yesterday…
Yes. Especially that rune that lit up out of nowhere.
See? If I just leave it like this, it's just a normal rune.
But, if I invoke its True Name...
…I can call forth the power sleeping within.
What invoked the one we saw before?
I have no idea... I tried to trace the source, but those runes seemed to come from nowhere.
It's worth a closer look. We should go back into the Dark Side.
Then we're going to need this.
Hello? Can you hear me, Didi? Wake up. It's Sigrika. Time to work.
Didi… Scientific Divination Unit. The name "Divinator" is retained due to high student approval ratings.
User login… Sigrika… Switching to Riddle Channel!

Sigrika speaks of the Dark Side's changes, such as the strange runes that keep appearing out of nowhere. While Sigrika is still in the dark about their origin and purpose, they remain a solid lead. 
She suggests using riddles as a way to get back into the Dark Side.
If you would like a riddle, please answer my questions.
A Q&A? Really?
The black of deep space, or the white of the frostlands?
Black.
White.
Any other colors to choose from?
Deep space and the frostlands both represent the unknown... but I like warmer tones. They remind me of the sun.
Solitary study, or collaborative gaming with friends?
Solitary study.
Gaming with friends.
Both.
The gift of miraculous comprehension, or earned recognition from others?
Miraculous comprehension.
Earned recognition from others.
Neither. I do what I want.
You answered so quickly!
You answered so quickly!
I didn't know you could answer like that!
As for me... guess I'll have to work harder then.
Didi... Analyzing data... Presenting results...
Look! Here's the riddle.
It's a picture.
Yes. All of Didi's riddles are pictures. The way into the Dark Side is hidden somewhere in it.
And finding your way out of the Dark Side solves the riddle.
(Inspect the picture.)
Look at where the student is standing. Hmm, I think I recognize this spot...
What's she drawing?
Runes. This one represents the "sun." It's super important to us Roya.
The sun blesses the land with its light. Everyone, from the past to the future, gets to bask in its warmth.
But this sun seems to be feeding the monsters in the shadows, too.
Doesn't that seem wrong?
Now that you mention it... it does. And it reminds me of that rune we saw before.
Then we're on the right track.
Any other clues on the riddle?
Hmm... Oh, here! A line is written on the back—
Through me, seek the "gift"... seek the...
...I've got it!
I think... it's telling us to find this sun.
For <ano=the Roya>us</ano>, the very first rune we ever learn, the most familiar one, is the sun.
To bathe in the blessing of sunlight is its own kind of <ano=gift>inheritance</ano>.
In other words, finding the sun rune is our way into the Dark Side.
That's right. It's just like a game I played when I was little.
The elders of our tribe would hide runes all over Bjartr Woods, each one leading to the next.
All we had to do was follow the trail to find our way out of the forest.
And now, the sun is the first rune in our trail!
To solve this riddle, you're going to need a guide who really knows Royan runes.
(She's right. Otherwise, I'd waste too much time.)
(And if she's connected to the Dark Side's disturbances, it's best I keep an eye on her anyway.)
What's wrong? Don't think I can handle it, Senior? I'm pretty good, you know!
You sure do like to help out, Sigrika.
Then I'll be counting on you.
Let's solve this riddle together.
Great! You can trust me, {PlayerName}! Let's go find the answer!

You receive a riddle from the Divinator hinting at a deeper transformation within the Dark Side—it is secretly spawning monsters. 
Sigrika realizes that the riddle-solving process resembles a game from her childhood and volunteers to guide you through it.
Mm, I see. I'll count on you, then, Dr. Luuk.
Ah, {PlayerName}'s here. I'll brief {Male=him;Female=her} on the situation.
President Lucilla! Whaddya need us for? And what did you mean by "the one from afar who touches 'truth'"?
Why don't you take a guess? It means exactly what it says.
...The one from afar is me.
And the "truth" that reveals the door of dreams is...?
The "truth" has waited for you here for a very long time.
That pillow is truth? Seriously?
What's that for? A nice nap?
You need a good pillow for a good sleep. When it comes to "dreams," that is the absolute truth.
Oh, quite. When it comes to "dreams," that is the absolute truth.
A simple riddle, isn't it?
Okay... but what's that got to do with us? You didn't call us here to solve a riddle, right?
You're here because I'd like you to investigate the "<te href=800032>Academy's Dark Side</te>." We believe the Grand Architect's next move is tied to it.
The Academy's Dark Side?
Think of it as the "Academy's reflection." It's a special Sonoro Sphere formed from the collective emotions of the student body.
It's an inseparable part of this place, a mirror into the thoughts of every student here... a reflection of their "youth."
"Youth"... a fascinating concept. So full of ideals and passion, but also anxiety and sorrow.
The Dark Side absorbs it all, reflecting their truest selves back at them. And that's not all.
Imagine the Dark Side as a vortex. Negative emotions like anxiety and sorrow form its eye.
They swell and collide, seeping into the students' minds. Over time, they come to affect the Academy itself.
Exactly. It's been troubling the Academy for some time.
Many of our students were hailed as "geniuses" back home, only to discover they're just one of many here. They've given their all, yet find the peak they once stood upon is now out of reach.
The Dark Side forces these young minds to face that "truth."
A harsh reality that can be difficult to accept.
In the end, the Research Institute found a way to confine the Dark Side within "riddles," turning it into a harmless game that students look forward to each year.
Solve a riddle, face your problems, and process the emotions festering in the Dark Side. That was the original purpose.
But recently, something's changed. Dr. Luuk has reported a sharp decline in students' mental states, as if they've been influenced somehow.
At the same time, I've detected a frequency in the Dark Side that doesn't belong to the Academy. It can't be traced or analyzed.

We need more information, but we're stretched thin. Between hunting for the Fractsidus agent, the celebration approaching, and dealing with the students' deteriorating mental health, it's not looking good.
The Grand Architect intends to create chaos in the Academy to conceal their true objective.
Looks like we'll have to investigate the Academy's Dark Side ourselves.
So this pillow… is the key to getting in?
Hehe, I see! This is our starting line!
Yes. Head in whenever you're ready.
I'll stay outside and keep in touch.

Lucilla detects a strange frequency not belonging to the Academy in its "Dark Side." Coincidentally, many students have been reporting mental disturbances. Suspecting a connection to the "game" the Grand Architect mentioned, you agree to Lucilla's request and enter the Dark Side to investigate.
(I should send this riddle to the President as well. She might find something we missed.)
(Send the riddle.)
Lucilla, Sigrika and I received this riddle from the Divinator at the celebration venue.
I've attached the photo and the coordinates.
I'm concerned other students might be getting similar riddles.
Very well. We'll trace it.
Focus on your investigation and be careful.
Found it! It should be here.
There's nothing here.
Do you have a camera?
Let me enchant it with a rune...
There! Now you should be able to see it too.
Here, try taking a picture.
There it is.
A concealed rune won't escape these eyes.
Now, I'll illuminate its True Name.
If we follow its guidance, we'll find the answer.
Look! A trail of runes to follow.
You know, when I played that rune-finding game in Bjartr Woods, I was always the first one out.
Everyone said I had a gift, that I'd be the first again, and again, and again.
They all believed in me, so... I had to work even harder to live up to it.
I spent so, so much time studying those runes.
Before I realized it, everyone had moved on to more important things… and the game had already ended.
See, all the runes lead to this place.
It has to be an entrance into the Dark Side.
Remember you asked what I was doing in the Dark Side yesterday?
I was there for the riddles. But what about you?
I'm looking into something important. I'm sorry, but I can't share the details with you yet.
Oh that's okay. Just tell me whenever you're ready.
Time to illuminate this rune. On three… two…
One...
Say cheese!
All clear. No lasting harm. If the runes didn't answer, it's likely because your heart wasn't quite in the right place to call them.
Do you still remember what I told you last time, Sigrika?
You said I should have more faith in myself.
And not to push yourself too hard. Here, have a candy.
That song we heard… it felt nostalgic.
You liked it?
It was beautiful.
It was effective.
Fleet Snowfluff's songs always do bring a little warmth to the soul.
Aemeath...
When we tried to enter the Dark Side to help you, we found our frequencies denied. That thing hijacked it. Only students were allowed in.
So we had to get creative. Luckily, it can't control the emotions already inside.
Every emotion leaves a mark. The fan meeting you held not long ago left the students with plenty of happy memories. That song helped guide you right through that thing's blockade.
It's no ordinary Tacet Discord. What exactly is that thing?
I want to know what I saw in there.
Please trust me, Professor… and you too, Senior. I really want to help.
Let's share what we know so far.
We need the full picture to act.
What we can confirm is that the Tacet Discord was sent by the Fractsidus.
The Fractsidus?
Their Grand Architect tipped us off about their plans in Lahai-Roi, that he will play a game with us.
It seems the "game" she referred to is this riddle event our students are so fond of.
We've already tracked the participants. The effects of these riddles are already spilling into their real lives.
Some abandoned their research projects. Others are lashing out at classmates... and a few have lost control entirely.
These students have all become pawns in the Fractsidus's little show.
You're one of them, Sigrika.
Me?
Those riddles and Tacet Discords we encountered in the Dark Side were clearly targeting you.
I thought you might've been linked to the recent disturbances, but now I see you're just another victim.
What kind of game would do something like this?! We have to stop it. I can help you solve these strange riddles.
Professor, Senior, please let me...
You need to rest, Sigrika.
Why? Because I'm not good enough?
Because it's dangerous.
I see how determined you are. But I won't risk my students' safety.
(Comfort her.)
(Support Lucilla.)
Just take it easy for now, Sigrika.
The President is right. The Dark Side is too volatile right now. Just take it easy.
Senior...
...I see.

Back outside the Dark Side, you piece together what just happened. 
You realize those Tacet Discords you ran into are the work of the Fractsidus trying to drag students into their twisted game. 
Lucilla urges Sigrika not to endanger herself further, but the girl has her own ideas about what she wants to do.
Hello, {PlayerName}. You free?
Wanna try some Rainbow Bean Pop Rocks?
What's that…?
You'll know once you're here!
I'll be waiting at the celebration venue. Please do come find me!
What's that…?
Senior, you're here!
I bought this for you. As a thank-you for your help lately.
Here, it's all yours!
This is...
...Rainbow Bean Pop Rocks?
That's right! This one is made specially for the New Solar Celebration. I had to wait in line forever to get it.
You never know what funny effect you're going to get! It's different each time. But it's supposed to help with relaxing.
Go on, give it a try!
(Take one boldly.)
(Take one hesitantly.)
(Return it to Sigrika.)
Are you sure? Oh, look—a big rabbit over there!
Rabbit—?
[Sigrika pops a candy into Rover's mouth.]
...It actually tastes pretty good. Wait—is that my voice?!
Can this really be?!
Let me try one too...
This one… tastes kind of weird—hic! Oh no—no, I wasn't—hic! Excuse me!
I have lungs, not gills—hic!
I—I can't—hic—make it stop!
Abby.
Huh? Think you can just summon—Hey, what did ya just give me—?!
Chuuu?!
Hic—you sound like a Soliskin now!
This is so much fun! Maybe we should share them with others too!
Hic... Don't worry, it won't last long and—hic!
I'm okay. But you'd better take it easy...
...If you're looking for a particular stall, find Lynae. If you're hurt, call N.A.N.A. If you lost something, bother that one running around in computers. Just don't bother me, kay?
But I'm here for you, Nia—hic!
Give me a break, Siggy. Can't a girl just enjoy the fresh air on a beautiful, class-free morning?
Oh, never mind. Your... excessive cheerfulness just ruined the vibe. Surprised you bounced back so fast. What do you want?
We want to—hic!
...Do you want some water?
Sigrika wants you to try this.
Why does your voice sound like that?
Chuuu!
Just try it, Denia! Please?
…I refuse. The last time I tried your candy, I was shooting rainbow beams out of my eyes and mouth for four minutes and thirty-five seconds.
That was a research sample! This is real! Just trust me and try—hic!
Case in point. Can someone just solve the riddle of who made these strange candies in the first place?
If you must find someone to try it, look for Lynae. She'd probably love this stuff. Here, take your tickets.
Now shoo. See you.
Hi, {PlayerName}! Hi, Sigrika!
Hello, Lynae—Hic!
Why are you hiccuping, Sigrika?
We just had some Rainbow Bean Pop Rocks. Want to try?
No way! Your voice is totally different! Gimme one, I gotta try this!
Lynae takes the candy under your watchful eyes.
Oh, that's "awful"!
Wait, that "is" what I meant...? Everything is "the same as" what I want to say... Huh?
It's making you say the opposite of what you're trying to say...
Hahaha! This is "not" interesting, how "boring" is this!
Oh, by the way, how's that thing from the other day going?
Still working on it.
I'll make sure it gets handled.
Aha, so you're taking a break, huh?
In that case, you need to take a "bad" rest! Here, I "don't think you should " try this game I co-developed. We "shouldn't" play ten rounds!
Ten rounds it is!
I'm good. You two play it.
Raiding time!!!
Alright. It's gaming time, Sigrika!
I want to try it! What do you say?
You watch them play. Lynae's hands fly across the screen with ease, while Sigrika scrambles to keep up. It's a welcome moment of peace.
Phew, I always "hate" playing games.
Ahem, I mean... Never mind. You know what I was trying to say.
You can't talk normally, Lynae.
But don't worry, the effect won't last long. I've already stopped hiccuping.
"It's not okay," talking like this is actually really "boring." I'm having a "terrible" time!
…I'll wait for it to wear off before I say anything else.
By the way, do you still have any candies left?
Of course! I bought plenty. Here.
Thanks! This candy is "the worst." I want some other people to try it too, you know, share the "frowns"!
Have a "bad" day, you two!
We will. Enjoy your day!
Have a "bad" day... Have a good day...
Different words, but you can tell what she means. I guess it's because Lynae always speaks from the heart.
That's really nice.
So? Did you have a good day?
Hm? Your voice is back to normal.
Well, I guess I had quite a "terrible" rest.
Everyone's enjoying the celebration.
When I close my eyes, I can hear all kinds of voices around me.
Vendors calling out new kinds of Pop Rocks, students cheering about new records...
Some are singing, others are just laughing... It's so nice.
But... besides all that, I still hear other voices.
The ones from the Dark Side, when I let everyone down... they made me feel so lost.
After we got out, you told me to walk away. For my own safety.
But when I was alone, I remembered all the encouraging things people have always said to me.
"You're going to do great things." "You can solve any riddle." "You can do it." "You can prove yourself"...
Their words shone like molten gold. So radiant, and so... warm.
I don't want to be the one to drop them.
So many voices... When you hear so many voices in your head, Senior, what do you do?
I listen to what my own heart is saying.
I try to live up to their expectations.
Hehe, I like that. The voice of my heart... I've never thought of that before.
Right... Living up to their expectations!
But sometimes, you don't need to overthink what you do.
Don't overthink what to do… So you mean just—
Just do it.
We have an emergency, {PlayerName}. Multiple students are trapped in the Dark Side.
I've already sent the coordinates.
The Fractsidus are making their move. The situation is serious.
I'm coming with you.
Alright. Let's go.

Amid the lively and relaxed atmosphere of the celebration, Sigrika opens up about what's been on her mind. 
Before you can talk long, Lucilla cuts in with an urgent message.
Good, you're here, {PlayerName}. And... Sigrika.
Professor Lucilla...
I know you want to prove yourself. But in your current state, I'm afraid I can't authorize it.
You must understand how dangerous this mission is. Our enemies hide in the dark, and we still don't know that Tacet Discord's weakness.
No, Professor. Please let me join.
I know you're worried, but I know the Dark Side better than anyone. How can I stand by when my classmates are trapped in there?
I can help you decipher the runes. I can be useful.
This isn't about proving myself anymore. It's about doing what's right.
She's made up her mind.
She can contribute to the mission.
These are the students whose signals vanished while in the Dark Side.
Chisa...? She's trapped in there too?
And also Isla?! Why would she...
They were all in the dormitory hall. Someone must have activated a riddle, and the Dark Side pulled everyone in.
Mornye is already on it. I have her searching for the students' locations.
And this is what I found.
Another runic riddle.
"Receive the sunlight's blessing"... What could it mean?
It's referring to our rite of passage.
When a Roya is deemed ready to bear the tribe's expectations, we go to the Reactor Drive to be Imprinted.
The Drive leaves markings on our bodies. It is a blessing for the next stage of our lives.
See these? They are the sunlight's Imprints.
