Yeah, I'm doing great today. Don't worry!
Denia's out of the ward, so I'm taking a walk with her...
I know what you're worried about. I remember everything from back then... Why would I ever contact those people?
...Then who are you calling?
This'll do. I'll just open the comm, and you can wait here with me for a while.
You've been doing this all along?
Yeah. It was all made up. To keep her happy. But I didn't realize how much effort it takes to keep a simple lie going.
This will only complicate things.
But I can't be honest with her, can I? She's all cheerful on the outside, but she bears more than enough worries for her size... As her friend, that's the least I can do.
And besides... having a sweet, trusting friend like her around is a great cover, isn't it?
That's self-deluding.
...I thought you'd put it more gently.
Alright. Looks like she's finished her call. Let's head over.
Perfect timing! We should go check out the new desserts!
This part, finally...
What made you want to buy cake today, Denia?
You'll find out soon enough.
Today's new desserts include: Frostwort Dumpling, Fern Spore Kelp Biscuit, Pine Needle Lichen Roll, and—on special—Jarred Fish Muffin...
Those names sound... intense.
Do you think you could assemble them into a cake?
What a terrifying thought, Nia...
(Taste aside, the operational procedure was very clear about food intake. I should check with Arman...)
Patients need to be careful about food safety.
I'm just going through the motions... She can eat it for me.
I happen to know a team that specializes in desserts. We could order a cake from them if you want.
What kind of style are you thinking of?
Oh, really? Then can I add Rainbow Bean Pop Rocks? And Creeping Torchpine nuts. Oh, and some Fruit Crackle too?
Denia, you can't put Pop Rocks on a cake. You need to start with a base flavor...
Hm... okay. Let me think...
Let's get an orange cake. I promised Sigrika we'd celebrate together. She likes oranges.
But make sure you add everything I mentioned earlier, okay?

Having promised to help out at the Reactor Drive, Sigrika won't be able to celebrate Denia's birthday together with you.
Before leaving, she promises Denia to spend her next birthday together.
Tell Arman about the cake.
Denia needs a birthday cake, but I don't think the ones sold at the Academy will work.
Even the vendors won't touch those. Don't buy them.
We'll take care of the cake. Ingredients and preparation will need to be vetted.
Did she specify what kind of cake she wants?
An orange cake.
An orange cake.
Copy.
There are some additional requirements.
Add Rainbow Bean Pop Rocks, Creeping Torchpine nuts, and Fruit Crackle.
Arman has withdrawn a message.
Understood. We'll make it happen. Expect completion this evening.
Have you decided yet? What's it going to be, Denia?
Keeping it a secret for now.
The cake will be ready by tonight.
Tonight...
Tonight might not work for me... I... I promised Professor Mornye I'd help out at the Reactor Drive today...
Well, that's a shame, Siggy. I was hoping to share the birthday cake with you, but I guess you'll just have to make do with the leftovers.
Birthday cake...? Wait, today's your birthday? So that's why Rover is...
Denia wanted to surprise you.
Then I... I'll leave Professor Mornye a message...
It's alright, Siggy. I'm sure you've got something really important to do with Professor Mornye.
Well, asking for a day off once in a while wouldn't...
Nope. No running away from it.
How can you become the kind of person you look up to, if you run away from something like this?
But... aren't you the one who's been telling me "it's okay to run away" this whole time, Denia?
It was just to make you feel better. I say it to everyone.
No. You're acting super weird today.
All of a sudden you asked me to come out, had me take pictures with you, revealed it's your birthday, and... told me not to run away... This... It's not like you at all...
Siggy, I...
Are you hiding something from me?
Oh, couldn't you be a little less perceptive at a time like this, Sigrika?
If you want me to keep playing dumb, I can do that, and I'll leave it there. As usual.
But, there's only one thing I want to make sure... Will you still be celebrating your birthday this time next year?
I will...
Then next year... we'll celebrate your birthday together. Promise?
Promise.
How about we make a cake together when the time comes?
I thought you said there's only one thing you wanted to make sure of...
Denia still has some check-ups to do tonight. Maybe after she's fully recovered in a few days...
You sound just like Dr. Herssen, Senior.
It's fine, we've made a promise... Right, off I go to sort out some files.
You go get those files, Sigrika...
Happy birthday, Denia!
Phew, that was tough... I'm never good at this with her around.
Well, that made things really awkward at the end... If you'd just listened to me and moved on...
Sigrika really cares about you.
You'll regret it.
Oh, sneaky you, being so nice and kind all of a sudden.
To be honest, I'm really impressed hearing those words from you, {PlayerName}... I suppose you must've gone through plenty of farewells, haven't you?
Strong, caring. Keep it up and I might actually fall for you.
All right, break time's over. I almost died of boredom being stuck in the sickbed these past few days. How about you and I go play some video games, {PlayerName}?

Having promised to help out at the Reactor Drive, Sigrika won't be able to celebrate Denia's birthday together with you.
Before leaving, she promises Denia to spend her next birthday together.
Look at all those games... What do you have in mind, {PlayerName}? I was thinking Lahai-Roi Blocks...
Catchow.
Wait, really...? I even gave you the hint.
Don't tell me you're the type who during a date wants to watch separate movies and just meet up afterward.
Playing Lahai-Roi Blocks with you brings back bad memories.
Ugh... You have such a good memory, {PlayerName}... Alright, let's start with your game.
{PlayerName} is here. Yes, I understand. Please rest assured.
Sorry to pull you in on such short notice, {PlayerName}. I'm Arman, I sent the message. The situation's worse than we anticipated, so I'll keep it short.
How's Denia?
She's... awake. But just as we feared, the Fractsidus did something to her.
After waking up, her frequency deteriorated rapidly into systemic failure. According to Rabelle College's estimate, she has... one week. At best.
What's gone wrong?
No idea. There's not enough time to even determine whether it's physiological... or caused by the Threnodian.
The New Federation is pressing charges over the Stridergate incident and the residual frequency on the Dimmr Plains. They want Denia handed over immediately.

We didn't comply, of course. Denia was a Startorch Academy student. Sending her there would turn her into a mere research subject... and cost us our only chance to reach the truth or contest the charges.
I see the picture... When you say "contest the charges," are you suggesting Denia is the key to breaking this stalemate?
Exactly. First, her connection to the Voidborne Threnodian has enormous research value. Even with the Stridergate sealed, she could open new directions for Voidmatter science.
And based on I.R.I.S.'s review of our prior interactions, Denia likely knows the source of the Threnodian frequency on the Dimmr Plains. The reason why her condition is worsening, too.
If she is willing to cooperate, we can resolve this before the New Fed forces our hand. We treat her. She helps with the report. It'll be a win-win, ideally.
Sounds like that didn't go very smoothly.
No. She's been... resistant. To any form of contact.

This is where we need you, {PlayerName}. I'm sure you understand, mental stability is a prerequisite for frequency control. You have prior contact with her, and... your experience with Threnodians also makes you a safer anchor in the negotiation.
(Denia might be a viable opening. But until I figure out what the Fractsidus is planning and where they are now, I shouldn't commit to anything reckless.)
I will speak to her and make my judgment from there.
Also, I want this meeting kept off the record. No files, not even in I.R.I.S.'s archive.
...Understood. Then I'll leave this in your hands, {PlayerName}. Her identity is only known to very few now, I can assure you.
Wait, that character you're using... Is that me?
That feels a bit... odd. And is that Sigrika next to you?
Oh, there's a cake coming down!
Keep the joystick steady.
I guess Sigrika and I don't make much of a tag team... Shame.
You know what they say: Get good.
What does that have to do with it?
I haven't figured out these new games yet. Let's just go play Lahai-Roi Blocks, {PlayerName}.
How about we compete for high scores? I've been really good at it since I was a child, you know.
Sure.
Is this why you threw blocks at me?
Awesome! Thanks, {PlayerName}.
Still holding grudges, are we? Or is this your way to get my attention?
I didn't know you were this good... Well...
Anyway, I was wondering, how did you and Siggy get acquainted, {PlayerName}?
We met during the New Solar Celebration.
Ah, I heard Siggy mention you were a great help... Any stories you mind sharing?
You know what happened. Weren't you the ones behind it all?
That wasn't my plan at all...
You were gonna say goodbye to her, right?
I suppose... I wanted to treat her to some cake, and then get it off my chest when the moment was right.
You mean the birthday, the goodbye, or you've been lying to her the whole time?
All of it, I guess... I actually hoped she'd be angry.
You want her to be mad at you? Why?
That way... by the time she realizes I'm gone, she won't feel as upset...
Knowing your ex-friend died is better than losing an actual friend, right?
She won't see it that way.
Sigh. That is why I hate people like you.
Keeping all the burdens on yourself when you know you can ignore them... The exact way of life I loathe.
But you still encouraged her.
Oh, sneaky you, beating my score while I was distracted talking.
How else am I supposed to beat you?
It was you who used this trick first...
Messing up little things like this every now and then can actually make you more likable, okay?
Anyway, it's getting late, we should keep moving... The Archive is usually my favorite place for pastime. I'd like another visit.

Inside the Mind Dive Arcade, you and Denia talk about Sigrika, and you learn what Denia truly thinks about her.
After a moment to collect herself, Denia continues with you through the day's arranged schedule.
Denia? I heard from Arman that you've been hospitalized in the infirmary for the last few days. How are you feeling?
I'm fine. There's nothing to worry about.
Well, you look paler than you were before. A patient should get plenty of rest.
And this is... Oh, wait, you must be {PlayerName}, right? I'm surprised to see Denia with you. She didn't cause you any trouble, did she?
No, not at all. It's her birthday today, and the infirmary asked me to take her out for some fresh air.
Did they now? That makes it sound even more suspicious.
Have you known each other long?
Sure. She wasn't hard to miss for taking naps here in her first week of school.
When she heard I needed data on the Void Storm at the time, she just rushed out of campus with that sketchy bubble of hers... What were you thinking, really?
That was ages ago... Can we please move on?
Well, I feel I should pass it on to as many people as possible before I graduate. And you—try not to be the hero all the time. Just learn to lean on the people around you more often.
Graduate?
Here, this is for you. I never got the chance to give it to you.
You were always nagging me about that Royan fairytales collection. I had a friend print it in color.
I had no idea it's your birthday today, so consider it a birthday gift from me, Denia.
Nastasha, your hands...
Just a minor issue from that incident earlier. Don't worry, Dr. Herssen said I'll barely notice it in a few years.
It's from that Voidmatter contamination...
But if it can heal as you said, then... there's really no need for you to leave, right? With all those advanced techs of the Spacetrek Collective...
Well, that's exactly why they deemed it's no longer safe for me to stay here. Something about Lahai-Roi's environment makes the contamination even worse for the nervous system.
B-But...
Who would've thought my own thesis would set me up for early retirement?
But you once said... your dream is to...
"Unveil the secrets of Voidmatter particles for all mankind?" I recall saying something like that, yeah... But listen, Denia, dreams are sometimes just...
No. That's not it. Even someone like me can tell... Everyone here...
Everyone here signed the agreement. If they choose to leave Lahai-Roi, that means...
Calling it quits? Not even close. Who knows, maybe I'll come back from the New Federation in a couple of years. It's too bad that you'd have already graduated by then.
That's not what I meant. You've always been a great student, Nastasha... It shouldn't have ended like this.
Calm down, Denia.
Everything that's happened, it's all my fault...
What's with you today? How is this your fault?
I'm sorry, Nastasha. Denia's not fully recovered yet. You'll have to excuse us.
I see. Keep your eyes on the road. She seems a little off today.
Oh. And happy birthday, Denia!

You and Denia meet with the librarian, Nastasha. When she learns it's Denia's birthday, she brings out a gift she's been waiting a long time to give her.
You both notice Nastasha's prosthetic hand. She admits she was contaminated by Voidmatter during the previous incident and will soon be leaving the Spacetrek Collective to recover.
You okay, Denia?
Your frequency is very unstable now. You should take your meds. Come with me.
I'm sorry. I lied to you. It's actually not my birthday today.
Why use this as your excuse?
That's because... a birthday is supposed to be proof that you were born. That's what they always say, right?
Everyone has a birthday... Sigrika has one, so does Nastasha... Even those TARD-E Units manufactured in factories have their own birthdays.
But I don't. The Fractsidus has no record of my birth. Nothing to prove my identity.
There's only this image burrowed inside my head, playing over and over again in my dreams...
In it, I would always step into the same lake. A woman sways her arms in the wind, crying.
She stares from afar, calling out to me: Denia, Denia... Dasvidaniya.
So if I truly had a name and a birthday, maybe I could then die as a real person, no?
What makes you think so?
Because I'm running out of time.

I'm out of time for so many things. But I can at least... try to die with a little dignity, right? I should get to act like a real person. Face what I've done, say a real goodbye... and then just end it the right way.
What a shame. I even picked a good day to do it, but I never practiced how to properly say goodbye to them.
Lying... is the only thing I'm good at.
Is this the ending you're happy with?
Of course not. But at least I was able to see their goofy smiles as I had them completely fooled just like before... Something to die happy about, I guess.
But you're crying.
It's just... a reaction. That's all. The idea that everything will just vanish, that it'll all go back to the void... it makes me cry. Instantly.
Just like years ago... When I touched it for the first time...
Even after you die, tomorrow, the sun still rises.
Of course I know that. It's not like I think the world will change once I die.
It will change.
Sigrika and Nastasha's lives will change. They'll lose an important friend. No matter how they ultimately break from the shadows, what is lost... is lost forever.
Ever thought about continuing your life?
Do I deserve to?
That's not for me to judge.
But in Rinascita... I've met people just like you.
In the lives forced upon them, happiness was always fleeting, leaving only pain and fear that never dissipate.
Yet, even so... they fought for those brief, gifted moments of happiness till the very end.
You once joked how the great {PlayerName} is a savior, but in Rinascita...
I failed to save them.
But it sounds like... they made their own choices.
True. Just like when you tried to drive me away. You also made what you thought was the best choice... You all hoped for more people to survive.
And so did I.
So, if the boundaries between humans and creations are already obscure, what is it that determines who we are?
I... I don't know.
It's the heart, Denia.
What you are isn't defined by where you're from, but by your heart.
Feeling better?
(Based on the frequency shown during her complications, things are worse than what Arman said.)
(At this rate, she won't even last a week... Is this why she chose today?)
Try to comfort her.
Try to sit closer to her.
Hand her Nastasha's present.
Nastasha's got talent. The Collective won't give up on her.
...You're right... I've been lying to myself all along.

Nastasha's condition shakes Denia deeply. Her time is running out, and she has to face the question of her true identity.
As a creation of the Fractsidus, what ending should she choose for herself?
You know there are no easy answers. So instead of offering one, you share your own truth with her.
The heart.
Are you willing to trust me?
This right here. A gift from the Grand Architect—the page buried within my frequency... is here.
(Could this be... Leviathan?)
..."Do find your way home more often"?
Ha, just as I thought...
You can really work wonders, {PlayerName}.
Denia?
You are... literally my least favorite type of person.
Now, can you tell me why you loathe me?
Hmm... Where do I start—
{PlayerName}, we've detected a severe frequency fluctuation! Is everything all right?
Everything's fine. We'll be back soon.
Very well... I'll see you soon.
Sounds like Professor Arman is getting a bit impatient. We should head back.
What about your answer?
Ahuhuh... No need to get ahead of yourself now, {PlayerName}. You're not quite there yet. I'm keeping it secret for now.
Plus, we still haven't fulfilled our agreement yet. Can't let the cake go to waste.
Would you want to come out with me again after tomorrow, {PlayerName}?
I would.
I wouldn't.
Hmm... Well, that makes things trickier. I... still have things I have to do, after all.
...If only today could be a bit longer.
Is that so? Then I'm relieved... I still have things I have to do, after all.
However, did it ever cross your mind, {PlayerName}, that my being alive and staying here might be an even bigger problem?
...If you feel you don't belong here, then some day in the future, would you be willing to—
Stop right there—it was just a joke. I don't want to put you in a tough spot.
Easy. Today is my birthday. I won't be going anywhere.
At least to you... this will be my last lie.

At last, Denia confesses the secret of the Grand Architect's "gift."
Following her instructions, you destroy the thing that has bound her all along—a page infused with the power of the Threnodian Leviathan. 
For now, Denia's immediate danger seems to have passed. You talk about the future as you make your way back toward the Academy.
N.A.N.A. is conducting a thorough checkup on Denia. I imagine this must have been a very long day for you, {PlayerName}.
Her conditions have greatly improved since this morning. As for the frequency fluctuation earlier... Did something happen?
About that...
You tell Arman about the book page left by the Grand Architect.

Residual energy of the Threnodian from Rinascita? Could there be some form of interaction between the Threnodians? Is the Fractsidus actually manipulating her and suppressing her abilities through such means?
It's no wonder we couldn't find the source of the symptoms. Fortunately, you were here to assist, {PlayerName}.
What will happen to Denia after tomorrow?
...It'll be the same as the past few days. Although she won't be sent to the New Federation, she'll still be kept under containment and assist with our research.
I know what you're thinking, {PlayerName}... I've been monitoring your itinerary and field reports all day.
But even if everyone recognizes her as a victim, the Spacetrek Collective's work and responsibilities will not change for her.
We don't have better solutions now. This is the fact.
What about her birthday cake?
We haven't had a chance to get it yet. It's still with Zahira. You can only get that specific Fruit Crackle she requested from Zahira...
But since she hopes you can accompany her on her birthday, I believe you should be the one to personally bring her the cake... We'll be waiting for you here.
Back when I taught at the Academy, there was a student who would always sleep in my lectures.
I would wake her up to answer questions on purpose, because she had no idea what she was wasting.
Later, a TA named Nastasha asked me to go easy on her, saying she could only sleep in a place where she felt secure, and that her grades in my class were still doing well.
...I knew that girl had helped collect data for many people in the Department of Voidmatters, but the issue was that I couldn't understand her behavior at all.
While everyone else was out pursuing their scientific dreams, how can you be here sleeping? Is your dream to be a research assistant for the rest of your life?
It was after the Threnodian incident that I finally knew the answer.
To be honest, when I just sent you the message, for a moment I even fantasized a reply in which you plan to take her far away from Lahai-Roi... to somewhere no one could find.
Haha... I'm glad you didn't do that, {PlayerName}, or else we'd all be done for.
Anything else you want to confirm, {PlayerName}?
Any progress on tracking the Threnodian frequency?
How was Denia acting when she spoke with you?
That call earlier, was it Lucilla?
That's all.

We've narrowed down the location, but Voidmatter contamination there is heavy, so cleanup and investigation will be slow. That said, recent spectral analysis points to a direct correlation between the frequency and Denia's physical condition.
"Cold" is the word. So cold that even N.A.N.A. can't establish any meaningful contact. We are still not sure if the Threnodian did this, but she is not the Denia we knew.
You've met Denia before?
I have. Back then, I was teaching a required course in Voidmatters Science, and she slept through a good portion of it, so I remember her.
Yes. The President is busy smoothing things over with some big names. She asked me to send her regards.
Oh, and she also has a message for you: "Only the kids who make it out alive get to grow up."
Is that supposed to be about Denia?
I honestly don't know. But that's her... always leaving you guessing.
Are you here to pick up the birthday cake? One moment please...
(Denia... She said she had to take care of something. But what, exactly? Does it have something to do with the Threnodian's frequency in the Dimmr Plains?)
(If the Spacetrek Collective finding Denia was part of the Grand Architect's plan, then what about removing that page from her? Or maybe...)
(If I were in Denia's shoes...)
"Easy. Today is my birthday. I won't be going anywhere."
You see the time shown by the Terminal: 00:15 a.m.
It's past Denia's birthday.
Here it is... I know it's a bit late, but I believe it's more than enough to convey your heart.
{PlayerName}, Denia has left the Academy and is heading towards the Dimmr Plains.
...How did she leave?
With her Forte. We've detected residual Voidmatter particles at the platform. Professor Arman was trapped inside a bubble. Luckily, no broken bones.
She hasn't removed her Resonance suppression device and tracker yet. Should we initiate the emergency protocol?
...No, give me her location.
Understood, coordinates sent... Good luck, {PlayerName}.
I thought you'd stop her.
I tried.
But with her condition now... she would die if I tried any harder.
That doesn't sound like you.
Trees will grow tall, and leaves will turn green, {PlayerName}...
That child simply made a grown-up decision.

For the final part of your deal with Denia, you go to Zahira to pick up a birthday cake. 
On the way, you receive an urgent call from I.R.I.S.—Denia has recovered some of her powers and escaped from Startorch Academy.
(Whatever her reason was for saving me and Hiyuki back then... she still carried out the Fractsidus's plan.)
(And the Grand Architect's next move is still unclear... Have to stay cautious.)
You can feel your eyelids sinking. In a haze, you seem to have returned to that familiar scene again.
Denia... Do you have any clues about that scene in your memory?
Nothing.
It was just a scene. Maybe from some movies I watched as a kid?
But maybe... in my opinion... you still have a chance to...
Now you're reminding me of what Nastasha once said.
Huh?
"Raise your head, what do you see?"
Lahai-Roi's night sky.
True enough. But my reply was "The void. The darkness."
What was her reaction?
She said it was actually light fighting against darkness.
"But it looks like darkness has the upper hand," I said.
But there was only darkness in Lahai-Roi at the beginning. Then came the light.
Haha, you answered exactly the same way as she did.
So light actually prevailed.
You're right, {PlayerName}.
I guess if you never give up, the story will one day have a good ending, no?

Sometimes you still think about Denia, and the times you sat together on that bench.
Will you see each other again?
Denia.
I just saw Sigrika. That was crazy, {PlayerName}. I didn't think you'd actually... you know, drive that thing off.
So... you're just gonna keep staring? Do you always come empty-handed when you visit patients?
(Looks like she's free of the Threnodian's influence now... but that way of talking...)
Are you aware of your condition right now?
Yeah. I'm dying, right?
That person gave me a gift a long time ago... Said when the time comes, I'd finally get a nice sleep.
A gift?
What is it exactly?
Who knows. But it's not hard to guess, is it? Just like a collar you put on cats and dogs, in case they get ideas.
Mm, no. "Cats and dogs" might be too generous. At least they can still bite. I'm probably closer to a lab mouse now.
So, {PlayerName}, did they send you to sweet-talk a lab mouse?
Denia, I'm here because I chose to be.
We've been on opposite sides before, but...
There you go, still all serious...
But I want to try trusting you.
Right... In that case, am I supposed to look more excited?
Too bad, {PlayerName}, I can't trust you in the same way.
You saw me at my worst there, and you're still playing this game... You want answers. That's why you're here.
I won't deny it.
You did save me once.
How honest. I don't hate that.
Hah... don't get the wrong idea... If you'd died back there, it would have been game over.
If you really want answers, how about we make a deal?
A deal?
Yes, a fair exchange. The Collective can't get what they want from me, but you just might get what you want.
What's your condition?
Maybe you could stay with me for my birthday? This weekend. I'd like to have a good stroll in the Academy again.
Your birthday is this weekend?
It could be, or not. Doesn't matter. What matters is... you are there.
I'm running out of time. Some things deserve a proper ending—with a good day.
(An ending... What is she planning to do? But in her current state...)
What, doesn't feel safe even if you're around? Then put another collar on me, or a bomb. What's one more, right?
...I'll see what I can do.
You mean that? But people at the Academy, do they know...
Spacetrek Collective never made your identity public. So for that day, you'll still be the Academy student Denia.
(Always the busybody.)
...Fine. Then it's a deal, right?
Relax. I'll cooperate with their research for the next few days. Just don't get your hopes up...
...The Grand Architect wouldn't be sloppy enough to leave me unhandled.
Anyway, no point worrying about it now. I'll see you this weekend, {PlayerName}.

You visit the infirmary at Arman's request to talk with Denia.
From Denia, you learn that her frequency decay was part of the Grand Architect's plan. She seems to have already accepted her fate.
Denia ultimately offers you a deal: spend her birthday with her, and in exchange, she will assist the Spacetrek Collective's research and provide you with intelligence regarding the Grand Architect.
...Don't overthink it. Let's go over there for a moment.
{PlayerName}. How did it go? Is she willing to cooperate?
You pass along Denia's request to Arman
A birthday... at the Academy?
...I see. That is an unexpected request.
But if that's the key to cooperation, the Collective will treat it as a special case.
She said she wants a "proper ending" for some things. But I don't know her true intent yet. We'd better be careful.
Noted. We'll initiate a full risk assessment immediately, and draft a comprehensive operational and contingency plan.
Thank you, {PlayerName}. Would you be available in the afternoons of this weekend? She asked for you specifically.
No problem.
I'll do my best.
Much appreciated. We'll ensure that all procedures and contingency measures are fully in place.
We really appreciate your support! I know this is a very personal request, but we'll keep everything under control. You can think of it as a special escort mission.
I'll send you the finalized plan before then. Let's stay in touch on WavesLine!
{PlayerName}... Something's still bothering you?
What do you know about the Grand Architect?
Do you miss life at the Academy?
Why did the Grand Architect leave you there?
Nothing.
I've never seen her true face. Wouldn't be surprised if the real one's already dead.
You care about that, do you? I'll tell you more once you've kept your side of the deal.
Miss my life at the Academy? What made you think that?
You keep staring out the window. That's where the dorms are.
...When you put it that way, maybe I do. The president once said that everyone ends up missing their school days when they grow up.
I guess that really was my golden age.
Trash gets dumped, you know... And those little tricks of mine? She probably noticed long ago.
Or maybe... she simply decided it was better if I died here.
Because you always try to save everyone, even someone like me... Heh. That kind of stubbornness must have gotten to her.
See you this weekend, {PlayerName}.
She's right, little one... You might still have a way out.

As the Moon-Chasing Festival approaches, you receive a call from Yangyang, Chixia, and Baizhi who invite you to join the celebration at Taoyuan Vale.

After catching up with the trio there, you share your recent experiences at Mount Firmament, while they fill you in on the tale of Moontree Lodge—where every wish made beneath its branches is said to come true. Chixia suspects that an unsung hero might be making these wishes happen and playfully suggests you try your luck under the Wishing Tree before you part ways.
On your way to the Wishing Tree, a peculiar red robot catches your eye.
You ask around and learn that this little robot might have some connection to the Moontree Lodge.

When you reach the Wishing Tree, you encounter the robot's owner, Xiangli Yao, Principal Investigator at the Huaxu Academy. Xiangli Yao explains that his robot, "Patty," is malfunctioning, and its nonsensical speech makes you realize that Xiangli Yao might just be the unsung hero Chixia mentioned. Xiangli asks you to keep that a secret. After learning you are there to make a wish, he suggests stopping by the Wishing Stall for a chat.

Xiangli Yao reveals that Patty has encountered some technical difficulties, likely due to four unreadable wishes, which he believes are causing the malfunction. Wanting to ensure everyone enjoys the festival, you offer to help Xiangli Yao resolve the issue.

The first wish is from a researcher, though you are unsure who they are. Xiang-LEE, a silver robot created by Xiangli, provides a reasonable analysis, helping you begin your search for the wisher's true desire. Just as you prepare to investigate, Xiangli Yao receives an emergency call—a prototype's core has gone out of control, and he must leave immediately, entrusting you and Xiang-LEE with the investigation.

Outside the Academy, Xiang-LEE analyzes the characteristics of the wisher, and they seem to match a young woman nearby. She introduces herself as Zhezhi, a painter, but it turns out she isn't the person you're looking for after all.

You overhear two researchers discussing something called "Nighttime Blues Syndrome" and decide to ask one of them, Shifan, about the wisher you are looking for. During your conversation, Xiang-LEE accidentally detects a connection between the wisher and the syndrome. As the robot processes the information, Shifan seems flustered for a moment and quickly bids you farewell.

Just then, a researcher named Jiuli, who had been eavesdropping, approaches and tells you that Shifan is indeed the wisher. Jiuli reveals that he and Shifan were once close friends, united by their passion for Echo research, but they've since grown distant. Jiuli is eager to understand what caused the rift between them and suggests you pique Shifan's interest by gathering Echo-related research data.
After collecting the necessary data, Xiang-LEE suddenly speaks in Xiangli Yao's voice. It turns out Xiangli Yao is remotely controlling Xiang-LEE to assist you in uncovering Shifan's true desire.

When you speak with Shifan again, he opens up about his true wish, confessing that he has been burdened with guilt ever since Jiuli was injured in a lab accident. At that moment, Jiuli appears, expressing his feelings. Though the two seem to argue, you can tell that their friendship is strong, and you are certain Shifan's wish will eventually come true.
The second wish involves a difficult choice. Following the same approach as with Shifan, you decide to track down the wisher, Ms. Heying, and hear her story.
During your conversation, Ms. Heying shares the promise she made to her late son, Xiuyuan. Wanting to ease her pain, you take her to Taoyuan Vale to experience the festival's joy.
While at the Moon Shooter Stall, you encounter some Midnight Rangers whom Xiuyuan once mentored. They speak fondly of Xiuyuan and his legacy, gradually helping to soothe Ms. Heying's grief.

With the second wish resolved, you hear two children, Li and Momo, arguing over something related to the Hero Plays. From their conversation, you discover that the third wisher, Mahn, is hiding in his secret base.

When you find Mahn, he is in awe of your past victory against the Tacet Discords and considers you the super Resonator from the Hero Plays. As you chat, you come to understand why he made his wish, and you decide to teach him what it truly means to be a hero. Naturally, the best way to do this is by finding a real-life hero to serve as his role model.

You return to the Wishing Stall and discuss potential candidates for Mahn's hero with Xiangli Yao. As you weigh the options, Xiangli Yao suggests that you are the best choice. To solidify this idea, Xiangli adjusts your Terminal to record your daily life, intending to use it as a reference for Mahn.

All I remember is being out at sea fishing not long ago.
But all I could hear was a song, drawing me in. It felt like my whole body was being beckoned to follow that tune.
The next thing I knew, I was drifting right out of Serene Bay, where the Tidebreaker is said to slumber.
The singing was still there, like it was rising from the depths. I swear I caught a glimpse of the Cetus's shadow... then another shadow of a massive fish.
Oh, the curves of that shadow. A true beauty...
I tossed everything I had into the sea, anything that could serve as bait, but still, it wouldn't bite.
Then, I felt a tug on the line as the singing grew louder... and everything went blank after that.
Did you catch this blue fish?
Yes! That's the one!
Wait, wait! Where is it...
Key! The key... Blast it, where'd that key go?
The key... I used it as bait...
Whoa, whoa! You're not—
Aha! I knew it! Molto bene! Got gobbled up by the fish!
Old Ahab had me keep it. You'll be needing it too, yes?
A key covered in rust. Seems like it's seen better days...
I can't recall much after that, but no doubt the Tidebreaker did make an appearance in Serene Bay.
If you're looking for it, go take a look around the bay. Oh, and thanks for the help...
Are you...
I'm forty-seven years old this year. After all these years at sea, I've caught more fish than you can imagine.
But the right fish and the right person have yet to cross my path.
Oh, but this beautiful lady here—
Ahem.
We should get going, Phoebe.
Farewell, Mr. Starbuck.
I wish you the best! May Imper... May the sea bring you blessings!
Uh, right... Okay then...
Starbuck reaches inside the blue fish and pulls out a key…

You and Phoebe finally manage to grab the fish from Starbuck, and the First Mate's sanity is restored. Starbuck claims he once saw Cetus the Tidebreaker at a place called Serene Bay, with a large fish swimming alongside it. He hands you the lighthouse key Captain Ahab entrusted in his care before you departed.
Let's light up the lighthouses on this island as Captain Ahab instructed.
After that, we should go visit that Serene Bay Mr. Starbuck talked about.
The Tidebreaker knocks over your boat, and you're washed ashore by the heavy waves...
Phoebe!
Get out of the way!
{PlayerName}! Are you hurt?
Still in one piece.
My fish...
The Tidebreaker attacked us! Thank Imperator none of us were hurt.
Quick, let's check if anything was lost!
You check your belongings...
You find a bizarre fish, its color all wrong, and its eyes glow with an unsettling shimmer.
Nothing's lost, except now we've got this...
What a strange fish...
How about we take it to Planck? Maybe it knows what this is.
The octopus Echo waves its tentacles around as it hands you a note from Ahab.
"Once it's safe, Planck can swim over to Serene Bay."
"Since the lighthouse on Starbuck's island is up and running, we can set sail again. We're counting on you and Miss White Hat."
"There'll be monsters swarming in those waters, ever since Cetus went missing."
"Word is, the key to Serene Bay's lighthouse got lost long ago. We only know it's somewhere at the bottom of the sea."
"I'll keep poking around and see what else I can dig up. I'll have Planck send word once I've got news."
"Oh, I reckon you'll be greeted by a few strange fish along the way."
There are rocks in the way.
{PlayerName}, we can clear it with Echo skills!
{PlayerName}! Look, it's the Tidebreaker!
They're heading towards that island to the west!
Their wounds seem to be healing, but I still feel the intense fury in their cries.
The Tidebreaker has indeed been wandering in Serene Bay. After the lighthouse was relit, the beast swam towards a small island covered in storm...
Are you the one looking for a ride to Riccioli?
That's me. Let's go.
Take a seat, and we'll be on our way!
I have other matters to attend to. Maybe later.
I'm gettin' old... Starbuck... old...
Let it take out the Albatross... This time I'll...
Ah, you're here.
That island Tidebreaker ran off to is also known as Reyes Ruins. They say it's filled with old mysteries.
The storm ragin' over it seems to keep folks from settin' foot there. Its own protection, if ye will.
But not to worry, I've already found a way to get past it.
If Starbuck isn't pullin' my leg, that storm and the siren are in cahoots. Which means...
Come on, let's move out! You and Miss White Hat will team up, and I'll be with Starbuck.
There's a wee island just east of the ruins. We'll meet there.
You see, Captain. What did I tell you?
It says here, "Riccioli, shower Neptunia with your light. The usurper slumbers in the depths of Reyes. Offer your love to Reyes' descendants and the eternal life of the sea."
What's all this nonsense?
Riccioli corresponds to Neptunia in Rinascitan astrology. In other words, the island is surrounded by the deepest waters in all of Rinascita.
Ho, ho. You know your astrology well, Miss White Hat.
I'm just stating what everyone in Rinascita knows. It's also mentioned in the legends of the Sentinel Imperator.
What about the second half?
I... I'm not sure.
"Offer your love..."
So it's asking us to fall in love with somethin'? That's just plain odd!
Bleh.
O great, noble descendants of Reyes, hear my words! I offer ye me love!
Umm... I shall offer ye my love! The ceaseless waves shall be my pledge of loyalty to you for all eternity!
Bah, I'm gettin' too old for this! What dunderheaded idea is this, anyway!
Go on, {Male=laddie;Female=missy}. You give it a go!
Me?
Aye, you. Just a few words, for the love of the sea! What, need a pen and paper, do ye?
O great, noble descendants of Reyes...
I offer you my sincere—
No, no, no! You're all doing it wrong!
What do you take love for? Is this a joke to you?
Step aside!
My love. You are the light of my life.
No storm can keep us apart, for in your presence, the might of my love can withstand any tempest, for it is even stronger!
My soul yearns to break free, for it has found its direction, yet I am tormented by my inability to reach you...
It's working! It's working!
Oh, my dearest love—
That's enough of that! Let's move out! We've got no time to dawdle!

As you find it impossible to pass through the storm looming over Reyes Islands, you head towards the nameless island Ahab mentioned. You attempt to dispel the storm following the inscription on the ancient steles, but to no avail. In the end, it's Starbuck's peculiar method of "offering his love" to the island that finally calms the storm.
Splendid! Now that we got rid of that storm, Planck can swim over here!
Can't say the same for Queequeg, though. The repaired Pequod is awaitin' her new captain before she can set sail.
Let's take a look around. Don't know much about the lighthouse here in Reyes, but I'll have that siren hangin' from the tip of me mast by day's end, ye mark me words.
You did well back there, {PlayerName}.
Not everyone can survive the weight of the sea. She's a merciful mistress, but she can be merciless, too.
Even in dreams, I see meself hurlin' sharp harpoons into the water. They must sink deep before they strike with true power and precision.
Though we are blessed by the sea, we stand ready to point our harpoons at it... and at that fella.
Strife, chaos... endless conflict. This is the fate of those who live with the tides.
How nice... Did you know? Some people die at the tide's ebb, some at low water...
Some at the full of the flood. And I'm just a billow that kisses the storm.
Go, Captain. Do what you must and whatever your heart desires.
Ugh. Hello...
Oh, actually, I should thank you.
If it weren't for you, I wouldn't have gotten this far.
Well... Captain Ahab has his own ambitions. So do I.
*Sign* My beloved. Wait for me, will you?
But then again, not too late is it, even now, to desist... Behold!
Ahab, you old fool! It seeks you not! It is you, you, that madly seeks him!
{PlayerName}, have you noticed that something doesn't feel right about Captain Ahab?
I can't say what it is for certain... But I just have a feeling that he's hiding something from us.
Why don't we split up the search?
If there's a connection between this island and Tidebreaker, I'm sure we'll find something, especially with all the scattered ruins.
I can decipher these ancient Rinascitan texts. We'll have the truth soon enough.
It says here that the key to the lighthouse among the ruins is sealed within the treasure of this island.
Perhaps it's over there?
"Present the trinity gifts of the sea, and thus the light shall burn eternally."
So this means... we need to find three "gifts" from the sea to break this seal?
Where the Reverberations converge. May they rest in peace.
The mysterious spirit seems to have enjoyed the fish and leaves feeling very much satisfied...
The mysterious spirit appears to have heard the callings of the sea and faded away...
The mysterious spirit gazes towards the last lighthouse, as if hoping it will shine once again...
We managed to get all four lighthouses lit again, {PlayerName}!
Do you hear the Tidebreaker's cries? They don't sound as sad, hurt, and angry as they did before.
Find anything, Phoebe?
The whale's cries do sound very emotional.
I've managed to decode inscriptions from a few stone tablets I found inside the ruins.
Cetus the Tidebreaker... is deeply connected to the Sentinel Imperator.
When the last lighthouse becomes operational once more, Cetus the Tidebreaker returns to its usual gentle self. Meanwhile, Phoebe has also made progress in her investigation of the island.
In legends
Cetus the Tidebreaker guides drowned ships and sailors
To the realm beyond
Yet they were fickle
When they sang in sorrow and fury
Tempests raged
Skies darkened
Until Imperator enlightened them with lantern light
Making them a ruler of marine life
And Guardian of the Sea
Some of these ancient stone tablets tell of tales from long before the Order ever existed.
Besides Cetus the Tidebreaker, I've also found information about the "siren" that might have enchanted Mr. Starbuck.
It's a Remnant Creature that dwells in the depths of Riccioli. It may even be the same kind as Lorelei, who we met in the Nimbus Sanctum.
With the Tidebreaker absent, the restless Reverberations of the departed likely accumulated in her body. Those lost souls were coaxing her to enchant the fishermen.
She and the Tidebreaker share a symbiotic relationship. However, she is still weak, not quite as fully formed as Lorelei.
I believe she was the one mending Tidebreaker's wounds...
We need to get her back to normal.
Time to put our experience in the Nimbus Sanctum to good use. I'm certain we can make it work.
It's just...
{PlayerName}, do you happen to speak the whale's language?
Maybe Abby can communicate with it.
I'd like to sit down and have a nice chat with Tidebreaker once this is all over.
But for now, let's make our way to find Captain Ahab.

After deciphering the ancient tablets, Phoebe believes the Tidebreaker is tasked to guide the lost souls to the realm beyond, and the "siren" invading these waters may be a creature similar in nature to Lorelei. With the information at hand, the two of you seek Captain Ahab's aid to deal with the "siren."
Damn you, you cold-blooded beast I've struggled so much to conquer...
I've gone old, and the curse you laid upon me ends today... But I will fight you till the very end.
I'll run you down, come hell or high water!
O waves, unleash your fury upon me! Increase your might to the storm that carries me to my coming doom!
Men of Pequod! Our promised rest is nigh!
The whirlpools that once claimed my life, and the tempest that once filled my sails, I now call upon you! And that beast as well!
Come! Let us sever these bonds that bind us as we dive into the abyss to embrace our fate!
{PlayerName}! You have returned!
Ishmael?
Where's Captain Ahab and the others?
I overheard that the Pequod was ready to sail, so I headed over to take a look.
But by the time I arrived, the beach was empty, and I only found Planck over there.
Well, if it isn't my First Mate, {PlayerName}?
Brant?!
This is quite the ship you've got here. Looks like it's seen better days though.
I pieced that ship together, plank by plank!
It seems you've grown a strong connection with it.
A few days ago, Ahab summoned me to take helm of this fine vessel…
So where is Captain Ahab?
To be honest, I haven't the slightest clue. By the way, where are you now?
Is that your Gondola that's sailing away into the waves?
Hello! Yoo-hoo!
I'm coming to see you, my love!
It's Starbuck!
The scoundrel's hightailing with the boat!
You there! Stop!
The might of my love can withstand any tempest, for it is ever stronger!
That's... He's heading straight into the storm! After him! The man's lost it!
This ship doesn't seem to require a full crew to operate. A captain will suffice.
All set and ready for sail?
Aye, aye, Captain Brant!
Not yet.
How did the lines tighten by themselves?
Make ready for cast off!
Over there!
My love!
Hahaha! Hold on tight!
Fight till the end, Pequod!
Let us venture into the abyss!
Run!
And I only am escaped alone...
{PlayerName}…
We're safe now.
Thank you, Cetus the Tidebreaker.
It appears that Pequod wasn't able to escape its fate after all...
Alas, my duty as acting captain has been fulfilled. Farewell, my friends!
The Tidebreaker...
Oh, hey, big guy! Nice to see you again!

I still remember when you flipped over our boat last time, you know. But considering you just saved us, I'll call it even! Hmph... Like the old Jinzhou saying, something like "Big folks let little things slide!"
It's obviously way bigger than you are.
The big guy says that "siren" helped care for its wounds, but then she went cuckoo after sucking in too many Reverberations.
That's why it didn't want to fight her earlier. After teaching her a lesson, maybe she'll know better.
Tidebreaker. I... I have something to ask you!
Have you fully recovered?
It says don't beat yourself up over it.
Sure we are! Nothing stands in our way when we tag team!
What if one day I manage...
To reel you in?
Uhh, what's up, big fella? Cat got your tongue?
Are they... laughing?
Whoa!!!
W-W-Where do you think you're goin'? Oh, I'm so catching that whale someday. Just you wait and see!
Of course it is! Look at it live and kicking. It's never been better.
You were tricked and deceived during the Carnevale... I know that an Acolyte like me is in no position to represent the Order...
But I still wish to offer you an apology, Cetus the Tidebreaker, even if it's only my own.
You've been following its trail all this time, helping fishermen and receiving gifts of the sea yourself. It's trying to protect that stuff, too.
Oh! It also wants me to tell you great job on catching that big fish earlier!
"Just be yourself, whether it's giving or receiving, belief or hope," it says.
I see. Thank you for telling me that!

As the storm subsides, you meet the Tidebreaker again after it carried you back from the depths of the sea. Phoebe wishes to express her apology to the beast for what happened during the Carnevale, but the Tidebreaker holds no grudge. Maybe one day in the future, as a pro angler, you might be able to reel the big guy in...
Hmm...
I wonder if you've noticed, {PlayerName}.
After you set the Tidebreaker and the sea right again, Captain Ahab, Mr. Starbuck, and Mr. Queequeg all disappeared...
I'm currently going over Captain Ahab's old journal, and it seems like they were searching for this "final harbor."
Captain Ahab spent his whole life on the waves. He was the finest captain and fisherman this place ever saw.
If we steer our course by Ahab's example, we might discover things, even treasures he left behind...
Can we catch Cetus the Tidebreaker?
It's a possibility. Captain Ahab always had an obsession with the Cetus, but why remains a mystery.
Well then, let's press on with this as our goal!
The sea feels ever so calm, and the whirlpools have finally settled.
Everything's returned to how it once was… To be honest, {PlayerName}, Captain Ahab and his crew met their fate at sea decades ago.
Their love of the sea and their promise to Cetus the Tidebreaker is what kept their spirits lingering here.
And now, the peaceful waters of Riccioli mark their final resting place. This is their "final harbor."
But the Rachel still sails on, and it seems to have taken a liking to you.
I believe that Captain Ahab also hoped you'd carry on his legacy...
What about you?
Me? I'm just a simple sailor and fisherman. I was born here, and I'll probably get married and have children here too. Eventually, I'll find my peace in these very waters.
So set sail, Captain {PlayerName}! Your journey leads to the very edge of the world.
Ship almost fixed up. Thank you. Only half to go.
Captain's orders. Almost working.
As long ship is repaired, will be fine. All will be fine.
By the way, that big "fish." Serene Bay.
We failed before. You be careful.
Ship getting better. Ahab lost his harpoon.
Ahab says, once ship is repaired, we can all go home.
Ahab is captain. He is right.
The ship is fixed. Thank you. It is time.
Pequod, needs a captain.
If Ahab not captain anymore, then... we still need a captain.
Pequod is ready, Ahab.
You can bring us all home, Ahab.
Go home. Home...
The once wreckage is starting look more like a ship now.
The ship repairs look almost complete.
Seeking out old Ahab, are you? He should be at the harbor over there.
He's no ordinary man, I tell you that. You'll spot him a mile away.
Zzz... Zzz...
Huh? Hmm... All right, cut it out...
Oh! Ahoy! A fish! We have a bite!
Well, don't just stand there, {Male=laddie;Female=missy}! Gimme a hand with this thing!
Oh, wait! Easy does it...
That's gotta be one hefty fish...
Too bad it got away...
A big fella like that? He won't be gettin' away from me, just a matter of time, no bother at all.
Oh, that? Pah, that was nothing. Back in me youth, I could hunt a whale for a whole day, I could!
You must be that young'un Ishmael mentioned.
Yes, I'm here to become a pro fisher.
Yes, I'm here to try deep sea fishing.
Aye, good! You've come to the right place. The name's Ahab, and I've been tied to this harbor longer than most.
That octopus merchant over there is Planck. It has all you need, from fishing gear to boat repairs.
But... I see you don't have a boat. We can fix that! You can use mine!
A Gondola?
The ones we use here for fishing are different from what you'll find in the city. We treat 'em like family—live and die together, we do.
She's called Rachel. Gettin' on in years, but she's still got some fire in her.
Since I retired, it's been a while since she and I crashed some waves. I reckon she misses the old fishing days as much as I do.
Well, now that we've shared a bit of fishing, I'd say we've forged a bond, eh?
What do you say we chase that big fella that gave us the slip? Let's head straight out to sea!
I'd like to see what kind of fish dares to run away from old Ahab!
Are you all right?
With Ishmael's guidance, you manage to find the old captain, Ahab, at the dock. Ahab gladly lets you borrow his old Gondola, and you can go fishing at sea with it.
Ahoy! That was some mighty fine sailing back there!
You picked it up quickly. Good, good！
Ah, don't forget to stop by the market when ye've got time to spare.
Minding the helm is only half the battle. You've got to know how to trade, too!
What's with all the ruckus over there?
I overheard that someone from the Order's here.
What? Are you certain? Are they here for the taxes?
My grandfather's still hiding that ribbon he picked up from that Acolyte we drove away...
Have you heard the news?
They say the Order's sending knights over soon!
No way. These rumors are getting more ridiculous by the minute!
Look, isn't that just a wee girl? What knights...
…Oi, the Order's got no authority here. Now, bugger off, will ya.
Come on, Mr. Coffin. Didn't she just help you fix your Echo...
Oh, pipe down, Coffin. The wee lassie was just asking you for some directions, for Imperator's sake.
Phoebe?
I'm sorry…
I'm only looking for Cetus the Tidebreaker. They were injured in Ragunna…
Cetus the Tidebreaker, you say? Well…
Hey, look. Isn't that the Resonator who showed up in Ragunna a while back? The Laureate…
The Order is not welcome around these parts! Yer hear me?
That's enough of that!
The Order's left us alone for years. If they really wanted to meddle in our affairs now, you think they'd just send one little girl?
We owe our trade to the blessings of Cetus the Tidebreaker and these very seas. Ye're tellin' me we can't accept a wee lass in an Acolyte hat?
Right then, that's enough of that. Business has been hard as it is lately. Break it up, folks.
If ye've got more complaints, toss 'em my way. Happy now? Off you go.
Thank you.
I'm here because I want to talk to the villagers about the Tidebreaker. No one has seen them since the Carnevale...
Friend of yours, {Male=laddie;Female=missy}?
Yeah, we go way back.
We're acquainted, yes.
All right, then. But know this—the Order's let these islands drift without a guide, so the folk around here aren't too keen on seeing someone wearin' that kind of hat wanderin' about.
My hat? Err...
Anyway, just say ye're here on personal business and ye'll be fine. Now, I hear ye're lookin' for Cetus the Tidebreaker. Well, lucky you, 'cause so am I.
Yes! The Tidebreaker showed unnatural signs during the Carnevale not long ago. I think I sensed their pain and anger...
Well, sail around in these waters and ye're bound to run into it, sooner or later. But if you want the simple way... See that lighthouse down yonder?
There are four of 'em across Riccioli Islands. As long as their lights are on, the Tidebreaker will answer our pleas as gently as ever.
Three of them went dark when the Tidebreaker vanished. Getting them lit again should do the trick.
You know what? Why don't you take Miss White Hat here on a wee boat ride, {PlayerName}?
A boat ride?
We're going fishing!
W-what? I've only ever read about Riccioli Islands' fishing trade in the Order's library before, but I've never actually fished on the sea...
How do you expect the sea to answer yer calls if you don't embrace it yerself?
Oh, and hold onto yer "hat" during the ride. If anything else comes up, just come find me.
What did he mean by that, {PlayerName}?
Just be yourself!
I see...
Then I'll help however I can with catching fish while we locate the Tidebreaker!
Hell if I know what she's playin' at!
Besides, do you really think she's helping you out for some devious reason? Being ungrateful isn't our way, is it?
But Ahab...

After you've recaptured the escaped fish, Ahab suggests you check out the market. To your surprise, Phoebe is there too. You find her in a sticky situation because of the locals' fraught history with the Order of the Deep. After You and Ahab help her out, Phoebe reveals she came here searching for Cetus the Tidebreaker. Ahab remarks that you'll run into the beast eventually just by going out fishing.
My leg... Where's my leg... Fetch me the harpoon...
...First Mate... Oil... Where's my oil...?
Ahoy. How did it go? Pull in a pretty big haul, did ye?
I'm gettin' closer to findin' the Tidebreaker meself. Just head over to the Helm Village and look for... What's his name again...?
Oh, right! Starbuck!
The man's lost a couple of his marbles these past few weeks. People say he only started actin' up after catchin' a glimpse of the Tidebreaker. Anyway, tell him I sent ye.
Also, notice that ship?
If you want to catch yourself a real prize, ye'll be needin' that one. She's still waitin' on repairs, but the watermen can fill ye in on that.
Ah, {PlayerName}? Ahab said of you.
Bring me wood.
What?
Wood. To fix ship.
Now not enough.
You bring material. Queequeg fix ship.
Rachel can't sail anymore. All has been lost to the sea...
The storm has subsided, and you finally make it to the last island...
The anchor's up, sails are hoisted, Pequod sets sail towards the center of the sea, and the eye of the storm...
You arrive near the Riccioli Islands on the fisherman's Gondola...
Enough staring. Come on, let's go.
What happened to her?
I heard her ranting about her {Male=brother;Female=sister}...
You're back. I've been keeping a close eye on her, just in case she gets any... wild ideas about hurting anyone.
Funny enough, she's been holding it together. It's like she really has been waiting on you.
Really? That's good to hear.
You're finally back! Now I won't ever go hungry again! You must be exhausted from that trip, I'll prepare something for you to eat!
Dana takes the fish and quietly begins to skin it with her bare hands.
She's starting to lose her grip again. But now that you're back, no offense, but I'll be taking my leave... Good luck.
Hold on, do you know any of the people she talked about?
Those fancy Mister and Madam types? Ha! You think I know any toffee-nosed snobs like that? You might try asking Ahab, he knows just about everyone!
Got it. Thank you.
Dana serves up a plate piled high with messy fish pieces. She gazes at you like she's serving a feast.
How about we go to Madam Claire's first, Dana?
Oh, she wants to see us? Well, what are we waiting for? Let's go!
Oh, dear Madam Claire. Where could you be?
Do you... not wish to see me?
Ah... Madam Claire went out fishing, Dana.
Oh... How could this be?!
Wait. Is this a note from Madam Claire?
"The folk from the city grow stranger by the day..."
"Why don't you craft a few specimens to sell, Ronald? It could be a profitable venture."
So you've been to see Uncle Ronald, haven't you? Madam Claire. I'm coming for you!
Here, {Male=brother;Female=sister}! I finally caught it! Look how pretty it is!
Best keep your distance, friend. There's something off about her. Best not to get too close.
It's a strange one. She seemed fine when I offered her some food not long ago...
Who is she?
What happened to her?
Haven't the slightest clue. Doesn't seem to be from the Riccioli Islands the way she's dressed. Maybe the promise of adventure drew her from the city.
Something must've shaken her up. She seems all scrambled in the head.
Doesn't seem to be from the Riccioli Islands the way she's dressed. Maybe the promise of adventure drew her from the city.
Unusual fish seem to flock to these waters. City folk love coming here in hope of adding another rare trophy to their exotic collections.

These unknown waters are perilous. Those who lack respect for them are sure to invite misfortune. Every day, fools set out, never to return, yet still, the lure of adventure continues to draw in newcomers.
I overheard someone say that she and her {Male=brother;Female=sister} arrived asking about fishing some time ago.
I wonder why it's just her now...
I can't convince her to leave, and I have no idea who her family might be. Perhaps you could try talking to her again.
I can't wait to see the look on their faces once I bring this pretty little fish back, {Male=brother;Female=sister}.
Dana extends her scarred arms, revealing the broken pieces of a wine bottle she was holding.
Huh? {Male=Brother;Female=Sister}, you're hurt.
Oh, marvelous! Do you remember Uncle Ronald spoke of peculiar fish here that are drawn to people's wounds?
Hurry, we need to head out to sea. We must catch one, even if it costs us our lives! Imagine showing it to everyone in the city!
Do you promise to return to the city after we catch this fish?
Absolutely! I shall be the first to present this fish, and then no one will ever be able to deny that I am truly the greatest collector there is!
What does it look like?
You don't remember? I'll make a sketch for you.
Okay, got it. I'll find it.
The wind is too strong! We're taking on water, {Male=brother;Female=sister}. I need your help!
Dana stamps her feet impatiently, her empty hands seeming to tug at something invisible.
I found the fish you're looking for.
A new fish! A fish no one's ever laid eyes on! Oh, don't you dare die on me now. I won't let you rot away...
Uncle Ronald. I have to find Uncle Ronald, he's the finest taxidermist I know. He'll preserve your beauty forever.
Dana skips away happily with the fish clutched in her hands.
My fish, Uncle Ronald, you promised me you would help me. Where's my fish?!
W-Who in tarnation are you?! Get away from me!
It hurts... My face hurts... Please don't bite my face... Save me, {Male=brother;Female=sister}. {Male=Brother;Female=Sister}?
Dana? What are you still doing on the island?
My fish. The fish you gave me. I can't find it...
You notice the fish you caught for Dana dangling from her waist, exuding a foul, rotten stench.
I'm so sorry! Please don't be angry with me! I'll find your favorite fish and make it up to you!
My favorite fish?
Dana quickly scribbles a drawing of a fish.
This one! You told me it was your favorite fish when we were children! It still is, right? Please tell me I didn't get it wrong.
You don't need to go look for it. I already have it.
