It rises from the primal, churning endlessly, echoing in our ears without end. I believe the melodies left by the Poets Society were witnessed by the wind, and it will carry them to us.
Ciaccona plays her instrument. The wind stirs, and the melody of the Poets Society fills the air.
Rimbaud and Selena must have returned to Ragunna by now. That lithograph of the Sentinel's true form… it has to be here somewhere.
Did that gentleman guide us intentionally? Who exactly was he...
Backpack stuffed with papers, claiming to be a common artist traveling in search of inspiration.
Yet he spoke like a nobleman... But I can't afford to think about that now.
If not for his help, we'd still be singing praises to a false Sentinel!
He's right. We cannot continue to sing for the Order anymore.
We must enlighten the people of Ragunna. They deserve to know the truth.
The knights of the Order defend only the Order's interests, and so... the time has come for us to become knights for the people of Ragunna.
What are you doing?
Playing a tune, of course. I want to capture the mood they must have felt when they were here... I'm curious as to what they left behind.

You find something that carries the melody—the wind. The wind is everlasting, recording and bringing back the Poets Society's melodies. Adopting the Poets Society's mindset, Ciaccona plays the melody once more, and the Society members' voices ring again.
Is this form of the Sentinel the same as the one you saw at Avinoleum, {PlayerName}?
The majestic steed carved on the lithograph looks the same as the Sentinel you saw before.
Like twins.
So the poets were indeed banished for uncovering the Order's secrets.
Even under interrogation, they held their silence. It wasn't until they met this mysterious man and learned the truth that they chose to become "Knights of Ragunna."
Resentment and curses are not songs of their own style. As for the true mastermind, we still have no direct proof linking him to the Order.
We must confront his lies and put an end to these Daemon incidents...
But once the truth of the Golden Anthem and Imperator is revealed, it will no longer be just a matter of Daemons... But... is now the right time?
The will of the people is strong. This mastermind is so sure that the lies about the Sentinel will go undiscovered, and that no one will easily believe the truth.
The truth exists to be uncovered. All we need is to plant the seeds of doubt in the people's hearts and let them take root and grow.
Yes... Let's get going then.
We'll go back to Margherita's. It's where our story began... and it's where it must end.

The members hid a lithograph here. They were actually guided by a mysterious figure, but there's no time to investigate who they are now. What's most important is returning to the restaurant to change the public's view of the "Golden Anthem."
In her world, poetry and music hold equal sway... Shh, listen carefully...
Follow the song to find her!
Ms. Margherita!
Well, hello, hello! If it isn't {PlayerName} and Ciaccona!
The two of you already know each other?
Oh, Miss Ciaccona is a regular around here, you know. I've even asked her to perform a few times. Helps bring in the crowds!
Actually, I've come to ask a favor of you today, Ms. Margherita. I'm sure you've heard the rumors circulating lately...
About the Poets Society's legacy. There's something important we'd like to share. Could you help us gather everyone?
Not a problem at all! Did you make any big discoveries? I'm so curious about what actually happened. It's driving me nuts!
Margherita agrees to your request and begins to gather an impressive crowd...
You and Ciaccona take your place on an impromptu "stage," the curtain poised to rise.
{PlayerName}, we'll begin when you're ready.
Let's do it. I believe in you.
Laureate, is this all real? What do you mean by the truth? Did you discover something?
The poets of the Golden Anthem, they...
A fascinating story indeed! You've certainly piqued everyone's curiosity.
Exactly. Someone used the story of the Golden Anthem to stir the public's curiosity. This is what created the Daemons.
If memory serves, official records of the Order of the Deep state the poets were charged with blasphemy against the Sentinel.
Surely you're not suggesting this was all the Order's doing? I dare say... such remarks would be considered a grave crime punishable by banishment.
Are you from a noble family? The city's elite have a habit of siding with the Order.
Haha, I'm afraid you misunderstand... I admit I do get that question quite often. I am but a traveling playwright.
Your presentation brings me back to a play I wrote in my youth.
A group of birds locked inside a cage. Convinced they will never fly, they do nothing but stand on a perch.
Then one day, the cage door opened. The young birds flapped their fragile wings attempting to fly, but plummeted to the ground one by one.
Many consider their fate a tragic one. What say you?
...I see it differently.
Even if they met their end falling into the abyss, they still had a chance to glimpse the sky and spread their wings.
And what of those who chose to remain in the cage, having witnessed their predecessors fall to their demise?
Will they still dare to reach for the skies after realizing the cost of choosing to fly? Does the "truth" exist to protect, or to harm? That is the question.
Miss Poet... I look forward to tomorrow's arrival.
This speech you made just now... You're implying the poets of the Golden Anthem were framed and their works deliberately misinterpreted?

As you finish your interpretation, the crowd in the restaurant grows restless, many surrounding you with questions. While you and Ciaccona are separated in the crowd, and Cristoforo appears next to Ciaccona, telling a story about a caged bird, as if hinting at something deeper.
A splendid retaliation. I witnessed all of your performance!
Like everyone present, I too eagerly anticipate tomorrow's arrival.
How's everything on your end?
As expected, the Order's fingerprints are all over it. According to our inside sources...
It was none other than Acolytes from the Order who salvaged the poets' lost works from the wreckage. They've long known of their existence and hid the poems in the Order's library.
It's possible this was a sham all along. Choosing to make it public now likely means they're using those poems to obscure the real truth.
Now, considering the fact that the untraceable article first began circulating among poets, musicians, and playwrights alike...
I think it's fair to say its author is a regular of such secret circles. He may even be the Resonator we've speculated about.
His collusion with the Order is why these rumors are allowed to run rampant in the streets.
I'll have someone follow this secret circle's trail and see what we can find.
Splendid work.
We should also share these findings with Ciaccona. As a poet, her insights would be much appreciated.
That's strange, she was just there a moment ago.
...Just like when we were children. Gone without a trace.
When she and her family disappeared without even a goodbye.

Carlotta greets you and shares that, through tracking the article's origin, she has uncovered some new leads. Just as you are about to share everything with Ciaccona, she disappears without a word. Carlotta sighs that Ciaccona has never changed since childhood, always vanishing without a word.
Ms. Ciaccona... Hmm, she was squirreling off towards the harbor earlier. I thought that's where you were meeting, so I didn't say a word.
She did look quite down, though. Never seen her wear such a gloomy face before.
Thank you for letting us know, Ms. Margherita.
Ms. Margherita, have you seen Ciaccona?
Why don't we split up and look for her at the harbor?
You search around but find no sign of Ciaccona.
The young birds left their cage, flapping frail wings as they fell to the ground.
I never thought his words would reach into the depths I sealed away so long ago.
You intend to reveal the truth of the Sentinel to the public. But that revelation... it comes with a price. One you've paid before, as a child. Remember?
And here I thought you'd be much wiser than this.
You know the dangers of pilgrimage, yet you all still cling to the same reckless path. Tell me, what drives such stubbornness?
The truth has its thorns, and the Golden Anthem has already paid its price. Do you wish to relive their fate?
Is that what you're trying to tell me with your play...? But you know nothing of how the Golden Anthem responded.
Allow me to share the answer, Sir Acolyte. Do you remember the very first voice from the heavens? The one the people of Rinascita kept alive in their hearts as they built their homes on this land?
Surely you've seen <te href=800009>The Golden Bough</te>, yes? A play where people from various clans wear masks, singing and celebrating together. An occasion you now call... "Carnevale."
And? What of it?
It is words and songs. We are not your enemies. What you face here is something that is hard to describe, something I call "Reverberation."
It exists forever, and you can never defeat it.
Hmph. You pitiful fool. Off to the seas with that "Reverberation" you believe in so dearly.
The Order of the Deep seeks to banish us to the seas because they know they can't banish the truth...
Hear that? The bell they tolled... I will be the one to carry its sound forward.
Oh, the parallels... so striking. Just like the day the Poets Society boarded their Sail. You, Ciaccona Toccata, blaspheming against the Sentinel.
Ha! So this is the resonance they babbled on about? After all these years, another group of fools is ready to march down the same path.
Why are there always those who believe the Sentinel is some damn horse?
Is that so, Sir Acolyte? I do hope you dream of this "Sentinel" of yours every night then.
Spare me your sarcasm, you insolent bard! You're nothing but a mouthy relic, the last of what remains of your wretched family! Do you not repent for your crimes?!
Ah, so you've already tasted their fate, haven't you? You and your family, banished in the name of... blasphemy!
Such a dramatic turn of events! As cantors of the Sentinel, both the Toccata family and the Poets Society committed the same crime. Tell me, what is the connection between you and those poets?
You're nothing but a figment of my imagination. None of this concerns you. It was a price we were willing to pay. We have no regrets.
When I was a child, I lacked the ability to prove the Sentinel's true form. But now, with the Inverted Tower shifting and the prophesied Laureate among us...
I believe the opportunity has presented itself for the truth to be—
Opportunity. Indeed... The moment of choice dawns once more.
Do you intend to repeat history? This time, dragging {PlayerName} along with you? Boarding the Pilgrim's Sail and clinging to hope as the storm carries you away.
You've unraveled the hand behind it all... but the Order will never allow such truths to see the light.
{PlayerName}, Ms. Carlotta, and all those you've gathered along the way will be forced to bear the consequences of your quest for the truth.
And perhaps even that... "Blessed Maiden" whose whereabouts remain a mystery to this day.
Even so, will you two still insist on stepping onto that stage tomorrow?
Have you really made your choice? I look forward to the arrival of tomorrow, Miss Poet.
Is this Ciaccona's sheet music? She was here.
The vision I just saw seems to have been recorded from this...
Ciaccona mentioned she always writes down her melodies on manuscript paper. Could this be...?
Wait. The title of this section...
The Golden Anthem...
Earlier before, Ciaccona walked to the harbor...
Coming here implies you worry about tomorrow's outcome.
This is... the past.
The poets were at least clever enough to hold their tongues. But you have the nerve to parade your blasphemy through the streets. It almost makes those poets look noble by comparison.
Isn't this what you're afraid of?

Cristoforo's words echo in Ciaccona's mind. As she walks toward the harbor, memories of the Poets Society and her own past resurface. She now understands what Cristoforo meant—if the truth is revealed, the past tragedies may be doomed to repeat themselves.
This song... it's the one she performed last time.
The melody is the same, but why does it sound so sad this time?
So Miss Poet. Have you made your decision?
I know what you're thinking. You're worried I might end up on the same path you did.
Go on.
Follow your heart. I'll be with you till the end.
This... is a poem I've never seen before. It's so different from what they used to write.
"Do not place flowers on my tomb, for I do not rest beneath the stone."
"I am the sea wind at Ragunna's walls. I am a dawn that breaks through thorns."
"I am a night hawk of wings aflame, soaring towards the Celestial Steed, whose praises I sing and whose true form I behold."
A penniless bard and the Laureate roving in a foreign land. Together, we rise up against the Order of the Deep itself...
But as long as the seeds of doubt are planted, the kindling in Ragunna will eventually ignite to forge its true gold.
There. Now how's that for a story worth telling?
Just like a knight's tale!
Ah! Speaking of which... Have you ever read that novel? It's about a knight on a quest to challenge a giant in the name of justice.
The knight is also accompanied by a squire. Time after time, they throw themselves at the seemingly invincible giant!
I am no Montelli, Acolyte of the Order of the Deep, or Knight of Ragunna...
But still, I shall lead the charge! Ya-hoo! Mount up, Sir Knight! To battle we go!
As the forgotten songs rise once more, a tale of the past I shall tell...
This is the story of those who were accused of blasphemy.
They were once poets, singing songs for the Divinity and the Order. This is how their music became known to all.
Until one day, they stumbled upon a "truth" that could not be proven.
The Sentinel, whom we've always revered, is not what They seem.
The true Divinity granting us blessings is a majestic Celestial Steed that gallops across the high seas and soars through the skies.
And the teachings in our scriptures? Lies. Lies told to us by the Order.
Ask yourselves this. Why would Imperator, who once sent Rinascita voices from the heavens, allow Their people to suffer aboard those Pilgrim's Sails?
How could poets who once sang the praises of the Sentinel come to curse and resent Rinascita, a land they loved so much?
People of Rinascita!
Have you ever wondered why the Order forbids us from seeing their earliest scriptures?
Imperator and Ragunna have always stood united, yet lately... they seem to have vanished from our dreams. Why is that?
Ciaccona Toccata, in the name of Imperator and Primus Fenrico, you are hereby under arrest. You will face the full weight of the law at the Order Penitentiary.
Is that so? And what are the charges this time, if I may ask?
Blasphemy!
Oh? The same old tricks again. Is this how the Order intends to keep the truth hidden?
Hmph. Save your empty words for your confession to the Sentinel.
Farewell, Sir Acolyte. Oh, and just a little tip for you. Keep your eyes on the audience below.
Let's see how much of the Order's hypocrisy these "empty words" can unveil...
Why did none of the Fools that boarded the Pilgrim's Sail ever thank the Sentinel?
The Acolytes are making their move.
Damnation! She's not working alone!
I have faith the music of the Golden Anthem will one day echo across Ragunna's skies again!

Ciaccona joins you in returning to Ragunna City, where, as planned, you will make your final revelation. However, your actions have drawn the attention of the Order, and the Acolytes are closing in on you.
{PlayerName}, Carlotta, it's been too long!
You really must adore that song. I remember hearing you sing it when I was little.
You knew each other as children?
When I was a child, whenever I passed by Ciaccona's house, I'd always hear music drifting from the courtyard. Lively, spirited and so full of emotion...
Oh, I remember it well! Those two guards of yours were like giants from Septimont, easily two hundred pounds of pure muscle!
Back then Ciaccona's family conducted the Order's choir.
Then why is Ciaccona a wandering bard?
How should I put it... Well, as they say, families are always rising and falling.
But a song is a song whether sung in a grand hall or beneath the open sky. As for family matters... let the past stay where it belongs.
Anyway, the two of you came in such a hurry. I suppose you're not here to take in the music.
Oh so... So you eavesdropped on a man rambling on in C3-sharp, and then poof, out pops a "monster"?
You're missing the point!
How sharp is C3-sharp?
It is the point! I need to know what kind of music could possibly have the power to conjure up those "monsters" of yours.
Let me see... it should sound something like this! About that sharp, {PlayerName}.
Yup, and just as grating.
I know right? We should suggest to Ms. Margherita that she add new signage: "Sing with civility, it starts with us!"
Ahem, can we discuss restaurant etiquette later?
Of course. But I still need to know what kind of music could possibly have the power to conjure up those "monsters" of yours.
The Golden Anthem... that name should never be spoken.
They're criminals. To conspire with them is to risk banishment at sea, or worse.
That's okay.
The Order of the Deep can't harm us one bit.
Don't worry. This won't be the first time we've crossed paths with the Order.
...Fine.
From what you've told me, the composers of this poem cursed Rinascita spelling the fall of Ragunna.
When the poem is played some type of horror appears. If I understand correctly, that's what attacked you and Carlotta.
If you ask me this story is a right load of codswallop. I don't believe a simple little poem could curse Rinascita.
Then you...
We need to get to the heart of this poem and music mystery. Let me join you. I can't resist a good adventure.
I'll help you find the link between the music and those Daemons. But in return, I want you to hand these pages to me for safekeeping.
It's just a few sheets of paper.
Sure, no problem.
Then we have a deal!
Since you believe this music summons them, how about we test it for ourselves? I've already memorized the sheet music.
It's risky, but there's no surer way to find out, wouldn't you agree, {PlayerName}?
Seeing is believing.
I'm well prepared.
I'm ready to fight.
The final work of poets banished to distant seas and condemned to death...
What, I wonder, did the verses forged in flames truly sing of?
Carlotta then leads you to Ciaccona, who seems hesitant to involve you in the mystery. After some persuasion, she agrees to help. To uncover the truth, Ciaccona decides to play the melody once more.
This room...
Is our final stage.
"You will witness a different world."
You arrogant hypocrits!
Led by curiosity and wonder, you step forward.
I am the gentle sea breeze,
Well, have you decided on your answer?
Perhaps our fates are not so different after all.
It is time, sinner against the Sentinel!
But you...
I will continue to sing.
As long as there are those who breathe and see.
My eternal summer will never fade.
Now, it's your turn to step onto it.
Sweeping through Whisperwind Haven and towards Ragunna's high walls.
I look forward to the public trial.
My Lord Primus, it seems your plan has not gone quite as you'd hoped.
You sought to revive the blasphemous Poets Society, spreading their legacy to stoke the fires of prejudice. And through my aid, summon Daemons to sow fear across Ragunna City...
I care not for labels of good or evil. My only care is Ragunna's order and chaos.
Fear... is but one tool among many to maintain stability.
Ah! Truly the words of one in possession of great power! Such lines are rare even in plays.
And yet... why do you seem so restless, Lord Fenrico? This is hardly the character I expected from you.
Is it that foreign Laureate that unsettles you so? Or perhaps that insignificant Toccata girl?
Or is it... something else you seek?
Out of respect for our partnership, some things are better left unsaid.
Of course. As you will, Lord Fenrico.
Wait... You were the one who led the Poets Society to that lithograph, weren't you?
I've heard whispers of your presence at Whisperwind Haven around that time. Whenever you were asked, you claimed to be seeking inspiration.
Why are you doing this?
As you've said yourself, out of respect for our partnership, some things... are better left unsaid.
There was no deception. Indeed, I was seeking inspiration. In the end... I found a story about birds in a cage.
The birds, having uncovered the truth, must decide—will they choose to fly into the unknown, or remain caged within the familiar?
Ah, Lord Fenrico, a word of reminder...
Just as the young Toccata mentioned, how long has it been since you last dreamed of your true "Divinity"?
Armed with a wooden spear and a broken helmet, the knight charged at the windmill...
His squire, ever loyal, trailed close behind as if becoming one with the knight. Together they charged again and again, true knights in spirit, ignoring the countless wounds they bore.
Truly astonishing... Even if you took such a script, what could you possibly accomplish, "Hecate"?
At the Cathedral of Mercury, Cristoforo reveals Fenrico's plan. In the confrontation, Fenrico suspect that Crisroforo was the one who secretly guided the Poets Society all those years ago.
Phew...
A masked hero suddenly appeared, rescuing the bard right when she was about to be apprehended by the Order.
But that's a story for another time.
You know what this means for you, right?
Even with a mask on, people will still recognize the Laureate.
I told you I'd stand by your side.
I'm now a wanted criminal by the Order.
So I guess that makes us... partners in crime?
Hahaha...
Now this is what a real poet... No, wait, a real knight is supposed to be!
Well then...
After escaping the city, Ciaccona is still filled with excitement for finally revealing the truth. You stop for a moment, and in her emotional state, she plays a song for you.
"Like the fire that dragged them to hell, these Daemons will spread throughout the land and burn all of Ragunna."
Is that really going to happen?
Unverifiable, yes, but not entirely dismissible. That said, a peculiar entity did indeed manifest, and it attacked you.
So, let's start at the very beginning. I have a friend who's an expert in deciphering music. I believe you've met her before...
She who resembles Topaz should still be near Whisperwind Haven at this hour.
They are... just like the ones that attacked us in the restaurant.
Let's pick up where we left off. What stories lie within these melodies?
Do you feel it? The breeze from Whisperwind Haven. You can even catch the faint scent of wet grass.
Next thing you know, maybe an apple will fall on our heads. Or maybe a big gray wolf will leap out and chase a squirrel down a rabbit hole...
Thank you, {PlayerName}.
I don't have the Blessed Maiden's miracles, nor the powers of a hero. I'm just a wandering bard.
The only thing I can offer is to immortalize this moment. I will carry all the stories about you with me...
By the way, I met a man at Margherita's who claims to be a playwright. You should watch out for him!
A playwright?
I've met a playwright before as well...
I'm not entirely sure who he really is... But my guess is that he might be the Resonator who's been working with the Order.
I'll keep that in mind.
Here, you can have this music sheet! I'm heading off on a new mission!
What kind of mission?
An escape mission! Starting today, I'm no longer just a wandering bard. I've got the Order hunting me now! A journey like this? It's begging to be written into a story.
Then I...
Don't you worry! I still remember our promise.
About the song I wrote you... We will meet again, and I'll sing it for you, I swear!
After all, we're partners in crime now!

Once the performance is over, Ciaccona warns you to watch out for a playwright in the city. Being wanted as a criminal, she will soon need to run again. This is your farewell, though not the last time you will meet.
Careful!
They burned in despair, resentful of the Order's verdict till their last breath. Their last work is nothing but a curse upon us all!
"With our bodies to fuel the fire, the ensuing inferno shall forge Ragunna's true gold." Is it saying Ragunna will burn to the ground??
They wanted their resentment to echo through the streets... Just by reading this, I can almost see their terrifying faces in the fire!
These voices... they're people of Ragunna, aren't they? I think I heard Mr. C3-sharp in the mix.
If the poets' resentful souls gave birth to Daemons, then shouldn't they sound like the poets themselves?
Those voices were just people who read or heard their work...
Perhaps the voices themselves are what causes the Daemons to manifest.
In the legends, Daemons are born of death and curses.
But what we've seen isn't like that, no. They're more like horrors created from peoples' words and imagination.
Of course, I'm just speculating. The voices were somewhat muddled. Perhaps I can refine the melody. This time we need to listen harder.
Let's find out what the true story really is...
The Daemons reappear. After defeating them, Ciaccona draws closer, hoping to use her Forte to uncover the story hidden in the frequencies.
It seems someone told the poets the truth about the Sentinel, and even suggested they stop singing solely for Divinity and begin singing for the common folk as well.
On the surface, what our "mystery man" said makes perfect sense. He even has knowledge of Imperator's true form.
And this hidden lithograph is evidence the poets were telling the truth...
Music and poetry are born from kindness and hope... yet now they've been twisted to create these monstrosities...
Whoever is behind this won't just sit back and watch.
...The thought of confronting them is already inspiring me to write a ballad! What should I call it? Which instruments would fit...
Our enemy hides in the dark, while we remain in the light. If that's the case...
We need to split up. With your tenacity and Ciaccona's expertise, we will uncover the truth.
And Opal?
Someone has pointed a gun at Cat's Eye. Someone ought to pull back the curtain and expose them.
The family has its ways. Tracing the article's source and finding this mastermind won't be a problem.
So, where do we start?
Where should we begin our investigation?
If we find the <te href=800012>Melody</te> connected to the Poets Society, I can bring the past into clearer focus...
I've got it, {PlayerName}. I know a place where they've definitely left their mark.
Let's go! Onward, to new melodies!
What is this place?
Ta-da! Welcome to <te href=800010>Requiem Paradise</te>!
This is where Ragunna's musicians lay their old instruments to rest.
For the people of Ragunna, the sea is everything. We live and sleep by the sea, and our souls drift out to sea when we pass.
Since an instrument is an extension of the musician, it's only fitting that it's buried by the sea. May its dreams be long and sweet before returning to the waves.
I'm certain this is where the poets of the Golden Anthem laid their instruments to rest before their banishment.
What's wrong? You seem troubled.
Have you found any leads?
Is that what's been on your mind this whole time? I say, if the answers aren't coming, let it all go and clear your mind.
To be honest... I haven't found any leads either. But worry not, this is what we bards call a "bottleneck."
Once, I spent three days just trying to find the right words to describe a tree... couldn't do it. Not one word.
So I stood under that tree and prayed for an apple to fall on my head.
You know, just like in those stories where inspiration strikes after an apple hits you. And, well... at least you'd get a snack out of it.
So did an apple hit you?
So did inspiration find you?
Sadly, the apples weren't ripe and none fell. No free nibbles for me, unfortunately.
The apples never fell. I stood under that tree until I couldn't any longer, but still no inspiration came.
Try it!
It's a real apple...
Later, when I finally decided to leave, I looked up through the gaps in the branches and suddenly saw a blooming flower atop a cliff.
Turns out, even without an apple, inspiration may yet strike. But if I hadn't stood there, I might've missed that unexpected burst of beauty.
So… maybe this is enough. Let's put aside heavy thoughts and continue our walk with a clear mind.
I'm starting to understand why Carlotta calls you <ano=Sunlit>"Topaz"</ano>.
Is that so? But I'm nowhere near as dazzling as the sun. If anything, I'd rather be like Icarus in the story.
Soaring freely in the sky, even if it means... falling in the end.
To learn more, you need more melodies. Ciaccona takes you to a moonlit shore, a place where Ragunna's poets and musicians are known to bury their instruments. There, you might find new clues.
I sense the melody of an instrument close by. Let's search for it.
Listen, I hear something up ahead...
It seems like... an interrogation room. This melody carries the weight of the Poets Society interrogation. Let's keep moving.
Take care with each step, {PlayerName}. The melodies left by these instruments are extremely fragile. The realm we're about to enter will appear fragmented.
Faroll of the Golden Anthem. Know that Imperator is stern, yet merciful.
The Codex teaches us, "Those whose sins are cleansed by the sea shall remain blessed by the sea."
It is a grave offense to slander the Sentinel. This includes your claim that "the Sentinel's true form is a steed of the skies."
I was told you found this lie carved on a lithograph. "In the face of the tempest, a giant Celestial Steed carved a path for the ark." How absurd.
If you admit you were mistaken at tomorrow's trial and reveal where you have hidden the evidence, I will move mountains to protect you and your companions.
Remember, Imperator only responds to repentance, not silence.
I'm sorry, Sir Acolyte. I'm doing my best to cooperate. Please don't mistake my silence for defiance. It's just... this room is freezing, and I've caught a chill. Makes it hard to talk.
I'm afraid that by the time I see the Sentinel, I will have lost my voice entirely. Perhaps then, They will judge you for silencing a poor transgressor's confession.
As long as you repent and help us destroy those blasphemous poems and songs, the Sentinel shall show mercy.
You are a wise man. I trust you will make the right choice. I look forward to seeing you tomorrow. Good night, Mr. Faroll.
I will always be here should you wish to receive the Sentinel's mercy.
No need to worry, Sir Acolyte. In fact, I'm beginning to enjoy the cold.

In the Realm of Melodies, you witness the Poets Society facing interrogation by the Order. Despite the pressure, Faroll, a member of the Society, does not resist, but calmly accepts whatever comes his way.
Where is this place? A study? Ciaccona are we... Ciaccona?
We must have gotten separated. Ciaccona did say even a slight misstep could draw us into other melodies. Am I...
..."You are to build a home here, like seabirds. Dwell upon the water, just as countless stars dot the night sky."
