A cave, you say? Tacet Discords love hanging out in places like that. Let’s hurry and check it out!
This place is huge! How on earth are we going to find her? Ugh, it's so frustrating!
Should we split up?
Do we have any other leads?
Easy there, young one. There’s a clue that could help us locate Linghan swiftly.
Now that you mention it, something just jogged my memory. It might help us locate Linghan swiftly.
If my memory serves me right, she should be gathering the Echo of Flautist. Given her health, she wouldn’t venture to Tacet Fields, so she must be exploring the wild for scattered Tacet Discords.
In our day, we relied on experience to locate Tacet Discords, but I’ve heard there are more advanced technologies available now.
Yep! The gourd just got upgraded with a search function. Let’s see if we can use it to spot any nearby Tacet Discords.
Let me try...
How to use it?

Don’t worry, {PlayerName}, it’s pretty straightforward. Normally, I’d give you time to figure it out yourself, but with Grandma Linghan missing, we can’t afford to waste any. Let me walk you through it.
You got it! I’ll be your guide through this.
Whoa, this new tech is amazing! We found her in no time flat.
Let’s not dawdle. Hang tight, Linghan! We’re on our way!
This place is seriously dangerous. Grandma Linghan isn’t in a good health condition. Why would she come here...
She must be here to collect the Echo of Flautist. After all, today is... a special day.
What special day?
Many years ago on this very day, Jinzhou was besieged by a fierce Tacet Discord outbreak. Tens of Midnight Rangers stood firm on the front lines, confronting thousands of Tacet Discords.
It was Linghan who proposed a brilliant strategy. With her deep understanding of Echoes, she suggested utilizing them to repel the enemies’ assault.
To minimize casualties, she led the entire squad here to gather hundreds of Flautist’s Echoes.
She was also a Midnight Ranger?
Yes...
Hey, isn't that person with the silver hair over there...? Grandma Linghan! GRANDMA LINGHAN! Over here!
Darn! She’s too far away to hear us!
No! The Tacet Discords are closing in on her!
Oh, man! We can’t even use overdashing to catch up from this distance!
Leave it to me!
Frostbite Tortoise, I choose you! Protect Linghan!
Phew! That was a close call!
Let’s take this chance...!
Your observation is sharp, young one. You have the makings of a soldier. Now is the moment to strike! Seize the opportunity given by the lull in Flautist’s attacks!
Let’s go!
Phew... Finally safe.
Young ones, are you alright?
W-We’re fine! Just needed to catch our breath after that crazy moment...
Instead of worrying us, go make sure Grandma Linghan’s okay!
Linghan, how are you feeling? Any injuries? Does it hurt?
Your Echo is Frostbite Tortoise, isn’t it?
You’ve raised it well, and the timing couldn’t be more perfect.
Linghan...
Seeing your Echo reminds me of my dear...
He shielded our entire squad with a humble Frostbite Tortoise, time and time again.
At first, everyone mocked him for choosing such a seemingly feeble Echo. Yet, they were all silenced by its might in the end.
After all, the strength of an Echo lies in the hands of its user.
I see. My judgment was clouded by strength before, capturing Echoes purely based on their appearances. You're right. You're always right.
Grandpa Jingzhu, why are you crying?
These tears... They’re tears of joy.
By the way, there’s a striking resemblance between you and my dear...
Both with a nose and two eyes, quite similar indeed, hehe.
But you’re nowhere near as handsome as him. In my eyes, he was incomparable—wise and brave beyond measure.
Y-Your cataracts seem to be worsening...
Hurry up! Get her reacquainted with you!
You’re right! Captain Linghan, it’s a pleasure to make your acquaintance. Allow me to introduce myself. I’m a member of the Vanguard of Midnight Rangers. You can call me Jingzhu.
Jingzhu... Did you just have flowers with you?
Oh yeah! I was too busy dealing with the Tacet Discords, and I dropped them somewhere.
Let me get them for you!
They’re right here. Let’s take them back to Grandpa Jingzhu!
Here, this Noctemint is for you. Please accept it, Linghan. Will you once again be my lifelong companion?
Ah, the scent of Noctemint... it’s so familiar. My dear used to bring me Noctemints. Just a whiff would lift my spirits.
Flowers, Echoes... they’re all the same. Practicality is key.
Y-Yes! From this moment onward, I’ll be by your side, soaking in the sunshine, engaging in conversation... Whatever you desire, I’ll be there with you!
As long as I can be by your side!
Because I made a promise to you, Linghan. I vowed to never let you be alone, and I intend to uphold that promise for eternity.
But alas, we can’t soak up the sun here.
Escort me back. Basking in the sun on my doorstep is where I feel most at ease.
Alright, alright, let’s go home!
Grandpa Jingzhu, where is Grandma Linghan?
Linghan isn’t in a good health condition, so I’ve let her return to rest for now.
Such a relief to hear that! I’m so glad she got home safe.
Oh, and by the way, I’ve got a ton of questions. {PlayerName}, you too, right?
Yes...
You might have noticed already: Linghan was once an exceptional Midnight Ranger, serving as the captain of the Vanguard.
She wasn’t just my captain; she's also my beloved wife, with whom I’ve shared many years...
Being captain, she had a lot on her plate, always leading the charge, protecting our squad, and teaching us survival skills.
As the battles escalated, she pushed herself beyond limits and suffered grave injuries.
After a major victory, she eventually fell ill. She started to feel mentally foggy, causing her memories to slowly fade away.
She forgot how to navigate the streets of Jinzhou, forgot to eat her favorite Helmet Flatbread while they were still warm, and then...
She even forgot about me...
So, that’s why you’ve been chasing after Grandma Linghan, huh?
You’re hoping to stick by her side as her special someone.
Yes, you’re correct. Our comrades, once vibrant youths, perished in battle, while others succumbed to illness.
I can’t help but fear that someday if she were to regain her memories, she’d feel a profound loneliness... I cannot bear the thought.
Sorry for bringing up sad things. Thank you for helping me find Linghan.
Linghan has accepted me. It’s a great joy! I should feel happy!
The past is the past. From now on, I’ll treasure every moment shared with Linghan!
Exactly! Let’s treasure every moment and live life to the max!
Hehe, if you have time, feel free to visit us, and we can chat about Echoes to our heart’s content.
I can’t express my gratitude enough for your assistance in resolving this matter.
Plus, seeing you must have made Linghan so relieved to know that the people we risked our lives for have turned into amazing adults.
Thank you for your efforts. Here are what you deserve.
Besides the compensation, this old man has a word of advice for you.
Take good care of your Echoes. The world beyond can be perilous, and they may come in handy in times of need.
To safeguard yourselves and those dear to you.
Upon coming to your senses, a soft hue blurs your vision.
As the mist clears, you find yourself standing in a place you know by heart—a landscape of winding rivers and jagged peaks woven beneath the clouds.

It is a perfect replica of Jinzhou. Every street, every narrow alley, the curve of every roof ridge, and the flow of every waterway has been recreated with precision. Even the whisper of the wind against your ears sounds exactly as it should.
You turn to get your bearings, but then—
AAAAAAH—
Someone crashes right into you.
S-sorry! I, um... I didn't mean to be SO LOUD!
As if startled by the volume of her own voice, the girl scrambles back, quickly clamping both hands over her mouth.
...Zhezhi?
Huh? {PlayerName}?!
I'm so sorry! I was just... in a hurry...
Her eyes light up the moment she recognizes you.
After piecing together her explanation, the situation finally starts to make sense.
I already delivered his commission! I really did!
We agreed on the final payment, but he kept making excuses, dragging it on and on! He even claimed he didn't speak the Huanglong language, and then he just... DISAPPEARED!
Zhezhi takes a deep breath, almost like gathering her courage.
So I... I just CALLED THE PATROLLERS!
I took this candy earlier, and now... I CAN'T KEEP MY VOICE DOWN!
THESE WERE SUPPOSED TO BE MY INNER THOUGHTS!
...Don't rush. Just slow down.
Is there something wrong with this candy?
O-okay... I'll SLOW DOWN! Phew...
I'm not sure. But if the effect is only temporary, I guess it's... ALL RIGHT!
At least I'll sound a lot more confident when I finally track down that deadbeat client and DEMAND WHAT I'M OWED!
Did you catch him?
Not yet... but the Patrollers said they've asked some experts to help...
She shouts again, then immediately covers her mouth in defeat. Hanging her head, she holds out her hand toward you. On her palm rests... a piece of candy?
Before you can get another word out, two shadows streak past you in a blur of motion, one after the other.
Ah! There they are!
In a blur of motion, the dark shadows scatter and dissolve. The black-haired girl turns, her gaze fixing on your face as she speaks with sudden gravity.
Passenger! Are you hurt?
Passenger? Who? Me?
Chisa, what happened to you?!
Realizing what she just said, Chisa awkwardly looks away, her expression tightens.
Actually... something did happen earlier.
I had a Rainbow Bean Pop Rock this morning, and then...
I just... started to talk like Namipon.
She frowns, clearly struggling to adapt to the change.
I find it strange too. But... there is no way to fix it for now.
Now you even sound like Namipon!
It's actually kind of fun...
You wipe away imaginary sweat from your forehead, mentally accepting this new reality.
The breeze of Honami sweeps through the streets, carrying the sweet scent of blossoms and the weight of old memories.
Taking a steady breath, you look toward the horizon.
The next stop after Honami should be...
Chisa follows your gaze, her expression turning serious.
It's Startorch Academy, right?
We'll meet you there, Passenger.
Mm. See you there.
Chisa lets out a faint smile.
When the time comes, let's fight side by side once again.
After defeating the Reactor Husk, you carefully settle Mornye by the charging device.
Once you're certain her condition has stabilized, you turn to Lynae to ask about the others.
The others? Well, I know Aemeath, Denia, and Dr. Herssen headed out to the frostlands. As for President Lucilla, she's... umm...
As Lynae is lost in her own thoughts, you realize you won't get a straight answer out of her anytime soon. You decide to head out to the frostlands first to see how the situation is unfolding.
Accident solved. Luuk Herssen flattens his outfit with a tone so casual you'd think he was just passing by.
Anyway, congratulations on getting the situation under control.
You stare at him, so intensely that he freezes for a second and looks away to avoid your gaze.
Alright, alright. I admit it. I didn't eat the candy.
And trust me, I'm not the one behind this anomaly. That, I can promise.
Weren't you the one who invented the candy in the first place?
Who is it then?
True... but I'm not the only one with access to it, am I?
Well, I think you're getting very close to the answer you seek.
You process his reply in silence.
Nearby, Denia stands with her arms crossed, wearing that insufferable "I know everything but I'm not telling" smirk.
Further off, Aemeath, who was just racing around on a seal, has grown so bored that she's started playing volleyball with the creature—Wait, can people even play volleyball on ice?
You shake your head to clear out the clutter and refocus your gaze on Luuk Herssen.
Luuk's eyebrow twitches, a sudden sense of dread washing over him.
A dangerous yet entirely reasonable thought strikes you.
Why should this foxy man get to stay perfectly composed while everyone else is dealing with his invention? Why not let him experience the "effects" firsthand?
There's no way he's escaping this.
He's lucky I'm feeling generous today.
You pull the strange candy from your pocket. The air goes still for a second.
Wait, are you planning to—
Before he can finish the sentence, you've thrust the candy toward him.
Denia finally bursts out laughing, and Aemeath leads her team of seals over to get a front-row seat.
Luuk Herssen stays silent for two seconds before sighing in defeat and popping the candy into his mouth.
See? I ate it. But I have no idea what happened. (I'm not the mastermind, but I know who is.)
The air freezes.
Pfft! Hahahahaha!
Even Luuk looks stunned, quickly clapping a hand over his mouth.
...That last part? Who said that?
What I'm trying to say is I really don't know what happened! (But I do know who's responsible for this!)
You cross your arms, enjoying the show. This is better than any ticketed performance.
Let me make this clear. (I'll keep telling the truth anyway.) This candy's effect is very serious... (And I know you're not going to go easy on me.)
Denia looks at you with a mischievous glint in her eyes.
{PlayerName}, anything else fun to show?
Forget it... I'll spare him today.
You look away, and Luuk lets out a massive sigh of relief.
Aww, it's getting boring.
Groaning, Aemeath rubs the seals' heads as they, too, slap the snow in shared disappointment.
{PlayerName}, isn't there anything else fun to do?
Anything else fun...
You ponder over this question.
Some of the things you've been through didn't exactly feel "fun" at the time, but... what if you looked at them through the lens of this game world?
Inside the SkyArk Space Station, fractured bands of light drift slowly like stardust. You find yourself treading softly at the sight of this.
Before you looms the imposing silhouette of the Nameless Explorer, and standing in its shadow is a woman holding a long blade, locked in a tense standoff.
It's Hiyuki.
She wears her miko attire with a sharp, disciplined grace, her snow-white hems fluttering slightly in the wind.
Her hair is as pale as frost, and crimson sakura patterns creep along her sleeves. She carries an aura of cold, silent intensity, like a blade held at the ready.
Sensing your presence, she shifts her focus.
You stare at her, your voice grave and direct.
Did you have that candy?
She slowly lifts her gaze to meet yours, a rare flicker of genuine confusion crossing her features. Her response comes after a moment of uncharacteristic hesitation.
...I did.
Her reply makes you frown.
Then you—
However, the Nameless Explorer has no intention of letting you confirm her state.
A searing beam of light tears through the space, its impact sending a cloud of metallic debris swirling through the air.
Frustrated by the enemy's complete ignorance of timing, you draw your blade with a grudge.
It's been so long since you last heard Xiangli Yao's voice.
He walks toward you, accompanied by his two small robots. The waveforms flickering across their screens suggest they've been observing the situation for quite some time.
My speculation is that this candy possesses a unique property that alters the consumer's traits and manifests them.
Unusual volume or distinct visual changes are both caused by it. Mm-hmm!
Then the effect on you is...
Your words make him pause, but he quickly responds in a nonchalant tone.
...A sudden verbal disorder involving the strange use of modal particles. Mm-hmm!
That said, these changes won't damage your persona. They only affect your movements and combat styles until the effect expires.
If you stay and explore further, it may be easier for you to adapt to these changes and uncover the clues you need. Mm-hmm!
How do you see it, {PlayerName}?
I need to ask for Qiuyuan's opinion...
I need to ask for Zhezhi's opinion...
I need time to consider it...
Mm. Sounds like the way to go.
Er? M-me? I, um... I think it does make some sense.
Looks like I can only play creative now.
That's right. There are so many more paths to be explored, {PlayerName}. Try to observe them carefully.
And if you find yourself in need, just let us know. Mm-hmm!
After bidding farewell to Zhezhi, Qiuyuan, and Xiangli Yao, you resume your exploration with unsolved questions.
What a strange world this game has created...
What an interesting world this game has created...
So, where to next?
Jinzhou City, the Bell-Borne Ravine, Qichi Village, the Court of Savantae Ruins... you replay the memories of every place you have ever traversed.
Suddenly, you smell the scent of dense petrichor clinging to the air. The tranquil plains beneath your feet shift the moment you step forward.
It's the Norfall Barrens.
Above, the grey clouds stir as if crumpled by an invisible hand, leaving the atmosphere damp and heavy. The weight of an impending storm presses down on you.
It feels exactly like the day you fought the Dreamless—another scene generated from the depths of your memory.
Only this time, it shows something new.
...{PlayerName}?
Before you stand three familiar figures—Jinhsi, Changli, and Jiyan all turn at once. The moment your eyes meet hers, Jinhsi instantly blushes.
...Jinhsi?
We'll explain later, {PlayerName}.
The moment the words leave her mouth, Changli has already refocused on the Dreamless. Beneath its sky-blocking wings, the radiance of Qingloong and the searing phoenix flames burst out.
As you step forward, Jinhsi follows your lead, unsheathing her blade with a resolute ring of steel.
The Dreamless fades with a haunting shriek. The wind then settles as a searing light pierces through the restless, gloomy clouds.
The battle has ended, but you remain tense.
Keep your guard up. I have something to tell you.
You share the details of the strange candy and Xiangli Yao's theory with the three of them. Before you can even finish, you notice Jinhsi is a bit out of it.
She stays still, as if processing your words, then her eyes widen in sudden realization.
A deep blush appears on her face. Tiny, delicate Loong scales shimmer into existence along her cheeks.
A heavy, awkward silence envelopes the group. It seems Jinhsi is already under the candy's influence.
Meanwhile...
As if in slow motion, a Gulpuff is lifted toward you with military solemnity.
Ensuring the Gulpuff is held securely in both hands, Jiyan finally speaks.
We... ate it.
All of us.
Sorry, I have to hold this to speak.
Jiyan's tone is as serious and heavy as a battlefield report, but the chubby Gulpuff in his palms just stares at you with zero remorse.
You press a hand to your forehead.
What about Changli...
Changli intentionally keeps her distance. Her expression is as composed as ever, but the air around her is intense and almost scorching. Looks like this is the effect she gets.
Worry not. It doesn't affect my moves. I just need to maintain a safe distance from you.
She pauses and continues.
At least... for now.
Should you call for our strength, we'll be there for you at any time.
Another flash of light. In the next moment, you hear the hustle and bustle of a city, echoing with the sound of laughter.
You stand there, dazed, as a gentle sea breeze caresses your cheeks. Its soothing, salty scent refreshes your mind instantly.
This is... Ragunna.
Yes. And to be precise, it is Ragunna on the eve of the Carnevale. Colorful banners, bright lights, and crowds filling the streets—everything is exactly as you remember.
You follow the flow of the crowd, lingering at the edge. Your gaze shifts between the grand stage, the lively market stalls, and the glowing lanterns hanging overhead.
The neon light is reflected in the fountain, shattering into a thousand iridescent shards across the water's surface. You blink, and for a moment, you see familiar silhouettes in the reflection.
Galbrena... and Lupa?
You try to push through the crowd to call out to them, but in the meantime, the lights in the square erupt.
Fireworks streak into the sky, the crowd bursting into a deafening cheer in perfect unison.
The Carnevale... has begun.

Confetti rains down from above. Music sweeps through the streets. Laughter, applause, and shouting overlap in symphony. The figures you saw only moments ago are now swallowed by the surging tide of people.
You are forced to stop, your chest tightening.
And you see it—a crimson Lycoris petal drifting down through the air.
You look up at the night sky, where light and shadow intertwine. The bleeding colors swirl across your vision, yet something feels unreal. It's like a thin veil waiting to be torn aside.
You gaze at it... and breathe the name of the one about to descend.
...Hecate.
With Hecate defeated, the Carnevale finally settles back into its natural rhythm. You exhale a long sigh of relief and quickly turn to check on your companions.
Are you both alright?
That's when you notice Lupa acting differently. She's far more hyperactive than usual, her eyes darting with an unusually bright spark as she bounces over to your side.
A brightly wrapped package of sweets is thrust toward you.
Here, Warrior! Try a Rainbow Bean Pop Rock! It's a new flavor!
You... ate one already?
Lupa... this candy has a special effect...
Yeah! Swallowed it right down! So yummy!
I know! But it's so funny that I just had to share!
Lupa says with a satisfied grin, her voice buzzing with an intensity you've never heard before.
However...
Where is Chimera?
The spot at Galbrena's side, usually occupied by Chimera, is now home to a Fae Ignis. Its violet-blue tail feathers sway gently before you.
For a moment, you could sense a wave of depression radiating from the Echo. Then, Galbrena pats its head.
It's right here.
Lupa gave me a piece of that candy. I just shoved it into Chimera's mouth.
The Fae Ignis (actually Chimera) lets out an indignant cry.
No way...
I should try this on Abby.
The effect is lingering, so it'll be stuck in this shape for a while.
Galbrena says with a shrug, and Lupa squeezes herself between the two of you.
So, Warrior! Where are you heading next?
Next...
You cast your gaze toward the horizon, where the ancient city-state with colossal statues stands in the distance.
On the other side, Galbrena stands nearby looking perfectly composed, arms crossed and expression calm.
After an ultimate thrilling battle, you sit down with Augusta and Iuno to savor the local delicacies of Septimont. Soon enough, it is time to part ways once more.
May... your journey... be... smooth, my friend.
Iuno stands slightly back, somehow upset, and scribbles on her board. She holds it up with a forceful snap, as if determined to make sure you don't miss a single word.
Come back soon! (I'm only asking for the sake of everyone else!)
The final stroke of the character trails off slightly.
Iuno puffs out her cheeks and looks away, hugging the board back to her chest as if to insist she's only acting as a messenger.
Of course. I'll see you around.
If there's a chance, I will.
Leaving Septimont behind, you embark on your journey again. As you reach the forest on the outskirts, the air itself seems to grow lighter.
A melody catches the breeze and drifts toward you—a playful rhythm where the notes seem to dance through the trees. You follow the sound.
A girl holding a lute comes into view, humming and strumming the strings with effortless grace.
♪Lulala! Lululala!♪
Ah! It's you, {PlayerName}! Long time no see!
Noticing your gaze, her eyes light up, and the melody takes a sudden, elegant turn.
She skips over to you, every word she speaks emerging as a lyric. You quickly realize the candy's strange influence has found its way to Ciaccona as well.
But unlike the others struggling with their "abnormalities," she seems... too well-adapted to it.
Before you can even ask, she tilts her head with a smile and sings.
♪It's just the effect of that candy. But it's not so bad, is it?♪
Ciaccona twirls in a small circle, her skirt fluttering to the beat.
♪It's like... stumbling upon another version of myself.♪
♪Maybe it'll spark some new inspiration!♪
The music begins to flow again, light and unrestrained.
You stand there watching her walk ahead, completely immersed in her own song. It's then the idea hits you.
Amidst this streak of "anomalies," at least someone is truly enjoying the strangely beautiful turn of events.
The next stop is...
You open your eyes as the light fades. Your gaze first lands on a sky-scraping tower before settling on a rolling Ferris wheel.
In a gentle rain of light pink petals, you recognize the city before you.
...Honami.
Standing by the street, you look around, letting your mind drift back into those memories.

The days spent trapped here, the repeated choices to defy the Lament, the cycles that felt like progress but always led back to the start—those experiences still seem vivid, yet they also feel a world away.
Now, Honami has finally broken the loop, following its true tracks toward a real tomorrow.
Your thoughts naturally turn to the companions who walked that path with you.
Chisa... and Namipon...
If I head to Shashou Cafe now, will I... find them there?
Just as you begin to map out a route, a low, distorted snarl echoes from behind you.
GET… OUT—!
Letting out a sigh, you draw your blade and turn toward the source of the roar.
In that split second, the air fractures. A girl with black hair and crimson eyes tears through the sky, landing firmly at your side.
Wait, who turned this on?
It's the first time I see its screen glow...
Really?! LET ME SEE!
That's weird—Oh, {PlayerName}! Didn't expect to see you here!
You know me?
What are we looking at?
You kidding? How could I not recognize the Academy's living legend!
Check this out. This arcade cabinet has been sitting here since my very first day of school. I've never seen it on before.
But its screen is actually live today!
Let's see...
You lean in and find a line of text emerging from the center of the screen.
"Attention faculty and students! Welcome to the world of Star Bouncing. Log in with your Persona Pinball and start a brand-new adventure!"
Looks interesting.
Hm, you gonna give it a try?

The arcade stands before you, its screen flickering with a rhythmic glow, almost like it's breathing. You get the strange impression that a single touch will pull you into an entirely different world.
Sure. Why not?
Ah, {PlayerName}. You finished it faster than I expected. Never let people down, hm?
Why do I see disappointment on your face now?
Care to explain all this, Madam President?
That's too much of a word. I know someone as sharp and smart as you would clear this game in no time. But isn't it normal to be a bit emotional when you finally finish a game?
Well, it's just a little game I made on a whim.
And don't worry, its underlying structure is completely safe.
It just brings your hidden persona to the surface for a while. Pretty funny, isn't it?
...True.

Well, even I find myself craving something fresh to break up the daily grind every now and then. And honestly, with so many brilliant students around, I never have to look far for a spark of inspiration.
So adding Rainbow Bean Pop Rocks into the game was also part of your plan?
It works like a catalyst. Otherwise, the game would be far too boring and bland.
And Dr. Luuk?
That's none of my business. He signed up for it himself.
He volunteered to make sure everything stayed under control. Makes sense to me. It's his invention, after all.
Mornye also helped work on the theories, though only a tiny part during the initial phase before she got buried under a mountain of student essays...
Sounds like another prank managed by the sly faculty together.
Ouch. No need to be so harsh. It was just an academic collaboration.
So, you did all this... just to let me have a try?
Exactly. You get to experience something different—reactions or personalities you don't normally get to see.
What's your verdict? A funny little surprise, I hope?
It's not bad.
What if I say no?
Haha. I'm glad you liked it.
Hmm... then I'll have to try something else next time.
I hope you did find a bit of unusual fun in this little interlude, {PlayerName}.
So a new story is about to begin?
Oh, actually... It's not that much of a big deal.
I've been conducting uninterrupted observations at this weather Observation Station...
Recent observation data shows that the weather changes in the surroundings share similarities with the storms happening here in the past...
But the similarity are still in the cradle. I can't jump to conclusions now.
Don't worry. I'll keep an eye on this.
That's right. The hero embarks on a journey in the vast wilderness, battling against the harsh natural environment and engaging in thrilling fights with bounty criminals...
I'm captivated by such a fearless and firm belief.
If you're into Westerns too, I'd be more than happy to share my long-cherished movie list with you!
The storm formed by the abnormal gravity field seems to be returning...
A new story?
So the storm is happening again?
If you have an express to send, please fill out the form according to the template.
The template is on the notice board over there. You can check it out.
Template?
Please pay special attention to the item type, as well as the expected delivery date.
We follow these strict rules just to ensure a smooth delivery.
Especially when your package has to travel through a timid, foggy swamp here in Whining Aix's Mire.
Most of the packages are bound for Frosting Harbor, and taking the Heron Wetland is the only shortcut.
To describe the dense fog... packages would be soaked by the fog in the past.
Quite strict rules for a delivery service.
Thankfully, Mumian, my colleague, invented a type of dehumidifier. When paired with our special delivery boxes, we can ensure the package stays dry for three days.
But even with this extra insurance, one can never be too careful when you're traveling through Whining Aix's Mire.
Oh, these dehumidifiers are quite effective!
Yeah. It's a must-have when delivering packages in Whining Aix's Mire.
Dehumidifiers?
Without it, even the delivery box can't shelter packages from the penetrating fog.
I have a stellar reputation for making dehumidifiers. I can assure that!
Look! I made these dehumidifier from Violet Coral ground into powder, mixed with Angelica!
Angelica repels insects, and Violet Coral powder absorbs water... With these, we don't have to fear the heavy fog anymore.

It's super lively out here!

W-wait, is this turning into some kind of item race now?

Welcome to this Relay Station!
Just ask if you need assistance using the station facilities. I am here to help.
On a field expedition, safety comes first. Everyone open your internship handbooks. I'll keep this brief.
Ironhoofs have such a reassuring presence... I wish I could keep one too.
Well... I'll be here for some time. Come and visit it, whenever you wish.
I've hit a roadblock lately. Would it be possible to borrow an Exoswarm for some experiments?
Don't be silly! Do you even know the extent of the procedures required to involve an Exoswarm in an experiment?
I've hit a roadblock in my research. Think I could... borrow an Exoswarm for some experiments?
Silly goose! Do you have any idea the amount of red tape you need to cut through to get an Exoswarm for an experiment?
I really don't, but I'm all ears.
First, you gotta write up your whole proposal, especially the part about why you need the Exoswarm, and submit it to your advisor.
If your advisor approves, they write a recommendation and send the whole packet to the Head of Division.
Next, the Head of Division and the Department Director will...
Whoa! Please stop, it's making me dizzy. I give up!
Actually, I'm interested in the process. Please go on.
Now that's the spirit! Now, where was I... Right, the Department Director!
Once the Director thinks an Exoswarm is justified, they send it to the Academic Committee. They'll call a meeting with all the different Department Directors to review everything.
If you pass that, you're done with the academics. Then comes the administrative side.
The Chief of General Affairs contacts the Royan representative here. Then you, with your Department Director, have to present your research to them in person.
If the Royan rep gives the thumbs-up, they'll present your report to the Solisylum. Don't worry, the rep is always a top academic. They won't mess it up.

If Solisylum agrees it's necessary, then things get easier. But then there's the actual logistics of transporting the Exoswarm, and the list of do's and don'ts while researching it... Well, that's a whole other story.
Just hearing the process shows how important Exoswarm are to Lahai-Roi.
That was actually interesting to hear. Thanks for explaining.
Exoswarm are able to adapt well to Lahai-Roi's complex and varied terrain.
Wouldn't it be great if we could borrow a few to help with our field research?
My big brother barely ever comes home since he left for his studies. I miss him so much.
Could you carry me across the Academy's walls to see my brother?
If I place a plant into a mech reindeer's mouth, it will be processed and synthesized within its body, right?
I'd just call it eating and digesting. Except what comes out... is raw materials.
I can't believe it! A band of Outcasts disguised themselves as ordinary Roya and scammed me!
Oh? Well, even a three-year-old Roya is scarily smart, let alone a grown Outcast.
Am I just imagining it? I swear the food here tastes way better than at any other station.
Don't you see all the Roya around us? It's all thanks to them!

They couldn't stand our cooking, so they stepped in and tweaked a few things themselves.
No way! This is so good, I'm almost tempted to switch my research focus to Royan cuisine.
First time this far out for an internship? Got the jitters?
I got totally lost back in my day. Seriously thought that was it for me.
"Brief," he said. It's been going on for at least 30 minutes now...
First time this far out for an internship? Got the jitters?
I got totally lost back in my day. Seriously thought that was it for me.

I wouldn't have made it without her. So, remember the social etiquette taught in Royan Culture lectures. Be respectful. It pays off.
Finally, my last stop for the day.
I should reward myself with some Royan cuisine after a day like this.
I have some tools made from Exoswarm material. Would you like one?
For real? Wait a sec... this doesn't seem right. What did they say about this in Royan Culture lectures again...?
What do you think about this spot? Nice and quiet, right?
Are you blind? Who would be stupid enough to rob a Spacetrek Collective station?
Beware of rapid currents and hazards in the wilds.
Visitors to the Solstream Cascade, please do not cross beyond the station's safe zone.
You're joking, right?
I wish. A bunch of Soliskin just made off with my expedition motorbike.
You're joking, right?
I wish. A bunch of Soliskin just made off with my expedition motorbike.
Please... tell me everything in detail.
I parked on a high ridge and hiked down on foot to collect some data.
Suddenly, I heard the engine start. I turned around and saw my motorbike being dragged to the other side of the hill.
Next thing I know, there's this group of round, chubby, glowing little things... just bouncing all over my bike. It was so bizarre, I just froze.
I see. I wish I was the one to see some Soliskin riding on a motorbike. Bet it was adorable.
Sure, I'll regret not getting a picture for the rest of my life. But think you can help get it back?
By the time I snapped out of it, they were already wobbling away on it.
Oh, we'll contact the Roya at the nearby camp and ask one of their herders for help. When it comes to Soliskin, they're the ones you want.
Freeze! I'll send you back to the Academy! This is my turf!
I'm telling the station master!
You spent your time at Solstream Cascade doing serious research, right? Not just gawking, right?
I'm sure submitting a report and taking an exam right after we get back won't be a problem, right?
What?! U-Uh, you're not ready for it either, right?
I'm sure I'll... Ugh, fine. I was too busy taking selfies by the cascades.
Squeezy Jelly, check. Cans, check. Reactor light spectrum measuring toolkit, check.
Next was... What was next again? Hmm... uh, Squeezy Jelly? Check.
The Cradle Lichen here is flourishing! Looks a lot better than what the Agro Wing is growing.
There aren't many plants here, but they're all huge. Look at that massive bed of Lichen!
We're not here to admire the cascades! We need to hurry up and collect the environmental data.
This trip was worth it! Solstream Cascade lives up to the hype!
How are you so chill? Are you sure we won't get caught for skipping class?
Ugh, lost again. I still can't wrap my head around all these rules.
You just need more practice. And not just against me.

You just need more practice. And not just against me.
Every night, a whole crowd gathers at the Howling Tunnel to play Peaks of Prestige. It's like the Exostrider's own whispers are the wind... the atmosphere is unreal.
Oh? It sounds worth checking out. I'll go one of these days.
Solstream Cascade shines with a new light now.
Solstream Cascade shines with a new light now.
You're one of the Heliodic Six..
I am the Binder. To the Reactor Drive, I am observer and keeper. Are you the Arbiter who aided the New Solar Ceremony? My gratitude, you have.
Today, the light upon the world... is known as Helios. My heart's shadows are swept away in its brilliance.
So beautiful. So warm. A tenderness in which I now abide.
Please convey my thanks to its creator. And may your path ahead be ever clear.
I'm an indoor person... Or maybe you can call me a lab-person.
Being forced to be outside for an internship is torture to me.
All my husband ever thinks about is his research. He even talks in his sleep about the lab.
Mine's no better. Always off doing stuff for the Solsworn, never any time for things at home.
Sundermere is a research site. Please leave immediately if you are not a member of this station.
If you have entered the zone by mistake, please contact station staff immediately.
What? You want a posting here? You've got a long way to go.
Do you even know what Sundermere is? Focus on learning the Academy ropes first.
That's right. It was a night just like this one. I was deep in the Howling Tunnel collecting data.
And then, out of nowhere... this low hum filled the air, like a chorus of whispers...
You know the Twin Nova was built to explore what's beyond the Stridergate, right?
Of course. Nobody knows what it's really like out there.
You know the Twin Nova was built to explore what's beyond the Stridergate, right?
Of course. Nobody knows what it's really like out there.
The Spacetrek Collective needs combat robots that can operate on their own and pull off those high-G maneuvers.
When the day comes to launch, seeing the Twin Nova in that formation... it's gonna be a hell of a sight.
Is it me, or is the canned food here even worse than at the Research Institute?
If you ask the Academy's staff, they'll just blame it on Sundermere.
Hello! Is this the check-in? I'm so excited to be assigned to Sundermere Station!
Whoa, someone's eager. Gotta warn ya, it gets tough out here. Don't let it break ya.
Other places I've been to are nothing compared to this.
Yeah. But the higher-ups know this is way above our pay grade. Best not to think about it too much.
Another sleepless night?
I had a nightmare, and when I woke up, it felt like I could hear Ingles' screaming again.
You look rough. Another sleepless night?
Had a nightmare. Woke up feeling like I could hear Ingles screaming all over again.
That's just in your head... But you went ahead and pulled strings to get stationed here, of all places? Why? I know you can't get over your brother's death, but...
He kept saying everything would be fine once the Hyvatia Space Telescope was launched, and then he could finally rest...
It kills me that the moment he was waiting for... is the same one that killed him.
Void Storms are unpredictable. Ingles knew the risks when he signed up.
I know, but... his life's work is right there. And it's "alive" in a way he never imagined. The least I can do is be here to see it through to the end.
Who called Brissett in? We don't have any results to show yet!
The Institute was never sold on our project to begin with! We can't afford any more screw-ups!
Who called Brissett in? We don't have any results to show yet!
The Institute was never sold on our project to begin with! We can't afford any more screw-ups!
Well, we managed to talk our way out of it this time. Getting Brissett as our reviewer is actually a lucky break.
I know. He's reasonable. Anyone else would have slashed our funding to the bone the second they heard what we're studying.
The whistling in the Howling Tunnel... the Roya call it the "Exostrider's Craw." Multiple researchers, including Mr. Duarte, have reported auditory hallucinations.
And those who hear them... they claim it's the voices of people lost to the Void Storms.
If we can prove that, maybe we can find out where the missing ended up after the Void Storms took them!
The more we talk, the more I think this is the profitable angle. Next time I'm at the Institute, I'm applying for more funding.
Ugh, I need a transfer. I haven't seen the sun in weeks. Look at my skin!
Are you saying the Reactor Drive's light is good for your skin?
Could he have heard victims of the Void Storm speaking from beyond the grave...?

He's so committed, he's almost got me believing it.

Aha! So does this waveform represent the "ooh" sound?
Who's shouting near the receiver? You're screwing up the data!
I heard the Apex Duelist from the birthplace of Peaks of Prestige has mastered every single deck!
No way! I haven't even finished learning all the cards yet.
A new player showed up and wiped the floor with all the local masters!
I heard that too! Slashed through them like the Exostrider's greatsword slicing through butter!
Wow! It's the Lahai-Roi reigning champion!
Good luck, champion of Lahai-Roi! I can't wait to see you play in the championship!
Wow... you even look like a champion. No wonder you're the best!
You've been playing too much Peaks of Prestige. Snap out of it!
Hmm... Didn't you swear you'd "never play again" after you lost this morning?
Details, details! Come on, just one more game!
You again? I told you not to come back until you get good!
Playing noobs is just going to hurt my game!
I agree with you completely! Go on, keep telling me how awesome I am!
Another challenger? I bet you won't last two rounds.
They're as based as an Ironhoof!
Nah, I think you mean to say Sabercat Prowler!

Ironhoof!
Sabercat Prowler!

Sir, your words... I haven't felt this moved since I first read the Trine Myth!
Right! We'll double our efforts! We'll recruit more members, upgrade to a full society so that more people will see how incredible the Trine Myth is!
You are both students, first and foremost. Do not let your studies fall behind.
And just as the Sacred Reactor Epoch foretold, forgotten the past, many of my people have. They do not worry about the future.

Field research, infrastructure projects, and exchanges between the Roya and the Spacetrek Collective all rely on a solid transportation network.
That's us! We provide transportation services for people and goods across the entire region.
Each Relay Station offers basic meal services for convoys, researchers, and students on field expeditions.
But thanks to our Royan partners, some stations are now serving even tastier meals!
The Lahai-Roi wilds can be unpredictable, so researchers often use a Relay Station as a base while surveying for nearby sites of interest.
They store their equipment temporarily with us. And rest assured, the Research Institute has equipment consultants at each station to manage and oversee stored items.
If anything goes wrong during an expedition, researchers can call our emergency line to request immediate help from a nearby station.
Whether it's a missing person, a safety threat, damaged equipment, or you just need us to deliver supplies you left behind, we'll respond immediately.
We usually offer large, medium, and small vehicle rentals, but the demand for vehicles across the region has been higher than anyone predicted.
And it's not just our heavy-duty freight Haulers. Even the Pathfinders we use for transporting personnel are all booked up thanks to the Academy's internship program.
Our smaller Sprinter has great cargo capacity, and its off-road capabilities are even better than those expedition motorbikes. Of course, those are also fully booked.
So, vehicle rentals are temporarily on hold at our Relay Stations. We're really sorry for the inconvenience!

Why can't you let me talk to the Magistrate?!
How far did you get? Did you manage to see the Magistrate?
I got to see... Lady Sanhua! She even looked back at me!
And I even got Lady Sanhua's verbal assurance... That I wasn't the guest the Magistrate was waiting for!
But who cares anyway.
I was able to witness Lady Sanhua in the flesh and be rejected by her in person!
Whew. First time seeing such a crowd in front of the City Hall.
I was surprised too. I've never seen so many non-staff personnel here before.
Are they all here for an audience with the Magistrate?
Most of the people here have applied for an audience, but I heard they've all been turned down.
Turned down by who?
It's me they're waiting for.
Perhaps the Magistrate is not here yet.

Most people were advised to leave by the Magistrate's bodyguard upon sending in their applications. The ones staying here are either trying to apply for some other people, or just too stubborn to leave.
The few that made it inside said it only took "one freezing look from Lady Sanhua", and they were compelled to leave.
What kind of description is that? Sounds like they've met some snake-haired lady, and got turned into stone.
Who's Sanhua?
She is the Magistrate's personal bodyguard.
Oh, I've heard of her before. She's the "All-round Death Glare slash Terminator Ice Beauty."
...That's what the rumors say, at least.
So this is the true confidence of our Rover!
I agree though. So far, you've been ticking all the boxes in our Magistrate's description.
There is a small chance she's not in the City Hall, but it is very unlikely for her not to be in Jinzhou.
Or rather, it's nearly impossible for the Magistrate to leave Jinzhou at all.
With her busy schedule, it's already difficult to find any time off. In addition, as the Magistrate of Jinzhou, leaving the land under her jurisdiction without authentication is not allowed.
Unless she's engaged on a business trip, or... when Jinzhou's safety is under threat.
Yup, there's gotta be something big if that's the case!
Can holographic messages be prerecorded?
Sure they can.
Have you thought of something, Rover?
Perhaps the Magistrate did not know who her guest was.
I'm wondering why the Magistrate wanted to meet her guest in person.
She must have a reason for attracting all this attention.
You mean...?
She's not doing this to avoid confusion for her guest.
She should have anticipated the follow-up of her public message.
Still, how does she decide who is her guest, and who is not...
Nothing in particular.
I can't really keep up with your thoughts, but I think a meeting with the Magistrate wouldn't hurt.
Same here. Anyway, our Magistrate's the best lead we have for now, no matter what she has in store for Rover.
I believe so.
What do you think?
What if I am not the person?
What if I am the person?
Huh? Me? I'm just wondering how to take you, Yangyang, and Baizhi for some chow after this!
But my shift's almost coming up. Dunno if we'll make it...
I don't have anything particular in mind.
It was me who... I mean, we took you to Jinzhou. I think we should keep you company, at least while you're still here.
Oh, I see.
VIP or not VIP, special or not special... That doesn't matter at all.
...unless there's money to earn, of course!
Then that's exactly what we're after!
That means we're on the right track then. You'll be getting your memories back in no time.
What do you think, Rover? Are you in a hurry to recover your memories?
Most certainly.
The loss of memory doesn't bother me.
I don't know what to do.
What really matters is how I'll live my life and create new memories.
In that case...
How about meeting with the Magistrate first? She may have the answers you're looking for.
We are not allowed to go with you. Chixia and I will be right outside the City Hall.
We'll be waiting for you.
That's right, we're not going anywhere! Just give us a shout if anything goes down—Wait, no, we won't be able to hear ya. Plus they've got this rule about not yelling inside the City Hall.

A crowd has gathered outside City Hall. They are all eager to meet Jinhsi, but each is turned away by her bodyguard, Sanhua. With questions swirling in your mind, you bide your time and hope for answers.
Please, follow me.
Pleased to make your acquaintance. I apologize for the delay. My name is Sanhua, the bodyguard of Madam Magistrate.
Call me Rover for now.
I regret to inform you that Madam Magistrate is currently away. Prior to her departure, she instructed me to bring you these tokens and a welcome gift.
Hello.
Sanhua instantly recognizes you as the guest Jinhsi is expecting. She informs you that Jinhsi is currently away but has left a welcome gift and some mysterious tokens for you.
Hearing Yangyang's calls, you slowly reclaimed consciousness...
Be careful! I can feel something dangerous over there...
Defense at the city gate has been strengthened.
It wasn't like this when we came back...
Access Pass is required if you're heading to the Norfall Barrens. That place is now off-limits.
What is your business, young lady? It's my third shift and you're still here.
Oh, you must be the soldier on duty at noon yesterday. Nice to see you again.
I'm a Resonator and a trained martial artist. I can handle myself. Please, I need to go look for someone.
I've promised the missing man's grandfather to bring him back. Would you let me through?
Be that as it may, I cannot let you given the current circumstances. My apologies.
Well, everything seems fine in the city. Are things really that bad on the frontlines?
That's why we must stay vigilant, so people in the city can go on peacefully with their lives.
Besides, General Jiyan is currently there at the Norfall Barrens base. Dangerous as it is, he will keep an eye on every soldier, including the one you're looking for.
We have already sent a report on your case. You could just go home and wait for the good news. What's the point of staying here?
Thank you, but I have already asked the Patrol Station for help and tried every method I could think of. Please, let me through. I promised him, so I gotta give it my all.
I understand your concern.

I don't want to be a bother. Would it help if I hid my presence and stayed somewhere further away? How about five miles? Or maybe a hundred? A thousand might be too far though, I wouldn't be able to see you clearly...
Listen. Nobody knows when the soldiers will return, and even if they do, you might not find the one you seek.
It's a dangerous road ahead if you want to reach the frontlines, and you don't even have an Access Pass...
...Ahem. Your Access Pass has been verified.
Just you two?
Yes.
The monk over there is coming with us.
Greetings. I'm Jianxin. Could you please do me a favor?
I want to go look for someone outside the city, but I don't have an Access Pass, so... May I tag along?
Okay.
What can you do for us?
What do I get out of this?
You'll have to ask the guards about that.
Thank you for your kindness!
I'm a jack-of-all-trades: Tai Chi, cooking, tea-making, mining, foraging, errand-running, fixing utilities, and caring for animals. Got something else in mind? I'm always up for learning new skills.
Alright then.
I see. I've got three Guokui Flatbreads, 34 Shell Credits, and the Mirrors of Clarity. They're all yours.
You seem to live a humble life.
You can keep them.
You're right. I should be open about my request. I don't want to lie and cause further trouble for the soldiers.
I intend to leave the city with them, and they have agreed. Will it be an issue for you?
I, uh...
Is it allowed?
Please.
Well, it says you have the highest level of access, so no procedural issues here.
(Honestly, {Male=he;Female=she} could lead an entire troop out of the city with that Access Pass and no one would question it...)
Let's go.
Master Jianxin?
Sure!
At the city gate, you encounter Jianxin, a Taoist who is being denied passage. After learning she is searching for a missing person, you use your authority to help her leave the city.
Thank you for your help! I really appreciate it!
Jianxin explains why she wants to leave the city. She tells you about the person she is looking for.
So you're looking for the relative of a veteran, and you believe he's in the Midnight Rangers camp in Desorock Highland?
Exactly.
What's your relationship with the person you're looking for?
Why is it so important for you to find him?
Do you know anything about the mangosteen?
Where are you from?
Got it.
His name is Zhiyuan. I don't know him in person. On my way down the mountain, I ran into his grandfather, who was looking for his grandson on his own but ended up lost.
I couldn't just leave an elderly person like him out there. So I thought I'd escort him to the nearest city and make further plans once we're safe.
You're willing to go to such lengths for someone you don't know...
You have a kind soul, Master Jianxin.
It's all thanks to many kind-hearted people. Without them, Mr. Zongye and I wouldn't have made it to Jinzhou.
Mr. Zongye seemed confused. He's gone through a lot searching for his enlisted grandson. Lending a helping hand was the least I could do.

I reported his situation to the Patrol Station, but with the chaos on the frontline, Mr. Zongye has been extremely worried about his grandson's safety... He'd sneak out to look for his grandson the moment no one was watching. I'm really worried about him.
This mangosteen?
It's got some fresh-looking leaves, soft springy skin, and eight fleshy segments fully ripened inside. It looks like a nice fruit.
Good to know.
Well... thanks for the tip on how to pick out the good ones.
How do you know that?
Nothing else?
Oh, one more thing I forgot to mention. There's a bruise at the bottom. If you don't eat that part soon, it'll spoil.
I grew up in my sect on a mountain. Spent most of my time training with my masters.
One day, I was told training in seclusion was not enough. I must engage with the world to further my skills.
So I started my self-cultivating journey. I've been to various cities and gained valuable lessons, but there is still so much more to learn.
...According to what I've gathered, Mr. Zongye's grandson is very likely in the Desorock Highland.
Thanks to your help, I can finally leave the city to find him.
That's where we are heading too.
Let's go together.
Master Jianxin, please keep us safe.
Of course.

Jianxin explains she is searching for a boy named Zhiyuan. He vanished after leaving the city, and his grandfather tasked her to find him. Sadly, she has no information about the tokens you are investigating.
You don't look like soldiers. Why are you here? The frontlines are right up ahead.
I am Yangyang, an Outrider of the Midnight Rangers.
Yangyang showed her Midnight Rangers badge and Jianxin asked him about Zhiyuan.
A missing person... Zhiyuan...
The one you're looking for. Is he an average person? Not a Resonator, I suppose?
Yes, have you seen him? Is he alright?
I met him once. He's not officially enlisted, but he seemed determined to join us. He's been secretly following our troops since last year.

He must be in the Rearguards Camp. He can't be anywhere else; the actual frontlines are right up ahead, and we the Midnight Rangers would never allow non-servicemen to approach and risk getting killed.
I see.
Master Jianxin.
Thank you!
Now if you're heading that way, I have a request for you, my Outrider comrade.
On your way there, you should run into two Detection Beacons. They just went offline. Could you go check on them?
Sure, we will.
Great. I'll send the coordinates to your Terminal.
I think a quartermaster of the Rearguards escorted him away, so if he's not in the city...
A Midnight Ranger reveals details about Zhiyuan's disappearance, and you agree to check on the Detection Beacons that have been disconnected.
Hmph, a tough nut, aren't you?
I just helped you. Why did you attack us?
You're not feedin' all of us with ya bread and pennies.  Hand over your goods and grub or face the consequences.
We ain't messin' with no kids, but don't test our patience. Just do as you're told!
Don't make it tough on yourselves. Or you'll be lucky to leave in one piece.
I will not bend to injustice.
Rover, Yangyang, please step back as I handle them.
Fine! You asked for this!
Is that the Beacon? Why are there so many people?
They don't look like soldiers...
Greetings. What might interest you here? It's dangerous.
Oh. We, uh... Nothing, really. You see, we're just on our way south, to the city.
Stop lying. I saw it.
Excuse me, about this Detection Beacon...
Run, everyone!
Something's fishy about them.
Don't let them run off.
As you near the first Detection Beacon, you stumble upon some shifty-looking "civilians." You move to confront them.
I-I can't move... So hungry...
P-please don't arrest us! We really had no choice!
What happened? Do you need help?
The battles are getting real bad up north, and we couldn't live there anymore. Figured we have to go back to the city.
We ain't eaten in ages, and we're broke. Some of us can barely move 'cause we're so damn hungry.
Then we found some expensive looking stuff here. Now that the military's out there fighting and nobody's really using these thingies, we thought it might get us a few pennies.
A damaged Detection Beacon might result in a sudden TD invasion from the direction it covers.
Our frontline troops would face attacks from both sides. Have you thought about the consequences?
We ain't got the time for that! If we don't steal, we'd starve to death before the Tacet Discords kill us.
You shouldn't be stealing public property. Please return the parts.
There's still some distance from here to Jinzhou city. Here, you can have my flatbreads.
And here's some money. This should be enough for you to reach the city.
You're giving us... all of these? Thank you. Thank you!
Hey! You! Come over and say thank you before you eat!
It was nothing. Master once told me, "The sage takes care of all men, and abandons none."
Watch out!
You offer assistance to the "civilians" responsible for damaging the Detection Beacon, but they repay your kindness with violence. You have no choice but to teach them a lesson.
We're beggin' ya, stop! We surrender. Take us in!
Why did you attack us when I already gave you food and funds?
Do you have other mouths to feed, aside from what we see here?
They seem trained... These are not ordinary people.
Who are you?
O-of course we are ordinary people! We just... we just joined the Exiles recently.

We done some wrongs. Tried to run from them Patrollers and left the city, but dang, didn't know the battles up north were so crazy. Our new boss ran outta food before we could even figure out the camp. Figured we'd be better off just go back to the city and get locked up...
Then we ran outta food and cash halfway. So we turned to thieving.
We ain't got the balls to rob the army, but with stuff just sitting around, why not?
Hey, since you're being so generous, how about you throw a little extra cash our way? There's a bunch of us, some injured too. Your first amount ain't gonna cut it for us to survive.
We have some spare supplies.
Wait. What I gave them was more than enough for them to make it to Jinzhou.
I used to travel alone when I left my Master. I know how much it takes for someone to survive.
Hey! What's wrong with you, girlie? It won't hurt to give us more!
Pain comes with coveting. He who knows he has enough is rich. It was only meant to sustain you long enough for you to reach the city.
You don't understand, girl. You don't make money very easily in a time like this. If we can't find jobs in the city, we gonna starve again.
I came from a seclusive place, learning the ways of the world from scratch. It's been a hard time, but even I have managed to make a living with my own hands.
If you really can't find any job in the city, come to Liuxian Teahouse and ask for Jianxin. I'll gladly help you search for jobs and work alongside you.
Tsk... Fine! Fine! We'll go.
Hurry, move! Let's get outta here. I'm not listening to this lecture anymore.
I wasn't trying to... Wait, please put that down.
Ugh, quite the sharp eye you got. Fine! Here you go!
Is this the only Detection Beacon you messed with?
Heck yeah! Just the first one we were trying to steal and you bumped right into it.
Really? Then why does that one over there seem broken too?
That ain't got nothing to do with us! It has been that way for ages. Plus, we ain't ever reaching it with all those thorns.
I see. You may leave now.
The military's base is not far from here. Shall we fix the Beacons before going?
Okay.
We shouldn't give them more.
Wait. What I gave them was enough for them to make it to Jinzhou, even when they are so many.
Upon subduing the Exiles masquerading as civilians, you reclaim the stolen components and head for the next Detection Beacon.
Is it... fixed?
Yes. Let's go and check on the next one.
Awesome, we've got the second Beacon fixed.
Master Jianxin, are you alright?
This is my first time on a battlefield. It feels so different here...
I know another shipment of supplies has just arrived. I've confirmed it, but it's not nearly enough. We must reach out to the city again and demand more supplies immediately.
But the approval process is going to...
Tell them it's an emergency. We are working around the clock here. Any delay could mean the end of our defense. Do they not comprehend? Here's the list of what we need.
I'll talk to them if you can't make them listen! Now go go go!
Move, move! What is it? Why are we still not done distributing these?
Hello.
You new here? Are you backups too?
Wait, you don't look like one of us...
I am Yangyang, an Outrider of the Midnight Rangers. And they are...
Excuse me. One moment, please.
Careful! This chest holds vital medical supplies. If the wounded return and find no medicine, it's on you. Handle with care and precision!
An Outrider? So you are part of the backup force, right? Now, I've got wounded soldiers coming soon, and you're just in time to help.
Sorry. Have to answer this.
Yes. What is it?
An Overclocked Resonator? Understood. I'll be there immediately.
I'm sorry... Erm, could you do me a favor?

The wounded soldiers are being sent back from the frontlines. We need someone to escort them to the medics, but I've got to deal with the Overclocked Resonator now. Could you please take care of them?
What exactly do you need us to do?
Just make sure they are safe. The medics will take care of their wounds.
Sure. Leave it to us.
Thank you.
It's so busy here... Looks like they don't even have the time to catch their breath.
Supplies, medical care, equipment maintenance, personnel management, and logistics... They must carefully manage these matters to provide vital support for our fighters.
So this is what a real war looks like. I had no idea it could get this bad.
Most people would never have the chance to witness any of this. It's natural for you not to know.
I think this is exactly what our military strives for—to ensure peace and safety for our citizens. It's a sacrifice made so others don't have to live in fear.
The wounded soldiers are here. Let's go check on them.
Yangyang showed her Midnight Rangers badge.

Upon arriving at the Rearguard Camp, you are greeted by a scene of chaos, revealing the grim state of the ongoing conflict. There, you meet logistic coordinator Xiulan and agree to help tend to the wounded.
Like I said, it's not a big deal! No need to fix me up! Let me go!
Please calm down. Your wound is still bleeding.
That's barely a scratch! You can't stop me!
Now is not the time for bravado.
That's not bravado! My wounds can close on their own. It's my Resonance ability. The medics should go take care of other people in need!
Stop squirming, will you? We're here because you need our help. Calm down and stay where you are!
Please hold him still for me.
Sure...
After some chaos, you helped medics in treating the wounded.
A severely wounded soldier begs to return to battle, insisting that resources should be reserved for those in greater need. You treat him, despite his loud protests.
Have you confirmed the inventory? What about the spare list? Sort out the consumables as soon as possible. Check our communication lines while you're at it...
Yue, deliver this list to Ase. Oh, you're not Yue. Where is she? What do you need?
You seem very busy.
Do you need our help?
(Tell him about the person Jianxin's looking for.)
Master Jianxin, do you want to go look for Zhiyuan first?
Jinzhou is the gateway to Huanglong, and the Desorock Highland is the gateway to Jinzhou. A single breach could have dire consequences. Our defense must hold at all costs.
The Tacet Discords are not humans. They don't do truces or ceasefires. For as long as they exist, this war will rage on endlessly.
Supply is the lifeblood of our army, and I am tasked with keeping it flowing. But now, we are facing a shortage.
I saw you help arrange the wounded there. Xiulan would need your help more than I do.
Thank you, but I must remain to oversee vital military supplies.
Jianxin asked the quartermaster about Zhiyuan's whereabouts.
Zhiyuan...
So he never sent a letter home? Not even once?

The Midnight Rangers are no longer recruiting non-Resonators lately, but Zhiyuan was a stubborn boy. Last year when the battles hadn't gotten so intense, he would trail us Rearguards, eager to join the frontline.
We sent him back to the city, time and time again, and he just kept finding ways to come back. Eventually I caved and took him in to help us here at the base.

With the battle escalating, it's getting increasingly dangerous out here. I shouldn't keep him here any longer. I was just thinking about having the logistics team bring him back to the city when you guys showed up.
Oh, now I remember. He should be currently on the floor above.
What... what are you doing!
What's going on?
(Hold your hands up.)
Oh... Please excuse me. Thought that was a grenade... Is this... a mangosteen?
A grenade?
What do you know about the mangosteen?
It's a type of old-fashioned explosive. The Lament caused a global technological regression and shortage of resources.
While Tacetite Weapons were being developed, most people had limited knowledge of Tacetite as an energy source. As a result, primitive products combining old and new technology emerged.
The hand grenade was one of them. With the rapid growth of Tacetite Weapons, these crude explosives were eventually phased out in favor of more advanced weaponry.

Well... it's not a local fruit, so we can only get it through imports. But, with the recent Tacet Discord outbreaks, we've had to prioritize bringing in the essentials. We'll get back to importing more of these after General Jiyan makes his triumphant return.
Excuse me. I'm an Outrider of the Midnight Rangers. This is Rover, and this is Master Jianxin who came here to look for someone.
Sure. Please excuse me. I'll join you later.
We'll be meeting up with you.
We'll be there soon.
(Take out the mangosteen.)
Thank you.
Currently, there's only one waterway open, from Port Gunchao in the <color=Highlight>south</color> of the city. The Rearguards would regularly go there to escort goods.
Hmm... What more do I know... The military rarely buys this fruit for rations due to its short shelf life. Plus, it looks too much like a grenade, and that could cause some issues.
Jianxin did a brief salute and left.

The quartermaster reveals Zhiyuan's likely whereabouts. Jianxin leaves to continue her search for Zhiyuan. You show the quartermaster the mangosteen, which he mistakes for a grenade. After the misunderstanding is resolved, he tells you about the dire situation in the Norfall Barrens.
Hah... hah...
Are you alright?
I'm okay... just... a little... out of breath...
You don't seem okay.
It's okay... I'm fine...
I'll go find a medic.
You brought the medic over to take care of Xinyu.
A wounded soldier is in distress. You summon a medic to his side.
Thank you for your assistance. You must be tired. Please take some rest.
They look badly injured...
Don't worry. They've received proper treatment now. They will recover in time. Thanks to General Jiyan, we've seen a significant drop in the number of casualties.
I've heard from veterans that our soldiers used to be ordinary people, not Resonators. The battles were even brutal back then, with the stench of blood lingering through the rain.
But things have improved.
Each injury represents countless Tacet Discords eliminated by our brave soldiers.
Resonators in the Midnight Rangers are incredible warriors. Those who have to retreat from injury must have already taken out hundreds of enemies.
They are our heroes.
They are the ones keeping our people safe. What I've been doing is not worth mentioning compared to them.
Please don't put it like that. Without your help. we couldn't have helped so many wounded soldiers in such a short time.
Now that they are all safe, you should go and take care of your own issues.
Thank you. May I ask where the quartermaster is?
The quartermaster isn't here. He's on the floor above, directing munitions distribution. Just take that lift and you should find him there.
Rover, where are we going next?
Let's follow Master Jianxin.
I want to talk to the quartermaster, too.
Here are some recipes for dietary supplements from my sect. They might help the wounded recover sooner.
Oh? Great. You have my thanks.
With the soldiers tended to, you start looking for the quartermaster as advised.
Rover?
According to Baizhi, the leaf showed residual fluctuations of Tacet Discords.
Those fluctuations pointed to a certain set of coordinates.
And that is... Qichi Village, in the Central Plains.
Inspired by Yangyang's words, you close your eyes and tap into your intuition, pinpointing the last token's location: Qichi Village in the Central Plains.
Master Jianxin, have you found the person you're looking for?
Yes, I've found Zhiyuan. We will return to the city with the logistics team. We will go find Mr. Zongye to let him know he is safe.
I heard Zhiyuan didn't want to leave?
I see. Farewell, Master Jianxin.
Zhiyuan is a man full of courage. Influenced by his veteran grandpa's tales, he longs to join the military and aid in humanity's battle against Tacet Discords.
The journey with you has exposed me to immense suffering, but the battles on the frontline must be even more brutal than what I've witnessed.
Countless lives have been lost in this war...
Master Rongfu once told me, "The best sages gain enlightenment in the military, the mediocre sages gain enlightenment in the bustling cities, and the worst sages gain enlightenment in seclusion."
I do share some of Zhiyuan's feelings.

However, Zhiyuan disagreed with the intense training and tests required to join the military. He saw no distinction between ordinary people and Resonators, and believed he could contribute on the battlefield, however small that contribution might be.
I agree with him.
Everyone has a part to play.
He's only causing trouble by staying on the battlefield.
He can contribute better without fighting on the frontlines.

I, too, found what Zhiyuan said was reasonable to an extent, and I couldn't change his mind with words. So I tried to imagine what my masters would do. They'd set up a spar in this case. And if I won, they'd let me do what I wanted.
So you beat him up?
Anything that works for you, I guess.
You pretended to lose.
You won.
"The shape changes, but not the forms; the more it moves, the more it yields. Less thinking, more knowing. Simplify for clarity.”
Yes, I pretended to lose, but Zhiyuan saw it through.
After our fight, Zhiyuan admitted he saw the gap between Resonators and ordinary people. He seemed to realize how he was still far from being able to fight the Tacet Discords.

He realized how he was just trying to convince himself that he could make a difference, not wanting to acknowledge his own limitations. Fighting on the battlefield requires physical and mental strength, and he was not yet prepared for that.
"All tangles untied, all glare tempered, all dust smoothed. It is like a deep pool that never dries. ” How true! I've come to understand this line more.
I promised not to use my Forte in the battle, but Zhiyuan still couldn't take a single blow from me.

After his defeat, Zhiyuan seemed to realize his weakness. Talking about confronting the Tacet Discords on the battlefield would be mere lip service, he said. He was just trying to convince himself that he could make a difference, not wanting to acknowledge his own limitations.
I heard you two still have other matters to attend to. When you have the time, let's catch up at Liuxian Teahouse.
It's my great pleasure to have met you.
Farewell.
See you.
I didn't mean to beat him up for nothing. My masters taught me valuable lessons through sparring, and I gained important insights from those fights. Now, who do you think won that fight?

Reuniting with Jianxin, you learn she has successfully found Zhiyuan and convinced him to return to Jinzhou. This journey has been enlightening for her, and she looks forward to seeing you and Yangyang again.
What's the matter? Are you alright?
I... I had a vision.
I was worried... You just stood there and gazed into the distance. You were unresponsive when I tried talking to you. What did you see?
It felt as if I was seeing through the eyes of a Tacet Discord. I think... I saw what was happening in the Norfall Barrens.
(Describe the general in teal first.)

An imposing warrior wielding the power of a <ano=teal dragon>Qingloong</ano>...  The Qingloong is the Midnight Rangers' emblem. It's also the symbol of General Jiyan, the leader of all Midnight Rangers.
The front lines are not far from here. General Jiyan must be there, fighting alongside our soldiers to keep the Tacet Discords away.
But I've never met him.
It doesn't seem like a coincidence. We arrived near the battlefield right when General Jiyan was leading an attack against the Tacet Discords...
A woman in red who can control the Tacet Discords...
The battle itself is a clear sign of an anomaly.
The Streams from the Norfall Barrens feel more suffocating than ever.
Rover... something on that battlefield must be connected to you, though we have no idea what it is.
I may have resonated with a Tacet Discord.
(Describe the woman in red first.)
Could it be... One of the Fractsidus...
Your vision... It might be what was happening on the battlefield not far away...
It's real.
Something's not right.
There's something inside me.
There's always been a voice.
Resonate with Tacet Discords...?
But I didn't hear anything... or sense any frequencies.

Little lambs cowered and huddled in their village, terrified of the relentless wolf packs.
Until a shepherd arrived, bearing the gift of wishes and providing shelter and sustenance.
Slowly, the shepherd gained control over the flock, and the lambs lived contented lives... but this is not the end of our story.
The shepherd found the solitary black lamb in his flock, and offered to grant any wish it desired. In exchange, he wanted one of its companions as a sacrifice.
The black lamb refused, and it was shunned by its flock, left without shelter or sustenance.
After the black lamb's exile, more lambs continued to vanish...

From the very beginning, the lambs knew the risk of making wishes—they too could become sacrifices for those of others.
