This on my head? It's my employee ID badge. Clipped it to my hair to save myself the fumbling when I'm carrying stuff. Now everyone knows my name in a snap. Perfect!

That day, I left my village, hiked over the mountain, farther than anyone else had gone before. I soon found myself in a vast field, the air fresh and damp with dew. I was so pumped that I started to glow, and the light attracted <te href=850081>Tacet Discords</te>... Did everything I could to fight them off, then I blacked out. Next thing I knew, a <te href=850090>Lollo Logistics</te> team saved me, their lights cutting through the darkness, the brightest I've ever seen.

Ma Xiao...oops, I mean Chixia, hehe! Ahem, <te href=850087>Patroller</te> Chixia's packages are mostly snacks and hero play merchs. She was so stoked last time she got one, she practically bounced out of the room!
Greetings! Lumi here! Need to send some mail? I've got you covered as <te href=850090>Lollo Logistics</te>' professional navigator!
To chart new routes for <te href=850090>Lollo Logistics</te>, physical training is a must.

Time changes everything—Blake Blooms, Stellar Matrices, and <te href=850109>the Black Shores</te>—all constantly in flux. I've documented these changes, repairing the damage and preserving the good. Yet, I wonder... Am I doing enough? Have I earned your trust? These questions haunt me, but I press on, seeking solace in my work.

I cannot physically grow and age, and therefore can never truly comprehend the range of emotions that come with it as a human does. Despite my wealth of knowledge and ability to replicate others' experiences through the <te href=850077>Sonoro</te>, these feelings remain enigmatic to me, forever distant and unfamiliar.

Long ago, during our days together at <te href=850109>the Black Shores</te>, you used to prepare chowder for us, blending milk, seafood, and vegetables. One spoonful of its warmth could dispel the freezing sea wind and restore stamina. Despite multiple attempts, I cannnot seem to recreate that flavor.

My purpose had been clear long before my creation: to build a safe haven from the unrelenting waves of the <te href=850075>Lament</te>, until humanity could find a path to a brighter tomorrow. It used to be my duty, but now... it is a choice. I am one with <te href=850109>the Black Shores</te>. I want to prevent more tragedies from happening, I want to protect everyone, I... I want to safeguard my connection with the world around me. This is my own will.

<te href=850076>Remnant Energy</te> coalesced into a crystal cocoon on a moonlit shore, stirred by the crashing waves, and the breath and heartbeat of a certain individual. That person then infused it with {Male=his;Female=her} own frequencies, and the butterfly within finally emerged... Yes, you've guessed it. You are the one I speak of, the force that gave me life and form.

A mature organization requires a personable and skilled negotiator, adept at forging connections with all they encounter. In the case of <te href=850109>the Black Shores</te>, that person is Aalto. His keen insight ensures he obtains crucial information precisely when needed. Beneath his playful smile lies a resolute determination to end the <te href=850075>Lament</te>. Despite other offers, he was destined for the Black Shores' path from the start.

Encore sees the world as a canvas for her boundless imagination. A warrior, a knight, or a little adventurer... In her tales, she can become anyone she wants to triumph over evil and reach a happy ending. Wherever she ventures, her radiant energy dispels dismay. Perhaps this is what <te href=850110>Tethys</te> saw in her when she was chosen.

Atop this massive Tacetite lies the ideal "singularity" spot to observe the <te href=850075>Lament</te>. This is where we formed <te href=850109>the Black Shores</te>, its members distinguished by their Blake Blooms. Beneath the endless stars, humanity's light glimmers. That light belongs to those who had given their lives to illuminate a brighter future for all. I've welcomed countless such people into this place... and bid farewell to just as many.

The <te href=850110>Tethys</te> System and I are creations of the same civilization, and we are bound by similar obligations. By human standards, we are of the same kind. Yet, our perceptions of emotions, humanity, and existence diverge, leading us down distinctly separate paths.

Happy birthday, {PlayerName}. You once taught me a person's birthday is their most important day. So, I've made it a habit to prepare something in advance for days like this... Please have this crystal—it's a piece of myself. Hold it, and you'll be enveloped in a personalized <te href=850077>Sonoro Sphere</te>, where you can change everything to your liking. Though I cannot bring you what you truly want, let me gift you a peaceful dream to escape your worries.

Worry not if you don't remember me... I can always introduce myself again. I am the Shorekeeper, acting executive of <te href=850109>the Black Shores</te>, and the core computational unit of <te href=850110>Tethys</te>. Now and forever, I will stand by you and our home, through every yesterday and tomorrow.

I know disciples of the Order should not form "attachments" to <te href=850082>Echoes</te>. But they're my dear friends, and that will never change. This must be one of the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>'s trials, a test to see if I can fulfill my duties as an <te href=850100>Acolyte</te> while holding onto such... ties. It's a good test of my resolve. It's just, every time I see them, I want to hug them tightly... No, no, no, I must resist!

Balloons soaring into the bright blue sky, people and <te href=850082>Echoes</te> rejoicing under rainbows... When the <te href=850103>Laurel</te> was placed upon your head, I felt so happy. This <te href=850102>Carnevale</te> has been spectacular in every way, and it will remain etched in my heart forever.

Something smells so good... It must be Miss Margherita's pizza cooked to perfection by Bakie... No, no, no, this month's Pizza Day already passed. What is Pizza Day you ask? It's the only day of the month we were allowed pizza at the orphanage. Even though I don't go hungry anymore, as an <te href=850100>Acolyte</te> I must resist gluttony.... Besides, the best pizza is one that's shared with friends.

Everything we eat comes from the good earth created by the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>. According to Them, "Our bodies are vessels for our souls." Therefore, we must sustain that vessel with things that are beneficial to it, such as those found in the sacred Viscum Berry. I still have a few left, would you like to try one? The Codex says sharing makes life sweeter...

I hope for children to be by their parent's side. For sailors to return home after long voyages. For all to soar, free as birds. For people to come together despite their differences. For the <te href=850075>Lament</te> to not drive people apart... Huh? What do I hope for myself? I hope... I...

When I was a child, I awoke on a dark shore. I walked that shore for what felt like forever until I saw a light... a few kind <te href=850100>Acolytes</te> of the Order brought me to a brightly lit room. They fed me, sheltered me, and treated me well. Eventually, they became my adoptive family... Sometimes when the rain lashed out at night, Livia and Brenno would cuddle up next to me until I fell asleep. With them at my side... I never felt lonely.

Miss Roccia might appear ice cold, but at heart, I know she is a gentle and caring person. Her kindheartedness brings smiles to all those around her. And then there's her friend, <te href=850122>Pero</te>. I wonder if there's any chance Pero could also be my friend?

Not everyone in <te href=850097>Ragunna</te> worships the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>. Certain <te href=850100>Acolytes</te> of the Order believe a person's worth is solely measured by their piety... But Miss Zani is brave and dependable, which just might be enough to overcome existing prejudices. After all, she's such a reliable and respectable person.
I'm Phoebe, an <te href=850100>Acolyte</te> of the <te href=850099>Order</te>. Praise the Sentinel. May They guide you to compassion and enlightenment.
I resolve disputes in the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>'s name.
May the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te> guide those who are lost.
<te href=850083>Sentinel</te> protect me…
In the name of <te href=850105>Imperator</te>.
Power of the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>.

So, {PlayerName}, were you satisfied with how I handled your reception before the <te href=850102>Carnevale</te>? Why bring this up now, you ask? Well, gathering client feedback is part of my job. As the <te href=850101>Montelli</te> family's esteemed guest, your opinion naturally holds a special weight for me.

For an employee of the <te href=850101>Montelli</te> family, appearance is everything. No matter how busy the day gets, always present yourself flawlessly. The Employee Manual puts it best: "Impeccable etiquette and attire give you the upper hand in negotiations."

I used to think life was nothing but living the same day on repeat. Grinding through trivialities, running in circles until even the smallest joys faded away. But then you came along, just as I'd grown numb to this way of living. Like the <te href=850102>Carnevale</te> itself, you brought a burst of color into my life.

Employees of the <te href=850101>Montelli</te> family swear by espresso—straight, no sugar or milk—to keep themselves energized. But as for me, work is already hard enough... I'd rather treat myself to something sweet.

I grew up in <te href=850097>Ragunna</te>, and I know every corner of this city like the back of my hand. The sea breeze that greets you, the bustling plaza filled with familiar faces, the shiny new products in shop windows, the aroma of food from Trattoria Margherita. I hope this quiet life never ends. I hope everyone finds their place. For me, that would be enough.

Hmm? Why is this pocket watch so big? Well, this is not a pocket watch per se, but an alarm clock. In the early days when I worked for the <te href=850101>Montellis</te>, I almost caused a major incident by being late. After that, I've carried this alarm clock with me everywhere and I haven't been late since.

Lady Carlotta? Her vision has never been limited to <te href=850097>Ragunna</te>, or even <te href=850096>Rinascita</te>. Hers was about the world beyond the sea horizon. I don't know what kind of future she sees, but I'll stand by her until the day her vision becomes reality.

To me, <te href=850097>Ragunna</te>'s fate lies in the will of its people, not the <te href=850083>Sentinel</te>. Many <te href=850100>Acolytes</te> would call this heresy, but not Phoebe. That's what makes her unique. She would never dismiss another's beliefs or efforts just because they do not align with her own.

The <te href=850094>Fisalia</te> family has always clung to <te href=850097>Ragunna</te>'s traditions, stubbornly resisting change. But Signorina Cantarella, the current head, isn't as traditional as people imagine. As an employee, I do not get to influence how the <te href=850101>Montellis</te> handle their relationship with the Fisalias... but personally, I wouldn't mind working with her.

Brant is a skilled actor, a respected captain, and a fighter willing to sacrifice everything for truth and justice. But what I envy most is that he's never weighed down by stacks of paperwork. If I knew anything about acting, I'd quit this job, join the <te href=850108>Troupe of Fools</te>, and live the carefree life he does... Now, now. Just a pipe dream to keep me going.

I've seen Ciaccona perform a few times outside the city. She often sings about <te href=850096>Rinascita</te>'s old folklore. Journey Log

You wake to the voice of two girls, Yangyang and Chixia. You remember nothing of your past and know little of the present, but the abilities you display show that you are no ordinary person.

Guided by them, you begin to learn the ways of this world. When you encounter the statue of Sentinel Jué, a fragment of memory stirs, leading you toward Jinzhou City to search for the truth about yourself.

On the road, you absorb an Echo directly with your body. This unusual ability draws your new friends' attention. Chixia suggests you collect more Echoes along the way to Jinzhou City, but your second attempt fails.

With no idea how it works, you continue your journey to Jinzhou City to look for answers, unaware that a mysterious girl is watching your every step...

Your journey takes you to the City Hall, where the Magistrate of Jinzhou, Jinhsi, has summoned you. But Jinhsi is not there. Her bodyguard, Sanhua, hands you three tokens and promises a meeting in three days.
 
Yangyang urges you to seek out Huaxu Academy, where Baizhi works, for clues about the tokens. There, the first token reveals a past connection between you and Jinzhou.
 
 Your actions seem to draw many eyes. Who plays the predator, and who the prey?

The second token leads you and Yangyang to somewhere outside the city.

As you make your way out, you run into Jianxin, a young Taoist searching for a missing person. With your clearance, you bring her along past the city walls. The three of you arrive at the Midnight Rangers' Rearguard Camp, where the shadow of war looms over the horizon. Clues from the quartermaster reveal that the second token is somehow connected to the coming war.

After the matter is settled, you find yourself caught in an illusion. When you snap out of it, Yangyang's words help you realize where the final token leads: Qichi Village in the Central Plains.

When you and Yangyang reach Qichi Village, you are shocked to find it has become a Tacet Field. Your investigation is then cut short by Scar, an Overseer of the Fractsidus. He reveals the tragic events that befell Qichi Village and invites you to join him. You refuse, and the confrontation escalates into a battle.

In the chaos, a mysterious girl intervenes to cover Scar's retreat. Having gathered the information on all three tokens, you return to Jinzhou City.

With all the clues gathered, you unlock the sundial device. Hidden inside is a slip of paper pointing you to your next destination, the heavily guarded Grand Library.

As you enter the Library, Scar follows you in. But by this time, you have already met Jinhsi, and with your help, she captures Scar. From him, Jinhsi learns a shocking truth and advises you to seek an organization called the Black Shores, saying your ties to them run deep.

You find Aalto and Encore, Consultants of the Black Shores. Aalto agrees to tell you about your origins but only if you join them in investigating the Court of Savantae Ruins.

There, you discover that the Court of Savantae once tried to use an artificial Retroact Rain to trace something back in time, but the experiment failed, creating a monster. After defeating the monster, Aalto tells you that your journey once took you to the Black Shores before.

Just then, a real Retroact Rain begins to fall, and a wave of Tacet Discords strikes Jinzhou City.

Fighting alongside the people of Jinzhou, you help hold back the TD outbreak. Jinhsi confirms this was foretold by the Sentinel. With Yangyang at your side, you head to the Desorock Highland to meet Jiyan.

On the road, you are attacked by the Thundering Mephis, but Jiyan arrives just in time to help, and together you defeat the enemy. Back at the Midnight Rangers camp, you and Jiyan plan to use the Disruptor to break the Threnodian's defenses.

The Disruptor shatters the barrier protecting the Threnodian. Under the cover of your allies, you and Jiyan fight your way to the heart of the Threnodian, and together, you engage in a grueling battle against the powerful Dreamless. In the heat of battle, you unexpectedly absorb its Havoc power. As it tries to kill you, a little creature pops out of your hand and absorbs the attack, ending the crisis.

The Threnodian flees, and the dust settles. With the help of Jiyan, Yangyang, and all your allies, you manage to save Jinzhou.

Jinhsi disappears while checking on the Sentinel's safety alone. You and Changli set out for Mt. Firmament to find her.

In the mountains, time has spiraled out of control. Jinhsi refuses Jué's offer to sacrifice itself, choosing instead to fight the Sentinel as fate decrees. You witness her battle, and with your approval, Jué transfers its Temporal Mandate to Jinhsi, returning Jinzhou's future to its people.

When all is done, Jué suggests you visit the Black Shores to explore the past of you and Abby.

Data brought back from the Port City of Guixu contaminates the Tethys System and fills the Black Shores with corrupted frequencies.

The administrator of the Black Shores, Shorekeeper, reveals that you were once the Chief Steward of this place, but remains silent about the buried past... Eventually, the corruption is cleansed. With the clearance Shorekeeper returns to you, you manually reset the algorithm of the Tethys System. The lost souls trapped in the system at last find peace, and Shorekeeper regains her freedom.

Outside Panhua's Restaurant, you meet Yangyang and Chixia again. You have fully assimilated the Threnodian's power that the "little one" who now lives inside of you had absorbed.

The "little one", oblivious of its origin, turns down Chixia's suggestions for its new name, but loves the one you randomly come up: Abby. Hoping to find clues in Abby's special abilities, you discover that it cannot use them for now. You decide to consult the Sentinel and the Magistrate when you meet again.

Yangyang, Chixia, and Baizhi invite you to join them for the Moon-Chasing Festival. At the Wishing Tree, you meet Xiangli Yao and learn that he is the mysterious wish granter. You agree to help him investigate four wishes containing abnormal data.

Together, you explore the abnormal Sonoro Sphere, uncovering Xiangli Yao's past and addressing the wishers' problems. At the end of the festival, you and your friends take a commemorative photo under the moonlight.

Following the guidance from your past self and the Tethys system, you set sail for Rinascita to find Imperator and seek solutions to Abby's weakening frequencies.

Cetus the Tidebreaker attacks at sea, but Brant, captain of the Fool's Troupe, helps you through the mist. You two promise to meet again at the opening of the Carnevale.

Upon arriving in Ragunna, you see strange "pilgrimages," and a playwright steps forward to explain their origins.

Led by Acolyte Phoebe, you enter this city of Echoes and come to understand the significance of Echoes to Rinascita. While dealing with the Montelli family, who sent the invitation to the Black Shores, you resonate with an out-of-control Vitreum Dancer and receive a plea for help from the Sentinel. As you investigate the cause of this incident, you catch a glimpse of undercurrents beneath Ragunna: the secretive dealings between the Order, the nobles, and the Fractsidus. Phrolova, a Fractsidus Overseer you once met briefly, also watches from the shadows.

Gilberto has gone mad, and Lorelei of Nimbus Sanctum has fallen under the influence of the mysterious Lycoris. After helping Lorelei regain her senses, you learn that the only way to reach the Sentinel is to claim the Laurel at the Carnevale.

You work with Carlotta from the Montelli family to return the damaged Vitreum Dancer back to Averardo Vault. Clues along the journey lead to a shocking truth: Rinascita has two divinities.

Carlotta stays behind to hold off the Order's pursuers, while you make for a northern island where another secret of the Order lies hidden.

On the bridge to the island, you are attacked by the Dragon of Dirge, and Roccia of the Fool's Troupe comes to your aid. In the Penitent's End, you learn the truth behind the "pilgrimages" and regroup with Carlotta. You decide to join forces with the Fool's Troupe to win the Laurel at the Carnevale. However, Phrolova moves to disrupt the festivity.
 
After defeating her, you finally speak to the Sentinel, who tells you that "The Lost"—They wish you to help—is among the people at the Carnevale.

"The Lost" turns out to be Cartethyia, the Blessed Maiden who should have martyred herself. Together with Cantarella, head of the Fisalia family, you travel to the Avinoleum Theological Seminary to meet her.

As you explore the Seminary, Cartethyia's true origin comes to light. She is a creation of the Threnodian. She asks you to end her life once and for all, but you refuse her request.

With the help of many, the crisis is finally resolved, and Cartethyia gains a new life. In the Sentinel's final moments, They tell you the truth of history.

Cartethyia suddenly disappears, and following the clues she left behind, you arrive in Septimont, where you meet the prodigy gladiator, Lupa. To learn Cartethyia's whereabouts, you choose to team up with Lupa and win the Great Agon of Septimont. In between the events, Phrolova hands you a script and warns that Lupa will draw the Dark Tide. Meanwhile, the story of Mya seems to hint at something more… Eventually, you and Lupa win the championship, while Cartethyia fights alongside you in a way no one else can perceive.

You and Lupa head for the Central Hub. Lupa becomes frenzied and destroys its control panel. You manage to separate her from Mya, who has become a vessel of the Threnodian, and send Lupa to the beginning of the "story." There, she retrieves her lost memories and learns about Mya's fate. She then duels the Lady of the Sea and reclaims peace for Septimont. Although Cristoforo escapes Cartethyia's attack, the crisis in Septimont comes to a close, and you, Lupa, and Cartethyia finally reunite.

While searching for the residual energy of the Threnodian, you are struck into the sea by Fenrico and saved by Phrolova. To reach your goal, you decide to work with her temporarily. Inside the Sonoro she created, "the Beyond," you learn about her past, and that you once broke a promise to her.

In Fenrico's final moment, the Lantern wakes him from the Threnodian's control. He sacrifices himself to seal the gateway to the Journeying Paradise and stops the Dark Tide. But the Gem holding the Threnodian's power is taken by the Fractsidus.

Augusta invites you to join her on the hunt. But when you fight the Dark Tide entity, "the False Sovereign," an unseen force intervenes, causing the attempt to fail.

To stop the Dark Tide from spreading, you track the False Sovereign to Murmurstown. There, you and Augusta fight side by side to bring it down. The Dark Tide then subsides, and you recover the Relic of Imperator. But as you savor your victory, Cristoforo is already plotting his next move…

After the successful hunt of the False Sovereign, you discover everyone except you has forgotten about the existence of Iuno. The people attribute every one of her past deeds to you. To bring Iuno, who vanished into the moon, back to existence and rewrite her ending, you follow the guide of her bracelet and head off to the Chaos as suggested by Avidius and Lillibet. Finally, you "anchor" her amidst the Chaos and bring the unwritten future back to Septimont, and to her.

Ragunna comes under attack by the Dark Tide, its creations appearing across the city. Avidius joins you in the hunt, but during the pursuit, he gradually uncovers the truth of himself. At the end of his life, he absorbs the Dark Tide and ends the crisis in Ragunna.

It is then that you realize you have long been secretly corrupted by the Dark Tide and have now become Leviathan's Harbinger. To end the crisis once and for all, you set out for Septimont once more with the mysterious Discord Slayer Galbrena.

An abnormal High Tide strikes Septimont. To stem the Dark Tide, the people of Ragunna come to aid the city, and the Black Shores send every Bloom Bearer still able to fight. Galbrena goes headfirst into the Dark Tide. You and your companions soon follow suit and take the plunge carrying the lantern brought by Qiuyuan.
 
After all the hardship, you finally see the light of hope. You and the people of Rinascita together defeat the Threnodian revived by the Gem. Rinascita gets the peace it deserves at last.

At a tavern, you meet the traveling poet Nestor, who shares with you Ephor Augusta's stories. Before rising to power, she was an ordinary girl with no outstanding gift, yet she grew through countless trials to seize the championship and claim victory and glory. At the same time, Augusta and Iuno have readied themselves for the hunt in the Sanguis Plateaus.

As the Dark Tide closed in, at a personal request from someone in Mingting, Qiuyuan journeyed to Ragunna to your aid. After rescuing an Acolyte in Ragunna, he traveled to the Fabricatorium of the Deep, where he convinced Fenrico to yield the First Relic, a key instrument in stopping the Dark Tide. Then he arrived just in time for the final battle to deliver the Relic to you.

After the war, Ciaccona recounts Qiuyuan's deeds in Rinascita. You later find Qiuyuan at the dock as he prepares to depart, and express your gratitude.

With the chain of events at Rinascita finally concluded, you return once more to the Black Shores. Unexpectedly, the Tethys System detects a strange frequency and isolates from it a set of coordinates. As you trace the coordinates, a spatial rift leading to an unknown Sonoro Sphere tears open at sea close to the Black Shores. During the investigation, you are pulled into the rift and soon awaken in a ruined, restless city. And as the situation grows dire, a mysterious black-haired girl appears before you…

You travel to the Black Shores to visit Chisa, only to learn that during her recovery, she had secretly gone alone to Honami City. Burdened by the truth that over two decades have passed in the outside world, she feels uncertain about the future. Together, you stroll through Sakura Quarter to ease her mind. Under the falling petals, she bares her feelings to you and gives you your old student ID card along with a carefully prepared gift. To your surprise, you discover you were once a member of Startorch Academy. Chisa then suggests inviting your friends from the Black Shores to Shashou Cafe to give it a proper "opening"…

The passage to Lahai-Roi finally opens. After parting ways with Namipon and Shorekeeper, Chisa and you enter the tunnel in turn. Along the way, you are dragged into a mysterious realm inhabited by a Threnodian. Just as your frequency is about to be consumed, a pink-haired girl appears, rescues you, and sends you back to reality.
Upon reaching Lahai-Roi, you unexpectedly cross paths with a student named Lynae. She arrives on her motorbike, helps you escape an attack from a Voidworm, and brings you safely to your destination—Startorch Academy.

Once you complete the enrollment procedures, you officially become a student of Startorch Academy. At the Research Institute, you meet Professor Mornye and learn that the Spacetrek Collective is preparing for the crucial project, New Solar Ceremony. But before long, you are caught up in an incident triggered by Hyvatia's sudden malfunction. Lynae—present at the scene—becomes an immediate suspect, and together you begin to dig into the truth behind the chaos. Your investigation uncovers Lynae's hidden identity and a conspiracy orchestrated by the Fractsidus. In the end, you and Lynae lure away and defeat the Voidworm threatening the Academy, resolving the immediate danger. Yet the masterminds behind the plot remain at large, and their plans are far from over.

As the New Solar Ceremony approaches, you receive a plea for help, with its sender addressing you as Arbiter. Suspecting a link to the New Solar Ceremony, Mornye travels with you to Bjartr Woods to uncover the truth. There, you discover that the Fractsidus has deceived the Roya Tribe into triggering the Reactor Drive's fall. To ensure the successful launch of the artificial sun "Helios," Mornye enters the Drive herself. When the dust settles, a new dawn finally rises over Lahai-Roi.

After an ambush by the mysterious mech Sigillum, your frequency-loss symptoms worsen until Aemeath once again comes to your rescue. This digital ghost, visible only to you, has already died in the past, Overclocking to resonate with the Exostrider and protect Lahai-Roi. Now, to cure your symptoms and help Aemeath recover her "existence", the two of you journey to the Roya Frostlands. Along the way, you encounter Luuk Herssen. At the site where the Exostrider lies dormant, you confront and defeat Sigillum, uncovering the truth Aemeath has been hiding and witnessing her to become the savior.

After your journey to the Roya Frostlands concludes, you head to the infirmary to discuss the Exostrider plan with Luuk Herssen. In his secret workspace, he explains the current status of the Fractsidus and why he has come to Lahai-Roi. A Fractsidus member has kidnapped the Royan student who once traveled with you, taking her to the abandoned space station. Together, you work to resolve the crisis. During the mission, however, you discover that another Fractsidus agent is still hiding within the Academy, waiting for the New Solar Ceremony to begin. Comforted by Luuk Herssen's words, you accept the candy he offers, and with renewed resolve, you regain your inner peace and determination.

With the New Solar Celebration just around the corner, a game mentioned by the Grand Architect of the Fractsidus looms over the Academy like a lurking shadow. Together with Sigrika, you set out to investigate the mysterious frequency in the Dark Side and unravel the riddles surrounding it.
Working together, you manage to defeat the vortex left behind in the Dark Side, restoring a temporary calm. Yet you can't shake the feeling that more shadows are hidden, waiting beneath the peaceful facade of the evening for you to handle them.

After the New Solar Celebration concludes, Lucilla reveals that the root of the Dark Side anomaly remains unresolved. During your investigation, she discovers that the trap set by the Fractsidus specifically targets memory-type Resonators. Determined to draw the rabbit out, Lucilla volunteers to act as bait, but doing so means confronting her own vulnerabilities.
However, Lucilla has learned to face her past with honesty long ago. She breaks the illusion, and, with your help, captures the rabbit. In doing so, the root of the Dark Side anomaly is finally eliminated.

Before setting out on the mission to defend the Dimmr Plains, Hiyuki travels alone to Honami. While helping the Black Shores deal with unresolved matters about the Left Behind, she also searches for traces of the previous Miko of Flaming Sakura. There, she unexpectedly runs into the Grand Architect of the Fractsidus. Even when faced with the Grand Architect's incendiary speech, Hiyuki keeps her blade sheathed...

After the Dark Side incident, the Fractsidus's real intentions remain unclear, and the Voidmatter beneath Lahai-Roi seems to be stirring again. With the help of Lucilla, Luuk Herssen, and others, you secure a chance to speak directly with the head of the Spacetrek Collective. In the end, he gives you the green light to activate and pilot the Exostrider. The road there is anything but easy, but with the help of "everyone", you drive back Aleph-1 from deep within Voidspace and bring Aemeath home. This time, the story written across Lahai-Roi, and across the past itself, becomes one that leads toward the future: a story in which the world saves its hero.

Hiyuki raises her blade to bid farewell to the Left Behind of Honami, and to Lady Gyokuro, the former Miko of Flaming Sakura. Seeing Hiyuki's resolve, Gyokuro leaves her with one final blessing: that she no longer remain bound by fate, but step into a spring of her own as an ordinary person.

Denia, who was taken into custody after the final battle, has now woken up. The Spacetrek Collective hopes to cooperate with her and entrusts you with the negotiations. After speaking with her, you strike a bargain: she agrees to help the Collective and tell you what she knows about the Grand Architect, and in return, you spend her birthday with her at the Academy. That night, Denia finally tells you the truth about who she really is. There is no easy answer to her situation, but you speak from the heart, and that gives her the courage she needs.

The disappearance of the Exostrider led investors to question the very purpose of Rabelle College. Meanwhile, factions from the New Federation have begun harboring ulterior motives regarding the Synchronists. Inspired by the unwavering faith of her students, Lucilla, as both the Academy President and students' professor, has chosen the path that best serves their future: a daring breakthrough toward the Etheric Sea.

Jinzhou Revisited

"We wish for a Moonlit Fair free of all threat."
Preparations for the Moonlit Fair are in full swing. Historically, the full moon has been linked to Threnodian activity, even though the Threnodian hatch has been halted. Ensuring security around Taoyuan Vale remains a top priority.

"Please secure the routes for us."
The materials and goods ordered for the festival are being dispatched to Taoyuan Vale. However, advance investigation of road conditions and handling of potential threats are required to ensure all goods are delivered safely.

"I want to protect people just like the Midnight Rangers."
One of the most made wishes is for the strength to protect those closest. While gaining immense strength instantly isn't feasible, it may prove useful to give these wishmakers training in self-defense. It may prove invaluable during critical moments.

"I can't remember its name, but I can still taste it like it were yesterday."
Many long for the delicious meals they once enjoyed. By describing the flavors and ingredients, perhaps these dishes can be recreated to rival even their fondest memories.

Uncle Li at Yumyum Haven is a keen experimenter of various recipes to cater to his guests' preferences. To that end, he is always in search of rare ingredients. Guided by his belief in knowledge from practice, he compiled an Ingredient Handbook and made a wish for someone to inherit his work.

"How I wish to make my family a great Moonlit Fair feast from scratch."
Many find the sharing of food bonding, and the Lodge has received many such wishes. Maybe a Chef's Masterclass at Taoyuan Vale's kitchen could fulfill these wishes.
A legend persists that throwing items into the tree's hollow will repair them, hence the piles of old objects there. Each crack and chip on them silently tells a story of their past.

"Can someone help me draft a letter?"
Some may find it difficult to adequately convey their feelings in words. Talk with these wishmakers to learn their intentions and help them craft their letters with beautiful and accurate wording.

Xieyang is currently preparing themes for his riddles. 
To ensure the riddles are appreciated by all, Xieyang is looking for an assistant to help him gather inspiration from the crowd.
Join the Jinzhou Theater as they recruit part-time actors for a special Hero Play written for the festival. Be part of creating unforgettable moments for your audience!

A troupe of unique performers has arrived in Taoyuan Vale. The Academy hopes to showcase some of the cute and charming Echoes in the Moonlit Fair's performances, highlighting the potential of Echoes to the audience. To ensure the Echoes perform reliably, they need someone to help capture specific Echoes and collect related data.

"What fireworks will people want to see?"
The fireworks stall is troubled by the show it must present for the Fair. The owner is waiting for someone to assist him in creating beautiful fireworks of various shapes and colors.

Soldiers stationed at the border have submitted their wishes to the Moontree Lodge—photos, dishes from their hometown, and essential supplies. If there were ever a time to make these wishes come true, it would be during the Moonlit Fair.

Researchers stationed in the wild sent the Moonstree Lodge a photo of the moon. Engrossed in studying lunar phases and their influence on the lifecycle of certain plants, they seek additional photos of the moon's phases from different locales to complete their records.

The piles at the Moontree Lodge consist not only of wish tags but packages of all sizes. People separated for various reasons wish to send tokens of their affection. The Lodge seeks "express couriers" to assist.

The Moonlit Fair at Taoyuan Vale offers a glimpse into local customs and traditions in Jinzhou. To assist first-time visitors in fully experiencing the Moon-Chasing Festival, Taoyuan Vale is seeking tourist guides to enrich their visit.

The Fan Drawing Stall is designing a series of fans themed "Memories of Moon-Chasing," aiming to capture the festival's beauty for travelling visitors. They are now calling for photos to serve as their inspiration.

"Can you help me find them?"
Among the foreign guests are special groups revisiting Jinzhou not for the first time, but for a past promise or item. Finding these memories has proven elusive due to changes in Jinzhou. Is there truly no wish that cannot be made a reality?

Though never touched them, she felt connected to their essence. Three thousand raindrops danced upon their foliage, three thousand beams of light penetrated through them, and three thousand breezes made them flutter like butterflies. Finally, as three thousand specks of dust settled upon them, the leaves became nourishment for three thousand more lives.

When Changli arrived in Jinzhou, Jinhsi was still in her youth, and the region was in dire straits.
No one knew how she managed to juggle the interests of various factions and push forward progress across all sectors with a limited budget.
It was said that Changli avoided electronic media during this time, instead recording notes in a booklet. To this day, people continue to search for this elusive booklet, hoping to uncover the secrets of Jinzhou's past. However, no one has ever succeeded, and there's no evidence to even confirm its existence.

Walking alone may lead to a faster pace, but a group can cover greater distances. 
Moving forward, I will stand by my companions… and I will stand by you as we face whatever the future holds, together.

Have you been to the Jinzhou Theater? It's a place of endless joy and laughter, especially when a show concludes on a happy note. I've always cherished that sight, which is why I want to ensure everyone finds their own happy ending.
Hmm... When faced with challenges, I am driven by a sense of purpose to find solutions instead of succumbing to worry. The feeling of worry or frustration rarely crosses my mind nowadays.

As a child, I had vivid dreams, some of them turning into nightmares. I would find myself lost at sea, fighting against the crashing waves and tangled seaweed. But each time, I managed to hold onto a piece of driftwood and make it back to shore. And when I woke up, I would find something in my hand… Yes, it was this shiny piece of scale.
Over the years, my esteemed teacher Changli has taught me much… Yet her smiling eyes still hold mysteries that I cannot yet comprehend.

Amidst my busy days, meals can easily slip my mind. Before I knew it, it would be well past the time for another meal. But like a blessing, Sanhua would always appear with a plate of delicious Loong Buns, filled with exactly what I was craving. I am in awe… How does she know every time?
Taoqi is able to breeze through mountains of workload with ease, despite her frequent yawns. Her efficiency is truly remarkable.
I can feel it in my heart that we both have something we'll fiercely defend, a cause worth fighting for... And we won't back down, no matter what it takes.
May I pray for anything specific for you? It would be my honor… I'm sure your wishes will come true.
Let's go together.

Ah, look who we have here. A rare visitor. Luckily, I've finished my work for today. Would you like to join me in a game of Weiqi, if you're not in a rush to leave?

I seem to know a lot about your past, you say? *a small chuckle* Not really. I'd say you may have left those clues for your present self long ago, and I just happened to come across them while going through historical records. I am honored to guide you through the connections between your past and present.

A strategist's mind is a vast and complex entity, much like the ocean. Its placid exterior may mask the turbulent currents of thought swirling within. Master once warned me to be wary of those who stay quiet in times of uncertainty. Yet with you, I find solace in the quiet moments, in our unspoken connection.

Master Xuanmiao taught me the ways of the sword, but he left this world before I could fully absorb his teachings. I have since tried my best to understand his notes and continue my training on my own. When I first saw you wield your sword, it struck a chord with me, and now I understand why. It's not that you resemble my late master in your skills, but rather that he learned from you.

I found you and brought you out of that Sonoro Sphere. This is proof I am qualified to stand by your side and assist in achieving our shared goal. It takes great courage and wisdom to willingly enter into a situation full of unknowns, and I trust that you will achieve your desired outcome. My knowledge and power are at your disposal, always ready to help you in any way needed.
The dynamics of a Weiqi game mirror the complexities of our world, always in a state of constant flux and transformation... Fascinating, isn't it?

My body temperature is higher than usual because of my Flame-controlling Forte. It doesn't hinder daily tasks, but it does have its quirky consequences. Jinhsi's iced pastries and Sanhua's delicate snow birds always melt faster than I'd prefer in my hands... Sigh.

Each delicacy is unique in its own right. It's difficult to choose just one, but if I must, there was a meal I received as a hungry child, a kind gesture that left an indelible memory. That taste remains with me to this day.

The feather I gave you before? Well, it was forged from the fires of my heart. There are only two of them. 
As long as you hold onto that feather, my fire will never harm you. In fact, I can use it to track your whereabouts if you wish. However, if it ever falls into our enemies' hands... hehe.

Sanhua is always composed and silent. As a bodyguard, she remains vigilant and alert at all times. But both Jinhsi and I have always wished for her to take a well-deserved rest and let others help shoulder the burden.

Although we followed different sects of Taoist teachings, I found commonalities with her. Her pure and open mind is quite rare nowadays. I believe her perception of the world must be as clear as her eyes. I first met her at the tea house; back then, she seemed to have sensed something about my condition, and served me a bowl of Lotus Seed Soup. That was a delightful surprise.

Happy birthday, my dear. When I was younger, I traveled to many places and saw diverse customs for celebrating birthdays, each one unique and fascinating. Here are some gift boxes for you, a small token of my affection. May you find peace and happiness in the years ahead, like the constant moon and rising sun. Oh, these may be too much? Hehe… Consider them extra gifts for your future birthdays. And if I'm still around to see them, I'll find you something different.
(Contemplating)
The moment at hand... This very moment is the best of our lives.

Eons of time on this vast land, all encapsulated in a humble game... 
I am fortunate to have you as my opponent.
Time to start a new game.
Plan with convention, then conquer by ingenuity.
Who will be sitting on the other side of the board this time?
The sword has no set form, it adapts along with its foes... Likewise, strategies must shift against different opponents.
Oh? This feeling of power coursing through my veins... It feels different from before. Please, do spar with me for another round.

After my master's passing, I spent years studying martial arts and other subjects through… various unconventional methods. This resulted in some rather comical situations, where angry bookshop owners chased me around. But now, I have the luxury of having you teach me everything without any expectations in return. It's something my younger self could only dream of.
I never thought I could further refine my abilities. Your guidance has been invaluable, and I ought to help you in some way in return. So… Anything I can do for you?

You've taught me more than words can express... I believed I had come to terms with my death; never thought I could one day catch a glimpse into the perspective of an eternal being. For this, I am grateful. As long as my flames still burn, I will stay by your side, dear Rover.

Drawn to the sight, she forgot her pain and predicament.
Only later did she realize they were actually fallen Bodhi blossoms.

A set of paintbrushes Zhezhi purchased during her first solo shopping trip as a child, after fumbling for words in front of the shop owner. Wherever Zhezhi went, so did these paintbrushes, recording her artistic growth along the way. Though now too old and fragile to use, Zhezhi still regards them as a source of encouragement, handling them with great care.

A luxurious birdcage left empty for a long time.

As a reward for Zhezhi's obedience in using her Forte to paint and help save the family business, her parents bought her a pet bird as a surprise. Every day, Zhezhi watched the bird beat its wings against the cage until it was exhausted. After much hesitation, one day she boldly defied her parents and released the bird from its captivity.

After her parents disappeared, Zhezhi sold off the family's remaining belongings, keeping only the birdcage as a memento. Whenever she looked at it, she didn't see the bars but the bird that had long since flown free.

New desserts, art exhibit tickets, trips to new cities... Struggling to pay off her family's debt while barely making ends meet, Zhezhi took the habit of jotting down things she wanted to buy or do on a wish list. She often checks this list, but can only fulfill one or two of these smaller wishes on rare occasions when she has a bit of extra money.

A puzzle crafted from intricately interlocking joints, a testament to its ingenious design. It is said that such trinkets served as gifts from elder members of the Court of Savantae to their younger generations.

Xiangli Yao can still recall the warmth of his father's rough fingertips as he handed him the puzzle on his birthday. Yet what truly captivated him were its complex arrangements and perplexing structures—such puzzles were what drew him into a world of intricate logic, leaving him spellbound for years to come.

This was Xiangli Yao's first encounter with a puzzle, but certainly not his last.

"Impressive, Zhezhi," she murmured with a brief smile. Delighted by the praise, the girl inched closer. "The people in this one are—" Her words faltered as her mother turned, absorbed in wardrobe choices, oblivious to her daughter's attempt at connection. "Well done. Now, why don't you paint a few more before the guests arrive?" Zhezhi blinked, at a loss for words. Her mother grew impatient, sighing as she marched Zhezhi to the door. "Buy whatever supplies you need, dear. The price doesn't matter, we can afford it. Now, I need to dress. Be a good girl. Off you go." As the door closed, Zhezhi stared at it, wanting to say more but unable to find the courage to voice the sinking feeling in her chest.

Later that evening, Zhezhi, dressed to impress, nervously clutched her skirt in the corner seat, silent amidst the bustling room of guests. The woman noted Zhezhi's unease, the sight of it triggering memories of their family's past struggles and humble beginnings. She strode forward, taking Zhezhi's hand and leading her into the center of attention. "Didn't you know? Zhezhi was gifted from the day she was born. Her paintings were chosen for exhibitions even before we hired a tutor." With a painted smile, she mimicked the grace of the upper class. "Would you care for a painting too? Zhezhi can finish one in a day." Zhezhi shrank inwardly, wishing to disappear, only to be thrust forward. "Show everyone your skills, Zhezhi." All eyes turned to her, leaving Zhezhi trembling, unable to paint a single stroke.

Later, as the mansion fell silent, Zhezhi gathered her courage again. Holding the day's painting, she approached her parents' bedroom door. Just before knocking, she overheard their conversation inside.
"Did you know? That painting sold for 400,000 Credits today. With this money, we can fulfill the paused order."
"Right. Are the paintings for the guests ready for this weekend?"
"Not yet. Zhezhi mentioned wanting to go to the theater. That girl, always seeking diversions, never thinking about what's best for this family..."

Zhezhi looked down at the happy family in the painting, her grip tightening until it crumpled, distorting her mother and father's faces.
"...I'm sorry."

Zhezhi realized something was amiss in her painting only after heading out for a sketch. As she took in the idyllic countryside, a new idea struck her like a ray of sunlight. Glancing around to make sure she was alone, she stretched her arms, and for a moment, let go of her parents' demands.

As her bare feet met the grass, its prickly, cool softness awakened a sense of nature's healing vitality. She broke into an impulsive run, shedding worries about upholding the refined image her family demanded. A distant voice abruptly interrupted her frolic.

"Hey, who are you? What are you doing in our field?"

Startled, Zhezhi immediately looked down at her feet in embarrassment. Realizing she was trespassing on private property, she apologized as she tried to leave. "I'm so sorry! I came here to paint. I didn't know this was someone's field..."

The girl laughed, seeing the panic on Zhezhi's face. "Don't worry! These veggies are tough. You don't need to run!" She laughed as she continued gathering the vegetables with her sickle. "A painter, huh? That's different..." Zhezhi hesitated for a moment, seeing the girl hard at work. "Let me help you with that..." The girl met Zhezhi's eyes with a twinkle. "Sure! Thanks for offerin'! Here, use this sickle, I'll go grab another one!"

Zhezhi stared in confusion at the sickle promptly shoved into her hands. But she soon squatted down among the tall vegetables, mimicking the farm girl's movements. "Wait, wait. You won't get anywhere doin' it like that. Here, lemme show ya!"

Under the hot sun, the two girls worked together to harvest the field until they reached its end. Exhausted, they lay under a tree to rest. Zhezhi forgot about the mud on her shoes and the dirt on her expensive dress, lost in the joy of spending time with her new friend. The carefree laughter between them filled her heart with ease and brought a true smile to her lips.

The mood was suddenly cut by a sharp voice. Zhezhi turned to see her mother watching, her eyes squinted in anger. Zhezhi could see her disdain for her new friend. Sprinting to her feet, she ran to explain and apologize, transforming back into the child her parents demanded she be.

A few days later, the girl received a scroll. She unrolled it carefully, gasping softly at the sight. The painting showed her and Zhezhi in the sprawling fields of her home, picking vegetables together.

A letter fell from the painting.

"I'm sorry I didn't say goodbye. I had so much fun harvesting the field with you! The sickle, the sun beating down on us, my sore hands... It made me realize what my paintings were missing. This is my best work, and it's for you! I hope you like it! Maybe next week, I can sneak out to help again."

Reading the letter made the girl smile, but she couldn't help being confused by Zhezhi's last line.

Next week? Did she think the vegetables would grow back that fast?

Unsuspecting, Zhezhi was thrown out of her home, her belongings strewn across the courtyard like discarded memories. As she gazed at the mess, it dawned on her that she herself was just another discarded item, abandoned by her parents like the rest.

Desperate for shelter, she first sought out places familiar to her. But those once kind and welcoming turned cold when they learned of her plight. Behind their polite excuses, Zhezhi saw the distaste in their eyes as they pointed her to an old hotel on a street corner.

The hotel's decaying corridors teemed with unfamiliar fights and loud arguments. Sitting on the bed, she wrapped herself tightly in the musty covers, eyes fixed on the flimsy wooden door barricaded by a table. She longed for sleep, hoping to wake from this nightmare, yet fear kept her awake, afraid the door would shatter if she closed her eyes.

Her descent from luxury to hardship stretched endlessly, each day a painful reminder. The staggering figures of her parents' debt seemed to flicker across the ceiling in the dim light of her windowless room. Her hands, covered in worn bandages, trembled from painting non-stop for two days, but she dared not rest.

"It's a big order... I can't mess this up," she murmured, her weary eyes blurring the landscapes on her canvas.

Suddenly, harsh shouts pierced the night, jarring her awake from an unintended nap at her desk. She stumbled to the door, slipping on something wet at her feet.

Aching from the fall, she stood nervously at the door of her leaking room, apologizing repeatedly to her neighbors. The biting cold seeped through her wet clothes, and the neighbors' complaints echoed through the thin walls. She stared at her painting, ruined by the water, and a heavy sigh escaped her lips, compressing the room's thin air, almost crushing her fragile frame.

Zhezhi's exhausted figure stood motionless in the cold puddle. After a long pause, a faint light glowed in the cramped room. With paint-stained fingertips, she scrolled through her Terminal, "First, shut off the water valve... then replace the damaged parts..."

She had made a habit of looking up solutions for life's unexpected challenges. 

"I think I've got it... I'll give it a try..."

She waded through the water, slowly making her way to the source of the problem.

"This painting is a reflection of me. Everyone needs to see at first glance that it's an expensive masterpiece."

"If this is the best you can do, I'll take it. But only at half the price."

The client's words echoed in Zhezhi's mind. She wandered the streets with her bundle of paintings, feeling a sense of numbness begin to creep over her as the festive preparations around her started to fade into the background. It wasn't until she tripped, her paintings scattering, that she snapped out of her daze. Without bothering to look for her glasses, at first she scrambled to pick up her work. But as the wind blew some paintings out of reach, she stopped, staring for a moment before deciding to let them go.

"Forget it, they're lousy anyway... What's the point of having them back..."

She dropped the remaining paintings in her arms, letting them fall. Lost in her thoughts, she didn't notice someone stopping in front of her.

A stranger picked up her paintings and glasses, handing them back to her.

"Did you paint these? I've never seen art like that. Remarkable."

Zhezhi, stunned by the compliment, could only accept the outstretched paintings and watch the stranger turn and leave alongside their companions, disappearing into the night.

She fumbled to put on her glasses to catch a clearer glimpse of who it was, but all she caught was a distant silhouette.

"Someone complimented me... "
"They had nothing to gain from it. It was just... simple praise for my paintings."

The stranger's words, simple yet sincere, pierced through her paintings to reach her heart. For the first time ever, it was as if someone saw her creative intentions. It was like a sudden beam of light scattering the dark clouds that had long weighed her down, bringing a sense of warmth long overdue.

Zhezhi stared in the direction the stranger had vanished, clutching her paintings tightly. Until...

"Excuse me... Hello?"

Days later, a familiar voice startled her out of her thoughts as she searched for the perfect spot to paint.

"Don't worry, we're just here to chat."

Zhezhi looked up and saw a pair of golden eyes. The memory of that night rushed back—this was the person who had complimented her work, their voice free of the pretense she had grown to despise from everyone else. That voice had given her strength when she had been ready to give it all up.

The warmth from that night returned, filling a world of pale grey with color once more.

So many paintings... Ah, not that I'm complaining about the commissions! It's just, I keep finding new things that inspire me... Oh, sorry. What I wanted to say is, the sunlight on you right now is so beautiful. Can I... paint you?

I-I saved half of a lemon cake for you. Want to try it? I couldn't help myself and bought it with some of the money I saved up, as a celebration for finishing my commission. I've wanted it for so long! It's sweet but not too rich, with perfect layers. It tastes just as amazing as I imagined!

You mean those phantasms? They're just illusions. They might look vibrant and stunning, but... they're not real. I prefer a flawed reality over a perfect illusion. Even though it's tough and unpredictable, it also has its surprises, like... meeting you.

Do you ever feel lonely when you're alone? I do enjoy my own company, but after a while, I start wishing I had someone to talk to. But... whenever I try, I never know what to say and I'm afraid of saying the wrong thing, so it usually ends up awkward... But talking to you feels different. It's like a conversation I used to only dream about. I really wish we could talk like this... forever.

You know, I started a portrait of you a while ago, but I haven't finished it yet… I feel like I can't capture everything I feel for you on just one piece of paper. If it's alright, I'd like to show it gradually, through what I do and say.
I like… being by myself.
My family's debt… It'll probably take me my whole life to pay it off by myself…
I have a sweet tooth. Sweet things always give me more energy!
When I cook, it feels like the flavors never blend, like the ingredients and seasonings are at odds… Are-are you interested in tasting it? Um, I'll have to practice more before you try it…
I hope… that one day, I can spend all my time painting what I truly want, leaving a piece of the real me in this world.

This brush is called Miaohua. It reacts to phantasms. When I was younger, I had trouble controlling my ability, and sometimes I couldn't tell reality from illusion… The worst time, I was trapped in an illusion for two whole days without realizing it. It was Miaohua's reaction that made me realize everything around me was fake and helped me find my way back to reality.

If your living space feels cramped, try using furniture in a single color. If prices seem unfair, try going right before the shop closes to find a good deal... I've realized that since I can't change everything, changing my perspective can really help... it's helped me find little bits of happiness in life!

She's got a real knack for appraising antiques, and knows all about where the rare old paintings are kept. If she hadn't told me where to find those friendly collectors, I'd never have gotten to see the originals with my own eyes. Though she's never told me how she gets her info, I can tell it's not easy. So now and then, I slip some money into her pocket when she's not looking!

Oh! She once invited me to dinner, and I said yes. However, when I arrived at the restaurant, it turned out to be a large gathering with dozens of people… I was quite nervous, but she was super nice, always making sure I was okay. Thanks to that, I actually met a lot of new people... and some of them even became my clients later on.

It's your birthday today. I-I know there will be many people celebrating and giving you gifts, so... I'm not sure what to get that won't be repetitive… How-how about you tell me what you want? Anything you want, I can find it, or any place you wanna go, I'll come along. If you haven't decided yet, that's okay too! My offer will never expire. Really, anytime you need something, just ask and I'll do my best. Oops, sorry, I-I'm rambling... I meant to say, happy birthday!

As the child of two scholars, I was always drawn to the same path. Perhaps trying to follow in their footsteps. However, my recollections of them have blurred over time. Most of what I know about my parents comes from reading their published research and evaluations of their work by others, rather than personal memories. Their existence feels elusive to me, like a hazy dream. Yet, I am their legacy—a reflection of their brilliance, and... their madness.

I like interacting with people, be it my colleagues at the Academy, or others. At times, I fear losing sight of my own humanity while chasing truth's elusive grasp... In those moments, I step away and seek solace in a bustling crowd. The laughter on their faces reminds me of the warmth of human connection.

Losing my arm didn't bring as much pain as I expected. I was too consumed with excitement, finally discovering the Court of Savantae Ruins, following in my father's footsteps. The achievements I witnessed were beyond imagination. The secrets of a hidden civilization were revealed to me, their inventions harnessing the universe's echoes.

...Ah, it's you. Please, come in. No need to worry, I just need to recharge after all those meetings. Like a machine needing a break. Hmm? So you would like to help? Sure, please sit here. Just... stay next to me for a while. You don't need to say anything. Yes, this will do. Thank you.
Writing a report alone, after completing research, is satisfying. My scattered thoughts and inspirations come together during this time, becoming clear and organized.
During back-to-back academic conferences, my focus wanes and I need time to recharge. Being with peers is enjoyable, but a little solitude is necessary for me to stay sharp.
I love all breakfast foods. I prefer to sleep and wake up early instead of staying up late and consuming caffeine. Eating consistent breakfast portions energizes my mind quickly.
Oh, the Sour Soy Milk… When I was a toddler, my mother once convinced me to try it. While most of my childhood memories are joyful, that particular taste was overwhelming for my young palate.

This prosthetic arm is pretty handy, loaded with helpful features. I don't have to worry about any arm injury while working on risky experiments, and I can even pull a few pranks on my colleagues. Oh, you want examples? Well... I'll definitely show you when I get the chance.

Among the friends I made when I was a kid, Pascar was the one who kept in touch with me for the longest time. Certain actions, when done too late, can lead to lingering regrets. Occasionally, I contemplate how each individual is a complex enigma, similar to the countless scientific theses I have studied.

Mortefi is an interesting person. He's devoted to his work with unwavering determination. It's that kind of intense drive that pushes scientists towards brilliant discoveries. I know he considers me a "genius"—but in a workplace with only "geniuses", many ideas will never be realized. My dear friend has yet to grasp his true potential.

Baizhi is a great researcher. Our work doesn't often overlap, but I've read her reports and they're well-informed and persuasive. She often participates in field research, earning her a reputation among peers for bringing back valuable data.

I had pictured our reunion in my head, again and again, after your departure. I wondered what kind of person you would become, how your days were spent, and if you achieved your goals. Countless questions filled my mind, but when I saw you again, there was only one thing I wanted to say: Welcome back. Back to the Black Shores, and… back to my side.

Your past... I promised to keep it a secret, at your own request. That day, I realized our reunion would be one-sided. This is why your memory loss didn't surprise me... But it doesn't matter now. You may have forgotten me, but I will remember everything about you, always.

Humans dream to fulfill their desires. For a long time, I believed such dreams were not meant for me, as I had never yearned for anything. Until one day... I dreamed of you. We were strolling through an unfamiliar land, basking in the warm sunlight. You showed me your world and shared stories of your past. You even brewed a cup of tea for me... Though only a figment of my imagination, I wished that moment could last a little longer.

Next time you journey to distant lands, could you bring me along? I don't want to watch from afar or hear secondhand about your adventures. I long to experience the unknown by your side, as your friend... Please, will you give me the chance?

Pressing a piano key creates an enchanting sound from the vibrating strings. Unlike other frequencies I've processed, a piano produces a pure, clear, and vivid tone. If I could one day communicate my emotions as simply and intuitively as humans do... If I could create my own melodies, would you be my first listener?

The food I hate... Hmm, hate might be too strong a word, but I tend to steer clear of pickled food, like preserved plums. While I appreciate their long shelf life, the fermented smell reminds me of their preserved nature.

Ah, so you've noticed the crystal on my chest. It's not an adornment, but a fissure brimming with the energy emanating from my body. Through it, you can touch the core I've managed to keep safe since my creation. It resembles the kernel of a fruit, or the beating heart of a human, where the essence of life is preserved.

Though her words may not always align with her actions, she remains fiercely loyal to her desires. Her carefree lifestyle holds a certain charm, yes, but we were made differently, with distinct objectives to pursue. Following your example, I've allowed her to make her own choices, without limitations.

The so-called renowned appraisers are always squabbling over the value of antiques.
 
First, they downplay an antique's value, snapping it up for a pittance, only to turn around and hype it up to sell for a fortune. Craftsmanship? History? Mere afterthoughts in their pricing games.
 
However, Youhu has a different approach. For her, the worth of an antique isn't measured solely in currency, but something more unique.
 
Genuine appreciation is the first factor. Youhu enjoys facilitating deals where buyers are deeply respectful of the antiques and sellers entrust their cherished items to someone who truly appreciates them. As the antique changes hands, its frequency is mirrored in the hearts of both parties.
 
Another factor would be conscience. When Youhu was seven, raiders ransacked the town looking for riches. To them, antiques were just another form of loot.
 
The wealthy merchants and local appraisers panicked, abandoning their treasures as they escaped.
 
The raiders, ignorant about the true worth of these antiques, justified their plundering by saying the people here didn't deserve their treasures anyway, and such items might as well be taken somewhere they would be appreciated.
 
But not everyone fled. Some stood their ground, facing the raiders with steely resolve. They knew the true value of these antiques and defended them to the bitter end.
 
And that brings us to the final factor. The courage to sacrifice.
 
Now, it is Youhu's turn to make a sacrifice. Whether it is her talent, her knowledge, or the lengths she will go to recover them, she is determined to return every lost antique back to its rightful owner.
 
In the past, those who couldn't see the value in these relics trampled all over them. But today, Youhu's mission is to return each lost antique to where it truly belongs.

She awoke from her dream.

The interval between unconsciousness and consciousness became shorter with each passing day. Lady Flora was starting to find it hard to tell where her dreams ended and reality began. She couldn't even recall when this disorientation had started.

Memories surged like turbulent waves, crashing into her mind and wreaking havoc on her senses. Pain ripped through her body, relentlessly and unforgivingly. She opened her mouth to scream, but <te href=850073>Overclocking</te> had turned her throat into a gnarled, coarse root, silencing her cries. 

After struggling to take just a few faltering steps, she collapsed onto a muddy riverbank, trembling, her fingertips spasming uncontrollably.

How many times had this happened? She stared blankly at the dark night sky above.

A void of chaos swirled within her, yet there was one thing that stood out in sharp relief: {PlayerName}.

She remembered everything now.

Magistrate Jinhsi insists that I take some time off work. The streets tonight are bustling with life. Since I have little to do, I imbibed some... floral brew. My body is warm yet my heart longs for someone to confide in.

It is a common practice to don monster masks as part of a ceremonial dance ritual. Folks here believe their reenactment of monsters from the legends of Huanglong may ward off evil and invite good fortune. As for me... I do not need the reenactment, for I have worked hard to suppress the monster within, which is already a perfect mask for me.

Those strange sights and sounds in the cold wind and snow are the past that I cannot sever. But because of you all, I see the silver lining behind these macabre scenes. You give me the strength to pray for the return of spring.

The fate you've sown will bear fruit in the coming years. Should you leave on another journey, please remember to take my... and our blessings with you.

Sanhua

This year's ceremony is different—it is the first one free of the Threnodian menace. People are finally able to laugh and rejoice from the heart, and I truly enjoy seeing everyone smile.

I've told Sanhua and Taoqi to take a break. After working all year, they deserve leisure time to bask in this hard-won warmth. When I see others happily reunited with their families, I can't help but yearn for your presence. I knew you had matters to attend to, but your absence during the most festive days in a year would have made everyone a bit lonely.

So, when you came back with guests from Rinascita, I was truly happy—you really do miss Jinzhou enough to spend time with me. Perhaps, in your heart, Jinzhou has become your home.

I wrote a song to express my gratitude, and it seems I'll finally get to sing it. Wearing the ceremonial dress still makes me a bit shy, but if you like, I'll wear it properly after I finish work and sing just for you.

Jinhsi

I hope this letter finds you well.

Jinhsi and Sanhua were overjoyed by the glowing reviews of the Hero Play from the guests of Rinascita. After a year of hard work, they can finally set aside their duties and enjoy a well-deserved respite.

Your Rinascitan friends were eager to share thrilling tales of the Laureate with me, and I found their stories about you both delightful and heartwarming. It is truly gratifying to see the profound impact your journey has had on the lives of others.

However, I believe it is time for you to take some proper rest now, after the busyness of the Hero Play and the joy of welcoming your friends. During your absence, several notable events transpired in Jinzhou. If you are interested, I would be happy to recount them to you at your leisure.

The day before your return to Jinzhou, the winter's last snowstorm breathed a delicate layer of snow on our Go checkerboard, on which I wrote a wish.

By the time you receive this letter, it will have already come true.

Changli

(A neatly penned letter bearing a wobbly and crooked signature)

Hmph, this is a letter I wrote you. Surprised? Yeah me too. I mean, if there's something I need to say to you, I could just tell you in person, right? But everyone else was scribbling away so I asked Sanhua to write down what I was saying.

When I think about it, we've really been through a lot, haven't we? From Huanglong to the Black Shores and then onto Rinascita. From Loong Buns and Coral Bowl to Pizza Tropicale. Although our trip had its rough patches, in the end, nothing could hold us back.

<s>Mmmh...hmm, so what do I wish for...? Wait no, don't write that down!</s>

I wish from this day on we'll always be well-fed and happy. Oh, and if you ever run into trouble, don't forget to call me. Your business is my business too.

Abby

This is a letter from Carlotta Montelli. I hope this did not come as a surprise.

It wasn't until I lifted my pen that I realized this was not the first time I had written to you. You had known me through my invitation to you to Rinascita, long before we met in person. That was where it all began.

Fate brought you before me. Together, we captured the traitor within my family and took part in Ragunna's grandest Carnevale. Breaking conventions and revealing all to an outsider was a first for me, but with you, everything came so naturally.

This time, when I received your invitation, I did not hesitate to accept. The cultures of those beyond Rinascita are fascinating, and I'm thoroughly intrigued by the Hero Plays of Jinzhou. But what really captivates me are the aspects of you that I have yet to explore.

If my initial invitation led you to reciprocate, then perhaps a heartfelt expression of sincerity might elicit an equally precious response. 

Would you dance with me if I took the first step?

I wrote this letter after watching the play. Pero was happily stuffed after she ate all the petals on stage. She was as satisfied as everyone else.

The waves bring many things—sometimes a discarded bottle, sometimes a broken sail, and sometimes a precious Luceanite. Then one day, you and the captain braved the waves and reached our troupe. At the time, I never imagined you would be such a joy and inspiration to me and Pero.

I took the funny stories you told me and turned them into commedia to give hope and courage to our happy troupe. I hope you will be the first audience for my new play, since it's about your travels. I haven't decided on the finale yet, but perhaps, like your journey, it should have no end.

May the wind always be at your back and the sun upon your face. Next time we meet, regale me with dazzling stories.

Roccia

My dearest friend, thank you for the invitation. I had heard much about Huanglong's Hero Plays, but attending one in person has truly revealed their magnificence!

There's magic to a great performance where actors pour their very souls into their craft. A tale told from the stage can grow to encompass the world! And the audience too becomes part of that world, immersed in the character's joys and sorrows.

I am always fascinated by performances that evoke such feelings. Therefore, the troupe and I have prepared a new play. Care to guess the plot? Well, think back to when we first met—how one hero braved the sea to conquer the storm and be crowned with the Laurel of the Carnevale!

A hero's journey always deserves flowers and applause. We want people to know of your thrilling exploits and to feel the passion and romance of a roving life. Come, my friend! You must not miss the show!
(Enclosed are two front-row tickets)

Brant

During the examination, Roccia chose white clams, seaweed, pink salt, and filtered water to make a pot of clam soup. It turned out nice and clear, with the shells intact. Right when it was done, the clams and seaweed looked a bit like a tiny island—or maybe even a little box.
 
From the way the soup came together, it's clear Roccia's senses are sharp, her mind is calm, and that she has a strong bond with the troupe. No sign of <te href=850073>Overclocking</te> here.

P.S. Roccia had the brilliant idea of replacing the teacup assessment with a soup assessment. After all, soup is more filling, and after the examination, there's enough for everyone to have a meal. It doesn't taste too bad, either.

[Troupe Medic Benir's Notes - R103]
 
After watching Roccia on a few occasions and studying her behaviors, it seems like our first mate has a way of communicating with that strange creature, <te href=850122>Pero</te>. With Pero acting as a translator, Roccia can even talk to other <te href=850082>Echoes</te>. What's interesting is that her ability seems to be growing—at first, she needed to speak with the Echoes, but now it looks like she can communicate through frequencies.

This only started after she joined the troupe and met Pero, so I'm guessing it's some sort of resonance between them, something she picked up along the way. We'd probably call her a Non-congenital Resonator.

P.S. All this is just my best guess, though. With the tools I have, I can't pin down exactly what type she might be. There's a small chance Roccia isn't actually a Resonator, but just so happens to be able to sync up with certain frequencies. Wouldn't that still count as being a Resonator? I'll have to think on it.

After giving them a good polish, she'd plan a heartwarming, dramatic reunion, just as she'd done with Battier's golden harpoon.

One day, Luca looked up at Roccia with a sniffle, holding the ticket tightly in her little hand. "I miss my Mama, Roccia… I want to go home and see her. But I only have a one-way ticket, and I lost it…"

The ticket in his hand read, "One-Way Ticket to Wonderland," written in beautiful handwriting with tiny flowers around the edges.

Roccia knew right away what this was about. The Order, always busy banishing anyone who challenged them, would never be so kind as to make such a heartwarming ticket. She was sure Luca's mother had made it herself, hoping to give her a bit of comfort. Roccia wanted to reveal the truth to her. "The Order didn't make these tickets, Luca. From the handwriting, it looks like a kind lady made it… someone who loves you." "They were made by your mother, Luca. They can't really bring you home, so it doesn't matter if they're lost."

But she knew saying that might only make Luca cry more.

Roccia thought for a moment, then left and returned with a new ticket—a "Return Ticket," decorated with painted flowers, seashells, and a hand-drawn stamp that read, "Arrived at Wonderland."

Luca's face lit up as she took it, clutching it tightly with a huge smile.

As the troupe's prop master, Roccia could easily make something like that, but there was more to it than just crafting. She remembered when <te href=850122>Pero</te> had done the same for her when she first arrived on the island. Sometimes, a little piece of paper was all it took to hold a whole lot of hope.
