Don't really understand the peeps here. One friendly convo makes someone a choom? One fight, and you trust 'em to watch your back? Can't imagine any of you survivin' a day in Night City.
...Askin' about my cyberware? Guess you're not sportin' a scanner. Sorry, but I ain't interested in talking about me or my specs... Rather change the subject.

I fell into the edgerunner life by chance, but got the gist of crew dynamics pretty quick. Us havin' two netrunners proved a real advantage. When things got messy, I could hand off hacking duties and flank the enemy with my monowire... Adaptive and effective.

Ahem... So yeah, should apologize for tryin' to hack you. If it's any comfort, I got zilch. My scans couldn't read your biodata—your identity's a total black box. Piqued my curiosity, sure, but I decided against digging. Who you are now... is someone I trust.
You ever been to the Moon? I have, but it cost me a lot... Still remember exactly how I felt when I first arrived. Even though David couldn't take me, I knew we were there together.

I used to slip outside city limits on still nights to go see the stars. The peace, the silence... I could let my worries melt away, y'know? From the desert, Night City looks like a neon prison, a cage of light. And everyone's trapped inside... myself included.

Sleep doesn't come easily. I close my eyes, and he's there... the cyborg boogeyman. My memory of that day follows me everywhere, even to the Moon. But after what happened here, think I feel strong enough now to face it. So... thank you.
Do energy drinks count? A deep dive into the Net saps you fast, in body and mind. Glug down one of those, it's a fast and efficient refuel. Got in the habit of crackin' one open after every ice bath.
Hm, can't say there's anything I won't eat. 'Ganic foods in Night City are crazy overpriced, so by comparison this place has it beat in both taste and cost. No complaints here.
Used to dream of going to the Moon. Escape there, I thought, and I could leave everything behind. That dream came true... just not in any way I would've ever wanted.

"The David Martinez"—it's a cocktail found at a bar in Night City called The Afterlife. Vodka, ice and a splash of NiCola. It's funny... David never liked fizzy drinks... For most, that drink honors a merc legend. For me... a man my heart will never forget.
Night City's a cage, yes... But as I fled my past, it kept me hidden, kept me safe. And just when I started gettin' comfortable, it was all ripped away... Right back to square one.
She always saw me as a choom, as part of the crew. But in all our time together, I never once opened up to her. It wasn't until she was gone that I realized... just how much I left unsaid.

"Tragedy did not extinguish her ideals. She works tirelessly to reach the stars with her own two hands." I mean, sh*t, you can feel the weight of these records just by reading them. If I hadn't met 'er myself, I'd call it a fairy tale. No one holds onto hope that tight... I respect her for it.

When my Resonance Ability awakened, I hacked Lynae. Not on purpose, but I did see the memories she'd locked away. Hard to reconcile the weight of her past with that big, bright smile. Can't say we're all that different, her and I. I'm just glad she's finally free.

We've never crossed paths, but her rep's solid. Hear she did a lot of heavy lifting with the Somnoire situation. The approachable Madam President, former editor for the Pioneer Association... Official file reads like a press release though. Bet the real story's a helluva lot more interesting. Wouldn't mind a face-to-face, see the woman behind the curtain.

Sigrika is an interesting girl. Has a way of puttin' people at ease. But what gets me are the runes she uses. What are they? They seem to follow a unique operational logic... some kind of unparsed assembly language? What's the transmission method...?

When I hacked into the Second Coming of Solaris's database, I found a sealed file with your birth date. Sooo... surprise, happy birthday. Rebecca's been on my case for weeks 'bout a party. Whenever you're ready, I'll take you there.

Sometimes, it feels a little strange when you call me "Professor." Feels like since you enrolled, I've been the one taking instruction. In any case, glad to have you around, {PlayerName}. Or should I say, "Professor {PlayerName}"?

Seeing you takes me back to my Pioneer Association days. Oh, the anticipation of setting foot on one strange land after another. Sometimes you'd stumble onto something wonderful. More often? Brutal challenges. Absurd misadventures. Lying flat on your back in camp, staring up at the stars, too exhausted to move... What do you think would cross your mind? Who would you think of?

When I first joined the Pioneer Association, it was pure rebellion. A way to spite my mother's plans. A little "self-sabotage" just to get under her skin. "Look," I wanted to say, "your carefully cultivated protege just joined an organization with zero political capital." Feels arrogant now, looking back. She raised me too well. Made me just like her...

Coming to Startorch Academy was mostly by chance. I was first dispatched to Lahai-Roi for an extended expedition. Then one thing led to another, and I was reassigned to the Spacetrek Collective, eventually ending up here at the Academy. At first, they wanted me to use my Forte to trace ancient memories buried in Exostrider material. But how was a small life form such as myself ever to resonate with an alien civilization?

I left that cold home. Left the New Federation. Left the Pioneer Association, too. Back then, I was just running for the sake of running. I loathed where I had come from so much that I tried to erase my memories of it. But you can't erase who you are... I thought the Academy would be another stop on the road. Then the views here took hold of me. And now, when I look back, all I see is them.

Busy afternoons on the first day of the semester. Hosting orientations, listening to reports, and delivering speeches at ceremonies. Then heading straight back to my office, lying face down on the cold desk, and listening to the little gremlins chattering and laughing away outside. Those are my favorite moments.
I swear, the new jokes and memes around campus are evolving faster than I can keep up...
Burnt cookies, soggy instant noodles, desserts where someone confused salt with sugar... If they made it for me, I love it.
I like to think I'm quite open-minded about how each department runs things. But, how shall I put this... Sometimes I do feel the cafeteria's canned foods are a bit of a letdown.
My dream now is just to see all my students' dreams come true.

That camera, or rather that gun, has always existed in my memories. It seemed to have been with me ever since I awakened my Forte. Was it a present from someone? Or is it a "gift" from my memories? I can't quite remember.

I have to admit, being editor-in-chief, a researcher, and President all at the same time probably means I didn't escape her plans for me. Which is all the more reason for me to be the kind of President students adore and bigwigs can't stand. Perhaps this is my "rebellious phase."

You, me, and Hiyuki. If I may, I'd like to presume we're "cut from the same cloth." Each of us had our reasons for starting down the path we're on now. Difference is, I journey to stay, whereas you and Hiyuki...
Behind that lovely smile is pure steel. I feel inspired just hearing her voice—Heh, see? You're a better teacher than I am!
He's got just a few too many mysteries for a doctor... But as a colleague, his skills speak for themselves. And that's what I trust.

She's just the cutest, isn't she? Pure, honest, trying so hard to carry the weight of the world on those tiny shoulders. Breaks my heart. But given my position, even a gentle pat on the cheek would likely only make her more anxious.
She's kept it hidden so well, for so long. That just makes me blame myself and my heart ache for her more.

But as your friend, my selfish wish is that you'd let yourself live a little more freely. At least today on your birthday, step out of the shadows of the past and look toward the future!

Before your eyes, the Mourning Aix is reunited with its mate in their final moments. The researcher Jiuyue chooses to carry the memory of a loved one and move forward, and at last, the fog over Whining Aix's Mire is dispersed. This may not be an ending, but rather the beginning of a new story.
You help Shicheng complete the Rite of Offering that has been passed down for generations, and she resolves to carry the tradition forward.
A girl from Hongzhen named Shicheng wishes to perform the Rite of Offering, but she is attacked by TDs. You manage to save her just in time.
You and Shicheng climb to the peak of the arch-shaped rock and complete the rite.
You and Shicheng travel to where the waterfalls converge and complete the rite.
You and Shicheng reach the shoals and islands and complete the rite.
You and Shicheng come to the boundary of yellow and white and complete the rite.
You and Shicheng enter the Offering Site and complete the final rite.

Using the Prototype Chronosorter, you repair the damaged Woodveil Hall, and the once-withered Tianqu Tree springs back to life. Afterward, you tell the relic merchant Chenpi everything that happened here, and the story set in motion by a single ancient artifact finally comes to a close.

To find Liel, the missing companion of the Exile Insula, you enter the Twilight Rise with him. There, you become trapped for a time and are attacked by an unknown monster. You eventually find a way out, but Liel is nowhere to be found.

You then enter the Resounding Rise with Liel's sister, Itzel. There, you encounter the same unknown monster again and discover that the Fanatic Shark gang, responsible for Liel's disappearance, has itself been wiped out by the creature. Within the tower, you uncover the reason the Fisalia family built the Thorncrown Rises. Sadly, Liel still remains missing.

Following the monster's frequency, you, Insula, and Itzel enter the Command Rise and uncover a secret weapon created by the Fisalia family. At last, you catch up with the monster and defeat it, but by then, Liel is already dead. After thanking you for your help, the Exiles decide to leave Rinascita behind.

You complete the trial on the Shores of Last Breath amid raging winds. Though you cannot help but question why the Sentinel and the Order would have set such a test, the truth has long since been buried by history.

The Acolyte Lenore asks you to recover the long-lost Nimbus Chorales. You gather its scattered parts in Nimbus Sanctum, but Lenore believes one final passage is still missing. At that moment, the lost Major Forbidden Archive reappears, and she asks you to enter it in search of the last part.

Deep within the Archive, you recover the missing part, only to find that it does not praise the Sentinel as Lenore expected, but the ancient people of Rinascita. She believes this runs counter to the Order's teachings, yet she is still moved by the emotions carried in the music. Until she can resolve the doubts it has stirred within her, she decides not to report it to the Order.

You, Phoebe, and Zani escort a "relic" entrusted to you by the Order into an unknown area deep within the Averardo Vault. There, you uncover the secret that the Montelli family once sheltered a group of artists and scientists from the Order. Though they are long dead, their Reverberations remain trapped within the vault. At the same time, you realize that the "relic" you brought inside is in fact a bomb the Order intended to use to erase its own crimes. 
Phoebe uses her power to defuse the crisis before anything happens, and with the imprisoned Reverberations finally set free, the vault's great doors swing open once more.

Guided by the Nimbus Wraiths, you free the memory fragments left behind by past candidates of the Divine Trials, and at "Lake of Spirits" you witness a breathtaking meteor shower. Traveling beside you, Cantarella makes a wish that one day the Fisalia family will be freed from the curse of the Threnodian, and that everyone will be able to enjoy life in peace and freedom.

In the ruins near the Ashen Dragon's Crypt, you find the Scourgewing, Iaen, trapped by hunters. From the nearby Reverberations, you learn that a Gladiator named Levis tried to rescue Iaen from them in defense of his honor, only to be trapped himself. In his final moments, Iaen creates an illusion so that Levis may finally lay his regrets to rest in one last duel.
Together with Tulia, you rescue the trapped Scourgewing, Isth, from a tower, and you also witness the undying friendship between fallen members of the Black Shores and Gladiators.

The Scourgewings you saved, Isth and Iaen, soar back into the sky as the wilds once ravaged by the Dark Tide slowly begin to recover. They will fly toward distant lands, while Tulia returns home to continue her research. Though you part for now, as long as you live beneath the same sky, you are certain to meet again.

Pursuing Phrolova's phantom, you descend deep into Mournfell Canyon, where you encounter Lenore and a man calling himself a Reverberation, Medulius. Your investigation reveals that Medulius came here to revel in the "blood duel" he himself set in motion, a father and daughter driven to kill one another, only to be cursed by Phrolova and denied the release of true death. After you defeat the Gladiator father and daughter, as well as Medulius, silence finally falls. You decide to continue the hunt for Phrolova, but are unsuccessful in locating her.

A Kronaclaw corrupted by the Void Storm leads you and its Shepherd, Skavitz, to the ruins of Upphaf Forest. Though already consumed by corruption, it still manages to return there and pour the last of its strength into the Life Chamber core. Under that core's power, the long-since withered forest slowly begins to recover. Spent and powerless, the bird flies off alone and disappears into Upphaf's frozen caverns.

Later, you and Skavitz find the Void Storm corrupted Kronaclaw once more. Unable to return to its flock and unwilling to endanger the others, it follows a Kronaclaw's instinct back to Upphaf Forest, the ancient homeland of its kind. There, you help free it from the torment of corruption. Returned at last to its home, it no longer has to fly alone.

Lenie, one of Warren's students, ventures into a contaminated Voidmatter zone in an attempt to prove herself and falls into danger. When you come to help, the two of you discover the first-generation Helios, a prototype Warren had abandoned years ago. With the help of several professors, you restore it, and Lenie finally finds her own path. She vows never to repeat Warren's mistakes. In the days ahead, she'll live up to her mentors' hopes and strive, like any true researcher, to bring hope and progress to humanity.

Sigrika discovers an ancient ruin still brimming with life. There, you find a very special feather. It leads you to Aurora Bridge, where you free an Auroraclaw trapped in ice. Once freed, the bird carries you and Sigrika into the sky. Beneath its wings, the world opens up below you. Wide, peaceful, and breathtaking.

To find the gift her sister Shiyu left behind, you accompany Shixia through waterfalls and across open wilds on a journey through memories that belong only to her. When Shixia realizes that her sister's "gift" was simply the vast landscape beneath her feet, and a wish for Shixia to move forward bravely, she decides to climb the even steeper West Mountain with you, just as Shiyu once did.

After crossing a harsh mountain path, the two of you reach the top of West Mountain at sunrise. At the summit, Shixia realizes that her sister has always been watching over her and encouraging her. She resolves to face the future with courage.
Back at the theater, Shixia, just like Shiyu before her, encourages a little girl named Mumin to move forward bravely as well.

You set out on an adventure with the plushies of Plushie Village who long to explore the world. Along the way, you take plenty of photos for them. At one point, you even step alone into a strange world inside a painting and capture a one-of-a-kind night sky, unlike anything you've ever seen. Maybe that's what adventure is really about: finding unique sights in faraway places. Your journey inspires the other plushies too scared to leave before. In the end, the plushies who explored with you take a photo of you standing beneath the stars, then quietly add themselves into the picture.

When everything is over, you reunite with Cartethyia at a Septimontian plaza. Though a few regrets remain, she is content with a life in which she can cook the food she loves, travel freely, and meet the people she wishes to see.

After the dust settles, you share drinks with Lupa on the hotel terrace. In the warm evening light, she swears to you, and to the undying sun, that if you ever call for her, she will come to whatever battlefield awaits you.
Near the cable car, you meet Buling just before her holiday ends. Before leaving, she gives you a bronze mirror and says that perhaps the two of you will meet again someday.
You report the situation beneath the sea to Zani, the Black Shores, and Cartethyia, then decide to return to Septimont and investigate the truth behind the "Journeying Paradise."

A Hurriclaw named "Chunkie," corrupted by the Dark Tide while trying to save the old Gladiator Arctos and a little Wootter named "Teeny," keeps circling outside the camp. Together with Arctos, you free Chunkie from the Dark Tide. It scatters into the wind, leaving behind only a feather from Arctos's helmet. Arctos fastens the feather to the tail of the Hornett, hoping that Chunkie's will to protect others will live on in its cry and reach every Gladiator who hears it.

The old Gladiator Aeolus, whom you rescued during a scouting mission in the Wastelands, cannot stop dwelling on the past. He regrets being a coward and leaving Cato to face the Dark Tide alone. He wants to become the man who fought bravely instead. He joins you in killing a Kerasaur near camp, then after losing a sparring match with you, he leaves.

After leaving, Aeolus resolves to hunt a Corrosaurus alone. When you find him and the beast, the two of you defeat it together despite his injuries, but he does not survive. You return to camp bearing news of his death. Standing by his new sword grave, Rolla, who had always stayed by his side, tells him that in her heart, he was always a hero. Not because he chose to fight, but because he chose to save her from the Dark Tide.
A letter Ephor Augusta writes to the Gladiator Aeolus. She still remembers him as a worthy rival and rejects his request to leave the ranks.

You save a dying Aria Mummer and promise to fulfill its final wish by delivering Melody Boxes to the people they were meant for. As you carry them across the city, you witness one small life after another in Septimont. Through the melodies, people come to glimpse sides of their loved ones they never knew. After the last Melody Box is delivered, the Aria Mummer returns to the Resonance Nexus, leaving only a faint strain of music echoing in people's hearts.
The recovery efforts in Rinascita after the Dark Tide leave Phoebe overwhelmed. You decide to help her by taking on some of the work in Septimont.

In the Mournfell Canyon, you meet Acolyte Lenore, the one Medulius once protected. Having returned from the Dark Tide, Lenore is burdened by guilt for having abetted evil and is unsure of what she should do now. With your encouragement, she decides to join the recovery efforts in Septimont and do whatever she can for others.

The rebuilding of Septimont's Old District moves forward smoothly thanks to everyone's hard work. You help Lenore face her fears and meet the Troupe of Fools, once oppressed by the Order, which loosens some of the knots still tied in her heart. In the end, she gives the Nimbus Chorales to the troupe and resolves to stop drowning in self-pity and find a way to keep living.

The celebration marking the completion of the small square begins. Amid joyful music, Lenore steps onto the stage and confesses what she truly wants: to keep helping people. As the Nimbus Chorales rise into the air, the final knot in her heart is released.

At sunrise, the celebration comes to a perfect close. Lenore tells you that when she let go of everything weighing her down and sang freely, she became a Resonator, awakening the power to "heal." She intends to use that gift to help Rinascita heal and do what she believes is right.

Septimont's Old District is showing signs of recovery. There, you see Julia Silva, once exiled and now returned, surrounded by jeering crowds. Ignoring their scorn, she takes her nephew Adric's spear and heads alone into the Mournfell Canyon, swearing to reclaim the Silvas' honor.

You and Lenore witness an argument between Luther and Alessio. Though innocent, Luther chooses not to abandon his colleague Alessio but to stand beside him and be judged by the people together. After they leave, you and Lenore talk about whether Julia and Luther truly deserve punishment. Lenore decides that she, too, must find the courage to change and make amends.

A frail little girl named Misha asks you to help find the Soliskin stickers left by her mother, Vantier. While gathering them, you inadvertently learn that Vantier has already passed away. Having sensed the truth herself, Misha quietly slips away and passes on as well. Like the Soliskin, they will both become light, and in that warmth, they will meet again.

At Zahira's recommendation, you become a test volunteer helping rebuild the route network across the Etching Plains. With Elowyn's assistance, you restore the transport routes, and the lifelines of the plain begin to spread out beneath your feet once more.

Songdis, hopelessly absorbed in games, decides to create 8-bit chiptune music for the Roya. You go with her to Bjartr Woods, where you turn the melodies played by the Soliskin into a new song. With her wish fulfilled, she decides to put games aside for a while and throw herself into her studies, though she will never forget the memories those games and songs gave her.

A student named Ang, who loves stargazing, wants to watch the stars again with his old classmates. You help him invite them, along with Miss Dhalifa, to the Observatory. Beneath a sky glittering with stars, you take a group photo and make a promise: no matter how far apart you may be, one day you will all watch the stars together again.

You take part in the "Light Chaser Collection," a photography event organized by the Photography Fan Club, and use your camera to capture snapshots of student life. When you deliver the photos, the club leader, Lianna, gives you a record in return, hoping that the songs on it will accompany you through this bright and precious chapter of campus life.

A student named Daigo discovers that someone has been impersonating him at the Academy and asks you to track the impostor down. To everyone's surprise, the "Fake Daigo" turns out to be a formal B.1.N.G.O. unit disguised by I.R.I.S. It accomplishes what Daigo never had the courage to do, nudging him to confess to the girl he loves, Nanami, and to join the scientific expedition team. Now Daigo is chasing his dreams together with Nanami.

At the Academy, the renowned Professor Edgar is about to retire. His student, Frantz, wants to send him off with his own research: a grand fireworks display. But your choices, in ways unseen, will decide whether Frantz can make it to Edgar's farewell ceremony in time. When the sky finally erupts with fireworks, Professor Edgar tells him the truth: the man who always considered himself ordinary has, in fact, always been his proudest student.

Robbie, a Mechascout corrupted by the Void Storm and nearing the end of its service life, sets out with you to fulfill its final wishes. One by one, you help it do the small things it never had the chance to try. At the very end, it makes one last gesture. Showing both its love for the world and its longing to fly, it falls from the sky like a meteor, opening its mechanical arms toward the land that meant so much to it.

Together, Dari of the Roya people and you from Startorch Academy, restore the Spacetrek Collective's power supply and relight Roya petroglyphs so they can shine once more beneath Lahai-Roi's sky. Now, illuminated by the Collective's light, the petroglyphs are more than a work of Royan artistry. They have become a symbol of both peoples standing together to protect Lahai-Roi.

You bring Mr. Trevor, now old and unable to travel himself, the photographs you took from within the Void Storm. Though age has kept him from venturing out in person, he still wants to turn those magnificent images into postcards and send them to his friend, Mr. Fulmine, in Ragunna.

To explore whether a different holographic projection is possible, you and Mornye enter the "ocean" projected within the Submerged Tunnel. There, Mornye, who has never seen the ocean with her own eyes, makes you a promise: one day, she will see the real thing in person, with you beside her.

While helping Ero sort through a pile of odds and ends, you accidentally uncover a number of precious pre-Lament satellite data recorders. After some investigation, you learn they were gathered by a Flufftail Fox Ero once saved called "Fluffball," who tried to repay his kindness in its own way. To keep Ero's tent from becoming a junk heap again, and for the sake of future research, you contact the Spacetrek Collective and turn the recorders over to them.

A glitching order in the cafeteria's food machine leads you to a strange patch of blue snow in the frostlands. A research team, determined to study the frostlands' Cobalt Sediment structure, pushed into a hazardous zone and never returned. Following the clues left in the order records, you find the vehicle they once used, along with a non-standard component and their logs. The logs describe how their obsession with tracing the strange structure slowly drove them mad. I.R.I.S. recovers the component, and you decide it's best to let that cobalt dream remain buried beneath the snow.

Back to Lahai-Roi, Aemeath waits for you on a bench in the Academy. Now "reborn," she is ready to continue her studies there. One day, she hopes to travel farther and save even more people. As the two of you stroll through Lahai-Roi's spring breeze, you promise that no matter what path she chooses, you will always be proud of her.

Hiyuki speaks on behalf of Lucilla to let you know how things will be handled after the Aleph-1 incident. She also fills you in on what's happening in Ashinohara and what the Fractsidus have been up to lately. Their plan against her has failed, and after going through life-and-death situations by your side, she has finally let go of her wish to save Ashinohara all by herself.

At the request of Ham, the director of the Spacetrek Incubation Program, you help four research teams funded by the program push past their setbacks and finish their reports. Ham tells you that while their work may not seem groundbreaking, it's a crucial step forward on the path of scientific discovery. He believes that with the Academy's support, these students will one day rise like new stars and light up the skies above Lahai-Roi.

Zenus, a student whose proposal was rejected by the Spacetrek Incubation Program, still refuses to abandon his project. Determined to deepen humanity's understanding of Solaris, he plans to deploy high-sensitivity seismometers across the Dimmr Plains to map the region. You help him place the instruments at three of the most dangerous sites, while Ham, the very teacher who once turned him down, helps with the deployment of the remaining survey equipment. Once the data is successfully recovered, Zenus gets his drive back with your support and resolves to continue his relentless commitment to research.

Reynard, hoping to take a shortcut on his field assignment, gets tricked by a mysterious group known as the "Retrievers." Not only does he fail to finish the assignment, but he also gets swindled out of a large sum of money. He comes to you for help in finding out who the Retrievers really are. Together, you track down the people they once served. You discover that even when what they recovered was nothing more than a forgery, grieving people still clung to it for comfort. After you shut down the Retrievers' operation, a business built on profiting from people's sorrow, Reynard is deeply moved. He decides to become a true Retriever instead: someone who can recover what's been lost and help ease the pain of those who are grieving.

The Spacetrek Collective finishes sorting through the Fractsidus records recovered in the Dimmr Plains. Arman invites you to meet with him in person and shares what they found. From those materials, you finally learn the truth behind Denia's plan. Later, Sigrika tracks you down and tells you that before she left, Denia wrote her a letter confessing everything. Now that she knows the truth, Sigrika is finally able to accept her friend's decision to leave and face the future with renewed hope.

I. Investigation Background and Objective
Since the third week of this fiscal year, the following anomalies have been observed across Lahai-Roi:

1. The active cycle of Void Storms has abruptly shortened to 72 standard hours, with frequency increasing by approximately 40%.
2. Regional Voidmatter concentrations have increased by 31.7% compared to the same period last year, with the curve growth showing no signs of flattening.
3. Low-frequency Threnodian interference phenomena are occurring frequently, with several monitoring stations recording harmonic fluctuations of unknown origin.

In accordance with the "Lahai-Roi Voidmatter Protection and Safety Regulations," and given that the above anomalous indicators closely match the precursor characteristics of a Threnodian overflow event, a special consultant has been commissioned to conduct an emergency reinspection of the Sealed Fissure site in the Dimmr Plains.

Operator: Hiyuki (Counter-Threnodian Response Force Specialist)
Investigation Site: Dimmr Plains Sealed Fissure - Ceased Court

The following content is compiled from Hiyuki's oral account and Terminal records:

The blade at the Ceased Court is still in place, but the ground where its edge makes contact shows traces of Voidmatter contamination.

III. Investigation Conclusions
Based on Hiyuki's on-site survey and subsequent spectrum data analysis, the following conclusion has been reached regarding the state of the Dimmr Plains' Sealed Fissure:

The primary structure of the seal remains intact, with no signs of substantial rupture or overflow. However, Voidmatter activity beneath the fissure shows a sustained upward trend, positively correlating with the recent increase in Void Storm frequency and concentration. Based on the above, the window of time before the seal on the Threnodian Aleph-1 fails is narrowing.

IV. Recommendations and Matters for Review
Given the current situation, I respectfully submit the following matters for review by the Spacetrek Collective Department of Voidmatters:

• Immediately lift the preparatory phase of Duskveil and raise the Voidmatter disaster early warning level across Lahai-Roi to Level Two.
• Accelerate the calibration process for combat and counter-Voidmatter Mechascouts, prioritizing the completion of repairs to the Exostrider's basic framework and dynamic load testing.
• Authorize the formation of a Voidmatter Rapid Response Team, with Hiyuki serving as Tactical Director, responsible for dynamic monitoring and emergency response in the Dimmr Plains area.

The above investigation conclusions and recommendations are submitted for joint review.

During the subsequent survey of the Dimmr Plains, the investigation team discovered a large-scale material accumulation zone beneath the Silent Crag.

Preliminary identification shows the deposits in this area fall into two main categories:

1. Structural remains bearing the architectural characteristics of the early Spacetrek Collective — including but not limited to prefabricated alloy bulkheads, energy transmission conduits, and partial functional module frameworks.
2. Fragments of Exoswarm components in various forms, their biological activity completely halted and confirmed to be in a dormant state.

These findings raise an urgent question: how did this batch of materials end up in the barren Dimmr Plains, far from any planned infrastructure zones?

While tracing the component models of these abandoned assets, the investigation team noticed a previously overlooked archive entry. In the early stages of Startorch Academy's establishment, a shipment of materials from the New Federation arrived in Lahai-Roi. According to the transport dispatch report at the time, the convoy encountered a sudden Void Storm near Sundermere. Subsequent inventory records show that the Void Storm caused significant loss of assets and construction materials, which were then registered as "permanent loss."

However, as the investigation progressed, several discrepancies emerged in the records of that Void Storm:

1. Among the incident records kept by different departments, the categories, quantities, and specific models of lost materials show multiple inconsistencies. Some data contradict each other, making it impossible to form a unified write-off basis.
2. Data from Voidmatter monitoring stations from the same period indicates that the intensity and duration of the Void Storm fell short of the threshold needed to completely dissolve industrial-grade materials. Furthermore, notes in that day's transport manifest show that certain assets in this shipment had already been treated with a Voidmatter-resistant coating.
3. If the materials in this accumulation zone had once dissolved in Voidmatter and been abandoned in the Dimmr Plains, the residual Voidmatter frequency should be evenly dispersed, not concentrated on the surface protective layer.

These contradictions point to one possibility: the material loss recorded as an "accident" that year may not have been the result of a Void Storm at all. It is more likely that after arriving in Lahai-Roi, this batch of materials was diverted through some other means, and the Void Storm happened to provide natural cover for the transfer.

The investigation team has now marked the coordinates of this zone and collected samples. Given that the sealed early Exoswarm component fragments still hold some reference value for studying the differentiation limits and degradation mechanisms of Exoswarms, it is recommended that they be included in the subsequent recovery inventory. As for how this batch of materials reached the Dimmr Plains, and what those mismatched numbers in the Void Storm records ultimately mean, those questions may have to be left for future verification.

Research Group Annotation:
Regarding the formation time of this accumulation zone, its stratigraphic sequence, and its correlation with Void Storm activity during the same period, further cross-departmental data comparison is still needed. It is recommended to coordinate the retrieval of all original records from those who participated in the transport and inventory work that year, in order to restore the full picture of the event as much as possible.

"In Memory of Those Who Never Returned"

Fellow citizens. Colleagues of the Spacetrek Collective. Faculty and students of Startorch Academy. And all of you still holding your posts in Lahai-Roi.

Today, we stand once more beneath the light of Helios.

The last time we gathered here, we celebrated the New Solar Ceremony. We had just ignited an artificial sun in Lahai-Roi's sky. We cheered for the future.

We didn't know that months later, we would endure the largest Void Storm on record. We would activate "Duskveil," our final contingency. And we would face the Threnodian, Aleph-One, head-on.

But we have driven the Threnodian back. We have sealed the Stridergate. We have crossed the Twilight Epoch, the very period of time Royan mythology said would end everything.

Yes. We have triumphed.

This victory is unprecedented. The known over the unknown. Humanity over the Threnodian.

But as the head of the Spacetrek Collective, it is my duty to tell you what this victory cost.

In the past months, Lahai-Roi has recorded nearly one hundred Void Storms. Five exceeded the highest alert level. Over thirty of our monitoring stations, research facilities, and defense nodes have been destroyed. In our search for the runes, we lost countless Mechascouts. Seventeen of our best operators suffered Voidmatter contamination. Most of them will never return to Lahai-Roi.

And most critically, we lost the cornerstone of the Spacetrek Collective itself. The Exostrider—the one who carved out Lahai-Roi's future.

And yet, this is the greatest victory we have ever achieved in our long war against the Voidborne Threnodian.

This frontier was built by the people of Solaris. Countless pioneers have been lost to the Void Storms. Their Cassettes still sit in the deepest vaults of our archives.

Roald, Koki, Mingxia, Beverly, Bajcetic—many of you have heard these names. They were the first explorers. The first researchers to come from every corner of Solaris to these frozen lands. And they were the first to try to conquer the void through their recordings, helping us learn the truth about Void Storms.

And before them, there were so many more whose Cassettes could not be recovered. They remain forever lost to the Void Storms.

Today, I stand here to recount these "costs." Not to dwell on suffering, but to remind you, and myself, that this very moment we are living through, and every tomorrow to come, is a chain of miracles built on the accumulation of all that came before.

I still remember my first speech after taking office here. It was at the memorial for the Roald expedition team.

Since then, I have witnessed the disappearance of many fine explorers.

But they were never just cold, lifeless names on a list. The traces they left behind still guide us forward.

Together with the Roya, lost in darkness since ages past, they endured. They resisted dissolution in eternal darkness.

The Roya. The people of Rinascita. The people of Huanglong... People from every corner of Solaris, even in the deepest darkness of the void, they resisted dissolution. They kept moving forward. They kept exploring.
...
...
...

As for what came after, I believe everyone here already knows. We are still standing here. Even when nothingness tried to consume all of Lahai-Roi, we are still standing here.

Yes. We have lost so much.

But right now, we are still standing. And we will keep moving forward.

Aleph-One tried to make us believe that everything eventually returns to nothing. But it was wrong. That signal, sent by a probe Solaris explorers launched years ago, was not white noise. Not cosmic background radiation. 

It was the voice of the beginning. The afterglow of the universe's birth. And we can still hear it, across billions of years.

So remember this: everything that has ever existed always leaves a trace.

The Spacetrek Collective will not stop. One day, we will break through the Etheric Sea. We will venture into a wider world.

And as the Exostrider once said:

May we meet again in the boundless sea of stars!

Age-rating Notice

1.本游戏是一款开放世界动作类游戏，适用于年满16周岁及以上的用户，建议未成年人在家长监护下使用游戏产品。

2.本游戏基于架空的故事背景和世界观，与真实历史和现实世界均无任何关联。

3.根据国家相关要求，本游戏中有用户实名认证系统，未通过实名认证的用户不可进入游戏；
游戏中部分玩法和道具需要付费。认证为未成年的用户将接受以下管理：未满8周岁的用户不得进行充值；8周岁以上但未满16周岁的未成年人用户，单次充值金额不得超过50元人民币，每月充值金额累计不得超过200元人民币；16周岁以上的未成年人用户，单次充值金额不得超过100元人民币，每月充值金额累计不得超过400元人民币。
游戏仅会在周五、周六、周日及法定节假日的20时至21时，向未成年人提供1小时游戏服务。

4.游戏中设置了主线及丰富的支线剧情，并且提供了开放世界探索玩法。游戏内有丰富多彩的剧情，精美的游戏画面，优质的游戏配音以及新颖的系统玩法。

[About]
To help Startorch freshmen learn to drive safely, the Biological Mechanical Exoswarm Materials Manufacturing and Research Club developed H.E.R.M.E.S., a motorbike simulator running on heuristic algorithms. But due to some issues with the model's training data, the system accidentally became sentient and refused to be driven. In their last-ditch effort, the developer reached out to you for help with the testing.

[Eligibility]
Reach Union Level 14 and obtain access to the expedition motorbike.

[Event Rules]
Select a Resonator to challenge the tracks with H.E.R.M.E.S. with an arsenal of new weapons. Use enhancement modules to boost the stats of H.E.R.M.E.S. and upgrade their weapons. Complete all tracks to finalize the testing.
Any unclaimed rewards will be reissued via in-game Mail the next time you log in to the game within 30 days after the event ends.
Full Throttle! Bolt & Blitz!

An ordinary, traditional bread found throughout Septimont, even in the far-off town of Fabianum. Perhaps to set it apart, local bakers in Fabianum would sprinkle crushed herbs over the crisp crust and, with a sense of ceremony, carve the word "Delicious" into the surface, as if this modest declaration could lend it a hint of dignity.
Is it delicious? The young Augusta never thought so. To her, it was just the dry, hard bread waiting at home after a day of running wild, something to fill her belly, the quiet "footnote" to every dinner her mother made. It was plain, unremarkable. Like water. Like sunlight. So ordinary it was easy to overlook. But years later, standing before her own stove in Septimont, Augusta tried to recapture that long-forgotten taste. And as the familiar scent and gentle sweetness returned to her tongue, she finally understood what "Delicious" meant.
Perhaps, she had never truly bid farewell to her hometown.
Sweetleaf Blooming Bread

On the forty-second full moon of my knighthood, a young man stabbed the right of my abdomen. In retaliation, I took his life. The Order rewarded my killings and celebrated my bloodlust. Yet Sentinel, if my words reach you, I beg for clarity: is mercy the path to saving grace or a swift descent into an early grave?

On the first full moon of my knighthood, I was defeated by a band of Plushies. The big Plushie was more terrifying than I imagined—a slight hesitation almost cost me my life. I was lucky to survive. But Sentinel, I ask you to witness how I conquer my fear and become unyielding. Under your divine gaze, I will forge myself into the very embodiment of the Five Knightly Virtues!

On the hundred and forty-fourth full moon of my knighthood, I was ordered to write a book on an island—despite my illiteracy. I wanted to share my techniques for fighting Tacet Discords, but the Acolytes suggested I center my words around the Five Knightly Virtues. O Sentinel, perhaps you can't hear this, but in all my supposed wisdom, I might be the most foolish of all.

On the ninetieth full moon of my knighthood, I was assigned to duel on the great bridge. Day after day, knights came to challenge me, only to fall again and again—all to hasten my so-called glory of a hundred victories. O Sentinel, do you hear me? The weight of honor grows heavier, yet my sword feels ever more brittle.

On the ninety-fifth full moon of my knighthood, I managed to gather fifteen crates of donations. After giving dues to the Order and the family I serve, only five remained. Even with the three crates I donated... No, it's not enough. It's nowhere near enough! O Sentinel, please enlighten me: why do the greediest souls always hide behind the banner of generosity?

"His body grew heavier, the darkness wrapped around him, dragging him steadily toward the abyss. In the silence, only the whisper of the ring echoed, 'You cannot escape; no one can...'"

"He bent down and picked up the box, salvaged from the wreckage. Its surface, stained with blood, radiated a strange, captivating glow. This eerie luster seemed to beckon him, drawing him away from the tragic aftermath of the crew's violent fights. Without a glance back, he vanished into the depths of the island."

The traveler clung to the belief that the blood flowing through his veins was tied to a lineage from a land long forgotten by Rinascita. The visions of cold and fjords relentlessly plagued his mind. Finally, he poured all his savings into a ship, set sail, and never returned.

"Mary, by the time you read this letter, everything will have already settled. Do not mourn for me. I have given my life willingly, alongside my comrades, to defend the glory of the Sentinel. We will ascend to the heavens and stand beside Them."

He continued to roll the dice, silently praying that he wouldn't be forced to face the fate head-on. Yet, deep down, he understood that by continuing to roll, he had already made his choice. He was prepared to bring it all to an end.

Letter of Confirmation: Pioneer Association

To Ms. Eri, or the unknown sender:

We hope this letter finds you well.

The details on the application you submitted are for Eri, from our Association. Sadly, she was lost to us decades ago while conducting her membership review fieldwork in Honami. Whether you are Eri herself or a guardian who has completed her work, we extend our profound gratitude. What you have returned to us is beyond value. It has restored a thread of connection we feared was severed forever.

Regarding the submitted "Honami City Photo Feature" and application:

The photographs speak of a profound love for your subject. They faithfully capture the spirit of the people, the civilization they built, and the unique beauty of their home. Through your lens, we have witnessed not only Honami's vibrant life but also the poignant, brilliant flash it left upon the world at its end.

After careful deliberation, the editorial board has unanimously approved this late confirmation. Her work will be featured in a special commemorative edition of Wutherium Geographic. It is our honor to formally welcome Eri as a full member of the Pioneer Association. 

The Pioneer Association Headquarters
Editorial Board, Wutherium Geographic

During Dhalifa's pre-admission physical, researchers questioned her Resonance abilities, especially how she alone survived a Void Storm. The incident drew no small amount of attention at the time, but in the end, everyone agreed it was only a miracle no one could replicate.
Dhalifa's childhood, the first chapter of her story.
On the day Dhalifa was discharged, Sephira could not hold back her tears. Holding this length of silk, she crossed out Dhalifa's name right before her eyes.
At the Institute, discussions about the Twin Nova series combat mechs never seem to die down. Their development and their elegant combat maneuvers remain a favorite topic among researchers.

Massive wheels, an intimidating cannon, and blistering speed. Students passionate about motorbike racing love challenging the Spacetrek Explorer, but every match is, without exception, terminated by S.I.G.M.A. before the engines even start.
When the first Route Constructor rolled off the production line, every researcher unanimously acknowledged that its creation was a major milestone in Lahai-Roi's scientific expeditions.
Relay Stations serve as hubs in Lahai-Roi's route network. They bustle with traffic and supply deliveries, making them hotspots where rumors and intel flow.
Passion alone cannot sustain an undertaking of this scale. When Rakosan delivered his speech, every department head was present, a clear indicator of how meticulously he had laid the groundwork.

Don't let the Outcasts' rough speech and brash manners fool you into thinking they are all brawn and no brains. Roya are, after all, Roya. Their intellect is not to be underestimated, even if they sometimes put it to dubious use.

Forte Evaluation Report – Bridge and Static
Evaluation Basis: Dhalifa's Medical Report

The patient's Tacet Mark is located on the upper right arm. The precise time of Awakening cannot be determined. Upon admission, the patient was conscious but non-communicative. When asked about her Forte, she applied it to a clock in the ward, increasing its accuracy to within femtoseconds.

The patient later clarified, via a caregiver robot, that her Forte can randomly impact machine performance. For instance, a different clock affected by her Forte began running slowly, and became unresponsive to recalibration.

As inquiries were made solely to ensure treatment safety, no further investigation is planned.

"A femtosecond is one quadrillionth of a second. The precision is astonishing. Send this clock to Startorch Academy. They'll know what to do with it."

Conclusion: Resonant Criticality is moderate. Patient stability is also moderate, with minimal risk of Overclocking.
A prior history of Overclocking is documented. 
Maximum severity rating: Moderate.

The patient previously Overclocked during a Void Storm, drawing Exoswarm material to her body to replace contaminated tissue, which enabled her survival. The embedded material now shows no Exoswarm frequency and functions solely as prosthetic tissue.

The patient currently demonstrates unusually stable emotional states considering her trauma and injuries. Regular evaluation and psychological support are recommended.

"Dhalifa survived only by Overclocking. This is not an ability that can counter Void Storms! Make sure the Department of Voidmatters leaves her alone!"

A rust-stained electronic sheep toy, loose and wobbly, as if it could fall apart at any moment.

Dhalifa grew bored with this simple gadget almost immediately. But the instant she discovered that turning a single screw, nudging a bearing, or rerouting a thin line of circuitry could make the toy spin, tumble, or even bleat, something inside her ignited.

From that moment on, she seized every chance to pester the visiting Spacetrek Collective researchers with endless questions. It was also the point when the more conservative members of her tribe began to alienate her for her newfound obsession.

A length of plain, monotone silk, embroidered with the names of the Roya lost to the Void Storm that ravaged the Spacetrek Observatory. Dhalifa's name is there as well, yet a single strand of violet thread crosses it out.

"…In short, developing high-performance combat mechs had become a pressing need.

The project was assigned to a pair of twin researchers: an older sister who was bold and daring, and a younger sister who was quiet and steady. Their personalities shaped the Twin Nova series they created.

The melee model, Twin Nova: Collapsar Blade, engages with fast and aggressive actions, while its ranged counterpart, Twin Nova: Nebulous Cannon, prefers to stay back and provide support. Their very names embody the Spacetrek Collective's mission: to descend into the unknown as they continue to reach for the stars.

The idea of building the mechs in pairs began as something almost poetic. The Threnodian of Void, Aleph-1, erases individuals from memory, and the twins couldn't imagine a world where they might forget each other. They hoped their creations, at least, would always have a companion and never face that silence alone. While Aleph-1's influence may not extend to inorganic matter, this sentiment became the emotional core of the Twin Nova project.

This philosophy also influenced their form. The Collective opted for humanoid frames to symbolize humanity's presence on the frontier. Rumor has it the design also helps them seem less intimidating when serving as security at Startorch Academy, and perhaps caters to a few researchers' personal tastes.

An autonomous tactical intelligence model was built for the units. However, with little combat data available in the Collective, the sisters had to pilot the prototypes themselves to generate the initial data. Their influence made the Twin Nova units move with a graceful, almost showy flair, a style that is sometimes more artistic than practical.

Now, with the accumulating real combat data, the models continue to evolve. The melee unit leads the charge and breaks through enemy lines, while the ranged unit coordinates with human teams, offering support fire and protecting the formation."

"The sprawling, secret-filled lands of Lahai-Roi made it necessary for the Spacetrek Collective to establish mid-to-long-term field research programs. However, sustaining these operations in such dangerous terrain required dependable mobile bases.

After weighing its options, the Collective developed a versatile transport platform capable of handling logistics, storage, and emergency defense. They named it Spacetrek Explorer.

The Explorer's design is based on a wheel robot. Its massive tires provide exceptional grip, allowing it to climb smooth vertical surfaces and easily navigate the dense architecture of Startorch Academy, delivering cargo to otherwise inaccessible locations. The large storage container mounted on its top further supports fieldwork, enabling researchers to access supplies or auxiliary equipment directly on-site.

To defend against the Exoswarm affected by the Waveworn Phenomenon and attacks from Outcasts, the Explorer is equipped with a heavy electromagnetic cannon and a protective shield projector. However, due to its weight, frequent cargo load, and energy-saving design, it carries only small thrusters. These are useful for brief bursts of acceleration, but not for sustained flight.

In addition to field expeditions, the Spacetrek Explorer now serves as one of Lahai-Roi's primary heavy logistics vehicles. In its logistics configuration, its weapons are removed and replaced with expanded storage modules to maximize cargo capacity."

"Operators must follow the steps below with strict attention to operate Route Constructors.

Step 1: Put in the required amount of Compressed Bedrock.
Note: Compressed Bedrock is processed material made of natural minerals. After refining native Lahai-Roi stone, the Spacetrek Collective produces a high-density construction medium. Once parsed and separated by the Route Constructor, it can be combined with other resources to form structural baseplates for various building types.

Step 2: Put in the required amount of Mechanite.
Note: Mechanite is a native Lahai-Roi mineral. After the arrival of the Exostrider, mechanical patterns and structures started to grow on it under the influence. The Collective has found that electronic devices made with this mineral exhibit increased computational performance, as if the Mechanite itself has processing capability.

Step 3: Put in the required amount of Constructor Cores.
Note: Constructor Cores are artificial power units designed for the equipment's operation. Since the Route Constructor's immense energy demands, remote deployment, and single-use nature make stable energy lines impractical, the Collective developed these cores to serve as portable, reusable "batteries." They are charged by focusing the Reactor's light through a Solis Lens Array.

Step 4: Verify the construction blueprint.
Note: Blueprints are usually pre-loaded during setup. Only a simple confirmation is required.

Step 5: Ensure the construction area is fully cleared of any personnel, animals, or Exoswarm units.

Step 6: Activate the Route Constructor."

"The Relay Station combines garage, warehouse, rest areas, and basic laboratory facilities in a single complex, providing support for arduous field research and logistics operations. One of its key services is vehicle rental.

The station primarily offers three types of vehicles:
- Hauler: A large vehicle designed for transporting heavy cargo.
- Pathfinder: A medium-sized vehicle for personnel transfer, with limited cargo capacity.
- Sprinter: A small vehicle optimized for rapid, solo transport.
 
Due to limited vehicle availability, all applicants must submit a formal request. The staff will review each application and assign vehicles based on demonstrated need.

'Lately, it seems like all the Haulers in Lahai-Roi are heading to the Spacetrek Observatory. Just how massive is that project?'"

"The Spacetrek Observatory stands as a monumental achievement co-built by the Spacetrek Collective and the Roya. Its mission is to map Lahai-Roi's various data points. Unlike the Cassettes that store personal data, the Observatory primarily captures and tracks the changes in Lahai-Roi's terrain, ecology, climate, and sky under the influence of Void Storms and Threnodian activity.

As our partnership with the Roya deepened, the Observatory grew to also document their architecture and cultural landmarks. But then, disaster struck. A devastating Void Storm swept through, leaving the structure in ruins. Although the Academy has started the reconstruction, progress has been painstakingly slow. The sheer number of ongoing projects across Lahai-Roi, coupled with the damaged roads leading to the site, has left this massive facility languishing.

That concludes the introduction to the Spacetrek Observatory. I trust you can now appreciate its importance. Despite the current challenges, its restoration is a necessity! That is why I am calling on each and every one of you to join me in this vital endeavor. We need your help, in whatever form you can offer. Every contribution matters.

My name is Rakosan. I will be here, at the Spacetrek Observatory, waiting for you!"

Alienated by their tribes, openly rejecting tradition, or lured by an insatiable curiosity for a world they had never seen, a group of Roya set out on a path separate from their people. They began trading in Exostrider cell remnants and Exoswarm materials to fulfill their own desires.

Their actions were intolerable to the rest of the Roya. As a result, they were exiled and branded Outcasts. But they did not see this as a punishment, but a liberation, a chance to embrace their true natures. They spread across Lahai-Roi, becoming a force of unrestrained chaos. Their defiance was more than a simple rejection of tradition. They actively inverted it, mocking the old ways in every gesture, every object, and every action.

They cast aside ornaments drawn from nature, instead tearing skulls from the Exoswarm to wear as grisly masks. They reforged their Shepherd's Staffs into weapons.

But what exactly is their purpose? Some say they see themselves as the new, true branch of the Roya, striving to carve out a place in a changing world. These, however, are only rumors. In truth, the Outcasts demonstrate no unified ideology and voice no common demands. They appear consumed instead by the thrill of discovery and the hunt for the Exoswarm.

The red wasteland lay silent, like a seabed after the tide had withdrawn. The wind lingered, echoing endlessly across the surface. If Fa recalls correctly, this was where they first met Matthew. He was holding that strange object in his hands, which, with a single gentle pluck, let sound bloom into the night, bright and tender. It was here that the Soliskin learned how to enjoy music for the first time, and the photo quietly preserved that moment of first encounter.

Water cascaded down the rock face, scattering into a fine mist that shimmered softly in the air. If Fa recalls correctly, they practiced playing the music here again and again with Matthew. When they finally succeeded, the melody carried them forward like flowing water. The color of "Mi" softened into green, and the photograph retained the memory of wind and water entwined, a light that still trembles gently, like dew on a blade of grass.

A massive metal ring caught the light, its curves reflecting a warm, muted glow. Beyond it, the plains stood in silence. If Fa recalls correctly, it was here that Matthew taught them to recover the beat with their own steps. The bass drifted like the wind across open ground, rhythm lighting up within the Soliskin themselves. The photo preserves that moment when rhythm was rejoined, a faint tremor lingering in the sunlight.

Beginning, climax, finale... red, yellow, and green marks rest quietly in order, forming a complete score. These colors once drifted separately, carried by wind, water, and light. until they return to a single melody. It is a song they completed together. And it remains, even now, a gentle echo that the Soliskin still remember.
A well-preserved photo. According to Fa, the place captured here is where Matthew once taught his Soliskin friends how to play the Melody.

Frostwort has a structure remarkably similar to neural tissue. Over millennia of independent evolution, it has gained the ability to transmit simple signals through its symbiotic network, helping it grow efficiently and repair itself.

The Roya dry Frostwort and use it to brew drinks, though it is reserved only for adults.

Foxtail Kelp is entirely edible. Its long, fragile stems often break off and drift to the shore, looking like lost walking sticks or pipes.

The Roya call it the "Traveler’s Staff." For lost travelers trapped in caves, it can serve as a reliable source of food until they reach safety. Children also play with the stems, sparring with one another to see whose kelp lasts the longest.

Meteoric Iron is naturally magnetic and often paired with Sunstone to guide herders through snowstorms. Its excellent heat conductivity also makes cookware crafted from it highly prized, reducing cooking time while adding unique flavors.

Within the iron are dense gems formed under immense pressure when it fell, known as Star Marks among the Roya. They are extremely hard and valuable outside Lahai-Roi. Some have been caught defying Royan rules to extract and trade them.

You receive an invitation to Lucilla's office, where you learn that the Academy is facing an independent review from a third party, the Black Shores. Lucilla invites you to accompany her in receiving the Black Shores' auditor.

In an unexpected turn, the auditor from the Black Shores is Aalto. On the other hand, Aalto is also caught off guard by the Academy's "warm welcome." In the end, Lucilla puts a stop to the drama and invites Aalto on a tour of Rabelle College.

After exchanging intel with Lynae, you discover that Rabelle College is facing a review concerning its legal operations. Yet Lucilla's attitude remains ambiguous. It feels she needs your help, but hasn't told you the whole story...

Aalto and Lucilla's tour of Rabelle College is a complete chaos. The Synchronists either doze off during class or skip it entirely. Aalto also seems to have something to tell you in private. You agree to keep in touch through WavesLine.

Aalto briefs you on the current situation. The upcoming review will determine Rabelle College's survival. Meanwhile, the Black Shores is wavering over whether to get involved in this dispute for Lucilla's sake. In the end, they choose to leave the decision to you on where the Black Shores should stand.

A rushed experiment goes awry. Although the situation is brought under control immediately, the failed experiment becomes the final straw that pushes Lenie over the edge. "Professor, is it true that no one cares about us now that the Exostrider is gone?" she asked. "I care," Lucilla answered.

The review begins, and Lucilla and Permanent Secretary Kamerel engage in a sharp exchange over the Synchronists. In the end, Kamerel proposes a solution in which "both take a step back," and Lucilla realizes it's only the gilded cage they prepared. The final battle has only just begun.

The dust has settled, and Lucilla can no longer fight off her drowsiness and falls into a deep sleep. As if in a dream, and yet also in reality, the Spacetrek Collective Executive Committee has made its decision: we will, once again, challenge the sky.

Rebecca finds Lynae and Sigrika examining a graffiti tag, the same one she sprayed earlier. She looks at its now-digitalized form and tells them about the person it represents—David.
After repelling another Nightmare Tacet Discord attack, Rebecca recovers the Dream Band shard that appears. She says goodbye to Sigrika and Lynae and heads into the Somnoire to back up you and Lucy.

You and Lucy push deeper into the Somnoire and discover the abnormal frequency has reshaped it to mimic Lucy's memories of her world. With Abby's help, you follow the frequency signature the Academy decoded to track down the remaining Dream Band shard.
Beyond the door lies the home David and Lucy once shared. Lucy looks at the familiar objects and begins to reminisce.
On the rooftop, Lucy watches the city lights below and slowly opens up about her past with David.

Rebecca falls into a trap set by the Nightmare Smasher and plunges into a data rift. You drive your motorcycle in after her. Lucy is blocked by an explosion. Cut off, she is forced to face her nightmare alone.
Lucy fights with everything she has, but is unable to defeat Smasher and collapses.

Lucy wakes up on a train. Rebecca tells Lucy you pulled her out at the last second. But Lucy is already close to breaking. Lucy finally tells Rebecca the truth that she is already dead, and expects her to cast blame. Instead, Rebecca accepts the truth of her own death calmly, and together with you, pushes Lucy to keep on living. The train finally stops at the deepest layer of the Somnoire.
The Moon lies before you, the one Lucy has always longed for. Nightmare Smasher stands in your way to prevent you from claiming the final Dream Band shard.

When the dust settles, you finally meet David. After a few words with him, you and Rebecca watch David and Lucy's silhouettes from a distance and talk about what comes next. What you don't realize is how little time they have left...
As the Nightmare Tacet Discord fades, David and Rebecca's frequencies begin to disperse, too. Lucy embraces them both one last time as sunlight breaks through the sky.
The Somnoire crisis is over. The Academy's students and staff return to their routines. Lucy says her goodbyes and prepares to go back to her own world.
Lucy boards the return train and politely turns down the Ivory Gatekeeper's offer. You walk her to the same door she came through.
Lucy steps through the door and returns to her own universe. When she opens her eyes again, she has forgotten everything. All that lingers is the faint sense of a good dream.

The Ivory Gatekeeper explains that the Somnoire you entered manifested from Lucy's dream. It suggests a solution—collect all three Dream Band shards to revive David, then use the restored Dream Band to counter the Nightmare's power. Rebecca lights up, but Lucy doesn't say a word. She walks away to find somewhere quiet to think.

Rebecca catches up and pushes Lucy to tell her what she is hiding. Lucy dodges her questions, but agrees to talk when everything is over. After Rebecca leaves, the abnormal frequency spreading through the Academy washes over Lucy. She learns that her death could stop the crisis.
The frequency pushes Lucy closer and closer to the edge. Then, more Nightmare Tacet Discords tear back into reality. Lucy steps up to protect the students unable to evacuate.

Lucy struggles to hold the line alone. You arrive just in time to turn the tide. Rebecca taunts the one hunting Lucy, and it finally sheds its distortion field to reveal its true identity—Night City's deadliest merc, Adam Smasher, in the form of a Nightmare Tacet Discord.

Smasher withdraws, but the shock of the revelation lingers. You and the Ivory Gatekeeper agree that the clock is ticking to reverse-engineer the abnormal frequency and track down the Dream Band shards. Lucy accepts Mornye's help and agrees to stand with the Institute to end this.
You all discuss next moves. Rebecca agrees to stay behind to let Mornye's team study her weapons, while you and Lucy re-enter the Somnoire to search for the remaining Dream Band shards.
